\begin{abstract}
The Renewal Grand Tensor is ultimately reconstructed from a fixed typed event
grammar, the actual occurrence interface, complete contextual prediction,
protected orientation, and absolute physical calibration, not from a hidden
state space, a selected target algebra, or separately supplied positive process
combs.  Before any generated ledger is adopted, complete future equivalence of
raw histories gives the unique coarsest persistent predictive relation carrier.
Every deterministic predictive presentation surjects onto it, and every
future-operational compiler factors through it.  A generated ledger is therefore
a finite compiled realization of this quotient rather than a foundational state
space.  Same-cut point readability, protected orientation, and absolute scale
remain separate physical rows and are not manufactured by future sufficiency.

In a finite compiled presentation, the ledger is reduced to the unique smallest
typed right congruence through which every admitted record-conditioned future
factors.  This minimization is terminating, stable under unread refinements,
and must precede completion of the record writers to a $C^*$-history algebra.
Dual-frame tomography then reconstructs the finite process tensors; ancillary
positivity, causal trace recursion, and prefix compatibility are consistency
tests on the contextual probability table.  The record-conditioned Hankel
quotient gives the minimal linear predictor and its table-native executable
algebra, while the positive comb selects the canonical support-minimal
sequential CP class.  The complete mixed-word maps generate the process-history
$C^*$-algebra, its contextual future radical gives the unique minimal
context-preserving separated envelope, and the normalized regular trace
produces a finite flat word-Gram hierarchy which reconstructs the unit,
involution, multiplication, minimal record algebra, conditional predictive
algebras, and every represented mixed history.

The definition used by the domain sections is strengthened accordingly.  The
structural tensor reconstructed from the original Store cylinder is retained as
an exact forgetful shadow, but the unqualified Renewal Grand Tensor means the
conservative readable enrichment
$\mathsf P_X^{\rm rel}=\mathsf P_X^{\rm old}\ltimes
\mathfrak P_X^{\rm rel,min}$.  In the recurrent same-history packet
$(Z_n,\Gamma_n,O_n,\Xi_n,Z_{n+1})$, the predictive component $Z_n$ is the
future-minimal history quotient of the augmented event law; the added physical
content is its same-cut realization together with the old Store outcome and its
$A_3$ root, the scheduler-separated fast root path, the determining-field,
nuisance, reward, orientation, calibration, and action marks, and the next
readable state.  Forgetting this enrichment recovers every old Store cylinder
exactly.  Across cutoffs, one paired old--detail polarization table supplies the
Schur-compatible refinement data.  Thus persistence is derived at the
predictive level, while point readability, spatial routing, protected
orientation, and the common field/action interface remain explicit occurrence
rows rather than unrelated downstream primitives.


The upstream basis is correspondingly closed relative to the fixed typed audit
category.  Actual occurrence, complete contextual prediction, protected
orientation, and absolute calibration have cofinally natural separating pairs
and are therefore row irredundant.  Orientation may be bundled into an enriched
occurrence packet only when an actual Read and decoder recover its section;
this reduces notation, not information.  In log-affine calibration coordinates,
physical incidence $Lx=b$ leaves the exact residual group
$\mathcal K_L^{\rm phys}=\Ker L/\operatorname{Im}J$, and one scalar anchor per
independent quotient direction is necessary and sufficient.  Predictive
persistence, positive process structure, reset, recurrence, excursion laws,
and waiting laws are derived or finitely decidable.  The conclusion is a
relative minimality theorem for the declared language and morphisms, not an
absolute metaphysical claim.

Finite certification is now subject to the same source and domain discipline.
Executable conclusions have four outcomes: pass, exact obstruction, unresolved
strict margin, and rejected ill-typed input; rejection is not a theorem verdict.
Uncertainty radii and quantitative floors carry explicit sign types, and a
singular state block may be eliminated only after its actual Moore--Penrose
support and range incidence have been verified.  The resulting supported Schur
identity prevents a counterfeit support projection from concealing an
indefinite full carrier.  On one frozen finite corpus, three independently
implemented exact-rational evaluators agree on all $3392$ complete command
conclusions, while mutation and sanitizer replays preserve the declared trust
boundary.  This is a corpus-relative verification theorem and supplies no
physical occurrence row.

The scheduler-separated geometric branch is realized explicitly rather than
left as a nonempty abstract alternative.  On the scalar-period $A_3$ quotient,
symmetric root clocks of order $h^{-2}$ and the fast speed measure produce a
faithful ten-dimensional ADM score frame, order-$h$ edge conductances, a
uniform three-dimensional cut margin, compact Hodge screens, and an exact flat
vacuum limit.  Multiplying the common root rate by $e^{-2Ht}$ and the speed
density by $e^{3Ht}$ gives a second conservative regulator with
$g(t)=e^{2Ht}g_0$, unit lapse, summable Cartan--Palatini consistency defects,
and the constant-curvature vacuum equation
$G_{\mu\nu}+3H^2g_{\mu\nu}=0$.  Thus the repaired primitive has both flat and
genuinely curved vacuum spacetime realizations without a primitive metric,
coframe, connection, or curvature tensor.


A differentially complete Grand Tensor also carries a canonical spectral
quotient.  A positive bimodule-compatible Gram on universal one-forms gives the
source-minimal one-form carrier and a real even finite spectral triple with
explicit Dirac operator, grading, opposite representation, and order-zero and
first-order identities.  The history algebra and regular trace alone do not fix
the differential scale.  On stationary renewal graphs the Hodge--Dirac square
is minus twice the symmetric generator and its commutator norm is the
pointwise carr\'e-du-champ norm.  On the flat and de~Sitter $A_3$ regulators, the
pure-state Connes distances converge to the independently reconstructed
renewal slice metrics.  Spectralization forgets divergence-free cycle currents:
the graph inverse fibre is an open polytope of dimension $b_1(G)$ and contains
laws with different entropy production.  More generally, every finite spectral
packet and every separable compact-resolvent packet have marked finite or
strong cofinal Renewal realizations, whereas the strict norm-monoidal image is
the proper spectrally quasidiagonal subclass.  An austere derivation-only source
selects the unique centered Dirac representative and leaves an explicit

On a loaded finite field shell, this spectral quotient has a sharper physical

The relational cutoff packet is further organized by a typed closure profile.
A loaded sector is classified by its native closure algebra---positive interior,

For a positive head--detail action carrying an actual boundary map, elimination
must be performed after the interior and boundary rows have been assembled.
If $S$ is the ordinary interior Schur complement, $E$ the boundary source on
the harmonic lift, and $K$ the detail boundary-relaxation operator, the exact
head action is
\[
 \boxed{S+E^*(I+K)^{-1}E.}
\]
The positive difference $E^*K(I+K)^{-1}E$ is the precise overestimate incurred

The canonical exceptional carrier at threshold $\beta$ is the spectral screen
$\one_{[0,\beta)}(A)$; it is the unique minimum reducing screen on which the
margin $A\succeq\beta(I-Z)$ can hold.

Part~I strengthens this finite theorem in three directions.  First, any finite

The joint-source calculus is further refined into a hierarchy of source,

For affine pair systems the radical--Euler source has a source-fixed two-sided

\section{Introduction and proof-status discipline}
\label{sec:introduction}
% =============================================================================

The Grand Tensor is the complete positive moment object of the operationally
accessible renewal histories.  Its corrected emergence chain is
\[
 \boxed{
 \begin{gathered}
 \text{fixed typed potential event grammar}\\
 +\text{ actual occurrence, complete contextual prediction,}\\
 \text{protected orientation, and absolute calibration}\\
 \Downarrow\\
 \text{minimal history-future quotient and persistent predictive carrier}\\
 \Downarrow\\

 \Downarrow\\

 \Downarrow\\

 \Downarrow\\
 \text{contextually separated finite structural shadow }\GToldX\\
 +\text{ readable geometric/field/action enrichment of the derived carrier}\\
 \Downarrow\\
 \text{relationally completed Grand Tensor }\GTrelX\\
 \Downarrow\quad
 \begin{matrix}

 \text{and verified domain-specific loadings}
 \end{matrix}
 \quad\Downarrow\\
 \text{physical loaded realization and terminal sector certificate}.
 \end{gathered}}
\]
The history-future quotient is unconditional relative to the complete
contextual event law and is prior to any chosen state presentation.  The finite
structural reconstruction arrows are unconditional at every cutoff relative to
the compiled operational data.  The relational-completion arrow is
unconditional once the derived predictive carrier has a physically occurring
same-cut realization and the scheduler, orientation, calibration, field, and
action marks are supplied; it preserves the old process exactly.  This is not a
claim that the marginal Store table secretly contained those richer occurrence
rows.  No part of the chain says that the complete process probability table
follows from a few scalar microscopic constants.

The raw history, a generated ledger, and the intrinsic operational record are
not identical.  Complete future equivalence may be taken directly on raw
histories, producing the canonical predictive relation carrier before a ledger
is supplied.  In any finite compiled ledger, two values are identified
precisely when every admitted continuation and every actual
record-conditioned response gives the same result.  The stable quotient is the
same coarsest typed right congruence.  When every ledger point has a physical
point Read, all generated values remain protected.  An unread finite decoration
does not enlarge the canonical tensor; a larger provenance record is a finite
bundle over the minimum and is a tensor product only under constant-fibre and
trivialization conditions.

This order is essential.  A $C^*$-ideal quotient cannot merge two surviving
orthogonal classical projections, so record minimization is performed before
record writers generate matrix blocks.  Afterward, the contextual future ideal
performs a different minimization: it is the largest two-sided $*$-ideal
invisible in every left and right word context.  The three objects
\[

 \begin{gathered}
 \text{minimal readable record}\quad\neq\quad
 \text{minimal linear predictor}\\
 \neq\quad\text{minimal separated $C^*$-history envelope}
 \end{gathered}}
\]
are therefore distinct and separately canonical.

At the scalar-table level, the operational response spaces give a direct

Cutoff functoriality is likewise layered.  Exact compression of every causal

The infinite-horizon boundary is explicit.  Part~I-B starts from one complete

The concrete renewal source has three entrances which must be kept separate:

The same order-of-operations discipline applies to spectral geometry.  The

The word ``duality'' has often been used for mathematically different
comparisons.  The paper therefore fixes both a proof-status discipline and a

\begin{definition}[Four proof statuses]
Every substantial conclusion belongs to one of the following classes.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(S\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item \emph{proved here}: a complete proof is included in this manuscript;
\item \emph{finite sector theorem}: a finite conclusion is proved from an
      explicitly displayed sector packet;
\item \emph{conditional bridge}: the implication is proved once a named
      comparison, coercivity, continuum, or resource certificate is supplied;
\item \emph{open certificate}: the named certificate is not supplied by the
      common architecture.
\end{enumerate}
A formal selector identity is never promoted to a problem-level theorem unless
its loading, comparison, and quantitative estimate are also established.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Seven levels of duality]
A comparison between two finite or regulated sectors may preserve successively
stronger structures.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(D\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item \emph{source duality}: pairwise source Grams and linear transfer moments;
\item \emph{transform duality}: an invertible Fourier, Mellin, Peter--Weyl,
      character, or spectral transform;
\item \emph{monoidal duality}: unit, involution, multiplication or fusion,
      tensoring, and all stabilized word Grams;
\item \emph{symmetry duality}: coproduct, intertwiners, projective multiplier,
      and a physical fibre functor;
\item \emph{chain duality}: grading, differential, cohomology, Hodge operator,
      determinant line, and torsion;
\item \emph{coercive duality}: positive cones, norms, resolvent bounds,
      singular values, gaps, and quantitative constants;
\item \emph{regulator/resource duality}: locality, scale, derivative or gate
      cost, sparse composition, and uniform control along a growing family.
\end{enumerate}
Only the structures actually preserved by a comparison may be transported.
\end{definition}

\subsection{Domain-safe finite certificates and exact replay semantics}
\label{subsec:GT-domain-safe-certificates}

The proof-status classes above concern mathematical strength.  A separate
question arises when a finite theorem is carried by an executable certificate.
The certificate language must distinguish a negative mathematical conclusion
from failure of the input to satisfy the theorem's own domain.  It must also
reconstruct the actual support of every singular positive block rather than
trust a submitted projection bearing that name.

\begin{definition}[Four-valued executable certificate semantics]
\label{def:GT-executable-status}
For a fixed finite command language, an executable audit returns exactly one of
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathsf{PASS},\qquad
 \mathsf{OBSTRUCTION},\qquad
 \mathsf{UNRESOLVED},\qquad
 \mathsf{ERROR}.}
 \tag{CERT.1}
\]
The first value proves the declared sufficient branch.  The second carries an
exact witness against that branch.  The third means that the submitted strict
margin is insufficient to decide the mathematical alternative.  The fourth
means that the command is ill typed, violates a declared domain, or fails its
defining equations.  Only the first three are theorem verdicts.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Input rejection is not a theorem verdict]
\label{thm:GT-error-not-verdict}
Suppose a verifier accepts a command whenever its computed status agrees with a
user-declared expected status.  Sound expected-branch verification requires
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathsf{expected}\in
 \{\mathsf{PASS},\mathsf{OBSTRUCTION},\mathsf{UNRESOLVED}\}.}
 \tag{CERT.2}
\]
If \(\mathsf{ERROR}\) is admitted into the expectation alphabet, every malformed
input which reaches that status can be made to pass by declaring the error in
advance, although no mathematical proposition has been established.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Choose any malformed command \(c\) for which the parser or domain checker
returns \(\mathsf{ERROR}\).  If that value is an admissible expectation, then
\(\operatorname{status}(c)=\operatorname{expected}(c)\) holds by construction.
Excluding it forces every accepted command to reach a mathematical branch of
the command semantics.
\end{proof}

\begin{principle}[Typed uncertainty and one-sided primal--dual alternatives]
\label{prin:GT-domain-safe-certificates}
A radius, norm upper bound, perturbation majorant, singular-value floor, or
contraction margin has a sign domain which is part of the theorem.  In
particular, for a rational uncertainty box
\[
 \mathbb B(d_0,r)
 =\{d:|d_j-d_{0,j}|\le r_j\},
 \qquad r\in\mathbb Q_+^m,
 \tag{CERT.3}
\]
negative entries of \(r\) are input errors rather than unusually strong bounds.
A strictly positive affine selector and a Farkas separator are independent
one-sided certificates.  Failure of the selector margin is
\(\mathsf{UNRESOLVED}\) unless an actual dual witness is supplied; it is not
silently promoted to an obstruction.
\end{principle}

\begin{theorem}[Canonical support and supported Schur completion]
\label{thm:GT-MP-supported-Schur}
Let \(D=D^*\succeq0\) be finite dimensional and put
\[
 \boxed{P_D=DD^\dagger=D^\dagger D.}
 \tag{CERT.4}
\]
Then \(P_D\) is the unique orthogonal projection onto
\(\Ran D=(\Ker D)^\perp\).  Let
\[
 M=\begin{pmatrix}A&B\\B^*&D\end{pmatrix}=M^*
\]
and assume the exact support incidence
\[
 \boxed{B(I-P_D)=0.}
 \tag{CERT.5}
\]
With
\[
 \boxed{S=A-BD^\dagger B^*,}
 \tag{CERT.6}
\]
one has, for every \(x,y\),
\[
 \boxed{
 \left\langle\binom{x}{y},M\binom{x}{y}\right\rangle
 =\langle x,Sx\rangle
 +\left\langle y+D^\dagger B^*x,
 D\bigl(y+D^\dagger B^*x\bigr)\right\rangle.}
 \tag{CERT.7}
\]
Consequently
\[
 \boxed{M\succeq0\iff D\succeq0\text{ and }S\succeq0}
 \tag{CERT.8}
\]
under \textup{(CERT.5)}.  A submitted support may be used in this theorem only
after equality with \(P_D\) has been verified.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The Penrose equations make both products in \textup{(CERT.4)} symmetric
idempotents.  On the spectral decomposition of \(D\), they are one on the
positive eigenspaces and zero on the kernel.  The support condition gives
\(B=BD^\dagger D\) and \(B^*=DD^\dagger B^*\).  Expansion of the second term in
\textup{(CERT.7)} then cancels the Schur subtraction.  Positivity follows in
both directions by restriction and minimization over \(y\).
\end{proof}

\begin{countertheorem}[A counterfeit support can hide an indefinite carrier]
\label{cth:GT-counterfeit-support}
Take
\[
 A=(3),\qquad
 B=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad
 D=\begin{pmatrix}2&0\\0&0\end{pmatrix}.
 \tag{CERT.9}
\]
The counterfeit projection \(P=I_2\) makes the formal test
\(B(I-P)=0\) vanish and leaves the apparent Schur value equal to three.  The
actual support is
\[
 P_D=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&0\end{pmatrix},
 \qquad B(I-P_D)=B\ne0,
\]
and the full block form takes the value \(-1\) on
\((x,y_1,y_2)=(1,0,-2)\).  Hence accepting an arbitrary submitted support can
certify a false positive branch.
\end{countertheorem}

\begin{theorem}[Finite exact replay and corpus-relative agreement]
\label{thm:GT-frozen-corpus-replay}
For the frozen finite certificate corpus used to validate the preceding
semantics, three independently implemented exact-rational evaluation stacks
produce identical complete conclusions on all \(3392\) command nodes contained
in \(2048\) certificate wrappers.  The common status distribution is
\[
 \boxed{
 \begin{array}{c|rrrr}
 &\mathsf{PASS}&\mathsf{OBSTRUCTION}&\mathsf{UNRESOLVED}&\mathsf{ERROR}\\
 \hline
 \text{count}&2266&584&272&270.
 \end{array}}
 \tag{CERT.10}
\]
All eight independent proof-structure mutations are rejected, and the
warning-clean and address/undefined-behaviour sanitizer replays preserve all
\(3392\) conclusion objects.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Each stack reads the same frozen rational command data and reconstructs the
entire conclusion object rather than comparing only its status.  Equality is
therefore a finite object-by-object statement.  The mutation tests alter,
respectively, a status, exact fact, rule tag, theorem flag, wrapper index,
command count, proof length, or proof multiplicity; each changed field is part
of the exact comparison.  The sanitizer execution repeats the same finite
comparison under the declared runtime instrumentation.
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[Executable proof objects do not populate physical rows]
\label{fire:GT-executable-not-physical}
\Cref{thm:GT-frozen-corpus-replay} is exact on its frozen corpus and relative

\begin{principle}[Source, coherence, and transport completeness]
\label{prin:GT-coherence-completeness}

\begin{definition}[Native closure classes and operational closure profile]
\label{def:GT-native-closure-profile}
A loaded finite or regulated sector is assigned the native closure type

For an audit-ready packet define
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathfrak P_X^{\rm cl}
 =\bigl(
 \tau_X,g_{{\rm obs},X},m_{{\rm cl},X},b_{{\rm resp},X},
 \alpha_X,\beta_X,Z_X,\mathfrak J_{\partial,X},

\]
Here $g_{\rm obs}$ is the least physical support grade of the terminal

boundary term, $\mathbf U_X$ records unbounded depth, scale, volume, height, or

\end{definition}


\begin{definition}[Structured source--coherence residual]
\label{def:GT-source-coherence-profile}
The source-completeness coordinate in \textup{(CL.1)} is resolved, whenever the

\[
 \boxed{
 \boldsymbol{\mathbb C}_X
 =\bigl(
 \mathbb C_X^{\rm ker},
 \mathbb C_X^{\rm rec},
 \mathbb C_X^{\rm mon},
 \mathbb C_X^{\rm occ},
 \mathbb C_X^{\rm cal},
 \mathbb C_X^{\rm tr},
 \mathbb C_X^{\rm cyc},
 \mathbb C_X^{\rm ord},
 \mathbb C_X^{\rm birth},
 \mathbb C_X^{\rm head},
 \mathbb C_X^{\rm ph},
 \mathbb C_X^{\rm abs},
 \mathbb C_X^{\rm pay}
 \bigr).}
 \tag{CL.1a}
\]
Here $\mathbb C^{\rm ker}$ is the missing cross-record source-kernel block,
$\mathbb C^{\rm rec}$ is the source hidden inside the proposed record fibres,
$\mathbb C^{\rm mon}$ is the unit/involution/product or fusion residual,
$\mathbb C^{\rm occ}$ is the failure of an executable score, action, Read,
or comparator family to occur on the declared same-history carrier and descend
through its physical word relations, $\mathbb C^{\rm cal}$ is the residual
calibration bias on the multiplier, conditioning, or reweighting class for
which that family is intended, $\mathbb C^{\rm tr}$ is the record-visible
source absent from the physical
transport carrier, $\mathbb C^{\rm cyc}$ is the action--Krylov or localizer-
moment leakage remaining after word flatness, $\mathbb C^{\rm ord}$ is the
missing matrix-order writer, future-visible lineality, or source/writer cone
defect, $\mathbb C^{\rm birth}$ is the cross-event source first-birth
innovation after source reuse is removed, $\mathbb C^{\rm head}$ is the dynamic
represented-head promotion or terminal bi-innovation residual,
$\mathbb C^{\rm ph}$ is the remaining phase, cycle, or primitive flat-source
residual, $\mathbb C^{\rm abs}$ is the missing unnormalized partition, volume,
direct-action, or measure-line row, and $\mathbb C^{\rm pay}$ is the mismatch
between the declared positive action debit and the canonical process-stock
payment.  The unresolved
scalar $\mathbb C_X$ in
\textup{(CL.1)} denotes this structured packet rather than the sum of its
entries.  Vanishing of a later component is not used to erase an earlier one.
\end{definition}

\begin{principle}[Upstream closure discipline]
\label{prin:GT-upstream-closure}
The closure audit is ordered as follows:
\[
 \boxed{
 \begin{gathered}
 \text{physical loading}
 \longrightarrow\text{complete assembly}
 \longrightarrow\text{source-kernel and record completeness}\\
 \longrightarrow\text{word/coherence and transport incidence}
 \longrightarrow\text{native localizer}\\
 \longrightarrow\text{screen/boundary control}
 \longrightarrow\text{regulator transport and independent selection}
 \end{gathered}}
 \tag{CL.2}
\]
The first unclosed arrow is the upstream obstruction.  A theorem at a later
arrow cannot repair an earlier defect: a stronger gap does not create an
unloaded source, local reweighting does not populate a missing mixed row, a
pairwise Gram does not reconstruct multiplication, a source overlap does not
create physical transport, a scalar agreement does not establish same-history
occurrence or the calibration class of its Read, a finite screen does not prove
cutoff tightness, and a fitted compatibility row is not an independent
selector.
\end{principle}


\begin{principle}[Predictive--action and global well-foundedness order]
\label{prin:GT-predictive-action-well-foundedness}
For a recurrent or cofinal physical packet, the closure audit continues beyond
\Cref{prin:GT-upstream-closure} in the order
\[
 \boxed{
 \begin{gathered}
 \text{minimum future-sufficient record}
 \longrightarrow
 \text{two-sided action-complete carrier}\\
 \longrightarrow
 \text{physically declared reveal path or stopping front}
 \longrightarrow
 \text{finite recurrent-component closure}\\
 \longrightarrow
 \text{source-paid first exit and cofinal screen control}.
 \end{gathered}}
 \tag{CL.2a}
\]
The arrows are not automatic implications.  Future sufficiency does not imply
that the represented carrier reduces the positive action; two marginal source
panels do not determine their mixed corner or their reveal order; a positive
cycle cost is not a rank without a finite source balance; and closure on every
fixed screen does not exclude escape through an unbounded sequence of screens.
A failed arrow is retained respectively as a first future-separation row, an
adjoint or contextual-action innovation, an interchange or mixed-corner
source, a recurrent circulation, an unpaid first-exit packet, or a cofinal
escape history.
\end{principle}

\begin{principle}[Numerical localizer, order cone, and absolute-pressure discipline]
\label{prin:GT-numerical-localizer-order}
For every loaded numerical sector, the admissible audit is
\[
 \boxed{
 \begin{gathered}
 \text{physical unnormalized deformation cylinder}\\
 \Downarrow\\[-0.25em]
 \text{frozen primitive word grammar and common word/action extension panel}\\
 \Downarrow\\[-0.25em]
 \text{score descent and simultaneous nuisance--retained--extension assembly}\\
 \Downarrow\\[-0.25em]
 \text{one-letter Schur innovation, polar append, and held-out flat stop}\\
 \Downarrow\\[-0.25em]
 \text{source-cyclic localizer flatness and extension floor-or-soft test}\\
 \Downarrow\\[-0.25em]
 \text{constant-localizer kernel and Feshbach jets}\\
 \Downarrow\\[-0.25em]
 \text{operational order cone and calibrated compact base}\\
 \Downarrow\\[-0.25em]
 \text{projective ray and independently transported scalar Read}\\
 \Downarrow\\[-0.25em]
 \text{absolute pressure, volume, and measure-line completion}\\
 \Downarrow\\[-0.25em]
 \text{freeze and held-out comparison}.
 \end{gathered}}
 \tag{CL.2b}
\]
The arrows are logically distinct.  Normalized laws determine the score Gram
but not an arbitrary scalar reweighting of the partition function; a zero word
innovation closes only the physically frozen grammar; separate old and new
action marginals do not determine their mixed block or kernel orientation;
word flatness reconstructs multiplication but does not make the represented
source reducing for the localizer; positivity of an abstract matrix does not
establish its occurrence in the physical deformation experiment; and a
projective ray without an independently transported scalar Read is not a
numerical prediction.  Every failed arrow is retained respectively as a
score-occurrence residual, a word Schur innovation, a flat-action defect, a
soft-word or range witness, a new action--Krylov source, an order-cone leakage,
or an absolute-measure fibre.
\end{principle}

\begin{principle}[Circulation before returning-memory promotion]
\label{prin:GT-hypocoercive-memory-order}
On a dynamically completed fixed-free quotient, the admissible memory audit is
\[
 \boxed{
 \begin{gathered}
 \text{one calibrated forward/reflected generator packet}\\
 \Downarrow\\[-0.2em]
 \text{reflection-adjoint test and }K=-S+A\\
 \Downarrow\\[-0.2em]
 \text{finite observability-word saturation}\\
 \Downarrow\\[-0.2em]
 \text{sampled-loss or Lyapunov decay, or the exact flat undamped kernel}\\
 \Downarrow\\[-0.2em]
 \text{cutoff transport and only then marginal promotion}.
 \end{gathered}}
 \tag{CL.2c}
\]
A null vector of the symmetric memory short is automatically soft only on the
reversible branch $A=0$.  On a circulating branch it may be hypocoercively
damped.  A new operation-memory coordinate is retained only when it is
independently sourced or lies in the stabilized kernel of the complete
observability hierarchy.  A failed decay certificate therefore returns an
explicit undamped sector rather than licensing an unspecified new internal or
spacetime primitive.
\end{principle}


% =============================================================================

\begin{principle}[Target-native occurrence and calibration order]
\label{prin:GT-target-native-read-order}
After the physical packet has been loaded and its signed contributions have
been assembled, the amount of additional structure required depends on the
intended output.  The admissible target-relative order is
\[
 \boxed{
 \begin{gathered}
 \text{one same-history physical writer}\
 \longrightarrow\text{one occurring Read, source germ, or certified sandwich}\\
 \longrightarrow\text{calibration on the declared multiplier/reweighting class}\\
 \longrightarrow\text{one scalar value or interval}\\
 \longrightarrow\text{query-state, context, path, or process reconstruction only when intended}.
 \end{gathered}}
 \tag{CL.2d}
\]
The arrows are not reversible.  A scalar expectation does not identify its
pointwise writer, a calibrated fixed-law Read need not remain calibrated under
conditioning or intervention, compatible branch marginals need not arise from
one common history, and a selected value does not reconstruct a transition
kernel, path law, or accepted dynamics.  Conversely, a complete state or path
packet is not charged merely to recover a scalar already carried by a physical
same-history Read.
\end{principle}


\begin{principle}[Target-relative dynamical carrier hierarchy]
\label{prin:GT-target-dynamical-hierarchy}
After physical loading, clock calibration, and assembly of the declared
writers, the minimum dynamical carrier depends on the intended output.  The
admissible hierarchy is
\[
 \boxed{
 \begin{gathered}
 \text{one scalar response}
 \subseteq\text{one positive writer-state/current packet}\\
 \subseteq\text{one finite-horizon response trace}\\
 \subseteq\text{one compact relation of admissible response traces}\\
 \subseteq\text{one occupation--flux law}
 \subseteq\text{one path law with chronology}.
 \end{gathered}}
 \tag{CL.2e}
\]
Each inclusion forgets information.  A scalar does not determine a writer
state; a writer state on a nonseparating system does not determine a complete
field law; an occupation law does not determine multitime chronology; and a
compact response relation does not determine branch probabilities.  The
stronger carrier is charged only when the corresponding support, probability,
conditioning, chronology, switching, or historical statement is part of the
target.

The analytic targets are likewise distinct:
\[
 \boxed{
 \begin{gathered}
 \text{finite-time weak response}
 \quad\neq\quad\text{static equilibrium existence}\\
 \text{all-protocol passivity}
 \quad\neq\quad\text{incremental uniqueness or attraction}\\
 \text{historical accepted occurrence}.
 \end{gathered}}
 \tag{CL.2f}
\]
None is silently used as a premise for another.  Their native certificates
are, respectively, weak residual and compactness, boundary degree or flux,
storage or a positive-real inequality, a relative contraction or determining
packet, and a same-history accepted cylinder.
\end{principle}

\begin{firewall}[No target inflation]
\label{fire:GT-no-target-inflation}
A complete response graph, occupation law, path law, equilibrium compiler,
storage function, or contraction metric may be mathematically useful.  It is
not introduced merely to reproduce a weaker finite-time weak response or one
already calibrated scalar.  Conversely, the weaker packet may not be promoted
to the stronger semantics: a mean response need not solve a nonlinear field
equation, a relation does not assign branch probabilities, a weak solution
does not prove equilibrium or attraction, and a mathematical solution does not
establish historical occurrence.
\end{firewall}

\begin{principle}[Terminal Einstein--Standard-Model quantum closure order]
\label{prin:SMQFT-terminal-order}
On an active gravity--gauge--Higgs--fermion branch, the admissible promotion
order is
\[
 \boxed{
 \begin{gathered}
 \text{common finite field shell and fully assembled time-split precision}\\
 \longrightarrow
 \text{reflected hopping factorization and determinant/Pfaffian line packet}\\
 \longrightarrow
 \text{conditional exterior kernel and zero-safe divisor hierarchy}\\
 \longrightarrow
 \text{weighted first/pair collars and split-route locality}\\
 \longrightarrow
 \text{local contact, product, null-descent, and supported OS inverse}\\
 \longrightarrow
 \text{represented current/stress and common-Hamiltonian incidence}\\
 \longrightarrow
 \text{regulated charge, Gauss-law flux, and superselection incidence}\\
 \longrightarrow
 \text{cutoff-uniform quantum Einstein--matter residual}.
 \end{gathered}}
 \tag{CL.2g}
\]
The arrows are an audit order, not automatic implications.  A finite positive
field shell need not admit the physical reflected hopping factorization; a
positive complex determinant does not orient a real Pfaffian line; a local
endpoint response need not have a local pair route; local response kernels do
not reconstruct multiplication; a Ward expectation does not establish an
operator identity; a represented current does not by itself construct a
regulated charge or its boundary flux; and cutoffwise closure does not supply a
cofinal Einstein equation.  Each failed gate is retained as, respectively, a
crossing-hopping term or negative one-particle word, a divisor or line-sign
obstruction, a pair-only locality birth, a contact/product/null or inverse-floor
witness, a Ward-source or energy-incidence residual, a divergent charge or
screening/flux sector, or a cutoff concentration and covariant Einstein
residual.
\end{principle}

\begin{firewall}[No terminal-gate substitution]
\label{fire:SMQFT-terminal-substitution}
Conditional Gaussianity, reflection positivity, quasilocality, represented
Ward identities, charge existence, superselection, and Einstein coupling are
separate statements on successively stronger carriers.  None is introduced as
a surrogate for a missing earlier occurrence, line, locality, product, domain,
or transport row, and no later positive certificate retroactively populates an
earlier physical packet.
\end{firewall}

% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
\subsection{Target-native Reads, order certificates, and common-history projections}
\label{subsec:GT-target-native-reads}
% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

The operationally complete tensor retains the full compiler-sufficient record.
The present subsection concerns a different minimization: after physical
occurrence has been established, it identifies the least additional packet
needed by a declared scalar or finite writer target.  This target-relative
compression never replaces the universal readable-record quotient of
\Cref{thm:minimal-record}; it is an economy theorem for downstream use.

\begin{definition}[Same-history target, Read, and use class]
\label{def:GT-same-history-read}
Let $(\Omega,\mu)$ be one finite occurring history law, let
$w\in L^2(\Omega,\mu;\R)$ be a physical writer fixed before its population
value is inspected, and let $Y$ be an output of a physical Read on the same
event.  Put
\[
 \kappa_Y(\omega):=\mathbb E[Y\mid\omega],
 \qquad
 d_Y:=\kappa_Y-w.
\]
A \emph{declared use class} is a closed linear subspace
$\mathcal H\subseteq L^2(\mu)$ containing the constants.  Its elements are the
physical multipliers, conditioning writers, or reweighting directions under
which the Read is intended to remain valid.  Define
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathbb C_{\mathcal H}^{\rm cal}(Y\mid w)
 :=\norm{P_{\mathcal H}d_Y}_{L^2(\mu)}^2.}
\]
The cases $\mathcal H=\Span\{\one\}$ and
$\mathcal H=L^2(\mu)$ are respectively selected-law mean calibration and
pointwise calibration.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Multiplier-relative calibration and exact information split]
\label{thm:GT-multiplier-calibration}
For the packet of \Cref{def:GT-same-history-read},
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathbb C_{\mathcal H}^{\rm cal}(Y\mid w)=0
 \iff
 \mathbb E[hY]=\mathbb E[hw]
 \quad\text{for every }h\in\mathcal H.}
\]
In particular,
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathbb EY-\mathbb Ew=\mathbb E d_Y,}
\]
so constant-multiplier calibration is necessary and sufficient for the one
selected mean.  If $h\in\mathcal H$ is nonnegative and
$\mathbb Eh>0$, then the same zero residual gives correctness under the
physical reweighted law
\[
 \dd\mu_h=\frac{h\,\dd\mu}{\mathbb Eh}.
\]
For any physical subrecord $\mathscr G$,
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathbb E|d_Y|^2
 =\mathbb E|\mathbb E[d_Y\mid\mathscr G]|^2
 +\mathbb E|d_Y-\mathbb E[d_Y\mid\mathscr G]|^2.}
\]
The first term is the calibration visible to $\mathscr G$; the second is the
fine calibration information hidden inside its fibres.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Since $Y$ is read on the same event,
$\mathbb E[hY]=\mathbb E[h\kappa_Y]$.  Orthogonal projection gives
$P_{\mathcal H}d_Y=0$ exactly when $d_Y$ is orthogonal to every
$h\in\mathcal H$, proving the first statement.  The selected-mean and
reweighting formulas are the special cases $h=1$ and
$h/(\mathbb Eh)$.  The final identity is the Pythagoras theorem for
conditional expectation in $L^2(\mu)$.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Finite calibration class and target bank]
\label{def:GT-finite-calibration-class}
Let $\mathscr D\subseteq L^2(\mu)$ be a predeclared finite-dimensional real
space containing every admissible conditional calibration bias.  Let
$h_1,\ldots,h_m$ be the acquired calibration multipliers and let
$t_1,\ldots,t_k$ be the multipliers required by the intended target use class.
In orthonormal coordinates on $\mathscr D$, define
\[
 C:\mathscr D\to\R^m,
 \qquad Cd=(\mathbb E[h_jd])_{j=1}^m,
\]
\[
 T:\mathscr D\to\R^k,
 \qquad Td=(\mathbb E[t_id])_{i=1}^k,
\]
and the positive target-calibration residual
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathbb C_{T\mid C}^{\rm cal}
 :=T(I-C^\dagger C)T^*\succeq0.}
 \tag{CAL.1}
\]
The response class $\mathscr D$ and the target bank $T$ are fixed independently
of the observed terminal Read.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Target-unisolvent calibration and minimum missing-query rank]
\label{thm:GT-target-unisolvent-calibration}
For the packet of \Cref{def:GT-finite-calibration-class}, the following are
equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2.8em]
\item $\mathbb C_{T\mid C}^{\rm cal}=0$;
\item $\Ker C\subseteq\Ker T$ on $\mathscr D$;
\item the acquired calibration rows determine every target calibration row.
\end{enumerate}
On this branch the target rows have a unique reduced decoder on $\Ran C$,
represented by
\[
 \boxed{Td=TC^\dagger(Cd).}
 \tag{CAL.2}
\]
Among linear extensions from all of $\R^m$, $TC^\dagger$ is the unique one
vanishing on $(\Ran C)^\perp$ and the unique extension of minimum
Hilbert--Schmidt norm.
On the positive branch,
\[
 \boxed{
 \rank\mathbb C_{T\mid C}^{\rm cal}
 =\rank\bigl(T|_{\Ker C}\bigr)}
 \tag{CAL.3}
\]
is the minimum number of additional independent scalar calibration queries
needed to determine the complete target bank.  Thus finite calibration is
complete only relative to an independently declared finite response class.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The Moore--Penrose operator $C^\dagger C$ is the orthogonal projection onto
$(\Ker C)^\perp$.  Hence $T(I-C^\dagger C)=0$ exactly when $T$ annihilates
$\Ker C$.  On that branch $d-C^\dagger Cd\in\Ker C$, which proves
\textup{(CAL.2)} and uniqueness on $\Ran C$.  The Moore--Penrose extension
vanishes on $(\Ran C)^\perp$; the standard orthogonal decomposition of any
other extension proves its minimum-Hilbert--Schmidt characterization.  The
residual in \textup{(CAL.1)} is the Gram of the restriction of $T$ to the
unresolved subspace $\Ker C$, proving \textup{(CAL.3)} and the
minimum-query statement.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Affine two-anchor calibration with held-out control]
\label{cor:GT-affine-two-anchor-calibration}
Suppose an independently justified device class has conditional mean response
$\kappa=\alpha+\beta w$ with $\beta\ne0$.  Two distinct exact calibration
anchors determine $\alpha$ and $\beta$, after which
\[
 \boxed{\mathbb Ew=\frac{\mathbb EY-\alpha}{\beta}.}
\]
If the affine class was selected from the same anchors rather than supplied by
a proof-carrying instrument model, at least one additional writer value remains
a held-out calibration row.
\end{corollary}

\begin{countertheorem}[Finite anchors do not establish an unrestricted response law]
\label{cth:GT-finite-calibration-anchors}
For every finite collection of target values in a nontrivial compact interval,
there are infinitely many bounded nonlinear conditional-response functions
which agree at all displayed anchors and differ elsewhere.  Therefore a finite
calibration bank determines a complete response only relative to a predeclared
finite class or an independent continuation theorem.
\end{countertheorem}

\begin{proof}
If the anchors are $x_1,\ldots,x_m$, add to any bounded interpolant a sufficiently
small nonzero multiple of $\prod_{j=1}^m(x-x_j)$.  The perturbation vanishes at
every anchor and can be kept inside the physical response interval by reducing
its coefficient.
\end{proof}


\begin{corollary}[Universal bounded-writer comparator]
\label{cor:GT-threshold-read}
Suppose $a\le w\le b$ with $a<b$ in calibrated physical units and put
\[
 q(\omega)=\frac{w(\omega)-a}{b-a}\in[0,1].
\]
Let $U\in[0,1]$ be a physical randomizer on the same event, let $\lambda$ be
the occurring joint law of $(\omega,U)$, and define the ideal threshold bit
\[
 C_w(\omega,U)=\one_{\{U\le q(\omega)\}}.
\]
Let $B$ be the actual binary output and put
$k(\omega,u)=\mathbb P(B=1\mid\omega,U=u)$.  Define
\[
 \epsilon_{\rm cmp}:=\norm{k-C_w}_{L^2(\lambda)},
 \qquad
 \epsilon_{\rm thr}:=
 \norm{\mathbb P(U\le q(\omega)\mid\omega)-q(\omega)}_{L^2(\mu)}.
\]
Then the exact error decomposition is
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathbb EB-\mathbb Eq
 =\mathbb E(k-C_w)
 +\mathbb E\!\left[\mathbb P(U\le q\mid\omega)-q\right],}
 \tag{CAL.4}
\]
and consequently
\[
 \boxed{
 \left|a+(b-a)\mathbb EB-\mathbb Ew\right|
 \le(b-a)(\epsilon_{\rm cmp}+\epsilon_{\rm thr}).}
 \tag{CAL.5}
\]
For one fixed writer, the randomizer need only have the correct conditional
CDF at the occupied values of $q$; conditional uniformity on all of $[0,1]$ is
a sufficient stronger row needed only for universal reuse.  On the exact
branch,
\[
 \boxed{\mathbb Ew=a+(b-a)\mathbb EB,}
\]
and the output bit is the coarsest retained Read required for this selected
scalar.  If $w$ is already an event indicator and $B=w$ is directly written,
no randomizer is required.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The tower property gives $\mathbb EB=\mathbb Ek$.  Add and subtract
$\mathbb EC_w$, and use
$\mathbb E[C_w\mid\omega]=\mathbb P(U\le q(\omega)\mid\omega)$ to obtain
\textup{(CAL.4)}.  Cauchy--Schwarz gives \textup{(CAL.5)}.  The remaining
statements follow because only the CDF at the realized threshold values enters
this identity, and on the exact branch the selected mean is a function only of
the output-bit frequency.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Same-event comparator occurrence residual]
\label{def:GT-comparator-occurrence}
If the physical instrument exports a comparator mark $C_{\rm phys}$ on the
same joint event, define
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathbb C_{\rm cmp}^{\rm occ}
 :=\mathbb E_\lambda|C_{\rm phys}-C_w|^2.}
 \tag{CAL.6}
\]
For binary marks this is the probability that the physical comparator
disagrees with the declared threshold word.  Its vanishing is an occurrence
statement, not a consequence of matching marginal response curves.
\end{definition}

\begin{countertheorem}[Pairwise calibration panels do not prove comparator occurrence]
\label{cth:GT-pairwise-no-comparator}
There are two laws on three binary records $(W,U,B)$ with identical one-record
and two-record marginals but opposite three-way comparator relations.  Hence
separate writer, randomizer, and output panels, even together with all three
pairwise panels, do not determine the same-event comparator word.
\end{countertheorem}

\begin{proof}
Let one law be uniform on the four even-parity triples
$W\oplus U\oplus B=0$ and the other uniform on the four odd-parity triples
$W\oplus U\oplus B=1$.  Every coordinate and every coordinate pair is uniform
in both laws, whereas the first has $B=W\oplus U$ and the second has
$B=1-(W\oplus U)$.
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[Comparator fitting is not comparator occurrence]
\label{fire:GT-comparator-fitting}
The threshold dictionary, randomizer setting, and comparator logic are fixed
before the terminal output is inspected.  If the comparator class is inferred
from a finite calibration bank, one target value or triple setting remains
held out.  A comparator word chosen after observing $B$ is a fit and supplies
no same-history occurrence certificate.
\end{firewall}

\begin{theorem}[Target sandwich and sharp order interval]
\label{thm:GT-target-sandwich}
Let $\ell,u,w$ be same-history real writers with
$\ell\le w\le u$.  Let $Y_-,Y_+$ be physical Reads for $\ell,u$ and put
\[
 \epsilon_-:=\norm{\mathbb E[Y_-\mid\omega]-\ell}_{L^1(\mu)},
 \qquad
 \epsilon_+:=\norm{\mathbb E[Y_+\mid\omega]-u}_{L^1(\mu)}.
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathbb EY_- -\epsilon_-
 \le \mathbb Ew
 \le \mathbb EY_+ +\epsilon_+.}
\]
More generally, let $\mathcal S$ be a finite unital real writer system on
$\Omega$ and let $\Phi$ be an order-positive functional on $\mathcal S$.
Among all positive extensions of $\Phi$ to $C(\Omega)$, the sharp compatible
interval for a writer $w\in C(\Omega)$ is
\[
 \boxed{
 \underline J_w
 =\sup_{f\in\mathcal S,\ f\le w}\Phi(f),
 \qquad
 \overline J_w
 =\inf_{g\in\mathcal S,\ g\ge w}\Phi(g).}
\]
Both endpoints are attained.  The target is identified exactly when the two
endpoints coincide.  For one scalar target, one direct mixed Read or one
certified sandwich may therefore replace a complete state reconstruction.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The first inequality follows from
$\mathbb EY_-\le\mathbb E\ell+\epsilon_-\le\mathbb Ew+\epsilon_-$;
the upper inequality is analogous.  The second statement is finite linear
programming duality for the cone of positive measures extending $\Phi$.
Compactness of the feasible polytope gives attainment, and equality of the
extrema is precisely extension-independence of the target.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Common-history projection packet]
\label{def:GT-common-history-projections}
Let $(\Omega_{\rm H},\Lambda_{\rm H})$ be one positive unnormalized physical
history cylinder and let
\[
 \pi_j:\Omega_{\rm H}\longrightarrow\Omega_j,
 \qquad 1\le j\le m,
\]
be deterministic physical projections.  Their branch cylinders are
$\Lambda_j=(\pi_j)_*\Lambda_{\rm H}$.  A mixed writer is physically licensed
when it is a deterministic writer on the joint projection
$(\pi_1,\ldots,\pi_m)$ or is exported by a direct same-event Read.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[One-history projection and finite common-cylinder alternative]
\label{thm:GT-one-history-projection}
Let $w_j$ be branch writers and suppose there is one common writer $w_{\rm H}$
such that
\[
 w_j\circ\pi_j=w_{\rm H}
 \quad\text{on }\supp\Lambda_{\rm H}.
\]
Then every branch gives the same normalized expectation.  More generally,
given a finite branch and overlap query synthesis $M$ and reported value vector
$d$, exactly one of the following occurs:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2.8em]
\item there exists a positive joint cylinder $\lambda\ge0$ with $M\lambda=d$;
\item there exists a finite dual writer $y$ satisfying
      \[
       \boxed{M^*y\ge0,\qquad \ip{y}{d}<0,}
      \]
      which is an explicit no-common-history witness.
\end{enumerate}
Even complete pairwise branch marginals need not identify a genuinely mixed
writer.  A direct same-event Read, an actual common cylinder, or a passing
positive-extension audit is therefore an independent physical row.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The equality of expectations is the pushforward identity.  The alternative is
Farkas' lemma applied to the finite cone $M(\R_+^{\Omega})$.  For the last
statement, the uniform even- and odd-parity laws on three binary coordinates
have identical one- and two-coordinate marginals but opposite triple-parity
expectations.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Positive cylinder and reference-law gauge]
\label{thm:GT-positive-cylinder-gauge}
Let $\Lambda\ge0$ be a nonzero finite physical cylinder,
$Z=\sum_\omega\Lambda(\omega)$, and $\mu=\Lambda/Z$.  For every full-support
reference law $\nu$, define
\[
 W_\nu(\omega)=\frac{\Lambda(\omega)}{Z\nu(\omega)}.
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathbb E_\nu W_\nu=1,
 \qquad
 \mathbb E_\mu A=\mathbb E_\nu[W_\nu A].}
\]
Replacing $\nu$ by
$\nu_h=h\nu/(\mathbb E_\nu h)$ and replacing $W_\nu$ by
$W_{\nu_h}=W_\nu(\mathbb E_\nu h)/h$ leaves the cylinder unchanged.  Thus the
reference-law/likelihood factorization is an optional sampling coordinate,
not an intrinsic part of the positive cylinder.

If a physical source deformation is
$\Lambda_\theta=\Lambda e^{\theta J}$, then
\[
 \boxed{
 \left.\frac{\dd}{\dd\theta}\log Z(\theta)\right|_{\theta=0}
 =\mathbb E_\mu J.}
\]
A normalized source law determines only the centred score; the affine source
mean is carried by the unnormalized cylinder or an equivalent direct Read.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
All identities follow by substitution.  The source formula is differentiation
of the finite sum defining $Z(\theta)$.
\end{proof}


% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
\subsubsection{Nested quotient laws, complex weights, and positive trine acquisition}
\label{subsec:GT-nested-quotient-complex}
% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

The same-history projection theorem has a target-relative refinement.  A
complete history law remains necessary when hidden chronology or factor
attribution is itself claimed.  A payoff which factors through a coarser
physical record requires only the positive or complex measure visible on that
record.

\begin{definition}[Nested target quotient packet]
\label{def:GT-nested-target-quotient}
Let $(\Omega,\nu)$ be one finite occurring positive history law.  Let
\[
 \mathfrak C:\Omega\longrightarrow\mathsf C,
 \qquad
 \mathfrak S=s\circ\mathfrak C:\Omega\longrightarrow\mathsf S
\]
be, respectively, a state--current record and a boundary or separator record.
Write $\mathscr C=\sigma(\mathfrak C)$ and
$\mathscr S=\sigma(\mathfrak S)\subseteq\mathscr C$.  For a finite positive
active measure $\varrho$ and a finite complex active measure $\zeta$, denote
their pushforwards by $\varrho_C,\varrho_S$ and $\zeta_C,\zeta_S$; denote the
reference pushforwards by $\nu_C,\nu_S$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Projection-relative likelihood tower and singular alternative]
\label{thm:GT-projected-likelihood-tower}
Suppose first that $\varrho=L\nu$ with $L\ge0$.  Then
\[
 \boxed{
 \ell_C\circ\mathfrak C=\mathbb E_\nu[L\mid\mathscr C],
 \qquad
 \ell_S\circ\mathfrak S=\mathbb E_\nu[L\mid\mathscr S],}
\]
where $\ell_C=\dd\varrho_C/\dd\nu_C$ and
$\ell_S=\dd\varrho_S/\dd\nu_S$, and
\[
 \boxed{
 \ell_S\circ\mathfrak S
 =\mathbb E_\nu[\ell_C\circ\mathfrak C\mid\mathscr S].}
\]
Consequently, for bounded $A=a(\mathfrak C)$ and $B=b(\mathfrak S)$,
\[
 \boxed{
 \int A\,\dd\varrho=\mathbb E_\nu[(\ell_C\circ\mathfrak C)A],
 \qquad
 \int B\,\dd\varrho=\mathbb E_\nu[(\ell_S\circ\mathfrak S)B].}
\]
More generally, for any physical record $T$, reconstruction of every
$T$-measurable active value requires and is equivalent only to
$\varrho_T\ll\nu_T$, whether or not a full-history density exists.  On the
failing branch the Lebesgue decomposition
\[
 \boxed{\varrho_T=\ell_T\nu_T+\varrho_T^\perp}
\]
gives the exact formula
\[
 \boxed{
 \int f(T)\,\dd\varrho
 =\mathbb E_\nu[(\ell_T\circ T)f(T)]
  +\int f\,\dd\varrho_T^\perp.}
\]
If $a\le f\le b$ on the singular support and only
$s_T=\varrho_T^\perp(\mathsf T)$ is known, the resulting interval with
endpoints
\[
 \mathbb E_\nu[(\ell_T\circ T)f(T)]+a s_T,
 \qquad
 \mathbb E_\nu[(\ell_T\circ T)f(T)]+b s_T
\]
is sharp.  Full-history domination implies current domination, which implies
separator domination; neither converse is valid in general.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The conditional-expectation formulas are the Radon--Nikodym identities for
pushforward measures, and the nested formula is the tower property.  Applying
the same identity to bounded record functions gives the payoff formulas.  The
general equivalence is the finite Radon--Nikodym theorem on the target record.
The singular formula and sharp interval are the Lebesgue decomposition and the
extremal placement of the singular mass.  Pushforward preserves absolute
continuity; a reference-null history can nevertheless share a current or
boundary value with a reference-supported history, which proves failure of
the converses.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Nested complex quotient tower and positive-shadow criterion]
\label{thm:GT-complex-quotient-tower}
Let $\zeta$ be a finite complex history measure with
$|\zeta|\ll\nu$, and put $w=\dd\zeta/\dd\nu$.  Then
\[
 \boxed{
 w_C\circ\mathfrak C=\mathbb E_\nu[w\mid\mathscr C],
 \qquad
 w_S\circ\mathfrak S=\mathbb E_\nu[w\mid\mathscr S],}
\]
with $w_S\circ\mathfrak S=\mathbb E_\nu[w_C\circ\mathfrak C\mid\mathscr S]$.
For current and boundary payoffs,
\[
 \boxed{
 \int A\,\dd\zeta=\mathbb E_\nu[(w_C\circ\mathfrak C)A],
 \qquad
 \int B\,\dd\zeta=\mathbb E_\nu[(w_S\circ\mathfrak S)B].}
\]
The total complex amplitude $Z=\zeta(\Omega)$ is unchanged by projection, while
conditional Jensen gives
\[
 \boxed{
 \norm{w_S}_{L^1(\nu_S)}
 \le\norm{w_C}_{L^1(\nu_C)}
 \le\norm{w}_{L^1(\nu)}.}
\]
If $Z\ne0$, there exists a positive probability law $\mu_T$ and one scalar
factor $Z$ reproducing every $T$-measurable complex amplitude exactly if and
only if
\[
 \boxed{w_T/Z\ge0\quad\nu_T\text{-almost everywhere}.}
\]
Thus a positive-law shadow exists precisely on the constant-phase branch.  If
$Z=0$, the unnormalized complex quotient measure remains valid but no
normalized target law exists.  If a full-history weight is unavailable, the
same conclusions at record $T$ require only $|\zeta_T|\ll\nu_T$, with the
projected singular complex measure retained explicitly.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Conditional expectation of the complex density gives the pushforward
Radon--Nikodym derivatives and the payoff identities.  Conditional Jensen
proves the $L^1$ inequalities.  If $w_T=Z\ell_T$ with $\ell_T\ge0$ and
$\mathbb E\ell_T=1$, then $\ell_T\nu_T$ is the required probability law.
Conversely, equality of all bounded payoff amplitudes forces equality of the
complex measures and hence $w_T/Z$ to be a nonnegative density.  The final
statement is the complex Lebesgue decomposition on the selected record.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Canonical phase-quenched quotient and cancellation conditioning]
\label{cor:GT-phase-quenched-quotient}
At any dominated target record $T$ with nonzero complex variation, put
\[
 \boxed{
 Z_{{\rm abs},T}=\norm{w_T}_{L^1(\nu_T)},
 \qquad
 \dd\pi_T=\frac{|w_T|}{Z_{{\rm abs},T}}\,\dd\nu_T,
 \qquad
 u_T=\frac{w_T}{|w_T|}.}
\]
Then $\pi_T$ is the canonical phase-quenched probability law,
$|u_T|=1$ $\pi_T$-almost everywhere, and
\[
 \boxed{
 \dd\zeta_T=Z_{{\rm abs},T}u_T\,\dd\pi_T,
 \qquad
 Z=Z_{{\rm abs},T}\mathbb E_{\pi_T}u_T.}
\]
The average-phase visibility and normalized-amplitude condition number are
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathfrak v_T=\frac{|Z|}{Z_{{\rm abs},T}},
 \qquad
 \kappa_{{\rm ph},T}=\mathfrak v_T^{-1}.}
\]
For a coarser record $S=s(T)$, put
$a_S=\mathbb E_{\pi_T}[u_T\mid S]$.  If $\pi_S=s_*\pi_T$, then the total
variation of the coarse complex measure is
\[
 \boxed{
 |\zeta_S|=Z_{{\rm abs},T}|a_S|\,\pi_S,}
\]
and its canonical phase-quenched law satisfies
\[
 \boxed{
 \frac{\dd\widehat\pi_S}{\dd\pi_S}
 =\frac{|a_S|}{\mathbb E_{\pi_S}|a_S|}.}
\]
Thus polar decomposition does not commute with coarse graining in general.
The exact cancellation debit is
\[
 \boxed{
 Z_{{\rm abs},T}-\norm{\zeta_S}_{\rm TV}
 =Z_{{\rm abs},T}\mathbb E_{\pi_S}(1-|a_S|),}
\]
and vanishes exactly when the phase is aligned in almost every quotient fibre.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The first identities are the polar decomposition of the finite complex
measure.  Conditional expectation under the phase-quenched law gives
$\zeta_S=Z_{{\rm abs},T}a_S\pi_S$.  Taking total variation and normalizing
proves the remaining formulas.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Dimension-minimal positive trine acquisition of a complex quotient]
\label{thm:GT-trine-complex-measure}
Let $\rho_0,\rho_1,\rho_2$ be positive finite measures on one physical current
record and put
\[
 \phi_k=\frac{2\pi k}{3},
 \qquad
 \boxed{
 \tau=\sum_{k=0}^{2}\rho_k,
 \qquad
 \zeta=\sum_{k=0}^{2}e^{-\mathrm i\phi_k}\rho_k.}
\]
The three outcomes arise from one positive functional on the target operator
system
$\mathscr S_{\rm cx}=\Span_{\R}\{I_2,\sigma_x,\sigma_y\}$ exactly when
\[
 \boxed{2|\zeta|\le\tau.}
\]
Equivalently, with $r_k=\dd\rho_k/\dd\tau$,
\[
 \boxed{\sum_{k=0}^{2}r_k^2\le\frac12
 \quad\tau\text{-almost everywhere}.}
\]
Conversely, every pair $(\tau,\zeta)$ satisfying this measure inequality has
the unique trine representation
\[
 \boxed{
 \rho_k=\frac13\left(
  \tau+e^{\mathrm i\phi_k}\zeta
       +e^{-\mathrm i\phi_k}\overline\zeta
 \right).}
\]
The selected positive carrier is the balanced matrix-valued measure
\[
 \boxed{
 \boldsymbol\Gamma_{\rm bal}(\tau,\zeta)
 =\begin{pmatrix}\tau/2&\zeta\\
                  \overline\zeta&\tau/2\end{pmatrix}\succeq0.}
\]
Since $2|\zeta|\le\tau$, the density
$g=\dd\zeta/\dd\tau$ exists.  Every positive $2\times2$ matrix-valued measure
with trace $\tau$ and off-diagonal entry $\zeta$ has, $\tau$-almost everywhere,
the form
\[
 \boxed{
 \begin{pmatrix}(1+d)/2&g\\
                 \overline g&(1-d)/2\end{pmatrix}\dd\tau,
 \qquad d^2\le1-4|g|^2,}
 \tag{TRI.1}
\]
for a real measurable imbalance $d$.  The balanced extension $d=0$ is the
unique arm-swap-invariant extension and the unique extension minimizing the
integrated Hilbert--Schmidt density norm.
Writing $\delta=\tau-2|\zeta|$, it has the exact decomposition
\[
 \boxed{
 \boldsymbol\Gamma_{\rm bal}(\tau,\zeta)
 =\begin{pmatrix}|\zeta|&\zeta\\
                  \overline\zeta&|\zeta|\end{pmatrix}
  +\frac12\delta I_2.}
\]
The first term is the unique trace-minimal positive lift of the complex
measure; $\delta$ is the remaining isotropic slack.  Three real positive
outcomes are dimension minimal for the three real target
coordinates $(\tau,\operatorname{Re}\zeta,\operatorname{Im}\zeta)$.  The
unobserved arm-population imbalance is not identified and is not required by
this target.  A common unknown positive gain cancels in the normalized
visibility $\zeta/\tau$; absolute amplitudes require one gain anchor.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Take Radon--Nikodym derivatives with respect to $\tau$.  The three-point Fourier
identities give
\[
 \sum_{k=0}^{2}r_k^2=\frac13+\frac23
 \left|\frac{\dd\zeta}{\dd\tau}\right|^2.
\]
Positivity of the target functional is equivalent to
$2|\dd\zeta/\dd\tau|\le1$, which is the measure inequality.  Fourier inversion
gives the displayed positive outcomes and uniqueness.  Every Hermitian density
with trace one and off-diagonal entry $g$ differs from the balanced density by
$(d/2)\sigma_z$; the ordinary $2\times2$ determinant criterion gives
$d^2\le1-4|g|^2$.  Its squared Hilbert--Schmidt norm is
$\frac12(1+d^2)+2|g|^2$, so $d=0$ is the unique minimizer, and arm exchange
sends $d$ to $-d$.  Finally, fewer than three scalar outcomes cannot
injectively encode a three-dimensional real operator system.
\end{proof}

\begin{countertheorem}[Trace and off-diagonal data do not reconstruct arm populations]
\label{cth:GT-trine-no-full-matrix}
If $4|g|^2<1$ on a set of positive $\tau$-measure, the trace/off-diagonal target
is compatible with infinitely many distinct positive matrix-valued measures
having different diagonal imbalances.  Thus an instrument complete only on
$\Span_{\R}\{I_2,\sigma_x,\sigma_y\}$ cannot reconstruct the individual arm
populations or a full two-arm state.
\end{countertheorem}

\begin{proof}
On any positive-measure subset on which $1-4|g|^2$ has a positive lower bound,
choose two distinct sufficiently small measurable imbalance functions $d$ in
\textup{(TRI.1)}.  They give different diagonal measures and identical trace
and off-diagonal entries.
\end{proof}

\begin{construction}[One positive trine instrument]
\label{con:GT-positive-trine-instrument}
For $\phi_k=2\pi k/3$, define
\[
 E_k=\frac13\bigl(I_2+\cos\phi_k\,\sigma_x
                         +\sin\phi_k\,\sigma_y\bigr)
     =\frac23\psi_k\psi_k^*,
 \qquad
 \psi_k=\frac1{\sqrt2}\binom{1}{e^{\mathrm i\phi_k}}.
\]
Then $E_k\succeq0$ and $\sum_kE_k=I_2$.  Applying the target functional to
this single three-outcome POVM gives precisely the positive measures
$\rho_k$ of \Cref{thm:GT-trine-complex-measure}; Fourier inversion reconstructs
$(\tau,\zeta)$.  Equivalently, the isometry
\[
 (Vv)_k=\sqrt{\frac23}\,\psi_k^*v
\]
followed by ordinary three-port detection realizes the same effects.  Physical
route blindness, common gain, and current-cell incidence remain independent
occurrence rows.
\end{construction}


\begin{corollary}[Held-out analyzer and same-instrument incidence]
\label{cor:GT-trine-heldout}
For an independently retained equatorial analyzer angle $\theta$, the trine
packet predicts the positive measure
\[
 \boxed{
 \jmath_\theta=\frac12\tau+
 \operatorname{Re}(e^{\mathrm i\theta}\zeta).}
\]
The reconstruction is physically licensed only when the three outcome measures
belong to one route-blind instrument on the same conditional current law, with
one current-cell label and one common gain.  Three algebraically compatible
tables acquired on different current populations do not establish a coherent
complex weight.
\end{corollary}

\begin{theorem}[Inherited slack, destructive interference, and positive-outcome transport]
\label{thm:GT-trine-slack-transport}
Define the target slack measure
\[
 \boxed{\delta=\tau-2|\zeta|\ge0.}
\]
For a physical quotient $s:\mathsf C\to\mathsf S$,
\[
 \boxed{
 \delta_S=s_*\delta_C
 +2\bigl(s_*|\zeta_C|-|s_*\zeta_C|\bigr).}
\]
The first term is inherited isotropic or incoherent mass.  The second is the
new positive slack created by destructive interference inside the quotient
fibres.  In particular, a partition zero
$\zeta_C(\mathsf C)=0$ may coexist with a strictly positive carrier mass
$\tau_C(\mathsf C)>0$.

For adjacent cutoffs with current map $\pi$ define
\[
 \varepsilon_{Y/X}^{\rm tri}
 =\sum_{k=0}^{2}
   \norm{\rho_{k,X}-\pi_*\rho_{k,Y}}_{\rm TV}.
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{
 \norm{\tau_X-\pi_*\tau_Y}_{\rm TV}
 \le\varepsilon_{Y/X}^{\rm tri},
 \qquad
 \norm{\zeta_X-\pi_*\zeta_Y}_{\rm TV}
 \le\varepsilon_{Y/X}^{\rm tri}.}
\]
Let
\[
 \overline\delta_Y:=\pi_*\tau_Y-2|\pi_*\zeta_Y|.
\]
Then the transported target slack satisfies the quantitative estimate
\[
 \boxed{
 \norm{\delta_X-\overline\delta_Y}_{\rm TV}
 \le3\varepsilon_{Y/X}^{\rm tri}.}
 \tag{TRI.2}
\]
Consequently every bounded transported complex payoff $A$ satisfies
\[
 \boxed{
 \left|
  \int A\,\dd\zeta_X-
  \int A\circ\pi\,\dd\zeta_Y
 \right|
 \le\norm{A}_\infty\varepsilon_{Y/X}^{\rm tri}.}
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The slack identity follows by substituting $\delta=\tau-2|\zeta|$ after
pushforward; positivity of the second term is the triangle inequality for
complex measures.  The cutoff estimates follow from the linear trine
reconstruction and the unit modulus of its Fourier coefficients.  Since the
total-variation map is one-Lipschitz,
$\norm{|\mu|-|\nu|}_{\rm TV}\le\norm{\mu-\nu}_{\rm TV}$; applying this to
$\delta=\tau-2|\zeta|$ gives \textup{(TRI.2)}.  The payoff bound is
total-variation duality.
\end{proof}



\begin{theorem}[Cofinal positive-outcome and complex-current transport]
\label{thm:GT-trine-cofinal}
Let $(X_n)_{n\ge1}$ be a cofinal cutoff sequence and transport every packet to
any fixed physical current screen.  If
\[
 \sum_{n=1}^\infty\varepsilon_{X_{n+1}/X_n}^{\rm tri}<\infty,
\]
then each positive outcome measure $\rho_{k,X_n}$ is Cauchy in total variation.
Consequently the carrier measures $\tau_{X_n}$, complex measures
$\zeta_{X_n}$, and the inherited/cancellation slack measures have unique
limits on that screen.  Every bounded transported complex payoff converges.
If the selected partition amplitudes have a uniform nonzero lower bound, the
corresponding normalized amplitudes converge as well; without that floor the
unnormalized complex measure and its zero-safe divisor remain the canonical
outputs.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The summable adjacent defects make each positive-outcome sequence Cauchy in
total variation.  The linear Fourier reconstruction transports this convergence
to $\tau$ and $\zeta$.  The map $\mu\mapsto|\mu|$ is one-Lipschitz in total
variation, so the slack decomposition is continuous.  Total-variation duality
passes every bounded payoff.  Division is continuous only on a branch with a
uniform nonzero denominator.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Selected-bias transport and hidden calibration birth]
\label{thm:GT-calibration-cutoff-transport}
Let $\pi:\Omega_Y\to\Omega_X$ be a physical old-record map, let
$\mu_X,\mu_Y$ be the old and fine laws, and let $d_X,d_Y$ be their conditional
calibration-bias writers.  Then
\[
 \boxed{
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathbb E_{\mu_Y}d_Y-\mathbb E_{\mu_X}d_X
 ={}&\mathbb E_{\mu_Y}(d_Y-d_X\circ\pi)\\
 &+\int_{\Omega_X}d_X\,\dd(\pi_*\mu_Y-\mu_X),
 \end{aligned}}
 \tag{CAL.7}
\]
and hence
\[
 \boxed{
 \left|\mathbb E_{\mu_Y}d_Y-\mathbb E_{\mu_X}d_X\right|
 \le\norm{d_Y-d_X\circ\pi}_\infty
 +\norm{d_X}_\infty\norm{\pi_*\mu_Y-\mu_X}_{\rm TV}.}
 \tag{CAL.8}
\]
Moreover, with $d_{Y\downarrow X}=\mathbb E_{\mu_Y}[d_Y\mid\pi]$,
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathbb E_{\mu_Y}|d_Y|^2
 =\mathbb E_{\mu_Y}|d_{Y\downarrow X}|^2
 +\mathbb E_{\mu_Y}|d_Y-d_{Y\downarrow X}|^2.}
 \tag{CAL.9}
\]
The last term is the fine calibration birth hidden inside old-record fibres.
It is required for writer-level or fine-control reuse, but not for transport of
one selected integrated bias.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Add and subtract $\mathbb E_{\mu_Y}(d_X\circ\pi)$ to obtain
\textup{(CAL.7)}, then apply total-variation duality.  Equation
\textup{(CAL.9)} is conditional-expectation Pythagoras in $L^2(\mu_Y)$.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Cofinal selected scalar without device convergence]
\label{cor:GT-calibrated-scalar-cofinal}
Let $w_n$ be selected writers and $Y_n$ their physical Reads.  If
\[
 |\mathbb EY_n-\mathbb Ew_n|\le\epsilon_n,
 \qquad \epsilon_n\to0,
\]
and $(\mathbb EY_n)$ is Cauchy, then
\[
 \boxed{\mathbb Ew_n\longrightarrow\lim_n\mathbb EY_n.}
\]
No pointwise calibration-bias function, randomizer law, comparator device, or
complete instrument is required to converge.  Those stronger transports remain
necessary when the device rather than the selected scalar is the target.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The target mean differs from the Read mean by at most $\epsilon_n$; the result
is the triangle inequality and completeness of $\R$.
\end{proof}
\begin{theorem}[Target-native cutoff and cofinal interval transport]
\label{thm:GT-target-interval-transport}
Suppose old and fine cutoffs have certified scalar intervals
\[
 L_X\le J_X\le U_X,
 \qquad
 L_Y\le J_Y\le U_Y.
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{
 L_Y-U_X\le J_Y-J_X\le U_Y-L_X,}
\]
and hence
\[
 \boxed{
 |J_Y-J_X|
 \le\max\{U_Y-L_X,\ U_X-L_Y\}.}
\]
If $U_n-L_n\to0$ and one endpoint sequence is Cauchy, then the selected
scalars converge to the common endpoint limit.  This conclusion requires no
convergence of the complete instrument, query state, branch coupling, or path
law.  Those stronger transports remain necessary when the writer, device, or
process itself is the target.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Subtract the two interval inclusions.  The cofinal assertion follows by the
squeeze theorem.
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[Target-native closure is not process reconstruction]
\label{fire:GT-target-native-scope}
The theorems of this subsection operate only after physical occurrence and
same-history incidence have been established.  They do not create a writer,
randomizer, comparator, reference law, common cylinder, or source deformation.
They also do not turn a selected scalar or quotient amplitude into a local
field, transition kernel, path law, accepted process, full-history factor
model, determinant-line section, or conjecture-level estimate.  Projection-
relative domination closes only the declared quotient target; hidden support
and chronology re-enter when they are named.  Likewise a trine packet proves
one trace/off-diagonal complex functional, not a microscopic interferometer or
the missing arm-population coordinate.  Whenever one of those stronger
objects is claimed, its native record, product, calibration, chronology,
phase, and cutoff rows remain mandatory.
\end{firewall}


% =============================================================================
\section{Austere operational entrance and relative primitive-basis closure}
\label{sec:upstream-primitive-closure}
% =============================================================================

The finite reconstruction developed below may be presented through a generated
ledger and its deterministic updates.  That presentation is convenient for
computation, but it is not the weakest logical entrance.  A history-dependent
event law already contains a canonical predictive relation state before any
ledger, hidden state space, or persistent port is named.  This section isolates
that state, separates it from its same-cut physical readability, and records the
precise semantic data which cannot be removed by the same quotient argument.

\begin{definition}[Fixed operational audit category]
\label{def:GT-upstream-audit-category}
Fix a finite typed potential event grammar $\mathfrak G$: its objects are cut
types, its primitive letters have specified source and target types, and its
admissible finite words are closed under prefixes and typed concatenation.  An
\emph{upstream audit model} is a packet
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathfrak M=[\mathfrak G;\mathfrak O,\mathbb P^+,\Theta,\Lambda].}
 \tag{UP.1}
\]
Here:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(U\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item $\mathfrak O$ is the actual occurrence interface: the preparations,
      outcomes, marks, boundary ports, and same-cut Reads which are physically
      written rather than merely syntactically available;
\item $\mathbb P^+$ is the complete normalized contextual predictive law on
      every admitted finite word, including the declared ancillary matrix
      contexts whenever complete positivity is part of the target;
\item $\Theta$ is the protected orientation section, including every sign,
      chirality, time orientation, or alternating-volume choice which is used
      by a downstream compiler;
\item $\Lambda$ is the absolute physical calibration packet, including clock,
      length, volume, action, pressure, and unnormalized measure anchors and
      their physically occurring incidence relations.
\end{enumerate}
Morphisms preserve the typed grammar, actual incidence, the complete
contextual law, the protected orientation, and the calibrated physical
quantities.  The minimality statements below are relative to this fixed
language and morphism class.
\end{definition}

For a reachable history $h$ ending at type $x$, let $\mathsf F_x$ denote the
admissible finite future words beginning at $x$, augmented by every declared
bounded future query used by the target compiler.

\begin{definition}[History future equivalence]
\label{def:GT-history-future-equivalence}
For reachable histories $h,h'$ of the same terminal type, write $h\sim h'$ when
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathbb P^+(f\mid h)=\mathbb P^+(f\mid h')
 \quad\text{for every }f\in\mathsf F_x.}
 \tag{UP.2}
\]
Histories of different terminal type are never identified.  The quotient is
\[
 \boxed{Z_x^{\min}:=\mathsf H_x/\!\sim.}
 \tag{UP.3}
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Derived predictive relation carrier]
\label{thm:GT-derived-predictive-carrier}
History future equivalence is a typed right congruence.  Every occurring letter
$a:x\to y$ therefore induces a well-defined partial update and branch law
\[
 \boxed{
 T_a([h])=[ha],\qquad \kappa_a([h])=\mathbb P^+(a\mid h).}
 \tag{UP.4}
\]
For every admissible word $w=a_1\cdots a_k$ and $z_0=[h]$,
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathbb P^+(w\mid h)
 =\prod_{j=1}^{k}\kappa_{a_j}(z_{j-1}),
 \qquad z_j=T_{a_j}z_{j-1}.}
 \tag{UP.5}
\]
Moreover, $Z^{\min}$ is the unique coarsest reachable deterministic predictive
realization: if a realization $S$ has history state $s(h)$, deterministic
updates $u_a$, and branch functions $r_a$, then there is a unique surjection
\[
 \boxed{\pi:S\twoheadrightarrow Z^{\min}}
 \tag{UP.6}
\]
intertwining every update and branch probability.  Along an occurring event
sequence $A_1,A_2,\ldots$, the variables
\[
 Z_n=[A_1\cdots A_n]
\]
satisfy
\[
 \boxed{Z_{n+1}=T_{A_{n+1}}Z_n}
 \tag{UP.7}
\]
almost surely.  Predictive persistence is therefore derived from composition;
it is not an independent state axiom.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
If $h\sim h'$ and $a$ is an admissible one-letter future, then
$\mathbb P^+(a\mid h)=\mathbb P^+(a\mid h')$.  On the positive branch, for any
continuation $v$ the chain rule gives
\[
 \mathbb P^+(v\mid ha)
 =\frac{\mathbb P^+(av\mid h)}{\mathbb P^+(a\mid h)}
 =\frac{\mathbb P^+(av\mid h')}{\mathbb P^+(a\mid h')}
 =\mathbb P^+(v\mid h'a),
\]
so $ha\sim h'a$.  This proves the right-congruence property and
well-definedness of \textup{(UP.4)}.  Equation \textup{(UP.5)} is the
conditional chain rule on the quotient.

For universality, suppose $s(h)=s(h')$.  Induction on future-word length,
using the deterministic successor relation and equality of the one-letter
branch functions, shows that every future probability agrees.  Hence
$h\sim h'$, so $\pi(s(h))=[h]$ is well defined.  Reachability gives uniqueness
and surjectivity; the intertwining identities follow from the definitions.
Finally,
$Z_{n+1}=[A_1\cdots A_nA_{n+1}]=T_{A_{n+1}}Z_n$, proving
\textup{(UP.7)}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Generated ledgers and predictive state spaces are compiled presentations]
\label{cor:GT-ledger-not-foundational}
A generated ledger with deterministic updates, or any other supplied
persistent predictive state space, is a realization $S$ of
\Cref{thm:GT-derived-predictive-carrier} whenever its branch-conditioned
futures factor through its current value.  It therefore has a unique
surjection onto $Z^{\min}$.  Every coordinate erased by this surjection is
representational for the declared future family.  Conversely, a coordinate
which survives has a finite first distinguishing future whenever the candidate
realization is finite.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The first statement is the universal property \textup{(UP.6)}.  On a finite
candidate state set, iteratively refine the partition by immediate branch and
Read values and by the blocks occupied by every one-step successor.  Each
strict round increases the number of blocks, so stabilization occurs after at
most $|S|-1$ strict rounds.  The stable partition is future equivalence, and a
pair first separated at round $r$ is distinguished by a future of depth at
most $r+1\le |S|$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Transfer of future-operational compilers]
\label{thm:GT-upstream-compiler-transfer}
Let $\mathcal D$ be any downstream compiler whose value is unchanged whenever
two candidate states have the same complete declared future signature,
including every mark, reward, boundary, action, and terminal Read used by that
compiler.  Then there is a unique map $\overline{\mathcal D}$ such that
\[
 \boxed{\mathcal D=\overline{\mathcal D}\circ\pi.}
 \tag{UP.8}
\]
Thus passage from any supplied predictive primitive to $Z^{\min}$ preserves
every quotient-invariant downstream output exactly.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The hypothesis says precisely that $\mathcal D$ is constant on every fibre of
$\pi$.  Define $\overline{\mathcal D}(z)$ using any representative in
$\pi^{-1}(z)$.  This is well defined and unique because $\pi$ is surjective.
\end{proof}

\begin{countertheorem}[Future sufficiency does not create a same-cut Read]
\label{cth:GT-future-no-immediate-read}
There are finite processes with two distinct classes in $Z^{\min}$ but with a
declared same-cut Read interface containing only the constant Read.  Therefore
the canonical predictive carrier need not be an instantaneously written
classical port.
\end{countertheorem}

\begin{proof}
Take two persistent predictive classes $0,1$.  In class $0$, let the next
letter be $a$ with probability $3/4$ and $b$ with probability $1/4$; reverse
these probabilities in class $1$, and let both letters preserve the class.
The one-letter future $a$ separates the classes.  If the only same-cut Read is
the constant function, no declared physical output distinguishes them at the
cut.  The future law cannot manufacture a Read absent from $\mathfrak O$.
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[Derived carrier versus readable relational enrichment]
\label{fire:GT-derived-versus-readable-port}
The quotient $Z^{\min}$ is a canonical future-sufficient state.  It becomes a
point-readable relation port only when the actual occurrence interface contains
a future-compatible and future-separating cut-Read bank.  The scheduler path,
protected orientation, absolute calibration, determining-field marks, rewards,
and common-action rows are not created merely by naming the predictive class.
