The relational completion of \Cref{sec:relational-completion} is therefore a
readable and physically enriched realization of the derived carrier, not a
second postulated predictive ontology.
\end{firewall}

\begin{definition}[Relative upstream semantic floor]
\label{def:GT-relative-upstream-floor}
In the audit category of \Cref{def:GT-upstream-audit-category}, the
\emph{relative upstream semantic floor} is
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathfrak B_{\rm up}
 =\bigl(\mathfrak G;\mathfrak O,\mathbb P^+,\Theta,\Lambda\bigr),}
 \tag{UP.9}
\]
where $\mathfrak G$ is language forming and the four displayed semantic rows
are evaluated before any quotient-derived predictor, comb, CP realization,
history algebra, reset law, metric, or domain loading is introduced.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Relative primitive-basis closure and cofinal row independence]
\label{thm:GT-relative-primitive-closure}
Within the fixed finite typed audit category, the floor
$\mathfrak B_{\rm up}$ has the following properties.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(B\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item It is sufficient for the derived predictive carrier, every finite
      quotient-invariant compiler, finite comb tomography after ancillary
      positivity is included in $\mathbb P^+$, and the reset/recurrence audit of
      \Cref{thm:GT-renewal-reset-recurrence}.
\item Each of $\mathfrak O,\mathbb P^+,\Theta,\Lambda$ is row irredundant:
      after forgetting that row, there are two finite anchored models with
      identical remaining rows and inequivalent full models.
\item The four separating pairs remain separating after tensoring both models
      with any common conservative spectator refinement and after cofinal
      reindexing.  No inductive limit, compact screen, Mosco limit, or continuum
      passage reconstructs the forgotten row functorially.
\item Reset, recurrence, excursion and waiting laws, predictive persistence,
      the relation carrier, positive process structure, and the structural
      Grand Tensor are derived objects or decidable branch properties rather
      than additional semantic basis rows.
\end{enumerate}
Consequently \textup{(UP.9)} is a minimal known sufficient and row-irredundant
basis relative to the declared operational language and morphism class.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Sufficiency of the predictive quotient and compiler transfer is
\Cref{thm:GT-derived-predictive-carrier,thm:GT-upstream-compiler-transfer}.
Ancilla-complete contextual positivity reconstructs the positive causal comb
by \Cref{thm:comb-tomography}; support reduction and the remaining finite
structural construction are the theorems of Part~I.

For row irredundancy, four elementary separating mechanisms suffice.  Two
Bernoulli laws with different parameters separate $\mathbb P^+$ while keeping
the grammar, occurrence labels, orientation, and calibration fixed.  A
potential branch which is or is not exported by an actual occurrence bit
separates $\mathfrak O$ after that bit is forgotten.  On one fixed positive
oriented plane, the alternating forms $\Theta$ and $-\Theta$ have identical
positive Gram data and separate orientation.  Finally, one projective event law
with physical duration $T=cS$ at two distinct positive values of $c$ separates
absolute calibration while preserving every uncalibrated probability.  These
pairs prove that no row is a functorial function of the other three.

Tensor both members of any pair with the same spectator process and retain a
physical spectator discard.  An isomorphism on a cofinal tail would descend,
after discard, to an isomorphism of the original finite pair, a contradiction.
The same argument is invariant under cofinal pullback.  The final item follows
from the quotient and finite-renewal theorems together with the structural
reconstruction of Part~I.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Orientation bundling and complete calibration residual]
\label{thm:GT-orientation-calibration-floor}
The surviving orientation and calibration rows admit exact finite
classifications.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(O\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item A positive inner-product packet cannot select between the two sections of
      a nontrivial orientation torsor.  Orientation may be absorbed into an
      enriched occurrence packet exactly when an actual Read $R_\Theta$ and a
      fixed decoder recover the chosen section.  This is an equivalence of
      presentations, not an information reduction.
\item Write all positive scales and additive origins in log-affine coordinates
      $x\in\R^N$.  If the physically established incidence relations are
      $Lx=b$, then every nonempty calibration fibre is
      \[
       \boxed{x_0+\mathcal K_L,\qquad \mathcal K_L:=\Ker L,}
       \tag{UP.10}
      \]
      of dimension $N-\rank L$.  Exactly that many independent scalar anchors
      are necessary and sufficient.
\item If $J:\R^d\to\R^N$ encodes conventional changes of base units with
      $LJ=0$, the intrinsic physical residual is
      \[
       \boxed{
       \mathcal K_L^{\rm phys}
       =\mathcal K_L/\operatorname{Im}J.}
       \tag{UP.11}
      \]
      When $J$ is injective its dimension is
      $N-\rank L-\rank J$.
\item Every cutoff calibration cocycle satisfies
      \[
       \boxed{\gamma_{m/n}=x_m-x_n}
       \tag{UP.12}
      \]
      and determines the object calibrations only up to one global element of
      $\mathcal K_L$.  A cofinal anchor bank closes calibration exactly when it
      separates $\mathcal K_L^{\rm phys}$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
An orientation-reversing symmetry preserves every positive inner product and
interchanges the two sections, so no natural construction from positive data
can choose one.  If $R_\Theta$ and its decoder occur, the decoded section and
the enriched occurrence packet determine one another; forgetting the decoder
restores the same torsor.

If $Lx=Lx_0=b$, then $x-x_0\in\Ker L$, and the converse is immediate.  Rank--
nullity gives the dimension.  A basis of $\mathcal K_L$ and its dual functionals
provide a sufficient anchor bank; fewer anchors have a nonzero common kernel
and are insufficient.  Quotienting the subgroup of unit conventions gives
\textup{(UP.11)}.  Finally, on a chain define $x_n=\gamma_{n/0}$; the cocycle
identity yields \textup{(UP.12)}.  Two choices with the same cocycle differ by
one constant translation, which lies in $\mathcal K_L$ when incidence is
preserved.  The quotient anchor statement follows.
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[Relative minimality and exact reopening criterion]
\label{fire:GT-upstream-reopening}
The closure theorem is not a claim of absolute metaphysical minimality across
all possible foundational languages.  It closes the declared finite typed
operational-predictive category.  The upstream audit is reopened only by one of
the following: a required target outside the sufficiency image after all
native rows are populated; a new physical principle which canonically
identifies one of the separating pairs; a change of audit language or morphism
category; or an error in the reduction or independence proofs.  A missing
Standard-Model writer, failed continuum estimate, unpaid source, unproved mass
gap, or unfinished OS/Lorentzian reconstruction does not by itself reopen the
primitive basis.
\end{firewall}

\section{Conservative relational completion and the revised Grand-Tensor convention}
\label{sec:relational-completion}
% =============================================================================

The complete contextual event law already determines the persistent
predictive carrier of \Cref{thm:GT-derived-predictive-carrier}.  The finite
structural object reconstructed from the marginal Store cylinder does not,
however, supply a same-cut Read of that carrier or the richer physical data
needed by the spacetime and common-action compilers.  In particular,
conservative extensions can preserve every old renewal probability while
differing in their global endpoint atlas, terminal-to-next-source carry,
scheduler path, protected orientation, calibration, or accepted field/action
law.  These countermodels do not invalidate either predictive or structural
minimality.  They show that a physically complete spacetime-capable object must
retain a readable enrichment of the derived carrier.  The following definition
adopts that minimal conservative enrichment as part of the object called the
Renewal Grand Tensor.

\begin{definition}[Compiler-minimal persistent relation packet]
\label{def:relational-port-monograph}
Fix a cutoff $X$ and let $\mathscr O_X$ be the old resolved Store outcome
alphabet.  A raw relational event is a point-readable tuple
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathfrak p_{X,n}
 =\bigl(Z_{X,n},\Gamma_{X,n},O_{X,n},\Xi_{X,n},Z_{X,n+1}\bigr).}
 \tag{RC.1}
\]
Its entries have the following operational meanings.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(R\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item $Z_{X,n}$ is the same-cut physical realization of the minimal
      predictive history class for the augmented event law.  Its predictive
      persistence is derived by \Cref{thm:GT-derived-predictive-carrier}; the
      additional premise is occurrence of a future-compatible and
      future-separating Read.  The class may carry the future-readable spatial
      and field/action information of that augmented law, but no product
      decomposition is assumed.
\item $O_{X,n}\in\mathscr O_X$ is the old Store outcome.  On an accepted
      branch its locked oriented $A_3$ root is reused; no second direction
      alphabet is introduced.
\item $\Gamma_{X,n}$ is the scheduler-separated fast root path between two
      slow cuts, including the directed root winners, waiting times,
      occupation statistics, and the speed or volume calibration needed by a
      geometric loading.
\item $\Xi_{X,n}$ contains the remaining same-history marks used by the
      declared compilers: initial and terminal determining-field Reads,
      update and reverse labels, nuisance and provenance, protected rewards,
      reference and observed slow rows, direct target Reads, randomizer and
      comparator marks when physically used, their calibration ledgers, and any
      physical boundary record.
\item $Z_{X,n+1}$ is the target relational state and is the source state of the
      next event.
\end{enumerate}
Two raw states are identified exactly when every admitted continuation,
compiler query, future mark cylinder, and terminal Read has the same
conditional law from the two states.  The resulting finite right-congruence
quotient is denoted
\[
 \boxed{\mathfrak P_X^{\rm rel,min}.}
 \tag{RC.2}
\]
It is called the compiler-minimal persistent relation packet.  Coordinates
which are deterministic functions of this quotient, including a derived
metric, coframe, connection, curvature, action comparator, or modulation
variable, are not independent primitive coordinates.
\end{definition}

Let $\{\Phi_{o,*}:o\in\mathscr O_X\}$ be the old Schr\"odinger-picture Store
instrument.  For a finite relational kernel
\[
 K_{X,o}(\gamma,\xi,z'\mid z)\ge0,
 \qquad
 \sum_{\gamma,\xi,z'}K_{X,o}(\gamma,\xi,z'\mid z)=1,
\]
define the refined branches on block states $\rho=(\rho_z)_z$ by
\[
 \boxed{
 [\widetilde\Phi_{o,\gamma,\xi,*}(\rho)]_{z'}
 :=\sum_zK_{X,o}(\gamma,\xi,z'\mid z)\Phi_{o,*}(\rho_z).}
 \tag{RC.3}
\]

\begin{definition}[Repaired process and relational Renewal Grand Tensor]
\label{def:relational-grand-tensor}
The conservative relational completion of the old process is denoted
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathsf P_X^{\rm rel}
 :=\mathsf P_X^{\rm old}\ltimes\mathfrak P_X^{\rm rel,min}.}
 \tag{RC.4}
\]
The symbol $\ltimes$ means the same-history conditional extension
\textup{(RC.3)}; it does not assert probabilistic independence or a tensor
factorization of the state space.

Apply the record minimization, Hankel reconstruction, support-minimal CP
completion, contextual history quotient, and regular-trace word-Gram
construction of Part~I to $\mathsf P_X^{\rm rel}$.  The resulting object is
\[
 \boxed{
 \boldsymbol{\mathbb T}_{\Grand,X}^{\rm rel}
 :=\left(
   \mathcal A_{X,{\rm rel}}^{\rm hist},
   \{\mathbb K_{X,r}^{\rm rel}\}_{r\ge0},
   \mathfrak R_{X,{\rm rel}}^{\min}
 \right).}
 \tag{RC.5}
\]
For a cutoff family, the definition additionally retains the physically
measured old--detail polarization tables of
\Cref{def:relational-refinement-profile}.  The structural tensor reconstructed
from $\mathsf P_X^{\rm old}$ alone is denoted
$\boldsymbol{\mathbb T}_{\Grand,X}^{\rm old}$ and is the canonical forgetful
shadow of \textup{(RC.5)}.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Conservativity, future minimality, and universality]
\label{thm:relational-completion}
The relational completion has the following exact properties.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(C\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item The branches \textup{(RC.3)} are completely positive and form a
      normalized refinement of the old instrument.
\item For the forgetful map
      $\mathsf F_X(\rho)=\sum_z\rho_z$,
      \[
       \boxed{
       \mathsf F_X\!\left(
         \sum_{\gamma,\xi}\widetilde\Phi_{o,\gamma,\xi,*}(\rho)
       \right)
       =\Phi_{o,*}(\mathsf F_X\rho).}
       \tag{RC.6}
      \]
      Hence forgetting the relation packet recovers every old finite Store
      cylinder, branch probability, payload map, completion law, accepted
      count, and old duration marginal exactly.
\item Future-signature partition refinement terminates at
      $\mathfrak P_X^{\rm rel,min}$, and every other finite persistent record
      sufficient for the same compiler family has a unique surjection onto it.
      Unread refinements therefore add neither classical nor source dimension.
\item The forgetful map induces a canonical process morphism
      \[
       \boxed{
       \boldsymbol{\mathbb T}_{\Grand,X}^{\rm rel}
       \longrightarrow
       \boldsymbol{\mathbb T}_{\Grand,X}^{\rm old}}
       \tag{RC.7}
      \]
      whose image contains the complete old history algebra and old word-Gram
      hierarchy.  The old tensor is consequently a quotient or absorbing
      corner of the revised tensor, not a competing definition.
\item If all coordinates in \textup{(RC.1)} are jointly point readable, one
      downstream thinning family reconstructs every within-sector and mixed
      source block as a covariance matrix.  Orthogonal projection onto the
      nuisance sigma-algebra is exactly simultaneous Anderson--Trapp shorting.
      In particular, edge routers, efficient kinetic tensors, reward
      innovations, and accepted/action cross blocks are outputs of one joint
      event law rather than independent relative orientations.
\end{enumerate}
The construction is unique up to the source-fixing, record-preserving unitary
already present in the support-minimal Grand-Tensor theorem.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Complete positivity of \textup{(RC.3)} follows because each target block is a
nonnegative scalar combination of old CP maps.  Summing the kernel over
$(\gamma,\xi,z')$ gives one, which proves \textup{(RC.6)}.  Induction on word
length gives preservation of every old cylinder.

The future-equivalence relation is a typed right congruence: prefixing one
primitive branch to two identical future signatures leaves the signatures
identical.  Finite partition refinement terminates because every strict round
increases the number of classes.  Its stable quotient has the stated universal
property by the same fibre argument as \Cref{thm:minimal-record}.  Applying the
finite comb, history-algebra, and contextual-quotient constructions to the
refined process gives \textup{(RC.7)} by functoriality of operational coarse
graining and \Cref{thm:cutoff-compatibility}.

For the last assertion, append a readable keep bit with exponential acceptance
weight in any finite family of point Reads.  Differentiation at the neutral
setting gives their centred score vectors; the complete Fisher block is their
joint covariance.  Conditional expectation onto nuisance Reads is the
orthogonal projection in $L^2$ and therefore gives exactly the Moore--Penrose
Schur short.  Source-minimal uniqueness is then
\Cref{thm:joint-source-universality}.
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[Meaning of the repaired definition]
\label{fire:relational-semidir}
The predictive class inside the relational completion is derived from complete
future equivalence; it is not a second hidden state postulate.  Its same-cut
Read, the scheduler-separated path, protected orientation, absolute
calibration, and field/action marks are explicit conservative enrichments and
are not inferred from the old marginal Store table.  Their occurrence does not
make historical terminal reuse automatic.  Conversely, once this readable
enrichment is adopted, historical reconstruction of its marks from the old
Store is a reuse question rather than a premise of spacetime or coupled-action
existence.
\end{firewall}

\begin{assessment}[Notation convention for the remainder of the manuscript]
\label{assess:relational-notation}
The structural construction stated in \Cref{def:grand-tensor} is retained
without a global notational rewrite.  It should now be read as
$\boldsymbol{\mathbb T}_{\Grand,X}^{\rm old}$ whenever only the original Store
cylinder is present.  From this section onward, the unqualified phrase
\emph{Renewal Grand Tensor} denotes the relationally completed object
$\boldsymbol{\mathbb T}_{\Grand,X}^{\rm rel}$ of \textup{(RC.5)}, unless the
text explicitly says ``old'', ``structural shadow'', or names a further domain
loading.  All earlier structural theorems remain valid because the old tensor
is recovered by \textup{(RC.7)}.  Thus the revised definition is
\[
 \boxed{
 \begin{aligned}
 \text{Renewal Grand Tensor}
 ={}&\mathsf P^{\rm old}
 +\text{ a same-cut realization of its derived predictive carrier}\
 &+\text{ the compiler-minimal scheduler/orientation/field/action marks},
 \end{aligned}}
 \tag{RC.8}
\]
where both plus signs are implemented by the conservative same-history
extension \textup{(RC.3)} rather than by direct sums.  The first added term is
a readable realization of a derived quotient; the second records genuinely
additional physical occurrence and calibration data.
\end{assessment}

% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
\subsection{Scheduler separation and the geometric output of the relation port}
\label{subsec:relational-scheduler}
% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

The locked Store already contains the integral $A_3$ root alphabet, and the
complete augmented future law determines its minimal predictive state.  What
was missing from the old structural shadow was a same-cut physical realization
of that state, an endpoint atlas on which the roots act, and a clock fast enough
to produce a nondegenerate kinetic bracket.  Predictive persistence, alphabet
identification, port occurrence, and scheduler identification are therefore
separate claims.

\begin{theorem}[Old root alphabet, independent fast scheduler, and complete ADM frame]
\label{thm:relational-scheduler-ADM}
Let $r_1,\ldots,r_6$ be the six unoriented $A_3$ root classes in an anchored
integral basis,
\[
 r_1=e_1,\quad r_2=e_2,\quad r_3=e_3,\quad
 r_4=e_2-e_1,\quad r_5=e_3-e_1,\quad r_6=e_3-e_2.
 \tag{RC.9}
\]
For directed rates $k_a^\pm$ and mesh $h$, define
\[
 \mathcal B_h
 =h^2\sum_{a=1}^{6}(k_a^++k_a^-)r_ar_a^{\mathsf T},
 \qquad
 \beta_h
 =h\sum_{a=1}^{6}(k_a^+-k_a^-)r_a.
 \tag{RC.10}
\]
Then:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(A\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item the six matrices $r_ar_a^{\mathsf T}$ form a basis of
      $\operatorname{Sym}_3$;
\item the six directed-rate differences have rank three onto $\beta_h$, and
      their three-dimensional kernel is the tetrahedral circulation space;
\item observing the winning root together with its waiting time gives a
      faithful score frame for all directed rates; discarding the waiting time
      loses the common rate scale;
\item with positive speed density $\varrho_h$, the analytic formulas
      \[
       \boxed{
       g_h=\varrho_h^{2/3}(\det\mathcal B_h)^{1/3}\mathcal B_h^{-1},
       \qquad
       N_h=\varrho_h^{1/3}(\det\mathcal B_h)^{1/6}}
       \tag{RC.11}
      \]
      reconstruct the six spatial metric components and lapse, while
      $\beta_h$ gives the three shift components;
\item an $h$-mesh bracket satisfying $\mathcal B_h\succeq cI_3$ requires total
      fast rate $\sum_a(k_a^++k_a^-)\ge c' h^{-2}$.  A clock of intensity
      $O(h^{-1})$, including the old renewal or accepted clock under its natural
      scaling, produces a bracket $O(h)$ and collapses.
\end{enumerate}
Thus the old root labels may be reused exactly, but the geometric scheduler
must be the scheduler-separated fast path $\Gamma_{X,n}$ of
\Cref{def:relational-port-monograph}.  No metric, coframe, connection, or
Einstein tensor is primitive data.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The three coordinate rank-one matrices give the diagonal entries of a
symmetric matrix.  Subtracting them from
$(e_j-e_i)(e_j-e_i)^{\mathsf T}$ gives the three independent off-diagonal
entries, proving item~\textup{(A1)}.  The roots span $\R^3$, so the difference
map in \textup{(RC.10)} has rank three; its kernel has dimension three and is
the cycle-current space of the tetrahedral edge graph.

For an exponential race with rates $k_b$, the log-rate score of one winner and
waiting time is
$s_b=\mathbf1_{\{A=b\}}-k_bT$.  Direct integration gives
$\mathbb E[s_bs_c]=\delta_{bc}k_b/(\sum_jk_j)$, which is faithful.  Winner
probabilities alone have covariance $\operatorname{diag}(p)-pp^{\mathsf T}$
and lose the common scale.  Formula \textup{(RC.11)} is inverted by
$\varrho_h=\sqrt{\det g_h}$ and
$\mathcal B_h=N_h^2g_h^{-1}$, so it is an analytic bijection on the positive
cone.

Finally, if $\|r_a\|\le R$, then
$\operatorname{tr}\mathcal B_h\le
 R^2h^2\sum_a(k_a^++k_a^-)$.  The lower bound
$\mathcal B_h\succeq cI_3$ makes the left side at least $3c$, proving the
$h^{-2}$ scheduler bound.  An $O(h^{-1})$ clock therefore gives a vanishing
bracket.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Bounded local relation audit]
\label{cor:relational-depth-four}
On the free additive $A_3$ accumulator, every equality of two root words with
the same endpoint is generated by translated copies of three relation types:
\[
 \boxed{
 \gamma(-\gamma),\qquad
 (e_j-e_i)e_i(-e_j),\qquad
 e_ie_j(-e_i)(-e_j).}
 \tag{RC.12}
\]
Their lengths are respectively two, three, and four.  Consequently every local
router, action-cochain, and flatness comparison is decided by same-history
cylinders of depth at most four.  Compact topology contributes only the
additional finite deck-period bank and cannot be inferred from bounded local
cylinders.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The inverse relations remove adjacent inverse letters.  The triangle relations
express every nonbasis $A_3$ root as a difference of two basis roots.  The
commutator squares make the three basis translations commute.  The resulting
presentation is the free abelian group $\Z^3$, so two words have the same
endpoint exactly when their quotient lies in the normal closure of the
relations in \textup{(RC.12)}.  A compact quotient adds precisely its period
subgroup.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Explicit conservative flat-vacuum branch]
\label{cor:relational-flat-vacuum}
Realize $\Lambda_{A_3}$ in its standard Euclidean three-dimensional space
$W_0$, let $V_d=\Lambda_{A_3}/d\Lambda_{A_3}$ and $h=d^{-1}$, and give each of
the twelve oriented roots rate $1/(8h^2)$ and every vertex mass $h^3$.  Take one point in
the field fibre, the identity router, zero nonvacuum cost, and the identity slow
row.  Then:
\[
 \boxed{\mathcal B_h=I_3,\qquad\varrho_h=1,
        \qquad g_h=I_3,\quad N_h=1,\quad\beta_h=0,}
 \tag{RC.13}
\]
every undirected root-edge conductance is $h/8$, the periodic cut margin is
uniformly positive, all depth-four router and action residuals vanish, and
forgetting the port recovers the old Store cylinder exactly.  Along any cofinal
scalar-period sequence, the spatial generators converge to
$\tfrac12\Delta_{\mathbb T^3}$ and the Lorentzian limit is
\[
 \boxed{(\R\times\mathbb T^3,-\dd t^2+\dd x_1^2+\dd x_2^2+\dd x_3^2),}
 \tag{RC.14}
\]
which satisfies the vacuum Einstein equation.  Thus the positive spacetime
branch of the repaired primitive is nonempty without inserting a metric or an
Einstein equation.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
For the chosen normalization the twelve-root identity is
$\sum_{\alpha\in\Phi_{A_3}}\alpha\alpha^{\mathsf T}=8I_3$; substituting the
rates gives \textup{(RC.13)}.  Reversal symmetry gives zero shift, and
\textup{(RC.11)} gives the ADM packet.  Multiplying the rate by the vertex mass
gives conductance $h/8$; the periodic three-dimensional cut estimate is then
uniform.  The constant coframe and identity router have zero torsion and
curvature, and the periodic regulator has no external spatial boundary, so the
finite vacuum action and its first variation vanish.  Fourier expansion gives
symbol
$h^{-2}\sum_a[1-\cos(2\pi h r_a\cdot k)]/4$, which converges to
$2\pi^2|k|^2$, proving the semigroup and metric limit.  Conservativity is
\Cref{thm:relational-completion}.
\end{proof}


\begin{theorem}[Explicit conservative homogeneous curved-vacuum branch]
\label{thm:relational-deSitter-branch}
Fix $H>0$ and retain the scalar-period carrier and the twelve oriented root
branches of \Cref{cor:relational-flat-vacuum}.  At physical time $t$, give each
oriented root the rate
\[
 \boxed{k_{\alpha,h}(t)=\frac{e^{-2Ht}}{8h^2}}
 \tag{RC.15a}
\]
and every vertex the mass
\[
 \boxed{m_h(t)=e^{3Ht}h^3.}
 \tag{RC.15b}
\]
Take one point in the matter fibre, trivial deck and projective sectors, and a
one-target slow geometry row.  Then:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(D\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item the predictable bracket, speed density, and ADM variables are
      \[
       \boxed{
       \mathcal B_h(t)=e^{-2Ht}I_3,
       \qquad \varrho_h(t)=e^{3Ht},
       \qquad g_h(t)=e^{2Ht}I_3,
       \quad N_h(t)=1,
       \quad\beta_h(t)=0;}
       \tag{RC.15c}
      \]
\item every undirected root-edge conductance is
      \[
       \boxed{u_{e,h}(t)=\frac{e^{Ht}}8h,}
       \tag{RC.15d}
      \]
      and on every compact time slab $|t|\le T$ the cut, Poincar\'e,
      $R^{3/2}$ counting, and compact-screen constants have one positive lower
      bound independent of $h$;
\item the continuum coframe
      \[
       \vartheta^0=\dd t,
       \qquad
       \vartheta^a=e^{Ht}\dd x^a
      \]
      with connection
      $\omega^a{}_0=H\vartheta^a$, $\omega^a{}_b=0$ is torsion free and has
      constant sectional curvature $H^2$;
\item with cosmological coefficient
      \[
       \boxed{\Lambda_{\rm cos}=3H^2,}
       \tag{RC.15e}
      \]
      the limiting Lorentzian metric
      \[
       \boxed{
       \mathbf g_H=-\dd t^2+e^{2Ht}
       (\dd x_1^2+\dd x_2^2+\dd x_3^2)}
       \tag{RC.15f}
      \]
      satisfies
      $G_{\mu\nu}+\Lambda_{\rm cos}(\mathbf g_H)_{\mu\nu}=0$;
\item on the explicit nested sequence
      $h_n=2^{-n^2}$ with time mesh $h_n$ and screen $[-n,n]$, exact
      parallel transport of the reconstructed Levi--Civita connection gives
      metric-unitary links, while the normalized torsion, plaquette-curvature,
      and Palatini first-variation defects are $O_T(h_n)$ on every compact
      slab and are summable along the diagonal exhaustion;
\item forgetting the curved port recovers every old Store cylinder exactly.
\end{enumerate}
Consequently the relationally repaired primitive has a genuinely curved,
nondegenerate, globally hyperbolic vacuum realization.  The metric in
\textup{(RC.15f)} is the compact spatial quotient of the flat de~Sitter
slicing; geodesic completion to the global hyperboloid is a stronger optional
global construction.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The twelve-root identity used in
\Cref{cor:relational-flat-vacuum} gives
$\mathcal B_h(t)=e^{-2Ht}I_3$.  Substitution in \textup{(RC.11)} with
$\varrho_h=e^{3Ht}$ gives \textup{(RC.15c)}.  Multiplying one directed rate by
the vertex mass gives \textup{(RC.15d)}.  On $[-T,T]$ the factor $e^{Ht}$ is
bounded above and below, so the periodic cut estimate and all consequences of
the protected spatial-screen theorem remain uniform.

Since $\dd\vartheta^a=H\vartheta^0\wedge\vartheta^a$, Cartan's first equation
vanishes for the displayed connection.  Cartan's second equation gives
$\Omega^{A}{}_{B}=H^2\vartheta^A\wedge\vartheta_B$ and hence
$R_{\mu\nu}=3H^2\mathbf g_{\mu\nu}$ and $R=12H^2$, proving the Einstein
equation.  Smooth Taylor expansion of exact link parallel transports gives a
face holonomy
$\log U_{\partial p}=-|p|\Omega_p+O_T(h_n^3)$ and an integrated torsion
remainder $O_T(h_n^3)$.  Division by face area yields the $O_T(h_n)$
defects.  Midpoint quadrature gives the same order for the finite
Palatini--Holst plus cosmological first variation.  The choice
$h_n=2^{-n^2}$ makes $\sum_ne^{Cn}h_n<\infty$ for every fixed $C$.
Conservativity follows from \Cref{thm:relational-completion} because the
curved port propagator is trace preserving.
\end{proof}

\begin{assessment}[Realization status of the repaired spacetime branch]
The old marginal Store tensor still does not determine a persistent endpoint,
a fast geometric clock, or a global period law.  Once the compiler-minimal
relational repair is adopted, however, spacetime existence is no longer merely
a certification alternative: \Cref{cor:relational-flat-vacuum} and
\Cref{thm:relational-deSitter-branch} give explicit flat and curved cofinal
vacuum realizations.  Historical terminal reuse remains a separate economy
audit and is not an existence premise.
\end{assessment}

\subsection{Refinement polarization and the relational cutoff packet}
\label{subsec:relational-refinement}
% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

\begin{definition}[Paired old--detail refinement profile]
\label{def:relational-refinement-profile}
For adjacent cutoffs $X<Y$, decompose the source-minimal fine carrier as
\[
 \mathcal H_Y=J_{Y/X}\mathcal H_X\oplus K_{Y/X}\mathcal D_{Y/X}.
\]
Let the physical positive form $M_Y=I+L_Y$ have polarization block
\[
 \boxed{
 M_Y=\begin{pmatrix}A_{Y/X}&B_{Y/X}\\
                     B_{Y/X}^*&D_{Y/X}\end{pmatrix}.}
 \tag{RC.15}
\]
On the supported detail space put
\[
 S_{Y/X}=A_{Y/X}-B_{Y/X}D_{Y/X}^{\dagger}B_{Y/X}^*,
 \tag{RC.16}
\]
\[
 \boxed{
 \sigma_{Y/X}=\|S_{Y/X}-M_X\|_{\op},\quad
 \mu_{Y/X}=\lambda_{\min}^{+}(D_{Y/X}),\quad
 \theta_{Y/X}=\|B_{Y/X}D_{Y/X}^{\dagger}\|_{\op}.}
 \tag{RC.17}
\]
The table \textup{(RC.15)}, reconstructed by finite polarization on old,
detail, and mixed probes, is the refinement component of the revised
Grand-Tensor cutoff system.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Exact harmonic lift and common-screen handoff]
\label{thm:relational-refinement-handoff}
Assume the range condition required for \textup{(RC.16)}.  The map
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal H_{Y/X}u
 =J_{Y/X}u-K_{Y/X}D_{Y/X}^{\dagger}B_{Y/X}^*u}
 \tag{RC.18}
\]
minimizes the fine energy over all detail completions and satisfies
\[
 \boxed{
 \langle\mathcal H_{Y/X}u,M_Y\mathcal H_{Y/X}u\rangle
 =\langle u,S_{Y/X}u\rangle.}
 \tag{RC.19}
\]
Thus $\sigma_{Y/X}=0$ is exact effective old-sector transport.  If along a
cofinal sequence
\[
 \sum_X\left(\sigma_X+\theta_X+\mu_X^{-1}\right)<\infty,
 \tag{RC.20}
\]
then the relational forms, resolvents, regular low-energy spectral projections,
Hodge complexes, traces, and every fixed finite internal-rank loading have the
same canonical common-screen limit furnished by Part~I-B.  A failed condition
returns respectively an old-sector Schur mismatch, a leakage direction, or a
finite detail soft mode.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Complete the square in \textup{(RC.15)} on the supported detail range.  The
minimizer is \textup{(RC.18)} and the remaining old quadratic form is the Schur
complement \textup{(RC.16)}, proving \textup{(RC.19)}.  Summability in
\textup{(RC.20)} is precisely the summable form/resolvent compatibility profile
used in
\Cref{thm:summable-metric-correction,thm:GT-Mosco,thm:compact-screen-alternative}.
Tensoring a fixed finite internal carrier multiplies screen ranks by its fixed
dimension and does not alter the summability powers.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Boundary-complete relational refinement]
\label{cor:relational-boundary-complete-refinement}
In the setting of \Cref{def:relational-refinement-profile}, suppose the fine
cutoff also carries a physical boundary map
\[
 \mathcal D_{Y/X}=(D_{X,Y}\;D_{\rm det,Y})
 :J_{Y/X}\mathcal H_X\oplus K_{Y/X}\mathcal D_{Y/X}
 \longrightarrow\mathcal B_{Y/X}.
\]
Put
\[
 E_{Y/X}
 =D_{X,Y}-D_{\rm det,Y}D_{Y/X}^{\dagger}B_{Y/X}^*,
 \qquad
 K_{Y/X}^{\partial}
 =D_{\rm det,Y}D_{Y/X}^{\dagger}D_{\rm det,Y}^*.
\]
After separating the detail kernel into the exceptional screen, the exact
boundary-complete effective old action is
\[
 \boxed{
 S_{Y/X}^{\partial}
 =S_{Y/X}
 +E_{Y/X}^*(I+K_{Y/X}^{\partial})^{-1}E_{Y/X}.}
 \tag{RC.21}
\]
Hence refinement transport of the complete closure packet requires only the
three effective rows
$(S_{Y/X},E_{Y/X},K_{Y/X}^{\partial})$; identifying arbitrary detail bases
between cutoffs is unnecessary.  Shorting before the boundary is assembled
loses exactly the positive dispersion of
\Cref{cor:GT-boundary-relaxation-dispersion}.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Apply \Cref{thm:GT-boundary-complete-short} to the old/detail polarization
\textup{(RC.15)} and the displayed boundary map.  The asserted data reduction
is immediate from the resulting formula.
\end{proof}

\begin{assessment}[Revised universal boundary]
The old Store process remains an exact, canonical structural shadow and the
countermodels separating it from global geometry remain valid.  The universal
primitive adopted by this manuscript is nevertheless no longer missing an
unspecified relation object: it is $\mathsf P^{\rm old}$ together with the
future-minimal relation packet \textup{(RC.1)} and the paired refinement table
\textup{(RC.15)}.  Domain sections should therefore test physical coefficients,
nonzero loads, global topology, and conjecture-specific estimates on this
common carrier rather than repeatedly re-admitting persistence, geometry, or
relative source orientation as unrelated primitives.
\end{assessment}



The higher-grade calculus obeys an additional order-of-operations principle.
A finite comparison of resolved laws supplies a Hellinger secant but not a
physical derivative; one-copy data supply neither a multi-copy carrier nor an
associative fusion; and a signed M\"obius interaction is not itself a positive
coercive action.  The admissible chain is therefore
\[
 \boxed{
 \begin{gathered}
 \text{actual panel}\longrightarrow\text{secant source}
 \longrightarrow\text{physical tangent}\\
 \longrightarrow\text{fusion/occurrence short}
 \longrightarrow\text{effective fixed or current sector}.
 \end{gathered}}
\]
At each arrow the missing structure is represented by a positive residual or a
concrete incompatibility witness.

\begin{assessment}[Exact meaning of full microscopic emergence]
The canonical finite object is complete relative to the declared operational
process and its minimal readable record.  ``Full'' may additionally mean a
finer provenance ledger only when its point Reads are actual physical
operations.  The finite theorem contains every represented mixed word, its
relations, and the minimal contextually separated quotient.  At the
pre-renewal level, completeness means that every returning hidden direction
and every declared passive provenance direction has been reduced to its unique
reachable--observable quotient.  It does not mean that an unread spectator,
a preferred hidden basis, or a finest microscopic dilation has been selected.
Nor does it contain by definition an unmeasured fringe, an undeclared source,
one finite infinite-horizon memory, a downstream synchronized Store loading
not verified by its residual, or a regulator-uniform gap.  Parts~I-B and I-C
canonically construct the structural carrier and an unconditional
certification-or-obstruction profile.  They do not force the positive branch or
supply a domain's missing metric, locality scale, unbounded-field domain, or
numerical coercive margin.
\end{assessment}

\part{Canonical minimal operational emergence of the Renewal Grand Tensor}
\label{part:full-microscopic-emergence}

\begin{assessment}[Internal architecture of Part I]
Part I-A consists of the finite tomographic, record, predictive, CP, history,
source, flat-reconstruction, and renewal theorems.  It also classifies finite
pre-renewal lifts into the visible quotient, the canonical returned-feedback
quotient, and Read-relative sealed provenance, thereby replacing a preferred
hidden primitive by a canonical operational floor.  Part I-B derives strict
cutoff systems from global cylinder data, constructs exact and summably
corrected AF/quasilocal states and source limits, reconstructs renormalization
cocycles, and treats changing-domain unbounded limits by Mosco and graph-screen
methods.  Part I-C reconstructs intrinsic operational hypergraphs and collars,
classifies recurrent memory, and assembles source, metric, field, locality,
coercivity, and nontriviality profiles into the universal
certification-or-obstruction theorem.  Domain sections evaluate those profiles;
they do not redefine the universal machinery.
\end{assessment}

% =============================================================================
\section{Tomographic entrance, generated ledgers, and minimal readable records}
\label{sec:minimal-datum}
% =============================================================================

The finite emergence theorem begins from complete operational process data, not
from a hidden state space or a target algebra.  Three classical objects must be
distinguished from the outset:
\[
 \boxed{
 \begin{aligned}
  &\text{the generated ledger of facts physically written by the protocol},\\
  &\text{the smallest record actually distinguishable by admitted futures},\\
  &\text{an optional finer provenance record when all of its point Reads are physical}.
 \end{aligned}}
\]
Only the second is intrinsic without a stronger point-Read policy.  Record
minimization occurs before deterministic writers are completed to a
$C^*$-history algebra; a $C^*$-ideal quotient cannot merge two surviving
orthogonal classical points.

\begin{definition}[Bare finite intervention--renewal datum]
\label{def:bare-predictive-renewal}
At cutoff $X$, a bare finite intervention--renewal datum consists of:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(R\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item a finite typed protocol with deterministic discard, finite sequential and
      parallel composition, finite classical control, and coarse graining;
\item finite typed preparation, intervention-outcome, and terminal-Read
      alphabets, together with finite exposed quantum port spaces and a finite
      physical CP frame spanning every exposed Hermitian Choi-coordinate space;
\item all admitted multitime probabilities on those frames, affine under
      randomization, additive under coarse graining, normalized on complete
      instruments and causal testers, and compatible on common prefixes;
\item a finite typed generated ledger
      $\widetilde{\mathscr R}_{X,x}$, partial deterministic updates $u_a$ for
      primitive branches, and a finite self-adjoint family of actual
      record-dependent response coordinates $\mathscr D_{X,x}$ containing the
      constant function, branch-domain indicators, terminal Reads, control
      predicates, and a spanning set of the record-dependent primitive CP
      response coordinates;
\item a distinguished deterministic Store step or Store instrument whenever a
      Store port is used later, but no Stinespring environment, scheduler,
      score collision, dwell law, or reset is included;
\item the requirement that the unique tensors reconstructed from the table pass
      the finite positivity and causal-prefix tests of
      \Cref{thm:comb-tomography}.
\end{enumerate}
No predictive state space, positive comb representative, hidden memory,
common dilation, formal adjoint, coherent fringe, flat depth, autonomous
renewal, regulator gap, domain semantic, or conjecture-specific coefficient is
part of the datum.
\end{definition}

\begin{assessment}[Exact meaning of minimal assumptions]
The entrance is assumption-minimal relative to tomographically complete finite
operational process data and the actual finite Read interface.  It is
informationally rich and is not claimed to follow from a few microscopic
Hamiltonian constants.  The theorem reconstructs every finite structural
object compatible with those data without adding a target-shaped algebra,
record, metric, arithmetic coefficient, or physical scheduler.  When a deeper
finite realization is considered, the operational table selects its minimal
active and Read-visible quotients but cannot select unread spectator fibres or
a preferred maximal dilation.
\end{assessment}


\begin{assessment}[Compiled presentation of the upstream semantic floor]
\label{assess:GT-compiled-upstream-presentation}
The datum of \Cref{def:bare-predictive-renewal} begins after the austere entrance
of \Cref{sec:upstream-primitive-closure} has been compiled into a finite
intervention table and record machine.  Its generated ledger is therefore a
computational presentation, not an additional foundational row.  The upstream
occurrence, contextual-prediction, orientation, and calibration data remain
visible through the corresponding physical branches and Reads; removing any of
those semantic rows is not licensed by the ledger quotient.
\end{assessment}

\begin{definition}[Generated operational record machine]
\label{def:protected-operational-record}
For a boundary type $x$, let $\widetilde{\mathscr R}_{X,x}$ be the finite set
of ledger values generated by the protocol.  For a primitive branch
$a:x\to y$, let
\[
 u_a:\operatorname{Dom}(u_a)\subseteq\widetilde{\mathscr R}_{X,x}
 \longrightarrow\widetilde{\mathscr R}_{X,y}
\]
be its deterministic ledger update.  The finite self-adjoint family
$\mathscr D_{X,x}\subset C(\widetilde{\mathscr R}_{X,x})$ contains exactly
the declared one-step scalar response coordinates needed to reconstruct every
record-conditioned primitive operation.  It may contain point indicators only
when the corresponding point Reads are physically admitted.
\end{definition}

For an admissible word $w=a_m\cdots a_1:x\to y$, write
$u_w=u_{a_m}\circ\cdots\circ u_{a_1}$ on its natural domain, and extend
$d\circ u_w$ by zero outside that domain.

\begin{definition}[Future equivalence and minimal readable record]
\label{def:minimal-readable-record}
For $r,s\in\widetilde{\mathscr R}_{X,x}$, write $r\sim_{X,x}s$ when
\[
 \boxed{d(u_w(r))=d(u_w(s))}
\]
for every admitted typed word $w:x\to y$ and every
$d\in\mathscr D_{X,y}$, including equality of all word-domain indicators.
Define
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathscr R_{X,x}^{\min}
 :=\widetilde{\mathscr R}_{X,x}/\!\sim_{X,x},
 \qquad
 q_{X,x}:\widetilde{\mathscr R}_{X,x}\twoheadrightarrow
 \mathscr R_{X,x}^{\min}.}
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Canonical minimal-readable-record theorem]
\label{thm:minimal-record}
The family $\mathscr R_X^{\min}$ is the unique coarsest typed classical record
through which every admitted record-conditioned future factors.  More
precisely:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(M\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item $\sim_{X,x}$ is an equivalence relation and a typed right congruence;
\item every primitive update descends uniquely to a partial deterministic map
      $u_a^{\min}$ satisfying $u_a^{\min}q_{X,x}=q_{X,y}u_a$;
\item every pulled-back future coordinate $d\circ u_w$ factors uniquely through
      $q_{X,x}$;
\item if $g_x:\widetilde{\mathscr R}_{X,x}\twoheadrightarrow S_x$ is any
      typed quotient through which all updates and all coordinates in
      $\mathscr D_{X,x}$ factor, then there is a unique surjection
      $h_x:S_x\twoheadrightarrow\mathscr R_{X,x}^{\min}$ with
      $q_{X,x}=h_xg_x$;
\item the construction is invariant under operational record-machine
      isomorphism and is idempotent.
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Reflexivity, symmetry, and transitivity follow from equality of all future
signatures.  If $r\sim s$ and $a$ is admitted at both records, then for every
continuation $w$ and Read $d$,
\[
 d(u_w(u_a(r)))=d(u_{wa}(r))=d(u_{wa}(s))=d(u_w(u_a(s))),
\]
so $u_a(r)\sim u_a(s)$; branch-domain indicators ensure simultaneous
admissibility.  This proves the right-congruence property and makes the
quotient update well defined.  The definition of $\sim$ proves factorization
of every future coordinate, and surjectivity of $q$ gives uniqueness.

For the universal property, if $g_x(r)=g_x(s)$, then every immediate coordinate
agrees because it factors through $g_x$.  Induction on word length, using
that the updates descend through $g$, shows equality of every future
coordinate, so $r\sim s$.  Hence each $g$-fibre lies inside one $q$-fibre,
which defines the unique map $h_x$ with $q_x=h_xg_x$.  Operational
isomorphisms preserve the complete signature family, and applying the same
construction to the quotient separates all distinct quotient classes, proving
canonicity and idempotence.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Smallest readable classical algebra]
\label{def:minimal-read-algebra}
Let
\[
 \mathfrak R_{X,x}^{\min}
 :=q_{X,x}^*C(\mathscr R_{X,x}^{\min})
 \subseteq C(\widetilde{\mathscr R}_{X,x}).
\]
Equivalently, let $\mathfrak B_{X,x}$ be the unital $C^*$-algebra generated by
all functions $d\circ u_w$.  
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Minimal Read-algebra characterization]
\label{thm:minimal-read-algebra}
For every type $x$,
\[
 \boxed{\mathfrak R_{X,x}^{\min}=\mathfrak B_{X,x}.}
\]
It is the smallest unital classical $C^*$-subalgebra containing the actual
response coordinates and invariant under every primitive pullback
$f\mapsto f\circ u_a$.  Its Gelfand spectrum is canonically
$\mathscr R_{X,x}^{\min}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Every generator $d\circ u_w$ is constant on future-equivalence classes, hence
belongs to $q_x^*C(\mathscr R_x^{\min})$.  Conversely, distinct quotient
classes are separated by some pulled-back future coordinate.  A unital
self-adjoint subalgebra of functions on a finite set which separates points is
the whole function algebra: its joint level-set projections are obtained by
finite Lagrange interpolation.  This proves equality.  Pulling back a generator
along $u_a$ produces the generator associated with the concatenated word, so
the algebra is update invariant.  Any other update-invariant algebra
containing the immediate response coordinates contains all their iterated
pullbacks and hence contains $\mathfrak B_{X,x}$.
\end{proof}

\begin{construction}[Terminating partition refinement]
\label{con:partition-refinement}
Let $\Pi_x^{(0)}$ group ledger values with equal immediate coordinates in
$\mathscr D_{X,x}$ and equal primitive branch-domain indicators.  Given
$\Pi^{(k)}$, place $r,s$ in the same block of $\Pi_x^{(k+1)}$ exactly when they
are in the same block of $\Pi_x^{(0)}$ and, for every primitive $a:x\to y$,
either $a$ is unavailable at both records or $u_a(r),u_a(s)$ lie in the same
block of $\Pi_y^{(k)}$.
\end{construction}

\begin{theorem}[Termination, exactness, and record margin]
\label{thm:minimal-record-audit}
Let $n_{\rm rec}=\sum_x|\widetilde{\mathscr R}_{X,x}|$.  Then:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(P\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item $\Pi_x^{(k)}$ identifies exactly the records not separated by a future
      word of length at most $k$;
\item the refinement stabilizes after at most $n_{\rm rec}-1$ strict rounds;
\item the stable partition is $\mathscr R_{X,x}^{\min}$;
\item choosing the finitely many response coordinates encountered before
      stabilization gives signature vectors $v(r)$ with
      \[
       \boxed{r\sim s\iff\Delta_{\rm rec}(r,s)
       :=\|v(r)-v(s)\|_2^2=0;}
      \]
\item if at least two classes occur, the minimum nonzero signature distance
      $\delta_{{\rm rec},X}$ is positive and gives robust recovery whenever
      every estimated signature is within $\varepsilon$ and
      $4\varepsilon<\delta_{{\rm rec},X}$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The first assertion is induction on $k$: a future of length $k+1$ is either an
immediate Read or a primitive branch followed by a future of length at most
$k$.  Each strict refinement increases the total number of blocks, which is at
most $n_{\rm rec}$, proving termination.  At stabilization, equality is
preserved by every primitive update and every immediate coordinate, hence by
every word; conversely future-equivalent records survive every finite round.
This proves the first three claims.  The stabilized finite coordinate family
separates exactly the stable blocks, proving the residual criterion.  Finiteness
makes the least nonzero distance positive.  The triangle and reverse-triangle
inequalities separate same-class distances, at most $2\varepsilon$, from
different-class distances, at least
$\delta_{{\rm rec},X}-2\varepsilon$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Unread refinements and the correct bundle decomposition]
\label{thm:record-refinement-bundle}
Let $\pi:\widetilde{\mathscr R}'\twoheadrightarrow
\widetilde{\mathscr R}$ intertwine all updates and suppose every admitted
response upstairs is exactly a pullback of a response downstairs.  Then
$\mathscr R'^{\min}\cong\mathscr R^{\min}$ canonically.  For the quotient
$q:\widetilde{\mathscr R}\twoheadrightarrow\mathscr R^{\min}$ and fibres
$F_\rho=q^{-1}(\rho)$,
\[
 \boxed{
 C(\widetilde{\mathscr R})
 \cong\bigoplus_{\rho\in\mathscr R^{\min}}C(F_\rho),
 \qquad
 q^*C(\mathscr R^{\min})
 =\bigoplus_\rho\C\one_{F_\rho}.}
\]
A base-preserving tensor factorization
$C(\widetilde{\mathscr R})\cong C(\mathscr R^{\min})\otimes C(D)$ exists if
and only if $|F_\rho|=|D|$ for every $\rho$; even then it is noncanonical
without a fibre trivialization, and compatibility with updates imposes a
further dynamical condition.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Intertwining gives
$(d\circ\pi)(u'_w(r'))=d(u_w(\pi(r')))$, so two fine records have the same
complete future signature exactly when their images do.  This gives the
canonical bijection of minima.  Restriction to the disjoint fibres gives the
direct-sum decomposition, and pullback functions are exactly the fibrewise
constant ones.  In a base-preserving tensor split, the corner over $\rho$ is
both $C(F_\rho)$ and $C(D)$, so their finite spectra have equal cardinality.
Conversely, equal cardinalities plus chosen bijections $F_\rho\cong D$ give a
split.  The chosen bijections are not determined by the operational table,
and an update intertwines the split only when it respects them.
\end{proof}

\begin{countertheorem}[$C^*$-quotients cannot merge surviving classical records]
\label{cth:record-cstar-merge}
Let $p,q$ be orthogonal projections and let $\pi$ be a $*$-homomorphism.  If
$\pi(p)=\pi(q)$, then $\pi(p)=\pi(q)=0$.  Consequently classical record
minimization cannot be delegated to a two-sided $C^*$-ideal quotient after
nonzero point projections and their writers have been generated.
\end{countertheorem}

\begin{proof}
Since $pq=0$,
$0=\pi(pq)=\pi(p)\pi(q)=\pi(p)^2$.  A projection with square zero is zero.
Thus a $C^*$-quotient may delete a classical point ideal but cannot identify
two nonzero orthogonal points.  The future-equivalence quotient must therefore
be performed on the classical record machine before its writer
$C^*$-envelope is formed.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Minimal operational record completion]
\label{def:operationally-complete-renewal}
Let
\[
 \mathfrak R_X^{\min}:=\bigoplus_x C(\mathscr R_{X,x}^{\min}).
\]
For a quotient record class $\rho$ and primitive branch $a$, write
\[
 W^{\rm rec}_{a,\rho}:=|u_a^{\min}(\rho)\rangle\langle\rho|.
\]
The minimal operational completion is
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathfrak O_X^{\min,\rm op}
 :=\operatorname{MinRec}_X(\mathfrak O_X)
 =\bigl(\mathfrak O_X,\mathfrak R_X^{\min}\bigr).}
\]
If a support-minimal core branch has Kraus operators $K_{a,\rho,j}$, its
record-completed Kraus operators are
\[
 \widetilde K_{a,\rho,j}
 =W^{\rm rec}_{a,\rho}\otimes K_{a,\rho,j}.
\]
An optional full-provenance completion retains the generated ledger itself,
but is canonical only relative to the stronger declared point-Read policy.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Operational-record completion theorem]
\label{thm:operational-record-completion}
The minimal completion is canonical and has the following properties.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(O\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item every completed branch is CP and trace-nonincreasing, and every completed
      instrument is normalized;
\item discarding the record recovers every original record-forgetting word map
      and intervention probability;
\item sequential and parallel composition, coarse graining, deterministic
      discard, and label-preserving operational morphisms are preserved;
\item unread record refinements yield canonically isomorphic minimal
      completions;
\item compatible cutoff morphisms induce compatible maps of minimal records
      whenever they preserve the complete old future signature;
\item if every generated ledger point has an actual terminal point Read, then
      the minimal record is the full generated ledger and no operational fact
      is erased.
\end{enumerate}
No target-domain coefficient or semantic predicate enters the construction.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
For a completed branch,
\[
 \sum_j\widetilde K_{a,\rho,j}^*\widetilde K_{a,\rho,j}
 =P_\rho\otimes\sum_jK_{a,\rho,j}^*K_{a,\rho,j}
 \preceq P_\rho\otimes I.
\]
Summing over a complete instrument gives the identity in every record block.
Record discard removes the deterministic writer, and induction on word length
recovers every core word and scalar probability.  Writer multiplication is
composition of the deterministic quotient updates; parallel writers tensor
and coarse graining sums the CP branches.  Functoriality and unread-refinement
invariance follow from \Cref{thm:minimal-record,thm:record-refinement-bundle}.
A cutoff map descends precisely when old future-equivalent records remain
future equivalent after restriction.  Finally, point Reads separate every pair
of generated ledger values, making all equivalence classes singletons.
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[Operational facts, not target-domain semantics]
\label{fire:record-semantic-firewall}
The minimal or full provenance record may store only facts independently
written by the protocol: preparation, intervention, outcome, chronology,
route, boundary, interface, regulator, and declared environment outcomes.  It
does not directly store primality, $\Lambda(n)$, $\mu(n)$, a metric, a gauge
group, a particle species, a Yukawa matrix, a chain equivalence, a complexity
answer, or the truth of a conjecture.
\end{firewall}

% =============================================================================
\section{Hankel reconstruction and the table-native executable algebra}
\label{sec:hankel-core}
% =============================================================================

For each boundary type $x$ and minimal readable record $\rho$, let
$\mathsf P_{x,\rho}$ and $\mathsf F_{x,\rho}$ be the admitted finite pasts and
futures meeting at $(x,\rho)$, and write
$\mathbb p_{x,\rho}(f,p)=\Pr(f\circ p)$.

\begin{definition}[Record-conditioned intervention Hankel operator]
\label{def:intervention-hankel}
Define
\[
 \mathsf H_{x,\rho}
 =[\mathbb p_{x,\rho}(f,p)]_{f,p},
 \qquad
 h_p(f)=\mathbb p_{x,\rho}(f,p),
 \qquad
 M_{x,\rho}=\Span_\R\{h_p\}.
\]
Its dimension is the typed Hankel rank $d_{x,\rho}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Canonical typed Hankel realization]
\label{thm:typed-hankel-realization}
For every primitive letter
$a:(x,\rho)\to(y,u_a^{\min}(\rho))$ there is a unique linear map
\[
 A_a:M_{x,\rho}\longrightarrow M_{y,u_a^{\min}(\rho)},
 \qquad A_ah_p=h_{a\circ p}.
\]
Every future defines $\lambda_f(m)=m(f)$, and
\[
 \boxed{\mathbb p(f,p)=\lambda_f(h_p),
 \qquad \lambda_fA_a=\lambda_{f\circ a}.}
\]
The realization is reachable and future separated in every minimal record
sector.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
If $\sum_jc_jh_{p_j}=0$, then for every target future $f$,
$\sum_jc_jh_{a\circ p_j}(f)=\sum_jc_j\mathbb p(f\circ a,p_j)=0$.
Thus appending $a$ respects all column relations and defines a unique map.
Evaluation gives the displayed identities.  Reachability holds by definition,
and a nonzero response function is detected by some future.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Hankel-rank minimality]
\label{thm:hankel-minimality}
For any linear realization $N_{x,\rho}$, let $N^{\rm reach}$ be its reachable
span and $N^{\rm unobs}$ the reachable vectors annihilated by every future.
Then
\[
 \boxed{N^{\rm reach}_{x,\rho}/N^{\rm unobs}_{x,\rho}
 \cong M_{x,\rho},
 \qquad \dim N_{x,\rho}\ge d_{x,\rho}.}
\]
Equality holds exactly for reachable future-separated realizations, and any
two minimal realizations are related by a unique record-preserving similarity
intertwining all primitive transitions and future effects.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
On the reachable span define $(Qn)(f)=\mu_f(n)$.  It maps the state of a past
$p$ to $h_p$, hence is onto, and its kernel is exactly the future-unobservable
subspace.  The first-isomorphism theorem gives the quotient and dimension
claims.  Mapping the state of each past in one minimal realization to the state
of the same past in another is well defined by equality of all future
probabilities, injective by future separation, onto by reachability, and
uniquely intertwines the generators.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Operational predictive cone]
For finite $d_{x,\rho}$ put
\[
 M_{x,\rho}^+
 :=\{m:m(f)\ge0\text{ for every positive admitted future }f\}.
\]
Let $u_{x,\rho}$ be deterministic discard.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Ordered predictive realization]
\label{thm:ordered-memory}
Each $M_{x,\rho}^+$ is closed, pointed, and generating; physical past columns
belong to it; every $A_a$ is positive; and every complete instrument
$\{a_o\}$ satisfies
\[
 \boxed{u\!\left(\sum_oA_{a_o}m\right)=u(m).}
\]
Thus order and normalization descend from the table rather than from a hidden
state-space model.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The cone is an intersection of closed half-spaces.  If both $m$ and $-m$ are
positive, every future vanishes on $m$, so $m=0$.  Physical columns span the
response space, making the cone generating.  Positivity of $A_a$ follows from
$(A_am)(f)=m(f\circ a)$, and instrument normalization holds on physical
columns by the operational axioms and hence on their span.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Record-conditioned predictive minimality]
\label{thm:conditional-core-minimality}
At finite cutoff the intrinsic linear predictive core is
\[
 \boxed{
 M_X^{\min,\rm op}
 =\bigoplus_{x,\rho\in\mathscr R_X^{\min}}
 |x,\rho\rangle\otimes M_{x,\rho}.}
\]
It preserves all intervention probabilities and every minimal Read.  An
optional full-provenance realization is the direct sum over the finer ledger,
but unread fibre contrasts are not part of the intrinsic minimum.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Take the direct sum of the Hankel quotients.  Every probability factors through
them by \Cref{thm:typed-hankel-realization}.  Distinct minimal record classes
are separated by an admitted future and therefore cannot be identified.
Unread refinements collapse by \Cref{thm:record-refinement-bundle}.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Table-native executable predictive algebra]
\label{def:executable-predictive-algebra}
Let $\mathfrak P_X^+$ be the finite typed forward path algebra generated by the
primitive executable letters and object units.  Its canonical response
representation sends a word to its action on the spaces $M_{x,\rho}$.  Define
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal B_X^{\rm pred}
 :=\rho_X^+(\mathfrak P_X^+)
 \cong\mathfrak P_X^+/\Ker\rho_X^+.}
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Realization-free executable algebra]
\label{thm:executable-predictive-algebra}
The scalar operational table determines $\mathcal B_X^{\rm pred}$ directly.
For a forward polynomial $q=\sum_wc_ww$,
\[
 \boxed{\rho_X^+(q)=0
 \iff
 \sum_wc_w\Pr(f\circ w\circ p)=0}
\]
for every compatible past $p$ and future $f$.  Every reachable,
future-separated linear realization of the same table is uniquely similar to
this response realization.  No Kraus map, Stinespring environment, Hilbert
metric, or formal reverse is used.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
A forward polynomial vanishes on the response spaces exactly when it sends
every past column to the zero response function, which is equivalent to the
displayed scalar identities against all futures.  The universal similarity is
the uniqueness part of \Cref{thm:hankel-minimality}, extended multiplicatively
from the primitive transitions.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Exact finite/infinite linear-predictive alternative]
\label{thm:predictive-alternative}
Let $H_n$ be an exhaustive increasing family of finite typed Hankel panels and
put $d_n=\rank H_n$.  The total infinite Hankel rank satisfies
\[
 \boxed{d_\infty=\sup_n d_n.}
\]
If $d_\infty=d<\infty$, the nondecreasing integer ranks stabilize at $d$ and
the complete process has a unique reachable future-separated linear predictor
of dimension $d$.  If $d_\infty=\infty$, no finite-dimensional linear
predictor represents all admitted histories.  No finite panel alone proves
that later innovations will never occur.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Every finite submatrix of the infinite Hankel table is contained in some
exhaustive panel, so its rank is at most $\sup_nd_n$; conversely each $H_n$ is
a finite submatrix, proving equality.  A bounded nondecreasing integer sequence
is eventually constant.  Once a basis of $d$ response columns has appeared,
every later column lies in their span and the canonical response construction
gives the global $d$-dimensional realization.  Infinite rank contradicts the
rank bound of every finite-dimensional realization.  For the last statement,
tensor any fixed finite-horizon process with a classical process which is
constant through that horizon and first emits an arbitrary number of
future-distinguishable states afterward.  This leaves the observed panel
unchanged while making the later rank arbitrarily large.
\end{proof}

% =============================================================================
\section{Finite comb tomography and the canonical minimal CP class}
\label{sec:comb-reconstruction}
% =============================================================================

At slot $k$, let
$E_k=\operatorname{Herm}(H_{2k-1}\otimes H_{2k-2})$.

\begin{lemma}[Physical CP branches span every Choi-coordinate space]
\label{lem:CP-frame-span}
The real span of
$\{M\succeq0:\Tr_{2k-1}M\preceq I\}$ is all of $E_k$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Write any Hermitian $X=X_+-X_-$ with $X_\pm\succeq0$ and scale each nonzero
part so its output partial trace is at most the identity.  Undoing the scales
expresses $X$ as a real linear combination of physical CP branches.
\end{proof}

Choose physical bases $M_{k,\alpha}$ and Hilbert--Schmidt duals
$D_{k,\alpha}$, and define
\[
 R^{(N)}
 =\sum_{\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_N}
 \mathfrak p_N(M_{1,\alpha_1},\ldots,M_{N,\alpha_N})
 D_{N,\alpha_N}\otimes\cdots\otimes D_{1,\alpha_1}.
\]

\begin{theorem}[Finite process-comb tomography]
\label{thm:comb-tomography}
The probability table determines a unique frame-independent Hermitian tensor
$R^{(N)}$ representing every multilinear intervention probability.  It is a
deterministic finite quantum process exactly when
\[
 \boxed{R^{(N)}\succeq0,
 \qquad
 \Tr_{2k-1}R^{(k)}=I_{2k-2}\otimes R^{(k-1)},
 \qquad R^{(0)}=1.}
\]
The positive causal prefix combs are therefore derived consistency outputs;
they are not separate entrance objects.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Tensor products of the selected frames form a basis, so the dual-frame formula
is the unique Riesz representative.  A second frame represents the same
multilinear functional and hence gives the same tensor.  Positivity and the
recursive trace identities are necessary by the Choi theorem and deterministic
causal normalization.  Conversely, minimal purifications of the positive
prefixes can be linked sequentially by purification uniqueness, giving a
completely positive normalized process with Choi tensor $R^{(N)}$.  Uniqueness
of tomography identifies it with the supplied table.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Canonical square-root prefix purification]
For each positive prefix put
\[
 E_k:=\supp R^{(k)},
 \qquad A_k:=\overline{E_k},
 \qquad
 |\Psi_k\rangle:=\operatorname{vec}\bigl((R^{(k)})^{1/2}\bigr)
 \in P_k\otimes A_k.
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Canonical comb-to-memory dilation]
\label{thm:canonical-comb-dilation}
There are finite memories $A_k\cong\overline{\supp R^{(k)}}$, $A_0=\C$, and
isometries
\[
 \boxed{
 V_k:H_{2k-2}\otimes A_{k-1}
 \longrightarrow H_{2k-1}\otimes A_k}
\]
whose sequential link, followed by tracing $A_N$, is $R^{(N)}$.  Every other
support-minimal sequential realization is related by unique memory unitaries
\[
 \boxed{V_k'=(I\otimes U_k)V_k(I\otimes U_{k-1}^*),}
\]
intertwining the minimal record representation.  Consequently all reduced
primitive maps, formal Hilbert--Schmidt reverses, mixed words, process ideals,
contextual ideals, regular traces, word Grams, and flat depths obtained from a
support-minimal representative are canonically isomorphic.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The causal prefix identity makes
$|I\rangle\!\rangle\otimes|\Psi_{k-1}\rangle$ and $|\Psi_k\rangle$
purifications of the same reduced positive operator.  Minimal purification
uniqueness supplies $V_k$; induction is the vectorized Choi-link law.  Applying
the same uniqueness theorem to two minimal sequential realizations gives the
unitaries $U_k$.  Conjugation by $U_k$ transports every Schr\"odinger branch,
and the induced conjugation on Hilbert--Schmidt operator space is unitary, so
it also transports the formal adjoints.  Kernels, contextual matrix
coefficients, regular traces, and word Grams are therefore preserved.
\end{proof}

\begin{countertheorem}[Arbitrary positive factorizations are not interchangeable]
\label{cth:nonminimal-factorization}
The same scalar operational process can have a one-dimensional support-minimal
history algebra and a nonminimal positive realization whose ambient
Hilbert--Schmidt-adjoint algebra is noncommutative.  Hence arbitrary unreduced
positive factorizations cannot define the structural Grand Tensor.
\end{countertheorem}

\begin{proof}
Take the trivial process for which every declared word has probability one.
Its minimal predictive and minimal CP realizations are one dimensional.  On
$M_2(\C)$, realize the same table by the reset channel
$T(X)=\Tr(X)P_0$ with source $P_0$ and terminal trace.  Then
$T=|P_0)(I|$ and $T_{\rm HS}^*=|I)(P_0|$.  On
$\Span\{P_0,I\}$ these two rank-one operators generate all of $M_2(\C)$;
on the off-diagonal complement they vanish and the unit acts scalarly.
Thus $C^*(I,T,T_{\rm HS}^*)\cong M_2(\C)\oplus\C$, although the complete
unmarked table is the trivial one.  The extra algebra is manufactured by the
ambient adjoint moving between reachable and spectator directions.  Support
reduction before adjoint closure is therefore necessary.
\end{proof}

\begin{countertheorem}[Scalar data do not select a $C^*$-adjoint]
\label{cth:metric-adjoint-no-go}
Let $A=\diag(\alpha,\beta)$ with $0<\alpha<\beta<1$.  With the standard metric,
$C^*(A,A^*)\cong\C^2$.  For
$G_t=\begin{psmallmatrix}1&t\\t&1\end{psmallmatrix}$, $0<t<1$, the
$G_t$-adjoint $A^{\dagger_t}=G_t^{-1}AG_t$ generates with $A$ the full
$M_2(\C)$.  Therefore a scalar Hankel realization does not by itself determine
its formal adjoint.
\end{countertheorem}

\begin{proof}
The standard adjoint equals $A$, so the algebra is diagonal.  Since $A$ has
distinct eigenvalues, its spectral projections $E_{11},E_{22}$ are polynomials
in $A$.  The matrix $G_t$ does not commute with $A$, and direct multiplication
shows that both off-diagonal entries of $A^{\dagger_t}$ are nonzero.  Hence
$E_{11}A^{\dagger_t}E_{22}$ and $E_{22}A^{\dagger_t}E_{11}$ are nonzero
multiples of $E_{12}$ and $E_{21}$; together with the diagonal units they
generate $M_2(\C)$.
\end{proof}

\begin{assessment}[Predictive and Stinespring minimality are distinct]
$\mathcal B_X^{\rm pred}$ is the smallest forward executable algebra needed
for scalar prediction.  The support-minimal CP history class is the canonical
positive completion which also supplies mathematical adjoints.  They need not
have the same dimension.  A direct operator-system $C^*$-envelope can bypass
sequential factorization only after a complete ancillary matrix order and
formal-adjoint panel has been supplied or derived; scalar probabilities alone
do not contain that additional structure.
\end{assessment}

% =============================================================================
\section{The support-minimal process-history algebra}
\label{sec:process-history-algebra}
% =============================================================================

Use the canonical support-minimal record-conditioned CP class of
\Cref{thm:canonical-comb-dilation}.  For each typed boundary object $\xi$, put
$\mathscr X_\xi=\mathcal B(A_\xi)$ with normalized Hilbert--Schmidt product and
$\mathscr X_X=\bigoplus_\xi\mathscr X_\xi$.  For a primitive branch
$a:\xi\to\eta$, let $T_a$ be its reduced Schr\"odinger CP superoperator and
put $\rho_X(a)=P_\eta T_aP_\xi$.  Adjoin a formal reverse $a^\sharp$ represented
by $\rho_X(a)^*_{\rm HS}$; this is a mathematical adjoint, not an asserted
executable reverse channel.

\begin{theorem}[Canonical process-history representation]
\label{thm:process-representation}
Let $\mathfrak F_X^{\min,\rm op}$ be the free finite-object path $*$-algebra on
the minimal core--record alphabet.  Then
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal A_X^{\rm proc}
 :=\mathfrak F_X^{\min,\rm op}/\Ker\rho_X
 \cong C^*(\rho_X(a):a\in\Sigma_X^{\min,\rm op})}
\]
is a finite-dimensional $C^*$-algebra.  It is independent of physical CP
frames, Kraus coordinates, square-root purification coordinates, and the
chosen support-minimal representative.  This independence does not extend to
arbitrary unreduced positive factorizations.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Typed concatenation is sent to block composition, object units to orthogonal
projections, and sharpening to Hilbert--space adjoint, so $\rho_X$ is a
$*$-homomorphism and its kernel is a two-sided $*$-ideal.  Its finite-dimensional
image is a $C^*$-algebra.  The support-minimal unitary covariance in
\Cref{thm:canonical-comb-dilation} conjugates the complete word representation
and therefore gives the unique generator-fixing $*$-isomorphism.  The final
qualification is \Cref{cth:nonminimal-factorization}.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Derived common finite CP completion]
\label{thm:common-CP-completion}
Every finite family of finite-dimensional CP trace-nonincreasing maps admits a
simultaneous finite controlled-unitary completion.  Every finite CP
decomposition of one Store channel has one common Stinespring--Naimark
dilation with orthogonal outcome projections, and every finite word family has
compatible path-labelled dilations under increasing word depth.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
A Stinespring contraction $V:H\to K$ has the Julia unitary
\[
 \begin{pmatrix}V&(I-VV^*)^{1/2}\\(I-V^*V)^{1/2}&-V^*\end{pmatrix}
 :H\oplus K\to K\oplus H.
\]
Taking finite direct sums gives simultaneous control.  For a decomposition
$\Psi_j\le_{\rm CP}\Phi$, the finite CP Radon--Nikodym theorem gives effects
$F_j$ in one minimal environment; adjoining
$F_0=I-\sum_jF_j$ and applying Naimark dilation gives orthogonal outcome
projections.  Tensoring fresh minimal environments along each finite word and
taking the finite direct sum yields path-labelled dilations; minimal
Stinespring uniqueness gives compatible source-cyclic compression.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Canonical source-ideal decomposition]
\label{thm:central-source-decomposition}
For any declared source packet $\mathcal S\subseteq\mathcal A_X^{\rm proc}$,
there is a unique central projection $z_{\mathcal S}$ such that
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal I(\mathcal S)=z_{\mathcal S}\mathcal A_X^{\rm proc},
 \qquad
 \mathcal A_X^{\rm proc}
 =z_{\mathcal S}\mathcal A_X^{\rm proc}
 \oplus(1-z_{\mathcal S})\mathcal A_X^{\rm proc}.}
\]
Residual histories are therefore retained as canonical central ideals rather
than assumed absent or manually routed.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
A finite-dimensional $C^*$-algebra is a direct sum of simple matrix blocks,
and every two-sided ideal is the direct sum of a unique subset of those blocks.
The sum of their central units is $z_{\mathcal S}$.
\end{proof}

% =============================================================================
\section{Contextual future separation and record survival}
\label{sec:predictive-history-quotient}
% =============================================================================

\begin{definition}[Complete contextual history-null ideal]
\label{def:history-null-ideal}
For the process algebra define
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal N_X^{\rm fut}
 :=\{q:R_j(uqv)=R_j(uq^*v)=0
 \text{ for every admitted }R_j\text{ and all }u,v\in\mathcal A_X^{\rm proc}\}.}
\]
All minimal readable-record coordinates are included among the $R_j$; optional
full-provenance point Reads are included only when physically declared.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Operational contextual nullity is a two-sided $*$-ideal]
\label{lem:contextual-null-ideal}
$\mathcal N_X^{\rm fut}$ is a two-sided $*$-ideal, and
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal A_X^{\rm hist}
 :=\mathcal A_X^{\rm proc}/\mathcal N_X^{\rm fut}}
\]
is a finite-dimensional contextually future-separated $C^*$-algebra.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
If $q$ is null and $c,d\in\mathcal A_X^{\rm proc}$, then
$R_j(u(cqd)v)=R_j((uc)q(dv))=0$ in every context.  The second family in the
definition makes the space $*$-stable.  A finite-dimensional $*$-ideal is
closed.  A nonzero quotient class fails at least one defining null test and is
therefore future visible.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Universal contextual history envelope]
\label{thm:contextual-envelope-universal}
$\mathcal A_X^{\rm hist}$ is the minimal context-preserving, contextually
future-separated $C^*$-history envelope.  Precisely, if
$\pi:\mathcal A_X^{\rm proc}\twoheadrightarrow B$ is a $C^*$-quotient through
which every contextual Read factors, then $\Ker\pi\subseteq\mathcal N_X^{\rm fut}$
and there is a canonical surjection
$B\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal A_X^{\rm hist}$.  If $B$ is itself contextually
future separated, this map is a $*$-isomorphism.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Every element of $\Ker\pi$ is zero in every factored context, so it belongs to
$\mathcal N_X^{\rm fut}$.  The quotient universal property gives the
surjection $A/\Ker\pi\to A/\mathcal N_X^{\rm fut}$.  If the kernel of that
surjection were nonzero, it would define a nonzero class in $B$ annihilated by
all factored contexts, contradicting contextual separation.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[A finite separating Read panel exists]
\label{lem:finite-read-panel}
At most $\dim\mathcal A_X^{\rm proc}$ scalar contextual coordinates have common
kernel $\mathcal N_X^{\rm fut}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Starting from the whole finite-dimensional algebra, whenever the intersection
of the selected kernels is larger than $\mathcal N_X^{\rm fut}$, choose one
vector outside the radical and one contextual coordinate which detects it.
The intersection dimension strictly decreases, so the procedure terminates.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Record-survival theorem]
\label{thm:record-survival}
In $\mathcal A_X^{\rm hist}$:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(S\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item distinct minimal readable-record classes remain distinct;
\item every nonzero minimal record projection survives;
\item every deterministic writer attached to a nonzero branch survives;
\item every optional provenance point whose Read is physically declared also
      survives;
\item unread fibre contrasts removed by $\operatorname{MinRec}$ never enter the
      intrinsic history algebra.
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Distinct minimal classes are separated by an admitted future coordinate, so
their projection difference is not contextually null.  A nonzero writer is
detected by a preparation on which its branch has nonzero probability followed
by the Read of its target class.  The same argument applies to physically
protected provenance points.  The final statement is the definition and
universal property of the minimal record, together with
\Cref{cth:record-cstar-merge}.
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[Order of the two minimizations]
Classical future-equivalence minimization must precede writer completion.
Afterward, the contextual $C^*$-ideal removes entire algebraic directions
invisible in all two-sided word contexts; it cannot merge surviving classical
points.  Minimal record, minimal linear predictor, and minimal contextual
$C^*$-history envelope are three distinct constructions.
\end{firewall}

% =============================================================================
\section{Intrinsic normalization and the finite structural Grand Tensor}
\label{sec:full-grand-tensor}
% =============================================================================

For a finite-dimensional unital $C^*$-algebra $\mathcal A$, let $L_a(b)=ab$.

\begin{definition}[Normalized regular trace]
\label{def:regular-trace}
Define
\[
 \tau_{\rm reg}^{\mathcal A}(a)=\Tr_\C(L_a),
 \qquad
 \widehat\tau_{\rm reg}^{\mathcal A}(a)
 =\frac{\tau_{\rm reg}^{\mathcal A}(a)}{\dim_\C\mathcal A}.
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Canonical faithful trace]
\label{thm:regular-trace}
The normalized regular trace is a faithful tracial state preserved by every
$*$-isomorphism.  If
$\mathcal A\cong\bigoplus_\lambda M_{n_\lambda}(\C)$, then
\[
 \boxed{
 \tau_{\rm reg}^{\mathcal A}(a)
 =\sum_\lambda n_\lambda\Tr(a_\lambda),
