 \qquad
 \dim_\C\mathcal A=\sum_\lambda n_\lambda^2.}
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
$L_{ab}=L_aL_b$, so cyclicity of the ordinary trace gives traciality.  On
$M_n(\C)$, left multiplication is $a\otimes I_n$, with trace $n\Tr(a)$.
The displayed formula gives positivity and faithfulness on $a^*a$.
Normalization follows from $L_1=I$, and isomorphism invariance follows because
left multiplication is conjugated by the isomorphism.
\end{proof}

Let $\mathcal W^{\min,\rm op}_{X,\le r}$ have basis the composable mixed
minimal core--record words of length at most $r$, and put
$W_{X,r}e_w=[w]\in\mathcal A_X^{\rm hist}$.

\begin{definition}[Structural minimal operational Renewal Grand Tensor]
\label{def:grand-tensor}
Define
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathbb K^{\min,\rm op}_{X,r}(v,w)
 :=\widehat\tau_{\rm reg}^{\mathcal A_X^{\rm hist}}([v]^*[w]).}
\]
The canonical minimal operational Grand Tensor is
\[
 \boxed{
 \boldsymbol{\mathbb T}^{\min,\rm op}_{\Grand,X}
 :=\left(\mathcal A_X^{\rm hist},
 \{\mathbb K^{\min,\rm op}_{X,r}\}_{r\ge0},
 \mathfrak R_X^{\min}\right).}
\]
If every generated record value has a physical point Read, then
$\mathfrak R_X^{\min}=C(\widetilde{\mathscr R}_X)$ and this object is also
denoted
$\boldsymbol{\mathbb T}^{\min,op}_{\Grand,X}$.  Otherwise the optional
full-provenance tensor
$\boldsymbol{\mathbb T}^{\rm full,prot}_{\Grand,X}$ is canonical only relative
to that stronger Read policy.
\end{definition}

\begin{remark}[Structural shadow of the revised Grand Tensor]
The object in \Cref{def:grand-tensor} is the tensor denoted
$\boldsymbol{\mathbb T}_{\Grand,X}^{\rm old}$ in
\Cref{sec:relational-completion}.  It remains the canonical answer to the
finite structural reconstruction problem for the original Store cylinder.
The revised Renewal Grand Tensor is obtained by applying this same construction
to the conservative relational process $\mathsf P_X^{\rm rel}$ and retaining
the paired cutoff-polarization data.  Consequently no formula below must be
rewritten merely to preserve the old structural shadow; the superscript
``rel'' is required only when the persistent relation packet is being used.
\end{remark}

\begin{theorem}[Automatic finite operational-history saturation]
\label{thm:automatic-history-saturation}
At every finite cutoff there is a least $r_X$ such that
\[
 \boxed{\rank\mathbb K_{X,r_X}=\rank\mathbb K_{X,r_X+1}.}
\]
At this depth the word span is the whole $\mathcal A_X^{\rm hist}$, and the
panel through depth $r_X+1$ reconstructs the object units, minimal record
algebra, multiplication, involution, conditional predictive core algebras, and
every represented mixed history.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Faithfulness of the regular trace makes the Gram kernel exactly the word
relation space.  The nested word spans stabilize in the finite-dimensional
algebra.  At the first rank equality two consecutive spans have equal
dimension and are equal.  Left multiplication by every generator preserves
the stabilized span; since it contains the units, it contains every generated
word.  The one-step extension records each generator's left multiplication on
a spanning basis, and reversed words reconstruct the involution.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Physical score/localizer descent through flat word relations]
\label{thm:GT-word-localizer-descent}
Let $H=W^*W\succeq0$ be a returned-word Gram on a finite coefficient space,
let $S$ be the synthesis of an independently executable normalized score
family on the same coefficient list, and put $G=S^*S$.  With
$P_H=HH^\dagger$, the following are equivalent:
\[
 \boxed{\Ker H\subseteq\Ker G,}
 \qquad
 \boxed{\Delta_{\rm occ}(H,G):=\Tr((I-P_H)G)=0,}
 \tag{NL.1}
\]
and the existence of a unique positive score localizer on the supported word
quotient.  On this branch its matrix in whitened word coordinates is
\[
 \boxed{\Lambda_H=H^{\dagger/2}GH^{\dagger/2}\succeq0.}
 \tag{NL.2}
\]

Now let $V$ synthesize a bank of all proposed one-letter extensions and write
\[
 H^+=\begin{pmatrix}H&C\\C^*&D\end{pmatrix},
 \qquad
 G^+=\begin{pmatrix}G&J\\J^*&K\end{pmatrix}.
\]
The ordinary word innovation and the reduced word relation are
\[
 \boxed{R_{\rm w}=D-C^*H^\dagger C\succeq0,}
 \qquad T=H^\dagger C.
 \tag{NL.3}
\]
If $R_{\rm w}=0$, then $V=WT$, and the same relation holds in the physical
score experiment exactly when
\[
 \boxed{
 R_{\rm sc}
 =K-T^*J-J^*T+T^*GT
 =(S_1-S_0T)^*(S_1-S_0T)=0.}
 \tag{NL.4}
\]
If $R_{\rm w}\ne0$, the polar synthesis of $(I-P_W)V$ is the canonical
source-minimal new word bank.  Thus a relation is admitted into the loaded
Grand Tensor only when it is simultaneously an ordinary word relation and a
relation of the physical score/action experiment.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
A coefficient vector lies in $\Ker H$ exactly when its synthesized word is
zero.  Since $G=S^*S$, the first inclusion is precisely the condition that the
score synthesis vanish on every zero word.  Positivity makes
$\Tr((I-P_H)G)=0$ equivalent to $(I-P_H)G(I-P_H)=0$ and hence to the same
kernel inclusion.  Whitened synthesis $WH^{\dagger/2}$ is an isometry from the
supported coefficient quotient onto the word range, which gives
\textup{(NL.2)} and uniqueness.

The Moore--Penrose projection formula gives
$R_{\rm w}=V^*(I-P_W)V$ and therefore the rank and polar-innovation
interpretation.  On its zero branch $V=WT$.  Expanding
$(S_1-S_0T)^*(S_1-S_0T)$ gives \textup{(NL.4)}.  Hence zero ordinary
innovation and zero score innovation are exactly the simultaneous flatness
conditions.
\end{proof}


\begin{theorem}[Source-minimal one-letter word/action extension]
\label{thm:GT-word-localizer-extension}
Let $W:E\to\mathcal K$ synthesize the retained words and let
$V:F\to\mathcal K$ synthesize every proposed one-letter extension on the same
physical carrier.  Put
\[
 H=W^*W,\qquad C=W^*V,\qquad D=V^*V,
\]
and, for one positive localizer $L\succeq0$ on that carrier, put
\[
 G=W^*LW,\qquad J=W^*LV,\qquad K=V^*LV.
\]
With
\[
 T=H^\dagger C,\qquad P_W=WH^\dagger W^*,\qquad
 N=(I-P_W)V,
\]
the new word Gram is
\[
 \boxed{R_{\rm w}=D-C^*H^\dagger C=N^*N\succeq0.}
 \tag{NL.4a}
\]
It has
\[
 \boxed{\rank R_{\rm w}
 =\dim\Ran(W,V)-\dim\Ran W,}
 \tag{NL.4b}
\]
and the polar synthesis
\[
 \boxed{\mathcal J_{\rm w}=NR_{\rm w}^{\dagger/2}}
 \tag{NL.4c}
\]
is the unique source-minimal isometry onto the orthogonal new-word range.
In the orthogonal carrier $\Ran W\oplus\Ran N$, the localizer is represented
exactly by
\[
 \boxed{
 \Lambda^+
 =\begin{pmatrix}A&B\\B^*&D_{\rm n}\end{pmatrix}\succeq0,}
 \tag{NL.4d}
\]
where
\[
 A=H^{\dagger/2}GH^{\dagger/2},
 \tag{NL.4e}
\]
\[
 \boxed{B=H^{\dagger/2}(J-GT)R_{\rm w}^{\dagger/2},}
 \tag{NL.4f}
\]
and
\[
 \boxed{
 D_{\rm n}
 =R_{\rm w}^{\dagger/2}
  (K-T^*J-J^*T+T^*GT)
 R_{\rm w}^{\dagger/2}.}
 \tag{NL.4g}
\]
Thus one common old/new word-action panel reconstructs both the exact new
source cost and the complete enlarged localizer.  Neither the mixed block nor
the kernel orientation is inferred from marginal action data.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The Moore--Penrose formula makes $P_W$ the orthogonal projection onto
$\Ran W$.  Since $WT=P_WV$, one has $V=WT+N$ with $W^*N=0$.  Taking Grams
gives \textup{(NL.4a)--(NL.4b)}, and polar decomposition gives
\textup{(NL.4c)}.  The old supported isometry $WH^{\dagger/2}$ and the new
isometry $\mathcal J_{\rm w}$ have orthogonal ranges spanning $\Ran(W,V)$.
Compressing $L$ to these ranges and expanding $(V-WT)^*L(V-WT)$ gives
\textup{(NL.4d)--(NL.4g)}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Exact flat-word/action compatibility]
\label{cor:GT-flat-word-action-compatibility}
The one-letter extension is flat exactly when $R_{\rm w}=0$.  On that branch
$V=WT$, and the action descends through the same word relation exactly when
\[
 \boxed{J=GT,\qquad K=T^*GT.}
 \tag{NL.4h}
\]
Equivalently,
\[
 \boxed{
 \Delta_{\rm act\mid word}^{\rm flat}
 =\|J-GT\|_{\rm HS}^2+\|K-T^*GT\|_{\rm HS}^2=0.}
 \tag{NL.4i}
\]
A positive value is a common-carrier failure: the apparent word relation and
the proposed action panel cannot both be physical on one carrier.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
When $R_{\rm w}=0$, the extension relation is $(-Tf,f)$.  The complete
positive action Gram
$\begin{psmallmatrix}G&J\\J^*&K\end{psmallmatrix}$ descends exactly when it
annihilates every such relation.  Its two block rows give the displayed
identities.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Adaptive source-minimal word/localizer stopping]
\label{thm:GT-adaptive-word-localizer-stop}
Fix a complete finite typed primitive alphabet and every physically admitted
left and right context.  At depth $r$, let $W_r$ span the represented words
and let $V_r$ contain all one-letter extensions.  If
$R_{{\rm w},r}\ne0$, append only its polar bank
\textup{(NL.4c)}; the represented dimension increases by exactly
$\rank R_{{\rm w},r}$.  If
\[
 \boxed{R_{{\rm w},r}=0,}
 \tag{NL.4j}
\]
then the represented span is invariant under every primitive letter, contains
the object units, and is the complete generated word carrier.  The procedure
terminates after at most
$\dim\mathcal A^{\rm hist}-\rank H_0$ strict one-dimensional increments, or
fewer rounds when an innovation has larger rank.

If the localizer blocks are acquired in the same extension panels, the first
zero word innovation is a genuine common-carrier stop only when
\Cref{cor:GT-flat-word-action-compatibility} also passes.  At least one direct
held-out word outside the spanning bank must be tested before operational
exhaustiveness is declared.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The rank increment is \textup{(NL.4b)}.  A zero innovation puts every
one-letter extension of a spanning word back in the current span; induction
then puts every generated word there.  Conversely, a missing generated
direction first appears at a letter whose prefix leaves the represented span,
producing a positive innovation.  Finite dimensionality forces termination.
The action statement is
\Cref{cor:GT-flat-word-action-compatibility}.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Generalized Schur floor-or-soft certificate]
\label{thm:GT-localizer-extension-floor}
For the enlarged localizer
$\Lambda^+=\begin{psmallmatrix}A&B\\B^*&D\end{psmallmatrix}$ and
$\delta\ge0$, put $A_\delta=A-\delta I$.  Then
\[
 \boxed{\Lambda^+\succeq\delta I}
 \tag{NL.4k}
\]
holds exactly when
\[
 \boxed{
 A_\delta\succeq0,\qquad
 \Ran B\subseteq\Ran A_\delta,\qquad
 S_\delta:=D-\delta I-B^*A_\delta^\dagger B\succeq0.}
 \tag{NL.4l}
\]
Under the range condition,
\[
 \boxed{
 \begin{aligned}
 &\left\langle\binom{x}{y},
 (\Lambda^+-\delta I)\binom{x}{y}\right\rangle\\
 &\quad=
 \langle x+A_\delta^\dagger By,
 A_\delta(x+A_\delta^\dagger By)\rangle
 +\langle y,S_\delta y\rangle .
 \end{aligned}}
 \tag{NL.4m}
\]
A negative eigenvector $y$ of $S_\delta$ therefore returns the explicit
physical soft-word witness
\[
 \boxed{(-A_\delta^\dagger By,y).}
 \tag{NL.4n}
\]
If the range condition fails, a vector in $\Ker A_\delta$ coupled to $By$
returns the corresponding range obstruction.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
This is the Moore--Penrose Schur criterion applied to
$\Lambda^+-\delta I$.  Completion of the square gives
\textup{(NL.4m)}.  Positivity of the two terms is equivalent to
\textup{(NL.4l)}, and the minimizing old completion gives the displayed soft
witness.
\end{proof}

\begin{countertheorem}[Action marginals do not determine the localizer kernel]
\label{cth:GT-localizer-marginals-no-kernel}
The positive matrices
\[
 \Lambda_b=\begin{pmatrix}1&b\\b&1\end{pmatrix},
 \qquad -1\le b\le1,
 \tag{NL.4o}
\]
have identical old and new diagonal action marginals.  Nevertheless
$\Lambda_0=I$ has floor one, while
\[
 \Ker\Lambda_1=\Span\{(1,-1)\},\qquad
 \Ker\Lambda_{-1}=\Span\{(1,1)\}.
\]
Thus the mixed old/new action row controls both the existence and the
orientation of a zero mode.  Choosing it after observing a desired projective
ray is a fit, not a prediction.
\end{countertheorem}

\begin{assessment}[Exact common-carrier numerical boundary]
The word/localizer entrance is now a terminating finite alternative.  It
returns a descent defect, a positive word innovation and its polar source, a
flat-action defect, a genuine common-carrier stop, an extended positive floor,
or an explicit soft-word or range witness.  Only after this stop and the
separate source-cyclic localizer audit may the constant kernel, order cone,
quadratic shell, projective ray, and held-out numerical comparisons be used.
The remaining Standard-Model difficulty is therefore literal population of
the physical word/action extension panels and their cutoff transport.
\end{assessment}

\begin{firewall}[Word flatness and localizer cyclicity are different]
\label{fire:GT-word-versus-localizer-flatness}
The preceding theorem reconstructs a positive localizer on the flat word
quotient.  It does not imply that the physical source range reduces that
localizer.  A global spectrum, floor, or kernel is licensed only after the
source-cyclic moment hierarchy generated by repeated localizer action has also
stabilized.  Before that point every reported floor is relative to the current
head and every nonzero moment leakage is a new physical action--Krylov source.
\end{firewall}

\begin{theorem}[Canonical minimal finite-emergence theorem]
\label{thm:grand-emergence}
Every bare finite intervention--renewal datum satisfying the finite consistency
tests determines a canonical minimal structural Renewal Grand Tensor with the
following exact properties.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(E\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item the combs are reconstructed from the probability table rather than
      supplied;
\item the generated ledger is reduced to the unique minimal future-readable
      record, while every actual point Read is preserved;
\item the table-native executable algebra and the minimal linear predictor are
      realization free;
\item the positive comb determines a canonical square-root support-minimal CP
      class, unique up to record-intertwining memory unitaries;
\item the support-minimal process algebra, contextual future quotient, central
      source atlas, and intrinsic regular trace are canonical;
\item the complete word hierarchy is positive, finite flat, and reconstructs
      the represented monoidal $*$-algebra;
\item unread record refinements do not enlarge the minimal tensor, whereas a
      larger readable provenance tensor decomposes as the finite bundle of
      \Cref{thm:record-refinement-bundle};
\item arbitrary unreduced positive factorizations and arbitrary Hilbert metrics
      do not define the structural $C^*$-history algebra;
\item a faithful physical future metric preserves word relations and the
      monoidal algebra, but quantitative conditioning remains metric dependent;
\item direct fringes, infinite-horizon finite memory, autonomous physical
      renewal, and regulator-uniform gaps are separate certificates.
\end{enumerate}
Thus finite structural emergence is unconditional relative to complete finite
operational data and the actual Read interface, not relative to an arbitrary
hidden ledger or a few microscopic constants.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Comb reconstruction is \Cref{thm:comb-tomography}; record minimality and
completion are
\Cref{thm:minimal-record,thm:minimal-read-algebra,thm:operational-record-completion}.
The executable and linear predictive statements are
\Cref{thm:typed-hankel-realization,thm:hankel-minimality,thm:executable-predictive-algebra}.
The minimal CP class is \Cref{thm:canonical-comb-dilation}; the necessity of
support reduction and the metric boundary are
\Cref{cth:nonminimal-factorization,cth:metric-adjoint-no-go}.
The process and contextual algebras are
\Cref{thm:process-representation,thm:contextual-envelope-universal,thm:central-source-decomposition}.
Regular-trace positivity and flatness are
\Cref{thm:regular-trace,thm:automatic-history-saturation}.  Record refinements
are \Cref{thm:record-refinement-bundle}, and physical-metric invariance is
\Cref{thm:metric-independence}.  The final limitations are established in the
cutoff, infinite-horizon, coherence, and autonomous-renewal theorems below.
\end{proof}

\begin{countertheorem}[Degree-one data do not reconstruct multiplication]
\label{cth:pairwise-not-monoidal-new}
There are two finite unital $C^*$-algebra structures on one Hilbert
source-transfer datum with identical degree-one and pairwise source moments,
while one is commutative and the other simple noncommutative.
\end{countertheorem}

\begin{proof}
Take $\mathcal A_1=\C^4$ and $\mathcal A_2=M_2(\C)$ with normalized traces.
Their GNS spaces both have dimension four.  Choose a unitary carrying unit to
unit and transport the second multiplication to the first Hilbert space.  With
source map the identity and transfer $T=I/2$, every pairwise transfer moment is
$2^{-n}I$ in both structures, while the center dimensions are four and one.
\end{proof}


\begin{theorem}[Word-level monoidal transport residual]
\label{thm:GT-monoidal-transport}
Let $\mathcal A$ and $\mathcal B$ be finite source-generated unital
$C^*$-algebras with faithful traces, and let $r_*$ be a common flat word depth.
Choose word bases $(w_\alpha)$ and $(\widetilde w_\alpha)$ through that depth,
and let $U:L^2(\mathcal A)\to L^2(\mathcal B)$ be a unitary carrying the
primitive degree-one source vectors to their proposed images.  Form the
residual synthesis whose columns are
\[
 U1-1,
 \qquad U(w_\alpha^*)-U(w_\alpha)^*,
 \qquad U(w_\alpha w_\beta)-U(w_\alpha)U(w_\beta),
\]
and put
\[
 \boxed{\mathbb I_{\rm mon}(U)=\mathscr R_U^*\mathscr R_U\succeq0.}
 \tag{GT.1}
\]
Then $\mathbb I_{\rm mon}(U)=0$ if and only if $U$ is the $L^2$ extension of a
trace-preserving unital $*$-isomorphism
$\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$.  For composable unital linear maps,
\[
 \boxed{
 R_{VU}(a,b)=V R_U(a,b)+R_V(Ua,Ub),
 \qquad R_U(a,b)=U(ab)-U(a)U(b).}
 \tag{GT.2}
\]
Thus a terminal product defect is the transported sum of the local product
writers.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
If the residual vanishes, $U$ preserves the unit, involution, and products of a
spanning word basis.  Bilinearity and the flat-depth reconstruction extend
these identities to the complete generated algebra, and unitarity preserves
the faithful trace inner product.  The converse is immediate.  The chain rule
is obtained by adding and subtracting $V(Ua) V(Ub)$.
\end{proof}

\begin{countertheorem}[Flat linear holonomy need not be monoidal]
\label{cth:GT-flat-linear-not-monoidal}
There is a two-edge cycle of Hilbert-unitary source transports whose total
linear holonomy is the identity while both edgewise monoidal residuals are
nonzero.
\end{countertheorem}

\begin{proof}
Take $\mathcal A=\C^3$ with its normalized trace.  On the mean-zero real plane
choose a rotation $R$ through an angle which is not induced by a coordinate
permutation, and let $R$ fix the constant vector.  Then $R$ is unitary on
$L^2(\mathcal A)$ but is not an algebra automorphism.  The cycle transports
$R$ and $R^{-1}$ have product $I$, whereas
$\mathbb I_{\rm mon}(R)$ and $\mathbb I_{\rm mon}(R^{-1})$ are positive.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Positive-congruence invariance of the finite algebra]
\label{thm:metric-independence}
Let $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle_0$ be the regular inner product and let
$\mathfrak g_X$ be any faithful physical future form.  There is a unique
$G_X\succ0$ such that
\[
 \mathfrak g_X(a,b)=\langle a,G_Xb\rangle_0,
 \qquad
 \mathbb K^G_{X,r}=W_{X,r}^*G_XW_{X,r}.
\]
If $g_-I\preceq G_X\preceq g_+I$, then
\[
 \boxed{g_-\mathbb K_{X,r}\preceq\mathbb K^G_{X,r}
 \preceq g_+\mathbb K_{X,r}.}
\]
Every faithful physical metric has the same word relations, ranks, flat depth,
unit, involution, multiplication, and history algebra.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Finite-dimensional Riesz representation gives $G_X\succ0$.  Conjugating the
operator bounds by $W_{X,r}$ gives the Gram bounds.  A coefficient vector has
zero physical quadratic form exactly when its synthesized word is zero,
because $G_X$ is positive definite.  Hence the Gram kernels, ranks, and all
relation-based reconstructions agree.
\end{proof}

\section{The degree-one Store shadow and source calculus}
\label{sec:degree-one-source}
% =============================================================================

\begin{theorem}[Predictive completely positive Radon--Nikodym envelope]
\label{thm:RN-envelope}
Let $V:\mathcal H\to\mathcal K\otimes\mathcal E$ be a minimal Stinespring
isometry for a finite UCP map
$\Phi:\mathcal B(\mathcal K)\to\mathcal B(\mathcal H)$.  For
$F\in\mathcal B(\mathcal E)$ define
$\Theta_V(F)(A)=V^*(A\otimes F)V$.  Then
\[
 \boxed{
 \{F:0\preceq F\preceq I\}
 \xrightarrow{\ F\mapsto\Theta_V(F)\ }
 \{\Psi:0\le_{\rm CP}\Psi\le_{\rm CP}\Phi\}}
\]
is an affine order isomorphism.  Finite POVMs correspond bijectively to finite
CP decompositions of $\Phi$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Positive contractions give dominated CP maps directly.  Conversely, the
finite CP Radon--Nikodym theorem gives a positive contraction in the commutant
of the represented system algebra.  For the representation
$A\mapsto A\otimes I_\mathcal E$, the commutant is
$I_\mathcal K\otimes\mathcal B(\mathcal E)$.  Minimality makes the derivative
unique: if $\Theta_V(F)=0$, matrix coefficients between the spanning vectors
$(A\otimes I)V\xi$ force $F=0$.  Summing coordinates proves the POVM claim.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Minimal-realization naturality]
\label{thm:minimal-naturality}
If a physical automorphism satisfies
$U_g^*\Phi(A)U_g=\Phi(Z_g^*AZ_g)$, there is a unique unitary $W_g$ on the
minimal environment such that
\[
 \boxed{(Z_g\otimes W_g)V=VU_g,}
 \qquad
 g\cdot\Theta_V(F)=\Theta_V(W_gFW_g^*).
\]
Projective multipliers obey
$W_gW_h=a(g,h)b(g,h)^{-1}W_{gh}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The isometries $VU_g$ and $(Z_g\otimes I)V$ are minimal dilations of the same
map, so minimal Stinespring uniqueness gives $W_g$.  Successive application
gives the cocycle law, and direct substitution gives the coordinate action.
\end{proof}

\begin{construction}[Degree-one latent source]
\label{con:degree-one-source}
Choose a minimal Stinespring realization of the marked Store channel $\Phi_X$.
For primitive Store-dominated basis ports let $F_{\alpha j,X}$ be their unique
Radon--Nikodym derivatives and put
\[
 \mathcal U_X^{(1)}=\Span_\C\{F_{\alpha j,X}\}_{\alpha,j}.
\]
Let $B_{\alpha,X}$ synthesize these derivatives and
$B_X=\bigoplus_\alpha B_{\alpha,X}$.  A chosen faithful physical future form
has source map $C_X$ and Riesz operator $G_X=C_X^*C_X$ after its null space is
shorted.  The calibrated degree-one pairwise shadow is
\[
 \boxed{\GTX:=B_X^*G_XB_X.}
\]
Its intrinsic regular version is obtained by taking the regular metric.
\end{construction}

\begin{corollary}[Block Cauchy--Schwarz inequality]
\label{cor:block-CS}
For $p\in\mathcal P_{\alpha,X}$ and $q\in\mathcal P_{\beta,X}$,
\[
 \abs{\ip{p}{\mathbb T_{\alpha\beta,X}^{\BR}q}}^2
 \le
 \ip{p}{\mathbb T_{\alpha\alpha,X}^{\BR}p}
 \ip{q}{\mathbb T_{\beta\beta,X}^{\BR}q}.
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Apply Cauchy--Schwarz to $C_XB_{\alpha,X}p$ and
$C_XB_{\beta,X}q$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Exact source Schur residual]
\label{thm:source-Schur}
Let $S_1:E_1\to\mathcal H$ and $S_2:E_2\to\mathcal H$ be finite source maps,
and put
\[
 A=S_1^*S_1,\qquad B=S_1^*S_2,\qquad D=S_2^*S_2.
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathbb G_{2\mid1}:=D-B^*A^\dagger B
 =S_2^*(I-P_1)S_2\succeq0,}
 \qquad P_1=S_1A^\dagger S_1^*,
\]
with
\[
 \mathbb G_{2\mid1}=0\iff\Ran S_2\subseteq\Ran S_1,
\]
and
\[
 \rank\begin{pmatrix}A&B\\B^*&D\end{pmatrix}-\rank A
 =\rank\mathbb G_{2\mid1}.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The Moore--Penrose formula gives the orthogonal projection
$P_1=S_1(S_1^*S_1)^\dagger S_1^*$.  Hence
$B^*A^\dagger B=S_2^*P_1S_2$.  Positivity, the range criterion, and the rank
increment follow from the orthogonal residual $(I-P_1)S_2$.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Joint-source universality, shorting, and score export}
\label{sec:joint-source-universality}

The preceding one-sided Schur residual becomes a complete comparison theorem
when two typed word families are operationally visible in one covered history
experiment.  This is stronger than reconstructing the two marginal sectors
separately.

\begin{definition}[Jointly visible typed source families]
\label{def:jointly-visible-sources}
Let $S_a:E_a\to\mathcal H$ $(a=1,2)$ be finite source syntheses in one
faithful operational history carrier.  They are \emph{jointly visible} when
the admitted word or differentiated-score panel contains every mixed pairing
$\langle S_2y,S_1x\rangle$.  Put
\[
 G_a=S_a^*S_a,
 \qquad C_{21}=S_2^*S_1,
 \qquad
 \mathbb G_{12}=
 \begin{pmatrix}G_1&C_{21}^*\\ C_{21}&G_2\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Separate visibility of $G_1$ and $G_2$ is not joint visibility.
\end{definition}

\begin{countertheorem}[Marginal canonicality does not determine relative orientation]
\label{cth:marginals-no-relative-orientation}
For fixed $G_1,G_2\succeq0$, the positive completions are precisely
\[
 \boxed{C_{21}=G_2^{1/2}KG_1^{1/2},\qquad \|K\|\le1,}
\]
where $K$ acts between the faithful source supports.  Thus two independently
canonical marginal sectors leave a full contraction ball of relative
orientations.
\end{countertheorem}

\begin{proof}
On the faithful supports, positivity of $\mathbb G_{12}$ is equivalent by the
Schur complement to
$G_1-C_{21}^*G_2^{-1}C_{21}\succeq0$.  Hence
$K=G_2^{-1/2}C_{21}G_1^{-1/2}$ is a contraction.  Conversely the factorization
with a contraction makes
$\begin{psmallmatrix}I&K^*\\K&I\end{psmallmatrix}\succeq0$ and therefore
makes the block Gram positive.  Moore--Penrose inverses give the same argument
on nonfaithful supports.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Canonical joint-source universality]
\label{thm:joint-source-universality}
For jointly visible source families, $\mathbb G_{12}$ is a canonical positive
operational coordinate.  The quotient
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal H_{12}^{\min}
 :=(E_1\oplus E_2)/\Ker\mathbb G_{12}}
\]
with inner product
$\langle[u],[v]\rangle=\langle u,\mathbb G_{12}v\rangle$ and synthesis
$S_{12}^{\min}u=[u]$ is source minimal and satisfies
\[
 \boxed{(S_{12}^{\min})^*S_{12}^{\min}=\mathbb G_{12},\qquad
 \dim\mathcal H_{12}^{\min}=\rank\mathbb G_{12}.}
\]
Every other source-minimal common realization with the same four Gram blocks
is related to it by a unique unitary fixing both source families.  The
construction is invariant under support-minimal Stinespring gauge and under
unread record refinements.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Positivity makes the displayed quotient inner product well defined and
positive definite.  The images of the two coefficient summands span the
quotient, so the realization is source minimal and its Gram is the prescribed
block.  If $T_1,T_2$ are another minimal realization, define
$U[S_1x+S_2y]=T_1x+T_2y$.  Equality of the complete block Gram makes this map
well defined and isometric; source minimality makes it onto.  It is unique
because the two source ranges span.  Support-minimal coordinate changes and
unread record refinements preserve every mixed operational pairing, so they
induce the same source-fixing unitary by this uniqueness.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Mutual range tests, normalized transport, and universal short]
\label{thm:joint-source-short}
Let $\Pi_a$ project onto $\Ran S_a$.  The two Schur residuals are
\[
 \boxed{R_{1\mid2}=G_1-C_{21}^*G_2^\dagger C_{21}
 =S_1^*(I-\Pi_2)S_1\succeq0,}
\]
\[
 \boxed{R_{2\mid1}=G_2-C_{21}G_1^\dagger C_{21}^*
 =S_2^*(I-\Pi_1)S_2\succeq0.}
\]
They vanish exactly on the corresponding range inclusions and both vanish
exactly when the source ranges coincide.  The normalized cross transport
\[
 \boxed{K_{21}=G_2^{\dagger/2}C_{21}G_1^{\dagger/2}}
\]
is a contraction; its singular values are the cosines of the principal angles
between the two source ranges.  Moreover the Anderson--Trapp short of
$\mathbb G_{12}$ to $E_1$ is
\[
 \boxed{
 \operatorname{Short}_{E_1}(\mathbb G_{12})
 =\begin{pmatrix}R_{1\mid2}&0\\0&0\end{pmatrix},}
\]
equivalently
\[
 \langle x,R_{1\mid2}x\rangle
 =\inf_{y\in E_2}\langle(x,y),\mathbb G_{12}(x,y)\rangle.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The projection formulas are the Moore--Penrose identities used in
\Cref{thm:source-Schur}.  Whitening gives
$K_{21}=V_2^*V_1$ for the isometric source embeddings
$V_a=S_aG_a^{\dagger/2}$, so it is contractive and has the stated principal
angle interpretation.  Minimizing
$\|S_1x+S_2y\|^2$ over $y$ subtracts the orthogonal projection of $S_1x$ onto
$\Ran S_2$ and yields $\|(I-\Pi_2)S_1x\|^2$, proving the short formula.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Corrected Douglas factor]
\label{thm:corrected-Douglas-factor}
If $R_{1\mid2}=0$, then the unique reduced factor
\[
 \boxed{D_{2\leftarrow1}=G_2^\dagger C_{21}}
\]
satisfies
\[
 \boxed{S_1=S_2D_{2\leftarrow1},\qquad
 D_{2\leftarrow1}^*G_2D_{2\leftarrow1}=G_1.}
\]
Thus it is an isometry for the two canonical source Gram norms.  It need not be
a contraction in arbitrary Euclidean coefficient norms.  The stronger order
\[
 S_1S_1^*\preceq S_2S_2^*
\]
is equivalent to the existence of a factor $S_1=S_2D$ with $\|D\|\le1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Zero residual gives $S_1=\Pi_2S_1=S_2G_2^\dagger S_2^*S_1$, proving the
factorization and uniqueness on $\supp G_2$.  Taking Grams gives the metric
isometry.  The final equivalence is the finite Douglas lemma: factorization by
a contraction implies the operator order; conversely polar reduction on the
range of $S_2$ constructs the contraction.  For example $S_2=1$, $S_1=2$ has
zero residual but reduced factor $2$, showing why range inclusion alone is not
an Euclidean contraction statement.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Simultaneous nuisance short]
\label{thm:simultaneous-nuisance-short}
Let $A:E\to\mathcal H$, $S:E\to\mathcal H$, and $N:F\to\mathcal H$ be
completed, Euler, and common nuisance syntheses with joint Gram blocks
\[
 M=A^*A,\quad \mathbb E=S^*S,\quad B=A^*S,
 \quad G_N=N^*N,\quad C_M=N^*A,\quad C_E=N^*S.
\]
With $P_N=NG_N^\dagger N^*$, put
$\widehat A=(I-P_N)A$ and $\widehat S=(I-P_N)S$.  Then
\[
 \boxed{\widehat M=M-C_M^*G_N^\dagger C_M,}
\]
\[
 \boxed{\widehat{\mathbb E}=\mathbb E-C_E^*G_N^\dagger C_E,}
\]
\[
 \boxed{\widehat B=B-C_M^*G_N^\dagger C_E.}
\]
The block
$\begin{psmallmatrix}\widehat M&\widehat B\\
\widehat B^*&\widehat{\mathbb E}\end{psmallmatrix}$ is positive and is the
short of the three-family Gram to the completed--Euler coefficient space.
Shorting the two marginals separately while leaving $B$ unchanged is generally
incorrect.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The formulas follow by expanding
$A^*(I-P_N)A$, $S^*(I-P_N)S$, and
$A^*(I-P_N)S$.  Their block is the Gram of the two shorted syntheses and is
therefore positive.  The variational characterization of the short follows by
minimizing the joint norm over the nuisance coefficient.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Operational score export and unread-refinement law]
\label{thm:operational-score-export}
Let $p_{\theta,\phi}$ be one finite positive record distribution in which
$\theta$ and $\phi$ deform two declared source families.  At the reference
point put
\[
 s_1=\partial_\theta\log p_{\theta,\phi}|_0,
 \qquad
 s_2=\partial_\phi\log p_{\theta,\phi}|_0.
\]
Then the joint Fisher block
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathbb I_{12}=
 \begin{pmatrix}
 \mathbb E[s_1s_1^*]&\mathbb E[s_1s_2^*]\\
 \mathbb E[s_2s_1^*]&\mathbb E[s_2s_2^*]
 \end{pmatrix}\succeq0}
\]
is the joint source Gram of the score syntheses.  If a fine record is
coarse-grained to a record $R_c$, then
\[
 s_c=\mathbb E[s_f\mid R_c],
 \qquad
 \boxed{
 \mathbb I_f=\mathbb I_c+
 \mathbb E[(s_f-s_c)(s_f-s_c)^*].}
\]
Thus genuinely unread refinements contribute zero joint innovation, while an
informative refinement adds a positive block.  Projecting both source scores
orthogonally away from a nuisance score family gives exactly the simultaneous
short of \Cref{thm:simultaneous-nuisance-short}.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Score centering follows from differentiating normalization.  The displayed
matrix is the Gram of the two score vectors in $L^2(p_0)$.  Differentiating the
coarse probability, which is the sum of the fine probabilities in a fibre,
gives the conditional-expectation identity.  Orthogonal decomposition into a
conditional expectation and a centred fibre contrast gives the covariance
Pythagoras formula.  Linear least-squares projection onto nuisance scores is the
Moore--Penrose Schur short.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Strict joint-source cutoff functor]
\label{thm:joint-source-cutoff-functor}
For $X\le Y$, let $j_{a,Y/X}:E_{a,X}\to E_{a,Y}$ be typed source isometries.
If all four blocks compress,
\[
 \boxed{j_{a,Y/X}^*G_{ab,Y}j_{b,Y/X}=G_{ab,X},
 \qquad a,b\in\{1,2\},}
\]
then there is a unique isometry
\[
 \boxed{\iota_{Y/X}:\mathcal H_{12,X}^{\min}
 \longrightarrow\mathcal H_{12,Y}^{\min}}
\]
satisfying
$\iota_{Y/X}S_{a,X}=S_{a,Y}j_{a,Y/X}$.  These maps compose strictly.  The
normalized transports obey compressed naturality
\[
 \sigma_{2,Y/X}^*K_{21,Y}\sigma_{1,Y/X}=K_{21,X}.
\]
They obey the stronger intertwining relation exactly when
\[
 \boxed{
 \Delta_{21,Y/X}^{\rm new}
 =\|(I-\sigma_{2,Y/X}\sigma_{2,Y/X}^*)
 K_{21,Y}\sigma_{1,Y/X}\|_{\HS}^2=0.}
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Define the cutoff map on Gram-quotient generators by
$[x_1,x_2]\mapsto[j_1x_1,j_2x_2]$.  Compression of the complete block Gram
makes it well defined and isometric; source minimality gives uniqueness.
Agreement on the source generators proves strict composition.  Whitening and
compression give the normalized cross-transport identity.  Decomposing
$K_{21,Y}\sigma_1$ into the old source-$2$ range and its orthogonal complement
shows that the displayed defect is precisely the obstruction to full
intertwining.
\end{proof}



% =============================================================================
\subsection{Cross-record source kernels, source-sufficient records, and transport separation}
\label{sec:source-kernel-record-transport}
% =============================================================================

Let $(\Omega,\nu)$ be one finite physical history law and let
$S_\omega:E\to\mathcal K$ be the pointwise profile of a complete typed source.

\begin{definition}[Complete weighted cross-record source kernel]
\label{def:GT-cross-record-kernel}
The complete source kernel is the positive block matrix
\[
 \boxed{
 (\mathbb K_{\mathcal S})_{\omega\eta}
 =\sqrt{\nu_\omega\nu_\eta}\,S_\omega^*S_\eta.}
 \tag{SK.1}
\]
Its diagonal blocks are the recordwise source energies; its off-diagonal
blocks retain the relative orientation between histories.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Source-minimal kernel realization and uniqueness]
\label{thm:GT-source-kernel-realization}
Every positive block kernel $\mathbb K=[K_{\omega\eta}]\succeq0$ on a faithful
finite law has a realization of the form \textup{(SK.1)}.  The least possible
carrier dimension is $\rank\mathbb K$, and any two source-minimal realizations
are related by one global unitary acting simultaneously on every profile.
The kernel does not determine the probabilities $\nu_\omega$: rescaling
$S_\omega$ by $\sqrt{\nu_\omega/\nu_\omega'}$ leaves $\mathbb K$ unchanged.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Realize $\mathbb K$ by its Gram quotient and divide the $\omega$-th block
synthesis by $\sqrt{\nu_\omega}$.  Gram minimality gives the rank and the
usual source-fixing unitary.  The displayed rescaling proves the final
independence statement.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Exact conditional-source variance and coarsest sufficient record]
\label{thm:GT-source-record-variance}
Let $\mathcal P$ be a partition of $\Omega$.  For $B\in\mathcal P$ put
\[
 \nu_B=\sum_{\omega\in B}\nu_\omega,
 \qquad
 \overline S_B=\nu_B^{-1}\sum_{\omega\in B}\nu_\omega S_\omega.
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{
 G_{\mathcal S}
 =\sum_{B\in\mathcal P}\nu_B\overline S_B^*\overline S_B
 +\mathbb I_{\mathcal S\mid\mathcal P},}
 \tag{SK.2}
\]
where
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathbb I_{\mathcal S\mid\mathcal P}
 =\frac12\sum_{B\in\mathcal P}\frac1{\nu_B}
 \sum_{\omega,\eta\in B}\nu_\omega\nu_\eta
 (S_\omega-S_\eta)^*(S_\omega-S_\eta)\succeq0.}
 \tag{SK.3}
\]
The unique coarsest source-sufficient record identifies exactly those
$\omega,\eta$ for which
$(S_\omega-S_\eta)^*(S_\omega-S_\eta)=0$.  Its innovation rank is the minimum
orthogonal source dimension omitted by the proposed record.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Expand the weighted variance inside each fibre.  Equality of two profiles is
equivalent to vanishing of their positive discrepancy operator.  Finiteness
and the universal property of the joint level-set partition give the coarsest
record statement.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Zero-innovation overlap is pure gauge]
\label{thm:GT-source-overlap-flatness}
Let a connected graph of equal-rank source profiles be realized in one common
carrier.  Whiten the supported profiles and write the normalized overlap on an
edge as $W_{j\leftarrow i}=V_j^*V_i$.  If every edge has zero source-range
innovation in both directions, then all source ranges coincide, every
$W_{j\leftarrow i}$ is unitary, and there are vertex unitaries $Q_i$ such that
\[
 \boxed{W_{j\leftarrow i}=Q_j^*Q_i,
 \qquad W(C)=I\quad\text{for every cycle }C.}
 \tag{SK.4}
\]
Hence nontrivial physical holonomy cannot be inferred from a globally glued
zero-innovation source atlas.  It requires an independent action, unit,
kinetic, return, or intervention transport, or a measured direct-versus-staged
mismatch.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Zero innovation in both directions makes the two whitened isometries have the
same range.  Choose one common isometry $V$ and write $V_i=VQ_i$; then
$V_j^*V_i=Q_j^*Q_i$, whose cycle products telescope.
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[Incidence is not dynamics]
\label{fire:GT-incidence-not-dynamics}
The complete source kernel determines linear incidence and record sufficiency.
It does not determine a semigroup, connection, conductance, writer law, or
physical-time generator.  Those objects require their own same-history panel.
In particular a nonflat physical connection may coexist with a trivial
source-overlap atlas.
\end{firewall}


\begin{theorem}[Chronological source first birth, common response, and dynamic-head promotion]
\label{thm:GT-source-terminal-nonduplication}
Let $S_j:E_j\to\mathcal H_{\rm src}$ $(1\le j\le N)$ be a chronological
family of completely assembled same-history source maps.  Write
$G_{mn}=S_m^*S_n$, and use $G_{j,<j}$ and $G_{<j,<j}$ for the corresponding
row and principal block of the complete chronological source Gram.  Let
$\mathcal M_{j-1}=\overline{\Ran(S_1\ \cdots\ S_{j-1})}$ and let
$P_{j-1}^{\rm src}$ be its orthogonal projection.  Define
\[
 F_j=(I-P_{j-1}^{\rm src})S_j.
\]
Then the fresh source Gram is the Moore--Penrose Schur innovation
\[
 \boxed{
 F_j^*F_j
 =G_{jj}-G_{j,<j}G_{<j,<j}^{\dagger}G_{<j,j}\succeq0,}
 \tag{JS.1}
\]
and the ranges $\Ran F_j$ are mutually orthogonal.

Let $\mathcal R:\mathcal H_{\rm src}\to\mathcal Y$ be one normalized physical
terminal response, and put
$\mathcal Y_{j-1}=\overline{\mathcal R\mathcal M_{j-1}}$ with projection
$P_{j-1}^{\rm term}$.  Then
\[
 \boxed{
 (I-P_{j-1}^{\rm term})\mathcal R P_{j-1}^{\rm src}=0.}
 \tag{JS.2}
\]
Thus an old source cannot create a genuinely new terminal direction under one
fixed common response.

Let $\mathcal K_-\subseteq\mathcal K_+$ be two protocol-fixed represented
terminal heads containing $\mathcal Y_{j-1}$, with projections
$\Pi_-\le\Pi_+$.  If $\mathcal R$ is contractive, the current source has the
exact five-arm decomposition
\[
 \boxed{
 \begin{aligned}
 \|S_j\|_{\rm HS}^2={}&
 \|P_{j-1}^{\rm src}S_j\|_{\rm HS}^2
 +\|\Pi_-\mathcal RF_j\|_{\rm HS}^2\\
 &+\|(\Pi_+-\Pi_-)\mathcal RF_j\|_{\rm HS}^2
 +\|(I-\Pi_+)\mathcal RF_j\|_{\rm HS}^2\\
 &+\|(I-\mathcal R^*\mathcal R)^{1/2}F_j\|_{\rm HS}^2.
 \end{aligned}}
 \tag{JS.3}
\]
These terms are respectively source reuse, fresh source represented by the old
head, fresh source promoted into the enlarged head, fresh irreducible terminal
response, and fresh response-null source.  The nested-head residuals obey
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal R^*(I-\Pi_-)\mathcal R
 =\mathcal R^*(\Pi_+-\Pi_-)\mathcal R
  +\mathcal R^*(I-\Pi_+)\mathcal R.}
 \tag{JS.4}
\]
Hence a provisional terminal birth which later enters the represented head is
reclassified as one promotion and cannot be charged twice.

For
\[
 L_j=(I-\Pi_+)\mathcal R|_{\Ran F_j},
 \qquad C_j=L_jL_j^*,
 \qquad q_j=L_jF_j,
\]
the only new irreducible source action is
\[
 \boxed{
 d_j^{\rm bi}
 =\Tr\!\bigl[q_j^*C_j^{\dagger}q_j\bigr]
 =\min_{L_jH=q_j}\|H\|_{\rm HS}^2
 \le\|F_j\|_{\rm HS}^2.}
 \tag{JS.5}
\]
Consequently
\[
 \boxed{\sum_{j=1}^N d_j^{\rm bi}
 \le\sum_{j=1}^N\|F_j\|_{\rm HS}^2
 \le\|S_{1:N}\|_{\rm HS}^2,}
 \tag{JS.6}
\]
where $S_{1:N}=(S_1\ \cdots\ S_N)$ is the completely assembled
chronological source synthesis.  Only a direction which is both source fresh
and terminal new after the final
dynamic head is eligible for an independent repeated-event charge.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The Schur formula is the Gram of the orthogonal residual
$(I-P_{j-1}^{\rm src})S_j$; the cumulative source projections make the fresh
ranges orthogonal.  Equation~\textup{(JS.2)} follows from
$\mathcal R\mathcal M_{j-1}=\mathcal Y_{j-1}$.  For the fresh source, decompose
its terminal image by the three mutually orthogonal projections
$\Pi_-$, $\Pi_+-\Pi_-$, and $I-\Pi_+$, and use
$\|F_j\|_{\rm HS}^2=\|\mathcal RF_j\|_{\rm HS}^2+
\|(I-\mathcal R^*\mathcal R)^{1/2}F_j\|_{\rm HS}^2$.
This proves \textup{(JS.3)}--\textup{(JS.4)}.  The Moore--Penrose minimum-norm
theorem gives \textup{(JS.5)}, and orthogonality of the source-first-birth
ranges gives \textup{(JS.6)}.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Source-core comparison, semigroup transport, and common-action routers}
\label{sec:source-core-comparison}

The finite joint-source calculus above compares source ranges.  The following
package compares an ambient generator with a proposed source compression.  It
is domain independent and applies equally to finite loaded sectors, unbounded
continuum generators, and cutoff families.

\begin{theorem}[Exact source-core Pythagorean comparison]
\label{thm:source-core-Pythagoras}
Let $E,H$ be Hilbert spaces, let $V:E\to H$ be an isometry, and put
$P=VV^*$.  Let $A$ and $N$ be closed densely defined operators on $E$ and $H$
with
\[
 V\mathcal D(A)\subseteq\mathcal D(N).
\]
On $\mathcal D(A)$ define
\[
 R:=NV-VA,
 \qquad
 L:=(I-P)NV,
 \qquad
 C:=V^*NV-A.
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{R=L+VC,\qquad \Ran L\perp\Ran(VC),}
\]
and for all $x,y\in\mathcal D(A)$,
\[
 \boxed{
 \langle Rx,Ry\rangle_H
 =\langle Lx,Ly\rangle_H+\langle Cx,Cy\rangle_E.}
\]
Equivalently, on the graph Hilbert space $\mathcal D(A)_A$,
\[
 \boxed{R^*R=L^*L+C^*C}
\]
as a bounded quadratic-form identity.  In particular,
\[
 \boxed{
 \|NVx-VAx\|^2
 =\|(I-P)NVx\|^2+\|V^*NVx-Ax\|^2.}
\]
Thus zero leakage and zero compression mismatch are equivalent to
\[
 \boxed{NV=VA\quad\text{on }\mathcal D(A).}
\]
If $\mathcal C\subseteq\mathcal D(A)$ is an $A$-core, it is enough that both
defects vanish on $\mathcal C$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Since $P=VV^*$,
\[
 NV-VA=(I-P)NV+P NV-VA=L+V(V^*NV-A)=L+VC.
\]
The first summand lies in $(\Ran V)^\perp$ and the second in $\Ran V$, proving
orthogonality and the inner-product identity.  The map
$NV:\mathcal D(A)_A\to H$ is closed: if $x_n\to x$ in graph norm and
$NVx_n\to y$, then $Vx_n\to Vx$ and closedness of $N$ gives $Vx\in\mathcal
D(N)$ and $NVx=y$.  The closed graph theorem therefore makes $NV$, and hence
$L,C,R$, bounded on the graph Hilbert space.  The quadratic-form identity
follows by polarization.

If the defects vanish on an $A$-core and $x\in\mathcal D(A)$, choose
$x_n\in\mathcal C$ with $x_n\to x$ and $Ax_n\to Ax$.  Then
$NVx_n=VAx_n\to VAx$.  Closedness of $N$ yields $NVx=VAx$.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Norm discipline]
The Pythagorean identity is exact pointwise, in Hilbert--Schmidt norm, and in
any weighted trace-source norm.  For operator norm one has the sharp general
bounds
\[
 \max\{\|L\|,\|C\|\}\le\|R\|
 \le\sqrt{\|L\|^2+\|C\|^2};
\]
an operator-norm equality with the sum of squares need not hold.
\end{remark}

\begin{theorem}[Generator, resolvent, and semigroup intertwining]
\label{thm:source-core-semigroup}
In the setting of \Cref{thm:source-core-Pythagoras}, suppose $A$ and $N$
generate strongly continuous semigroups $S(t)$ and $T(t)$.  Then
\[
 \boxed{NV=VA\text{ on }\mathcal D(A)
 \iff T(t)V=VS(t)\text{ for every }t\ge0.}
\]
For $z\in\rho(N)\cap\rho(A)$ the exact defect identity is
\[
 \boxed{
 (z-N)^{-1}V-V(z-A)^{-1}
 =(z-N)^{-1}R(z-A)^{-1}.}
\]
If $R:\mathcal D(A)_A\to H$ is graph bounded, then for
$x\in\mathcal D(A)$,
\[
 \boxed{
 T(t)Vx-VS(t)x
 =\int_0^tT(t-s)R S(s)x\,\dd s.}
\]
Consequently, if
$\|T(t)\|\le M_Ne^{\omega_Nt}$ and
$\|S(t)\|_{\mathcal D(A)_A\to\mathcal D(A)_A}
 \le M_Ae^{\omega_At}$, then
\[
 \boxed{
 \|T(t)V-VS(t)\|_{\mathcal D(A)_A\to H}
 \le M_NM_A\Phi_t(\omega_N,\omega_A)
      \sqrt{\Delta_{\rm leak}+\Delta_{\rm comp}},}
\]
where
\[
 \Phi_t(\omega_N,\omega_A)
 :=\int_0^te^{\omega_N(t-s)+\omega_As}\,\dd s,
\]
$\Delta_{\rm leak}=\|L\|^2$, and
$\Delta_{\rm comp}=\|C\|^2$ in graph norm.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
If $NV=VA$, then for sufficiently large $\operatorname{Re}z$,
$(z-N)V=V(z-A)$ on $\mathcal D(A)$; inversion gives
$(z-N)^{-1}V=V(z-A)^{-1}$.  Equality of Laplace transforms gives the
semigroup intertwining.  Conversely, differentiating at $t=0$ on
$\mathcal D(A)$ gives the generator relation.

For a nonzero defect, multiply
$(z-N)V-V(z-A)=-R$ by the two resolvents to obtain the displayed resolvent
identity.  Differentiating
$T(t-s)VS(s)x$ in $s$ gives
$-T(t-s)RS(s)x$; integration from $0$ to $t$ gives Duhamel's formula.  The
norm estimate follows from the semigroup bounds and
\Cref{thm:source-core-Pythagoras}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Quantitative history-Gram transport]
\label{cor:source-core-Gram-transport}
Let $S_0:K\to\mathcal D(A)_A$ be bounded and, on a finite time window, put
\[
 B_N(t)=T(t)VS_0,
 \qquad
 B_A(t)=VS(t)S_0.
\]
If $\eta_t=\|B_N(t)-B_A(t)\|$, then
\[
 \boxed{
 \|B_N(t)^*B_N(t)-B_A(t)^*B_A(t)\|
 \le(\|B_N(t)\|+\|B_A(t)\|)\eta_t.}
\]
Moreover the two mutual source Schur residuals are bounded by
$\eta_t^2I$.  Hence, for a cutoff family with uniform graph and semigroup
bounds and
\[
 \Delta_{{\rm leak},X}+\Delta_{{\rm comp},X}\longrightarrow0,
\]
every finite time-window, Krylov, or atomic Hankel Gram obeys
\[
 \boxed{G_{A,X}\preceq G_{N,X}+o(1)I,}
\]
and the mutual source innovations are $o(1)$ at the quadratic defect rate.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Write $B_N=B_A+E$.  Then
$B_N^*B_N-B_A^*B_A=B_A^*E+E^*B_A+E^*E$, which gives the norm estimate in its
symmetric form.  The component of either source orthogonal to the other source
range is the orthogonal projection of $E$, and therefore has norm at most
$\eta_t$; \Cref{thm:source-Schur} gives the Schur bounds.  Apply
\Cref{thm:source-core-semigroup} uniformly and integrate or stack finitely many
times to obtain the cutoff statement.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Common-action Hessian, Schur residual, and Ward router]
\label{thm:common-action-router}
Let $\mathscr A$ be a $C^2$ nonnegative functional of two Hilbert variables
$(\theta,\phi)$ and suppose at a reference point it has a positive Hessian
\[
 H=
 \begin{pmatrix}
 G_\Gamma&C\\ C^*&G_E
 \end{pmatrix}\succeq0.
\]
Equivalently, for the square-root source maps
$B_\Gamma=H^{1/2}|_{X_\Gamma}$ and
$B_E=H^{1/2}|_{X_E}$,
\[
 G_\Gamma=B_\Gamma^*B_\Gamma,
 \qquad C=B_\Gamma^*B_E,
 \qquad G_E=B_E^*B_E.
\]
Assume $\Ran B_\Gamma$ is closed and define
\[
 K=G_\Gamma^\dagger C,
 \qquad
 \mathsf S_E=G_E-C^*G_\Gamma^\dagger C.
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathsf S_E=B_E^*(I-P_\Gamma)B_E\succeq0,}
\]
\[
 \boxed{
 \langle y,\mathsf S_Ey\rangle
 =\inf_x\left\langle\binom{x}{y},H\binom{x}{y}\right\rangle,}
\]
and
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathsf S_E=0
 \iff B_E=B_\Gamma K
 \iff G_E=K^*G_\Gamma K.}
\]
If a source-native infinitesimal symmetry has graph direction
$\mathcal R_Wy=(-Wy,y)$ and the Ward identity gives
$H\mathcal R_W=0$, then
\[
 \boxed{C=G_\Gamma W,
 \qquad G_E=W^*G_\Gamma W,
 \qquad K=W,
 \qquad\mathsf S_E=0.}
\]
Thus the mixed block and router are derivatives of one action rather than an
independently loaded comparison.

If instead
$0\preceq\mathcal R_W^*H\mathcal R_W\preceq\varepsilon^2I$, then
\[
 \boxed{0\preceq\mathsf S_E\preceq\varepsilon^2I.}
\]
If additionally $G_\Gamma\succeq m^2I$ on its support, then
\[
 \boxed{
 \|K-W\|\le \frac{\sqrt{\|H\|}}{m^2}\,\varepsilon.}
\]
In the source-fixing case $W=I$, this gives
$K=I+O(\varepsilon)$ and
$G_E\preceq G_\Gamma+O(\varepsilon)I$ under uniform upper metric bounds.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Let $P_\Gamma$ project onto $\Ran B_\Gamma$.  Moore--Penrose calculus gives
$B_\Gamma G_\Gamma^\dagger B_\Gamma^*=P_\Gamma$, hence
\[
 C^*G_\Gamma^\dagger C
 =B_E^*P_\Gamma B_E.
\]
This proves the source form of the Schur residual.  Minimizing
$\|B_\Gamma x+B_Ey\|^2$ over $x$ subtracts the orthogonal projection of
$B_Ey$ onto $\Ran B_\Gamma$, proving the variational identity and the exact
range criterion.

If $H\mathcal R_W=0$, its two block rows are
$-G_\Gamma W+C=0$ and $-C^*W+G_E=0$, giving the Ward formulas.  For the
approximate statement, the variational formula implies
$\mathsf S_E\preceq\mathcal R_W^*H\mathcal R_W$.  Also
$\|H\mathcal R_W\|^2\le\|H\|\,\|H^{1/2}\mathcal R_W\|^2
\le\|H\|\varepsilon^2$.  The first block row gives
$G_\Gamma(K-W)=C-G_\Gamma W$, and inversion on the supported range yields the
router estimate.  Expanding $K^*G_\Gamma K$ about $W$ gives the final Gram
bound.
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[What common action does not supply]
A zero Schur residual gives an intrinsic source-metric isometry, not equality
of arbitrary coefficient-space Euclidean metrics.  Domination by a specified
marginal requires either a source-fixing Ward symmetry, protected anchor and
metric normalization, or a separately proved metric contraction.  Likewise,
the abstract theorem does not construct a domain's action, source core, or
uniform closed-range margin.
\end{firewall}



% =============================================================================
\subsection{Physical secants, protected influence, and effective actions}
\label{sec:physical-secants-effective-actions}
% =============================================================================

The preceding common-action theorem starts from a differentiated positive
functional.  In applications, however, the first physical data may consist only
of finitely many neighbouring laws or deterministic response values.  The
following results separate finite secant geometry, a physical tangent, and a
dynamical action.  This order prevents an arbitrarily chosen interpolation or
positive operator from being promoted to a source-native action.

\begin{definition}[Hellinger source bank]
\label{def:GT-Hellinger-bank}
Let $\Omega$ be finite and let $p_0,p_1,\ldots,p_m$ be full-support
probability laws on $\Omega$.  Put
\[
 \mathfrak h(p):=2\sqrt p\in\ell^2(\Omega),
 \qquad v_a:=\mathfrak h(p_a)-\mathfrak h(p_0),
\]
where the square root is taken coordinatewise.  The Hellinger source synthesis
is
\[
 V_{\rm Hel}:\C^m\longrightarrow\ell^2(\Omega),
 \qquad V_{\rm Hel}c=\sum_{a=1}^mc_av_a,
\]
and its finite secant Gram is
\[
 \boxed{G_{\rm Hel}:=V_{\rm Hel}^*V_{\rm Hel}\succeq0.}
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Finite secant geometry, nuisance shorting, and Fisher limit]
\label{thm:GT-Hellinger-Fisher}
The construction in \Cref{def:GT-Hellinger-bank} has the following properties.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2.8em]
\item For any two full-support laws,
      \[
       \boxed{
       \|\mathfrak h(p)-\mathfrak h(q)\|_2^2
       =8\left(1-\sum_{\omega\in\Omega}\sqrt{p(\omega)q(\omega)}\right).}
      \]
\item If $V_{\rm Hel}=[N\ S]$ is split into nuisance and retained secants, then
      the efficient retained Gram is exactly
      \[
       \boxed{
       G_{S\mid N}^{\rm Hel}
       =S^*(I-P_N)S
       =G_{SS}-G_{SN}G_{NN}^{\dagger}G_{NS}\succeq0,}
      \]
      where $P_N=N(N^*N)^\dagger N^*$.
\item Let $\theta\mapsto p_\theta$ be an independently physical $C^1$ family
      with $p_0=p_{\theta=0}$ and score
      $s_j=\partial_{\theta_j}\log p_\theta|_0$.  Then
      \[
       \boxed{
       \partial_{\theta_j}\mathfrak h(p_\theta)|_0
       =\sqrt{p_0}\,s_j,}
      \qquad
       \boxed{
       \left\langle\partial_i\mathfrak h,
       \partial_j\mathfrak h\right\rangle
       =\mathbb E_{p_0}[s_i\overline{s_j}].}
      \]
\item For a physical $C^2$ family $p_{\alpha,\beta}$ with nuisance score bank
      $N$ and retained score bank $S$, assume the profile is local at
      $(\alpha,\beta)=(0,0)$ and second-order regular: minimization over the
      local nuisance branch commutes with the quadratic Taylor germ (as it
      does, for example, for a locally identifiable interior nuisance branch).
      Then the locally profiled relative entropy
      \[
       \mathcal I_{\rm prof}(\beta)
       :=\inf_{\alpha\ {m near}\ 0}
       D(p_{\alpha,\beta}\Vert p_{0,0})
      \]
      has Hessian
      \[
       \boxed{
       D^2\mathcal I_{\rm prof}(0)
       =S^*(I-P_N)S.}
      \]
\end{enumerate}
Thus an actual shrinking family converts the canonical finite secant geometry
into the efficient Fisher action, while a finite secant by itself does not
select a tangent or generator.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The first identity is the direct expansion
\[
 4\sum_\omega(\sqrt{p(\omega)}-\sqrt{q(\omega)})^2
 =8-8\sum_\omega\sqrt{p(\omega)q(\omega)}.
\]
The second assertion is the orthogonal projection formula and the
Moore--Penrose identity for the Anderson--Trapp short.  Differentiating
$2\sqrt{p_\theta}$ gives
$\partial_j(2\sqrt p)=p^{-1/2}\partial_jp=\sqrt p\,s_j$, which proves the
third assertion.  Finally,
\[
 D(p_{\alpha,\beta}\Vert p_{0,0})
 =\frac12\left\|N\alpha+S\beta\right\|_{L^2(p_0)}^2
  +o(\|\alpha\|^2+\|\beta\|^2).
\]
Minimizing the quadratic term over $\alpha$ subtracts the orthogonal
projection onto $\Ran N$ and gives the displayed Schur short.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Physical score occurrence, one-sided tomography, and absolute pressure]
\label{thm:GT-score-pressure}
Let $w_\theta(\omega)>0$ be an independently executable finite family of
unnormalized weights,
\[
 Z(\theta)=\sum_\omega w_\theta(\omega),
 \qquad p_\theta=Z(\theta)^{-1}w_\theta,
\]
and define
\[
 a_i=\partial_i\log w_\theta|_0,
 \qquad b_{ij}=\partial_i\partial_j\log w_\theta|_0,
 \qquad s_i=a_i-\mathbb E_0a_i.
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{\mathbb I_{ij}=\mathbb E_0[s_is_j]\succeq0,}
 \tag{NL.5}
\]
\[
 \boxed{
 \partial_i\partial_j\log Z(0)
 =\mathbb E_0[b_{ij}]+\mathbb I_{ij}.}
 \tag{NL.6}
\]
For $w_\theta=e^{-A_\theta}$ this is
\[
 \boxed{
 \partial_i\partial_j\log Z(0)
 =-\mathbb E_0[A_{ij}]
  +\operatorname{Cov}_0(A_i,A_j).}
 \tag{NL.7}
\]
The covariance is the positive score localizer; the direct second-action row
is independent and need not be positive.

Let $\mathfrak h(\theta)=2\sqrt{p_\theta}$ and, for a physically executable
one-sided probe, put
\[
 q_\varepsilon(u)
 =\varepsilon^{-2}\|\mathfrak h(\varepsilon u)-\mathfrak h(0)\|^2,
\]
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathbb I_\varepsilon(x,y)
 =\frac12\bigl(q_\varepsilon(x+y)-q_\varepsilon(x)-q_\varepsilon(y)\bigr).}
 \tag{NL.8}
\]
Then $\mathbb I_\varepsilon(x,y)\to\mathbb I(x,y)$.  If
$\|D\mathfrak h(0)u\|\le L\|u\|$ and
$\|D^2\mathfrak h(tu)[u,u]\|\le M\|u\|^2$ on the probe interval, then
\[
 \boxed{
 |\mathbb I_\varepsilon(x,y)-\mathbb I(x,y)|
 \le\frac12\sum_{u\in\{x,y,x+y\}}
 \left(ML\varepsilon\|u\|^3
 +\frac{M^2\varepsilon^2}{4}\|u\|^4\right).}
 \tag{NL.9}
\]
Thus the mixed positive localizer is reconstructed from actual neighbouring
laws with a finite error certificate, while the absolute pressure requires the
unnormalized partition/action experiment.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Differentiating $Z$ gives
$\partial_i\log Z=\mathbb E_0a_i$.  A second derivative separates the direct
expectation of $b_{ij}$ from the covariance of $a_i,a_j$, proving
\textup{(NL.6)} and \textup{(NL.7)}.  Differentiating
$2\sqrt{p_\theta}$ gives $D\mathfrak h(0)[u]=\sqrt{p_0}s_u$, so its Gram is
\textup{(NL.5)}.  Taylor's formula writes
$\mathfrak h(\varepsilon u)-\mathfrak h(0)
=\varepsilon D\mathfrak h(0)u+r_u$ with
$\|r_u\|\le M\varepsilon^2\|u\|^2/2$.  Expanding the squared norm and applying
Cauchy--Schwarz gives the summand in \textup{(NL.9)}; polarization yields
\textup{(NL.8)}.
\end{proof}

\begin{countertheorem}[Normalized laws do not determine absolute pressure]
\label{cth:GT-normalized-no-pressure}
For any smooth scalar $c(\theta)$ with $c(0)=0$, the family
$\widetilde w_\theta=e^{c(\theta)}w_\theta$ has exactly the same normalized
laws and score localizer as $w_\theta$, while
\[
 \boxed{
 D^2\log\widetilde Z(0)
 =D^2\log Z(0)+D^2c(0).}
 \tag{NL.10}
\]
Hence normalized tomography and one base partition value do not determine the
absolute pressure Hessian, volume curvature, or measure modulus.
\end{countertheorem}

\begin{proof}
The scalar factor cancels in normalization and adds $c(\theta)$ to
$\log Z(\theta)$.  Differentiation gives the claim.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Exact cutoff information-loss Gram for physical scores]
\label{thm:GT-score-cutoff-loss}
Let $\pi:\Omega_Y\to\Omega_X$ be a deterministic physical coarse graining,
let $J_{Y/X}f=f\circ\pi$ be the isometric pullback, and let
$A_{Y/X}:E_X\to E_Y$ transport deformation coefficients.  If $S_Y$ is the
fine centered score synthesis, then the coarse synthesis is
\[
 \boxed{S_X=J_{Y/X}^*S_YA_{Y/X}.}
 \tag{NL.11}
\]
The score localizers obey the exact Pythagoras
\[
 \boxed{
 A_{Y/X}^*\mathbb I_YA_{Y/X}
 =\mathbb I_X+\mathbb R_{Y/X}^{\rm loss},}
 \tag{NL.12}
\]
where
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathbb R_{Y/X}^{\rm loss}
 =(S_YA_{Y/X})^*(I-J_{Y/X}J_{Y/X}^*)S_YA_{Y/X}\succeq0.}
 \tag{NL.13}
\]
It vanishes exactly when every transported fine score is measurable on the
coarse cylinder.  For three nested deterministic cutoffs the losses telescope
as orthogonal martingale increments.  If the complete joint nuisance and
retained score bank has zero loss, simultaneous nuisance shorting commutes with
cutoff transport.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Conditional expectation gives the coarse score and is the orthogonal
projection $J_{Y/X}J_{Y/X}^*$ in $L^2(p_Y)$.  Decomposing a transported fine
score into its conditional expectation and fibre-centred remainder proves
\textup{(NL.12)--(NL.13)}.  Nested conditional expectations give the orthogonal
three-level decomposition.  Applying the same isometry to the complete joint
score bank transports its orthogonal nuisance projection and hence its Schur
short.
\end{proof}

\begin{countertheorem}[Finite endpoint laws do not determine a physical tangent]
\label{cth:GT-secant-no-tangent}
Two full-support $C^1$ paths can have the same initial and terminal laws and
different derivatives at the initial point.  Consequently no tangent, score,
or dynamical action is determined by two endpoint laws alone.
\end{countertheorem}

\begin{proof}
On the two-point space take $p_0=(1/2,1/2)$ and
$p_1=(1/2+\delta,1/2-\delta)$ with $0<\delta<1/4$.  The linear path
$p_t=p_0+t(p_1-p_0)$ and, for sufficiently small nonzero $\eta$, the path
\[
 q_t=p_t+\eta t(1-t)(1,-1)
\]
remain full support and have the same endpoints.  Their initial derivatives
differ by $\eta(1,-1)$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Protected-observable Riesz theorem]
\label{thm:GT-protected-Riesz}
Let $L\succeq0$ act on a finite-dimensional Hilbert space $H$, and let
$E:K\to H$ satisfy $\Ran E\subseteq\Ran L$.  Define
\[
 \boxed{\mathcal R_E(L):=E^*L^\dagger E\succeq0.}
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{
 \|E^*v\|^2
 \le \|\mathcal R_E(L)\|\,\langle v,Lv\rangle
 \qquad(v\perp\Ker L),}
\]
and the constant is optimal.  If $c$ is a unit eigenvector of
$\mathcal R_E(L)$ with eigenvalue $\lambda>0$, then
\[
 z=\lambda^{-1}L^\dagger Ec
\]
satisfies
\[
 \boxed{E^*z=c,\qquad \langle z,Lz\rangle=\lambda^{-1}.}
\]
Thus an unbounded influence sequence is equivalent to a unit protected output
whose action tends to zero.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Since $E=L^{1/2}L^{\dagger/2}E$,
\[
 \|E^*v\|^2
 =\|(L^{\dagger/2}E)^*L^{1/2}v\|^2
 \le\|E^*L^\dagger E\|\,\langle v,Lv\rangle.
\]
Taking $v=L^\dagger Ec$ for a top eigenvector gives equality after scaling.
The displayed identities for $z$ follow from
$E^*L^\dagger Ec=\lambda c$ and
$LL^\dagger E=E$.
\end{proof}


\begin{definition}[Reverse influence and target-normalized source coercivity]
\label{def:GT-reverse-influence}
Let $B,C\succeq0$ act on one finite source carrier, with $C\ne0$.  Define
\[
 \boxed{
 \Lambda(B,C):=\inf\{\Lambda\ge0:C\preceq\Lambda B\},}
 \tag{RI.1}
\]
with value $+\infty$ when no finite order constant exists, and define
\[
 \boxed{
 \mu_C(B):=\inf\{\langle x,Bx\rangle:\langle x,Cx\rangle=1\}.}
 \tag{RI.2}
\]
The first quantity is the optimal reverse influence of the protected target
through the source action; the second is its target-normalized coercive floor.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Exact source-coercivity/inverse-influence duality]
\label{thm:GT-source-coercivity-influence}
For the packet of \Cref{def:GT-reverse-influence}:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2.8em]
\item
\[
 \boxed{\Lambda(B,C)<\infty\iff\Ker B\subseteq\Ker C.}
 \tag{RI.3}
\]
\item On the finite branch,
\[
 \boxed{
 \Lambda(B,C)
 =\|B^{\dagger/2}CB^{\dagger/2}\|
 =\sup_{x\notin\Ker B}
   \frac{\langle x,Cx\rangle}{\langle x,Bx\rangle}.}
 \tag{RI.4}
\]
\item With the conventions $1/0=+\infty$ and $1/(+\infty)=0$,
\[
 \boxed{\mu_C(B)=\Lambda(B,C)^{-1}.}
 \tag{RI.5}
\]
\item If $0<\Lambda(B,C)<\infty$, a target-normalized extremizer exists and
satisfies, on the supported quotient,
\[
 \boxed{
 \langle z,Cz\rangle=1,
 \qquad
 \langle z,Bz\rangle=\Lambda(B,C)^{-1},
 \qquad
 Bz=\Lambda(B,C)^{-1}Cz.}
 \tag{RI.6}
\]
If $\Lambda(B,C)=+\infty$, there is instead a nonzero target-visible source
null $z$ with $Bz=0$ and $\langle z,Cz\rangle>0$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The order inequality implies the kernel inclusion.  Conversely, the inclusion
forces $C$ to be supported on $\supp B$, where $B$ is positive definite, and
there
\[
 C\preceq\|B^{-1/2}CB^{-1/2}\|B.
\]
Whitening by $B^{1/2}$ gives the Rayleigh quotient in \textup{(RI.4)}.
Homogeneity gives
\[
 \inf_{\langle x,Cx\rangle=1}\langle x,Bx\rangle
 =\left(
   \sup_{\langle x,Bx\rangle>0}
   \frac{\langle x,Cx\rangle}{\langle x,Bx\rangle}
  \right)^{-1},
\]
which proves \textup{(RI.5)}.  A top eigenvector of
$B^{\dagger/2}CB^{\dagger/2}$ gives the extremizer; the Euler--Lagrange
equation gives \textup{(RI.6)}.  Failure of the kernel inclusion supplies the
stated exact target-visible null.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Protected target-short reduction]
\label{thm:GT-target-short-influence}
Let $K=\supp C$ and write, relative to $K\oplus K^\perp$,
\[
 B=\begin{pmatrix}A&D\\D^*&E\end{pmatrix}\succeq0.
\]
The protected short
\[
 \boxed{S_K(B):=A-DE^\dagger D^*\succeq0}
 \tag{RI.7}
\]
satisfies
\[
 \boxed{
 \Lambda(B,C)=\Lambda(S_K(B),C|_K),
 \qquad
 \mu_C(B)=\mu_{C|_K}(S_K(B)).}
 \tag{RI.8}
\]
If
\[
 mP_K\preceq C\preceq MP_K,
 \qquad 0<m\le M<\infty,
\]
and $\beta_K(B)=\lambda_{\min}(S_K(B))$, then
\[
 \boxed{
 \frac{m}{\beta_K(B)}
 \le\Lambda(B,C)
 \le\frac{M}{\beta_K(B)},}
 \tag{RI.9}
\]
with the usual infinite convention when $\beta_K(B)=0$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
For $x=y+v$, with $y\in K$ and $v\in K^\perp$, the target energy depends only
on $y$, whereas positivity and Moore--Penrose completion of the square give
\[
 \inf_{v\in K^\perp}\langle y+v,B(y+v)\rangle
 =\langle y,S_K(B)y\rangle.
\]
Taking the optimal quotient proves \textup{(RI.8)}.  The target metric window
and the minimum eigenvalue of the short then give \textup{(RI.9)}.
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[Protected compression is not protected coercivity]
The raw compression $P_KBP_K$ freezes all nuisance and tail coordinates.  It
can therefore report a false lower floor.  The source action relevant to a
protected target is the short $S_K(B)$, after every physically admitted
relaxation has been allowed.
\end{firewall}

\begin{theorem}[Exact tail elimination and influence preservation]
\label{thm:GT-effective-action}
Let $H=H_P\oplus H_Q$ and let
\[
 L=\begin{pmatrix}A&B\\B^*&C\end{pmatrix}\succeq0,
 \qquad C\succeq\gamma I\quad(\gamma>0).
\]
Define the effective head action
\[
 \boxed{S_P(L):=A-BC^{-1}B^*\succeq0.}
\]
Then for $p\in H_P$ and $q\in H_Q$,
\[
 \boxed{
 \left\langle\binom pq,L\binom pq\right\rangle
 =\langle p,S_P(L)p\rangle
 +\left\langle q+C^{-1}B^*p,
 C(q+C^{-1}B^*p)\right\rangle.}
\]
Consequently,
\[
 \inf_q\left\langle\binom pq,L\binom pq\right\rangle
 =\langle p,S_P(L)p\rangle,
\]
\[
 \boxed{
 \Ker L
 =\left\{\binom{p}{-C^{-1}B^*p}:p\in\Ker S_P(L)\right\}.}
\]
If $E:K\to H_P$ and $\Ran E\subseteq\Ran S_P(L)$, then, after embedding
$E$ into $H_P\oplus H_Q$,
\[
 \boxed{E^*L^\dagger E=E^*S_P(L)^\dagger E.}
\]
Thus every protected influence and every mixed influence innovation is exactly
preserved by physical tail elimination.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Expanding the square gives
\[
 \langle q,Cq\rangle+2\Re\langle p,Bq\rangle
 =\langle q+C^{-1}B^*p,C(q+C^{-1}B^*p)\rangle
  -\langle p,BC^{-1}B^*p\rangle,
\]
which proves the first assertions.  The kernel formula follows because both
nonnegative terms must vanish.  For a head source $Ec$, the minimum-energy
solution of $Lx=Ec$ has tail component $-C^{-1}B^*p$ and head equation
$S_P(L)p=Ec$.  Hence the minimum-energy representative is obtained by applying
$S_P(L)^\dagger$ on the head, and taking its source pairing gives the final
identity.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Certified approximate corrector]
\label{cor:GT-effective-corrector}
In the setting of \Cref{thm:GT-effective-action}, let $K:H_P\to H_Q$ be any
proposed tail corrector and put
\[
 \rho_K:=CK-B^*,
\]
\[
 \widetilde S_K
 :=A-BK-K^*B^*+K^*CK.
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{\widetilde S_K=S_P(L)+\rho_K^*C^{-1}\rho_K.}
\]
If $\widetilde S_K\succeq\delta I$ and $\|\rho_K\|\le\varepsilon$, then
\[
 \boxed{S_P(L)\succeq
 \left(\delta-\frac{\varepsilon^2}{\gamma}\right)I.}
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Write $K=C^{-1}B^*+C^{-1}\rho_K$ and expand.  The cross terms cancel, leaving
the exact positive error.  Since $C^{-1}\preceq\gamma^{-1}I$, the lower bound
follows.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Boundary-complete head--detail packet]
\label{def:GT-boundary-complete-packet}
Let $\mathcal H$ be a retained head, $\mathcal T$ a detail carrier, and
$\mathcal B$ a physical boundary space.  Let
\[
 L=\begin{pmatrix}A&B\\B^*&C\end{pmatrix}\succeq0
 \quad\text{on }\mathcal H\oplus\mathcal T,
 \qquad
 \mathcal D=(D_H\;D_T):\mathcal H\oplus\mathcal T\to\mathcal B,
 \tag{BC.1}
\]
with $C\succ0$ on the declared detail support.  Put
\[
 S=A-BC^{-1}B^*,\qquad
 E=D_H-D_TC^{-1}B^*,\qquad
 K=D_TC^{-1}D_T^*\succeq0.
 \tag{BC.2}
\]
The complete action is $G=L+\mathcal D^*\mathcal D$.  Its
boundary-complete head short is the positive form $G_{/\mathcal T}$ defined by
\[
 \langle x,G_{/\mathcal T}x\rangle
 =\inf_{y\in\mathcal T}\langle x\oplus y,G(x\oplus y)\rangle.
 \tag{BC.3}
\]
A kernel of $C$ is first retained in the exceptional screen and the definition
is applied on its supported complement.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Exact boundary-complete Schur formula]
\label{thm:GT-boundary-complete-short}
For the packet of \Cref{def:GT-boundary-complete-packet},
\[
 \boxed{G_{/\mathcal T}=S+E^*(I+K)^{-1}E.}
 \tag{BC.4}
\]
The minimizing detail correction is
\[
 \boxed{
 y_*(x)=-C^{-1}B^*x
 -(C+D_T^*D_T)^{-1}D_T^*Ex.}
 \tag{BC.5}
\]
The first term is the interior harmonic corrector; the second is the additional
boundary-relaxation corrector.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Write $y=-C^{-1}B^*x+u$.  Completion of the interior square gives
\[
 \langle x\oplus y,L(x\oplus y)\rangle
 =\langle x,Sx\rangle+\langle u,Cu\rangle,
\]
while the boundary value is $Ex+D_Tu$.  The remaining minimization is
\[
 \inf_u\bigl(\langle u,Cu\rangle+\|Ex+D_Tu\|^2\bigr).
\]
Its normal equation gives \textup{(BC.5)}.  Substitution yields
\[
 E^*\!
 \left[I-D_T(C+D_T^*D_T)^{-1}D_T^*\right]E.
\]
The Woodbury identity identifies the bracket with
$(I+D_TC^{-1}D_T^*)^{-1}=(I+K)^{-1}$, proving \textup{(BC.4)}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Boundary-relaxation dispersion]
\label{cor:GT-boundary-relaxation-dispersion}
Shorting the interior first and then evaluating the boundary only on the frozen
harmonic lift gives $G_{\rm naive}=S+E^*E$.  The exact discrepancy is
\[
 \boxed{
 G_{\rm naive}-G_{/\mathcal T}
 =E^*K(I+K)^{-1}E\succeq0.}
 \tag{BC.6}
\]
It vanishes exactly when $K^{1/2}E=0$.  If $C\succeq\gamma I$ and
$\|D_T\|\le d$, then
\[
 \boxed{
 S+\frac{1}{1+d^2/\gamma}E^*E
 \preceq G_{/\mathcal T}\preceq S+E^*E.}
 \tag{BC.7}
\]
In particular, every interior floor $S\succeq gI$ survives the
boundary-complete elimination unchanged.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Use $I-(I+K)^{-1}=K(I+K)^{-1}$.  The two positive factors commute by
functional calculus, proving \textup{(BC.6)} and its zero condition.  The
bounds on $C$ and $D_T$ give $0\preceq K\preceq(d^2/\gamma)I$; applying the
order-reversing function $x\mapsto(1+x)^{-1}$ and taking the congruence by $E$
gives \textup{(BC.7)}.
\end{proof}

\begin{countertheorem}[Short-then-attach has no uniform multiplicative control]
\label{cth:GT-boundary-short-order}
There is no universal constant bounding $G_{\rm naive}$ by a multiple of the
boundary-complete short.  In the scalar packet
$A=B=0$, $C=1$, $D_H=1$, $D_T=t$, one has
\[
 \boxed{G_{\rm naive}=1,\qquad G_{/\mathcal T}=(1+t^2)^{-1}.}
\]
Thus the ratio is unbounded.
\end{countertheorem}

\begin{proof}
Here $S=0$, $E=1$, and $K=t^2$; apply
\Cref{thm:GT-boundary-complete-short}.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Assembly before shorting and router dispersion]
\label{thm:GT-assembly-before-short}
For $i=1,\ldots,m$, let
\[
 G_i=\begin{pmatrix}A_i&B_i\\B_i^*&D_i\end{pmatrix}\succeq0,
 \qquad A_i\succ0,
\]
and put
\[
 K_i=A_i^{-1}B_i,
 \quad S_i=D_i-B_i^*A_i^{-1}B_i,
\]
\[
 A=\sum_iA_i,
 \quad B=\sum_iB_i,
 \quad K=A^{-1}B,
 \quad S=\sum_iD_i-B^*A^{-1}B.
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{
 S=\sum_iS_i+
 \sum_i(K_i-K)^*A_i(K_i-K).}
\]
Equivalently,
\[
 \boxed{
 \sum_iB_i^*A_i^{-1}B_i-B^*A^{-1}B
 =\sum_i(K_i-K)^*A_i(K_i-K)\succeq0.}
\]
Hence shorting after coherent assembly retains a positive router-dispersion
coordinate which is lost by separately shorting the local packets.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Since $B_i=A_iK_i$ and $B=AK$, expand
\[
 \sum_i(K_i-K)^*A_i(K_i-K)
 =\sum_iK_i^*A_iK_i-K^*AK,
\]
because the two cross sums equal $K^*AK$.  Substitute
$K_i^*A_iK_i=B_i^*A_i^{-1}B_i$ and
$K^*AK=B^*A^{-1}B$.
\end{proof}


\begin{theorem}[Finite geometric spectral-layer compiler]
\label{thm:GT-geometric-threshold-bank}
For $S\succeq0$, $q>1$, and $\tau>0$, put
\[
 Q_S(t)=\one_{[t,\infty)}(S)
\]
and define the finite geometric layer sum
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathfrak D_{\tau,q}(S)
 =\tau Q_S(\tau)
 +\sum_{\substack{k\ge1\\q^k\tau\le\|S\|}}
   (q-1)q^{k-1}\tau\,Q_S(q^k\tau).}
 \tag{RI.10}
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathfrak D_{\tau,q}(S)\preceq S
 \preceq q\mathfrak D_{\tau,q}(S)+\tau I.}
 \tag{RI.11}
\]
For $B=\sum_{i=1}^rS_i$, choose resolutions $\tau_i$, put
\[
 \mathfrak D=\sum_i\mathfrak D_{\tau_i,q}(S_i),
 \qquad
 \rho=\sum_i\tau_i,
\]
and let $\kappa=\lambda_{\min}(\mathfrak D)$ and
$\beta=\lambda_{\min}(B)$.  Then
\[
 \boxed{\kappa\le\beta\le q\kappa+\rho.}
 \tag{RI.12}
\]
If $mI\preceq C\preceq MI$ on the same carrier, then
\[
 \boxed{
 \frac{m}{q\kappa+\rho}
 \le\Lambda(B,C)
 \le\frac{M}{\kappa}.}
 \tag{RI.13}
\]
Thus a finite threshold bank detects small but nonzero spectral mass even when
all exact support projections have full range.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Apply scalar functional calculus.  If an eigenvalue $\lambda<\tau$, the layer
sum is zero and $\lambda<\tau$.  Otherwise, if $q^k\tau\le\lambda<q^{k+1}\tau$,
the scalar layer sum telescopes to $q^k\tau$, which lies below $\lambda$ and
whose $q$-multiple lies above it.  This proves \textup{(RI.11)}.  Summing over
the source components gives
$\mathfrak D\preceq B\preceq q\mathfrak D+\rho I$ and hence
\textup{(RI.12)}.  Apply \Cref{thm:GT-source-coercivity-influence} to the
target metric window to obtain \textup{(RI.13)}.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Protected-angle localizer]
\label{def:GT-protected-angle-localizer}
Let $P$ be an independently fixed predictor projection, put $Q=I-P$, and let
$t_0=Qt$, $p_0=Qp$.  For $0\le\eta\le1$, define
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathbb L_\eta(t,p\mid P)
 =\begin{pmatrix}
   \eta\|t_0\|^2&-\langle t_0,p_0\rangle\\
   -\langle p_0,t_0\rangle&\eta\|p_0\|^2
  \end{pmatrix}.}
 \tag{PA.1}
\]
If either residual vanishes, set the protected angle to zero; otherwise put
\[
 \rho(t,p\mid P)
 =\frac{|\langle t_0,p_0\rangle|}{\|t_0\|\,\|p_0\|}.
 \tag{PA.2}
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Exact protected-angle criterion]
\label{thm:GT-protected-angle}
For every packet of \Cref{def:GT-protected-angle-localizer},
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathbb L_\eta(t,p\mid P)\succeq0
 \iff \rho(t,p\mid P)\le\eta.}
 \tag{PA.3}
\]
If a readout has the exact form
$f=\mathfrak p+\langle t_0,p_0\rangle$ and
$|\mathfrak p|\le a$, then positivity of the localizer implies
\[
 \boxed{|f|\le a+\eta\|t_0\|\,\|p_0\|.}
 \tag{PA.4}
\]
A negative eigenvector of $\mathbb L_\eta$ is an explicit violating linear
combination of the residual total and phase sources.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The diagonal entries are nonnegative and the determinant is
$\eta^2\|t_0\|^2\|p_0\|^2-|\langle t_0,p_0\rangle|^2$.  Positivity of a
$2\times2$ Hermitian matrix is therefore equivalent to \textup{(PA.3)}.
Equation \textup{(PA.4)} follows by the triangle inequality.
\end{proof}

\begin{countertheorem}[Protected angle is not monotone under predictor enlargement]
\label{cth:GT-angle-predictor-nonmonotone}
Adding a predictor direction can either increase or decrease the residual
protected angle.  Consequently the predictor bank must be fixed by the
physical cylinder before the terminal readout is inspected.
\end{countertheorem}

\begin{proof}
In $\R^2$, take $t=e_1$, $p=e_2$.  With $P=0$ the angle is zero, whereas
projection onto $\Span(e_1-e_2)$ leaves both residuals equal to
$(e_1+e_2)/2$ and the angle becomes one.  In $\R^3$, take
$t=e_1+e_3$, $p=e_2+e_3$.  The initial angle is $1/2$, whereas projecting onto
$\Span(e_3)$ leaves the orthogonal vectors $e_1,e_2$ and the angle becomes
zero.
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[Secants, tangents, and actions]
\label{fire:GT-secant-tangent-action}
A finite Hellinger Gram is a canonical comparison of actual laws.  A Fisher
matrix additionally requires a physical shrinking family.  A dynamical or
field action further requires a physical process, residual map, transfer, or
pressure whose derivative or Hessian is being used.  None of these stronger
objects may be manufactured by choosing an interpolation or by selecting a
positive operator with the desired kernel.
\end{firewall}
