one same-history law compares its repeated use with a finite source stock, a
lower-bounded action, or an independently well-founded ancestry order.
\end{countertheorem}


\begin{corollary}[Process-paid recurrence and cofinal exclusion]
\label{cor:GT-process-paid-cofinal}
Let a sequence of recurrent excursions be measured on the process filtration
of \Cref{thm:GT-process-stock-Jordan}.  Suppose the $j$th excursion has a
nonnegative declared debit $c_j\ge\delta_j$, and suppose the action-to-stock
ordered law holds with total comparison error $\sum_j\mathbb{E}\varepsilon_j<
\infty$.  If
\[
 \mathbb{E}B_0+\sum_j\mathbb{E}i_j+\sum_j\mathbb{E}r_j<\infty,
\]
then
\[
 \boxed{\sum_j\mathbb{E}c_j<\infty.}
 \tag{GW.8a}
\]
Consequently a cofinal family with $\sum_j\delta_j=\infty$ is impossible.
Before the debits are summed, repeated event sources must also pass the
source-first-birth and dynamic-head tests of
\Cref{thm:GT-source-terminal-nonduplication}; reuse, promotion, or
response-null mass is retained as a separate branch rather than charged again.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Apply \textup{(SC.4e)}, sum, and use \textup{(SC.4b)} with the stated finite
stock, inflow, replenishment, and error bounds.  The final assertion is the
contrapositive of the resulting finite total debit, together with
\textup{(JS.6)}.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Cofinal first-passage packet and joint source balance]
\label{def:GT-cofinal-first-passage}
Let
$\Omega_{h_0}\subseteq\Omega_{h_0+1}\subseteq\cdots$
be source-native finite screens.  Once every history trapped in a fixed screen
has been closed by the recurrent-component compiler, let $P_h$ denote the
literal stopped history from first entry into the $h$th annulus to first upper
exit, lower return, basin entry, or a declared finite witness.  A physical
first-passage cost $c_h(P_h)$ has margin $\delta_h>0$ when every realized upper
exit satisfies $c_h(P_h)\ge\delta_h$.  The costs possess a joint source balance
when one actual source action satisfies
\[
 \boxed{
 A_H+\sum_{h=h_0}^{H}c_h(P_h)
 \le A_{h_0-1}+E_H,
 \qquad A_H\ge A_*,
 \qquad \sup_HE_H\le E_*<\infty.}
 \tag{GW.9}
\]
The single inequality is essential: annuluswise estimates may not reuse one
physical stock several times.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Source-anchored cofinal descent]
\label{thm:GT-source-anchored-cofinal-descent}
Assume every fixed screen is well founded after its finite recurrent-component
analysis.  If the upper first-passage margins and joint balance of
\Cref{def:GT-cofinal-first-passage} satisfy
\[
 \boxed{\sum_{h=h_0}^{\infty}\delta_h=\infty,}
 \tag{GW.10}
\]
then no source history crosses cofinally many screens.  More precisely, no
history can cross the level
\[
 \boxed{
 H_*(s)=\min\left\{H:
 \sum_{h=h_0}^{H}\delta_h>
 A_{h_0-1}-A_*+E_*
 \right\}.}
 \tag{GW.11}
\]
The finite obstruction-tree height inside $\Omega_{H_*(s)}$ is consequently a
global natural-valued rank.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
A history crossing through level $H$ pays at least
$\sum_{h=h_0}^{H}\delta_h$.  The joint balance bounds the same sum by
$A_{h_0-1}-A_*+E_*$.  This contradicts the defining inequality for
$H_*(s)$.  The history is therefore confined to one finite well-founded screen,
whose maximum nonterminal path length is finite.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Finite-recurrence and cofinal-escape alternative]
\label{thm:GT-global-well-foundedness-alternative}
For every source-reachable family of finite stopping packets, the passing
branch is obtained when all displayed closure hypotheses hold; otherwise the
compiler returns at least one of the following finite or cofinal witnesses.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(W\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item every recurrent component is closed by a physically paid Bellman current,
      a finite holonomy/resource budget, or an independently well-founded source
      ancestry, and the cofinal first-passage margins satisfy
      \Cref{thm:GT-source-anchored-cofinal-descent};
\item a balanced recurrent circulation defeats the complete admitted physical
      current bank;
\item a positive separator exists but has no finite common source balance;
\item a source-flat recurrent component remains and no independent ancestry or
      boundary law is loaded;
\item a cofinal first-passage margin collapses, one screen is not future or
      boundary complete, or the joint balance fails;
\item one literal cofinal history, with all source, boundary, action,
      provenance, and stopping marks retained, escapes every certified screen.
\end{enumerate}
Only the first branch is global well-foundedness.  The remaining branches are
finite or cofinal source witnesses and are not erased by reweighting the same
incomplete localizer.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Apply \Cref{thm:GT-physical-circulation-minimax} to every recurrent component.
On the positive branch use \Cref{thm:GT-Bellman-action-rank}, the existing
holonomy/open-current calculus, or a separately loaded ancestry order.  If all
fixed screens close, apply \Cref{thm:GT-source-anchored-cofinal-descent}.  Every
failure of one of these hypotheses is one of the displayed witnesses; the list
is exhaustive by finite SCC condensation and the first-passage alternative.
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[Local positivity, finite screens, and cofinal closure]
\label{fire:GT-local-not-global}
A strict local gap does not by itself supply a recurrent current, a physical
source budget, or an annular first-passage margin.  Conversely, finite-screen
well-foundedness does not exclude the path
$0\to1\to2\to\cdots$, whose every finite restriction is acyclic.  Global
closure always retains both the recurrent-flow packet and the source-anchored
cofinal screen ledger.
\end{firewall}

\subsection{Exact AF, quasilocal, source, and finite-memory modules}

\begin{definition}[Directed operational Grand-Tensor system]
\label{def:directed-GT-system}
Let $(\mathcal D,\le)$ be a countable directed set.  A \emph{directed
operational Grand-Tensor system} consists of finite structural tensors
$\boldsymbol{\mathbb T}_{\Grand,X}$, $X\in\mathcal D$, together with the
support-completed unital $*$-monomorphisms
\[
 \iota_{Y/X}:\mathcal A_X^{\rm cut}\longrightarrow
 \mathcal A_Y^{\rm cut},\qquad X\le Y,
\]
obtained from prefix-exact operational morphisms, such that
\[
 \iota_{Z/Y}\iota_{Y/X}=\iota_{Z/X},\qquad
 \iota_{X/X}=\id.
\]
It is \emph{contextually strict} when the contextual innovation Grams vanish,
so the maps descend to the separated history algebras.  A finite collection of
typed source families is \emph{jointly strict} when all marginal and mixed
source Gram blocks compress under the corresponding coefficient embeddings.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[AF structural limit and compatible physical states]
\label{thm:AF-limit-state}
Let $X_1\le X_2\le\cdots$ be a cofinal prefix-exact cutoff family with the
support-completed injections of \Cref{thm:cutoff-compatibility}.  Then the raw
support-completed history algebras have a canonical AF $C^*$-inductive limit
$\mathcal A_\infty^{\rm cut}$.  If every contextual innovation Gram in
\Cref{thm:cutoff-compatibility} vanishes, the separated history algebras also
form an AF inductive system.

If states $\omega_n$ satisfy
$\omega_{n+1}\circ\iota_{n,n+1}=\omega_n$, there is a unique state
$\omega_\infty$ on the inductive limit.  Its GNS representation is bounded and
obeys $\|\pi_{\omega_\infty}(a)\|\le\|a\|$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
An inductive limit of finite-dimensional $C^*$-algebras is AF.  The contextual
quotients form a covariant system exactly when the innovation criterion gives
ideal descent and reflection.  Define $\omega_\infty$ on the algebraic union by
$\omega_\infty(\iota_{n,\infty}(a))=\omega_n(a)$; compatibility makes this
well defined, positivity and normalization pass to the norm completion, and
uniqueness follows from density.  The standard GNS estimate
$\|\pi(a)[b]\|^2=\omega(b^*a^*ab)\le\|a\|^2\omega(b^*b)$ gives boundedness.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Projective compactness of finite-stage states]
\label{thm:projective-state-compactness}
Let
$\mathcal A_1\xrightarrow{}\mathcal A_2\xrightarrow{}\cdots$
be an injective sequence of finite-dimensional unital $C^*$-algebras.  For
each $n$, let $\omega_n$ be an arbitrary state on $\mathcal A_n$.  There are a
subsequence $n_j$ and compatible states $\omega_m^\infty$ on every fixed stage
such that
\[
 \omega_{n_j}(\iota_{n_j/m}(a))\longrightarrow\omega_m^\infty(a)
 \qquad(a\in\mathcal A_m),
\]
and
\[
 \omega_\ell^\infty(\iota_{\ell/m}a)=\omega_m^\infty(a)
 \qquad(m\le\ell).
\]
Consequently the subsequence determines a state on the AF inductive limit.  If
the original states are exactly compatible, the limit is unique and no
subsequence is required.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The state space of each finite-dimensional $\mathcal A_m$ is compact.  Choose a
subsequence whose restrictions to $\mathcal A_1$ converge, then a further
subsequence whose restrictions to $\mathcal A_2$ converge, and continue.  The
diagonal subsequence converges on every fixed stage.  Positivity and
normalization pass to the limit.  For $m\le\ell$, strict composition gives
\[
 \omega_{n_j}(\iota_{n_j/\ell}\iota_{\ell/m}a)
 =\omega_{n_j}(\iota_{n_j/m}a),
\]
so the limits are compatible.  Apply \Cref{thm:AF-limit-state}.  Under exact
compatibility every later restriction already equals the earlier state,
proving uniqueness.
\end{proof}



\begin{theorem}[Joint-source inductive-limit universality]
\label{thm:joint-source-inductive-limit}
Let $a=1,\ldots,m$ label finitely many jointly strict source families.  At
cutoff $X$, let
\[
 S_{a,X}:E_{a,X}\longrightarrow\mathcal H_X^{\min},
 \qquad G_{a,X}=S_{a,X}^*S_{a,X},
\]
be their canonical joint source realization, and suppose every mixed block
compresses under coefficient isometries $j_{a,Y/X}$:
\[
 j_{a,Y/X}^*S_{a,Y}^*S_{b,Y}j_{b,Y/X}
 =S_{a,X}^*S_{b,X}
 \qquad(a,b=1,\ldots,m).
\]
Give the faithful Gram-source quotient
\[
 \mathcal E_{a,X}^{G}:=E_{a,X}/\Ker G_{a,X}
\]
the inner product
$\langle[x],[y]\rangle_G=\langle x,G_{a,X}y\rangle$, and let
$V_{a,X}[x]=S_{a,X}x$ be its canonical isometric synthesis.  Then:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(J\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item the coefficient maps induce strict source-support isometries
      $\sigma_{a,Y/X}[x]=[j_{a,Y/X}x]$;
\item there are unique common-carrier isometries
      \[
       \iota^{\rm src}_{Y/X}:\mathcal H_X^{\min}\to\mathcal H_Y^{\min},
       \qquad
       \iota^{\rm src}_{Y/X}V_{a,X}=V_{a,Y}\sigma_{a,Y/X},
      \]
      and they compose strictly;
\item the Hilbert direct limits
      $\mathcal E_{a,\infty}^{G}$ and $\mathcal H_\infty^{\min}$ carry unique
      compatible isometries
      $V_{a,\infty}:\mathcal E_{a,\infty}^{G}\to
      \mathcal H_\infty^{\min}$ reproducing every finite marginal and mixed
      Gram by compression;
\item for two families, the normalized cross transports define one limit
      contraction $K_{21,\infty}$ exactly when the new-direction defects
      \[
       \Delta^{\rm new}_{21,Y/X}
       =\bigl\|(I-\sigma_{2,Y/X}\sigma_{2,Y/X}^*)
       K_{21,Y}\sigma_{1,Y/X}\bigr\|_{\HS}^2
      \]
      vanish on every cutoff arrow.
\end{enumerate}
Thus complete mixed-block functoriality excludes cutoff-dependent relative
rotations; separate marginal canonicality does not.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Marginal compression gives
\[
 \langle j_{a,Y/X}x,G_{a,Y}j_{a,Y/X}y\rangle
 =\langle x,G_{a,X}y\rangle.
\]
It therefore sends $\Ker G_{a,X}$ into $\Ker G_{a,Y}$ and induces the source
isometry $\sigma_{a,Y/X}$.  On the joint coefficient direct sum, put
$J_{Y/X}=\bigoplus_aj_{a,Y/X}$.  Compression of every mixed block is exactly
$J_{Y/X}^*\mathbb G_YJ_{Y/X}=\mathbb G_X$.  Hence
$[u]_X\mapsto[J_{Y/X}u]_Y$ is well defined and isometric on the joint Gram
quotients.  Its action on the source summands gives the displayed
intertwining; those summands span the source-minimal carrier, proving
uniqueness.  Strict composition follows because both composites agree on every
source generator.

The source-support and common-carrier isometries are strict directed systems,
so their algebraic direct limits carry well-defined inner products and their
completions are Hilbert direct limits.  The finite isometries $V_{a,X}$
intertwine the arrows and therefore define $V_{a,\infty}$.  Inner products of
finite-stage source vectors are exactly the finite mixed Gram entries, proving
the compression claim.

For two families, whitening gives the compressed transport identity of
\Cref{thm:joint-source-cutoff-functor}.  Decompose
$K_{21,Y}\sigma_{1,Y/X}$ into the old source-$2$ range and its orthogonal
complement.  The old component is
$\sigma_{2,Y/X}K_{21,X}$ and the displayed defect is the squared norm of the
new component.  It vanishes exactly when the transports intertwine.  The
resulting compatible contractions define a contraction on the algebraic
source-support direct limit and hence on its Hilbert completion.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Canonical causal efficient-score record]
\label{cor:causal-efficient-score-record}
For a finite causal path process with finitely many declared score coordinates,
apply the minimal-readable-record construction to the current scores and to all
future score-cylinder probabilities.  The resulting quotient is the unique
coarsest causal score-sufficient record: every score factors through it, its
quotient transition is well defined, and every other causal score-sufficient
record maps onto it.  Under a cutoff refinement preserving all old score
futures, these minimal score records form a strict quotient system.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The selected coordinates are a finite instance of the response family in
\Cref{thm:minimal-record}.  Its right-congruence property is exactly strong
lumpability of the quotient transition, and its universal property gives the
unique factor map from every other sufficient record.  Preservation of the old
future signatures is the cutoff descent criterion in
\Cref{thm:operational-record-completion}.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Quasilocal Grand-Tensor net]
\label{def:quasilocal-GT-net}
Let $\mathfrak L$ be a countable directed family of finite regions.  A
\emph{quasilocal Grand-Tensor net} is a family of finite-dimensional unital
$C^*$-algebras $\mathcal A_\Lambda$, $\Lambda\in\mathfrak L$, with isotonic
unital embeddings, such that disjoint region algebras commute.  Its
quasilocal algebra is
\[
 \mathcal A_{\rm ql}:=
 \overline{\bigcup_{\Lambda\in\mathfrak L}\mathcal A_\Lambda}^{\|\cdot\|}.
\]
A family of local states or local UCP maps is compatible when its restrictions
agree under every inclusion.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Quasilocal completion, states, and local dynamics]
\label{thm:quasilocal-completion}
Every quasilocal Grand-Tensor net has a unique $C^*$-inductive-limit algebra
with the stated local embeddings.  Every compatible family of local states
extends uniquely to a state on $\mathcal A_{\rm ql}$.  Every compatible family
of unital completely positive contractions
$\Phi_\Lambda:\mathcal A_\Lambda\to\mathcal A_\Lambda$ extends uniquely to a
UCP contraction on $\mathcal A_{\rm ql}$.  If the local maps form a semigroup,
so does the extension.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The algebraic union is a well-defined $*$-algebra because the embeddings are
strict.  The inductive-limit norm is consistent on every local algebra, and its
completion gives $\mathcal A_{\rm ql}$.  A compatible state is a positive
normalized functional on the algebraic union and is norm bounded by one, hence
extends uniquely.  The same argument applies to compatible UCP maps because a
unital positive map between $C^*$-algebras is contractive; complete positivity
passes on each matrix level by density.  Composition identities hold on the
dense local union and therefore on the completion.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Compatible future forms and the exact module bound]
\label{thm:compatible-future-forms}
Suppose faithful forms $\mathfrak g_n$ satisfy
$\mathfrak g_{n+1}(\iota_{n,n+1}a,\iota_{n,n+1}b)=\mathfrak g_n(a,b)$.
They define a positive-definite Hilbert direct limit.  An old history
$a\in\mathcal A_n$ acts boundedly on this limit exactly when
\[
 \boxed{
 \beta_{\mathfrak g}(a)
 :=\sup_{m\ge n}
 \|L_{\iota_{nm}(a)}\|_{\mathfrak g_m\to\mathfrak g_m}<\infty.}
\]
Compatible inner products alone do not imply this bound; compatible GNS forms
do.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Compatibility identifies finite-stage vectors isometrically and hence defines
the algebraic direct-limit inner product.  Left multiplication by $a$ is
well defined by the algebra embeddings.  Its operator norm on the dense union
is the supremum of its finite-stage norms, proving necessity and sufficiency.
For a state form, the GNS estimate in \Cref{thm:AF-limit-state} gives the
uniform bound $\|a\|$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Uniform finite-horizon CP feasibility]
\label{thm:CP-memory-compactness}
Fix a finite set of boundary types, finite exposed port spaces, a finite
primitive branch alphabet, fixed instrument-normalization equations, fixed
terminal Reads, and one reusable memory dimension $M$.  Let
$\Theta_M$ be the finite-dimensional parameter space of source density
matrices, primitive branch Choi matrices, and terminal effects satisfying the
normalization constraints.  Then the complete infinite process has one
$M$-dimensional recurrent CP realization if and only if every finite horizon
has an $M$-dimensional realization in this same presentation.

The same conclusion holds when the horizon-$N$ realization errors tend to zero.
For a one-type $M$-dimensional quantum memory, the infinite Hankel rank obeys
$d_\infty\le M^2$, so
\[
 \boxed{M\ge\lceil\sqrt{d_\infty}\rceil.}
\]
Finite Hankel rank alone is not sufficient for CP realizability.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Positivity and fixed normalization make $\Theta_M$ compact: density matrices,
subnormalized Choi matrices, and effects lie in compact bounded semialgebraic
sets.  Let $\mathcal K_N(M)\subseteq\Theta_M$ be the closed set reproducing all
probabilities through horizon $N$.  These sets are nested.  If each is
nonempty, compactness and the finite-intersection property give an element of
$\bigcap_N\mathcal K_N(M)$, which realizes every finite word and hence the
complete process.  The converse is immediate.  With errors
$\varepsilon_N\to0$, take a convergent subsequence of parameter tuples and pass
each fixed finite probability identity to the limit.

The Hermitian operator space of an $M$-dimensional memory has dimension $M^2$,
so every Hankel column is represented in a space of that dimension.  This gives
the rank bound.  Positivity of an invariant cone is an additional constraint
not encoded by linear rank, so the converse need not hold.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Protected-record dimension obstruction]
\label{thm:record-dimension-obstruction}
If the minimal readable record at cutoff $X$ has $r_X$ point-readable values,
then every faithful Hilbert-space representation of the full record-bearing
history algebra has dimension at least $r_X$.  Consequently, if
$r_X\to\infty$, no single finite-dimensional faithful carrier stores the
complete protected record.  Exact point-readable chronology
$1,\ldots,X$ has $r_X\ge X$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The $r_X$ point Reads are mutually orthogonal nonzero projections.  In a
faithful representation each has nonzero range, and these ranges are mutually
orthogonal, so the carrier dimension is at least $r_X$.  Chronological point
Reads are pairwise separated and therefore give at least $X$ such projections.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Finite recurrent core versus growing ledger]
A finite recurrent quantum or classical core may emit an indefinitely growing
external classical ledger.  It is incorrect to identify finite recurrent
memory with a finite faithful carrier for the complete infinite protected
chronology.
\end{corollary}

\begin{theorem}[Flat depth requires alphabet control]
\label{thm:flat-alphabet-bound}
If a cutoff history algebra is generated by $m_X$ primitive typed letters and
is flat by depth $r_X$, then
\[
 \boxed{
 \dim_\C\mathcal A_X^{\rm hist}
 \le1+m_X+\cdots+m_X^{r_X}.}
\]
Hence uniform bounds on both $m_X$ and $r_X$ force uniform algebra dimension
and eventual stabilization of every injective cutoff system.  Uniform flat
depth alone is insufficient when the primitive alphabet grows.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The stabilized algebra is spanned by words of length at most $r_X$, of which
there are at most the displayed number.  If this number is uniformly bounded,
the nondecreasing dimensions of an injective directed system are eventually
constant, and an injective map between equal finite dimensions is an
isomorphism.  For the negative statement, take
$\mathcal A_X=\C^X$ and declare all $X$ coordinate projections primitive.  The
algebra is flat at depth one while its dimension diverges.
\end{proof}

\begin{countertheorem}[Prefix purification support is not recurrent memory]
\label{cth:prefix-support-memory}
For iid fair bits, the infinite Hankel rank and recurrent classical/CP memory
dimension are one, while the $N$-output cylinder density is $2^{-N}I_{2^N}$
and every one-shot purification of that cylinder requires environment
dimension at least $2^N$.
\end{countertheorem}

\begin{proof}
Every future probability is independent of the past, so all Hankel columns are
multiples of one column and a one-state generator suffices.  The cylinder
density has rank $2^N$, and the Schmidt rank of every purification equals the
rank of the reduced density.  Thus the canonical prefix support is a
finite-horizon purification resource, not the reusable memory cost.
\end{proof}



\subsection{Summable compatibility defects and projective state branches}
\label{sec:summable-compatibility}

For a chain of isometric embeddings write
$\iota_{n/m}=\iota_{n-1}\cdots\iota_m$.  The exact theory above has two
natural quantitative extensions: summable defects, which admit a canonical
correction, and arbitrary defects, which admit a compact projective cluster
set and a finite separator whenever the limit is nonunique.

\begin{theorem}[Canonical correction of summably incompatible states]
\label{thm:summable-state-correction}
Let $\omega_n$ be states on $\mathcal A_n$ and put
\[
 \delta_n^\omega
 :=\|\omega_{n+1}\circ\iota_n-\omega_n\|,
 \qquad
 D_m^\omega:=\sum_{n\ge m}\delta_n^\omega.
\]
If $D_1^\omega<\infty$, then for every $a\in\mathcal A_m$ the limit
\[
 \boxed{
 \widehat\omega_m(a)
 :=\lim_{n\to\infty}\omega_n(\iota_{n/m}a)}
\]
exists.  The family $\widehat\omega_m$ consists of states and satisfies
\[
 \widehat\omega_{m+1}\circ\iota_m=\widehat\omega_m,
 \qquad
 \boxed{\|\widehat\omega_m-\omega_m\|\le D_m^\omega.}
\]
It therefore defines one state $\widehat\omega_\infty$ on the AF limit.  It is
the unique exactly compatible family with
$\|\widetilde\omega_m-\omega_m\|\to0$ along the defect tail.

The same conclusion holds for any inverse system of Banach spaces with
contractive restriction maps.  Dually, if bounded observables, vectors, or UCP
maps have summable direct-system intertwining defects, they possess canonical
limits with the corresponding defect-tail estimate.  Closed convex constraints
preserved by the arrows, including positivity, normalization, self-adjointness,
and complete positivity, pass to the corrected family.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
For $n>m$ and $\|a\|\le1$, telescoping gives
\[
 \left|
 \omega_{n+1}(\iota_{n+1/m}a)
 -\omega_n(\iota_{n/m}a)
 \right|
 \le\delta_n^\omega.
\]
Hence the fixed-stage sequence is Cauchy, uniformly on the unit ball, and the
limit defines a bounded functional.  Positivity and normalization are closed
conditions, so $\widehat\omega_m$ is a state.  Passing the identity
$\iota_{n/(m+1)}\iota_m=\iota_{n/m}$ to the limit proves compatibility, while
summing the telescoping estimate gives the displayed tail bound.

If $\widetilde\omega$ is another compatible family asymptotically tracking the
original one, then for $a\in\mathcal A_m$ and $n\ge m$,
\[
 \widetilde\omega_m(a)
 =\widetilde\omega_n(\iota_{n/m}a).
\]
Letting $n\to\infty$ and comparing with $\omega_n$ proves uniqueness.  The
Banach-space and direct-system statements use the same telescoping argument;
closedness of the listed constraints proves the final assertion.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Summable positive mixed-Gram correction]
\label{thm:summable-mixed-Gram-correction}
Let $\mathbb G_n=[G_{ab,n}]_{a,b=1}^r\succeq0$ be the complete mixed-source
Gram on $E_n=\bigoplus_aE_{a,n}$, and let $J_n:E_n\to E_{n+1}$ be coefficient
isometries.  If
\[
 \sum_n\|J_n^*\mathbb G_{n+1}J_n-\mathbb G_n\|<\infty,
\]
then
\[
 \boxed{
 \widehat{\mathbb G}_m
 :=\lim_{n\to\infty}J_{n/m}^*\mathbb G_nJ_{n/m}}
\]
exists in norm, is positive, and obeys
\[
 J_m^*\widehat{\mathbb G}_{m+1}J_m=\widehat{\mathbb G}_m.
\]
Moreover
\[
 \|\widehat{\mathbb G}_m-\mathbb G_m\|
 \le
 \sum_{n\ge m}\|J_n^*\mathbb G_{n+1}J_n-\mathbb G_n\|.
\]
The faithful Gram quotients of the corrected blocks therefore possess a
canonical source-minimal Hilbert direct limit.  If the least positive corrected
source eigenvalue is bounded below by $\mu>0$, support projections, whitening
maps, normalized cross transports, and mutual Schur residuals are norm stable
with constants depending only on $\mu$ and the uniform Gram bound.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The compressed blocks form a Cauchy sequence by the same telescoping estimate
as in \Cref{thm:summable-state-correction}.  Positivity is norm closed and
compression commutes with the limit, proving exact corrected compatibility.
The tail bound is the telescoping sum.  Exact block compatibility gives the
Hilbert direct limit by the Gram-quotient construction of
\Cref{thm:joint-source-inductive-limit}.  On a spectral interval
$[\mu,M]$, the functions $t\mapsto t^{-1}$ and $t\mapsto t^{-1/2}$ are
operator Lipschitz with constants controlled by $\mu$; standard spectral
projection perturbation and substitution in the whitening and Schur formulas
give the last statement.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Projective cluster-state set]
\label{def:projective-cluster-state-set}
For arbitrary finite-stage states, let $\mathfrak S_\infty$ be the set of all
compatible families $(\omega_m^\infty)_m$ obtained as fixed-stage limits along
cofinal subsequences.  Equivalently, it is the inverse-limit cluster set of the
restrictions of $\omega_n$ to each earlier algebra.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Compact projective alternative and finite separator]
\label{thm:projective-state-alternative}
The set $\mathfrak S_\infty$ is nonempty and compact.  It is a singleton if
and only if, for every fixed $m$ and $a\in\mathcal A_m$, the sequence
$\omega_n(\iota_{n/m}a)$ converges.  If it contains two distinct elements,
there are one finite stage $m$, one self-adjoint $a\in\mathcal A_m$, two
cofinal subsequences, and $\varepsilon>0$ such that the two subsequential
expectations differ by at least $\varepsilon$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The product of the compact finite-dimensional state spaces is compact.
Diagonal extraction gives a compatible cluster family, and the compatibility
relations are closed, so the set of all such families is compact.  A singleton
cluster set is equivalent to convergence of every scalar coordinate in the
product topology.  Distinct compatible families differ on some finite algebra;
their difference is a nonzero Hermitian functional and is therefore separated
by a self-adjoint element of its unit ball.  Choosing convergent subsequences
realizing the two cluster states gives the stated margin.
\end{proof}

\begin{countertheorem}[Nonsummable defects need not obstruct a unique limit]
\label{cth:nonsummable-defects-convergent}
On the fixed algebra $\C^2$, let $\omega_n$ be the Bernoulli state with
parameter
\[
 p_n=\frac12+\frac{(-1)^n}{n+2}.
\]
Then $\omega_n\to(1/2,1/2)$ uniquely, while
$\sum_n\|\omega_{n+1}-\omega_n\|=\infty$.  Hence summability is a sharp
sufficient condition for a quantitative correction, not a necessary condition
for convergence.
\end{countertheorem}

\begin{proof}
The parameters converge to $1/2$.  Their successive differences have size
$1/(n+2)+1/(n+3)$, whose series diverges.  Total variation on $\C^2$ is the
absolute parameter difference.
\end{proof}


\subsection{Primitive score geometry, conditional entropy, and canonical noise short}
\label{sec:primitive-score-information}

The score calculus of \Cref{thm:operational-score-export} becomes completely
explicit on the resolved primitive renewal.  This provides a canonical finite
metric, a stochastic continuum source, and the correct separation between
fresh fluctuations and a predictable continuum mean before any spacetime
semantic is imposed.

Let $X_n\in\{H,P\}$ be the stationary active phase and let
\[
 \Sigma_{\rm ren}=\{hh,hp,pp,b_+,b_-\}
\]
be the one-step resolved branch alphabet.  The current and next phases and the
stationary branch probabilities are
\[
\begin{array}{c|ccccc}
 a&hh&hp&pp&b_+&b_-\\ \hline
 X_n&H&H&P&P&P\\
 X_{n+1}&H&P&P&H&H\\
 \mu(a)&1/11&4/11&2/11&2/11&2/11.
\end{array}
\]
Put $\mathcal H_{\rm br}=L^2(\Sigma_{\rm ren},\mu)$ and
\[
 \mathscr I_{\rm br}
 :=\Ker\mathbb E[\,\cdot\mid X_n].
\]
Let $\varphi(H)=-6/\sqrt{30}$ and $\varphi(P)=5/\sqrt{30}$, so that
$\mathbb E_\pi\varphi=0$, $\|\varphi\|_{L^2(\pi)}=1$, and
$M_0\varphi=\rho\varphi$ with $\rho=-7/15$.

\begin{theorem}[Exact primitive score bank and tangent exhaustion]
\label{thm:primitive-score-bank}
The space $\mathscr I_{\rm br}$ has dimension three.  The functions
\[
 u_H=\sqrt{\frac{11}{20}}
      \bigl(-4\one_{hh}+\one_{hp}\bigr),
\]
\[
 u_P=\sqrt{\frac{11}{12}}
      \bigl(2\one_{pp}-\one_{b_+}-\one_{b_-}\bigr),
 \qquad
 u_E=\sqrt{\frac{11}{4}}
      \bigl(\one_{b_+}-\one_{b_-}\bigr)
\]
form an orthonormal basis.  Define the active Doob innovation
\[
 \eta_n:=\varphi(X_{n+1})-\rho\varphi(X_n),
 \qquad q_0:=\|\eta_n\|_2^2=1-\rho^2=\frac{176}{225},
\]
and put
\[
 \widehat\eta=q_0^{-1/2}\eta,
 \qquad
 \zeta=\sqrt{\frac58}u_H-\sqrt{\frac38}u_P,
 \qquad
 \epsilon=u_E.
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{
 \widehat\eta=\sqrt{\frac38}u_H+\sqrt{\frac58}u_P,
 \qquad
 \{\widehat\eta,\zeta,\epsilon\}\text{ is orthonormal}.}
\]
Moreover:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2.8em]
\item the real tangent space of every fixed-support branch-local deformation is
      exactly $\mathscr I_{\rm br}^{\R}$;
\item every finite family $f_1,\ldots,f_m\in\mathscr I_{\rm br}^{\R}$ is
      realized by the conditional exponential family
      \[
       p_\theta(a\mid x)=p_0(a\mid x)
       \exp\!\left(\sum_j\theta_jf_j(a)-\psi_x(\theta)\right),
      \]
      and its Fisher matrix at the origin is
      $[\langle f_i,f_j\rangle]$;
\item the Doob map
      \[
       f(X_{n+1})\longmapsto
       f(X_{n+1})-\mathbb E[f(X_{n+1})\mid X_n]
      \]
      has one-dimensional centered range $\C\eta$;
\item $\zeta$ and $\epsilon$ have zero conditional expectation given
      $X_{n+1}$ and are orthogonal to every later active future.
\end{enumerate}
Thus every one-step local score source has source-minimal rank at most three,
and in the physical coordinates $(\eta,\zeta,\epsilon)$ its Gram is
\[
 \boxed{G_0=\diag\!\left(\frac{176}{225},1,1\right).}
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Conditional on $H$, the branch probabilities of $hh,hp$ are $1/5,4/5$;
conditional on $P$, the probabilities of $pp,b_+,b_-$ are all $1/3$.
The displayed functions therefore have conditional mean zero.  Direct
calculation gives unit norms and mutual orthogonality.  Conditional expectation
from a five-dimensional function space onto the two-dimensional current-phase
space is surjective, so its kernel has dimension three.

The branch values of $\eta$ are obtained by substituting the two values of
$\varphi$.  Comparison with $u_H,u_P$ gives
\[
 \eta=\sqrt{\frac{22}{75}}u_H+\sqrt{\frac{22}{45}}u_P,
\]
whose squared norm is $176/225$; normalization gives the formula for
$\widehat\eta$.  The displayed change of basis in
$\Span\{u_H,u_P\}$ is orthogonal.

Differentiating conditional normalization of an arbitrary fixed-support family
gives $\mathbb E[s\mid X_n]=0$ for every score.  Conversely, row centering
makes $\partial_{\theta_j}\psi_x(0)=0$, so the displayed exponential family
has scores $f_j$ and Fisher Gram $[\langle f_i,f_j\rangle]$.  The centered
space of functions of the binary next phase is one dimensional, and its Doob
image is nonzero because $\eta\ne0$; hence it equals $\C\eta$.
Finally, $\zeta$ and $\epsilon$ are orthogonal to constants, to
$\varphi(X_n)$, and to $\eta$.  From
$\varphi(X_{n+1})=\rho\varphi(X_n)+\eta$ they are orthogonal to every function
of $X_{n+1}$.  Conditional on $X_{n+1}$, the later active path is independent
of the resolved branch at time $n$, which proves orthogonality to every later
active future.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Primitive conditional information action]
\label{def:primitive-information-action}
For a positive conditional branch law $q(a\mid x)$ with the same support as
$p_0$, define
\[
 \mathscr A_{\rm ren}(q)
 :=\sum_x\pi_x\sum_{a\in\Sigma_x}
 q(a\mid x)\log\frac{q(a\mid x)}{p_0(a\mid x)}.
\]
For the score vector $s=(\eta,\zeta,\epsilon)^{\mathsf T}$ put
\[
 p_\theta(a\mid x)=p_0(a\mid x)
 e^{\langle\theta,s(a)\rangle-\psi_x(\theta)},
 \quad
 \Psi(\theta)=\sum_x\pi_x\psi_x(\theta),
 \quad m(\theta)=\nabla\Psi(\theta),
 \quad G(\theta)=\nabla^2\Psi(\theta).
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Entropy Hessian, Fisher window, and expectation coordinates]
\label{thm:primitive-information-geometry}
The primitive law is the unique minimizer of $\mathscr A_{\rm ren}$.  If
$u=p_0s_u$ and $v=p_0s_v$ are row-centred tangent vectors, then
\[
 \boxed{
 D^2\mathscr A_{\rm ren}(p_0)[u,v]
 =\langle s_u,s_v\rangle_{L^2(\mu)}.}
\]
In particular, in the physical score coordinates,
\[
 \boxed{D^2\mathscr A_{\rm ren}(p_0)=G_0.}
\]
There are $r>0$ and $0<g_-\le g_+<\infty$ such that
\[
 \boxed{g_-I\preceq G(\theta)\preceq g_+I
 \qquad(\|\theta\|\le r),}
\]
and the expectation map is bi-Lipschitz on this ball:
\[
 g_-\|\theta-\phi\|
 \le\|m(\theta)-m(\phi)\|
 \le g_+\|\theta-\phi\|.
\]
For two tilted laws, their conditional relative entropy is the Bregman
divergence
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal D(\theta\Vert\phi)
 =\Psi(\phi)-\Psi(\theta)
  -\langle m(\theta),\phi-\theta\rangle}
\]
and satisfies
\[
 \boxed{
 \frac{g_-}{2}\|\theta-\phi\|^2
 \le\mathcal D(\theta\Vert\phi)
 \le\frac{g_+}{2}\|\theta-\phi\|^2.}
\]
Thus the primitive itself supplies a noncollapsing local information metric;
no independent source-frame floor is needed on this score branch.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Nonnegativity and the equality condition are those of relative entropy.
Taylor expansion of
$(p_0+\varepsilon u)\log((p_0+\varepsilon u)/p_0)$ gives second variation
$u^2/p_0$; row-centering removes the first variation and polarization yields
the source-Gram identity.  The matrix $G(0)$ is therefore $G_0\succ0$.
Each $\psi_x$ is the logarithm of a finite positive exponential sum, hence is
real analytic, and
\[
 G(\theta)=\sum_x\pi_x\operatorname{Cov}_\theta(s\mid x).
\]
Continuity of its eigenvalues gives the uniform Fisher window on a sufficiently
small ball.  The fundamental theorem of calculus gives
\[
 m(\theta)-m(\phi)
 =\int_0^1G(\phi+t(\theta-\phi))(\theta-\phi)\,\dd t,
\]
which proves strong monotonicity and the two Lipschitz estimates.  Substitution
of the exponential-family formula gives the Bregman identity, and Taylor's
formula with integral remainder gives the quadratic bounds.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Predictable-mean/martingale-noise Pythagoras]
\label{thm:renewal-mean-noise-short}
Let $S:E\to\mathcal H$ be a current source, let $M:F\to\mathcal H$ be the
predictable outgoing mean source, and let $N:F\to\mathcal H$ be a fresh source
satisfying
\[
 S^*N=0,\qquad M^*N=0.
\]
Put $Y=M+N$ and $Q=N^*N$.  For every model router $W:F\to E$,
\[
 \boxed{
 (Y-SW)^*(Y-SW)
 =(M-SW)^*(M-SW)+Q.}
\]
The complete Gram of $(S,Y,N)$ is
\[
 \begin{pmatrix}
 S^*S&S^*M&0\\
 M^*S&M^*M+Q&Q\\
 0&Q&Q
 \end{pmatrix},
\]
and its Anderson--Trapp short away from the declared noise source is exactly
\[
 \boxed{
 \begin{pmatrix}S^*S&S^*M\\M^*S&M^*M\end{pmatrix}.}
\]
Hence the noise-shorted Ward form is precisely the Ward form of the predictable
mean; the stochastic order-$\tau$ covariance and deterministic
$o(\tau^2)$ residual are distinct positive coordinates.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Expand $Y-SW=M-SW+N$.  The cross term vanishes because
$(M-SW)^*N=M^*N-W^*S^*N=0$.  The displayed Gram follows by taking all pairings.
Shorting the final block subtracts
$\binom{0}{Q} Q^\dagger\begin{psmallmatrix}0&Q\end{psmallmatrix}$, which removes
exactly $Q$ from the outgoing marginal and leaves every current/mean block
unchanged.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Exact primitive score fluctuation--dissipation continuum]
\label{cor:primitive-score-continuum}
Let $\xi_n=(\eta_n,\zeta_n,\epsilon_n)^{\mathsf T}$ be the physical primitive
score bank.  Then
\[
 \mathbb E[\xi_n\mid\mathcal F_n]=0,
 \qquad
 \mathbb E[\xi_n\xi_n^*]=G_0,
 \qquad
 \mathbb E[\xi_m\xi_n^*]=0\quad(m\ne n).
\]
For $\tau\downarrow0$,
\[
 \boxed{
 Z_\tau(t):=\sqrt\tau\sum_{n< t/\tau}\xi_n
 \Longrightarrow G_0^{1/2}B_3(t)}
\]
in $D([0,T],\R^3)$ for every $T<\infty$.  At $t_n=n\tau$, the integrated
current/outgoing panel satisfies
\[
 G_n=t_nG_0,
 \qquad C_n=t_nG_0,
 \qquad H_{2,n}=(t_n+\tau)G_0,
\]
and therefore
\[
 \boxed{H_{2,n}-C_n^*G_n^\dagger C_n=\tau G_0.}
\]
The integrated normalized active phase has Brownian diffusion coefficient
\[
 \boxed{
 \frac{1-\rho^2}{(1-\rho)^2}
 =\frac{1+\rho}{1-\rho}=\frac4{11},}
\]
which equals the stationary renewal-boundary flux.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Each component is row centred, and the Markov branch law depends on the past
only through $X_n$, so $(\xi_n)$ is a bounded martingale-difference sequence.
Its stationary covariance is $G_0$ by \Cref{thm:primitive-score-bank}; temporal
orthogonality follows by conditioning the later increment on $\mathcal F_n$.
The predictable quadratic variation is
$\tau\sum_{n<t/\tau}\mathbb E[\xi_n\xi_n^*\mid\mathcal F_n]$.
The finite-state ergodic theorem makes it converge almost surely to $tG_0$,
and boundedness gives the Lindeberg condition.  The martingale functional
central limit theorem gives the asserted Brownian limit.

Orthogonality of successive increments gives the three integrated Gram
identities and their Schur complement.  Finally,
$\eta_n=\varphi(X_{n+1})-\rho\varphi(X_n)$ implies
\[
 (1-\rho)\sum_{n=0}^{N-1}\varphi(X_n)
 =\sum_{n=0}^{N-1}\eta_n+\varphi(X_0)-\varphi(X_N).
\]
The bounded endpoint term is negligible under diffusive scaling, and
$\operatorname{Var}(\eta_n)=1-\rho^2$, which gives the displayed coefficient.
\end{proof}

\begin{assessment}[Exact scope of the primitive information branch]
The resolved primitive supplies an unconditional finite source metric, an
information action, a three-component stochastic continuum, and the exact
noise short required before testing deterministic Ward convergence.  These
outputs do not select a spatial graph, a neighbouring-cell router, or a
spacetime field interpretation.  Those are connected-source and domain-loading
questions treated in Part~I-C.
\end{assessment}

\subsection{Renormalization cocycles, source routers, and metric profiles}
\label{sec:renormalization-cocycles}

\begin{definition}[Linear and affine renormalization arrows]
\label{def:renormalization-arrow}
Let $G_m\succeq0$ be the physical source or observable Gram on a finite
coefficient space $E_m$.  A linear renormalization arrow is a map
$Z_{n/m}:E_m\to E_n$ satisfying
\[
 Z_{n/m}^*G_nZ_{n/m}=G_m.
\]
An affine arrow is
\[
 \mathcal Z_{n/m}(x)=Z_{n/m}x+c_{n/m}.
\]
It is a strict cocycle when
\[
 Z_{\ell/n}Z_{n/m}=Z_{\ell/m},
 \qquad
 c_{\ell/m}=Z_{\ell/n}c_{n/m}+c_{\ell/n}.
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Finite metric congruence and cocycle obstruction]
\label{thm:renormalization-cocycle}
Let $A\succeq0$ on $E$ and $B\succeq0$ on $F$.  There exists
$Z:E\to F$ with $Z^*BZ=A$ if and only if
$\rank A\le\rank B$.  Every solution is
\[
 \boxed{Z=B^{\dagger/2}UA^{1/2}+N,}
\]
where $U:\supp A\to\supp B$ is an isometry and
$\Ran N\subseteq\Ker B$.  Thus the faithful modulus is the Stiefel space of
isometries between the Gram supports; equal ranks leave a unitary modulus.

For proposed arrows define the diamond
\[
 D_{\ell/n/m}:=Z_{\ell/n}Z_{n/m}-Z_{\ell/m},
 \qquad
 \boxed{\mathbb D_{\ell/n/m}:=D_{\ell/n/m}^*G_\ell D_{\ell/n/m}\succeq0.}
\]
The faithful quotient arrows form a strict cocycle exactly when every diamond
Gram vanishes.  A nonzero singular vector of $G_\ell^{1/2}D_{\ell/n/m}$ is a
finite cocycle-failure witness.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
If $Z^*BZ=A$, the map $B^{1/2}Z$ has Gram $A$ and therefore rank
$\rank A\le\rank B$.  Conversely choose an isometry
$U:\supp A\to\supp B$ and put $Z_0=B^{\dagger/2}UA^{1/2}$; direct
multiplication gives $Z_0^*BZ_0=A$.  Adding a map with range in $\Ker B$ does
not change the congruence.  Conversely, polar decomposition of $B^{1/2}Z$ on
$\supp A$ gives the displayed $U$, while the component of $Z$ in $\Ker B$ is
$N$.  The diamond statement is immediate because a vector is zero in the
faithful target quotient exactly when its $G_\ell$-norm is zero.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Canonical source-native router and Pythagoras]
\label{thm:source-native-renormalization}
Let
$S_m:E_m\to\mathcal H_m$ and $S_n:E_n\to\mathcal H_n$ be source syntheses,
let $I_{n/m}:\mathcal H_m\to\mathcal H_n$ be a physical carrier isometry, and
put $G_m=S_m^*S_m$.  The minimum-norm source router is
\[
 \boxed{Z_{n/m}^{\rm src}=S_n^\dagger I_{n/m}S_m.}
\]
With $P_n$ the projection onto $\Ran S_n$ and
$R_{n\mid m}^{\rm old}=(I-P_n)I_{n/m}S_m$, one has
\[
 \boxed{
 G_m=(Z_{n/m}^{\rm src})^*G_nZ_{n/m}^{\rm src}
 +(R_{n\mid m}^{\rm old})^*R_{n\mid m}^{\rm old}.}
\]
Hence exact metric transport is equivalent to inclusion of the old physical
source range in the new source range.  The independent new-source innovation
is
\[
 \mathbb I_{n\mid m}^{\rm new}
 :=S_n^*(I-I_{n/m}P_mI_{n/m}^*)S_n\succeq0.
\]
Old-source loss and legitimate source growth are therefore distinct profiles.
If the old-source residuals vanish on every arrow, the reduced source routers
compose strictly.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
$S_nS_n^\dagger=P_n$, so
$S_nZ_{n/m}^{\rm src}=P_nI_{n/m}S_m$.  Orthogonal decomposition of
$I_{n/m}S_m$ into this projection and $R_{n\mid m}^{\rm old}$ gives the Gram
identity.  Vanishing of the residual is exactly range inclusion.  The new
innovation is the Gram of the component of the new source orthogonal to the
embedded old range.  Under zero old residuals, both composites of source
routers synthesize the same embedded old source; minimum-norm uniqueness on
the faithful support gives strict composition.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Weighted summable correction of metric arrows]
\label{thm:summable-metric-correction}
Let $Z_n:E_n\to E_{n+1}$ be a fixed linear cocycle along a chain and define
\[
 E_n:=Z_n^*G_{n+1}Z_n-G_n.
\]
If for every $m$
\[
 D_m^{Z,G}
 :=\sum_{n\ge m}\|Z_{n/m}\|^2\|E_n\|<\infty,
\]
then
\[
 \boxed{
 \widehat G_m
 :=\lim_{n\to\infty}Z_{n/m}^*G_nZ_{n/m}}
\]
exists, is positive, and satisfies
\[
 Z_m^*\widehat G_{m+1}Z_m=\widehat G_m,
 \qquad
 \|\widehat G_m-G_m\|\le D_m^{Z,G}.
\]
The transport weights are essential: unweighted summability of the one-step
errors need not survive an amplifying renormalization cocycle.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
For $n>m$, consecutive transported metrics differ by
$Z_{n/m}^*E_nZ_{n/m}$.  Their norm is bounded by the summand in
$D_m^{Z,G}$, so the transported sequence is Cauchy.  Positivity and the exact
congruence identity pass to the norm limit.  The error bound is the telescoping
sum.  If $\|Z_{n/m}\|$ grows, errors small in their native cutoff norm can be
large after transport, proving the final qualification.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Structural, state, selection, and RG closure]
\label{def:GT-closure-levels}
For a finite cutoff family the following properties are distinct.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(L\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item \emph{structural closure}: the declared source/operator bank represents
      the exact finite law at one cutoff;
\item \emph{calibration closure}: the represented coefficients are identifiable
      relative to an independently fixed reference and microscopic state;
\item \emph{selection closure}: a fixed-point, compatibility, or held-out row
      selects the coefficient among the calibrated family;
\item \emph{state closure}: the retained state is future saturated, or is
      augmented by its minimum returned-memory quotient;
\item \emph{RG closure}: exact or tail-controlled shell maps compose along the
      cutoff tower and preserve the required physical positivity.
\end{enumerate}
None of these properties implies a later one without the corresponding
operational row.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Held-out two-shell nesting row]
\label{def:GT-heldout-nesting}
Let the first exact shell be
$\Sigma_1(c)=(F_1(c),G_1(c))$ on retained and tail coordinates, and let
$F_2(c,r)$ be the retained component of a second exact shell.  Define
\[
 \boxed{
 h_{21}^{\rm nest}(c)
 =F_2(F_1(c),G_1(c))-F_2(F_1(c),0).}
 \tag{RG.1}
\]
The row is held out only when the direct two-shell law entering the first term
was not used to fit the projected one-shell maps.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Exact first-return nesting derivative]
\label{thm:GT-heldout-nesting}
If $F_1,G_1,F_2$ are $C^1$, then
\[
 \boxed{
 h_{21}^{\rm nest}(c)
 =\int_0^1
 D_rF_2(F_1(c),tG_1(c))[G_1(c)]\,\dd t.}
 \tag{RG.2}
\]
At a tail-free point $G_1(c_0)=0$, put
$B_2=D_rF_2(F_1(c_0),0)$ and $C_1=DG_1(c_0)$.  Then
\[
 \boxed{Dh_{21}^{\rm nest}(c_0)=B_2C_1.}
 \tag{RG.3}
\]
Thus $\rank(B_2C_1)$ is the exact number of retained tangent directions tested
by the first independently measured two-shell return.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Apply the fundamental theorem of calculus to
$t\mapsto F_2(F_1(c),tG_1(c))$.  At $c_0$, differentiation cancels the common
$D_cF_2\,DF_1$ term from the direct and projected maps, leaving $B_2C_1$.
\end{proof}

\begin{countertheorem}[One-shell exactness is not projected nesting]
\label{cth:GT-one-shell-no-nesting}
Exact representation of each retained one-shell map does not imply that
discarding the intermediate tail preserves a direct two-shell law.
\end{countertheorem}

\begin{proof}
Take one-dimensional retained and tail spaces with
$F_1(c)=c$, $G_1(c)=c$, and $F_2(x,r)=x+r$.  Both one-shell retained formulas
are exact, but the direct and tail-deleted outputs are $2c$ and $c$.
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[Fitted composition versus independent validation]
The value of $h_{21}^{\rm nest}$ computed solely from the same model used to
fit both one-shell maps is a model prediction.  It is a validation or selector
row only when an independent direct shell, same-history mixed table, or
physically equivalent statistic supplies its value.
\end{firewall}

\begin{definition}[Metric and renormalization obstruction profile]
\label{def:metric-obstruction-profile}
For $G_n\ne0$, put
\[
 \alpha_n=\Tr G_n,
 \qquad
 \widetilde G_n=G_n/\alpha_n,
 \qquad
 s_n=\lambda_{\min}^{+}(\widetilde G_n),
 \qquad
 Q_n=\supp G_n.
\]
The profile records scale collapse or blowup of $\alpha_n$, shape collapse of
$s_n$, old-support loss, new-support innovation, affine-anchor failure, and
nonzero cocycle diamonds.  The stable branch has
\[
 0<\alpha_-\le\alpha_n\le\alpha_+<\infty,
 \qquad
 s_n\ge s_*>0,
\]
together with zero old-support and diamond residuals, modulo a declared compact
gauge.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Metric profile alternative]
\label{thm:metric-profile-alternative}
Every cofinal metric family has a subnet on which one or more of the following
occurs:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(R\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item the stable metric branch of \Cref{def:metric-obstruction-profile};
\item $\alpha_n\to0$ or $\alpha_n\to\infty$;
\item $s_n\to0$, with a normalized collapsing eigenvector;
\item an old source direction is lost or a new source direction is acquired;
\item a metric diamond or affine-anchor residual stays bounded away from zero;
\item no physical anchor removes a remaining positive scale or compact
      orientation modulus.
\end{enumerate}
Every negative branch carries the displayed eigenvector, source direction,
diamond vector, or unresolved modulus as its obstruction witness.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Compactness of the normalized positive cone and of finite Grassmannians gives a
cofinal subnet with convergent scale behavior, normalized spectra, and support
projections whenever those quantities remain bounded.  Failure of the stable
bounds produces the stated scalar or eigenvector sequences.  The source
Pythagoras theorem supplies old-loss and new-innovation vectors, while
\Cref{thm:renormalization-cocycle} supplies diamond witnesses.  If all such
residuals vanish, the remaining freedom is exactly the Stiefel or affine
modulus classified above; it is removed only by a declared physical anchor.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Changing Hilbert spaces, Mosco limits, and spectral witnesses}
\label{sec:GT-Mosco-limits}

\begin{definition}[Grand-Tensor Mosco convergence]
\label{def:GT-Mosco}
Let $J_n:\mathcal H_n\to\mathcal H_\infty$ be the canonical isometries of a
strict Hilbert direct system.  Let $q_n$ be closed forms with common lower
bound $-c$, and extend them to $\mathcal H_\infty$ by
\[
 \mathscr Q_n(x)=
 \begin{cases}
  q_n[J_n^*x],&x\in J_n\mathcal D(q_n),\\
  +\infty,&\text{otherwise}.
 \end{cases}
\]
They converge to a closed form $q_\infty$ in the Grand-Tensor Mosco sense when:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(M\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item $x_n\rightharpoonup x$ implies
      $q_\infty[x]\le\liminf_n\mathscr Q_n(x_n)$;
\item for every $x\in\mathcal D(q_\infty)$ there are $x_n\to x$ with
      $\mathscr Q_n(x_n)\to q_\infty[x]$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Mosco--resolvent--semigroup equivalence]
\label{thm:GT-Mosco}
Let $A_n$ and $A_\infty$ be the self-adjoint operators associated with the
forms in \Cref{def:GT-Mosco}.  The following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(Q\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item $q_n$ converges to $q_\infty$ in the Grand-Tensor Mosco sense;
\item for one, hence every, $\lambda>c$,
      \[
       \boxed{
       J_n(A_n+\lambda)^{-1}J_n^*
       \longrightarrow(A_\infty+\lambda)^{-1}}
      \]
      strongly on $\mathcal H_\infty$;
\item the embedded semigroups converge strongly and uniformly on compact
      time intervals:
      \[
       \boxed{
       J_ne^{-tA_n}J_n^*f\longrightarrow e^{-tA_\infty}f}
      \]
      for every $f$ and $t$ in a compact subset of $[0,\infty)$.
\end{enumerate}
It is enough to test the resolvent convergence on a countable dense family of
primitive source words.  Failure then produces one finite source word, one
positive discrepancy margin, and one cofinal subsequence.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
After adding $cI$, assume the forms are nonnegative.  For $\lambda>0$, the
resolvent vector is the unique minimizer of
\[
 x\longmapsto q_n[x]+\lambda\|x\|^2-2\operatorname{Re}\langle f,x\rangle.
\]
The Mosco lower condition bounds every weak cluster point from below, while a
recovery sequence gives the matching upper bound.  Strict convexity therefore
forces convergence of the minimizers and their norms, hence strong resolvent
convergence.  Conversely the resolvent determines the Moreau envelope of the
extended form.  Strong convergence at one resolvent point, followed by the
resolvent identity, gives convergence for every $\lambda$; monotone exhaustion
of the form by its Moreau envelopes yields the lower and recovery conditions.
The semigroup statement follows from the Laplace transform and functional
calculus, with recovery vectors controlling the endpoint $t=0$.  Uniform
boundedness of the resolvents makes convergence on a dense countable source
family equivalent to strong convergence; its failure is separated by one dense
source vector and a subsequence.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Compact graph-screen profile]
\label{def:compact-graph-screen}
Let $D_n=(A_n+cI)^{1/2}$ and let
$\Gamma_nu=(J_nu,J_nD_nu)$ be the embedded graph vector.  For increasing
finite-rank projections $\Pi_R$ on
$\mathcal H_\infty\oplus\mathcal H_\infty$, put
\[
 \Theta_R^{\rm gr}
 :=\limsup_n\sup_{\|u\|^2+q_n[u]\le1}
   \|(I-\Pi_R)\Gamma_nu\|.
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Compact screens, spectrum, and mass escape]
\label{thm:compact-screen-alternative}
Assume \Cref{thm:GT-Mosco}.  If
$\Theta_R^{\rm gr}\to0$, then the embedded resolvents are collectively
compact and converge in operator norm.  Consequently the limit resolvent is
compact, isolated eigenvalues converge with multiplicity, the associated
spectral projections converge in norm, and every finite low-energy source Gram
converges.

If the screen profile does not vanish, there are $R_j\to\infty$, cutoffs
$n_j$, and vectors $u_j$ with
\[
 \|u_j\|^2+q_{n_j}[u_j]\le1,
 \qquad
 \boxed{\|(I-\Pi_{R_j})\Gamma_{n_j}u_j\|\ge\varepsilon>0.}
\]
This is the canonical graph or spectral-mass-escape witness.  Strong resolvent
convergence alone does not exclude this branch.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The screen condition makes the union of embedded graph unit balls totally
bounded: first approximate uniformly by one finite-dimensional screen and then
use compactness on that screen.  Resolvents map the Hilbert unit ball into a
uniformly graph-bounded set, so they are collectively compact.  Strong
convergence plus collective compactness gives norm convergence.  Standard
Riesz-contour calculus then gives norm convergence of isolated spectral
projections and convergence of eigenvalues with multiplicity.  Failure of
uniform total boundedness is exactly the displayed tail sequence.  The moving
rank-one example $A_n=I-|e_n\rangle\langle e_n|$ on $\ell^2$ has strong
resolvent limit $I$ while its zero eigenvectors escape, proving the final
boundary.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Gap passage and primitive-word soft modes]
\label{thm:gap-soft-mode-alternative}
Let $E_n$ be compatible kernel projections and suppose
\[
 q_n[u]\ge\gamma_n\|(I-E_n)u\|^2.
\]
Under Mosco convergence and strong convergence of the embedded $E_n$,
\[
 \boxed{
 q_\infty[u]
 \ge(\liminf_n\gamma_n)\|(I-E_\infty)u\|^2.}
\]
If $\gamma_{n_j}\to0$, there are normalized transient vectors $v_j$ with
$q_{n_j}[v_j]\to0$.  When primitive source words form an operator core, they
may be chosen as finite primitive-word combinations with vanishing kernel
component and vanishing operator residual.  Their squared residuals are finite
source-Gram panels and constitute operational soft-mode witnesses.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Choose a Mosco recovery sequence for $u$ and use the finite lower bound together
with strong convergence of the kernel projections; taking the liminf gives the
limit estimate.  If the floors collapse, choose almost-minimizers of the
transient Rayleigh quotient.  Approximation in the graph norm by the primitive
operator core preserves normalization, transience, and vanishing energy.  The
operator residual norm is the Gram of the corresponding inserted primitive
word.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Canonical threshold screen]
\label{def:GT-canonical-threshold-screen}
For a finite positive action $A$ and a proposed margin $\beta>0$, define
\[
 \boxed{Z_\beta(A):=\one_{[0,\beta)}(A).}
 \tag{SC.1}
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Minimality and transport of the canonical screen]
\label{thm:GT-canonical-screen}
Let $Z$ be an orthogonal projection commuting with $A$.  Then
\[
 \boxed{A\succeq\beta(I-Z)\iff Z\succeq Z_\beta(A).}
 \tag{SC.2}
\]
Hence $Z_\beta(A)$ is the unique minimum-rank reducing screen on which the
margin can hold.  If
$\spec(A_X)\cap[\beta-g,\beta+g]=\varnothing$ and
$\|A_Y-A_X\|\le\varepsilon<g/2$, then
\[
 \boxed{
 \rank Z_\beta(A_Y)=\rank Z_\beta(A_X),\qquad
 \|Z_\beta(A_Y)-Z_\beta(A_X)\|
 \le\frac{2\varepsilon}{g-\varepsilon}.}
 \tag{SC.3}
\]
Thus an exceptional screen is a spectral output of an independently physical
action and threshold, not a subspace chosen after observing the desired
conclusion.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Commutation of $A$ and $Z$ reduces the assertion to each eigenspace.  Every
eigenvector with eigenvalue below $\beta$ must lie in $\Ran Z$, proving the
forward implication; the converse follows from the spectral theorem.  The
rank statement follows from Weyl's inequality, and the norm estimate is the
finite-dimensional Davis--Kahan projection bound across the open gap.
\end{proof}


\subsection{Covariant information forms and explicit mean-field continuum branches}
\label{sec:covariant-information-continuum}

Let $\Gamma=(V,E)$ be a finite connected graph, let each vertex carry the
primitive score coefficient space $F\cong\C^3$ with metric $G_0$, and let
$U_{xy}:F\to F$ be $G_0$-unitary routers with
$U_{yx}=U_{xy}^{-1}$.  Assume the routers act by symmetries of the local score
exponential family, so that $\Psi(U_{xy}\theta)=\Psi(\theta)$.  For positive
edge weights $\kappa_{xy}$ define
\[
 \mathscr I_\Gamma(\theta)
 :=\frac12\sum_{\{x,y\}\in E}\kappa_{xy}
 \bigl[\mathcal D(\theta_y\Vert U_{xy}\theta_x)
      +\mathcal D(\theta_x\Vert U_{yx}\theta_y)\bigr].
\]
Put
\[
 (D_Uv)_{xy}=\sqrt{\kappa_{xy}}(v_y-U_{xy}v_x).
\]

\begin{theorem}[Entropic Hodge form and minimizing movement]
\label{thm:entropic-Hodge-continuum}
For every field whose edge segments remain in the Fisher window,
\[
 \boxed{\mathscr I_\Gamma(\theta)\ge\frac{g_-}{2}\|D_U\theta\|^2.}
\]
At the primitive law,
\[
 \boxed{
 D^2\mathscr I_\Gamma(0)[v,v]
 =q_{U,G_0}(v)
 :=\sum_{\{x,y\}}\kappa_{xy}
 \langle v_y-U_{xy}v_x,G_0(v_y-U_{xy}v_x)\rangle.}
\]
Its kernel is the space of covariantly parallel fields.  If
\[
 \lambda_U:=\inf_{v\perp\Ker D_U}
 \frac{\|D_Uv\|^2}{\|v\|^2}>0,
\]
then
\[
 \boxed{q_{U,G_0}(v)\ge\frac{176}{225}\lambda_U\|v\|^2}
\]
on the protected-parallel complement.

Let $L_U$ be the self-adjoint operator associated with $q_{U,G_0}$.  The
unique minimizer of
\[
 f\longmapsto\frac1{2\tau}\|f-f_n\|_{G_0}^2+\frac12q_{U,G_0}(f)
\]
is
\[
 \boxed{f_{n+1}=W_\tau f_n,
 \qquad W_\tau=(I+\tau L_U)^{-1}.}
\]
Moreover,
\[
 \boxed{W_\tau^{\lfloor t/\tau\rfloor}\longrightarrow e^{-tL_U}}
\]
in operator norm on every fixed finite graph, uniformly for $t$ in compact
intervals.  For a cutoff family whose forms converge in the Grand-Tensor Mosco
sense, the embedded minimizing movements converge strongly to the semigroup of
the limiting form.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Apply the lower Bregman bound of
\Cref{thm:primitive-information-geometry} to both orientations of every edge.
Metric invariance makes their parameter differences have the same norm.  The
second variation at the origin is the sum of the local Fisher Hessians, which
gives $q_{U,G_0}$.  Positivity of $G_0$ identifies the kernel with
$\Ker D_U$ and gives the Poincar\'e floor.

The Euler--Lagrange equation of the strictly convex minimizing functional is
$\tau^{-1}(f-f_n)+L_Uf=0$.  Spectral calculus yields the resolvent step and
$(1+\tau\lambda)^{-\lfloor t/\tau\rfloor}\to e^{-t\lambda}$ uniformly on the
finite spectrum.  In a changing cutoff family, Mosco convergence is equivalent
to strong resolvent and semigroup convergence by \Cref{thm:GT-Mosco}; the
standard resolvent-product approximation transfers the minimizing movements to
the same limiting semigroup.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Periodic covariant information regulator]
\label{thm:periodic-covariant-information-limit}
Let $\Gamma_N=(\Z/N\Z)^d$, $h_N=N^{-1}$, and let
$A_1,\ldots,A_d$ be constant $G_0$-skew-adjoint matrices.  Put
\[
 U_{j,N}=e^{-h_NA_j},
 \qquad
 (D_{j,N}f)(x)=h_N^{-1}
 \bigl(f(x+h_Ne_j)-U_{j,N}f(x)\bigr),
\]
\[
 L_N=\sum_jD_{j,N}^{\dagger_0}D_{j,N},
 \qquad
 L_A=\sum_j(\partial_j+A_j)^{\dagger_0}(\partial_j+A_j)
\]
on $L^2(\Torus^d;F,G_0)$.  Under discrete Fourier interpolation $I_N$, for
every $\lambda>0$,
\[
 \boxed{
 \left\|I_N(L_N+\lambda)^{-1}I_N^*P_N
 -(L_A+\lambda)^{-1}\right\|\longrightarrow0.}
\]
Consequently the semigroups converge strongly, isolated eigenvalues and
spectral projections converge with multiplicity, and after shorting the kernel
\[
 \lambda_N^+\longrightarrow\lambda_A^+.
\]
The primitive information Hessians therefore have asymptotic coercive floor
\[
 \boxed{\frac{176}{225}\lambda_A^+.}
\]
For a plaquette in directions $i,j$,
\[
 U_{i,N}U_{j,N}U_{i,N}^{-1}U_{j,N}^{-1}
 =I+h_N^2[A_i,A_j]+O(h_N^3),
\]
so noncommuting matrices give a genuine non-Abelian continuum curvature.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Conjugating by $G_0^{1/2}$ reduces the metric to the Euclidean one.  On a
Fourier mode $k$, the discrete symbol is
\[
 \ell_N(k)=\sum_j h_N^{-2}
 \bigl(e^{2\pi ik_jh_N}I-e^{-h_NA_j}\bigr)^*
 \bigl(e^{2\pi ik_jh_N}I-e^{-h_NA_j}\bigr),
\]
which converges on each fixed mode to the symbol of $L_A$.  Uniform quadratic
lower bounds in $\|k\|_\infty$ make both resolvent tails uniformly small;
inside a fixed Fourier box, matrix-symbol convergence and continuity of
inversion give uniform convergence.  This proves norm-resolvent convergence.
Functional calculus gives the semigroup and spectral conclusions.  The
coercive floor follows by multiplying the graph gap by
$\lambda_{\min}(G_0)=176/225$.  The plaquette expansion is the
Baker--Campbell--Hausdorff formula through second order.
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[Explicit positive branches versus the actual regulator]
The preceding theorem proves a deterministic covariant continuum for an
explicit regulator whose routers and graph are specified by its connected
source panels.  It does not infer those panels from the marginal one-cell
renewal law.  The actual microscopic process must still reconstruct its
interaction support, router, curvature, and mean-step comparison.
\end{firewall}

\subsection{Physical continuum realization as the positive profile branch}
\label{sec:continuum-realization-definition}

\begin{definition}[Physical Grand-Tensor continuum realization]
\label{def:GT-continuum-realization}
A \emph{physical Grand-Tensor continuum realization} of an operational
regulator family is a tuple
\[
 (\mathcal A_\infty,\omega_\infty,\pi_\infty,
  \mathcal H_\infty,\{\mathcal O_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in I},
  \mathfrak P_{\Grand})
\]
with the following properties.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(C\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item $\mathcal A_\infty$ is the AF or quasilocal structural limit and
      $\omega_\infty$ is a selected compatible or canonically corrected state.
\item $(\pi_\infty,\mathcal H_\infty,\Omega_\infty)$ is its GNS
      representation.
\item Every declared observable or source has a specified linear or affine
      renormalization cocycle, including its residual compact gauge, positive
      scale, and centering modulus.
\item Every bounded family converges strongly on a common dense local domain;
      every unbounded family is represented by a named closed-form, resolvent,
      graph, or operator topology, with the corresponding domain profile.
\item Every algebraic relation, symmetry, locality statement, memory bound,
      tightness assertion, or coercive estimate attributed to the limit is the
      limit of an explicitly controlled finite residual.
\item The relevant field laws are tight, and no source, graph-energy, or
      spectral mass escapes from the declared local screens unless that escape
      is part of the stated physical limit.
\item The realization is nontrivial: a determining self-adjoint family has a
      positive limiting centered variance.
\end{enumerate}
The definition is structural and metrological.  Identifying the limit with a
manifold field, gauge theory, arithmetic operator, or PDE solution remains a
domain loading with its own comparison theorem.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Bounded observable convergence on the GNS direct limit]
\label{thm:GNS-observable-limit}
Let $\mathcal D_0=\bigcup_X\pi_\infty(\iota_{X,\infty}
\mathcal A_X)\Omega_\infty$, which is dense in $\mathcal H_\infty$.  For each
$X$, let $O_X$ be a bounded operator on the finite-stage GNS space, transported
to the later stages.  Suppose
\[
 \sup_X\|O_X\|\le C<\infty
\]
and, for every $\xi\in\mathcal D_0$, the vectors $O_X\xi$ are eventually
defined and Cauchy.  Then there is a unique bounded operator $O_\infty$ with
$\|O_\infty\|\le C$ and $O_X\xi\to O_\infty\xi$ for every
$\xi\in\mathcal D_0$.

If $p$ is a noncommutative $*$-polynomial in finitely many such families and
$\|p(O_{1,X},\ldots,O_{r,X})\xi\|\to0$ on $\mathcal D_0$, then
$p(O_{1,\infty},\ldots,O_{r,\infty})=0$.  If the centered vacuum vectors
converge and
\[
 \liminf_X\|(O_X-\omega_X(O_X))\Omega_X\|\ge c>0,
\]
then the limiting observable is non-scalar.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Define $O_\infty\xi=\lim_XO_X\xi$ on $\mathcal D_0$.  The uniform norm bound
gives $\|O_\infty\xi\|\le C\|\xi\|$, so the map extends uniquely to the
Hilbert completion.  Strong convergence on a common dense domain, together
with uniform boundedness, passes finite sums, products, and adjoints when the
adjoint families satisfy the same hypothesis.  The polynomial residual
therefore vanishes on a dense domain.  The last lower bound gives a nonzero
centered limiting vector, excluding a scalar operator.
\end{proof}

\begin{assessment}[Exact scope of Part I-B]
Part I-B now has four distinct unconditional outputs.  A globally consistent
operational process gives the raw structural limit or a finite cutoff
innovation.  Approximate families give either a canonical summable correction,
a projective limit set, or a finite separator.  Every declared bounded or
unbounded observable has a renormalization class and a convergence profile
which either yields a limit or returns a metric, domain, resolvent, spectral,
or mass-escape witness.  In addition, the resolved primitive branch table
supplies its complete three-dimensional score tangent, the noncollapsing Fisher
metric $G_0$, the conditional information action, the exact predictable
mean/noise short, and a canonical Brownian fluctuation--dissipation continuum.
Covariant information forms give an explicit deterministic semigroup branch,
including flat and constant-curvature periodic regulators with norm-resolvent
convergence.  These concrete branches do not infer the actual physical graph,
router, or field semantic from one-cell renewal data.  The positive physical-
continuum branch still requires the connected and domain-specific margins to
pass; it is not inferred from finite structural existence alone.
\end{assessment}


% =============================================================================
\section{Part I-C: Intrinsic locality, memory, and complete continuum alternatives}
\label{sec:universal-continuum-certification}
\label{sec:robust-certification}
% =============================================================================

Part I-B constructs the structural carriers, corrected state families,
renormalization classes, and bounded or unbounded analytic limits.  Part I-C
asks whether the selected physical source is saturated, whether locality and
memory are intrinsic and regulator stable, whether fields and spectral mass
remain tight, and whether coercivity and nontriviality survive.  The universal
result is not that every family lies on the positive branch.  It is that every
audit-ready family has a complete profile and therefore yields either a
controlled continuum realization or a concrete operational obstruction.

\subsection{Source saturation and exact Hankel exhaustion}
\label{sec:source-completeness}

\begin{definition}[Physical source-cyclic subspace]
For a finite triple $(\mathcal U,G,B)$ with $G=G^*\succeq0$, define
\[
 \mathcal U_{\rm cyc}
 :=\Span\{p(G)Bv:p\in\C[z],\ v\in\mathcal P\}.
\]
The triple is source minimal when $\mathcal U_{\rm cyc}=\mathcal U$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Physical-source completeness and unique minimal realization]
\label{thm:source-minimality}
For every finite triple $(\mathcal U,G,B)$:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2.8em]
\item $\mathcal U_{\rm cyc}$ reduces $G$;
\item every moment $B^*G^nB$ and every block $B^*f(G)B$ depends only on the
      compression to $\mathcal U_{\rm cyc}$;
\item $\mathcal U_{\rm cyc}^{\perp}$ is invisible to all declared source
      correlations and may be removed from the minimal operational
      realization;
\item two finite source-minimal triples with identical all-order moments are
      related by a unique source-fixing unitary intertwining their positive
      responses.
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Polynomial invariance makes $\mathcal U_{\rm cyc}$ invariant under $G$.
Because $G$ is self-adjoint, the orthogonal complement is invariant as well,
so the subspace reduces $G$.  Compression proves the moment statements.

For uniqueness, define on polynomial source vectors
\[
 W_0\left(\sum_{j=0}^NG^jBv_j\right)
 :=\sum_{j=0}^N(G')^jB'v_j.
\]
Every pairwise inner product is a finite linear combination of the common
moments, so $W_0$ is well defined and isometric.  Source minimality makes its
domain and range the full spaces.  Its unitary extension satisfies $WB=B'$
and $WG=G'W$, and polynomial source vectors prove uniqueness.
\end{proof}


\begin{theorem}[Primitive-writer saturation]
\label{thm:primitive-writer-saturation}
Let $\mathcal A$ be a unital $C^*$-algebra represented in the GNS space of a
state $\omega$, and let $z$ be a central projection selecting a retained
source sector.  If a $*$-subalgebra $\mathfrak B\subseteq z\mathcal A$ with unit $z$
is norm dense in $z\mathcal A$, then
\[
 \boxed{\overline{\pi_\omega(\mathfrak B)\Omega_\omega}
 =\overline{\pi_\omega(z\mathcal A)\Omega_\omega}.}
\]
At finite cutoff, algebraic generation of the selected finite-dimensional
algebra is sufficient.  If the state is faithful on $z\mathcal A$, every
nonzero selected algebra element is detected by a finite primitive-word
combination.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The GNS map $a\mapsto\pi_\omega(a)\Omega_\omega$ is norm continuous because
$\|\pi_\omega(a)\Omega_\omega\|^2=\omega(a^*a)\le\|a\|^2$.  Therefore the
image of a norm-dense subalgebra is dense in the image of the full selected
algebra.  In finite dimension, a generating unital $*$-subalgebra is already
closed and equals the selected algebra.  Faithfulness makes
$\pi_\omega(a)\Omega_\omega=0$ equivalent to $a=0$, so a nonzero element has a
nonzero matrix coefficient against a finite dense primitive span.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Global-record obstruction to local saturation]
\label{thm:global-record-saturation-obstruction}
Let a unitary $U$ fix the physical source vector $\Omega$ and every primitive
writer in $\mathfrak B$.  If $v$ satisfies $Uv=\chi v$ with $\chi\ne1$, then
$v\perp\overline{\mathfrak B\Omega}$.  Consequently a source sector carrying a
nontrivial global record character cannot be recovered after that record has
been discarded from the primitive interface.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
For every $b\in\mathfrak B$,
$U(b\Omega)=b\Omega$.  Hence
$\langle v,b\Omega\rangle=\langle Uv,U(b\Omega)\rangle
=\overline\chi\langle v,b\Omega\rangle$, which vanishes because
$\chi\ne1$.  Closure gives the result.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Universal block-Hankel exhaustion]
\label{thm:universal-Hankel-exhaustion}
Let $0\preceq T\preceq I$ on a Hilbert space and let
$S_R:E_R\to\mathcal H$ be a nested finite source family.  Put
\[
 \mathbb H_{R,n}^{(r)}
 =[S_R^*T^{i+j+r}S_R]_{0\le i,j<n},\qquad r=0,1,2,
\]
and
\[
 \mathcal K_{R,n}=\Span\{T^j\Ran S_R:0\le j<n\}.
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{\rank\mathbb H_{R,n}^{(0)}=\dim\mathcal K_{R,n},}
\]
and the generalized radius
\[
 q_{R,n}=
 \sup_{c\notin\Ker\mathbb H_{R,n}^{(0)}}
 \frac{c^*\mathbb H_{R,n}^{(1)}c}
      {c^*\mathbb H_{R,n}^{(0)}c}
\]
is the norm of the compression of $T$ to $\mathcal K_{R,n}$.  If
$\overline{\bigcup_{R,n}\mathcal K_{R,n}}=\mathcal H_{\mathrm{sel}}$, then
\[
 \boxed{\|T|_{\mathcal H_{\mathrm{sel}}}\|=\sup_{R,n}q_{R,n}.}
\]
No independent cyclicity hypothesis remains once primitive-writer saturation
has supplied the displayed density.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
For $c=(c_0,\ldots,c_{n-1})$, let
$\mathcal C_{R,n}c=\sum_{j=0}^{n-1}T^jS_Rc_j$.  Then
$\mathcal C_{R,n}^*\mathcal C_{R,n}=\mathbb H_{R,n}^{(0)}$ and
$\mathcal C_{R,n}^*T\mathcal C_{R,n}=\mathbb H_{R,n}^{(1)}$.
The Gram rank is therefore the Krylov dimension, and the generalized quotient
is the Rayleigh quotient of the compressed positive operator.  The finite
Krylov spaces are nested.  The quadratic form of a bounded self-adjoint
operator is norm continuous, so taking the supremum over a dense union gives
the full selected norm.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Universal moment-exact leakage]
\label{thm:universal-moment-leakage}
Let $P_{R,n}$ be the orthogonal projection onto $\mathcal K_{R,n}$.  On
$\mathcal E_{R,n}=\Ran\mathbb H_{R,n}^{(0)}$, define
\[
 A_{R,n}=(\mathbb H_{R,n}^{(0)})^{\dagger/2}
          \mathbb H_{R,n}^{(1)}
          (\mathbb H_{R,n}^{(0)})^{\dagger/2}
\]
and
\[
 \boxed{\mathbb V_{R,n}
 =(\mathbb H_{R,n}^{(0)})^{\dagger/2}
   \mathbb H_{R,n}^{(2)}
   (\mathbb H_{R,n}^{(0)})^{\dagger/2}-A_{R,n}^2.}
\]
Then $\mathbb V_{R,n}\succeq0$,
\[
 \boxed{\|\mathbb V_{R,n}\|
 =\|(I-P_{R,n})TP_{R,n}\|^2,}
\]
and
\[
 \boxed{\rank\mathbb V_{R,n}
 =\dim(\mathcal K_{R,n+1}\ominus\mathcal K_{R,n}).}
\]
It vanishes exactly when the finite head is invariant under $T$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Whiten the controllability map by
$(\mathbb H_{R,n}^{(0)})^{\dagger/2}$ to obtain an isometry $V_{R,n}$ onto
$\mathcal K_{R,n}$.  With $P_{R,n}=V_{R,n}V_{R,n}^*$ and
$Q_{R,n}=I-P_{R,n}$,
\[
 \mathbb V_{R,n}=V_{R,n}^*TQ_{R,n}TV_{R,n}
 =(Q_{R,n}TV_{R,n})^*(Q_{R,n}TV_{R,n}).
\]
Its norm is the squared head-to-tail coupling and its range is precisely the
new component of $T\mathcal K_{R,n}$.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Two-stage flatness and finite localizer saturation]
\label{cor:GT-two-stage-localizer-flatness}
At a finite cutoff, first reconstruct the flat word algebra and descend the
physical score localizer by \Cref{thm:GT-word-localizer-descent}.  Let $T$ be
that positive localizer on the supported word quotient and let $S$ be the
physical source synthesis.  The Krylov spaces
\[
 \mathcal K_n=\Span\{T^j\Ran S:0\le j<n\}
\]
form an increasing finite sequence.  At each stage the leakage Gram of
\Cref{thm:universal-moment-leakage} has rank
$\dim(\mathcal K_{n+1}\ominus\mathcal K_n)$ and its polar synthesis is the
canonical new action--Krylov bank.  The sequence terminates after finitely many
strict increases.  At the first zero leakage, $\mathcal K_n$ reduces $T$ and
contains every localizer moment visible from the physical source.  On a
source-minimal or atlas-complete branch this is the complete physical localizer
carrier, so its spectrum, floor, kernel, and functional calculus are global.
Before that zero, they are only head-relative quantities.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The rank statement and zero criterion are
\Cref{thm:universal-moment-leakage}.  Each nonzero leakage strictly increases
the finite Krylov dimension, so termination is forced.  At zero leakage the
head is invariant under the self-adjoint localizer and therefore reducing.
Source minimality or zero atlas residual identifies the reducing Krylov carrier
with the complete selected physical carrier.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Complete physical writer atlas]
\label{def:GT-complete-writer-atlas}
Let $U:\C^M\to\mathcal H_{\rm phys}$ be an independently physical writer
synthesis with $\Ran U=\mathcal H_{\rm phys}$.  Its frame floor is
\[
 \boxed{m_U:=\lambda_{\min}(UU^*)>0.}
 \tag{SA.1}
\]
For a candidate response carrier $\mathcal K\subseteq\mathcal H_{\rm phys}$,
put
\[
 \boxed{\mathbb C_{U\mid\mathcal K}
 =U^*(I-P_{\mathcal K})U\succeq0.}
 \tag{SA.2}
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Atlas-relative source completeness]
\label{thm:GT-atlas-completeness}
For the packet of \Cref{def:GT-complete-writer-atlas},
\[
 \boxed{
 \rank\mathbb C_{U\mid\mathcal K}
 =\dim\mathcal H_{\rm phys}-\dim\mathcal K,}
 \tag{SA.3}
\]
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathbb C_{U\mid\mathcal K}=0
 \iff\mathcal K=\mathcal H_{\rm phys}.}
 \tag{SA.4}
\]
If $\mathcal K\neq\mathcal H_{\rm phys}$, then
\[
 \boxed{\|\mathbb C_{U\mid\mathcal K}\|\ge m_U.}
 \tag{SA.5}
\]
The source-minimal missing bank is
\[
 \boxed{
 J_{U\mid\mathcal K}^{\rm miss}
 =(I-P_{\mathcal K})U
 \mathbb C_{U\mid\mathcal K}^{\dagger/2},}
 \tag{SA.6}
\]
and its coefficient dimension is exactly the number of missing physical source
directions.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The map $(I-P_{\mathcal K})U$ is onto $\mathcal K^\perp$ because $U$ is onto
$\mathcal H_{\rm phys}$, proving the rank and zero criteria.  For a unit vector
$y\in\mathcal K^\perp$,
$\|U^*y\|^2=\langle y,UU^*y\rangle\ge m_U$, while
$\|U^*y\|\le\|(I-P_{\mathcal K})U\|$; this gives \textup{(SA.5)}.  The
Moore--Penrose normalization in \textup{(SA.6)} is an isometry on the support
and has range $\mathcal K^\perp$.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Linear response-backbone dimension]
\label{def:GT-response-backbone}
For a finite self-adjoint physical response $T$ on $\mathcal H$, define
\[
 \boxed{
 b_{\rm resp}(T)
 =\min\bigl\{r:\exists J:\C^r\to\mathcal H,
 \ \Span_{n\ge0}T^n\Ran J=\mathcal H\bigr\}.}
 \tag{SA.7}
\]
The source columns of $J$ must be physical linear combinations of a complete
writer atlas.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Spectral multiplicity and the minimum response backbone]
\label{thm:GT-response-backbone}
For finite self-adjoint $T$,
\[
 \boxed{
 b_{\rm resp}(T)
 =\max_{\lambda\in\spec T}\dim\Ker(T-\lambda I).}
 \tag{SA.8}
\]
Consequently occurrence grade, physical-carrier dimension, and response-
backbone dimension are independent invariants.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
