Let $T_0$ be an old finite transfer and let an enlarged transfer be
\[
 \widetilde T=\begin{pmatrix}A&B\\ C&D\end{pmatrix}
\]
relative to the old carrier and an external carrier.  If
$X_n=P\widetilde T^nJ$, then
\[
 \boxed{K_k=BD^kC,\qquad
 X_{n+1}=AX_n+\sum_{j=0}^{n-1}K_{n-1-j}X_j,\quad X_0=I,}
\]
and
\[
 \boxed{\sum_{n\ge0}X_nz^n
 =[I-zA-z^2B(I-zD)^{-1}C]^{-1}.}
\]
Moreover,
\[
 \boxed{X_n=T_0^n\ \forall n
 \iff A=T_0\text{ and }BD^kC=0\ \forall k\ge0.}
\]
In finite external dimension it is enough to test
$0\le k<\dim\mathcal E$.  The stabilized block-Hankel rank of
$[BD^{i+j}C]_{i,j}$ is the minimal added linear feedback memory.  More
precisely, it is the dimension of the canonical quotient
\[
 \frac{\Span\{D^kC\mathcal L:k\ge0\}}
 {\Span\{D^kC\mathcal L:k\ge0\}
  \cap\bigcap_{k\ge0}\Ker(BD^k)},
\]
which is the unique reachable--observable realization of the returned kernels.
The kernels themselves are recursively recovered from the compressed powers
by \Cref{thm:pre-renewal-visible-recovery}.

If $\widetilde T$ and $T_0$ are contractions, then
\[
 \boxed{\|X_n-T_0^n\|
 \le n\|A-T_0\|+
 \sum_{k=0}^{n-2}(n-1-k)\|BD^kC\|.}
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Block multiplication groups every old-to-old path according to its last
external excursion, giving the convolution equation; summing formal series
gives the Schur resolvent.  Equality at $n=1$ gives $A=T_0$.  Once
$K_0,\ldots,K_{r-1}$ vanish, the first possible additional term in
$X_{r+2}$ is $K_r$, so induction gives the exact criterion.  Cayley--Hamilton
reduces the infinite list to the first $\dim\mathcal E$ powers.  Standard
reachable/observable realization theory identifies the stabilized Hankel rank
with the external reachable subspace modulo its future-unobservable part.

For the norm estimate, put $e_n=\|X_n-T_0^n\|$.  Contractivity and the
convolution equation give
\[
 e_{n+1}\le e_n+\|A-T_0\|+\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}\|BD^kC\|.
\]
Iterating from $e_0=0$ and reversing the order of summation yields the displayed
bound.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Source-minimal retained-tail derivative]
\label{cor:GT-returned-tail-derivative}
For a retained-plus-tail linearization
$\begin{psmallmatrix}A&B\\C&D\end{psmallmatrix}$ with $\|D\|<1$, the exact
reduced derivative on the invariant tail graph is
\[
 \boxed{
 A+B(I-D)^{-1}C
 =A+\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}BD^nC.}
 \tag{RT.1}
\]
It depends only on the reachable--observable returned quotient already
identified in \Cref{thm:universal-feedback-memory}.  The stabilized Hankel rank
of $[BD^{i+j}C]$ is the exact minimum tail dimension relevant to this retained
linear response.
\end{corollary}

\begin{theorem}[Associativity of invariant-tail elimination]
\label{thm:GT-staged-tail-elimination}
Let the tail split as $R=R_1\oplus R_2$, write
\[
 B=(B_1\ B_2),\quad C=\binom{C_1}{C_2},\quad
 D=\begin{pmatrix}D_{11}&D_{12}\\D_{21}&D_{22}\end{pmatrix},
\]
and assume $\|D\|<1$.  Put $R_2^0=(I-D_{22})^{-1}$ and
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \widetilde A&=A+B_2R_2^0C_2,&
 \widetilde B&=B_1+B_2R_2^0D_{21},\\
 \widetilde C&=C_1+D_{12}R_2^0C_2,&
 \widetilde D&=D_{11}+D_{12}R_2^0D_{21}.
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{RT.2}
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{
 A+B(I-D)^{-1}C
 =\widetilde A+\widetilde B(I-\widetilde D)^{-1}\widetilde C.}
 \tag{RT.3}
\]
Thus exact elimination of finitely many tail strata is order independent.  A
stratum with no direct retained entrance can still be indispensable through a
path entering it from another tail stratum and returning to the head.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Solve the $R_2$ component of the invariant-tail equation
$r=Cx+Dr$ and substitute it into the $R_1$ component.  The resulting system is
\textup{(RT.2)}, and uniqueness of the full solution gives \textup{(RT.3)}.
Repeated elimination is block Gaussian elimination of the same invertible
system.
\end{proof}

\begin{countertheorem}[Zero aggregate self-energy is not no return]
\label{cth:GT-return-cancellation}
The equality $B(I-D)^{-1}C=0$ does not imply that the returned quotient
vanishes.  There are finite stable packets with nonzero returned words which
cancel in the aggregate sum.
\end{countertheorem}

\begin{proof}
Take a one-dimensional retained space, a two-dimensional tail,
$0<t<1$, and
\[
 C=\binom10,\qquad
 D=\begin{pmatrix}0&0\\t&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad
 B=\begin{pmatrix}1&-t^{-1}\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Then $BD^0C=1$, $BDC=-1$, and $BD^nC=0$ for $n\ge2$.  The aggregate correction
vanishes, while the returned Hankel sequence has positive rank.
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[Scope of the returned quotient]
A tail direction absent from the returned quotient is silent only for the
declared linear retained response at the chosen point.  It may still affect
higher nonlinear jets, another observable, reflection positivity, global
stability, or a different boundary row.  The quotient is source minimal for
one response problem; it is not a license to delete the full physical shell
law.
\end{firewall}

\begin{theorem}[Connected residual under exact factorization]
\label{thm:connected-residual-factorization}
Suppose a parameterized operational transfer and state factor exactly as
\[
 T_{\boldsymbol\theta}=\bigotimes_{c\in\mathcal C}T_{c,\theta_c},
 \qquad
 \Omega_{\boldsymbol\theta}=\bigotimes_{c\in\mathcal C}
 \Omega_{c,\theta_c},
\]
and a centered source is supported in one component $c_0$.  Then every mixed
Taylor coefficient of its vacuum-relative future residual vanishes whenever
the differentiated components contain a connected component disjoint from
$c_0$.  Thus nonzero coefficients are supported on connected interaction
clusters meeting the source.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Split the differentiated components into the component $A$ containing $c_0$
and a disjoint union $B$.  Exact tensor factorization makes the normalized
vacuum-relative source residual equal to its $A$-residual tensored with the
identity on $B$; it is therefore independent of every parameter in $B$.
Every mixed derivative using a parameter from $B$ vanishes.
\end{proof}



% =============================================================================
\subsection{Weighted critical locality, pair-collar propagation, and quasilocal
Osterwalder--Schrader transport}
\label{sec:GT-weighted-critical-locality}
% =============================================================================

The finite interaction and compactness calculus must retain locality as a
separate physical coordinate.  Ordinary operator-norm analyticity controls
critical response but need not control spatial tails; a local endpoint can
hide a long insertion route; and source-local contact subtraction need not
produce a quasilocal represented operator.  The following weighted calculus
separates these issues and transports the resulting collar data through the
Osterwalder--Schrader quotient.

\subsubsection{Purpose, upstream audit, and the locality target}
\label{subsec:GTLOC-purpose}

\begin{assessment}[Why locality is the first new analytic row]
The preceding critical-form construction closes the critical half-form first and pair responses, their
form-compatible regularization, source-relative contact limit, local
counterterm quotient, and norm-form/resolvent transport.  It also proves by an
explicit off-diagonal example that a common holomorphic form domain does not
imply locality.  Consequently another critical-pair existence theorem,
minimum-norm lift, same-source Green transform, or finite sampling argument
would be downstream repetition.

The first unsupported analytic row is now spatial: whether the selected
positive-time first and pair responses admit one regulator-uniform local or
quasilocal collar, whether that collar survives contact subtraction and cutoff
transport, and whether it descends to the selected Osterwalder--Schrader
quotient.  The present locality calculus supplies an exact weighted finite-cutoff calculus, a
source-relative locality leakage Gram, pair-path estimates, locality-preserving
renormalization and transport, and a terminating OS handoff.  No physical
metric, local decomposition, common form family, pair response, connected
writer, or determinant/Pfaffian line is manufactured.
\end{assessment}

\begin{firewall}[Three locality claims]
The following targets are distinct:
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \begin{gathered}
 \text{endpoint locality of an integrated response},\\
 \text{route locality of the ordered split insertion},\\
 \text{quasilocality of the represented OS algebra}.
 \end{gathered}}
 \label{eq:GTLOC-three-locality-targets}
\end{equation}
An endpoint response may return to its original source after a long hidden
excursion.  Route locality therefore requires the split response or an
equivalent physical support panel.  Quasilocality of the OS algebra further
requires that the local representatives descend through the OS null ideal and
remain compatible with products and cutoff transport.
\end{firewall}

% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
\subsubsection{Weighted block algebra and exact locality leakage}
\label{subsec:GTLOC-weighted-algebra}
% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

\begin{definition}[Metric block carrier and weighted Schur algebra]
\label{def:GTLOC-weighted-Schur}
Let $(\Gamma,d)$ be a finite or countable metric set and let
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathcal H_\Gamma=\bigoplus_{x\in\Gamma}\mathcal H_x}
 \label{eq:GTLOC-block-carrier}
\end{equation}
be one physical block decomposition, with block projections $P_x$.  For
$T\in\mathcal B(\mathcal H_\Gamma)$ write $T_{xy}=P_xTP_y$.  For
$\alpha\ge0$ define
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \begin{aligned}
 \norm{T}_{\alpha,\mathrm{Sch}}
 =\max\Bigl\{&
 \sup_{x\in\Gamma}\sum_{y\in\Gamma}
 e^{\alpha d(x,y)}\norm{T_{xy}},\\
 &\sup_{y\in\Gamma}\sum_{x\in\Gamma}
 e^{\alpha d(x,y)}\norm{T_{xy}}
 \Bigr\}. 
 \end{aligned}}
 \label{eq:GTLOC-weighted-Schur-norm}
\end{equation}
Denote the resulting Banach space by
$\mathfrak B_\alpha(\Gamma)$.  For $X\subseteq\Gamma$ put
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 X^{[R]}=\{y\in\Gamma:d(y,X)\le R\},
 \qquad P_X=\sum_{x\in X}^{\mathrm{s}}P_x.}
 \label{eq:GTLOC-collar-projection}
\end{equation}
The sum defining $P_X$ is taken in the strong operator topology.  The metric
and block decomposition are physical data and must be fixed before any decay
exponent is fitted.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Weighted Schur algebra]
\label{thm:GTLOC-weighted-Schur-algebra}
For every $\alpha\ge0$ and $S,T\in\mathfrak B_\alpha(\Gamma)$,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \norm{ST}_{\alpha,\mathrm{Sch}}
 \le
 \norm{S}_{\alpha,\mathrm{Sch}}
 \norm{T}_{\alpha,\mathrm{Sch}},
 \qquad
 \norm{T^*}_{\alpha,\mathrm{Sch}}
 =\norm{T}_{\alpha,\mathrm{Sch}}.}
 \label{eq:GTLOC-Schur-submultiplicative}
\end{equation}
Moreover,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \norm{T}_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le\norm{T}_{\alpha,\mathrm{Sch}},}
 \label{eq:GTLOC-Schur-dominates-op}
\end{equation}
and for $X,Y\subseteq\Gamma$ with $d(X,Y)\ge R$,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \norm{P_YTP_X}_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le e^{-\alpha R}\norm{T}_{\alpha,\mathrm{Sch}}.}
 \label{eq:GTLOC-offdiagonal-Schur}
\end{equation}
Thus $\mathfrak B_\alpha(\Gamma)$ is a finite Banach $*$-algebra encoding one
exponential quasilocal collar.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
For the row part of the product norm, use
$d(x,z)\le d(x,y)+d(y,z)$ and obtain
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 &\sum_z e^{\alpha d(x,z)}\norm{(ST)_{xz}}\\
 &\quad\le
 \sum_y e^{\alpha d(x,y)}\norm{S_{xy}}
 \sum_z e^{\alpha d(y,z)}\norm{T_{yz}}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Taking the supremum gives the product of the two row bounds.  The column bound
is identical.  Adjoint exchanges the row and column expressions.  The ordinary
Schur test gives \eqref{eq:GTLOC-Schur-dominates-op}.  On the restricted block
$P_YTP_X$, every nonzero matrix block has $d(x,y)\ge R$; removing the weight
therefore contributes $e^{-\alpha R}$ in both the row and column Schur sums.
A second application of the ordinary Schur test proves
\eqref{eq:GTLOC-offdiagonal-Schur}.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Source-relative locality leakage Gram]
\label{def:GTLOC-locality-leakage}
Let $J_X:E\to\mathcal H_\Gamma$ be a finite source synthesis with
$P_XJ_X=J_X$.  For $T\in\mathcal B(\mathcal H_\Gamma)$ define
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathbb L_R^{\mathrm{loc}}(T\mid J_X)
 =J_X^*T^*(I-P_{X^{[R]}})TJ_X\succeq0.}
 \label{eq:GTLOC-locality-leakage-Gram}
\end{equation}
Its rank is the number of selected response directions which first leave the
physical collar $X^{[R]}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Exact collar criterion and exponential bound]
\label{thm:GTLOC-locality-leakage}
For the packet of \Cref{def:GTLOC-locality-leakage},
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathbb L_R^{\mathrm{loc}}(T\mid J_X)=0
 \iff
 (I-P_{X^{[R]}})TJ_X=0.}
 \label{eq:GTLOC-exact-collar-zero}
\end{equation}
If $T\in\mathfrak B_\alpha(\Gamma)$, then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 0\preceq
 \mathbb L_R^{\mathrm{loc}}(T\mid J_X)
 \preceq
 e^{-2\alpha R}
 \norm{T}_{\alpha,\mathrm{Sch}}^2
 J_X^*J_X.}
 \label{eq:GTLOC-locality-leakage-bound}
\end{equation}
The polar synthesis of
$(I-P_{X^{[R]}})TJ_X$ is the unique source-minimal missing collar bank.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The Gram vanishes exactly when its synthesized operator vanishes.  Since the
source lies in $X$, \eqref{eq:GTLOC-offdiagonal-Schur} gives
\[
 \norm{(I-P_{X^{[R]}})TP_X}
 \le e^{-\alpha R}\norm{T}_{\alpha,\mathrm{Sch}}.
\]
Taking the congruence by $J_X$ gives the operator-order estimate.  The final
claim is the ordinary polar minimality theorem for a finite source synthesis.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Target-relative collar radius]
\label{def:GTLOC-collar-radius}
For a tolerance $\varepsilon>0$, define
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 R_\varepsilon(T\mid J_X)
 =\inf\left\{
 R\ge0:
 \norm{\mathbb L_R^{\mathrm{loc}}(T\mid J_X)}
 \le\varepsilon^2
 \right\}.}
 \label{eq:GTLOC-target-collar-radius}
\end{equation}
This target-relative radius is the native locality output when a uniform global
decay exponent is stronger than the intended physical claim.
\end{definition}

% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
\subsubsection{Critical half-form locality by weighted holomorphy}
\label{subsec:GTLOC-critical-locality}
% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

For this complementary similarity-weight formulation, write
$\Lambda=\Gamma$ and
$\mathfrak A_\mu(\Lambda)=\mathfrak B_\mu(\Gamma)$.

\begin{definition}[Lipschitz-weight similarity norm]
\label{def:GTLOC-Lipschitz-norm}
At one finite cutoff, let $\mathrm{Lip}_1(\Lambda)$ be the real
$1$-Lipschitz functions on $\Lambda$.  For $\phi\in\mathrm{Lip}_1(\Lambda)$
and $a\in\mathbb R$, put
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 W_{a,\phi}
 =\bigoplus_{x\in\Lambda}e^{a\phi(x)}I_{\mathcal H_x}.}
 \label{eq:GTLOC-Lipschitz-weight}
\end{equation}
Define
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \norm{T}_{\mu,\mathrm{Lip}}
 =\sup_{\phi\in\mathrm{Lip}_1(\Lambda)}
   \sup_{|a|\le\mu}
 \norm{W_{a,\phi}TW_{a,\phi}^{-1}}.}
 \label{eq:GTLOC-Lipschitz-norm}
\end{equation}
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Schur-to-Lipschitz domination]
\label{lem:GTLOC-Schur-Lipschitz}
For every $T\in\mathfrak A_\mu(\Lambda)$,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \norm{T}_{\mu,\mathrm{Lip}}
 \le\norm{T}_{\mu,\mathrm{Sch}}.}
 \label{eq:GTLOC-Schur-Lipschitz}
\end{equation}
Moreover, for every $X,Y\subseteq\Lambda$,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \norm{P_XTP_Y}
 \le e^{-\mu d(X,Y)}\norm{T}_{\mu,\mathrm{Lip}}.}
 \label{eq:GTLOC-Lipschitz-offdiagonal}
\end{equation}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
The $(x,y)$ block of the weighted conjugate is multiplied by
$e^{a(\phi(x)-\phi(y))}$, whose modulus is at most
$e^{\mu d(x,y)}$.  The block Schur test proves
\eqref{eq:GTLOC-Schur-Lipschitz}.  For the second claim, choose
$\phi(x)=d(x,Y)$, truncated if desired.  Then $\phi=0$ on $Y$ and
$\phi\ge d(X,Y)$ on $X$.  Writing
\[
 P_XTP_Y
 =P_XW_{\mu,\phi}^{-1}
   (W_{\mu,\phi}TW_{\mu,\phi}^{-1})
   W_{\mu,\phi}P_Y
\]
gives the stated factor.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Weighted critical common-form packet]
\label{def:GTLOC-weighted-critical-packet}
Let $A(z,w)$ be an inherited critical common-form family on a finite metric carrier,
holomorphic on
\[
 \mathbb D_{r_B,r_C}
 =\{(z,w):|z|<r_B,\ |w|<r_C\}.
\]
It has a \emph{$(\mu,M,v)$ weighted collar} on a time interval $I$ when
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \sup_{\substack{\phi\in\mathrm{Lip}_1(\Lambda),\ |a|\le\mu\\
                  |z|=r_B,\ |w|=r_C,\ t\in I}}
 e^{-vt}
 \norm{
 W_{a,\phi}e^{-tA(z,w)}W_{a,\phi}^{-1}}
 \le M.}
 \label{eq:GTLOC-weighted-critical-collar}
\end{equation}
The same physical metric, command family, and reflected semigroup must be used
for every entry in this supremum.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Critical weighted first/pair locality]
\label{thm:GTLOC-critical-weighted-locality}
If \eqref{eq:GTLOC-weighted-critical-collar} holds, then for every $t\in I$,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \norm{\mathfrak D_{t,A}^{\mathrm{crit}}(B)}_{\mu,\mathrm{Lip}}
 \le\frac{M}{r_B}e^{vt},}
 \label{eq:GTLOC-critical-first-weighted}
\end{equation}
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \norm{\mathfrak Q_{t,A}^{\mathrm{crit}}(B,C)}_{\mu,\mathrm{Lip}}
 \le\frac{M}{r_Br_C}e^{vt}.}
 \label{eq:GTLOC-critical-pair-weighted}
\end{equation}
Consequently
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \norm{P_X\mathfrak D_{t,A}^{\mathrm{crit}}(B)P_Y}
 \le\frac{M}{r_B}e^{vt-\mu d(X,Y)},}
 \label{eq:GTLOC-critical-first-offdiagonal}
\end{equation}
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \norm{P_X\mathfrak Q_{t,A}^{\mathrm{crit}}(B,C)P_Y}
 \le\frac{M}{r_Br_C}e^{vt-\mu d(X,Y)}.}
 \label{eq:GTLOC-critical-pair-offdiagonal}
\end{equation}
Thus the inherited critical pair inherits a physical exponential collar without
being represented by an absolutely convergent factorwise simplex majorant.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Fix $a,\phi$ and conjugate the holomorphic semigroup family by
$W_{a,\phi}$.  Cauchy's formula on the two command circles gives
\[
 \norm{W_{a,\phi}\partial_zP_t(0,0)W_{a,\phi}^{-1}}
 \le r_B^{-1}Me^{vt},
\]
\[
 \norm{W_{a,\phi}\partial_z\partial_wP_t(0,0)
 W_{a,\phi}^{-1}}
 \le(r_Br_C)^{-1}Me^{vt}.
\]
Taking the supremum proves the weighted bounds.  Apply
\eqref{eq:GTLOC-Lipschitz-offdiagonal} for the spatial estimates.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Bounded conjugation-defect certificate]
\label{prop:GTLOC-conjugation-defect}
Suppose every command on the closed polydisc generates a quasi-contractive
semigroup
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \norm{e^{-tA(z,w)}}\le e^{v_0t}.}
 \label{eq:GTLOC-unweighted-command-growth}
\end{equation}
Assume that for every $\phi\in\mathrm{Lip}_1(\Lambda)$, $|a|\le\mu$, and
command in that polydisc, the conjugated generator satisfies on one common
domain
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 W_{a,\phi}A(z,w)W_{a,\phi}^{-1}
 =A(z,w)+K_{a,\phi}(z,w),
 \qquad
 \norm{K_{a,\phi}(z,w)}\le\kappa_\mu.}
 \label{eq:GTLOC-bounded-conjugation-defect}
\end{equation}
Then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \norm{W_{a,\phi}e^{-tA(z,w)}W_{a,\phi}^{-1}}
 \le e^{(v_0+\kappa_\mu)t}.}
 \label{eq:GTLOC-conjugation-semigroup-bound}
\end{equation}
Hence \Cref{thm:GTLOC-critical-weighted-locality} applies with
$M=1$, $v=v_0+\kappa_\mu$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
The conjugated generator is a bounded perturbation of the quasi-contractive
semigroup generator.  The bounded perturbation theorem, or its Duhamel series,
gives the growth bound $e^{(v_0+\kappa_\mu)t}$.
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[The weighted collar is a physical row]
The bounded conjugation defect is a sufficient analytic certificate.  It is
not inferred from positivity, common-domain holomorphy, or unweighted
norm-resolvent convergence.  In an actual regulator the metric labels,
Lipschitz weights, coefficient commands, and physical slab must be jointly
available before \eqref{eq:GTLOC-weighted-critical-collar} is reported.
\end{firewall}

% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
\subsubsection{Commutator hierarchy and its information boundary}
\label{subsec:GTLOC-commutators}
% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

\begin{theorem}[Lipschitz commutator hierarchy]
\label{thm:GTLOC-commutator-hierarchy}
Let $f:\Lambda\to\mathbb R$ be $1$-Lipschitz and let $M_f$ be diagonal
multiplication.  For $T\in\mathfrak A_\mu(\Lambda)$ and every integer $n\ge1$,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \norm{\operatorname{ad}_{M_f}^{n}(T)}
 \le\frac{n!}{\mu^n}\norm{T}_{\mu,\mathrm{Sch}}.}
 \label{eq:GTLOC-commutator-hierarchy}
\end{equation}
In particular, the weighted first and pair responses have finite
commutators of every order with every physical Lipschitz coordinate.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The $(x,y)$ block of the $n$-fold commutator is
$(f(x)-f(y))^nT_{xy}$.  Since
$|f(x)-f(y)|\le d(x,y)$ and
\[
 r^n\le n!\mu^{-n}e^{\mu r}
 \qquad(r\ge0),
\]
the ordinary row and column Schur sums of the commutator are bounded by the
right side of \eqref{eq:GTLOC-commutator-hierarchy}.
\end{proof}

\begin{countertheorem}[Finitely many commutator bounds do not prove exponential locality]
\label{cth:GTLOC-finite-commutators-no-exponential}
Fix $N\in\N$.  On $\ell^2(\mathbb Z)$ let $T$ be convolution by
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 k(n)=(1+|n|)^{-p},
 \qquad p>N+2.}
 \label{eq:GTLOC-polynomial-kernel}
\end{equation}
Then $T$ is bounded and
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \operatorname{ad}_{X}^{j}(T)\in\mathcal B(\ell^2(\mathbb Z))
 \qquad(0\le j\le N),}
 \label{eq:GTLOC-finite-commutators}
\end{equation}
where $Xe_n=ne_n$.  Nevertheless
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \norm{T}_{\mu,\mathrm{Sch}}=\infty
 \qquad\text{for every }\mu>0.}
 \label{eq:GTLOC-no-exponential-tail}
\end{equation}
Thus a finite commutator panel is a finite regularity certificate, not an
exponential quasilocality theorem.
\end{countertheorem}

\begin{proof}
The $j$-fold commutator is convolution by $n^jk(n)$.  This kernel is in
$\ell^1(\mathbb Z)$ for $j\le N$, so Young's inequality gives boundedness.
For every $\mu>0$, however,
$\sum_ne^{\mu|n|}|k(n)|=\infty$.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Finite locality audit]
\label{def:GTLOC-finite-locality-audit}
For a finite family of physically declared Lipschitz coordinates
$f_1,\ldots,f_m$, define the order-$N$ commutator Gram of a response $T$ by
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathbb C_{N}^{\mathrm{com}}(T)
 =\bigoplus_{j=1}^{N}\bigoplus_{a_1,\ldots,a_j}
 \operatorname{ad}_{f_{a_1}}\cdots
 \operatorname{ad}_{f_{a_j}}(T)^*
 \operatorname{ad}_{f_{a_1}}\cdots
 \operatorname{ad}_{f_{a_j}}(T).}
 \label{eq:GTLOC-commutator-Gram}
\end{equation}
It is a positive finite diagnostic.  Exponential locality additionally
requires a uniform factorial/exponential envelope such as
\eqref{eq:GTLOC-commutator-hierarchy}, not merely finiteness of a fixed order.
\end{definition}

% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
\subsubsection{Weighted holomorphy of the critical first and pair responses}
\label{subsec:GTLOC-weighted-holomorphy}
% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

\begin{definition}[Weighted holomorphic critical packet]
\label{def:GTLOC-weighted-holomorphic-packet}
Retain the inherited jointly commanded common-form family and write
\[
 P_t(z,w)=e^{-tA(z,w)}.
\]
Fix radii $\rho_z,\rho_w>0$.  The family has an
$(\alpha,t,\rho_z,\rho_w)$ \emph{weighted holomorphic packet} when
$P_t(z,w)$ is holomorphic with values in
$\mathfrak B_\alpha(\Gamma)$ on the bidisk and
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 M_{\alpha,t}(\rho_z,\rho_w)
 =\sup_{|z|\le\rho_z,\,|w|\le\rho_w}
 \norm{P_t(z,w)}_{\alpha,\mathrm{Sch}}<\infty.}
 \label{eq:GTLOC-weighted-holomorphic-bound}
\end{equation}
This is a locality statement in addition to the ordinary norm holomorphy proved by the inherited norm-form construction.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Critical quasilocality from weighted holomorphy]
\label{thm:GTLOC-weighted-Cauchy}
For the packet of \Cref{def:GTLOC-weighted-holomorphic-packet}, the critical
first and pair responses
\[
 \mathfrak D_{t}^{\mathrm{crit}}(B)
 =-\partial_zP_t(0,0),
 \qquad
 \mathfrak Q_{t}^{\mathrm{crit}}(B,C)
 =\partial_z\partial_wP_t(0,0)
\]
belong to $\mathfrak B_\alpha(\Gamma)$ and obey
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \norm{\mathfrak D_t^{\mathrm{crit}}(B)}_{\alpha,\mathrm{Sch}}
 \le
 \frac{M_{\alpha,t}(\rho_z,\rho_w)}{\rho_z},}
 \label{eq:GTLOC-weighted-first-Cauchy}
\end{equation}
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \norm{\mathfrak Q_t^{\mathrm{crit}}(B,C)}_{\alpha,\mathrm{Sch}}
 \le
 \frac{M_{\alpha,t}(\rho_z,\rho_w)}{\rho_z\rho_w}.}
 \label{eq:GTLOC-weighted-pair-Cauchy}
\end{equation}
Consequently every selected collar leakage of either response has the
exponential estimate of \eqref{eq:GTLOC-locality-leakage-bound}.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The Cauchy integral formula is valid in every complex Banach space.  Integrate
$P_t(z,0)$ on $|z|=\rho_z$ for the first derivative and integrate successively
on $|z|=\rho_z$, $|w|=\rho_w$ for the mixed derivative.  Taking the weighted
Banach norm gives the two displayed bounds.  Apply
\Cref{thm:GTLOC-locality-leakage} to the resulting operators.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Weighted regularization criterion]
\label{cor:GTLOC-weighted-regularization}
Let $P_t^{(n)}(z,w)$ be any inherited form-compatible bounded regularizations.  If
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \sup_{|z|=\rho_z,\,|w|=\rho_w}
 \norm{P_t^{(n)}(z,w)-P_t(z,w)}_{\alpha,\mathrm{Sch}}
 \longrightarrow0,}
 \label{eq:GTLOC-weighted-boundary-convergence}
\end{equation}
then their first and pair Duhamel derivatives converge in the weighted norm to
the canonical critical responses.  In particular, the limit and every collar
leakage Gram are independent of the chosen form-compatible regularization.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Apply the Cauchy integral formulas to the difference of the regularized and
limiting families.  The first derivative defect is bounded by the left side of
\eqref{eq:GTLOC-weighted-boundary-convergence} divided by $\rho_z$, and the pair
defect by the same quantity divided by $\rho_z\rho_w$.  Continuity of
$T\mapsto J^*T^*QTJ$ on bounded sets gives convergence of the leakage Grams.
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[Ordinary norm convergence is not weighted convergence]
The inherited norm-resolvent theorem gives ordinary operator-norm convergence on the
selected finite source or identified form carrier.  It does not imply
\eqref{eq:GTLOC-weighted-boundary-convergence}.  Locality transport requires its
own weighted, collar, or target-tail row.
\end{firewall}

% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
\subsubsection{Duhamel convolution and insertion-path collars}
\label{subsec:GTLOC-Duhamel-collars}
% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

\begin{theorem}[Weighted Duhamel convolution]
\label{thm:GTLOC-weighted-Duhamel}
Let $P_t=e^{-tH}$ belong to $\mathfrak B_\alpha(\Gamma)$ for $t>0$, and put
\[
 m_\alpha(t)=\norm{P_t}_{\alpha,\mathrm{Sch}}.
\]
For bounded insertions $V,W\in\mathfrak B_\alpha(\Gamma)$, the ordinary first
and symmetric pair Duhamel responses satisfy
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \norm{\mathfrak D_{t,H}(V)}_{\alpha,\mathrm{Sch}}
 \le
 \norm{V}_{\alpha,\mathrm{Sch}}
 \int_0^t m_\alpha(t-s)m_\alpha(s)\,\dd s,}
 \label{eq:GTLOC-first-convolution}
\end{equation}
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \begin{aligned}
 \norm{\mathfrak Q_{t,H}(V,W)}_{\alpha,\mathrm{Sch}}
 \le{}&2\norm{V}_{\alpha,\mathrm{Sch}}
          \norm{W}_{\alpha,\mathrm{Sch}}\\
 &\times
 \int_{\substack{r_0,r_1,r_2\ge0\\r_0+r_1+r_2=t}}
 m_\alpha(r_0)m_\alpha(r_1)m_\alpha(r_2)\,\dd\sigma_t.
 \end{aligned}}
 \label{eq:GTLOC-pair-convolution}
\end{equation}
If
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{m_\alpha(t)\le Me^{\omega t},}
 \label{eq:GTLOC-semigroup-weighted-growth}
\end{equation}
then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \norm{\mathfrak D_{t,H}(V)}_{\alpha,\mathrm{Sch}}
 \le M^2te^{\omega t}\norm{V}_{\alpha,\mathrm{Sch}},}
 \label{eq:GTLOC-first-exponential-bound}
\end{equation}
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \norm{\mathfrak Q_{t,H}(V,W)}_{\alpha,\mathrm{Sch}}
 \le M^3t^2e^{\omega t}
 \norm{V}_{\alpha,\mathrm{Sch}}
 \norm{W}_{\alpha,\mathrm{Sch}}.}
 \label{eq:GTLOC-pair-exponential-bound}
\end{equation}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Use the Duhamel integral formulas and the submultiplicativity of
\Cref{thm:GTLOC-weighted-Schur-algebra} inside the Bochner integrals.  The pair
response is the sum of the two insertion orders.  Under
\eqref{eq:GTLOC-semigroup-weighted-growth}, every first integrand is bounded by
$M^2e^{\omega t}\norm V_\alpha$ and every ordered pair integrand by
$M^3e^{\omega t}\norm V_\alpha\norm W_\alpha$.  The interval has length $t$
and the two-dimensional simplex has volume $t^2/2$; the two insertion orders
cancel the factor $1/2$.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Region-supported insertion]
\label{def:GTLOC-local-insertion}
An insertion $V$ is supported in $Z\subseteq\Gamma$ when
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{V=P_ZVP_Z.}
 \label{eq:GTLOC-strict-insertion-support}
\end{equation}
A semigroup has an $(C,\omega,\alpha)$ block collar on a family of physical
regions when
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \norm{P_YP_tP_X}
 \le
 Ce^{\omega t-\alpha d(X,Y)}}
 \label{eq:GTLOC-block-collar}
\end{equation}
for all regions in that family and all admitted positive durations.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Insertion-path locality]
\label{thm:GTLOC-insertion-path}
Assume \eqref{eq:GTLOC-block-collar}.  Let $V$ be supported in $Z$.  Then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \begin{aligned}
 \norm{P_Y\mathfrak D_{t,H}(V)P_X}
 \le{}&C^2t e^{\omega t}\norm V\\
 &\times
 e^{-\alpha[d(Y,Z)+d(Z,X)]}.
 \end{aligned}}
 \label{eq:GTLOC-first-path-bound}
\end{equation}
If $V$ and $W$ are supported in $Z_V$ and $Z_W$, respectively, then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \begin{aligned}
 &\norm{P_Y\mathfrak Q_{t,H}(V,W)P_X}\\
 &\quad\le
 \frac{C^3t^2e^{\omega t}}{2}\norm V\norm W
 \Bigl(
 e^{-\alpha\ell_{V,W}(Y,X)}
 +e^{-\alpha\ell_{W,V}(Y,X)}
 \Bigr),
 \end{aligned}}
 \label{eq:GTLOC-pair-path-bound}
\end{equation}
where
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \ell_{V,W}(Y,X)
 =d(Y,Z_V)+d(Z_V,Z_W)+d(Z_W,X).}
 \label{eq:GTLOC-ordered-path-length}
\end{equation}
Thus the pair response propagates along the two possible ordered insertion
paths rather than merely through the union of the endpoint supports.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Insert $P_Z$ on both sides of $V$ in the first Duhamel integral.  The two
semigroup blocks are bounded by
\[
 Ce^{\omega(t-s)-\alpha d(Y,Z)},
 \qquad
 Ce^{\omega s-\alpha d(Z,X)}.
\]
Their product is independent of $s$ apart from the total factor
$e^{\omega t}$, and integration gives \eqref{eq:GTLOC-first-path-bound}.
For the ordered term
$P_{r_0}VP_{r_1}WP_{r_2}$, insert the two support projections and apply the
three collar bounds along
$X\to Z_W\to Z_V\to Y$.  The other ordering gives the reversed insertion
path.  Each simplex integral has volume $t^2/2$.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Massive Green locality]
\label{cor:GTLOC-Green-locality}
Under \eqref{eq:GTLOC-semigroup-weighted-growth}, if $\mu>\omega$, then the
Laplace--Green transforms obey
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \left\|
 \int_0^\infty e^{-\mu t}\mathfrak D_{t,H}(V)\,\dd t
 \right\|_{\alpha,\mathrm{Sch}}
 \le
 \frac{M^2}{(\mu-\omega)^2}
 \norm V_{\alpha,\mathrm{Sch}},}
 \label{eq:GTLOC-first-Green-locality}
\end{equation}
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \left\|
 \int_0^\infty e^{-\mu t}\mathfrak Q_{t,H}(V,W)\,\dd t
 \right\|_{\alpha,\mathrm{Sch}}
 \le
 \frac{2M^3}{(\mu-\omega)^3}
 \norm V_{\alpha,\mathrm{Sch}}
 \norm W_{\alpha,\mathrm{Sch}}.}
 \label{eq:GTLOC-pair-Green-locality}
\end{equation}
The same estimates hold for the inherited critical Green responses whenever the
weighted holomorphic packet supplies the corresponding positive-time majorant.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Integrate \eqref{eq:GTLOC-first-exponential-bound} and
\eqref{eq:GTLOC-pair-exponential-bound} against $e^{-\mu t}$.  Use
\[
 \int_0^\infty te^{-at}\,\dd t=a^{-2},
 \qquad
 \int_0^\infty t^2e^{-at}\,\dd t=2a^{-3}.
\]
\end{proof}

% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
\subsubsection{Endpoint locality, route locality, and pair-only source birth}
\label{subsec:GTLOC-route-locality}
% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

\begin{definition}[Ordered split-response packet]
\label{def:GTLOC-split-packet}
For a bounded insertion $V$, define its unsummed first split response by
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathscr R_{t;s}^{(1)}(V)
 =P_{t-s}VP_s,
 \qquad 0\le s\le t.}
 \label{eq:GTLOC-first-split-response}
\end{equation}
For two insertions define the ordered pair responses
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathscr R_{t;\mathbf r}^{(2),V\leftarrow W}
 &=P_{r_0}VP_{r_1}WP_{r_2},\\
 \mathscr R_{t;\mathbf r}^{(2),W\leftarrow V}
 &=P_{r_0}WP_{r_1}VP_{r_2},
 \end{aligned}}
 \label{eq:GTLOC-pair-split-response}
\end{equation}
where $r_0+r_1+r_2=t$.  Their simplex integrals give the endpoint Duhamel
responses.  A route-locality claim concerns these split maps or an equivalent
same-history support record, not only their integrals.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Split collar leakage]
\label{def:GTLOC-split-leakage}
For a source $J_X$ and a prescribed collar $X^{[R]}$, define the first split
leakage
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathbb L_{R,t}^{(1),\mathrm{split}}(V\mid J_X)
 =\int_0^t
 J_X^*
 (\mathscr R_{t;s}^{(1)}(V))^*
 (I-P_{X^{[R]}})
 \mathscr R_{t;s}^{(1)}(V)
 J_X\,\dd s.
 \end{aligned}}
 \label{eq:GTLOC-first-split-leakage}
\end{equation}
For a pair packet, one may analogously insert an outside-collar projection
after the first insertion in each ordered word and integrate the resulting
positive Grams over the simplex.  The resulting matrix is denoted
$\mathbb L_{R,t}^{(2),\mathrm{route}}(V,W\mid J_X)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Route-locality Gram]
\label{thm:GTLOC-route-locality-Gram}
The split leakage Grams are positive.  Their zero is equivalent to vanishing of
the corresponding outside-collar split synthesis for almost every physical
split time.  Under the insertion-path assumptions of
\Cref{thm:GTLOC-insertion-path}, their norms are bounded by the integrals of the
squares of the corresponding ordered path bounds.

A zero endpoint leakage
\[
 \mathbb L_R^{\mathrm{loc}}
 (\mathfrak Q_{t,H}(V,W)\mid J_X)=0
\]
does not imply zero route leakage.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Each object is an integral of operators of the form $S^*S$ and is therefore
positive.  A positive Bochner integral has zero quadratic form exactly when
its nonnegative scalar integrand vanishes almost everywhere for every source
vector.  The norm bound follows by applying
\Cref{thm:GTLOC-insertion-path} before integration.  The failure of the converse
is established by the following counterexample.
\end{proof}

\begin{countertheorem}[A local endpoint can hide an arbitrarily long pair excursion]
\label{cth:GTLOC-local-endpoint-hidden-route}
Let $\mathcal H=\ell^2(\{0,N\})$, $H=0$, $J=e_0$, and
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 V_N=|e_0\rangle\langle e_N|
     +|e_N\rangle\langle e_0|.}
 \label{eq:GTLOC-long-hop}
\end{equation}
Then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 J^*\mathfrak D_{t,0}(V_N)J=0,}
 \label{eq:GTLOC-long-hop-first-zero}
\end{equation}
while
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 J^*\mathfrak Q_{t,0}(V_N,V_N)J=t^2.}
 \label{eq:GTLOC-long-hop-pair-return}
\end{equation}
The endpoint pair response is supported at the original source, but every
ordered pair path visits the site at distance $N$.  Hence endpoint locality,
first-response invisibility, and route locality are logically distinct.
\end{countertheorem}

\begin{proof}
Since $H=0$, one has
$\mathfrak D_{t,0}(V_N)=tV_N$ and
$\mathfrak Q_{t,0}(V_N,V_N)=t^2V_N^2=t^2I$.  The first matrix element at
$e_0$ vanishes and the second equals $t^2$.  Between the two insertions the
state is $e_N$, so every route exits every collar of radius smaller than $N$.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Pair locality is an independent physical row]
\label{cor:GTLOC-pair-locality-independent}
A complete selected first-response packet, even at every duration, does not
establish locality of the quadratic pair response or of its ordered physical
route.  The minimum additional row is one of:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2.8em]
\item the split pair response with its collar labels;
\item a proof-carrying local insertion law implying
      \Cref{thm:GTLOC-insertion-path};
\item a positive route-leakage Gram and its polar missing source.
\end{enumerate}
\end{corollary}

\begin{countertheorem}[Ordinary norm convergence does not transport a locality exponent]
\label{cth:GTLOC-norm-not-weighted}
On $\ell^2(\mathbb N_0)$ with its usual distance, fix $\alpha>0$ and set
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 T_n=e^{-\alpha n/2}
 \bigl(
 |e_0\rangle\langle e_n|
 +|e_n\rangle\langle e_0|
 \bigr).}
 \label{eq:GTLOC-norm-small-long-hop}
\end{equation}
Then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \norm{T_n}_{\mathrm{op}}=e^{-\alpha n/2}\longrightarrow0,}
 \label{eq:GTLOC-norm-small}
\end{equation}
but
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \norm{T_n}_{\alpha,\mathrm{Sch}}
 =e^{\alpha n/2}\longrightarrow\infty.}
 \label{eq:GTLOC-weighted-large}
\end{equation}
Thus operator-norm, norm-resolvent, or compact-source convergence alone does
not provide a regulator-uniform quasilocal exponent.
\end{countertheorem}

\begin{proof}
The operator is a two-dimensional off-diagonal matrix of amplitude
$e^{-\alpha n/2}$, giving the ordinary norm.  The weighted row through the
sites $0,n$ multiplies this amplitude by $e^{\alpha n}$, giving the weighted
norm.
\end{proof}

% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
\subsubsection{Locality-preserving contact subtraction}
\label{subsec:GTLOC-contact-locality}
% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

\begin{definition}[Quasilocal counterterm projector]
\label{def:GTLOC-quasilocal-counterterm}
Let $L_1,\ldots,L_m\in\mathfrak B_\alpha(\Gamma)$ be a predeclared finite
local counterterm bank.  Let
$\varphi_1,\ldots,\varphi_m\in\mathfrak B_\alpha(\Gamma)^*$ be bounded dual
functionals satisfying
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{\varphi_i(L_j)=\delta_{ij}.}
 \label{eq:GTLOC-counterterm-duality}
\end{equation}
Define
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \Pi_{\mathrm{ct}}T
 =\sum_{j=1}^{m}L_j\varphi_j(T),}
 \label{eq:GTLOC-counterterm-projector}
\end{equation}
and its weighted conditioning constant
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 C_{\mathrm{ct},\alpha}
 =\sum_{j=1}^{m}
 \norm{L_j}_{\alpha,\mathrm{Sch}}
 \norm{\varphi_j}_{\mathfrak B_\alpha^*}.}
 \label{eq:GTLOC-counterterm-conditioning}
\end{equation}
The bank and its dual calibration must be fixed by the physical local action
before the terminal contact is examined.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Quasilocal contact-renormalization criterion]
\label{thm:GTLOC-quasilocal-contact-renormalization}
For every $T\in\mathfrak B_\alpha(\Gamma)$,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \norm{\Pi_{\mathrm{ct}}T}_{\alpha,\mathrm{Sch}}
 \le
 C_{\mathrm{ct},\alpha}
 \norm T_{\alpha,\mathrm{Sch}}.}
 \label{eq:GTLOC-counterterm-projection-bound}
\end{equation}
Let $\mathcal C_\varepsilon$ be a family of regularized contacts.  If
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 (I-\Pi_{\mathrm{ct}})\mathcal C_\varepsilon
 \quad\text{is Cauchy in }\mathfrak B_\alpha(\Gamma),}
 \label{eq:GTLOC-weighted-contact-Cauchy}
\end{equation}
then its limit is one quasilocal renormalized contact and its collar leakages
obey \eqref{eq:GTLOC-locality-leakage-bound}.  If only ordinary operator-norm
Cauchy convergence is known, quasilocality need not survive.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Apply the triangle inequality to
\eqref{eq:GTLOC-counterterm-projector} and use the dual norm bounds.  Since
$I-\Pi_{\mathrm{ct}}$ is bounded on the weighted Banach space, the weighted
Cauchy condition gives a unique limit in that space.  The locality estimate is
then \Cref{thm:GTLOC-locality-leakage}.  The final statement follows by inserting
the long-hop family of \Cref{cth:GTLOC-norm-not-weighted} into an otherwise
local contact sequence.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Target-relative local counterterm independence]
\label{cor:GTLOC-local-counterterm-target}
Let $\mathcal T$ be a selected target on the renormalized contact.  Its value is
independent of the local counterterm representative exactly when
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathcal T(\Ran\Pi_{\mathrm{ct}})=\{0\}.}
 \label{eq:GTLOC-local-counterterm-target-zero}
\end{equation}
When this condition fails, the minimum number of additional scalar Reads is
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 r_{\mathrm{ct}}^{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathcal T)
 =\rank\bigl(\mathcal T|_{\Ran\Pi_{\mathrm{ct}}}\bigr).}
 \label{eq:GTLOC-local-counterterm-read-rank}
\end{equation}
This repeats the inherited information floor on the smaller quasilocal counterterm
carrier rather than on an arbitrary ambient coefficient space.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Two renormalized representatives differ by an element of
$\Ran\Pi_{\mathrm{ct}}$.  The target is constant on every affine fibre exactly
when it annihilates that difference space.  The finite rank formula is the
ordinary quotient information count.
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[Unweighted minimum norm can be nonlocal]
A Moore--Penrose minimum in an unweighted Hilbert--Schmidt coefficient metric
need not minimize or even control the weighted locality norm.  A contact
subtraction is licensed as local only when its synthesis and dual calibration
have a bound such as \eqref{eq:GTLOC-counterterm-conditioning}, or when a direct
physical support/collar audit supplies the equivalent information.
\end{firewall}

% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
\subsubsection{Local contact targets and collar-renormalization alternatives}
\label{subsec:GTLOC-contact-collar}
% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

\begin{definition}[Physical collar compression]
\label{def:GTLOC-collar-compression}
All contact spaces in this subsection carry their finite-cutoff
Hilbert--Schmidt norm.  Let $U\subseteq\Lambda$ be the frozen support of the
source and coefficient command under audit, and put
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 U_R=\{x\in\Lambda:d(x,U)\le R\},
 \qquad
 \Pi_R(T)=P_{U_R}TP_{U_R}.}
 \label{eq:GTLOC-collar-compression}
\end{equation}
For a family $T_\varepsilon$, define its anchored tail modulus
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \Theta_{\mu,U}(T)
 =\sup_{\varepsilon>0}\sup_{R\ge0}
 e^{\mu R}\norm{T_\varepsilon-\Pi_R(T_\varepsilon)}.}
 \label{eq:GTLOC-anchored-tail-modulus}
\end{equation}
A finite value is an explicit exponential contact collar.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Local contact-counterterm bank]
\label{def:GTLOC-local-contact-bank}
For a fixed radius $R$, let
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathcal L_R:U_R^{\mathrm{ct}}
 \longrightarrow
 P_{U_R}\mathcal B(\mathcal H)P_{U_R}}
 \label{eq:GTLOC-local-contact-bank}
\end{equation}
be the predeclared finite synthesis of local contact counterterms.  Let
$P_{\mathcal L_R}$ be the Hilbert--Schmidt projection onto its range on the
finite collar carrier.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Exact collar-relative contact quotient]
\label{thm:GTLOC-collar-contact-quotient}
Let $\mathfrak C_\varepsilon$ be regularized contact operators and fix $R$.
There are local coefficients $u_\varepsilon\in U_R^{\mathrm{ct}}$ such that
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \Pi_R(\mathfrak C_\varepsilon)
 -\mathcal L_Ru_\varepsilon
 \quad\text{converges}}
 \label{eq:GTLOC-local-contact-convergence}
\end{equation}
if and only if
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 (I-P_{\mathcal L_R})
 \Pi_R(\mathfrak C_\varepsilon)
 \quad\text{is Cauchy}.}
 \label{eq:GTLOC-local-contact-Cauchy}
\end{equation}
The canonical minimum-norm local subtraction is
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 u_{\varepsilon,R}^{\min}
 =\mathcal L_R^\dagger
   P_{\mathcal L_R}\Pi_R(\mathfrak C_\varepsilon).}
 \label{eq:GTLOC-local-minimum-counterterm}
\end{equation}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
This is the inherited quotient-Cauchy theorem applied to the finite collar
compression.  Local counterterms have no component outside
$P_{U_R}\mathcal H$, so the orthogonal projection onto their range is the exact
quotient map on that carrier.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Target-local contact economy]
\label{thm:GTLOC-target-local-contact}
Let $\mathcal T:\mathcal B(\mathcal H)\to Y$ be a linear physical target
satisfying
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathcal T(T)=\mathcal T(\Pi_R(T))
 \qquad\text{for every admitted }T.}
 \label{eq:GTLOC-target-collar-factor}
\end{equation}
Then the target is independent of every local subtraction exactly when
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathcal T(\operatorname{Ran}\mathcal L_R)=\{0\}.}
 \label{eq:GTLOC-local-target-independence}
\end{equation}
With an additional scalar Read bank $\mathcal R_R$ on
$\operatorname{Ran}\mathcal L_R$, the target is identified exactly when
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \ker\mathcal R_R
 \subseteq
 \ker(\mathcal T|_{\operatorname{Ran}\mathcal L_R}).}
 \label{eq:GTLOC-local-target-read-condition}
\end{equation}
The minimum number of scalar Reads is
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 r_{\mathcal T,R}^{\mathrm{ct}}
 =\rank(\mathcal T|_{\operatorname{Ran}\mathcal L_R}).}
 \label{eq:GTLOC-local-contact-read-rank}
\end{equation}
No contact coefficient outside $U_R$ is charged to this target.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
By \eqref{eq:GTLOC-target-collar-factor}, all admissible target differences are
represented by the collar compression.  Two local renormalizations differ by
an element of $\operatorname{Ran}\mathcal L_R$.  The kernel and rank arguments
are therefore identical to the finite target-relative quotient theorem.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Nonlocal contact-tail obstruction]
\label{def:GTLOC-contact-tail-obstruction}
For regulator values $\varepsilon,\delta$ and collar radius $R$, define
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathbb C_{\varepsilon,\delta}^{\mathrm{tail}}(R)
 =\bigl[(I-\Pi_R)(\mathfrak C_\varepsilon-
                 \mathfrak C_\delta)\bigr]^*
   \bigl[(I-\Pi_R)(\mathfrak C_\varepsilon-
                 \mathfrak C_\delta)\bigr]
 \succeq0.}
 \label{eq:GTLOC-contact-tail-obstruction}
\end{equation}
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Finite-collar no-go and exponential rescue]
\label{thm:GTLOC-contact-tail-alternative}
Assume the local counterterm ranges are nested with $R$, and put
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathcal L_{\mathrm{loc}}
 =\overline{\bigcup_{R<\infty}\operatorname{Ran}\mathcal L_R}}
 \label{eq:GTLOC-local-counterterm-closure}
\end{equation}
in the Hilbert--Schmidt contact space.  Then:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(T\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item If for every $R$ there are arbitrarily small
      $\varepsilon,\delta$ such that
      \begin{equation}
       \boxed{
       \norm{(I-\Pi_R)(\mathfrak C_\varepsilon-
                       \mathfrak C_\delta)}_{\mathrm{HS}}\ge c_*}
       \label{eq:GTLOC-persistent-nonlocal-tail}
      \end{equation}
      with one $c_*>0$, then no counterterm bank supported in any fixed finite
      collar makes the complete contact family Cauchy.
\item Suppose $\Theta_{\mu,U}(\mathfrak C)<\infty$ and, for every fixed $R$,
      \begin{equation}
       \boxed{
       (I-P_{\mathcal L_R})\Pi_R(\mathfrak C_\varepsilon)
       \quad\text{is Cauchy as }\varepsilon\downarrow0.}
       \label{eq:GTLOC-all-collar-Cauchy}
      \end{equation}
      Then $\mathfrak C_\varepsilon$ is Cauchy in the quotient by
      $\mathcal L_{\mathrm{loc}}$.  More precisely,
      \begin{equation}
       \boxed{
       \begin{aligned}
       \operatorname{dist}_{\mathrm{HS}}
       (&\mathfrak C_\varepsilon-\mathfrak C_\delta,
          \mathcal L_{\mathrm{loc}})\\
       &\le
       \norm{(I-P_{\mathcal L_R})
       \Pi_R(\mathfrak C_\varepsilon-
             \mathfrak C_\delta)}_{\mathrm{HS}}
       +2e^{-\mu R}\Theta_{\mu,U}(\mathfrak C)
       \end{aligned}}
       \label{eq:GTLOC-contact-global-quotient-bound}
      \end{equation}
      for every $R$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
A counterterm supported in $U_R$ has zero $(I-\Pi_R)$ component, so
\eqref{eq:GTLOC-persistent-nonlocal-tail} survives every such subtraction and
prevents Cauchy convergence.  For the second branch, the best local subtraction
from the collar difference is its orthogonal projection onto
$\operatorname{Ran}\mathcal L_R$.  The remaining collar norm is the first term
on the right of \eqref{eq:GTLOC-contact-global-quotient-bound}.  The two raw
contact tails are each bounded by
$e^{-\mu R}\Theta_{\mu,U}(\mathfrak C)$.  Since
$\operatorname{Ran}\mathcal L_R\subseteq\mathcal L_{\mathrm{loc}}$, the
triangle inequality proves the displayed bound.  First choose $R$ so the tail
term is small, then use \eqref{eq:GTLOC-all-collar-Cauchy}.
\end{proof}

\begin{assessment}[Contact locality is stronger than source contact]
The inherited source-contact theorem may close on one finite source even when
\eqref{eq:GTLOC-persistent-nonlocal-tail} holds outside every fixed collar.  A
local coincident-field target is stronger: it requires a physically frozen
local counterterm bank and control of the contact tail.  The two targets are
not conflated.
\end{assessment}

% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
\subsubsection{Weighted cutoff transport and locality tightness}
\label{subsec:GTLOC-cutoff-transport}
% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

\begin{definition}[Weighted holomorphic cutoff defect]
\label{def:GTLOC-weighted-cutoff-defect}
Let $X<Y$ be adjacent cutoffs with one physical isometric identification
$U_{Y/X}:\mathcal H_X\to\mathcal H_Y$ preserving the old block labels and their
physical distances.  After embedding both sides in the fine metric carrier,
define
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \begin{aligned}
 \varepsilon_{Y/X}^{\mathrm{hol}}(t)
 =\sup_{\substack{|z|=\rho_z\\|w|=\rho_w}}
 \norm{
 P_{t,Y}(z,w)U_{Y/X}
 -U_{Y/X}P_{t,X}(z,w)
 }_{\alpha,\mathrm{Sch}}.
 \end{aligned}}
 \label{eq:GTLOC-weighted-holomorphic-defect}
\end{equation}
The block identification and physical metric are part of the cutoff packet; an
arbitrary unitary identification is not admitted.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Cauchy transport of critical local responses]
\label{thm:GTLOC-weighted-critical-transport}
For the packet of \Cref{def:GTLOC-weighted-cutoff-defect},
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \norm{
 \mathfrak D_{t,Y}^{\mathrm{crit}}U_{Y/X}
 -U_{Y/X}\mathfrak D_{t,X}^{\mathrm{crit}}
 }_{\alpha,\mathrm{Sch}}
 \le
 \frac{\varepsilon_{Y/X}^{\mathrm{hol}}(t)}{\rho_z},}
 \label{eq:GTLOC-first-weighted-transport}
\end{equation}
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \norm{
 \mathfrak Q_{t,Y}^{\mathrm{crit}}U_{Y/X}
 -U_{Y/X}\mathfrak Q_{t,X}^{\mathrm{crit}}
 }_{\alpha,\mathrm{Sch}}
 \le
 \frac{\varepsilon_{Y/X}^{\mathrm{hol}}(t)}{\rho_z\rho_w}.}
 \label{eq:GTLOC-pair-weighted-transport}
\end{equation}
If the right sides are summable along a cofinal sequence, the selected critical
first and pair responses have unique weighted quasilocal limits on every fixed
positive-time window.  Their fixed-mass Green transforms also converge in the
weighted norm whenever the time majorants are uniformly Laplace integrable.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Apply the one- and two-variable Cauchy formulas to the cross-cutoff holomorphic
defect.  This gives the first two inequalities.  Summable adjacent defects make
the pulled-back responses Cauchy in the complete weighted Banach algebra.  The
Green assertion follows by dominated Bochner integration in that algebra.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Uniform target-tail tightness]
\label{def:GTLOC-locality-tightness}
For a cutoff sequence with selected sources $J_n$ supported in physical regions
$X_n$, a response family $T_n$ has uniform target-tail tightness when
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \lim_{R\to\infty}
 \sup_n
 \norm{(I-P_{X_n^{[R]}})T_nJ_n}=0.}
 \label{eq:GTLOC-uniform-tail-tightness}
\end{equation}
This is the target-relative locality requirement when one uniform global
exponent $\alpha$ is stronger than necessary.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Target-relative quasilocal limit]
\label{thm:GTLOC-target-quasilocal-limit}
Assume the selected source vectors and response outputs are transported to one
inductive-limit Hilbert space, and suppose
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 T_nJ_n\longrightarrow TJ
 \quad\text{in operator norm on the finite source space}.}
 \label{eq:GTLOC-selected-response-convergence}
\end{equation}
If \eqref{eq:GTLOC-uniform-tail-tightness} holds and the physical collar
projections converge strongly on every fixed $R$, then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \lim_{R\to\infty}
 \norm{(I-P_{X^{[R]}})TJ}=0.}
 \label{eq:GTLOC-limit-quasilocal-tail}
\end{equation}
Thus the selected continuum response is quasilocal even when no uniform
ambient weighted exponent has been established.

A uniform estimate
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \sup_n\norm{T_n}_{\alpha,\mathrm{Sch}}<\infty
 \quad\text{for one }\alpha>0}
 \label{eq:GTLOC-uniform-alpha-sufficient}
\end{equation}
is sufficient for \eqref{eq:GTLOC-uniform-tail-tightness}, but is not required.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Fix $\varepsilon>0$ and choose $R$ so that the supremum in
\eqref{eq:GTLOC-uniform-tail-tightness} is at most $\varepsilon$.  Transport to
the limit, use strong convergence of the fixed collar projection on the
finite-dimensional source image, and then use
\eqref{eq:GTLOC-selected-response-convergence}.  This gives a limiting tail at
most $\varepsilon$; let $\varepsilon\downarrow0$.  The sufficient condition is
\Cref{thm:GTLOC-locality-leakage}, uniformly in $n$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Transport of locality leakage Grams]
\label{thm:GTLOC-leakage-Gram-transport}
Let
\[
 A_n=(I-P_{X_n^{[R]}})T_nJ_n
\]
be represented on one transported output carrier, and assume
$\sup_n\norm{A_n}\le M_R$.  Then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \norm{A_{n+1}^*A_{n+1}-A_n^*A_n}
 \le
 2M_R\norm{A_{n+1}-A_n}.}
 \label{eq:GTLOC-leakage-Gram-transport}
\end{equation}
Consequently summable response, source, and collar-projection defects transport
every fixed-radius locality leakage Gram.  If, in addition, the tail-tightness
modulus is uniform, the complete selected locality packet has a cofinal limit.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Use
\[
 A_{n+1}^*A_{n+1}-A_n^*A_n
 =A_{n+1}^*(A_{n+1}-A_n)
 +(A_{n+1}^*-A_n^*)A_n
\]
and the uniform bound.  The final claim follows by summation and then by
sending the collar radius to infinity.
\end{proof}

\begin{assessment}[Uniform exponent versus selected locality]
A regulator-uniform $\alpha>0$ gives a convenient global quasilocal algebra.
It is not charged merely to close one source-cyclic observable.  Conversely,
pointwise positive exponents $\alpha_n>0$ prove nothing when the corresponding
weighted norms or locality lengths diverge.  The selected physical target is
closed by the uniform tail condition \eqref{eq:GTLOC-uniform-tail-tightness}; a
full quasilocal net requires a common exponent or an equivalent uniform local
approximation theorem for every local generator.
\end{assessment}

% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
\subsubsection{Quasilocal products and OS descent}
\label{subsec:GTLOC-OS-quasilocal}
% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

\begin{definition}[Quasilocal approximation packet]
\label{def:GTLOC-quasilocal-approximation}
Let $\mathcal A_X$ be a bounded operator represented in the selected OS Hilbert
space and labelled by a physical region $X$.  A local approximation packet is a
family $\mathcal A_X^{[R]}$ satisfying
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \supp\mathcal A_X^{[R]}\subseteq X^{[R]},
 \qquad
 \norm{\mathcal A_X-\mathcal A_X^{[R]}}
 \le\eta_{\mathcal A}(R),}
 \label{eq:GTLOC-local-approximant}
\end{equation}
with $\eta_{\mathcal A}(R)\to0$.  The support statement refers to the physical
local word algebra before OS completion, and the quotient map is required to
be contractive on these representatives.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Quasilocal commutator from local collars]
\label{thm:GTLOC-quasilocal-commutator}
Let $\mathcal A_X,\mathcal B_Y$ have local approximation packets, and suppose
local representatives with disjoint supports commute.  If
$d(X,Y)>2R$, then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \begin{aligned}
 \norm{[\mathcal A_X,\mathcal B_Y]}
 \le{}&2\eta_{\mathcal A}(R)\norm{\mathcal B_Y}\\
 &+2\bigl(\norm{\mathcal A_X}+\eta_{\mathcal A}(R)\bigr)
       \eta_{\mathcal B}(R).
 \end{aligned}}
 \label{eq:GTLOC-quasilocal-commutator-bound}
\end{equation}
In particular, if
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \eta_{\mathcal A}(R)\le C_{\mathcal A}e^{-\alpha R},
 \qquad
 \eta_{\mathcal B}(R)\le C_{\mathcal B}e^{-\alpha R},}
 \label{eq:GTLOC-exponential-approximants}
\end{equation}
then choosing $R=d(X,Y)/3$ gives an explicit exponential commutator bound with
rate $\alpha/3$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Since $X^{[R]}$ and $Y^{[R]}$ are disjoint, the local approximants commute.
Write
\[
 [\mathcal A,\mathcal B]
 =[\mathcal A-\mathcal A^{[R]},\mathcal B]
 +[\mathcal A^{[R]},\mathcal B-\mathcal B^{[R]}]
\]
and use $\norm{[S,T]}\le2\norm S\norm T$ together with
$\norm{\mathcal A^{[R]}}\le
 \norm{\mathcal A}+\eta_{\mathcal A}(R)$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Conditional quasilocal OS completion]
\label{thm:GTLOC-quasilocal-OS-completion}
Assume one reflected word packet has already passed the inherited reflected-word positivity,
flatness, duration, action, Green, and OS-null tests.  Suppose further that:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(Q\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item every selected local word and every critical first/pair response has a
      local approximation packet on the same physical metric net;
\item the OS quotient map and represented transfer are contractive on those
      packets;
\item products of disjoint local representatives commute before quotienting;
\item the approximation tails are uniform under cutoff transport;
\item the connected insertion and every claimed local counterterm satisfy the
      same collar packet.
\end{enumerate}
Then the norm closure of the selected represented local words is a quasilocal
$C^*$-algebra.  Its commutators satisfy
\eqref{eq:GTLOC-quasilocal-commutator-bound}, its critical first and pair
responses act as quasilocal operators, and its fixed-mass Green writers remain
quasilocal by \Cref{cor:GTLOC-Green-locality}.

If a coherently transported local connected operator has one held-out Rayleigh
value bounded away from zero, then the continuum OS sector is both quasilocal
and non-Gaussian on that selected local algebra.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Contractivity of the OS quotient transports the approximation errors to the
reconstructed Hilbert space.  \Cref{thm:GTLOC-quasilocal-commutator} gives
asymptotic commutation of separated represented words.  Uniformity and the
$C^*$-norm closure give the quasilocal algebra.  The critical response and
Green claims are the weighted and Laplace bounds already proved.  The final
statement is the preceding critical pair construction coherent connected-Rayleigh transport theorem applied to
the local connected operator; a nonzero connected fourth or stronger row
excludes Gaussianity on the generated local algebra.
\end{proof}

\begin{countertheorem}[Local response kernels do not reconstruct local multiplication]
\label{cth:GTLOC-local-response-not-product}
Pairwise local response Grams and exponentially decaying first/pair kernels do
not determine the product of the represented local word algebra.  Two finite
$C^*$-algebra structures can have the same Hilbert carrier, source vectors,
transfer moments, and block-decay bounds while one is commutative and the other
noncommutative.
\end{countertheorem}

\begin{proof}
Use the existing degree-one nonmonoidal counterexample:
transport the multiplication of $M_2(\C)$ to the Hilbert space of $\C^4$ by a
unitary fixing the unit and take a scalar transfer.  Give all four basis vectors
the same physical site label.  Every source moment and locality bound is then
identical, while the centers have dimensions one and four.  Multiplication
therefore remains a separate word-level OS row.
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[Local positive response is not a local quantum measure]
A weighted critical response does not supply the determinant/Pfaffian line,
its divisor, a component or quotient-loop character, or a real orientation.
Nor does it prove reflection positivity or a common local product.  Those rows
remain independently physical even when every positive response operator has
an arbitrarily strong collar.
\end{firewall}

% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
\subsubsection{Locality after the Osterwalder--Schrader quotient}
\label{subsec:GTLOC-OS-locality}
% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

\begin{definition}[Supported local word head]
\label{def:GTLOC-local-word-head}
Let $\mathscr W=\{W_1,\ldots,W_N\}$ be a finite future-word bank.  Each word
has a physical support $S_a\subseteq\Lambda$.  On the OS-supported quotient,
choose individually normalized word coordinates and define the support
pseudometric
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 d_{\mathscr W}(a,b)=d(S_a,S_b).}
 \label{eq:GTLOC-word-support-metric}
\end{equation}
Let
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 G=I+E\succ0}
 \label{eq:GTLOC-normalized-word-Gram}
\end{equation}
be the normalized reflected word Gram and let $C=C^*$ be one genuine
same-cylinder connected form on the same word list.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Quasilocal inverse square root on a supported word head]
\label{thm:GTLOC-local-inverse-square-root}
If, for some $\mu>0$,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \norm{E}_{\mu,\mathrm{Sch}}\le\eta<1,}
 \label{eq:GTLOC-local-Gram-smallness}
\end{equation}
then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 G^{-1/2}\in\mathfrak A_\mu(\mathscr W),
 \qquad
 \norm{G^{-1/2}}_{\mu,\mathrm{Sch}}
 \le(1-\eta)^{-1/2}.}
 \label{eq:GTLOC-local-inverse-square-root}
\end{equation}
In particular the OS whitening does not destroy the physical exponential
collar on this branch.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The binomial series
\[
 (I+E)^{-1/2}
 =\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\binom{-1/2}{n}E^n
\]
converges in the weighted Banach algebra because $\norm E_{\mu,\mathrm{Sch}}<1$.
The absolute values of its scalar coefficients are those of
$(1-x)^{-1/2}$, so the algebra norm is bounded by
$(1-\eta)^{-1/2}$.  The operator obtained from the series is the positive
inverse square root by ordinary functional calculus.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Quasilocal connected operator on the OS quotient]
\label{thm:GTLOC-local-connected-OS}
Under \eqref{eq:GTLOC-local-Gram-smallness}, suppose
$C\in\mathfrak A_\mu(\mathscr W)$.  The represented connected operator
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 K_{\mathrm{conn}}
 =G^{-1/2}CG^{-1/2}}
 \label{eq:GTLOC-OS-connected-operator}
\end{equation}
obeys
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \norm{K_{\mathrm{conn}}}_{\mu,\mathrm{Sch}}
 \le
 \frac{\norm C_{\mu,\mathrm{Sch}}}{1-\eta}.}
 \label{eq:GTLOC-OS-connected-locality}
\end{equation}
Consequently
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \norm{P_AK_{\mathrm{conn}}P_B}
 \le
 \frac{e^{-\mu d_{\mathscr W}(A,B)}}{1-\eta}
 \norm C_{\mu,\mathrm{Sch}}.}
 \label{eq:GTLOC-OS-connected-offdiagonal}
\end{equation}
A held-out nonzero connected Rayleigh value therefore lies inside one
quasilocal represented OS carrier rather than in a Euclidean factor erased by
the null quotient.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Apply the Banach-algebra product estimate twice and use
\Cref{thm:GTLOC-local-inverse-square-root}.  The off-diagonal conclusion is
\Cref{thm:GTLOC-weighted-Schur-algebra} on the word-support metric.
\end{proof}

\begin{countertheorem}[A local Gram without a uniform floor need not have a local inverse]
\label{cth:GTLOC-local-Gram-no-inverse}
Let $L_N$ be the nearest-neighbour graph Laplacian on a path of length $N$ and
let
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 G_N=\varepsilon_NI+L_N,
 \qquad \varepsilon_N\downarrow0.}
 \label{eq:GTLOC-local-Gram-floor-collapse}
\end{equation}
The matrices $G_N$ have uniformly bounded finite propagation and uniformly
bounded weighted Schur norm for every fixed $\mu$.  Nevertheless
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \norm{G_N^{-1/2}}_{\mu,\mathrm{Sch}}
 \ge\norm{G_N^{-1/2}}
 =\varepsilon_N^{-1/2}\longrightarrow\infty.}
 \label{eq:GTLOC-inverse-locality-collapse}
\end{equation}
Thus locality of the reflected Gram does not by itself transport through OS
whitening; a supported floor or a separate inverse-locality theorem is
load bearing.
\end{countertheorem}

\begin{proof}
The path Laplacian is nearest neighbour and has minimum eigenvalue zero.  The
minimum eigenvalue of $G_N$ is $\varepsilon_N$, so the operator norm of its
inverse square root is $\varepsilon_N^{-1/2}$.  Every weighted Schur norm
dominates the operator norm.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[OS locality residual]
\label{def:GTLOC-OS-locality-residual}
For a proposed exponential bound $b_{ab}=Ce^{-\mu d_{\mathscr W}(a,b)}$, let
$\mathscr R_{\mathrm{loc}}$ synthesize the excess blocks
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 R_{ab}=P_aK_{\mathrm{conn}}P_b
 \quad\text{on every pair where }
 \norm{R_{ab}}>b_{ab}.}
 \label{eq:GTLOC-OS-locality-excess}
\end{equation}
The positive Gram
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathbb C_{\mathrm{OS}}^{\mathrm{loc}}
 =\mathscr R_{\mathrm{loc}}^*
  \mathscr R_{\mathrm{loc}}\succeq0}
 \label{eq:GTLOC-OS-locality-Gram}
\end{equation}
is zero exactly when the selected finite word head obeys the proposed collar.
Its polar range is the minimum violating word-pair bank.
\end{definition}

\begin{firewall}[Positive locality does not orient the measure line]
The weighted reflected Gram, critical pair, and connected OS operator are
positive or Hermitian data.  They do not determine the determinant-line chord,
component character, quotient-loop holonomy, divisor multiplicity, or real
Pfaffian sign.  A local pair response may coexist with arbitrary source-visible
line phase.  The determinant-line packet therefore remains independent.
\end{firewall}

\subsubsection{Terminating locality compiler and selected handoff}
\label{subsec:GTLOC-compiler}
% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

\begin{theorem}[Finite weighted-locality alternative]
\label{thm:GTLOC-terminating-alternative}
Freeze one inherited common-form packet, one physical block metric, one declared
local word grammar, one selected source region, one positive-time window, one
critical first/pair response, one contact/counterterm packet when needed, one
reflected word/OS quotient, and one cutoff identification.  The audit
terminates at the first applicable branch:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(A\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item the block metric or local decomposition is not physically loaded; return
      the missing locality carrier;
\item the common form family is ordinary-norm holomorphic but has neither a
      weighted holomorphic packet nor a direct physical collar; return the
      weighted occurrence row;
\item a bounded insertion branch is used; evaluate the convolution bounds of
      \Cref{thm:GTLOC-weighted-Duhamel};
\item the critical family has a weighted packet; apply either
      \Cref{thm:GTLOC-critical-weighted-locality} or
      \Cref{thm:GTLOC-weighted-Cauchy};
\item the endpoint response is local but the ordered split packet has positive
      route leakage; retain the polar missing collar source of
      \Cref{thm:GTLOC-route-locality-Gram};
\item the first response passes but the pair collar fails; return the pair-only
      locality birth rather than modifying the first quotient;
\item contact subtraction is required but the quasilocal counterterm projector
      is unbounded, a fixed-collar quotient fails, or the nonlocal tail persists;
      return the corresponding local contact witness;
\item adjacent cutoffs converge in ordinary norm but fail weighted transport
      and target-tail tightness; return the escaping long-range block;
\item a uniform exponent is unavailable but the selected target-tail packet
      passes \Cref{thm:GTLOC-target-quasilocal-limit}; retain only that
      target-relative locality claim;
\item local representatives fail to descend through the OS null ideal, their
      disjoint products fail to commute, or the supported OS inverse floor
      collapses; return the local word/product/inverse obstruction;
\item the supported word Gram has a local inverse and the connected form passes
      \Cref{thm:GTLOC-local-connected-OS};
\item the critical pair and Green rows are local but the connected,
      determinant/Pfaffian line, reflection, boundary, noncollapse, or
      ultraviolet row fails; return that independent obstruction;
\item every selected row passes; invoke the inherited critical-form OS
      reconstruction on the quasilocal selected algebra.
\end{enumerate}
No global decay exponent is inferred from one source tail, and no source-local
endpoint response is promoted to a local insertion route.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Conditional quasilocal critical-form OS handoff]
\label{thm:GTLOC-selected-handoff}
A selected quasilocal interacting Einstein--Standard-Model OS sector follows
from the inherited reconstruction theorem if:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(H\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item one literal jointly commanded inherited common-form family and one physical
      metric/block decomposition occur on the same history;
\item its critical first and pair responses possess either a weighted
      holomorphic packet or a direct source-relative collar packet;
\item every route-locality claim is supported by a split response or a
      proof-carrying local insertion law;
\item the inherited pair ambiguity of the stress/contact and field-shell packets, shrinking contact, and direct-action rows
      pass, and every stronger contact target uses a bounded local counterterm
      projector and passes the contact-tail audit;
\item the selected response and locality leakage packets transport with either
      one uniform weighted exponent or the target-tail condition of
      \Cref{thm:GTLOC-target-quasilocal-limit};
\item the reflected word packet descends to one quasilocal OS algebra by
      \Cref{thm:GTLOC-quasilocal-OS-completion};
\item on the represented word head, either the Gram whitening is already part
      of that local quotient or it passes the supported inverse-floor condition
      of \Cref{thm:GTLOC-local-inverse-square-root};
\item one local connected or Wick row survives coherently outside the Gaussian
      fit and, when represented explicitly, obeys
      \Cref{thm:GTLOC-local-connected-OS};
\item the independent Green analyser where required, determinant/Pfaffian line,
      divisor, component, loop, sign, reflection, boundary, noncollapse, and
      ultraviolet rows all pass.
\end{enumerate}
The endpoint is exactly one selected quasilocal pair-complete interacting OS
sector.  A complete local net or exhaustive Einstein--Standard-Model QFT
requires the same packet on a source-complete local grammar and elimination of
all source-orthogonal action, pair, locality, contact, and line fibres.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Items~\textup{(H1)--(H4)} provide the canonical critical pair, its physical
action incidence, and a local endpoint or split-route realization.  Item
\textup{(H5)} gives regulator-safe quasilocality; items~\textup{(H6)--(H8)}
supply the represented local product, inverse metric, OS quotient, and
connected witness.  The last item is precisely the inherited Green, line,
reflection, domain, boundary, tightness, and reconstruction packet.  No
source-orthogonal local net is inferred.
\end{proof}
