\subsection{Infinite-regulator feedback, rational memory, and delay-mass escape}
\label{sec:feedback-limit-classification}

For each cutoff, let
\[
 K_{k,n}=B_nD_n^kC_n
\]
be the returned-feedback kernel of the old visible carrier.  Pointwise
convergence in the delay variable does not control the total memory: mass may
move to later delays while every fixed coefficient tends to zero.

\begin{theorem}[Exact operator-valued \texorpdfstring{$\ell^1$}{l1} feedback limit]
\label{thm:feedback-l1-limit}
Assume $K_{k,n}\to K_k$ in operator norm for every fixed $k$.  Then
\[
 \sum_{k\ge0}\|K_{k,n}-K_k\|\longrightarrow0
\]
if and only if
\[
 \boxed{
 \lim_{R\to\infty}\sup_n\sum_{k\ge R}\|K_{k,n}\|=0.}
\]
On this branch $K\in\ell^1$, and if $A_n\to A$, the retained responses satisfy
the limiting Volterra recursion
\[
 \boxed{
 X_{m+1}=AX_m+\sum_{j=0}^{m-1}K_{m-1-j}X_j,
 \qquad X_0=I.}
\]
If
\[
 q:=\sup_n\|A_n\|+\sup_n\sum_k\|K_{k,n}\|<1,
\]
the response generating functions
\[
 \mathscr X_n(z)
 =[I-zA_n-z^2\mathscr K_n(z)]^{-1}
\]
converge uniformly on $|z|\le1$, with
\[
 \sup_{|z|\le1}\|\mathscr X_n(z)-\mathscr X(z)\|
 \le\frac{\|A_n-A\|+\|K_n-K\|_{\ell^1}}{(1-q)^2}.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The forward implication gives uniform tail control by splitting the tail of
$K_{\cdot,n}$ into the tail of $K$ and the $\ell^1$ difference.  Conversely,
choose $R$ with uniformly small tails; convergence of the finitely many
coefficients below $R$ gives convergence of the heads, proving $\ell^1$
convergence.  Passing to the limit in the finite convolution gives the Volterra
recursion.  On the unit disk,
$\|zA_n+z^2\mathscr K_n(z)\|\le q$, so the inverses are bounded by
$(1-q)^{-1}$.  The resolvent identity gives the displayed estimate.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Operator-valued Hankel realization]
\label{thm:feedback-Hankel-realization}
For a kernel $K=(K_k)_{k\ge0}$ define
\[
 \mathbb H_{p,q}(K)=[K_{i+j}]_{0\le i<p,\ 0\le j<q},
 \qquad
 r_{\rm fb}(K)=\sup_{p,q}\rank\mathbb H_{p,q}(K).
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{
 r_{\rm fb}(K)=r<\infty
 \iff
 K_k=BD^kC}
\]
for a reachable and observable $r$-dimensional linear realization.  Every
realization has dimension at least $r$, minimal realizations are uniquely
similar, and
\[
 \mathscr K(z)=B(I-zD)^{-1}C
\]
is rational.  For a minimal finite realization,
\[
 (K_k)\in\ell^1\iff\rho(D)<1.
\]
Thus finite memory dimension and temporal summability are independent axes.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
If $K_k=BD^kC$, the block Hankel factors as an observability matrix times a
controllability matrix and has rank at most the state dimension.  Conversely,
finite stabilized Hankel rank identifies the quotient of finite past columns
by equality against all future rows; the shift of a column descends to a
well-defined state transition $D$, while the zeroth row and column define
$B$ and $C$.  Reachability and observability are built into the quotient and
its dimension is the stabilized rank.  The standard reachable--observable
argument gives unique similarity.  The rational formula is the geometric
series.  In finite dimension, $BD^kC$ is summable on the minimal realization
exactly when every visible eigenvalue of $D$ lies strictly inside the unit disk;
minimality makes every eigenvalue visible.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Corrected feedback-memory classification]
\label{thm:feedback-limit-classification}
Every limiting feedback kernel belongs to exactly one row and one column of
\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c}
 & K\in\ell^1 & K\notin\ell^1\\ \hline
r_{\rm fb}(K)<\infty
 &\text{stable rational memory}
 &\text{persistent rational memory}\\
r_{\rm fb}(K)=\infty
 &\text{infinite-dimensional short memory}
 &\text{infinite-dimensional long memory}.
\end{array}
\]
All four branches occur.  Uniformly bounded finite-stage Hankel ranks imply a
finite-dimensional limiting realization under fixed-delay convergence, but do
not by themselves give one transition matrix reusable at every cutoff.
A strict realization arrow or one common annihilating recurrence is sufficient
for such reusable memory.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The table is the Cartesian product of the two independent properties in
\Cref{thm:feedback-l1-limit,thm:feedback-Hankel-realization}.  The examples
$2^{-k}$, $1$, $1/(k+1)!$, and $1/(k+1)$ realize the four entries; the last two
have nonrational generating functions and hence infinite Hankel rank.  Every
finite Hankel minor passes to the pointwise limit, so a uniform rank bound
passes to the limit.  However the rank-one family $K_{k,n}=\lambda_n^k$ with
infinitely many distinct $\lambda_n$ cannot be realized by one fixed finite
matrix, since its transfer functions have infinitely many distinct poles.
Strict realization intertwiners give a finite direct-limit carrier, while a
common recurrence gives the usual companion realization.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Temporal-tail and rank-growth witnesses]
\label{thm:feedback-witnesses}
If the uniform $\ell^1$ tail condition fails, there are cutoffs $n_j$, delay
intervals $I_j$ escaping to infinity, and $\varepsilon>0$ such that
\[
 \sum_{k\in I_j}\|K_{k,n_j}\|\ge\varepsilon.
\]
After a subsequence, either:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(T\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item an atomic delayed route survives:
      $\|K_{k_j,n_j}\|\ge\eta>0$ for some $k_j\to\infty$; or
\item the escape is diffuse:
      $\sup_{k\in I_j}\|K_{k,n_j}\|\to0$ while $|I_j|\to\infty$.
\end{enumerate}
In finite input dimension, one normalized input vector detects a fixed fraction
of every diffuse packet.

If no memory of dimension $M$ represents the family, some finite feedback
Hankel block satisfies
\[
 \boxed{\sigma_{M+1}(\mathbb H_{p,q}(K_n))>0.}
\]
Its left and right singular vectors are a finite delayed-source experiment
excluding $M$ recurrent coordinates.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Failure of uniform tail tightness gives the escaping finite intervals.  If the
largest coefficient on a subsequence has a positive lower bound, choose its
maximizing delay; otherwise the maxima vanish and the fixed total mass forces
the interval lengths to diverge.  Averaging over an orthonormal input basis
shows that one basis direction captures at least the reciprocal input-dimension
fraction of the sum.  The Hankel statement is the Eckart--Young rank criterion:
a realization of dimension $M$ makes every block rank at most $M$, while a
positive $(M+1)$st singular value gives the explicit separating bilinear
combination.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Spatiotemporal feedback influence]
\label{thm:spatiotemporal-feedback}
For the operational atom graph define
\[
 \|L\|_\mu
 :=\sup_i\sum_j e^{\mu d(i,j)}\|Q_jLQ_i\|,
 \qquad
 \kappa_{\mu,\eta}(K)
 :=\sum_{k\ge0}e^{\eta k}\|K_k\|_\mu.
\]
If
\[
 q_{\mu,\eta}
 :=e^\eta\|A\|_\mu
 +e^{2\eta}\kappa_{\mu,\eta}(K)<1,
\]
then the Volterra response satisfies
\[
 \boxed{
 \|Q_jX_mQ_i\|
 \le
 \frac{e^{-\mu d(i,j)}e^{-\eta m}}{1-q_{\mu,\eta}}.}
\]
Long memory and spatial nonlocality remain independent: a kernel may be
nonsummable and on-site, or delay zero and spatially nonlocal.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The weighted influence norm is submultiplicative by the triangle inequality for
the graph distance.  Multiply the Volterra recursion by the temporal weight
$e^{\eta m}$ and take the weighted spatial norm.  The resulting scalar
convolution is dominated by a geometric series with ratio
$q_{\mu,\eta}$.  Removing the spatial and temporal weights gives the estimate.
The two independence examples are immediate from kernels of the form
$K_k=a_kI$ and $K_0=L_{\rm nonlocal}$, respectively.
\end{proof}


% =============================================================================
\subsection{Hodge-screen reduction and canonical field completion of loaded feedback}
\label{sec:Hodge-loaded-feedback}
% =============================================================================

The abstract feedback classification distinguishes delay tails and realization
rank.  On the positive spatial branch, the Hodge screen gives a stronger
conclusion: low loaded modes form a uniformly finite physical carrier at every
fixed resolution, while high modes become a small local correction plus a
compact memory tail.

\begin{theorem}[Fast loaded feedback collapses to a local generator]
\label{thm:fast-feedback-collapse}
Let the compressed physical-step responses satisfy
\[
 X_{0,h}=I,
 \qquad
 X_{n+1,h}=A_hX_{n,h}
 +\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}K_{k,h}X_{n-1-k,h}.
\]
Assume
\[
 \frac{A_h-I}{h}\longrightarrow G,
\]
and suppose there are operators $(R_k)_{k\ge0}$ such that
\[
 \sum_{k\ge0}(k+1)\|R_k\|<\infty,
 \qquad
 \frac1h\sum_{k\ge0}(k+1)\|K_{k,h}-hR_k\|\longrightarrow0.
\]
Then, with $R=\sum_kR_k$,
\[
 \boxed{
 \sup_{0\le nh\le T}
 \|X_{n,h}-e^{nh(G+R)}\|\longrightarrow0}
\]
for every $T<\infty$.  In particular, feedback supported on $O(1)$ raw steps
has vanishing physical delay and renormalizes the local generator rather than
producing a continuum memory kernel.

If $K_{k,h}=B_hD_h^kC_h$, $D_h\to D_0$,
$\|D_h^k\|\le Cr^k$ with $r<1$, and
$h^{-1/2}B_h\to B$, $h^{-1/2}C_h\to C$, then
\[
 \boxed{R=B(I-D_0)^{-1}C.}
\]
If instead $\|B_h\|\|C_h\|=o(h)$, the fast feedback disappears at generator
scale.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The assumptions imply uniform bounds
$\|A_h\|\le1+Ch$ and $\sum_k\|K_{k,h}\|\le Ch$.  Discrete Gronwall therefore
gives a uniform bound on $X_{n,h}$ for $nh\le T$ and, from the recursion,
$\|X_{n+1,h}-X_{n,h}\|=O(h)$.  Rewrite the recursion as
\[
 X_{n+1,h}=X_{n,h}+h(G+R)X_{n,h}+hE_{n,h}.
\]
The accumulated error from $(A_h-I)/h-G$ tends to zero.  The kernel
approximation contributes at most
$T h^{-1}\sum_k(k+1)\|K_{k,h}-hR_k\|$.  Replacing
$X_{n-1-k,h}$ by $X_{n,h}$ costs
$O(h\sum_k(k+1)\|R_k\|)$ per unit physical time, and the missing initial tail
has total size
$O(h\sum_k(k+1)\|R_k\|)$.  Thus this is a perturbed Euler scheme for
$\dot X=(G+R)X$ with vanishing integrated error.

In the geometric-decay specialization,
$h^{-1}K_{k,h}\to BD_0^kC$ and dominated convergence holds with the weight
$k+1$.  Summation gives the resolvent correction.  The little-$o$ product
bound makes the normalized kernel mass vanish.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Canonical Markovian completion of finite physical-time memory]
\label{thm:continuum-memory-completion}
Let
\[
 M(t)=Be^{tH}C
\]
be a finite-dimensional physical-time feedback kernel.  The Volterra equation
\[
 \dot x(t)=Gx(t)+\int_0^tM(t-s)x(s)\,\dd s,
 \qquad x(0)=x_0,
\]
is equivalent to the local system
\[
 \boxed{
 \frac{\dd}{\dd t}\binom{x}{y}
 =\begin{pmatrix}G&B\\C&H\end{pmatrix}\binom{x}{y},
 \qquad \binom{x(0)}{y(0)}=\binom{x_0}{0}.}
\]
The source-reachable quotient
\[
 \mathcal F_{\rm mem}
 =\frac{\Span\{H^nCx:n\ge0\}}
 {\{e:BH^ne=0\text{ for every }n\ge0\}}
\]
is the unique minimal auxiliary carrier.  If
\[
 \mathsf H_{p,q}^{\rm mem}=[BH^{i+j}C]_{0\le i<p,\,0\le j<q},
\]
then, for sufficiently large $p,q$,
\[
 \boxed{
 \rank\mathsf H_{p,q}^{\rm mem}=\dim\mathcal F_{\rm mem}.}
\]
Thus the stabilized feedback-Hankel rank is the exact minimum number of
continuum fields needed to Markovianize a finite persistent kernel.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Set
$y(t)=\int_0^te^{(t-s)H}Cx(s)\,\dd s$.  Differentiation gives
$\dot y=Hy+Cx$ and the first equation becomes $\dot x=Gx+By$; variation of
constants proves the converse.  The reachable space and its future-unobservable
subspace are $H$-invariant, so the maps descend to a reachable and observable
realization.  The Hankel block factors as its finite observability matrix times
its finite controllability matrix.  Reachability and observability make these
maps surjective and injective after at most $\dim\mathcal F_{\rm mem}$ rank
changes.  Standard minimal-realization uniqueness gives the final assertion.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Hodge-dominated loaded transient packet]
\label{def:Hodge-loaded-transient}
Let $H_X=H_X^*\succeq\lambda_{\rm tr}I$ act on a loaded transient carrier
$\mathcal E_X$ after every protected zero mode and already-declared persistent
field has been separated.  Let
\[
 \mathsf B_X:\mathcal E_X\to\mathcal H_{0,X},
 \qquad
 \mathsf C_X:\mathcal H_{0,X}\to\mathcal E_X
\]
obey $\|\mathsf B_X\|\le b_*$ and $\|\mathsf C_X\|\le c_*$.  Assume
\[
 \boxed{H_X\succeq c_H\Delta_X^{\rm sp}-C_HI}
\]
with $c_H>0$, where $\Delta_X^{\rm sp}$ satisfies the counting law of
\Cref{thm:operational-Sobolev-Weyl}.  Put
\[
 M_X(t)=\mathsf B_Xe^{-tH_X}\mathsf C_X,
 \qquad
 \Sigma_X(z)=\mathsf B_X(z+H_X)^{-1}\mathsf C_X.
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Hodge-screen spectral reduction of loaded memory]
\label{thm:Hodge-feedback-tail}
Let $P_{X,R}=\one_{[\lambda_{\rm tr},R]}(H_X)$ and
$Q_{X,R}=I-P_{X,R}$.  Under
\Cref{def:Hodge-loaded-transient},
\[
 \boxed{
 \rank P_{X,R}
 \le N_X\!\left(\frac{R+C_H}{c_H}\right)
 \le C_{\rm W,H}(1+R^{3/2})}
\]
for a cutoff-independent constant $C_{\rm W,H}$.  The high-energy memory
satisfies
\[
 \boxed{
 \|\mathsf B_Xe^{-tH_X}Q_{X,R}\mathsf C_X\|
 \le b_*c_*e^{-Rt},}
\]
\[
 \boxed{
 \int_0^\infty\|M_{X,>R}(t)\|\,\dd t
 \le\frac{b_*c_*}{R},
 \qquad
 \int_0^\infty t\|M_{X,>R}(t)\|\,\dd t
 \le\frac{b_*c_*}{R^2}.}
\]
For $\operatorname{Re}z\ge0$,
\[
 \boxed{
 \Sigma_X(z)
 =\Sigma_{X,\le R}(z)+\mathcal R_{X,>R}
  +\mathcal E_{X,>R}(z),}
\]
where
\[
 \mathcal R_{X,>R}
 =\mathsf B_XH_X^{-1}Q_{X,R}\mathsf C_X,
\]
\[
 \boxed{
 \|\mathcal R_{X,>R}\|\le\frac{b_*c_*}{R},
 \qquad
 \|\mathcal E_{X,>R}(z)\|
 \le\frac{|z|b_*c_*}{R^2}.}
\]
Thus high loaded modes contribute a small time-local Feshbach correction and a
smaller frequency-dependent remainder.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
If $u\in P_{X,R}\mathcal E_X$, then
$\langle u,H_Xu\rangle\le R\|u\|^2$.  Hodge domination gives
$\langle u,\Delta_X^{\rm sp}u\rangle\le(R+C_H)c_H^{-1}\|u\|^2$.
The min--max principle bounds the dimension of this subspace by the spatial
counting function, and \Cref{thm:operational-Sobolev-Weyl} gives the
$R^{3/2}$ law.

On $Q_{X,R}\mathcal E_X$, functional calculus gives
$\|e^{-tH_X}Q_{X,R}\|\le e^{-Rt}$; multiplication by the two couplings and
integration give the time-domain estimates.  Split the resolvent with
$P_{X,R}+Q_{X,R}$ and use
\[
 (z+H_X)^{-1}-H_X^{-1}
 =-z(z+H_X)^{-1}H_X^{-1}
\]
on the high-energy range.  Both inverse factors have norm at most $R^{-1}$,
which gives the Feshbach estimates.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Feedback-Hankel compactness and the dimension-three decay law]
\label{thm:feedback-Hankel-Weyl}
Define
\[
 (\mathfrak H_Xf)(t)
 =\int_0^\infty M_X(t+s)f(s)\,\dd s
\]
on $L^2(\R_+;\mathcal H_{0,X})$.  The low-energy truncation has rank at most
$\rank P_{X,R}$ and
\[
 \boxed{
 \|\mathfrak H_X-\mathfrak H_{X,\le R}\|
 \le\frac{b_*c_*}{2R}.}
\]
Consequently every $\mathfrak H_X$ is compact and, uniformly in the cutoff,
\[
 \boxed{s_n(\mathfrak H_X)\le C_{\rm fb}n^{-2/3}}
\]
for all sufficiently large $n$.

For every frequency window $|z|\le Z$, $\operatorname{Re}z\ge0$, and every
$\varepsilon>0$, choosing
$R=(Zb_*c_*/\varepsilon)^{1/2}$ gives an approximation by the finite
Markovian carrier $P_{X,R}\mathcal E_X$ plus the local correction
$\mathcal R_{X,>R}$, with error at most $\varepsilon$ and field count
\[
 \boxed{
 N_{\rm aux}(Z,\varepsilon)
 \le C'\left[1+
 \left(\frac{Zb_*c_*}{\varepsilon}\right)^{3/4}\right].}
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The low-energy Hankel operator factors through $P_{X,R}\mathcal E_X$.
For the high-energy part, its controllability and observability factors have
norms at most $c_*/\sqrt{2R}$ and $b_*/\sqrt{2R}$ by Cauchy--Schwarz and the
spectral exponential bound.  Their product gives the approximation estimate.
Choose $R\asymp n^{2/3}$ in the counting law of
\Cref{thm:Hodge-feedback-tail} to obtain the singular-value decay.  The
finite-frequency statement is the Feshbach remainder estimate with the
specified $R$, and substitution in the $R^{3/2}$ counting law gives the field
count.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[No amorphous loaded-memory branch on the positive spatial sector]
\label{cor:finite-resolution-memory}
Under \Cref{def:Hodge-loaded-transient}, every loaded memory on a fixed compact
region has the exhaustive finite-resolution profile
\[
 \boxed{
 \text{declared physical low modes}
 \;\oplus\;
 \text{canonical finite field innovations}
 \;\oplus\;
 \text{a vanishing high-energy tail}.}
\]
The source and dynamic-containment residuals determine whether each low mode is
already part of the declared connection or matter carrier.  A fixed-resolution
growing-rank or noncompact-memory obstruction can persist only if spatial
low-energy counting, the transient floor, the physical coupling bounds, or
cutoff compactness fails.
\end{corollary}

\begin{firewall}[A local Feshbach correction is not automatically a counterterm]
The operator $\mathcal R_{X,>R}$ is local in physical time, but it is an
admissible action counterterm only after it passes the locality, symmetry,
exactness, common-action, and cutoff-transport tests of the spacetime loading.
High energy alone is also insufficient when the physical couplings grow with
the energy scale.
\end{firewall}


\subsection{Escape--head compression, return synthesis, and source-anchored first return}
\label{sec:escape-head-return-synthesis}

The compact-screen and feedback theorems control several positive branches.
The following synthesis identifies the exact mixed object whose tightness is
required and separates endpoint sampling from continuous first-entry killing.

\begin{theorem}[Quantitative escape-to-head concentration]
\label{thm:GT-escape-head-concentration}
Let
\[
 0\preceq T=
 \begin{pmatrix}A&B\\B^*&D\end{pmatrix}
 \preceq I
 \tag{ER.1}
\]
relative to a source-native head and its complement.  Put
$q=\|D\|<1$, $b=\|B\|$, and
$\delta_T(u)=1-\langle u,Tu\rangle$ for a unit vector
$u=x\oplus y$.  Then
\[
 \boxed{
 \|y\|\le
 \frac{b+\sqrt{\delta_T(u)}}{1-q}.}
 \tag{ER.2}
\]
Moreover
\[
 \boxed{
 \|(I-A)x\|
 \le\sqrt{\delta_T(u)}+b\|y\|.}
 \tag{ER.3}
\]
Thus a near-unit sequence can retain macroscopic remote mass only if the escape
edge collapses, the assembled interface remains macroscopic, or the vector is
not actually near critical.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Because $0\preceq I-T\preceq I$,
$\|(I-T)u\|^2\le\langle u,(I-T)u\rangle=\delta_T(u)$.  The tail component of
$(I-T)u$ is $(I-D)y-B^*x$, so
$(1-q)\|y\|\le b+\sqrt{\delta_T(u)}$.  The head component gives
$(I-A)x-By$ and proves \textup{(ER.3)}.
\end{proof}

Let the positive deficit $M=I-T$ be written as
\[
 M=
 \begin{pmatrix}M_{\rm H}&C\\C^*&M_{\rm T}\end{pmatrix}\succeq0.
 \tag{ER.4}
\]
Positivity gives the Moore--Penrose range condition.  Define the
compliance-normalized return synthesis
\[
 \boxed{\mathscr S=M_{\rm T}^{\dagger/2}C^*.}
 \tag{ER.5}
\]
For a source-fixed increasing tail head $\mathcal H_R$, let $\Pi_R$ project
onto the energy-image space
$\overline{M_{\rm T}^{1/2}\mathcal H_R}$.

\begin{theorem}[Exact return-synthesis tail]
\label{thm:GT-return-synthesis-tail}
The effective head deficit after allowing the radius-$R$ tail to relax is
\[
 \boxed{K_R=M_{\rm H}-\mathscr S^*\Pi_R\mathscr S,}
 \tag{ER.6}
\]
while complete tail relaxation gives
\[
 \boxed{
 K_\infty
 =M_{\rm H}-\mathscr S^*\mathscr S
 =M_{\rm H}-CM_{\rm T}^{\dagger}C^*.}
 \tag{ER.7}
\]
Consequently
\[
 \boxed{
 K_R-K_\infty
 =\mathscr S^*(I-\Pi_R)\mathscr S,\qquad
 \|K_R-K_\infty\|
 =\|(I-\Pi_R)\mathscr S\|^2.}
 \tag{ER.8}
\]
The remote return is therefore controlled by the mixed source normalized by the
actual tail compliance, not by the raw interface $C$ or the tail action alone.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Whiten the supported tail action by $M_{\rm T}^{1/2}$.  The mixed quadratic
term becomes $\mathscr S$, and minimizing over the represented energy-image
head subtracts the squared projection of $\mathscr S$ onto that range.
Minimizing over the complete supported tail gives the Moore--Penrose Schur
complement.  Subtraction proves \textup{(ER.8)}.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Collective return compactness and proper moments]
\label{thm:GT-return-collective-compactness}
Assume the cutoff return syntheses $\mathscr S_X$ have a common finite source
space, $\sup_X\norm{\mathscr S_X}<\infty$, and their tail energy spaces are
transported to one Hilbert space with finite-rank projections
$\Pi_R\uparrow I$.  The following are equivalent.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(C\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item
$\lim_{R\to\infty}\sup_X\|(I-\Pi_R)\mathscr S_X\|=0$;
\item the set
$\{\mathscr S_Xx:X,\ \|x\|\le1\}$ has compact closure;
\item for the orthogonal shells $\Delta_r=\Pi_r-\Pi_{r-1}$ there are proper
      weights $w_r\uparrow\infty$ and $C<\infty$ such that
      \[
       \boxed{
       \sum_rw_r\mathscr S_X^*\Delta_r\mathscr S_X
       \preceq CI}
       \tag{ER.9}
      \]
      uniformly in $X$.
\end{enumerate}
On these branches,
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathscr S_X^*(I-\Pi_R)\mathscr S_X
 \preceq\frac{C}{w_{R+1}}I.}
 \tag{ER.10}
\]
Failure returns a normalized remote source orthogonal to every fixed tail head
while retaining an order-one mixed return to the protected sector.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Uniform finite-rank approximation of a bounded family is equivalent to total
boundedness of its union of unit-ball images.  The moment bound implies
\textup{(ER.10)} by monotonicity of the weights and hence gives uniform
approximation.  Conversely, choose radii along which the uniform tails fall
below a summable sequence and assign a slowly increasing constant weight to
each intervening shell block; the resulting proper weighted sum is uniformly
bounded.  If uniform approximation fails, choose unit coefficients attaining a
fixed tail norm and normalize their remote projections.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Positive first-return renewal on the source-cyclic carrier]
\label{thm:GT-positive-first-return-renewal}
Let $0\preceq K\preceq I$ act on the source-cyclic carrier generated by a
physical source projection $P$, put $Q=I-P$, and write
\[
 K=
 \begin{pmatrix}A&B\\B^*&D\end{pmatrix}.
 \tag{ER.11}
\]
Then $\|D\|<1$.  Define
\[
 \boxed{F_1=A,\qquad F_n=BD^{n-2}B^*\quad(n\ge2).}
 \tag{ER.12}
\]
Every $F_n$ is the positive kernel of a first return to the source at sampled
time $n$.  With
\[
 G_n=PK^nP|_{P\mathcal H},\qquad G_0=I,
\]
\[
 \mathcal G(z)=\sum_{n\ge0}z^nG_n,
 \qquad
 \mathcal F(z)=\sum_{n\ge1}z^nF_n
 =zA+z^2B(I-zD)^{-1}B^*,
\]
one has the exact renewal equation
\[
 \boxed{\mathcal G(z)=[I-\mathcal F(z)]^{-1}.}
 \tag{ER.13}
\]
For every $r>0$,
\[
 \boxed{
 \|K\|<r^{-1}
 \iff
 r\|D\|<1
 \ \text{and}\ 
 \|\mathcal F(r)\|<1.}
 \tag{ER.14}
\]
Thus a cutoff-uniform source edge is exactly one strict exponential
first-return estimate on a common physical chronology, not merely a strict
total return deficit at $r=1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
If $Dy=y$ for a nonzero tail vector, positivity of $I-K$ forces $Ky=y$ and
hence produces a source-invisible invariant direction, contradicting
source-cyclicity.  Thus $\|D\|<1$.  Decomposing a return path at its first return
gives
$G_n=\sum_{j=1}^nF_jG_{n-j}$ and therefore \textup{(ER.13)}.  Finally,
$I-rK\succ0$ is equivalent by the Schur complement to
$I-rD\succ0$ and
$I-rA-r^2B(I-rD)^{-1}B^*\succ0$, which is precisely
$I-\mathcal F(r)\succ0$.  Positivity converts these inequalities into the norm
conditions in \textup{(ER.14)}.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Endpoint sampling versus continuous first-entry killing]
\label{thm:GT-sampled-versus-killed}
Let
\[
 H=\begin{pmatrix}A&B\\B^*&D\end{pmatrix}\succeq0
 \tag{ER.15}
\]
be a completely assembled generator and let $Q$ project onto the tail.
Continuous killing at first entry into the head gives $e^{-tD}$, whereas
endpoint sampling gives $Qe^{-tH}Q$.  Their first difference is
\[
 \boxed{
 Qe^{-tH}Q-e^{-tD}
 =\frac{t^2}{2}B^*B+O(t^3).}
 \tag{ER.16}
\]
The two protocols agree for all sufficiently small $t$ exactly when $B=0$.
For endpoint sampling the canonical static tail deficit is
\[
 \boxed{S=D-B^*A^\dagger B.}
 \tag{ER.17}
\]
If $S\succeq sI$ with $s>0$, then
\[
 \boxed{
 0\preceq Qe^{-tH}Q
 \preceq(I+tS)^{-1},\qquad
 \|Qe^{-tH}Q\|\le(1+ts)^{-1}.}
 \tag{ER.18}
\]
Thus a diagonal tail gap does not control a sampled slab until the coherent
head relaxation has been assembled and shorted.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The Taylor series of $e^{-tH}$ gives the $QQ$ block
$I-tD+\tfrac12t^2(D^2+B^*B)+O(t^3)$, proving
\textup{(ER.16)} and the protocol criterion.  Functional calculus gives
$e^{-tH}\preceq(I+tH)^{-1}$.  The $QQ$ block of the resolvent is the inverse of
$I+tD-t^2B^*(I+tA)^{-1}B$.  On the supported range,
$t^2(I+tA)^{-1}\preceq tA^\dagger$, so this denominator dominates
$I+tS$.  Inversion reverses the order and proves \textup{(ER.18)}.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Assembly before positivity and first-return shorting]
\label{thm:GT-assembly-before-return-positivity}
For real signed current rows $j_a$,
\[
 \boxed{
 \sum_a(j_a)_+-\left(\sum_aj_a\right)_+
 =\frac12\left(\sum_a|j_a|-\left|\sum_aj_a\right|\right)\ge0.}
 \tag{ER.19}
\]
For an interface $B=\sum_aB_a$, the physical first-return kernel is
\[
 \boxed{
 BD^{n-2}B^*
 =\sum_{a,b}B_aD^{n-2}B_b^*,}
 \tag{ER.20}
\]
not the sum of the diagonal positive channel kernels.  Cross terms may cancel
or reinforce the return.  Consequently signed physical rows, boundary terms,
and mixed interfaces must be assembled before positive parts, Schur
complements, or first-return Grams are formed.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Use $x_+=(x+|x|)/2$ for \textup{(ER.19)} and expand
$B=\sum_aB_a$ for \textup{(ER.20)}.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Source-anchored predictive--action closure]
\label{thm:GT-source-anchored-predictive-action-closure}
Consider a cutoff family of nonterminal relational histories.  Suppose:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(P\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item a physical reveal grade satisfies the uniform stopping-front tightness of
      \Cref{thm:GT-stopping-front-tightness};
\item the bounded represented head is action complete, or its nonflat
      contextual memory is retained through
      \Cref{thm:GT-contextual-renewal-associativity};
\item the genuine escape complement satisfies a common marked first-return edge
      as in \Cref{thm:GT-positive-first-return-renewal};
\item every finite obstruction-return graph on the resulting head closes its
      recurrent components by \Cref{thm:GT-global-well-foundedness-alternative};
\item the remaining source-native first exits possess the joint balance and
      divergent margins of \Cref{thm:GT-source-anchored-cofinal-descent}.
\end{enumerate}
Then no infinite nonterminal history exists.  If any hypothesis fails, the
construction returns respectively a remote future/action source, a contextual
memory source, a long or remote first-return excursion, a recurrent
circulation, an unpaid boundary packet, or a literal cofinal escape history.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The first two hypotheses reduce the complete physical source to one bounded
action-complete head plus a controlled complement.  The third excludes an
unresolved repeated-return tail.  The fourth makes every fixed screen well
founded.  The fifth excludes passage through cofinally many screens.  The
failure list is exactly the collection of witnesses supplied by the cited
theorems.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Uniform gaps, compactness, and continuum certification}
\label{sec:uniform-continuum-certification}

\begin{theorem}[State compactness and spectral tightness]
\label{thm:state-compactness-tightness}
Let $\mathcal A_{\rm ql}$ be a separable unital quasilocal $C^*$-algebra.
Every sequence of states has a weak-$*$ convergent subsequence.  If the
restrictions converge on a norm-dense local $*$-subalgebra, the full sequence
converges to the unique extension.

For self-adjoint observables $F_X$ affiliated with the finite-stage
representations, a uniform $p$-moment bound
\[
 \sup_X\omega_X(|F_X|^p)\le C_p<\infty
\]
implies the spectral tightness estimate
\[
 \boxed{\omega_X(\mathbf1_{\{|F_X|>R\}})
 \le C_pR^{-p}.}
\]
Bounded-state compactness is automatic; tightness of unbounded continuum fields
is an additional moment certificate.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The state space is weak-$*$ compact by Banach--Alaoglu and metrizable on bounded
sets because the algebra is separable, giving a subsequence.  Pointwise
convergence on a norm-dense subalgebra and uniform norm one determine a unique
continuous extension.  On the spectral subspace $|F_X|>R$ one has
$|F_X|^p\ge R^p$, so functional calculus and positivity give the Markov bound.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Universal coercive continuum handoff]
\label{thm:universal-coercive-continuum}
Let compatible positive contractions $T_X$ act in compatible physical GNS
spaces, with fixed-space projections $E_X$ and source-saturated transient
spaces.  Suppose either:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(H\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item source-native heads have uniform bounds $a_X\le a<1$,
      $d_X\le d<1$, and leakage $b_X\le b$ with
      $b^2<(1-a)(1-d)$; or
\item a predeclared grading has weighted influence constants
      $\kappa_{w,X}\le q<1$.
\end{enumerate}
Then
\[
 \sup_X\|(I-E_X)T_X(I-E_X)\|\le q_*<1,
\]
where in branch~\textup{(H1)} one may take
\[
 q_*=\frac{a+d+\sqrt{(a-d)^2+4b^2}}2.
\]
Consequently the direct-limit transfer has the same noncollapsing contraction
and a gap at least $-\tau^{-1}\log q_*$ at physical time $\tau$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Source saturation and \Cref{thm:universal-Hankel-exhaustion} identify the full
transient norm with the supremum over source heads.  Branch~\textup{(H1)} is
\Cref{thm:sharp-positive-head-tail}, while branch~\textup{(H2)} is the weighted
Schur estimate of \Cref{thm:weighted-source-influence}.  The uniform-gap limit
theorem below transports the common bound to the Hilbert direct limit, and
spectral calculus gives the Hamiltonian gap.
\end{proof}


\subsection{Field tightness, triviality, and the complete limit alternative}
\label{sec:complete-limit-alternative}

\begin{definition}[Field-tightness profile]
\label{def:field-tightness-profile}
For a self-adjoint regulated field $F_n$ in the state $\omega_n$, define
\[
 \Theta_F(R)
 :=\sup_n\omega_n(\mathbf1_{\{|F_n|>R\}}),
 \qquad
 \Xi_F(R)
 :=\sup_n\omega_n\!\left(\frac{F_n^2}{F_n^2+R^2}\right).
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Exact field-tightness and mass-escape alternative]
\label{thm:field-tightness-alternative}
One has
\[
 \boxed{
 \Theta_F(R)\longrightarrow0
 \iff
 \Xi_F(R)\longrightarrow0.}
\]
If the condition fails, there are cutoffs $n_j$, radii $R_j\to\infty$, and
$\varepsilon>0$ such that
\[
 \boxed{
 \omega_{n_j}(\mathbf1_{\{|F_{n_j}|>R_j\}})\ge\varepsilon.}
\]
Thus field nontightness always returns a spectral projection carrying positive
mass to arbitrarily large values.  A uniform positive moment is sufficient for
tightness but is not necessary.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
For $|x|>R$, $x^2/(x^2+R^2)\ge1/2$, while for every $0<M<R$,
\[
 \frac{x^2}{x^2+R^2}
 \le\mathbf1_{\{|x|>M\}}+\frac{M^2}{R^2}.
\]
Functional calculus and expectation give both implications after first sending
$R\to\infty$ and then $M\to\infty$.  Failure of uniform tightness is exactly
the displayed sequence.  Markov's inequality proves the moment sufficient
condition.  Tight distributions with increasingly rare large tails show that
no fixed positive moment bound is necessary.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Source leakage: persistence, splitting, or escape]
\label{thm:source-leakage-limit-alternative}
Let $y_n$ be normalized source-leakage vectors transported to a common Hilbert
carrier.  After passing to a subsequence,
$y_n\rightharpoonup y$, and
\[
 \boxed{\|y_n-y\|^2\longrightarrow1-\|y\|^2.}
\]
Hence the missing source either persists strongly $(\|y\|=1)$, splits into a
persistent and an escaping component $(0<\|y\|<1)$, or escapes every compact
source head $(y=0)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Weak convergence gives
$\langle y_n,y\rangle\to\|y\|^2$.  Expanding
$\|y_n-y\|^2$ and using $\|y_n\|=1$ gives the formula.  The three cases are
exhaustive.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Determining variances and exact operational triviality]
\label{thm:operational-triviality}
Let $\mathscr D$ be a self-adjoint family generating a unital $C^*$-algebra
$\mathcal A$, and let $\omega$ be a state.  Put
\[
 \nu_\omega(a)=\omega(a^2)-\omega(a)^2.
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{
 \nu_\omega(a)=0\ \forall a\in\mathscr D
 \iff
 \dim\mathcal H_\omega=1
 \iff
 \omega\text{ is a character of }\mathcal A.}
\]
If a finite-dimensional selected central component admits no character, then
for every fixed finite self-adjoint generating frame $\mathscr D$ there is a
uniform margin
\[
 \inf_{\omega}\max_{a\in\mathscr D}\nu_\omega(a)>0.
\]
A nondetermining panel cannot certify triviality.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
In the GNS representation,
\[
 \nu_\omega(a)
 =\|(\pi_\omega(a)-\omega(a)I)\Omega_\omega\|^2.
\]
Zero variance makes every generator act scalarly on the cyclic vector.  The
same is then true for every noncommutative polynomial in the generators and,
by norm density, for all of $\mathcal A$.  Cyclicity makes the GNS space one
dimensional and the state multiplicative.  The converse is immediate.  On a
finite character-free component, the continuous function
$\omega\mapsto\max_{a\in\mathscr D}\nu_\omega(a)$ is positive on the compact
state space and therefore has a positive minimum.  If the panel does not
generate the algebra, it may be scalar on the cyclic vector while an orthogonal
factor remains nontrivial.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Complete Grand-Tensor audit profile]
\label{def:complete-GT-profile}
For an audit-ready countably cofinal regulator family, define
\[
 \mathfrak P_{\Grand}
 =(
 \mathfrak P_{\rm cut},
 \mathfrak P_{\rm state},
 \mathfrak P_{\rm ren},
 \mathfrak P_{\rm src},
 \mathfrak P_{\rm form},
 \mathfrak P_{\rm field},
 \mathfrak P_{\rm loc},
 \mathfrak P_{\rm mem},
 \mathfrak P_{\rm coer},
 \mathfrak P_{\rm nontriv}).
\]
The coordinates are respectively the cutoff innovations, projective state
set, renormalization/metric profile, source saturation and leakage, Mosco and
graph-domain profile, field-tightness profile, operational hypergraph and
influence profile, feedback-memory profile, gap/soft-mode profile, and
determining-variance profile.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Universal Grand-Tensor limit and obstruction alternative]
\label{thm:GT-universal-limit-alternative}
Every countably cofinal audit-ready operational regulator family admits a
cofinal subnet on which its complete profile is defined.  The following
nonexclusive branches exhaust the possibilities.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(U\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item \emph{Canonical controlled continuum}: the projective state is unique,
      the renormalization is fixed modulo declared compact gauge, sources and
      forms converge, fields are tight and nontrivial, locality or weighted
      memory is controlled, and the coercive floor remains positive.
\item \emph{Nonunique controlled continuum}: the analytic profiles pass, but
      more than one projective state or inequivalent renormalization modulus
      remains; two states are separated by a finite observable.
\item \emph{Controlled trivial continuum}: the analytic profiles pass and all
      determining centered variances vanish, so the generated GNS theory is one
      dimensional.
\item \emph{Cutoff incompatible}: a prefix, record, predictor, context, source,
      state, observable, or dynamics innovation remains nonzero.
\item \emph{Source incomplete or escaping}: a Hankel/Schur leakage vector
      persists, splits, or escapes every compact source head.
\item \emph{Metric degenerate}: scale or shape collapses, old support is lost,
      a cocycle diamond survives, or an essential normalization modulus remains
      unanchored.
\item \emph{Domain unstable or spectrally escaping}: a Mosco lower/recovery,
      graph-domain, resolvent, or compact-screen witness survives.
\item \emph{Field nontight}: the mass-escape projections of
      \Cref{thm:field-tightness-alternative} survive.
\item \emph{Nonlocal}: a connected-support, shortcut, collar, direct-transfer,
      or feedback route violates the declared operational locality.
\item \emph{Long or growing memory}: delay mass is not tight or feedback-Hankel
      rank is unbounded.
\item \emph{Noncoercive}: a primitive-word transient soft mode has vanishing
      energy or transfer deficit.
\item \emph{Undeclared}: no conclusion is made about a target-domain object for
      which no physical loading, Read, mixed panel, or convergence topology was
      supplied.
\end{enumerate}
When every obstruction profile vanishes and the positive margins remain
noncollapsing, the physical-continuum theorem below applies.  Otherwise the
universal output is the corresponding finite or sequential witness, not an
unresolved hypothesis.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The raw structural carrier and cylinder state follow from
\Cref{thm:global-cylinder-descent}.  Compactness of the finite-stage state
spaces, normalized metric cones, support Grassmannians, and bounded weak graph
balls gives a cofinal subnet on which all compact profile coordinates have
limits.  The state, metric, form, field, locality, memory, coercivity, and
triviality theorems above are each exhaustive and each attach a witness to
failure.  Taking their product yields the listed branches.  The labels are
nonexclusive because, for example, a field may be simultaneously nontight and
noncoercive.  If no negative profile occurs, the hypotheses of the positive
physical-continuum branch are exactly the surviving profile statements.
\end{proof}

\begin{principle}[Priority of obstruction diagnosis]
\label{prin:profile-priority}
For interpretation, the natural order is
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \text{cutoff}&\to\text{state}\to\text{renormalization}\to\text{source}
 \to\text{domain}\to\text{field}\\
 &\to\text{locality}\to\text{memory}\to\text{coercivity}
 \to\text{nontriviality}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
The first failed coordinate is the most upstream obstruction, but every later
failed profile is retained because several physical mechanisms may coexist.
\end{principle}

\begin{theorem}[Positive physical-continuum branch under reconstructed profiles]
\label{thm:universal-physical-continuum}
Let a countably cofinal directed Grand-Tensor system satisfy the following
certificates along one subnet or subsequence:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(P\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item the local history algebras form a quasilocal net and the finite states
      converge projectively, either exactly, by the canonical summable correction
      of \Cref{thm:summable-state-correction}, or along a selected element of the
      compact projective state set in \Cref{thm:projective-state-alternative};
\item every declared bounded observable satisfies the common-domain Cauchy
      condition of \Cref{thm:GNS-observable-limit}, while every declared
      unbounded self-adjoint readout has a fixed renormalization class, a Mosco or
      equivalent resolvent limit as in \Cref{thm:GT-Mosco}, and the exact
      tightness profile of \Cref{thm:field-tightness-alternative};
\item at least one centered declared observable has a positive limiting
      $L^2$ norm;
\item the primitive source family is saturating and its mixed source blocks are
      jointly strict;
\item the physical source metrics lie on the stable branch of
      \Cref{thm:metric-profile-alternative}, the intrinsic operational locality
      profile is identified and controlled, and the feedback family lies in one
      of the controlled branches of \Cref{thm:feedback-limit-classification};
\item one uniform head--tail, influence, domination, or gap certificate holds
      on the saturated selected sector.
\end{enumerate}
Then the limit package is a nontrivial physical Grand-Tensor continuum
realization in the sense of \Cref{def:GT-continuum-realization}.  The declared
finite word relations, positive Gram inequalities, joint-source orientation,
locality statements, and uniform coercive estimate pass to the limit.  Under
exact compatibility the realization is canonical; otherwise the theorem is
subsequential.  No domain semantic is inferred.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The AF/quasilocal algebra and limiting state follow from
\Cref{thm:global-cylinder-descent,thm:AF-limit-state,thm:summable-state-correction,thm:projective-state-alternative,thm:quasilocal-completion}.  Their GNS representation is bounded.  Bounded
observables converge by \Cref{thm:GNS-observable-limit}; unbounded operators
converge by \Cref{thm:GT-Mosco}, and the field profile gives tight spectral
laws without requiring an unnecessarily strong common moment bound.  The positive lower
centered norm excludes a scalar or zero realization.

Primitive-writer saturation identifies the selected cyclic sector, and
\Cref{thm:joint-source-inductive-limit} fixes every retained relative source
orientation.  Uniform metric bounds preserve faithfulness and norm equivalence.
The intrinsic hypergraph and propagation theorems pass the operational
locality estimate to the limit on the common local domain.  The feedback
classification either removes the external memory, passes a stable or
persistent rational kernel, or retains an explicitly controlled
infinite-dimensional short-memory kernel.  Finally,
the common coercive bound holds on every finite source vector; saturation and
continuity extend it to the limiting selected sector.  Entrywise limits of
positive Gram matrices remain positive, and polynomial relations pass by the
bounded common-domain theorem.  Exact compatibility removes all subsequence
choices.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Regenerative discharge of the positive physical-continuum branch]
\label{cor:renewal-positive-continuum}
Assume the regenerative packet of
\Cref{def:renewal-regenerative-packet} and the conclusions of
\Cref{thm:renewal-regenerative-continuum}.  If the remaining declared bounded
and unbounded observables have the renormalization, common-domain, Mosco or
resolvent, and semantic-identification limits required in items~\textup{(P1)--(P2)}
of \Cref{thm:universal-physical-continuum}, then the family has a canonical
nontrivial physical Grand-Tensor continuum realization.  In particular, no
separate compatible-state, source-metric, determining-variance, field-tightness,
compact-screen, or uniform-gap assumption is needed on this branch.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
\Cref{thm:renewal-regenerative-continuum} supplies the state, source,
nontriviality, tightness, metric, locality, feedback, compactness, and coercive
profile coordinates.  The additional hypotheses supply the remaining
observable and domain convergence.  Apply
\Cref{thm:universal-physical-continuum}.
\end{proof}



% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
\subsection{Target-relative weak responses, relation-valued limits, and finite-query completion}
\label{sec:GT-target-relative-response}
% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

The universal continuum profile above controls complete structural and
analytic carriers.  A weaker but often sufficient question is whether one
specified finite-time target has at least one weak response.  The following
results isolate the minimum information for that question and identify the
additional rows required for deterministic, probabilistic, or historical
semantics.

\begin{definition}[Finite-horizon target response]
\label{def:GT-finite-horizon-response}
Let $X$ be a compact admitted initial-data space, let $K$ be a compact metric
writer-value space, let $T>0$ be a physical horizon, and let
$\Phi_{t,s}:X\to X$ be a continuous evolution on the declared branch.  For a
finite self-adjoint target writer bank $h:X\to K$, define
\[
 \Sigma_T(x)(t):=h(\Phi_{t,0}x),\qquad 0\le t\le T,
\]
and the response pseudometric
\[
 \boxed{d_T^h(x,y):=\|\Sigma_T(x)-\Sigma_T(y)\|_{C([0,T];K)}.}
 \tag{TR.1}
\]
The deterministic finite-horizon response quotient is
$Q_T^h=X/\{d_T^h=0\}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Canonical finite-horizon response quotient]
\label{thm:GT-finite-horizon-response-quotient}
For the packet of \Cref{def:GT-finite-horizon-response}, the map induced by
$\Sigma_T$ is an isometry
\[
 \boxed{Q_T^h\cong\Sigma_T(X)\subseteq C([0,T];K).}
 \tag{TR.2}
\]
It is the unique coarsest factor preserving every selected response on
$[0,T]$: if $q:X\to Z$ and every coordinate of $\Sigma_T$ factors through
$q$, then there is a unique surjection $Z\twoheadrightarrow Q_T^h$ compatible
with the response maps.  No constant-rank distribution, smooth quotient
atlas, or finite-dimensional factor coordinate is required.

For $0<T_1<T_2$, restriction of traces gives a canonical surjection
$Q_{T_2}^h\to Q_{T_1}^h$.  The all-future quotient, when intended, is the
inverse limit of this finite-horizon system and is strictly stronger than any
single $Q_T^h$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The pseudometric identifies exactly the fibres of $\Sigma_T$.  The quotient
metric therefore makes the induced map injective and isometric onto its image.
Compactness of $X$ makes the image compact.  If all responses factor through
$q$, two points in one $q$-fibre have identical response traces and hence the
same $Q_T^h$ class; the universal factor map follows.  Restriction of a longer
trace to a shorter horizon proves the final statement.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Compact response relation and branch law]
\label{def:GT-response-relation}
When the physical finite evolution is nonunique, a finite-horizon response
packet is a compact relation
\[
 \Gamma\subseteq X\times\mathcal Y,
 \qquad \mathcal Y=C([0,T];K),
\]
with nonempty compact fibres $\Gamma(x)$.  A \emph{branch law} is an additional
Markov kernel $\kappa_x\in\mathcal P(\Gamma(x))$.  The relation records which
responses are admissible; the kernel records their probabilities.  The former
does not determine the latter.
\end{definition}

% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
\subsubsection{One-sided response cylinders and canonical indefinitely extendible pruning}
\label{sec:GT-response-cylinder-pruning}
% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

\begin{definition}[One-sided compact response-cylinder system]
\label{def:GT-one-sided-response-cylinders}
Let $(K,d_K)$ be a compact metric response alphabet and let
\[
 D_1\subseteq D_2\subseteq\cdots\subseteq[0,T],
 \qquad \overline{\bigcup_{m\ge1}D_m}=[0,T],
\]
be nested finite physical query sets.  For $n\ge m$, let
$r_{n,m}:K^{D_n}\to K^{D_m}$ be restriction.  A \emph{one-sided compact
response-cylinder system} is a family of nonempty compact sets
\[
 \boxed{C_m\subseteq K^{D_m}}
 \tag{TRP.1}
\]
satisfying only
\[
 \boxed{r_{m+1,m}(C_{m+1})\subseteq C_m.}
 \tag{TRP.2}
\]
For $n\ge m$ put
\[
 C_m^{[n]}:=r_{n,m}(C_n),
 \qquad
 \boxed{C_m^\infty:=\bigcap_{n\ge m}C_m^{[n]}.}
 \tag{TRP.3}
\]
Fibrewise equality in \textup{(TRP.2)} is not part of the definition.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Existential inverse limit and canonical response pruning]
\label{thm:GT-response-cylinder-pruning}
Every system of \Cref{def:GT-one-sided-response-cylinders} has a nonempty
compact inverse limit
\[
 \boxed{
 \varprojlim C_m
 =\{(z_m)_m:z_m\in C_m,\ r_{m+1,m}z_{m+1}=z_m\}
 \ne\varnothing.}
 \tag{TRP.4}
\]
Moreover:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(P\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item each $C_m^\infty$ is nonempty and compact;
\item the stable system is fibrewise surjective,
      \[
       \boxed{r_{m+1,m}(C_{m+1}^\infty)=C_m^\infty;}
       \tag{TRP.5}
      \]
\item $C_m^\infty$ is exactly the level-$m$ projection of
      $\varprojlim C_m$;
\item $(C_m^\infty)_m$ is the unique largest subsystem of $(C_m)_m$ in which
      every displayed coarse response extends indefinitely.
\end{enumerate}
Thus fibrewise surjectivity is an all-coarse-branches property, not a minimum
assumption for existence of one compatible response thread.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The product $\prod_mC_m$ is compact.  For $M\ge1$, let $F_M$ be the closed set
of product points satisfying the first $M-1$ compatibility equations.  Choose
any $z_M\in C_M$, define $z_m=r_{M,m}z_M$ for $m<M$, and choose arbitrary
higher coordinates.  Hence every $F_M$ is nonempty.  The sets are nested, so
compactness gives a point in $\bigcap_MF_M$, which is the inverse limit.

For fixed $m$, the nonempty compact sets $C_m^{[n]}$ decrease with $n$, so
$C_m^\infty$ is nonempty compact.  The forward inclusion in
\textup{(TRP.5)} is immediate.  For the reverse inclusion, fix
$a\in C_m^\infty$ and define, for $n\ge m+1$,
\[
 B_n=\{b\in C_{m+1}^{[n]}:r_{m+1,m}b=a\}.
\]
Each $B_n$ is nonempty compact and the family decreases; its intersection
contains a point $b\in C_{m+1}^\infty$ restricting to $a$.  Every inverse-limit
thread projects into every $C_m^{[n]}$, hence into $C_m^\infty$.  Conversely,
surjectivity of the stable system extends every stable point to a thread.  Any
indefinitely extendible subsystem lies in every image $C_m^{[n]}$, proving
maximality and uniqueness.
\end{proof}

\begin{countertheorem}[Nonempty finite response tables need not be compatible]
\label{cth:GT-nonempty-response-tables}
Nonemptiness at every finite depth does not imply a response thread when
one-sided restriction closure fails.  Take $K=\{0,1\}$,
$D_1=\{0\}$, $D_2=\{0,1\}$,
\[
 C_1=\{0\},
 \qquad
 C_2=\{(1,0)\}.
\]
Both tables are nonempty, but the fine response at time zero restricts to one
and is incompatible with the only coarse value.
\end{countertheorem}

\begin{firewall}[One response, all responses, and probabilities]
\label{fire:GT-one-response-not-all}
The pruned packet retains exactly the branches surviving arbitrarily deep
finite queries.  It does not assert that a discarded coarse branch was a
physical source, nor that every coarse candidate extends.  One thread is
sufficient for an existential weak response; the complete compact response
relation, held-out reconstruction diameter, branch kernels, and path law remain
necessary when all admissible branches, probabilities, or chronology are part
of the target.
\end{firewall}

\begin{definition}[Finite-query witness thread]
\label{def:GT-response-thread}
Fix the query hierarchy of
\Cref{def:GT-one-sided-response-cylinders}.  A finite-query response thread is a sequence
$y_m\in K^{D_m}$ satisfying a common modulus
\[
 d_K(y_m(t),y_m(s))\le\omega(|t-s|)
 \qquad(t,s\in D_m),
 \tag{TR.3}
\]
where $\omega(r)\downarrow0$ as $r\downarrow0$.  Its projective Cauchy defect
is
\[
 \boxed{
 \eta_m:=\sup_{n\ge m}\max_{t\in D_m}
 d_K(y_n(t),y_m(t)).}
 \tag{TR.4}
\]
An exact thread has $\eta_m=0$; a coherent approximate thread has
$\eta_m\to0$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Projectively Cauchy response-thread completion]
\label{thm:GT-response-thread-completion}
Every coherent approximate thread in
\Cref{def:GT-response-thread} determines a unique trace
$y\in C([0,T];K)$ with modulus $\omega$ and
\[
 \boxed{
 \max_{t\in D_m}d_K(y(t),y_m(t))\le\eta_m.}
 \tag{TR.5}
\]
A sufficient finite condition is summability of adjacent restriction defects:
if
\[
 \delta_m:=\max_{t\in D_m}d_K(y_{m+1}(t),y_m(t)),
 \qquad \sum_m\delta_m<\infty,
\]
then
$\eta_m\le\sum_{j\ge m}\delta_j$.

Let $\mathfrak d_1,\mathfrak d_2,\ldots$ be nonnegative continuous cylinder
functionals on $C([0,T];K)$, each depending on finitely many physical time and
writer queries.  If, for every fixed $j$, the corresponding finite response
values satisfy
\[
 \mathfrak d_j(y_m)\longrightarrow0
 \qquad(m\to\infty),
 \tag{TR.6}
\]
then $\mathfrak d_j(y)=0$ for every $j$.  Thus one coherent thread and one
complete finite-core residual sequence produce a response satisfying the full
countable weak core.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
For each $t$ in the dense union, the values $y_m(t)$ are eventually defined
and Cauchy by \textup{(TR.4)}.  Define $y(t)$ by their limit.  The common
modulus passes to the dense-set limit and gives a unique continuous extension
to $[0,T]$.  Taking $n\to\infty$ in the definition of $\eta_m$ proves
\textup{(TR.5)}.  The telescoping estimate gives the adjacent-defect bound.
Every cylinder functional is continuous in the uniform topology on the finite
coordinates on which it depends, so \textup{(TR.6)} passes to the limit.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Quantitative residual passage and one-scalar thread certificate]
\label{cor:GT-response-thread-master-defect}
For each finite-query defect $\mathfrak d_j$, let $m(j)$ be a depth on which it
depends and write $\mathfrak d_j[y_m]$ for its evaluation on the restriction of
$y_m$ to that finite query set.  If $\mathfrak d_j$ is $L_j$-Lipschitz, then
for every $m\ge m(j)$,
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathfrak d_j(y)
 \le\mathfrak d_j[y_m]+L_j\eta_m.}
 \tag{TR.6a}
\]
Define the scalar master defect
\[
 \boxed{
 \Delta_m^{\rm resp}
 :=\eta_m+
   \sum_{j=1}^{m}2^{-j}\min\{1,\mathfrak d_j[y_m]\}.}
 \tag{TR.6b}
\]
If $\Delta_m^{\rm resp}\to0$, the thread has a continuous limit satisfying
every member of the countable defect core.  Thus compatibility and finite-core
closure may be certified by one nonnegative scalar sequence without acquiring
a complete response family.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The estimate \textup{(TR.5)} controls the finite coordinates on which
$\mathfrak d_j$ depends, and Lipschitz continuity gives \textup{(TR.6a)}.  The
first term of \textup{(TR.6b)} gives projective-Cauchy compatibility.  For each
fixed $j$, the corresponding nonnegative summand tends to zero, so
\Cref{thm:GT-response-thread-completion} closes the complete core.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Thread-native cutoff compactness and full-sequence alternatives]
\label{thm:GT-thread-cutoff-compactness}
Let $N\nearrow\infty$ index regulators.  After the declared physical writer
identifications, suppose each cutoff supplies one certified trace
$y_N\in C([0,T];K_\infty)$, where $K_\infty$ is compact, and all traces obey
one continuation modulus.  Then $(y_N)$ is relatively compact in
$C([0,T];K_\infty)$.  If every fixed member of a complete continuum defect core
satisfies
\[
 \mathfrak d_j^\infty(y_N)\longrightarrow0,
\]
then every convergent subsequence has a limit satisfying the complete declared
core.  No Hausdorff transport of the complete response graphs is required for
this subsequential existence conclusion.

The full regulator sequence converges if either the limiting target response is
unique or the selected traces obey a summable Cauchy estimate
\[
 \boxed{
 \sum_N\norm{y_{N+1}-I_{N+1/N}y_N}_\infty<\infty.}
 \tag{TR.6c}
\]
Absent one of these selection rows, the canonical conclusion is subsequential
existence rather than an arbitrarily chosen limiting branch.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Compactness of $K_\infty$ and the common modulus give Arzel\`a--Ascoli
compactness.  Continuity of every fixed defect passes its vanishing to each
subsequential limit.  Uniqueness identifies all cluster points; alternatively,
the summable estimate makes the physically identified traces Cauchy in the
uniform norm.
\end{proof}


\begin{theorem}[Relation-valued compactness and tracewise weak closure]
\label{thm:GT-relation-valued-limit}
Let $X$ and $\mathcal Y=C([0,T];K)$ be compact metric spaces after the declared
field, writer-tail, and continuation estimates.  Let
$\Gamma_n\subseteq X\times\mathcal Y$ be nonempty compact response graphs with
\[
 d_{\rm H}(\Gamma_n,\Gamma)\longrightarrow0
 \tag{TR.7}
\]
for a compact graph $\Gamma$.  Let
$\mathfrak d_{j,n}\ge0$ be continuous tracewise weak, stress, constraint,
gauge, source--work, or boundary defects, and suppose that on the common
compact carrier
\[
 \mathfrak d_{j,n}\longrightarrow\mathfrak d_j
 \quad\text{uniformly},
 \qquad
 \sup_{(x,y)\in\Gamma_n}\mathfrak d_{j,n}(x,y)\longrightarrow0
 \tag{TR.8}
\]
for every fixed $j$.  Then every $(x,y)\in\Gamma$ satisfies
$\mathfrak d_j(x,y)=0$ for all $j$.

If the response fibres are asymptotically equicontinuous over the base, in
the precise sense that for every $\varepsilon>0$ there are $\delta>0$ and
$n_0$ such that
\[
 \begin{gathered}
 n\ge n_0,\quad (x,y),(x',y')\in\Gamma_n,\quad
 d_X(x,x')<\delta\\
 \Longrightarrow\quad d_{\mathcal Y}(y,y')<\varepsilon,
 \end{gathered}
 \tag{TR.9}
\]
then $\Gamma$ is the graph of a single-valued continuous response.  Without
\textup{(TR.9)} or an independent uniqueness theorem, the correct conclusion
is relation valued.  A probability law on $\Gamma$ requires, in addition,
convergent branch kernels or finite-cylinder probabilities.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
For $(x,y)\in\Gamma$, Hausdorff convergence gives
$(x_n,y_n)\in\Gamma_n$ converging to $(x,y)$.  Uniform convergence and
\textup{(TR.8)} imply $\mathfrak d_j(x,y)=0$.  Applying \textup{(TR.9)} to
simultaneous approximants of two limiting graph points yields the same uniform
modulus on $\Gamma$.  Two points in one limiting fibre therefore have zero
distance, and the resulting response is continuous on the projected domain.
A compact support set admits many probability measures unless a kernel is
separately supplied.  Mere convergence of the individual fibre diameters is
not enough: the singleton graphs of $x\mapsto\operatorname{clamp}(nx)$ can
converge to a relation with a vertical segment at the origin.
\end{proof}

\begin{countertheorem}[A strong differential defect is not necessary for weak closure]
\label{cth:GT-strong-defect-not-necessary}
For the equation $\dot u=0$ on $[0,T]$, set
\[
 u_N(t)=N^{-1}\sin(N^2t).
\]
Then $u_N\to0$ uniformly, and the integrated residual against every
$C^1$ test tends to zero, while
\[
 \int_0^T|\dot u_N(t)|\,\dd t\asymp N
\]
diverges.  Consequently a vanishing strong residual is a sufficient compiler,
not a minimum requirement for a weak continuum.
\end{countertheorem}

\begin{proof}
Uniform convergence is immediate.  Integration by parts writes the weak
residual as endpoint terms and an integral of $u_N$ against the test
derivative, all of which tend to zero.  Since
$\dot u_N=N\cos(N^2t)$, its absolute integral grows linearly in $N$.
\end{proof}

\begin{countertheorem}[Barycentric closure fails for nonlinear dynamics]
\label{cth:GT-barycenter-not-solution}
For
\[
 \dot x=2\sqrt{x_+},\qquad x(0)=0,
\]
both $x_0(t)=0$ and $x_1(t)=t^2$ are exact solutions.  The equal mixture is
supported entirely on exact responses, but its barycenter
$\bar x(t)=t^2/2$ satisfies
\[
 \dot{\bar x}(t)=t
 \ne 2\sqrt{\bar x(t)}=\sqrt2\,t
 \qquad(t>0).
\]
Thus an occupation or branch law must evaluate nonlinear writers before
averaging unless concentration or an exact affine closure has been proved.
\end{countertheorem}

\begin{theorem}[Positive writer evolution and derived current]
\label{thm:GT-writer-state-derived-current}
Let $\mathcal S$ be a finite-dimensional unital self-adjoint writer system and
let $\mathcal T(t,s):\mathcal S\to\mathcal S$ be a positive unital evolution.
For every positive normalized initial state $\omega_0$, define
\[
 \boxed{\omega_t(f):=\omega_0(\mathcal T(t,0)f).}
 \tag{TR.10}
\]
Then each $\omega_t$ is positive and normalized.  If the right generator
$\mathcal L_t$ exists on a core $\mathcal S^1$ and the declared source and
boundary writer is $\mathfrak s_t$, the target current is derived by
\[
 \boxed{
 \jmath_t(f)=\omega_t(\mathcal L_tf)+\mathfrak s_t(f),
 \qquad f\in\mathcal S^1.}
 \tag{TR.11}
\]
No independent current is required on this invariant writer branch.

A positive extension of $\omega_t$ to a complete field law may exist without
being unique.  It is unique only when the writer system separates the relevant
physical states, and a nonlinear writer outside the generated system is not
determined by \textup{(TR.10)} alone.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Positivity and unitality of $\mathcal T(t,0)$ preserve positivity and the value
of the unit under composition with $\omega_0$.  Differentiation of
\textup{(TR.10)} on the generator core gives \textup{(TR.11)} after the
declared source and boundary term is separated.  The extension and
nonuniqueness statements are the ordinary positive-extension and
nonseparation alternatives for a finite operator system.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Structure-preserving finite-scheme descent]
\label{cor:GT-structure-preserving-response}
Suppose a regulator family supplies finite trial and physical test spaces, a
Fortin map from an exhausting continuum test core, and a discrete weak update
whose complete assembled residual vanishes on the finite test space.  Assume:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(S\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item one coercive discrete energy remains uniformly below the energy of the
      boundary of the occupied gauge, follower, support, and coefficient chart;
\item the update gives a uniform negative-norm time-translation bound;
\item the target nonlinear writers are compact in the topology required by the
      weak equation;
\item the Fortin and coefficient/stencil defects tend to zero.
\end{enumerate}
Then the finite solutions or approximate solutions contain a coherent response
thread satisfying the full continuum weak core.  The resulting limit is
subsequential unless the limiting weak response is unique or a Cauchy estimate
is supplied.  No equilibrium, storage, contraction, or path-law packet is
required for this finite-time conclusion.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The energy barrier prevents chart exit.  The coercive spatial bound and the
negative-norm time estimate give the compactness required by the discrete
Aubin--Lions or screen--tail argument.  Galerkin orthogonality and the Fortin
map pass every fixed continuum test, while the target-specific strong
compactness passes the nonlinear writers.  Applying
\Cref{thm:GT-response-thread-completion} gives one trace satisfying the complete
weak core.  Uniqueness is precisely the additional selection needed to remove
subsequence dependence.
\end{proof}

\begin{principle}[Response birth before source birth]
\label{prin:GT-response-before-source-birth}
A new fine writer, harmonic, field component, or response pattern is first a
\emph{response birth}.  It is generated rather than externally sourced when it
is already the output of the transported old state under the common fine
nonlinear writer.  A new physical source is charged only to the constitutive
residual remaining after subtraction of:
\[
 \boxed{
 \begin{gathered}
 \text{transported old dynamics}
 +\text{ deterministic fine nonlinear generation}\\
 +\text{ declared source/work}
 +\text{ gauge, constraint, and boundary terms}.
 \end{gathered}}
 \tag{TR.12}
\]
A positive response innovation or larger factor dimension is therefore not by
itself a source innovation.
\end{principle}

\begin{firewall}[Finite-time response, equilibrium, passivity, stability, and occurrence]
\label{fire:GT-dynamical-target-separation}
The five target classes in
\Cref{prin:GT-target-dynamical-hierarchy} are genuinely distinct.  Uniform
rotation on a circle gives a global finite-time evolution with no equilibrium;
$\dot x=x$ has an equilibrium which is unstable; a passive one-copy energy may
coexist with several invariant states and hence need not give incremental
uniqueness; and a mathematically constructed solution need never occur in an
accepted physical cylinder.  The native certificate for each target is kept on
its own branch.
\end{firewall}

\subsection{Universal continuum firewalls}
\label{sec:universal-continuum-firewalls}

\begin{countertheorem}[Finite source completeness is not uniform observability]
\label{cth:finite-complete-not-uniform}
For every $\varepsilon>0$, the synthesis
\[
 S_\varepsilon=
 \begin{pmatrix}1&1\\0&\varepsilon\end{pmatrix}
\]
is invertible and hence source complete, while
$\lambda_{\min}(S_\varepsilon^*S_\varepsilon)\to0$ as
$\varepsilon\downarrow0$.  Therefore pointwise finite source completeness does
not imply a uniform frame floor, bounded pseudoinverse, or continuum
observability estimate.
\end{countertheorem}

\begin{proof}
The determinant equals $\varepsilon$, so the map is invertible for every
positive $\varepsilon$.  Its column difference is $(0,\varepsilon)^\mathsf T$;
using the coefficient vector $(1,-1)/\sqrt2$ gives a Rayleigh quotient
$\varepsilon^2/2$, which forces the least eigenvalue to zero.
\end{proof}

\begin{countertheorem}[Uniform second moments need not preserve nontriviality]
\label{cth:second-moment-nontriviality}
There are centered probability measures $\mu_n$ with
$\int x^2\,\dd\mu_n(x)=1$ for every $n$ which converge weakly to $\delta_0$.
Consequently a finite-stage variance floor does not pass through weak
convergence without uniform integrability.  A uniform $p$-moment with $p>2$,
or the covariance domination in
\Cref{thm:renewal-fluctuation-dissipation}, supplies the missing control.
\end{countertheorem}

\begin{proof}
Let $\mu_n=(1-n^{-2})\delta_0+\frac1{2n^2}(\delta_n+\delta_{-n})$.  It is
centered, has second moment one, and converges weakly to $\delta_0$.
\end{proof}

\begin{countertheorem}[Random-scan scheduling can close independent local gaps]
\label{cth:random-scan-gap}
Let $C$ be a positive self-adjoint one-cell transfer with fixed projection $E$
and transient norm $q<1$.  On $N$ independent cells, let one uniformly chosen
cell be updated at each global opportunity:
\[
 P_N=\frac1N\sum_{i=1}^{N}C_i.
\]
On the complement of the all-fixed product sector,
\[
 \boxed{\|(I-E^{\otimes N})P_N(I-E^{\otimes N})\|
 =1-\frac{1-q}{N}.}
\]
Thus independent local gaps and zero inter-cell influence do not give a
volume-uniform global gap under a fixed-rate random-scan clock.  A noncollapsing
physical event intensity per cell is a separate scaling certificate.
\end{countertheorem}

\begin{proof}
The commuting positive operators $C_i$ are simultaneously diagonalizable.
The largest nontrivial product eigenvalue is obtained by placing one cell in an
eigenvector of eigenvalue $q$ and every other cell in the fixed space, giving
$[(N-1)+q]/N$.  Every other nontrivial eigenvalue is no larger.
\end{proof}

\begin{countertheorem}[Blocking does not create a gap]
\label{cth:blocking-does-not-create-gap}
Let $0\preceq T\preceq I$ and let $E$ project onto its fixed space.  For every
$m\ge1$,
\[
 \boxed{\|(I-E)T^m(I-E)\|
 =\|(I-E)T(I-E)\|^m.}
\]
Thus rewriting a regulator as a thicker block proves no gap unless the
integrated block is estimated by information not already equivalent to the
original gap.
\end{countertheorem}

\begin{proof}
The fixed space reduces a positive self-adjoint $T$.  The spectral theorem on
its orthogonal complement gives
$\sup_{\lambda\in\spec T_\perp}\lambda^m
=(\sup_{\lambda\in\spec T_\perp}\lambda)^m$.
\end{proof}

\begin{countertheorem}[Norm-small comparison with a gapless family]
\label{cth:norm-small-gapless}
If positive contractions $S_X,S_{0,X}$ satisfy
$\|S_X-S_{0,X}\|\to0$ and $\|S_{0,X}\|\to1$, then
$\|S_X\|\to1$.  Hence a uniformly norm-small perturbation of a gapless
reference transfer cannot establish a noncollapsing gap.
\end{countertheorem}

\begin{proof}
The reverse triangle inequality gives
$\|S_X\|\ge\|S_{0,X}\|-\|S_X-S_{0,X}\|\to1$, while every $S_X$ is a
contraction.
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[Structural limits are not physical continuum limits]
An AF or quasilocal structural limit supplies a common algebraic carrier.  It
does not by itself supply a compatible physical state, nontrivial renormalized
observables, tight unbounded fields, locality at a physical scale, a uniform
metric, a noncollapsing gap, or identification with a target continuum theory.
Each of these is a separate certificate in
\Cref{def:GT-continuum-realization,thm:GNS-observable-limit,thm:state-compactness-tightness,thm:universal-coercive-continuum,thm:universal-physical-continuum}.
\end{firewall}


\subsection{Uniform limit and finite robustness audits}

\begin{theorem}[Exact uniform-gap theorem]
\label{thm:uniform-gap-limit}
Let compatible Hilbert-space contractions $T_X$ intertwine isometric cutoff
embeddings, and let compatible projections $E_X$ project onto their fixed
spaces.  Put $Q_X=I-E_X$ and
$\rho_X=\|Q_XT_XQ_X\|$.  On the Hilbert direct limit,
\[
 \boxed{\|Q_\infty T_\infty Q_\infty\|=\sup_X\rho_X.}
\]
Therefore a noncollapsing limit gap $\gamma_0>0$ exists exactly when
$\sup_X\rho_X\le1-\gamma_0$, in which case
\[
 \boxed{\|T_\infty^k-E_\infty\|\le(1-\gamma_0)^k.}
\]
Positive gaps at every finite cutoff do not imply a uniform gap.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The transient finite-stage subspaces embed isometrically and their union is
dense in the limit transient subspace.  Intertwining gives an operator of norm
at most $\sup_X\rho_X$ on the union and hence on its closure.  Conversely the
restriction of the limit operator to every finite stage has norm $\rho_X$, so
the limit norm is at least their supremum.  The power estimate follows by
iteration.  For collapse, on $\Span\{e_1,\ldots,e_X\}$ let
$T_Xe_j=(1-1/j)e_j$ and $E_X=0$.  Every finite norm is $1-1/X<1$, but the
supremum and limit norm are one.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Singular-gap certification of predictive rank]
\label{thm:robust-hankel-gap}
Let an exact finite Hankel panel $H$ have rank $d$ and
$\sigma_d(H)\ge\gamma>0$.  If
$\|\widetilde H-H\|_{\op}\le\varepsilon<\gamma/2$, then
\[
 \boxed{
 \sigma_d(\widetilde H)\ge\gamma-\varepsilon,
 \qquad
 \sigma_{d+1}(\widetilde H)\le\varepsilon.}
\]
Any threshold in $(\varepsilon,\gamma-\varepsilon)$ recovers the exact rank.
Without a positive least-nonzero singular value, rank and flat depth are not
robust.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Weyl's singular-value perturbation inequality gives
$|\sigma_j(\widetilde H)-\sigma_j(H)|\le\varepsilon$.  Use
$\sigma_{d+1}(H)=0$.  Rank is discontinuous when the least nonzero singular
value tends to zero.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Finite reset and record-leakage audits]
\label{thm:reset-record-audit}
For a nonzero finite CP branch $\mathcal R$, complete atomic reset is equivalent
to rank one of its Hermitian transfer matrix, equivalently
\[
 \boxed{\mathcal R(X)=\Tr(EX)\omega}
\]
for one effect $E\succeq0$ and state $\omega\succeq0$.  The second singular
value is the exact distance to rank one.  Separately, for a record-forgetting
map $\mathfrak F$, complete future map $C$, and
$\Ran J_{\rm rec}=\Ker\mathfrak F$, exact operational future-nullity is
\[
 \boxed{\mathbb G_{\rm rec}=J_{\rm rec}^*C^*CJ_{\rm rec}=0.}
\]
Target mixing, a fresh endpoint, or reference renewal does not imply either
atomic reset or global record erasure.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
A rank-one linear map is $X\mapsto\ell(X)\omega$.  Complete positivity makes
$\omega\succeq0$ and makes $\ell$ a positive functional, hence
$\ell(X)=\Tr(EX)$ with $E\succeq0$.  The converse is immediate, and
Eckart--Young identifies the second singular value as the distance to rank one.
The record identity is
$\mathbb G_{\rm rec}=(CJ_{\rm rec})^*(CJ_{\rm rec})$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Selection-safe adaptive coordinate audit]
\label{thm:anytime-audit}
Suppose bounded intervention coordinates $X_t\in[0,1]$ are sampled
predictably, coordinate $j$ has mean $p_j$, sample count $N_j(t)$, and empirical
mean $\widehat p_j(t)$.  Choose $w_j>0$ with $\sum_jw_j\le1$.  With probability
at least $1-\alpha$, simultaneously for every coordinate and every time with
$N_j(t)=k\ge1$,
\[
 \boxed{
 |\widehat p_j(t)-p_j|
 \le\sqrt{\frac1{2k}\log\!\left(\frac{\pi^2k^2}{3\alpha w_j}\right)}.}
\]
Thus a packet, depth, mark partition, or failure witness chosen after adaptive
exploration remains valid when its margin holds throughout this simultaneous
confidence region.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Apply the conditional Hoeffding bound at the $k$th predictably selected sample
of coordinate $j$.  Allocate error probability
$6\alpha w_j/(\pi^2k^2)$ and take the union bound over $j,k$, using
$\sum_{k\ge1}k^{-2}=\pi^2/6$.  Adaptive selection and stopping are
post-processing of the same covered probability vector.
\end{proof}


\begin{countertheorem}[Ambient saturation is not data identifiable]
\label{cth:ambient-invisible}
Let $(\mathcal H,U,T,S)$ be an equivariant source realization and let a
nonzero space $\mathcal Z$ carry an arbitrary representation $V$ and a
positive contraction $A$ commuting with it.  Put
\[
 \mathcal H'=\mathcal H\oplus\mathcal Z,
 \quad U'_g=U_g\oplus V_g,
 \quad T'=T\oplus A,
 \quad S'=S\oplus0.
\]
Then all declared source moments are unchanged although $\mathcal Z$ may carry
arbitrary additional sectors.
\end{countertheorem}

\begin{proof}
For every source vector, $(T')^kS'f=T^kSf\oplus0$.  Applying $U'_g$ and then
$(S')^*$ gives the old moment.  The representation and spectrum on
$\mathcal Z$ are otherwise unconstrained.
\end{proof}

\begin{assessment}[Exact unconditional/conditional boundary after Parts I-B and I-C]
The intervention table, minimal record, finite comb, predictive quotient,
process and contextual history algebras, intrinsic regular word hierarchy,
automatic flatness, joint-source calculus, strict cutoff functor, AF/quasilocal
structural limit, compatible-state extension, and the finite-memory alternatives
are universal theorems.  Primitive-writer saturation, exact Hankel exhaustion,
moment-exact leakage, head--tail and influence criteria, relative metric
densities, Calder\'on frames, causal innovation dilations, locality and feedback
residuals, state compactness, and the uniform-gap handoff are likewise universal
certification mechanisms.

For the resolved primitive renewal, the one-step score tangent, Fisher metric,
conditional information action, martingale covariance, Brownian limit, three
orthogonal tetrahedral score triplets, and local fibre-frame floor are exact.
For any complete differentiated pair table, the efficient connected short,
edge-action Pythagoras, operational router and holonomy, tree--holonomy
coercivity, and support-order obstruction witnesses are exact.  Under verified
$S_4$ covariance, the complete four-cell interaction audit reduces to one
prototype per support order, and the complete tetrahedral connection and local
gap reduce to one edge and one triangle.  Explicit flat and constant-connection
information regulators have rigorous resolvent and semigroup continuum limits.

What remains domain specific is whether the actual microscopic process has a
nonzero pair prototype and vanishing higher-order prototypes, whether its edge
innovation vanishes, which internal connection fibre or twist is physically
loaded, whether the reconstructed graph has the required uniform atlas margin,
and whether the actual predictable mean step agrees with the connected-action
minimizing movement at $o(\tau_X)$.  The physical metric, matter occurrence,
field semantic, unbounded-domain tightness, nonperturbative dynamics, and
conjecture-specific estimates also remain domain certificates.  A structural
inductive limit is therefore not promoted to a physical continuum theory
without the explicit certificates of \Cref{def:GT-continuum-realization}.
\end{assessment}

\part{Domain-specific Grand-Tensor loadings}
\label{part:domain-specific-loadings}
