existing typed occurrence and multiplicity-one incidence theorems applied to
the same physical word.
\end{proof}

Let $G\cong\C^3$ be the rank-three endpoint quotient of the locked $K_4$ edge
packet and let $P_{\rm loop}$ be its orthogonal cycle triplet.  The generation
carrier is $G$; $P_{\rm loop}$ remains provenance.  This allocation is made on
the complete mixed Gram and is not inferred from the common dimension three.

\begin{theorem}[Unconditional active finite structural Standard Model]
\label{thm:SM-active-SM-I}
Assume the explicit geometry short of
\Cref{thm:SM-active-residual-short}, the faithful private plane, the
operation-native weak reset \textup{(SM.0n)}, one colour bridge with
$\omega_{\rm col}>0$, and one typed word satisfying
\Cref{thm:SM-active-determinant-incidence}.  Then, at every finite cutoff:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(S\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item the internal algebra is the relative commutant
      \[
       M_3(\C)\oplus M_2(\C)\oplus\C\oplus\C;
      \]
\item the reconstructed determinant seed has unitary stabilizer
      \[
       \boxed{
       G_{\rm SM}=S(U(3)\times U(2))
       \cong
       \frac{SU(3)\times SU(2)\times U(1)}{\mathbb Z_6};}
       \tag{SM.0u}
      \]
\item anomaly freedom fixes, up to simultaneous orientation,
      \[
       \boxed{6Y:(Q,u,d,L,e,\nu,H)
       =(1,4,-2,-3,-6,0,3);}
       \tag{SM.0v}
      \]
\item the endpoint source supplies exactly three future-visible structural
      generations, while the orthogonal cycle triplet remains loop provenance;
\item the packet contains one weak Higgs doublet and one nonzero self-adjoint
      grading-odd finite Dirac operator; the five numerical residue matrices
      are typed contractions of this one operator in one common generation
      frame.
\end{enumerate}
Relative to the already completed spacetime and private carrier, the active
completion adds no persistent Hilbert direction.  Its minimum declared
operation content is one colour bridge and one typed determinant--Clifford
word; if one physical word carries both shadows, the operation count decreases
without changing the theorem.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The internal algebra is
\Cref{thm:SM-active-internal-commutant}.  The determinant stabilizer and anomaly
weights are \Cref{thm:SM-group,thm:SM-anomaly-forced-weights}.  The one-word
handoff is \Cref{thm:SM-active-determinant-incidence}; the generation statement
is the endpoint/loop allocation of the locked $K_4$ source.  All conclusions
are preserved under the forgetful map to the old Store, so the construction is
a conservative active completion.
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[Active realization versus historical identification]
\label{fire:SM-active-historical}
The theorem proves a finite structural Standard Model for the explicitly
completed active primitive.  It does not infer the private support operations,
colour bridge, weak reset, or typed determinant--Clifford word from their
marginal source Grams.  A historical claim about the old Store must evaluate
the corresponding flat word hierarchy, relative-commutant multiplicities, and
mixed operation corners.  Flatness with zero colour or determinant shadow is a
finite historical no-go, not a reason to reopen spacetime or add a target-shaped
Hilbert factor.  Numerical couplings, masses, flavour matrices, running, and
the fermion measure are not consequences of the structural packet.
\end{firewall}


\begin{theorem}[Finite-Heisenberg revision and no-hiding packet]
\label{thm:SM-qutrit-packet}
Let $H_3=\mathbb F_3^2$ and let unitaries $R_a$ satisfy
\[
 R_aR_bR_a^*R_b^*=\omega^{[a,b]}I,
 \qquad \omega=e^{2\pi i/3},
\]
for a nondegenerate alternating form $[\cdot,\cdot]$ on $H_3$.  Then
\[
 \boxed{C^*(R_a:a\in H_3)\cong M_3(\C).}
\]
The uniform revision twirl is exact qutrit erasure,
\[
 \frac19\sum_aR_aAR_a^*=\Tr(A)\frac{I_3}{3},
\]
and its minimal Stinespring environment has dimension nine and factors,
canonically up to a unitary, as
$\C^3_{\rm key}\otimes\C^3_{\rm rec}$.  The relative-revision operators
$\overline{R_a}\otimes R_a$ form an ordinary representation whose Fourier
projections are the rank-one Bell pointer.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
For $a\ne0$, choose $c$ with $[c,a]\ne0$.  Conjugation by $R_c$ multiplies
$R_a$ by a nontrivial cubic root, so $\Tr R_a=0$.  Hence the nine $R_a$ are
Hilbert--Schmidt orthogonal and span a nine-dimensional simple complex
$C^*$-algebra, necessarily $M_3(\C)$.  The twirl commutes with this full matrix
algebra and is therefore scalar; trace preservation fixes the scalar to
$\Tr(A)/3$.  The nine orthogonal Kraus operators give Choi rank nine, so the
minimal environment has dimension nine.  The standard minimal erasure
isometry sends $\psi$ to a maximally entangled key state tensored with
$\psi$ in the record factor, proving the factorization.  Complex conjugation
cancels the projective cocycle in
$\overline{R_a}\otimes R_a$; Fourier inversion on $H_3$ gives the Bell
projections.
\end{proof}

Let $C$ and $W$ be Hermitian spaces of dimensions three and two.

\begin{definition}[Standard-Model determinant seed]
A Standard-Model determinant seed is
$\mathfrak S_{\rm SM}=(C,W,\tau)$ with a unitary isomorphism
\[
 \tau:\det C\otimes\det W\xrightarrow{\sim}\C.
\]
Only the determinant line and its stabilizer are physical in the finite group
reconstruction: replacing $\tau$ by $e^{i\theta}\tau$ changes neither the
stabilizer nor any completely positive incidence branch.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Automorphism reconstruction of the global gauge group]
\label{thm:SM-group}
The unitary tensor automorphism group of the determinant seed is
\[
 \boxed{
 \Aut_{\rm U}(C,W,\tau)=S(\U(3)\times\U(2))
 \cong\frac{\SU(3)\times\SU(2)\times\U(1)}{\Z_6}.}
\]
An explicit quotient map is
$\Phi(g_3,g_2,z)=(z^{-2}g_3,z^3g_2)$, with kernel
$\{(z^2I_3,z^{-3}I_2,z):z^6=1\}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
A pair $(A,B)\in\U(C)\times\U(W)$ preserves $\tau$ exactly when
$\det(A)\det(B)=1$, giving $S(\U(3)\times\U(2))$.  The displayed map has
image in this subgroup.  Given $(A,B)$ there, choose $z^6=\det B$ and put
$g_3=z^2A$, $g_2=z^{-3}B$; these are special unitary and map to $(A,B)$.
The kernel is the displayed order-six central subgroup.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Anomaly-forced central weights]
\label{thm:SM-anomaly-forced-weights}
Let the central infinitesimal action on $C\oplus W$ be
$iaI_C\oplus ibI_W$.  On the tensor types
\[
 Q=C\otimes W,\quad u=\Lambda^2C^*,\quad d=C,
 \quad L=W^*,\quad e=\Lambda^2W^*,\quad H=W,
\]
the corresponding weights are
\[
 (a+b,-2a,a,-b,-2b,b).
\]
After replacing right-handed matter by left-handed conjugates, all local mixed,
cubic, and gravitational anomalies vanish exactly when
\[
 \boxed{3a+2b=0.}
\]
Up to reversal of the $U(1)$ orientation, the primitive integral solution is
$(a,b)=(-2,3)$ and therefore
\[
 \boxed{y=6Y:\quad (Q,u,d,L,e,H)=(1,4,-2,-3,-6,3).}
\]
Thus the finite hypercharge table is fixed by the dimensions $(3,2)$, the
tensor type packet, and anomaly freedom; it is not an independent loading
parameter.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Direct trace over the left-handed chiral packet gives
\[
 \mathcal A_{\SU(3)^2Y}=\mathcal A_{\SU(2)^2Y}
 =\frac12(3a+2b),
 \qquad
 \mathcal A_{{\rm grav}^2Y}=3(3a+2b),
\]
and
\[
 \mathcal A_{Y^3}=3(3a+2b)(3a^2+2b^2).
\]
The pure colour anomaly cancels as $2-1-1$, and four weak doublets remove the
Witten anomaly.  Since $3a^2+2b^2>0$ for a nontrivial action, simultaneous
vanishing is equivalent to $3a+2b=0$.  The coprime integral solution is
$(-2,3)$ up to sign, and substitution gives the displayed weights.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Renewal-admissible finite real algebra]
\label{thm:SM-finite-real-algebra}
Assume a charged finite real geometry has at most three charged central
summands and total non-scalar real algebra dimension at most $22$.  Assume it
contains an independent complex scalar factor, a quaternionic factor carrying
a minimal pseudoreal weak doublet, and a genuinely complex faithful colour
factor of rank at least three.  Then, up to permutation of summands,
\[
 \boxed{\mathcal A_F^{\rm ch}\cong
 \C\oplus\mathbb H\oplus M_3(\C).}
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The quaternionic factor has real dimension $4$.  A genuinely complex matrix
factor of rank at least three has real dimension at least
$2\cdot3^2=18$.  These two factors already exhaust the non-scalar dimension
bound $22$.  The independent scalar channel contributes no non-scalar
dimension.  Replacing $M_3(\C)$ by a smaller complex matrix algebra violates
the colour-rank hypothesis; omitting $\mathbb H$ violates pseudoreal weak type;
omitting $\C$ removes the independent scalar channel; and adding another
non-scalar factor exceeds the bound.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Central descent selector]
\label{thm:SM-selector}
An irreducible $\SU(3)\times\SU(2)\times\U(1)$ representation with colour
triality $t\in\Z/3$, weak parity $s\in\Z/2$, and integer charge $y=6Y$
descends to the quotient in \Cref{thm:SM-group} exactly when
\[
 \boxed{2t+3s+y\equiv0\pmod6.}
\]
Its indicator is the finite Fourier projector
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathbf1_{2t+3s+y\equiv0\ (6)}
 =\frac16\sum_{k=0}^5
 \exp\!\left(\frac{2\pi ik}{6}(2t+3s+y)\right).}
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
A generator of the quotient kernel acts by
$\exp(2\pi i(2t+3s+y)/6)$.  Triviality gives the congruence, and character
orthogonality on $\Z/6\Z$ gives the indicator.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Tensor generation of one chiral matter packet]
\label{thm:SM-generation}
Define
\[
 Q=C\otimes W,
 \quad u=\Lambda^2C^*,
 \quad d=C,
 \quad L=W^*,
 \quad e=\Lambda^2W^*,
 \quad H=W.
\]
Their $(\SU(3),\SU(2))_y$ labels are
\[
\begin{array}{c|c}
 Q&(\mathbf3,\mathbf2)_1\\
 u&(\mathbf3,\mathbf1)_4\\
 d&(\mathbf3,\mathbf1)_{-2}\\
 L&(\mathbf1,\mathbf2)_{-3}\\
 e&(\mathbf1,\mathbf1)_{-6}\\
 H&(\mathbf1,\mathbf2)_3.
\end{array}
\]
The seed supplies one-dimensional intertwiner spaces for
$Q\otimes H\to u$, $Q\otimes H^*\to d$, and $L\otimes H^*\to e$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
By \Cref{thm:SM-anomaly-forced-weights}, the primitive central weights are
$C\sim(\mathbf3,\mathbf1)_{-2}$ and
$W\sim(\mathbf1,\mathbf2)_3$.  Tensor products add charge, and
$\Lambda^2\overline{\mathbf3}\cong\mathbf3$.  Evaluation gives the down
channel, exterior multiplication gives the lepton channel, and the determinant
seed identifies the up channel.  Each target irreducible occurs once, so the
intertwiner space is one dimensional by Schur's lemma.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Anomaly cancellation of the generated packet]
\label{thm:SM-anomaly}
After replacing right-handed fields by left-handed conjugates, the packet
$Q\oplus u^c\oplus d^c\oplus L\oplus e^c$ has vanishing local gauge and mixed
gravity anomalies and no Witten $\SU(2)$ anomaly.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
With quadratic index $1/2$ for defining representations, the anomaly
coefficients are
\[
 2-1-1=0,
\]
\[
 2(1)\frac12+(-4)\frac12+(2)\frac12=0,
 \qquad
 3(1)\frac12+(-3)\frac12=0,
\]
\[
 6(1)^3+3(-4)^3+3(2)^3+2(-3)^3+6^3=0,
\]
and
\[
 6(1)+3(-4)+3(2)+2(-3)+6=0.
\]
There are four weak doublets after colour multiplicity is included, so the
global $\SU(2)$ anomaly also vanishes.
\end{proof}

\begin{countertheorem}[Gauge data do not determine generation number]
\label{cth:generation-number}
For every $g\ge1$, tensor the anomaly-free one-generation matter packet by a
trivial multiplicity space $F_g\cong\C^g$.  The gauge types, central descent
law, incidence slots, and anomaly cancellation remain unchanged, while the
generation number is $g$.
\end{countertheorem}

\begin{proof}
Tensoring by a trivial representation changes no irreducible gauge type and
multiplies each local anomaly coefficient by $g$, so zero remains zero.  The
number of weak doublets becomes $4g$ and remains even.  The multiplicity space
lies in the commutant and is therefore invisible to the associative gauge
relations alone.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Incidence-before-interference firewall]
\label{thm:SM-incidence-firewall}
Let $P_R,P_L$ be two typed supports.  If every primitive coefficient $K_a$
satisfies $P_LK_aP_R=0$, then every finite coefficient obtained from the
$K_a$ by sums, products, adjoints, ancillary matrix coefficients, coherent
order control, postselection, environment measurement, or norm limits also
has zero $P_R\to P_L$ block.  In particular, no character, Maslov, Walsh, or
relative-history compression can create a grading-changing occurrence that is
absent from the primitive coefficient algebra.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The coefficients preserving the support decomposition form a unital
$C^*$-algebra.  It is closed under sums, products, adjoints, tensoring with
ancillas, taking ancillary matrix coefficients, and norm limits.  Every listed
network operation remains in this algebra.  Character and Walsh compressions
are finite linear combinations, so their cross block also vanishes.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Common-row top-Walsh occurrence reconstruction]
\label{thm:SM-top-Walsh}
Let $X_j^2=\delta_jI$ with $\delta_j>0$, put
$N_j=\delta_j^{-1/2}X_j$, and let one typed occurrence row be
$\mathcal C:Q_0\to Y$.  For $\varepsilon\in\{\pm1\}^m$ define
\[
 K_\varepsilon(\mathbf t)=\mathcal C
 e^{-i\varepsilon_1t_1X_1}\cdots e^{-i\varepsilon_mt_mX_m}.
\]
For $S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\}$ let
$\chi_S(\varepsilon)=\prod_{j\in S}\varepsilon_j$ and
$K_S=2^{-m/2}\sum_\varepsilon\chi_S(\varepsilon)K_\varepsilon$.  Then
\[
 \boxed{
 K_S(\mathbf t)=2^{m/2}
 \prod_{j\notin S}\cos(\sqrt{\delta_j}t_j)
 \prod_{j\in S}[-i\sin(\sqrt{\delta_j}t_j)]
 \mathcal C N_S,}
\]
with the $N_j$ kept in their displayed order.  At quarter dwells
$t_j=(2k_j+1)\pi/(2\sqrt{\delta_j})$, every proper Walsh column vanishes and
the top column is a nonzero scalar times $\mathcal C N_1\cdots N_m$.
Consequently, when the ordered product is unitary, the top column reconstructs
$\mathcal C$ and has the same rank.  The conclusion requires the physical
common-row residual to vanish; equal resolved branch effects alone do not
supply that relation.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Use
$e^{-i\varepsilon_jt_jX_j}=\cos(\sqrt{\delta_j}t_j)I
-i\varepsilon_j\sin(\sqrt{\delta_j}t_j)N_j$ and expand the ordered product.
Walsh orthogonality kills every monomial whose sign set differs from $S$.
At quarter dwell every cosine is zero, so only the full sign set survives.
If the ordered product is unitary, right multiplication by its adjoint recovers
the occurrence row.  Without one common terminal row, branch-dependent phases
can preserve every resolved effect while changing the top Walsh column, so the
common-row certificate is necessary.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Principal matter-module theorem]
\label{thm:SM-principal-module}
Let $Q_0\cong\C^2$ and let $C_0:Q_0\to Y$ be a nonzero loaded occurrence row
with
\[
 C_0^*C_0=\kappa I_{Q_0},\qquad \kappa>0.
\]
Then
\[
 \mathcal J_{C_0}:M_2(\C)\to\operatorname{Hom}(Q_0,Y),
 \qquad \mathcal J_{C_0}(X)=\kappa^{-1/2}C_0X,
\]
is an isometric faithful right $M_2(\C)$ module map:
\[
 \boxed{\mathcal J_{C_0}(X)^*\mathcal J_{C_0}(Y)=X^*Y.}
\]
The Choi or Stinespring rank of the complete occurrence column is environment
memory and is not a generation count.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The identity is
$\kappa^{-1}X^*C_0^*C_0Y=X^*Y$.  Hence the range is one standard faithful
right module.  Replacing $C_0$ by a minimal Stinespring column changes only the
environment basis; its rank is therefore an implementation dimension and does
not change the source-side module.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Source-derived commutator--Hodge generation carrier]
\label{thm:SM-commutator-Hodge}
Let $W_0=\mathbf1^\perp\subset\R^4$ and let
$F:W_0\to\operatorname{Herm}_0(M_2(\C))$ be a tetrahedrally covariant writer
with
\[
 \tau_2(F(x)F(y))=\lambda\langle x,y\rangle,
 \qquad \lambda>0.
\]
Under $H^1(K_4;\R)\cong\bigwedge^2W_0$, define
\[
 \mathcal C_F(x\wedge y)=-\frac i2[F(x),F(y)].
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{
 \tau_2(\mathcal C_F(\xi)\mathcal C_F(\eta))
 =\lambda^2\langle\xi,\eta\rangle,}
\]
so $\lambda^{-1}\mathcal C_F$ is an orthogonal isomorphism
\[
 \boxed{H^1(K_4;\R)\cong\operatorname{Herm}_0(M_2(\C)).}
\]
Composing with the occurrence row of \Cref{thm:SM-principal-module} produces
six physical commutator-edge histories spanning one source-derived
three-dimensional generation carrier.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Choose an orthogonal coordinate map $O:W_0\to\R^3$ with
$F(x)=\sqrt\lambda\,Ox\cdot\sigma$.  The Pauli identity gives
$-\frac i2[F(x),F(y)]=\lambda(Ox\times Oy)\cdot\sigma$.  The cross-product
inner product is the exterior-square inner product, proving the metric formula
and bijectivity.  Multiplication on the left by $C_0/\sqrt\kappa$ preserves
that Gram and therefore transports the carrier into the physical occurrence
space.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Copy--deformation separation and multiplicity saturation]
\label{thm:SM-multiplicity-saturation}
Let the complete future-cyclic carrier support the faithful right
$M_2(\C)$ action of \Cref{thm:SM-principal-module}.  Suppose the future
transfer $T$ commutes with that action; equivalently, its writer--Casimir
commutator Gram vanishes.  Then, up to a multiplicity-space unitary,
\[
 \mathcal K=\mathcal M\otimes\C^2,
 \qquad T=A\otimes I_2,
 \qquad S=B\otimes I_2.
\]
For
\[
 \mathbb G_{{\rm mult},n}
 =\bigl[B^*A^{*i}A^jB\bigr]_{0\le i,j<n},
\]
the matter and generation Grams factor as
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathbb G_{{\rm mat},n}=\mathbb G_{{\rm mult},n}\otimes I_2,
 \qquad
 \mathbb G_{{\rm gen},n}=\mathbb G_{{\rm mult},n}\otimes I_3.}
\]
If $g_n$ and $h_n$ are the cross and next-layer blocks, then
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathfrak L_{{\rm mult},n}
 =h_n-g_n^*\mathbb G_{{\rm mult},n}^\dagger g_n\succeq0}
\]
has rank equal to the next multiplicity-rank increment.  The minimal
future-visible realization has exactly one generation copy precisely when,
for some $n$,
\[
 \boxed{\rank\mathbb G_{{\rm mult},n}=1,
 \qquad \mathfrak L_{{\rm mult},n}=0.}
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Every finite unital representation of $M_2(\C)$ is a direct sum of defining
representations, giving $\mathcal K\cong\mathcal M\otimes\C^2$.  Its
commutant is $\End(\mathcal M)\otimes I_2$, so the zero deformation condition
gives $T=A\otimes I_2$ and module naturality gives $S=B\otimes I_2$.
The displayed matrices are Grams of the Krylov columns $A^jB$ tensored with
the identity on the matter or Hodge carrier.  The generalized Schur complement
is the Gram of the orthogonal part of the next column, proving the rank and
saturation statements.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Marked bi-Hankel reconstruction of the finite Dirac operator]
\label{thm:SM-marked-Dirac}
Let $S$ be the common source synthesis, $M$ the reconstructed future transfer,
and assume the ordinary block Hankel Gram
\[
 \mathbb H_d=[S^*M^{i+j}S]_{0\le i,j\le d}
\]
is flat.  Let
\[
 \mathbb N_d=[S^*M^iDM^jS]_{0\le i,j\le d}
\]
be an independently measured one-insertion panel and put
$P_{\mathbb H}=\mathbb H_d\mathbb H_d^\dagger$.  If
\[
 \Delta_{\rm null}^D
 =\|(I-P_{\mathbb H})\mathbb N_d\|_{\HS}^2
 +\|\mathbb N_d(I-P_{\mathbb H})\|_{\HS}^2=0,
\]
then for every full-row-rank Gram factorization $\mathbb H_d=R_d^*R_d$,
\[
 \boxed{D_{R_d}=(R_d^\dagger)^*\mathbb N_dR_d^\dagger}
\]
is the unique packet operator with $\mathbb N_d=R_d^*D_{R_d}R_d$.
Different Gram factors conjugate $D_{R_d}$ by the same packet unitary.  After
self-adjointness, grading, reality, order, one-leg, generation, slot, and
Majorana tests, this one operator exports
\[
 \boxed{Y_u,Y_d,Y_e,Y_\nu,M_R}
\]
in one common physical generation frame.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The same-null condition says that the sesquilinear form encoded by
$\mathbb N_d$ descends to the quotient determined by $\mathbb H_d$.  The
Moore--Penrose formula is the unique representing operator on the row space.
Two full-row-rank Gram factors differ by one unitary, so the reconstructed
operator transforms by that same unitary.  All support, type, and slot
projections are reconstructed on the same packet; therefore every Yukawa block
is obtained by one common orthogonal compression and all blocks share the same
generation gauge.  The Majorana block transforms by congruence because it is a
symmetric singlet form.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Exact no-matter obstruction for the displayed six-state source]
\label{thm:SM-six-state-no-matter}
Suppose every primitive system-bearing coefficient of a source commutes with a
common central-support and grading refinement.  Then every finite or
norm-convergent network formed from those coefficients by serial or parallel
composition, coherent order control, ancillas, feedback, postselection,
environment measurement, and chronological limits is support preserving.
Consequently every grading-changing Maslov/Walsh coefficient and every marked
finite-Dirac block is zero.  In particular, for the displayed six-state source,
\[
 \boxed{K_\mu=0,\qquad Q_\mu=0,\qquad D_F=0.}
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The block-preserving coefficients form a unital $C^*$-algebra closed under all
listed operations and norm limits.  Every effective coefficient therefore has
zero cross-support block.  Finite character compression and the marked-panel
reconstruction are linear or quotient operations on those coefficients and
cannot create an absent block.
\end{proof}

\subsubsection{Generator-native occurrence and typed Radon--Nikodym geometry}
\label{sec:SM-generator-native-occurrence}

The incidence firewall says that a stationary grading-even source cannot create
matter.  The correct next object is therefore the cross-support first derivative
of the actual pre-release semigroup, not another stationary likelihood or a
chosen Yukawa matrix.

\begin{theorem}[Cross-support extraction from a CP generator]
\label{thm:SM-cross-support-generator}
Let $\mathcal T_{t,*}=e^{t\mathcal L_*}$ be a finite-dimensional completely
positive trace-preserving semigroup on
$\mathcal H=\mathcal H_L\oplus\mathcal H_R$.  Define
\[
 \boxed{\Phi_{L\leftarrow R}(X)
 =P_L\mathcal L_*(P_RXP_R)P_L}
\]
and similarly $\Phi_{R\leftarrow L}$.  These maps are completely positive and
are reconstructed operationally by
\[
 \boxed{\Phi_{L\leftarrow R}(X)
 =\lim_{t\downarrow0}t^{-1}P_L\mathcal T_{t,*}(P_RXP_R)P_L.}
\]
In every GKSL representation only the support-changing jump amplitudes survive:
\[
 \boxed{\Phi_{L\leftarrow R}(X)
 =\sum_\alpha(P_LV_\alpha P_R)X(P_RV_\alpha^*P_L).}
\]
The Hamiltonian and anticommutator terms vanish under this compression.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Insert the GKSL formula.  Since $P_LP_R=0$, both the commutator with the
Hamiltonian and each anticommutator term has zero $L\leftarrow R$ compression.
The remaining sum is Kraus form and hence CP.  Differentiability of the
semigroup at zero gives the operational limit.  Because the map is defined
from $\mathcal L_*$ itself, it is independent of the chosen GKSL coordinates.
\end{proof}



% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
\subsubsection{Channel-native Hamiltonian tangents and noisy coherent compilation}
\label{sec:SMST-channel-native-tangent}
% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

The principal-log branch of \Cref{thm:SMST-store-native-route} is an exact
finite-time reconstruction, but exact unitary pulses are stronger than finite
SM emergence requires.  The weaker operational datum is a two-sided physical
channel family through the identity whose first derivative is a Hamiltonian
derivation on the canonical source core.  Dissipative or leakage terms which
begin at second order may be suppressed by physical subdivision and are not
first-order matter obstructions.

Let \(M_d=M_d(\C)\), with matrix units \(E_{ab}\).  For linear maps
\(\mathcal L_1,\mathcal L_2:M_d\to M_d\), define
\[
 \boxed{
 \langle\!\langle\mathcal L_1,\mathcal L_2\rangle\!\rangle
 :=\sum_{a,b=1}^{d}
   \langle\mathcal L_1(E_{ab}),\mathcal L_2(E_{ab})\rangle_{\HS}.}
\]
Write \(\|\cdot\|_{\rm sup,HS}\) for the associated norm, using the real
Hilbert structure on Hermiticity-preserving maps.

\begin{lemma}[Exact conditioning of inner derivations]
\label{lem:SMST-inner-derivation-norm}
For \(H=H^*\),
\[
 \boxed{
 \|\operatorname{ad}_H\|_{\rm sup,HS}^2
 =2d\left\|H-\frac{\Tr H}{d}I\right\|_{\HS}^2.}
\]
Thus \(H\mapsto-i\operatorname{ad}_H\) is injective on traceless Hermitian
matrices and has smallest singular value \(\sqrt{2d}\).
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Expand
\(\sum_{a,b}\|HE_{ab}-E_{ab}H\|_{\HS}^2\).  The two diagonal sums are
\(d\Tr(H^2)\), while the two mixed sums total \(2|\Tr H|^2\).  Their
difference is the displayed expression.
\end{proof}

Choose an orthonormal basis
\((T_\alpha)_{\alpha=1}^{d^2-1}\) of the traceless Hermitian matrices and put
\(\mathcal C_\alpha=-i\operatorname{ad}_{T_\alpha}\).  Let
\[
 G^{\rm Ham}_{\alpha\beta}
 =\langle\!\langle\mathcal C_\alpha,\mathcal C_\beta\rangle\!\rangle,
 \qquad
 b_\alpha(\mathcal L)
 =\langle\!\langle\mathcal C_\alpha,\mathcal L\rangle\!\rangle.
\]

\begin{definition}[Canonical Hamiltonian tangent]
\label{def:SMST-Hamiltonian-tangent}
For a Hermiticity-preserving map \(\mathcal L:M_d\to M_d\), define
\[
 \boxed{
 H_{\mathcal L}
 =\sum_\alpha
 \bigl((G^{\rm Ham})^{-1}b(\mathcal L)\bigr)_\alpha T_\alpha,}
\]
\[
 \boxed{
 \Delta_{\rm Ham}(\mathcal L)
 =\|\mathcal L+i\operatorname{ad}_{H_{\mathcal L}}\|_{\rm sup,HS}^2.}
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Finite Hamiltonian-tangent certificate]
\label{thm:SMST-Hamiltonian-tangent-certificate}
The operator \(H_{\mathcal L}\) is the unique traceless Hermitian minimizer of
\[
 H\longmapsto\|\mathcal L+i\operatorname{ad}_H\|_{\rm sup,HS}^2.
\]
Moreover
\[
 \boxed{
 \Delta_{\rm Ham}(\mathcal L)=0
 \iff
 \mathcal L=-i\operatorname{ad}_{H_{\mathcal L}}.}
\]
On the positive branch,
\[
 \frac{\mathcal L+i\operatorname{ad}_{H_{\mathcal L}}}
      {\sqrt{\Delta_{\rm Ham}(\mathcal L)}}
\]
is an explicit non-Hamiltonian first-order channel direction.  Removing it
after the fact is a projection fit.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The normal equations for orthogonal projection onto
\(\Span_{\R}\{\mathcal C_\alpha\}\) are
\(G^{\rm Ham}h=b(\mathcal L)\).  Positive definiteness follows from
\Cref{lem:SMST-inner-derivation-norm}; hence the minimizer is unique and the
residual is exactly the squared orthogonal distance.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Finite Leibniz and star residuals]
\label{def:SMST-Leibniz-star}
For a linear map \(\mathcal L:M_d\to M_d\), put
\[
 \Delta_{\rm Leib}(\mathcal L)
 =\sum_{a,b,c,e}
 \|\mathcal L(E_{ab}E_{ce})
 -\mathcal L(E_{ab})E_{ce}
 -E_{ab}\mathcal L(E_{ce})\|_{\HS}^2,
\]
\[
 \Delta_*(\mathcal L)
 =\sum_{a,b}
 \|\mathcal L(E_{ab}^*)-\mathcal L(E_{ab})^*\|_{\HS}^2.
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Finite star derivations are inner]
\label{thm:SMST-finite-inner-derivation}
If
\[
 \Delta_{\rm Leib}(\mathcal L)=\Delta_*(\mathcal L)=0,
\]
then there is a unique traceless Hermitian \(H\) such that
\[
 \boxed{\mathcal L=-i[H,\,\cdot\,].}
\]
It equals \(H_{\mathcal L}\).
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The Leibniz residual makes \(\mathcal L\) a derivation.  Put
\[
 A=\sum_{k=1}^{d}\mathcal L(E_{k1})E_{1k}.
\]
Using \(E_{ij}=E_{i1}E_{1j}\) and differentiating \(E_{11}^2=E_{11}\), one
checks directly that \(\mathcal L(E_{ij})=[A,E_{ij}]\) for every matrix unit.
The star identity implies \([A+A^*,X]=0\) for every \(X\), so \(A+A^*\) is
scalar.  Replacing \(A\) by its skew-Hermitian part does not change the
commutator, and
\[
 H=\frac{i}{2}(A-A^*)
\]
is Hermitian.  Subtracting its scalar trace gives the unique traceless
representative.
\end{proof}

Let \(C:\C^d\to\mathcal H_F\) be the canonical source-fixing isometry between
a logical score carrier and the saturated full-cell carrier, and put
\[
 \iota(X)=CXC^*,\qquad P=CC^*.
\]
Such an encoder is internal whenever the logical and full-cell source families
have vanishing mutual Schur residuals: the normalized cross transport of
\Cref{thm:joint-source-short} is then unitary and uniquely fixes both source
families.

Let \(\Phi_+(t),\Phi_-(t)\) be physical CPTP curves on the full-cell algebra,
defined for \(0\le t\le t_0\), with
\(\Phi_\pm(0)=\id\).  Denote their derivatives at zero by
\(\widetilde{\mathcal L}_\pm\), and define
\[
 \mathcal L_\pm^C(X)
 =C^*\widetilde{\mathcal L}_\pm(\iota(X))C.
\]

\begin{definition}[Reversible channel-tangent defect]
\label{def:SMST-channel-tangent-defect}
Put
\[
 \Delta_{\rm core}^\pm
 =\sum_{a,b}
 \|\widetilde{\mathcal L}_\pm(\iota(E_{ab}))
   -\iota(\mathcal L_\pm^C(E_{ab}))\|_{\HS}^2,
\]
\[
 \boxed{
 \begin{aligned}
 \Delta_{\rm tan}
 ={}&\Delta_{\rm core}^++\Delta_{\rm core}^-\\
 &+\Delta_{\rm Ham}(\mathcal L_+^C)
  +\Delta_{\rm Ham}(\mathcal L_-^C)
  +\|\mathcal L_+^C+\mathcal L_-^C\|_{\rm sup,HS}^2.
 \end{aligned}}
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Exact channel-native reversible mixer tangent]
\label{thm:SMST-channel-native-tangent}
The defect \(\Delta_{\rm tan}\) is nonnegative.  Its zero branch is equivalent
to the existence of one unique traceless Hermitian \(H\) on the logical
carrier such that
\[
 \boxed{
 \widetilde{\mathcal L}_+(\iota(X))
 =\iota(-i[H,X]),}
\]
\[
 \boxed{
 \widetilde{\mathcal L}_-(\iota(X))
 =\iota(+i[H,X])}
\]
for every \(X\in M_d\).  Exact finite-time unitarity is not required.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Vanishing of the two core terms says that both derivatives preserve the
encoded matrix algebra.  The Hamiltonian residuals give traceless Hermitian
\(H_+,H_-\) with
\(\mathcal L_\pm^C=-i\operatorname{ad}_{H_\pm}\).  The last term gives
\(\operatorname{ad}_{H_++H_-}=0\); tracelessness implies \(H_-=-H_+\).
The converse is immediate.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Source-core leakage Pythagoras]
\label{prop:SMST-channel-core-Pythagoras}
If
\[
 \widetilde{\mathcal L}=-i\operatorname{ad}_{\widetilde H},
 \qquad \widetilde H=\widetilde H^*,
\]
put
\[
 K=C^*\widetilde HC,\qquad B=(I-P)\widetilde HC.
\]
Then the compressed derivative is \(-i\operatorname{ad}_K\) and
\[
 \boxed{\Delta_{\rm core}=2d\|B\|_{\HS}^2.}
\]
Thus the Hamiltonian tangent preserves the encoded carrier exactly when
\(B=0\).
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Relative to \(P\mathcal H_F\oplus(I-P)\mathcal H_F\), the commutator with
\(\iota(E_{ab})\) has internal block \([K,E_{ab}]\) and off-core blocks
\(BE_{ab}\) and \(-E_{ab}B^*\).  Compression removes the internal block.
Summing the squared norms over \(a,b\) gives \(2d\|B\|_{\HS}^2\).
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Exact inverse and robust Choi-purity branches]
\label{thm:SMST-channel-unitarity-branches}
Let \(\Phi,\Psi:M_d\to M_d\) be CPTP.
If
\[
 \boxed{
 \Delta_{\rm inv}
 =\|J_{\Psi\circ\Phi}-J_{\id}\|_{\HS}^2
 +\|J_{\Phi\circ\Psi}-J_{\id}\|_{\HS}^2=0,}
\]
then
\[
 \boxed{\Phi=\Ad_U,\qquad\Psi=\Ad_{U^*}}
\]
for one unitary \(U\).

More generally, if \(\Phi\) has unnormalized Choi matrix \(J\) and
\[
 \delta=d^2-\Tr(J^2),
\]
then there is a unitary \(U\) such that
\[
 \boxed{
 \|J-J_{\Ad_U}\|_1
 \le2\sqrt\delta+\frac{\delta}{d}.}
\]
These are stronger sufficient branches; neither is required by
\Cref{thm:SMST-channel-native-tangent}.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Choose Kraus families \((A_i)\), \((B_j)\) for \(\Phi,\Psi\).  If the two
composition residuals vanish, every \(B_jA_i\) is a scalar multiple of \(I\),
because the identity channel has Choi rank one.  Trace preservation of
\(\Psi\) gives \(A_i^*A_k\in\C I\), so all nonzero \(A_i\) are proportional
to one unitary and \(\Phi=\Ad_U\); similarly \(\Psi=\Ad_{U^*}\).

For the robust statement, normalize \(\rho=J/d\) and let \(p_1\) be its
largest eigenvalue.  Since
\(p_1\ge\Tr(\rho^2)=1-\delta/d^2\), put
\(\tau=1-p_1\le\delta/d^2\).  Writing the leading Choi component as
\(|A\rangle\!\rangle\langle\!\langle A|\), trace preservation gives
\(A^*A\preceq I\) and
\(\Tr(I-A^*A)=d\tau\).  Extending the polar partial isometry of \(A\) to a
unitary \(U\) yields
\(\|A-U\|_{\HS}^2\le d\tau\).  The rank-one trace-norm estimate contributes
\(2d\sqrt\tau\), while the discarded positive Choi tail has trace \(d\tau\).
Substitution proves the bound.
\end{proof}

\begin{countertheorem}[Axis populations do not certify coherence]
\label{cth:SMST-axis-populations-no-coherence}
A unitary pulse and a nonunitary random-unitary channel can have identical
transition probabilities between all three score axes at every pulse time.
\end{countertheorem}

\begin{proof}
Let \(X_{01}\) swap \(e_0,e_1\) and fix \(e_2\).  The channel
\(\Ad_{e^{-itX_{01}}}\) and
\[
 \Psi_t=(1-\sin^2t)\id+\sin^2t\,\Ad_{X_{01}}
\]
have the same axis transition table.  For \(0<\sin^2t<1\), the second has
Choi rank two.  Its derivative at the origin is zero, whereas the unitary
curve has derivative \(-i\operatorname{ad}_{X_{01}}\).
\end{proof}

Assume now that \(\Delta_{\rm tan}=0\) and that
\(t\mapsto\Phi_\pm(t)\circ\iota\) is twice continuously differentiable in
diamond norm, with second derivative bounded by \(M_2\).  Put
\[
 \mathcal L_H=-i\operatorname{ad}_H,\qquad
 M_L=\|\mathcal L_H\|_\diamond,
\]
\[
 \boxed{
 \kappa=\frac12\left(M_2+M_L^2e^{t_0M_L}\right).}
\]

\begin{theorem}[Quadratic noisy-channel remainder]
\label{thm:SMST-quadratic-channel-remainder}
For \(0\le t\le t_0\),
\[
 \boxed{
 \|\Phi_\pm(t)\circ\iota
 -\iota\circ e^{\pm t\mathcal L_H}\|_\diamond
 \le\kappa t^2.}
\]
If the projected first-derivative error is at most
\(\epsilon_{\rm tan}\), the right-hand side becomes
\[
 \boxed{t\epsilon_{\rm tan}+\kappa t^2.}
\]
Thus arbitrary dissipative or carrier-leakage effects are admissible when they
begin at second order.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The physical and ideal curves agree at zero and, on the exact tangent branch,
have the same first derivative.  Taylor's formula with integral remainder
bounds the physical curve relative to its linearization by \(M_2t^2/2\).
The exponential series gives
\[
 \|e^{\pm t\mathcal L_H}-I\mp t\mathcal L_H\|_\diamond
 \le\frac12t^2M_L^2e^{tM_L}.
\]
The approximate statement adds the first-derivative error.
\end{proof}

Let \(P_0,P_1,P_2\) be three sharp score-axis projections and put
\[
 \mathsf K
 =\{\epsilon\in\{\pm1\}^3:\epsilon_0\epsilon_1\epsilon_2=1\},
 \qquad
 Z_\epsilon=\sum_{j=0}^2\epsilon_jP_j,
\]
\[
 \chi_{ij}(\epsilon)=\epsilon_i\epsilon_j,
 \qquad
 \boxed{
 H_{ij}
 =\frac14\sum_{\epsilon\in\mathsf K}
 \chi_{ij}(\epsilon)Z_\epsilon HZ_\epsilon.}
\]
The three \(H_{ij}\) are the exact off-diagonal edge blocks of \(H\).
Assume the sign channels \(\Ad_{Z_\epsilon}\) are physical on the encoded
carrier.  For \(s<0\), define \(\Phi(s)=\Phi_-(-s)\), and for \(s\ge0\),
\(\Phi(s)=\Phi_+(s)\).

\begin{theorem}[Noisy Klein refocusing]
\label{thm:SMST-noisy-Klein-refocusing}
For an edge \(e=\{i,j\}\), define
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathfrak T_{e,n}^{\Phi}(t)
 =\left[
 \prod_{\epsilon\in\mathsf K}
 \Ad_{Z_\epsilon}\circ
 \Phi\!\left(\frac{\chi_e(\epsilon)t}{4n}\right)
 \circ\Ad_{Z_\epsilon}
 \right]^n.}
\]
Let \(M=\|H\|_{\op}\).  Then
\[
 \boxed{
 \|\mathfrak T_{e,n}^{\Phi}(t)\circ\iota
 -\iota\circ\Ad_{e^{-itH_e}}\|_\diamond
 \le
 |t|\epsilon_{\rm tan}
 +\frac{(3M^2+\kappa)t^2}{4n}.}
\]
The total absolute physical mixer time is \(|t|\), independently of \(n\).
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
There are \(4n\) elementary channel factors, each of parameter magnitude
\(|t|/(4n)\).  Telescoping in diamond norm and
\Cref{thm:SMST-quadratic-channel-remainder} gives
\[
 |t|\epsilon_{\rm tan}+\frac{\kappa t^2}{4n}.
\]
For the ideal Hamiltonian channels, Klein character orthogonality isolates
\(H_e\).  The unitary product formula has operator error
\(3M^2t^2/(8n)\); the inequality
\(\|\Ad_U-\Ad_V\|_\diamond\le2\|U-V\|_{\op}\)
adds \(3M^2t^2/(4n)\).
\end{proof}

Put
\[
 r_{ij}=\|P_iHP_j\|_{\HS},
\]
and let \(\alpha>0\) be the protected-plane matter amplitude.

\begin{theorem}[Direct and bracket noisy-channel compilers]
\label{thm:SMST-channel-direct-bracket}
The connected Hamiltonian support graph has one of the following two
branches.

\emph{Direct branch.}  If \(r_{12}>0\), put
\[
 D_{12}=\frac{\alpha}{r_{12}}H_{12},
 \qquad
 t=\frac{\alpha h}{r_{12}}.
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{
 \begin{aligned}
 &\|\mathfrak T_{12,n}^{\Phi}(t)\circ\iota
 -\iota\circ\Ad_{e^{-ihD_{12}}}\|_\diamond\\
 &\qquad\le
 \frac{\alpha h}{r_{12}}\epsilon_{\rm tan}
 +\frac{(3M^2+\kappa)\alpha^2h^2}
 {4nr_{12}^2}.
 \end{aligned}}
\]
Fixed \(n\) and \(\epsilon_{{\rm tan},h}\to0\) give \(o(h)\) error.

\emph{Bracket branch.}  If \(r_{12}=0\), connectedness forces
\(r_{01},r_{02}>0\).  Put
\[
 D_{\rm br}
 =-i\left[\frac{H_{01}}{r_{01}},
          \frac{H_{02}}{r_{02}}\right].
\]
A four-edge channel commutator \(\mathfrak W_{h,n}^{\rm br}\) satisfies
\[
 \boxed{
 \begin{aligned}
 &\|\mathfrak W_{h,n}^{\rm br}\circ\iota
 -\iota\circ\Ad_{e^{-i\alpha hD_{\rm br}}}\|_\diamond\\
 &\quad\le
 64\alpha^{3/2}h^{3/2}
 +2\sqrt{\alpha h}
  (r_{01}^{-1}+r_{02}^{-1})\epsilon_{\rm tan}\\
 &\qquad+
 \frac{(3M^2+\kappa)\alpha h}{2n}
 (r_{01}^{-2}+r_{02}^{-2}).
 \end{aligned}}
\]
Hence \(n_h\to\infty\) and
\(\epsilon_{{\rm tan},h}=o(\sqrt h)\) give \(o(h)\) error.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The direct estimate is
\Cref{thm:SMST-noisy-Klein-refocusing} with the displayed time.  For the
bracket branch, use refocused edge times
\(\sqrt{\alpha h}/r_{01}\) and
\(\sqrt{\alpha h}/r_{02}\).  The ideal four-factor commutator differs from
the target by at most \(64\alpha^{3/2}h^{3/2}\) in channel norm.  Each edge
flow occurs twice, and summing the first-derivative and quadratic refocusing
errors gives the remaining terms.
\end{proof}

For either compiled physical channel \(\mathfrak W_h\), let \(D\) denote the
direct or bracket target and define
\[
 \mathcal L_h
 =h^{-1}\left(
 C^*\mathfrak W_h(\iota(\,\cdot\,))C-\id\right),
 \qquad
 H_h=H_{\mathcal L_h}.
\]

\begin{theorem}[Compiled-channel generator convergence]
\label{thm:SMST-compiled-channel-generator}
If
\[
 \|\mathfrak W_h\circ\iota
 -\iota\circ\Ad_{e^{-ihD}}\|_\diamond=o(h),
\]
then
\[
 \boxed{\mathcal L_h\longrightarrow-i\operatorname{ad}_D,}
\]
and
\[
 \boxed{
 H_h\longrightarrow D-\frac{\Tr D}{d}I}
\]
in Hilbert--Schmidt norm.  Quantitatively, for a dimension-dependent
norm-equivalence constant \(c_d\),
\[
 \boxed{
 \left\|H_h-\left(D-\frac{\Tr D}{d}I\right)\right\|_{\HS}
 \le\frac{c_d}{\sqrt{2d}}
 \|\mathcal L_h+i\operatorname{ad}_D\|_\diamond.}
\]
Every typed block, positive occurrence Choi packet, support-polar residue
system, and relative Howe Gram is therefore a continuous source-native output
of the actual compiled channel.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The ideal channel has expansion
\[
 \Ad_{e^{-ihD}}
 =\id-ih\operatorname{ad}_D+O(h^2)
\]
in diamond norm.  Divide the assumed error by \(h\).  Orthogonal projection
onto the Hamiltonian-derivation subspace is contractive in the superoperator
Hilbert norm, finite-dimensional norm equivalence contributes \(c_d\), and
\Cref{lem:SMST-inner-derivation-norm} inverts the commutator map.
Continuity of finite compression, positive partial trace, polar support, and
Gram formation gives the final statement.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Classical reversible shuffles have maximal tangent obstruction]
\label{thm:SMST-classical-shuffle-obstruction}
Let \(\Psi\) be an inverse-paired random-permutation channel and put
\(\mathcal S=\Psi-\id\).  Then
\[
 \boxed{
 H_{\mathcal S}=0,\qquad
 \Delta_{\rm Ham}(\mathcal S)=\|\mathcal S\|_{\rm sup,HS}^2.}
\]
Thus every nontrivial counting-reversible shuffle is orthogonal to the
Hamiltonian tangent space and cannot replace the coherent channel entrance at
first order.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Inverse-paired weights make \(\mathcal S\) self-adjoint on Hilbert--Schmidt
operator space.  Every \(-i\operatorname{ad}_H\) is skew-adjoint.  The two real
subspaces are orthogonal, so the Hamiltonian projection is zero.
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[A coherent component is not a coherent tangent]
\label{fire:SMST-Hamiltonian-component}
A differentiated CPTP family may have
\[
 \mathcal L=-i\operatorname{ad}_H+\mathcal D,
 \qquad\mathcal D\ne0.
\]
A nonzero projected Hamiltonian \(H_{\mathcal L}\) does not make the complete
physical tangent Hamiltonian.  The Hamiltonian, reversal, and source-core
residuals must vanish or satisfy the branch-appropriate scaling.  Likewise,
one isolated rank-one Choi matrix proves only that one channel is unitary; it
does not supply a differentiable two-sided family or an unaliased generator.
\end{firewall}

\begin{corollary}[Channel-native finite-SM entrance]
\label{cor:SMST-channel-native-entrance}
Assume the protected type and grading records, the canonical source encoder,
the sharp axis sign controls, and one forward/reverse CPTP channel pair through
the identity.  If:
\[
 \boxed{\Delta_{\rm tan}=0,}
\]
the Hamiltonian support graph is connected, the second channel derivatives are
bounded, and the direct or bracket branch satisfies the corresponding
asymptotic conditions of
\Cref{thm:SMST-channel-direct-bracket}, then the compiled channel reconstructs
one nonzero grading-changing Hamiltonian generator on the source core.

If its finite-Dirac relation residual and admissible odd-provenance residual
vanish and the relative Howe Gram is positive, the resulting complete odd
generator is the source-native finite-Dirac operator and its five typed residue
blocks and multiplicity commutant are canonical outputs.  Exact finite-time
Choi purity is a sufficient stronger branch, not an entrance requirement.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The tangent theorem reconstructs the unique Hamiltonian \(H\).  Noisy Klein
refocusing and the branch estimates give an actual compiled channel whose
canonical Hamiltonian projection converges to the direct or bracket matter
target.  Apply the existing relation/provenance Pythagoras and
\Cref{thm:SMST-relative-Howe-certificate}; the typed residue and support-polar
conclusions then follow from
\Cref{prop:SM-typed-transition-audit,thm:SMST-support-polar-commutant,thm:SMST-quiver-commutant}.
\end{proof}


\begin{theorem}[Canonical occurrence Choi source]
\label{thm:SM-occurrence-Choi-source}
Let $\Phi_{\rm occ}=\Phi_{L\leftarrow R}+\Phi_{R\leftarrow L}$ and
$J_{\rm occ}=J(\Phi_{\rm occ})$.  Then
\[
 \boxed{J_{\rm occ}\succeq0,
 \qquad \mathcal E_{\rm occ}^{\min}=\supp J_{\rm occ},
 \qquad \Gamma_{\rm occ}=J_{\rm occ}^{1/2}}
\]
is the canonical source-minimal occurrence factor.  Every other minimal factor
is related by a unique source-fixing unitary.  If
$F_0,\ldots,F_{15}$ is any Hermitian Hilbert--Schmidt orthonormal basis of
$M_4(\C)$, then
\[
 \boxed{J_{\rm occ}=\sum_{\alpha=0}^{15}
 F_\alpha^{\mathsf T}\otimes\Phi_{\rm occ}(F_\alpha),}
\]
so sixteen differentiated Hermitian outputs reconstruct the complete untyped
colour occurrence.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Complete positivity gives Choi positivity.  The positive square root is a
minimal Gram factor on the Choi support, and uniqueness is ordinary minimal
Gram uniqueness.  The reconstruction formula is the Choi identity in an
orthonormal operator basis.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Edge-resolved CP occurrence and endpoint-source closure]
\label{thm:SM-occurrence-endpoint-closure}
Fix one determinant-sign and one current-type branch of the locked oriented
edge packet.  Suppose the actual cross-support occurrence map has protected
ordered-edge branches
\[
 \Phi_{r}^{\rm occ}=\sum_{i\ne j}\Phi_{ij,r},
 \qquad J_{ij,r}:=J(\Phi_{ij,r})\succeq0,
\]
whose sum is exhaustive and whose Choi operators obey exact $S_4$ covariance.
Then every ordered-edge branch has the same Choi mass
\[
 \boxed{
 m_r:=\Tr J_{ij,r}
 =\frac1{12}\Tr J(\Phi_r^{\rm occ}).}
\]
Moreover
\[
 \boxed{
 m_r>0
 \iff \Phi_r^{\rm occ}\ne0
 \iff J_{ij,r}\ne0\quad\text{for every }i\ne j.}
\]

Let $Q_r$ and
$T_r^{\rm chr}=Q_r\partial^*$ be the edge and endpoint sources of
\Cref{thm:SMST-record-native-generations}, so
\[
 Q_r^*Q_r=\alpha_rP_{\rm cut}+\beta_rP_{\rm cyc},
 \qquad
 (T_r^{\rm chr})^*T_r^{\rm chr}=4\alpha_rI_{W_0}.
\]
For $m_r>0$ define the canonical positive CP-modulus endpoint export
\[
 \boxed{
 T_r^{\rm occ}:=\sqrt{\frac{m_r}{\alpha_r}}\,T_r^{\rm chr}.}
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{
 (T_r^{\rm occ})^*T_r^{\rm occ}=4m_rI_{W_0},
 \qquad
 (T_r^{\rm chr})^*T_r^{\rm occ}
 =4\sqrt{\alpha_rm_r}\,I_{W_0},}
\]
and its endpoint Schur residual vanishes identically:
\[
 \boxed{
 (T_r^{\rm occ})^*T_r^{\rm occ}
 -(T_r^{\rm occ})^*T_r^{\rm chr}
 \bigl((T_r^{\rm chr})^*T_r^{\rm chr}\bigr)^\dagger
 (T_r^{\rm chr})^*T_r^{\rm occ}=0.}
\]
Thus every nonzero covariant edge-resolved CP occurrence packet has exactly the
chronological endpoint range.  No coherent Kraus phase or protected-record
eraser is required.  Literal source equality holds exactly when
$m_r=\alpha_r$, and
\[
 \boxed{
 \|T_r^{\rm occ}-T_r^{\rm chr}\|_{\HS}^2
 =12(\sqrt{m_r}-\sqrt{\alpha_r})^2.}
\]
If each $J_{ij,r}$ has rank one, the branch determines one Kraus ray up to
phase; the polar supports, weak CAR relations, and endpoint Gram are phase
independent.  Higher Choi rank is a genuine occurrence multiplicity and is
retained by the support-polar or multiplicity-quiver calculus.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Covariance and transitivity of $S_4$ on ordered pairs make all branch Choi
operators unitarily conjugate, hence give equal trace and rank.  Exhaustion
then gives the trace formula.  A positive operator has zero trace exactly when
it is zero, proving the occurrence equivalences.

The endpoint identities follow by substituting
$T_r^{\rm occ}=\sqrt{m_r/\alpha_r}\,T_r^{\rm chr}$.  With
$A=4\alpha_rI$, $C=4\sqrt{\alpha_rm_r}I$, and $D=4m_rI$, the Schur complement
is $D-C^*A^{-1}C=0$.  The norm formula follows from
$\Tr((T_r^{\rm chr})^*T_r^{\rm chr})=12\alpha_r$.  Rank-one Choi
factorization is unique up to phase, while the positive supports and all Gram
relations are phase invariant.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Unsplit-generator audit of typed residue support]
\label{prop:SM-typed-transition-audit}
Let $G_F=G_F^*$ be the calibrated unsplit full-cell generator and let
$(P_a)_a$ be orthogonal protected type projections.  Put
\[
 B_{ba}=P_bG_FP_a,
 \qquad
 U_s=e^{-isG_F},
\]
and define the finite-time type subchannel
\[
 \Psi_{b\leftarrow a,s,*}(X)
 :=P_bU_sP_aXP_aU_s^*P_b
 \qquad(a\ne b).
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{
 \frac12\frac{\dd^2}{\dd s^2}\Big|_{s=0}
 \Psi_{b\leftarrow a,s,*}(X)
 =B_{ba}XB_{ba}^*.}
\]
Consequently
\[
 \boxed{
 w_{ab}:=\|P_bG_FP_a\|_{\HS}^2
 =\Tr J\!\left(\frac12\Psi_{b\leftarrow a}^{\prime\prime}(0)\right).}
\]
For the normalized type-$a$ source $\rho_a=P_a/d_a$,
\[
 \boxed{
 \frac{\dd^2}{\dd s^2}\Big|_{s=0}
 \Tr\Psi_{b\leftarrow a,s,*}(\rho_a)
 =\frac{2}{d_a}w_{ab}.}
\]
Moreover, for a protected type potential
$D(x)=\sum_ax_aP_a$,
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathscr Q_{\rm type}(x)
 :=\frac12\|[G_F,D(x)]\|_{\HS}^2
 =\sum_{a<b}w_{ab}|x_a-x_b|^2.}
\]
On the five one-generation modules
$Q\oplus u\oplus d\oplus L\oplus e$, if the only allowed incidence supports
are $Q\leftrightarrow u$, $Q\leftrightarrow d$, and
$L\leftrightarrow e$, put
\[
 a=w_{Qu},\qquad b=w_{Qd},\qquad c=w_{Le}.
\]
The Hessian of $\mathscr Q_{\rm type}$ has reduced determinants
\[
 \boxed{
 \det\mathsf H_q^{\rm red}=4ab,
 \qquad
 \det\mathsf H_\ell^{\rm red}=2c.}
\]
Thus $a+b+c>0$ is a nonzero typed matter route, while $a,b,c>0$ is the
strictly stronger statement that the complete displayed one-generation
incidence graph is nonzero.  Its type-potential kernel is then exactly the
quark/lepton constant subspace; when the endpoint type algebras are the full
matrix blocks, this is the residual central commutant.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Since $P_bP_a=0$,
$P_bU_sP_a=-isB_{ba}+O(s^2)$ in operator norm.  Multiplying the two expansions
gives
$\Psi_{b\leftarrow a,s,*}(X)=s^2B_{ba}XB_{ba}^*+O(s^3)$, proving the CP
second derivative.  The Choi trace of a one-Kraus map $X\mapsto BXB^*$ is
$\Tr(B^*B)$, and evaluation on $P_a/d_a$ gives the probability curvature.

The $(a,b)$ block of $[G_F,D(x)]$ is
$(x_b-x_a)P_aG_FP_b$.  Summing the Hilbert--Schmidt norms of both orientations
and dividing by two gives the graph form.  Its Hessian is twice the weighted
graph Laplacian.  Deleting the $Q$ row and column from the quark star leaves
$\diag(2a,2b)$, while deleting the $L$ row and column from the lepton edge
leaves $(2c)$, proving the determinant formulas and the final distinction.
\end{proof}



% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
\subsubsection{Positive occurrence packets, orbit exhaustion, and pulse-native Howe rigidity}
\label{sec:SM-positive-packet-orbit}
% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

The type-transition curvatures above determine positive source packets rather
than arbitrarily phased seed vectors.  This makes source-native odd-sector
exhaustion a finite isotypic rank problem.

\begin{theorem}[Positive-packet compact-orbit decomposition]
\label{thm:SM-positive-packet-orbit}
Let a compact group \(K\) act unitarily on
\[
 \mathscr D
 \cong\bigoplus_\lambda V_\lambda\otimes M_\lambda,
\]
where the \(V_\lambda\) are pairwise inequivalent irreducibles and
\(d_\lambda=\dim V_\lambda\).  For a positive source packet \(J\succeq0\), put
\[
 \mathcal F_J
 =\int_K\rho(g)J\rho(g)^*\,\dd g,
\]
\[
 \boxed{
 B_\lambda(J)
 =\Tr_{V_\lambda}(P_\lambda JP_\lambda)\succeq0.}
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal F_J
 =\bigoplus_\lambda
 \frac1{d_\lambda}I_{V_\lambda}\otimes B_\lambda(J),}
\]
and
\[
 \boxed{
 \Ran\mathcal F_J
 =\Span\{\rho(g)\Ran J:g\in K\}
 =\bigoplus_\lambda
 V_\lambda\otimes\Ran B_\lambda(J).}
\]
Consequently the controlled packet exhausts \(\mathscr D\) if and only if
\[
 \boxed{B_\lambda(J)\succ0\quad\text{for every }\lambda.}
\]
On that branch its exact frame floor is
\[
 \boxed{
 c_J=\min_\lambda
 \frac{\lambda_{\min}(B_\lambda(J))}{d_\lambda}>0.}
\]
If one \(B_\lambda(J)\) is singular, every nonzero vector in its kernel gives
an explicit admissible multiplicity direction missed by the complete physical
control orbit.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The Haar average commutes with \(\rho(K)\).  Schur's lemma gives
\(P_\lambda\mathcal F_JP_\lambda=I_{V_\lambda}\otimes C_\lambda\).
Partial trace over \(V_\lambda\) is invariant under the group action, so
\(d_\lambda C_\lambda=B_\lambda(J)\).  For any \(x\),
\[
 \langle x,\mathcal F_Jx\rangle
 =\int_K\|J^{1/2}\rho(g)^*x\|^2\,\dd g.
\]
This vanishes exactly when \(x\) is orthogonal to every controlled source
range, proving the range formula and the eigenvalue criterion.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Finite phase-free orbit audit]
\label{cor:SM-finite-positive-packet-orbit}
The orbit frame of \Cref{thm:SM-positive-packet-orbit} admits an exact finite
positive quadrature
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal F_J
 =\sum_{\ell=1}^{L}
 w_\ell\rho(g_\ell)J\rho(g_\ell)^*,
 \qquad
 L\le(\dim_\C\mathscr D)^2+1.}
\]
Thus orbit exhaustion is a finite physical control experiment and requires no
choice of Kraus representative.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The Haar average belongs to the convex hull of the compact orbit of \(J\) in
the real vector space of Hermitian operators on \(\mathscr D\), whose
dimension is at most \((\dim_\C\mathscr D)^2\).  Caratheodory's theorem gives
the finite quadrature.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Explicit tetrahedral odd pulse frame]
\label{thm:SM-tetrahedral-two-pulse-frame}
Let
\[
 W_0=\{x\in\R^4:\one^{\mathsf T}x=0\}
\]
carry the standard representation \(\rho_0\) of \(S_4\), and put
\[
 T=\frac14
 \begin{pmatrix}
  2&0&-1&-1\\
  0&-2&1&1\\
  -1&1&0&0\\
  -1&1&0&0
 \end{pmatrix}\Bigg|_{W_0}.
\]
Let \(F_0=\R^3\) have oriented basis \((e_0,e_1,e_2)\), grading
\(Z=\diag(1,1,-1)\), and skew generators
\[
 L_{02}=e_2e_0^*-e_0e_2^*,
 \qquad
 L_{12}=e_2e_1^*-e_1e_2^*.
\]
Consider the real skew operators on \(W_0\otimes F_0\) which commute with
\(\rho_0((34))\otimes I\), are odd under
\(\rho_0((12))\otimes I\), satisfy the cyclic relation
\[
 A+(R_0\otimes I)A(R_0^{-1}\otimes I)
 +(R_0^2\otimes I)A(R_0^{-2}\otimes I)=0,
 \qquad R_0=\rho_0((123)^{-1}),
\]
and are odd under \(I\otimes Z\).  Their complete relation space is
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathscr R_{\rm tet}^{\rm odd}
 =T\otimes\Span_{\R}\{L_{02},L_{12}\}.}
\]
In particular it is two dimensional.  Let \(R_\theta\) rotate the positive
score plane \(\Span\{e_0,e_1\}\) and fix \(e_2\).  The two predetermined
conjugates
\[
 A_0=T\otimes L_{12},
 \qquad
 A_{\pi/2}=(I\otimes R_{\pi/2})A_0(I\otimes R_{\pi/2})^*
 =-T\otimes L_{02}
\]
form an exact orthogonal frame:
\[
 \boxed{
 \langle A_0,A_{\pi/2}\rangle_{\HS}=0,
 \qquad
 \|A_0\|_{\HS}^2=\|A_{\pi/2}\|_{\HS}^2=2.}
\]
Hence two fixed protected pulse settings exhaust the entire real tetrahedral
odd relation sector with frame floor \(2\).  On the complex Hermitian branch,
the two real and two imaginary quadratures of the same two matrix entries form
an orthogonal four-real-dimensional frame.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
There is an orthogonal Hilbert--Schmidt decomposition
\[
 \mathfrak{so}(W_0\otimes F_0)
 =\bigl(\operatorname{Sym}(W_0)\otimes\mathfrak{so}(F_0)\bigr)
 \oplus
 \bigl(\mathfrak{so}(W_0)\otimes\operatorname{Sym}(F_0)\bigr).
\]
The three tetrahedral relations act only on the \(W_0\)-factor.  Extending
operators by zero on \(\R\one\), direct solution of the commutation and
oddness equations leaves one symmetric spatial candidate, the displayed
matrix \(4T\), and one skew candidate.  Substitution into the cyclic relation
keeps \(T\) and annihilates the skew candidate.  Thus the full relation space
is \(T\otimes\mathfrak{so}(F_0)\).  Grading oddness retains exactly the two
skew matrices joining the negative line \(\R e_2\) to the positive plane.
The rotation identity
\[
 R_\theta L_{12}R_\theta^*
 =\cos\theta\,L_{12}-\sin\theta\,L_{02}
\]
gives the second pulse.  The two elementary skew matrices have disjoint
Hilbert--Schmidt coefficients and squared norm \(2\), while
\(\|T\|_{\HS}=1\), proving the frame identities.  The complex statement adds
the independent Hermitian and skew-Hermitian quadratures of the same two
entries.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Robust tetrahedral orbit exhaustion]
\label{cor:SM-tetrahedral-frame-robustness}
If the measured two-column synthesis \(\widetilde S\) differs in operator norm
from the exact real synthesis \(S\) by at most \(\varepsilon<\sqrt2\), then
\[
 \boxed{
 \widetilde S\widetilde S^*
 \succeq(\sqrt2-\varepsilon)^2
 I_{\mathscr R_{\rm tet}^{\rm odd}}.}
\]
Thus a positive physical frame margin, rather than exact pulse equality, is
sufficient for complete tetrahedral odd exhaustion.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
For every \(y\) in the relation space,
\(
 \|\widetilde S^*y\|
 \ge\|S^*y\|-\|(\widetilde S-S)^*y\|
 \ge(\sqrt2-\varepsilon)\|y\|
\).
Squaring gives the result.
\end{proof}

Let the admissible finite-Dirac odd relation space decompose orthogonally into
protected typed and reality sectors
\[
 \mathfrak D_F=\bigoplus_{\eta}\mathfrak D_\eta,
\]
and let \(J_\eta^{\rm occ}\) be the direct occurrence Choi packet obtained from
the shrinking type transition or from the canonical Hamiltonian projection of
\Cref{thm:SMST-compiled-channel-generator}.

\begin{theorem}[Edgewise positive-packet exhaustion of the odd relation space]
\label{thm:SM-edgewise-positive-packet-exhaustion}
Assume the complete odd generator is relation compatible.  For each
\(\eta\), decompose
\[
 \mathfrak D_\eta
 \cong\bigoplus_\lambda
 V_{\eta,\lambda}\otimes M_{\eta,\lambda}
\]
under the actual protected control group and put
\[
 \boxed{
 B_{\eta,\lambda}^{\rm occ}
 =\Tr_{V_{\eta,\lambda}}
 \bigl(P_{\eta,\lambda}
 J_\eta^{\rm occ}
 P_{\eta,\lambda}\bigr).}
\]
If
\[
 \boxed{
 B_{\eta,\lambda}^{\rm occ}\succ0
 \quad\text{for every }\eta,\lambda,}
\]
then the controlled occurrence packets exhaust \(\mathfrak D_F\).  Hence the
selected-phase projection equals the complete admissible odd projection and
the admissible-extra-odd residual vanishes.  If a nonzero residue slot is
claimed, the additional necessary and sufficient occurrence condition is
\[
 \boxed{\Tr J_\eta^{\rm occ}>0.}
\]
A zero mass is an absent direct slot; a null multiplicity vector is a missing
admissible copy.  Neither may be repaired by inserting a residue after the
audit.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Apply \Cref{thm:SM-positive-packet-orbit} on each orthogonal protected sector.
Positive multiplicity matrices make the controlled span equal to
\(\mathfrak D_\eta\); their direct sum equals \(\mathfrak D_F\).  Relation
compatibility places the complete odd generator inside this space, so no
orthogonal admissible odd component remains.  The scalar statement follows
from positivity of the occurrence packet.
\end{proof}

The same finite pulse can test the numerical commutant without first choosing a
logarithm.  Let \(V_t=e^{-itG}\) on the saturated carrier and let
\(\mathscr X_{\mathcal M}\) be the Hilbert--Schmidt complement of a proposed
protected multiplicity algebra.  Put
\[
 \mathcal A_tX=t^{-1}[V_t,X],
 \qquad
 \mathcal A_0X=-i[G,X],
\]
\[
 \mathbb G_t^{\rm pHowe}=\mathcal A_t^*\mathcal A_t,
 \qquad
 \mathbb G_0^{\rm Howe}=\mathcal A_0^*\mathcal A_0.
\]

\begin{theorem}[Quantitative pulse-to-Howe comparison]
\label{thm:SM-pulse-Howe-comparison}
Let \(M=\|G\|_{\op}\).  Then
\[
 \boxed{\|\mathcal A_t-\mathcal A_0\|_{\op}\le|t|M^2,}
\]
and
\[
 \boxed{
 \|\mathbb G_t^{\rm pHowe}-\mathbb G_0^{\rm Howe}\|_{\op}
 \le(4M+|t|M^2)|t|M^2.}
\]
Therefore, if the measured finite-pulse gap \(\gamma_t\) satisfies
\[
 \boxed{
 \gamma_t>(4M+|t|M^2)|t|M^2,}
\]
the generator relative Howe gap is positive and obeys
\[
 \boxed{
 \gamma_0\ge
 \gamma_t-(4M+|t|M^2)|t|M^2>0.}
\]
On a spectral window
\(\spec(tG)\subset(-\pi,\pi)\), the pulse and generator commutants coincide
exactly.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Write
\(V_t=I-itG+R_t\), with
\(\|R_t\|_{\op}\le t^2M^2/2\).  Then
\[
 (\mathcal A_t-\mathcal A_0)X=t^{-1}[R_t,X],
\]
and the Hilbert--Schmidt ideal inequality proves the first estimate.  Since
\(\|\mathcal A_0\|\le2M\) and
\(\|\mathcal A_t\|\le2M+|t|M^2\), the identity
\(A^*A-B^*B=A^*(A-B)+(A^*-B^*)B\) gives the Gram bound.
Weyl's inequality gives the gap estimate.  On the stated spectral window,
\(G=(i/t)\operatorname{Log}V_t\), so \(C^*(G)=C^*(V_t)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[Orbit exhaustion and Howe rigidity are distinct]
\label{fire:SM-orbit-versus-Howe}
Positive orbit matrices prove that the prescribed physical occurrence packet
spans the complete admissible odd tangent.  A positive relative Howe Gram
proves that the numerical residue operator has exactly the proposed
flavour/generation commutant.  Either may hold without the other, so the two
tests remain sequential.
\end{firewall}


\begin{corollary}[The displayed release is the exact zero-occurrence branch]
\label{cor:SM-literal-zero-occurrence}
For the displayed six-state grading-preserving source,
$J_{\rm occ}=0$.  Relative to the independently reconstructed five-channel
word covariance of total trace $65/32$, its squared Bures discrepancy is
\[
 \boxed{d_{\rm B}^2(0,\mathcal K_{\rm word})=65/32.}
\]
No Kraus rotation, record refinement, scalar acceptance tilt, or functional
calculus inside the old release algebra changes this value.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
\Cref{thm:SM-six-state-no-matter} makes every support-changing jump block zero,
so the generator extraction vanishes.  The Bures distance from zero to a
positive operator is its trace.  All listed operations preserve the zero
cross-support map.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Typed singlet--adjoint Radon--Nikodym reduction]
\label{thm:SM-typed-occurrence-RN}
Let $G_{\rm typ}\succ0$ be an independently exported eight-dimensional typed
source metric, with exact record algebra
\[
 \mathfrak A_{\rm typ}
 \cong\C_u\oplus\C_d\oplus\C_\tau\oplus\C_\mu\oplus\C_e
 \oplus M_2(\C)_{\nu D}\oplus\C_M.
\]
Every positive $SU(4)$-covariant typed occurrence covariance has the unique
form
\[
 \boxed{\mathbb Q_{\rm typ}
 =P_{\mathbf1}\otimes G_\Phi
 +\frac1{15}P_{\mathbf{15}}\otimes G_\Omega,}
\]
where $G_\Phi,G_\Omega\succeq0$.  If
$G_{\rm typ}=G_\Phi+G_\Omega$, there is a unique effect
\[
 \boxed{0\preceq K_{\rm rep}\preceq I,
 \quad G_\Phi=G_{\rm typ}^{1/2}K_{\rm rep}G_{\rm typ}^{1/2},
 \quad G_\Omega=G_{\rm typ}^{1/2}(I-K_{\rm rep})G_{\rm typ}^{1/2}.}
\]
It is nondemolition for the typed record exactly when
$K_{\rm rep}\in\mathfrak A_{\rm typ}'$.  In that case
\[
 K_{\rm rep}=k_uP_u+k_dP_d+k_\tau P_\tau+k_\mu P_\mu+k_eP_e
 +K_{\nu D}+k_MP_M,
\]
with six scalars in $[0,1]$ and one $2\times2$ effect.  Hence ten real
conditional probes are generically necessary and sufficient; nine suffice if
the singlet conductance $\Tr(G_{\rm typ}K_{\rm rep})$ is independently
exported from the same primitive source.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Conjugation on $M_4(\C)$ is the multiplicity-free representation
$\mathbf1\oplus\mathbf{15}$, so Schur's lemma gives the first block form and
its uniqueness.  The positive-operator Radon--Nikodym theorem applied to
$0\preceq G_\Phi\preceq G_{\rm typ}$ gives the effect formula.  A binary
Naimark measurement preserves the typed record precisely when its effect
commutes with that record algebra.  The commutant is scalar on the six
one-dimensional atoms and arbitrary Hermitian on the neutral two-dimensional
atom, giving $6+4=10$ real parameters.  One independently known affine trace
removes one parameter.
\end{proof}

\begin{countertheorem}[Typed and colour marginals do not select occurrence]
\label{cth:SM-occurrence-marginal-nonselection}
Fix $G_{\rm typ}$ and one interior colour conductance
$0<c<\Tr G_{\rm typ}$.  The feasible effects
\[
 \{K\in\mathfrak A_{\rm typ}':0\preceq K\preceq I,
 \ \Tr(G_{\rm typ}K)=c\}
\]
form a compact spectrahedron of affine dimension nine.  Consequently the
complete typed marginal and the complete untyped colour marginal do not
select the representation--type correlation, the fine source-minimal factor,
or its environment rank.
\end{countertheorem}

\begin{proof}
The real commutant has dimension ten.  The conductance is one nonzero affine
functional, and the scalar interior effect
$(c/\Tr G_{\rm typ})I$ lies in the relative interior, so the affine dimension
is nine.  Distinct traceless record-compatible perturbations preserve the
marginal sum and conductance while changing the joint covariance.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Occurrence environment rank]
\label{cor:SM-occurrence-environment-rank}
For faithful $G_{\rm typ}$, the source-minimal colour--typed environment rank is
\[
 \boxed{r_{\rm env}=\rank K_{\rm rep}
 +15\rank(I-K_{\rm rep}).}
\]
It is therefore a physical output of the occurrence effect rather than a
predetermined generation count or environment size.
\end{corollary}

% =============================================================================
\subsubsection{Bare-universal boundary and the protected score-square completion}
\label{sec:SM-proper-matter-entrance}
% =============================================================================

The operationally complete Grand Tensor already retains every pre-central type,
left/right, branch, revision, source/target, chronology, routing, and outcome
label that the microscopic protocol generated and left readable.  This record
protection is essential: a future quotient may minimize the predictive core
inside each record sector, but it may not identify two protected record values.
It is equally important that the record contains only operational facts.  A
left/right label can record which support was occupied; it cannot create a
coefficient carrying one support into the other.

\begin{countertheorem}[Bare operational completeness does not force matter]
\label{cth:SM-bare-universal-no-go}
There is no implication
\[
 \boldsymbol{\mathbb T}^{\min,op}_{\Grand,X}
 \Longrightarrow
 \text{nonzero grading-changing matter occurrence}
\]
for every bare finite intervention--renewal datum.  More strongly, one and the
same grading-even operational tensor embeds conservatively into both a
zero-occurrence extension and a nonzero-occurrence extension.
\end{countertheorem}

\begin{proof}
Let the old operational process act on a finite carrier \(H_0\).  Adjoin a
resolved grading factor
\[
 H_{\rm gr}=\C|L\rangle\oplus\C|R\rangle,
 \qquad P_L=|L\rangle\langle L|,
 \qquad P_R=|R\rangle\langle R|,
\]
and let every old core letter act as its old reduced map tensored with the
identity on \(H_{\rm gr}\).  Add only the two diagonal grading Reads and their
protected labels.  Every represented coefficient then commutes with
\(Z_{\rm gr}:=P_L-P_R\), so the incidence firewall
\Cref{thm:SM-incidence-firewall} makes every opposite-grading coefficient zero.

In a second extension adjoin the physical routing unitary
\[
 X_{\rm gr}=|L\rangle\langle R|+|R\rangle\langle L|.
\]
Every old intervention probability and every old record-forgetting word map is
unchanged under the natural embedding and record discard, while
\(P_LX_{\rm gr}P_R=|L\rangle\langle R|\ne0\).  Hence the old operational tensor
cannot distinguish the two extensions and cannot force the positive one.
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[Exact role of the constructive fallback]
\label{fire:SM-completion-not-bare}
The source-native branch of
\Cref{thm:SMST-store-native-route,thm:SMST-phase-grading-route} must be tested
first.  When the protected grading sign is available and its odd cross-support
margin is nonzero, no score-square routing is added during loading; the complete
Store generator may simultaneously contain grading-even dynamics.  The
canonical completion below is retained only as a minimal, parameter-free
physical extension when the required odd route is absent or when an
independently controlled completion is the intended physical model.  It is not a theorem that the unchanged six-state source, or
every bare renewal source, executes that extension.  Once the fallback packet
is physically admitted, its occurrence, coefficient, Choi factor, and record
map are theorems.
\end{firewall}

Put
\[
 F_{\rm br}=|L\rangle\langle R|,
 \qquad
 X_{\rm gr}=F_{\rm br}+F_{\rm br}^*,
 \qquad
 Y_{\rm gr}=i(F_{\rm br}-F_{\rm br}^*),
 \qquad
 Z_{\rm gr}=P_L-P_R.
\]
These operators form a Pauli triple, up to the harmless sign convention for
\(Y_{\rm gr}\).

\begin{definition}[Protected score-square matter-completion packet]
\label{def:SM-canonical-completion}
A \emph{protected score-square matter-completion packet} consists of:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(B\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item the resolved grading support \(H_{\rm gr}\) retained before the central
      expectation \(A\mapsto P_LAP_L+P_RAP_R\);
\item one physically admitted score-to-grading routing implementing
      \(X_{\rm gr}\), together with the grading phase rotation which supplies
      \(Y_{\rm gr}\);
\item two fresh independent fair score bits \(a,b\in\{0,1\}\), with resolved
      branch unitaries
      \[
       U_{00}=I,\qquad U_{01}=I,\qquad
       U_{10}=X_{\rm gr},\qquad U_{11}=Y_{\rm gr};
      \]
\item deterministic writers for the new score-square, source/target, and
      routing labels into the protected operational record whenever a later
      admitted operation may read them;
\item if those new score labels are later discarded, an explicit one-way
      transient-record sink in the sense of
      \Cref{def:fresh-record-sink,thm:record-sink-nullity}.
\end{enumerate}
The fine resolved branch maps are
\[
 \mathcal J_{ab,*}(\rho)=\frac14U_{ab}\rho U_{ab}^*.
\]
The record-forgetting coarse channel is denoted \(\Psi_{\rm sb}\).
\end{definition}

\begin{proposition}[One new routing relation is necessary and sufficient]
\label{prop:SM-one-routing}
A coefficient on \(H_{\rm gr}\) crosses the grading exactly when it fails to
commute with \(Z_{\rm gr}\).  Consequently an extension contained in
\(\{Z_{\rm gr}\}'\) cannot create matter.  Conversely, adjoining one physical
routing relation implementing \(X_{\rm gr}\) is sufficient; phase conjugation
supplies \(Y_{\rm gr}\), and
\[
 C^*(X_{\rm gr},Y_{\rm gr},Z_{\rm gr})=M_2(\C).
\]
Thus the packet of \Cref{def:SM-canonical-completion} is minimal at the level
of support-changing routing.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Relative to \(P_L\oplus P_R\), an operator commutes with \(Z_{\rm gr}\) exactly
when it is block diagonal.  Hence a nonzero cross block requires a
noncommuting coefficient.  The displayed \(X_{\rm gr}\) has cross block
\(F_{\rm br}\ne0\).  Conjugation by
\(\exp(-i\pi Z_{\rm gr}/4)\) rotates \(X_{\rm gr}\) to \(Y_{\rm gr}\) up to
sign, and the three Pauli axes generate the full two-by-two matrix algebra.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Compatibility with the operationally complete Grand Tensor]
\label{thm:SM-completion-conservative}
The protected score-square completion is conservative over the old operational
process in the following exact sense.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2.8em]
\item Discarding the new grading and score-square records recovers every old
      intervention probability and old record-forgetting word map.
\item The old process-history algebra embeds by a unital \(*\)-monomorphism;
      all old word relations, multiplication, involution, and future-null
      classes are preserved.
\item If the physical future metric on the extension restricts isometrically
      to the old source, all old physical word Grams are identical.
\item For the intrinsic normalized regular trace, the pullback Gram is the
      central-density transport of \Cref{thm:cutoff-compatibility}; it need not
      equal the old normalized regular Gram unless that density is the identity.
\item Every protected old record and every newly protected score-square record
      survives the contextual quotient.  Only a separately certified transient
      score record may be forgotten.
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The completed branch Kraus operators are tensor products of deterministic
record writers with \(2^{-1}U_{ab}\).  Their effects sum to the identity, and
record discard removes the writers.  Induction on word length therefore gives
item~\textup{(i)} by the operational-record completion theorem.  The natural
embedding preserves products and adjoints, and the old Reads still separate
old non-null classes, proving item~\textup{(ii)}.  Item~\textup{(iii)} is the
isometric physical-metric clause of \Cref{thm:cutoff-compatibility}.  The
regular trace of a larger finite algebra restricts to a faithful trace on the
embedded old algebra, hence differs from its normalized regular trace by the
unique positive central density of the same theorem, proving
item~\textup{(iv)}.  Item~\textup{(v)} is
\Cref{thm:record-survival,thm:record-sink-nullity}.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Canonical protected score-square mixer]
\label{thm:SM-score-bus}
The record-forgetting channel of \Cref{def:SM-canonical-completion} is
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \Psi_{{\rm sb},*}(\rho)
 =\frac12\rho
  +\frac14X_{\rm gr}\rho X_{\rm gr}
  +\frac14Y_{\rm gr}\rho Y_{\rm gr}.}
 \label{eq:SM-score-bus}
\end{equation}
It is completely positive, trace preserving, unital, tracially self-adjoint,
phase covariant, and deck covariant.  On the Pauli basis,
\[
 \Psi_{\rm sb}(I)=I,
 \qquad
 \Psi_{\rm sb}(X_{\rm gr})=\frac12X_{\rm gr},
 \qquad
 \Psi_{\rm sb}(Y_{\rm gr})=\frac12Y_{\rm gr},
 \qquad
 \Psi_{\rm sb}(Z_{\rm gr})=0.
\]
Its fixed algebra is \(\C I\), and the least positive eigenvalue of
\(I-\Psi_{\rm sb}\) on the traceless grading space is \(1/2\).  Each fine
score-square branch has the input-independent probability \(1/4\).
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The four resolved Kraus operators are \(U_{ab}/2\); their effects sum to
\(I\), proving complete positivity and trace preservation, while the same
formula in the Heisenberg picture proves unitality.  The unitary list is closed
under adjoints, so the map is Hilbert--Schmidt self-adjoint.  Equal weights on
\(X_{\rm gr}\) and \(Y_{\rm gr}\) give covariance under rotations about
\(Z_{\rm gr}\), and conjugation by \(X_{\rm gr}\) preserves the channel.
The Pauli anticommutation relations give the four displayed eigenvectors and
eigenvalues.  The fixed and gap statements follow, and
\((U_{ab}/2)^*(U_{ab}/2)=I/4\) gives the branch probabilities.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Exact cross-support occurrence and Kossakowski operator]
\label{thm:SM-score-cross}
For \(T\in B(P_RH_{\rm gr})\) and \(S\in B(P_LH_{\rm gr})\),
\begin{align}
 \boxed{
 \mathcal R_{L\leftarrow R}^{\rm sb}(T)
 =P_L\Psi_{{\rm sb},*}(P_RTP_R)P_L
 =\frac12F_{\rm br}TF_{\rm br}^*,}
 \label{eq:SM-score-cross-forward}\\
 \boxed{
 \mathcal R_{R\leftarrow L}^{\rm sb}(S)
 =\frac12F_{\rm br}^*SF_{\rm br}.}
 \label{eq:SM-score-cross-reverse}
\end{align}
Consequently
\[
 A_{L\leftarrow R}^{\rm sb}=\frac12P_L,
 \qquad
 A_{R\leftarrow L}^{\rm sb}=\frac12P_R.
\]
If \(e_{\rm br}\) is the unit Hilbert--Schmidt bridge vector, put
\(P_{\rm br}=|e_{\rm br}\rangle\langle e_{\rm br}|\).  The intrinsic
link-mode Kossakowski operator and minimal occurrence row are
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathsf K_{\rm sb}
 =\frac12|e_{\rm br}\rangle\langle e_{\rm br}|,
 \qquad
 B_{\rm br}=\frac1{\sqrt2}F_{\rm br}.}
 \label{eq:SM-score-K}
\end{equation}
Thus no positive occurrence coefficient remains to be chosen.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The two identity branches vanish under opposite-support compression.
Moreover
\(P_LX_{\rm gr}P_R=F_{\rm br}\) and
\(P_LY_{\rm gr}P_R=iF_{\rm br}\).  The two positive contributions are equal
and each has weight \(1/4\), proving
\eqref{eq:SM-score-cross-forward}; the reverse formula follows by adjunction.
The one-column Kraus factor is \(F_{\rm br}/\sqrt2\), whose coefficient Gram
is \eqref{eq:SM-score-K}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[No independent matter amplitude on a typed route]
\label{cor:SM-route-amplitude}
Let a typed carrier row \(C_e:Q_e\to Y_e\) satisfy
\(C_e^*C_e=\kappa_e I\) with \(\kappa_e>0\).  The completed occurrence row
\[
 K_e=C_e\otimes B_{\rm br}
\]
satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{K_e^*K_e=\frac{\kappa_e}{2}I.}
 \label{eq:SM-route-effect}
\end{equation}
It is nonzero and has the same source rank as \(C_e\).  Hence the common-row
Walsh theorem and the principal matter-module theorem apply without an
additional edgewise matter rate.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Tensor-factor multiplication gives
\(K_e^*K_e=(C_e^*C_e)\otimes(B_{\rm br}^*B_{\rm br})\), and
\(B_{\rm br}^*B_{\rm br}=P_R/2\) on the source support.  Tensoring by a
nonzero rank-one bridge does not change the source rank.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Exact singlet--adjoint colour occurrence]
\label{thm:SM-colour-orbit}
Let \(P_\ell\) be a rank-one projection in \(\C^4\), let
\(P_c=I_4-P_\ell\), and put \(R_{3|1}=P_\ell-P_c=2P_\ell-I_4\).  On the
Hilbert--Schmidt space \(M_4(\C)=\mathbf1\oplus\mathbf{15}\), let
\(\Pi_{\mathbf1}\) and \(\Pi_{\mathbf{15}}\) be the scalar and traceless
projections.  Then normalized Haar averaging gives
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \int_{SU(4)}
 |UR_{3|1}U^*\rangle\langle UR_{3|1}U^*|\,\dd U
 =\Pi_{\mathbf1}+\frac15\Pi_{\mathbf{15}}.}
 \label{eq:SM-colour-covariance}
\end{equation}
After the score-square bridge,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathsf K_{1|15}^{\rm sb}
 =\frac12\Pi_{\mathbf1}+\frac1{10}\Pi_{\mathbf{15}}.}
 \label{eq:SM-colour-score}
\end{equation}
Both irreducible occurrence modules are strictly positive.  A finite exact
positive orbit quadrature exists with at most \(257\) orbit points.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
With \(E_0=I_4/2\), one has
\(\langle E_0,R_{3|1}\rangle_{\rm HS}=-1\).  Thus
\(R_{3|1}=-E_0+R_0\), where \(R_0\) is traceless.  Since
\(R_{3|1}^2=I_4\), its squared Hilbert--Schmidt norm is four and
\(\|R_0\|_{\rm HS}^2=3\).  Haar covariance commutes with conjugation.  The
conjugation representation is the multiplicity-free sum of the scalar line
and the irreducible fifteen-dimensional adjoint module, so Schur's lemma makes
the covariance scalar on each summand.  Its scalar coefficient is one and its
adjoint trace is three, hence the adjoint coefficient is \(3/15=1/5\).
Multiplication by the bridge weight \(1/2\) gives
\eqref{eq:SM-colour-score}.  The Haar average belongs to the convex hull of
rank-one orbit operators in a real affine space of dimension at most \(256\);
Carath\'eodory's theorem gives at most \(257\) points.
\end{proof}
