\subsubsection{Typed record action and common-origin finite-Dirac alternatives}
\label{sec:SM-record-common-origin}
% =============================================================================

Let one typed edge act between
\[
 H_R=V_R\otimes M_R,
 \qquad
 H_L=V_L\otimes M_L,
\]
where the carrier algebra acts on \(V_R,V_L\) and trivially on the
multiplicity spaces.  Assume the carrier-intertwiner space is the line
\(\Hom_{\mathfrak C}(V_R,V_L)=\C D_e\), with \(\|D_e\|_{\rm HS}=1\).
Let \(\mathfrak R_R\subseteq B(M_R)\) and
\(\mathfrak R_L\subseteq B(M_L)\) be the endpoint protected typed-record
algebras reconstructed from the flat loaded tensor.

\begin{theorem}[Canonical typed link bimodule and record representation]
\label{thm:SM-record-bimodule}
Every carrier-equivariant edge has a unique factorization
\[
 Y_e=D_e\otimes F_e,
 \qquad F_e\in\operatorname{HS}(M_R,M_L).
\]
The canonical link-mode Hilbert space is
\(\mathcal E_e=\operatorname{HS}(M_R,M_L)\), and the endpoint record algebra
\[
 \mathfrak R_e=\mathfrak R_L\otimes\mathfrak R_R^{\rm op}
\]
acts by the faithful representation
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \pi_e(a\otimes b^{\rm op})F=aFb.}
 \label{eq:SM-record-representation}
\end{equation}
At flat loaded depth, the carrier line, multiplicity spaces, endpoint record
algebras, and \(\pi_e\) are reconstructed by finite central, commutant, and
intertwiner calculations before an occurrence factor is chosen.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The natural tensor decomposition gives
\[
 \Hom_{\mathfrak C}(V_R\otimes M_R,V_L\otimes M_L)
 \cong
 \Hom_{\mathfrak C}(V_R,V_L)\otimes\Hom(M_R,M_L),
\]
which is \(D_e\otimes\Hom(M_R,M_L)\).  Hilbert--Schmidt norms factor, so this
identification is unitary.  Multiplication in the opposite algebra gives
\((b^{\rm op})(d^{\rm op})=(db)^{\rm op}\); hence
\(F\mapsto aFb\) is multiplicative and its Hilbert--Schmidt adjoint is
\(F\mapsto a^*Fb^*\).  Flat reconstruction gives the action algebra; its
centre, endpoint commutants, and the kernel of the intertwiner equations are
finite linear-algebra outputs, proving the last statement.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[One-matrix protected record map]
\label{thm:SM-record-map}
Let \(\mathsf K_e\succeq0\) be the actual typed Kossakowski operator on
\(\mathcal E_e\).  Then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \Theta_{e,\rm rec}(c)
 =\mathsf K_e^{1/2}\pi_e(c)\mathsf K_e^{1/2},
 \qquad c\in\mathfrak R_e,}
 \label{eq:SM-Theta-record}
\end{equation}
is completely positive and satisfies
\(\Theta_{e,\rm rec}(1)=\mathsf K_e\).  Its unique minimal
record-sufficient Stinespring space is the cyclic hull
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathcal F_e^{\rm rec}
 =\Span\{\pi_e(c)\mathsf K_e^{1/2}x:
          c\in\mathfrak R_e,\ x\in\mathcal E_e\}.}
 \label{eq:SM-record-hull}
\end{equation}
For the score-square bridge,
\[
 \Theta_{e,\rm rec}^{\rm sb}(c)
 =\frac12P_{\rm br}\pi_e(c)P_{\rm br}.
\]
This construction retains, rather than erases, every protected endpoint and
branch record represented on the hull.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Equation \eqref{eq:SM-Theta-record} has Stinespring form
\(V^*\pi_e(c)V\) with \(V=\mathsf K_e^{1/2}\), proving complete positivity
and the unit identity.  The standard minimal Stinespring reduction is the
cyclic span of \(\pi_e(\mathfrak R_e)\Ran V\), which is
\eqref{eq:SM-record-hull}.  Minimal Stinespring uniqueness transports both the
factor and the record representation by one intertwining unitary.  Substituting
\(\mathsf K_{\rm sb}^{1/2}=2^{-1/2}P_{\rm br}\) gives the final formula.
Protected labels remain distinct because their projections belong to
\(\mathfrak R_e\) and survive by \Cref{thm:record-survival}.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Common-Hodge finite-Dirac branch]
\label{thm:SM-common-Hodge-Dirac}
Assume the finite odd residue is the orthogonal compression of the same ambient
Hodge derivation that produces the occurrence.  Let
\(J_F:\mathcal E_{e,\rm occ}\to\mathcal E_{e,\rm res}\) be the induced
unitary, and assume the record-naturality residual
\begin{equation}
 \Delta_{\rm nat}
 :=\sum_j\|J_F\pi_{\rm occ}(c_j)
          -\pi_{\rm res}(c_j)J_F\|_{\rm HS}^2
 \label{eq:SM-record-naturality}
\end{equation}
vanishes for one generating family \((c_j)\) of \(\mathfrak R_e\).  Then
\begin{align}
 \boxed{\mathsf K_{e,\rm res}
 =J_F\mathsf K_{e,\rm occ}J_F^*,}
 \label{eq:SM-Hodge-K}\\
 \boxed{\Theta_{e,\rm res}(c)
 =J_F\Theta_{e,\rm occ}(c)J_F^*.}
 \label{eq:SM-Hodge-Theta}
\end{align}
Thus occurrence and residue have one record-intertwining minimal Stinespring
factor and no independent relative speed or factor-orientation modulus.
If, in addition, the occurrence and residue are represented in one physical
future metric and their common-router or measured two-phase panel is supplied,
the direct record-constrained common-origin residual vanishes.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Orthogonal Hodge descent gives the covariance identity
\eqref{eq:SM-Hodge-K}.  Functional calculus commutes with unitary conjugation,
so
\(\mathsf K_{e,\rm res}^{1/2}
 =J_F\mathsf K_{e,\rm occ}^{1/2}J_F^*\).  Vanishing of
\eqref{eq:SM-record-naturality} gives
\(\pi_{\rm res}(c)=J_F\pi_{\rm occ}(c)J_F^*\) on the generated record
algebra.  Substitution into \eqref{eq:SM-Theta-record} proves
\eqref{eq:SM-Hodge-Theta}.  Minimal Stinespring uniqueness gives the
record-intertwining factor.  A common physical cross Gram then has the form
\(X=G_{\rm occ}U\) for that unitary \(U\); its Schur complement, unitarity
defect, and record commutators all vanish.  The final cross Gram is a physical
metric or fringe datum in the sense of Part~I; it is not inferred from diagonal
CP branches alone.
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[General finite-Dirac fallback]
\label{fire:SM-Dirac-fallback}
The common-Hodge theorem does not assert that every finite Dirac/Yukawa
operator is already present.  Outside the common-origin orthogonal-Hodge
branch, numerical finite-Dirac data still require the independently measured
same-null compatible marked bi-Hankel panel of
\Cref{thm:SM-marked-Dirac}.  Ordinary unmarked transport moments and the
universal grading bridge do not determine the residue matrices.
\end{firewall}

\subsubsection{Autonomous-source comparison and the exact remaining source test}
\label{sec:SM-autonomous-source-test}
% =============================================================================

The score-square packet is a constructive physical completion.  Equality with
the \emph{unchanged} autonomous microscopic Store is a stronger source
statement.  It must be tested at a noninvertible renewal reset: the exact
score-square channel has a zero eigenvalue, whereas every finite-time map
\(e^{t\mathcal L}\) of a bounded finite-dimensional generator is invertible as
a linear map.

Let \(P_{\rm ret}\) be a proposed pre-central return head,
\(Q_{\rm tr}=I-P_{\rm ret}\), and let \(T_\rho\) be the one-step marked
transfer twisted by a finite-dimensional representation \(\rho\) of the
grading normalizer.  Whenever \(1\notin\spec(Q_{\rm tr}T_\rho Q_{\rm tr})\),
define the first-return operator
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathcal F_\rho
 =P_{\rm ret}T_\rho P_{\rm ret}
 +P_{\rm ret}T_\rho Q_{\rm tr}
  (I-Q_{\rm tr}T_\rho Q_{\rm tr})^{-1}
  Q_{\rm tr}T_\rho P_{\rm ret}.}
 \label{eq:SM-first-return}
\end{equation}
Use the trivial, parity-sign, and two-dimensional off-diagonal normalizer
representations, and write the resulting blocks as
\[
 \mathcal F_{\mathbf1}=B,
 \qquad
 \mathcal F_{\rm sgn}=S,
 \qquad
 \mathcal F_{\rm off}
 =\begin{pmatrix}C_0^-&C_2^+\\ C_2^-&C_0^+\end{pmatrix}.
\]

\begin{definition}[Autonomous first-return residual]
\label{def:SM-autonomous-residual}
Define
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \Delta_{\rm FR}
 =\|\mathcal F_{\rm sgn}\|_{\rm HS}^2
 +\left\|
  \mathcal F_{\rm off}
  -\frac12\begin{pmatrix}
    \mathcal F_{\mathbf1}&0\\0&\mathcal F_{\mathbf1}^*
   \end{pmatrix}
  \right\|_{\rm HS}^2.}
 \label{eq:SM-autonomous-residual}
\end{equation}
After \(\Delta_{\rm FR}=0\), let \(\Delta_{\rm rec}\) be the finite
Stinespring intertwining residual comparing the protected autonomous record
representation with the score-square record representation.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Terminating autonomous identification theorem]
\label{thm:SM-autonomous-test}
The three twisted first returns determine the complete coarse autonomous
grading channel.  Moreover,
\[
 \Delta_{\rm FR}=0
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 S=0,\qquad C_0=\frac12B,\qquad C_2=0,
\]
which is equivalent to equality with the coarse score-square channel.  The
unchanged autonomous reset is record-equivalent to the protected score-square
instrument exactly when
\[
 \boxed{\Delta_{\rm FR}+\Delta_{\rm rec}=0.}
\]
In finite dimension the resolvent in \eqref{eq:SM-first-return} is a polynomial
in \(Q_{\rm tr}T_\rho Q_{\rm tr}\) of degree at most
\(\dim(Q_{\rm tr}H)-1\); hence all three first returns and both residuals are
finite loaded Grand-Tensor panels.  For the displayed grading-preserving
six-state source, \(S=B\ne0\), so \(\Delta_{\rm FR}>0\).
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Conjugation by the grading normalizer on
\(\Span\{I,Z_{\rm gr},F_{\rm br},F_{\rm br}^*\}\) decomposes as the direct sum
of the trivial representation, the parity-sign representation, and the
two-dimensional off-diagonal representation.  The corresponding twisted
first-return operators therefore give all matrix blocks of the coarse grading
channel.  Expanding the square in \eqref{eq:SM-autonomous-residual} gives
\[
 \Delta_{\rm FR}
 =\|S\|_{\rm HS}^2
 +2\|C_0-B/2\|_{\rm HS}^2
 +2\|C_2\|_{\rm HS}^2,
\]
so its zero criterion is the displayed moment identity, which is exactly the
score-square normalizer packet.  Once the coarse channels agree, minimal
Stinespring uniqueness reduces fine-instrument equality to one unitary
intertwining the protected record representations; the squared commutator
sum is \(\Delta_{\rm rec}\).  Cayley--Hamilton expresses the inverse of
\(I-A\) as a polynomial in \(A\) whenever \(1\notin\spec A\), proving finite
Grand-Tensor reconstructibility.  A grading-preserving source has no odd
return, hence its signed return equals its unsigned return and the first term
is positive.
\end{proof}

\subsubsection{Flavour-transparent bridge and basis-free finite flavour readouts}
\label{sec:SM-flavour-transparent}
% =============================================================================

The canonical bridge closes matter incidence.  It does not determine flavour.
For a multiplicity-one edge \(Y_e=D_e\otimes F_e\), the residue is recovered
canonically by
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 F_e=\frac1{\|D_e\|_{\rm HS}^2}
 \Tr_{V_R}\bigl[(D_e^*\otimes I)Y_e\bigr].}
 \label{eq:SM-residue-contraction}
\end{equation}

\begin{theorem}[Universal grading-bridge transparency]
\label{thm:SM-bridge-transparent}
Let \(F_e=U_eP_e\) be the polar decomposition and suppose
\(D_e^*D_e=c_ep_e\), \(D_eD_e^*=c_eq_e\).  Then
\begin{align}
 \boxed{Y_e^*Y_e=c_ep_e\otimes P_e^2,}
 \label{eq:SM-edge-right-square}\\
 \boxed{Y_eY_e^*=c_eq_e\otimes U_eP_e^2U_e^*.}
 \label{eq:SM-edge-left-square}
\end{align}
An operator in the internal-carrier commutant has the form
\(\bigoplus_\lambda I_{V_\lambda}\otimes R_\lambda\), and it commutes with
all \(Y_e,Y_e^*\) exactly when
\[
 R_\mu F_e=F_eR_\lambda,
 \qquad
 R_\lambda F_e^*=F_e^*R_\mu.
\]
Hence the generation/flavour algebra, transported positive polar metrics,
relative-cycle holonomies, and all normalized source comparisons are
independent of every nonzero carrier factor, including the score-square
bridge and its scalar rate.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Tensoring the polar decompositions gives the two square identities.  For a
commutant operator,
\[
 XY_e-Y_eX=D_e\otimes(R_\mu F_e-F_eR_\lambda),
\]
and the adjoint equation has the analogous factor \(D_e^*\).  Since
\(D_e\ne0\), the tensor product vanishes exactly when its residue factor does.
For invertible \(F_e\), the two equations are equivalent to
\([R_\lambda,P_e^2]=0\) and
\(R_\mu=U_eR_\lambda U_e^*\).  A common carrier factor with
\(C^*C=cI\) multiplies every marginal and cross Gram by \(c\); generalized
Schur complements also multiply by \(c\), while source whitening cancels it.
Thus ranks, flatness, normalized cross Grams, polar holonomies, and commutants
are bridge independent.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[The \(K_4\) cycle--flavour test is bridge transparent]
\label{cor:SM-K4-transparent}
Tensoring a flavour source with the universal grading bridge leaves every
normalized Krylov moment, saturation rank, transfer-intertwining residual, and
source-whitened \(K_4\) cycle--flavour comparison unchanged.  The bridge can
neither prove three generations nor repair a failed cycle--flavour comparison.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
At every Krylov depth, all source Grams acquire the same positive scalar
factor.  Ranks and flatness are unchanged, Schur residuals acquire that scalar,
and whitening removes it.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Basis-free CKM/PMNS and CP panels]
\label{thm:SM-mixing-invariants}
Let \(A=A^*\) and \(B=B^*\) be two reconstructed Hermitian residue squares on
a common generation space.  On simple spectral branches let \(P_i,Q_j\) be
their rank-one spectral projections and define
\[
 \mathcal P_{AB}(i,j)=\Tr(P_iQ_j),
 \qquad
 \mathcal Q_{AB}(i,j;k,\ell)=\Tr(P_iQ_jP_kQ_\ell).
\]
If \(V_{ij}=\langle u_i,d_j\rangle\) is the relative eigenframe, then
\begin{align*}
 \mathcal P_{AB}(i,j)&=|V_{ij}|^2,\\
 \mathcal Q_{AB}(i,j;k,\ell)
 &=V_{ij}\overline{V_{kj}}V_{k\ell}\overline{V_{i\ell}}.
\end{align*}
On the full-support branch these panels determine \(V\) up to diagonal row and
column rephasings.  In dimension three, with
\(\Delta_\circlearrowright(A)=(a_1-a_2)(a_2-a_3)(a_3-a_1)\),
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathcal J_{AB}
 =\frac{\Im\Tr([A,B]^3)}
 {6\Delta_\circlearrowright(A)\Delta_\circlearrowright(B)}}
 \label{eq:SM-Jarlskog}
\end{equation}
is the rephasing-invariant Jarlskog quartet, with sign fixed by the cyclic
orders.  All these quantities are independent of the universal grading
bridge.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
For rank-one projections,
\(\Tr(P_iQ_j)=|\langle u_i,d_j\rangle|^2\); multiplying four rank-one
projections gives the quartet formula.  Fix row and column phases so the first
row and column are positive.  When all entries are nonzero,
\(\mathcal Q_{AB}(i,1;1,j)\) then determines every remaining complex entry,
proving reconstruction up to rephasing.

In an \(A\)-eigenbasis,
\([A,B]_{ij}=(a_i-a_j)B_{ij}\).  Only cycles through three distinct indices
contribute to the trace of the cube, giving
\[
 \frac1{6i}\Tr([A,B]^3)
 =\Delta_\circlearrowright(A)\Im(B_{12}B_{23}B_{31}).
\]
Expanding \(B=V\diag(b_1,b_2,b_3)V^*\) and using unitarity gives
\[
 \Im(B_{12}B_{23}B_{31})
 =\Delta_\circlearrowright(B)
  \Im(V_{11}V_{22}\overline{V_{12}V_{21}}).
\]
This proves \eqref{eq:SM-Jarlskog}.  Bridge independence is
\Cref{thm:SM-bridge-transparent} and the cancellation of positive scalar
rescalings between the numerator and the two Vandermondes.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Generation commutant and rigidity margin]
\label{thm:SM-generation-Laplacian}
For Hermitian residue squares \(A,B\), define
\[
 \mathscr L_{A,B}(X)=[A,[A,X]]+[B,[B,X]].
\]
Then \(\mathscr L_{A,B}\succeq0\) and
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{\Ker\mathscr L_{A,B}=\{A,B\}'.}
 \label{eq:SM-generation-Laplacian}
\end{equation}
If \(\lambda_{A,B}>0\) is its least positive eigenvalue, then
\[
 \|X-P_{\{A,B\}'}X\|_{\rm HS}^2
 \le\lambda_{A,B}^{-1}
 \bigl(\|[A,X]\|_{\rm HS}^2+\|[B,X]\|_{\rm HS}^2\bigr).
\]
Thus the zero eigenspace reconstructs the exact surviving generation algebra
and the first positive eigenvalue is a quantitative flavour-rigidity margin.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
For Hermitian \(A\), \(\operatorname{ad}_A\) is self-adjoint in the
Hilbert--Schmidt inner product.  Hence
\[
 \langle X,\mathscr L_{A,B}X\rangle_{\rm HS}
 =\|[A,X]\|_{\rm HS}^2+\|[B,X]\|_{\rm HS}^2.
\]
The form vanishes exactly on the common commutant.  On its orthogonal
complement, the positive operator is bounded below by its least positive
eigenvalue, which gives the estimate.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Minimum positive generation residue for Dirac CP]
\label{prop:SM-residue-minimum}
A positive rank-one additive residue cannot generate a nonzero Dirac triangle
phase: if \(R=vv^*\), then
\[
 R_{12}R_{23}R_{31}=|v_1v_2v_3|^2\in\R_{\ge0}.
\]
A positive rank-two residue is sufficient.  For
\[
 v=(1,1,1)^{\mathsf T},
 \qquad
 w=(1,i,0)^{\mathsf T},
 \qquad
 R=vv^*+ww^*,
\]
one has \(R\succeq0\), \(\rank R=2\), and
\[
 R_{12}R_{23}R_{31}=1-i.
\]
Thus, within positive low-rank additive generation residues, rank one may
produce nonzero mixing but not Dirac CP, while rank two is the minimum capable
of a nonzero CP triangle phase.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
For \(R=vv^*\), the three factors are
\(v_1\bar v_2\), \(v_2\bar v_3\), and \(v_3\bar v_1\), whose product is the
stated nonnegative real number.  In the rank-two example the two vectors are
linearly independent, so the positive sum has rank two.  Direct calculation
gives \(R_{12}=1-i\), \(R_{23}=1\), and \(R_{31}=1\), proving the nonreal
triangle product.
\end{proof}

\begin{assessment}[Standalone finite-SM status after the source-native reduction]
\label{assess:SM-standalone-status}
The exact finite status is now:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(S\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]

      determinant stabilizer, quotient group, chiral types, and
      multiplicity-one carrier lines are exact finite results.

      grading-preserving six-state release remains exactly on the no-matter
      branch.
\item If the locked signed-return writer is literally the pre-central grading
      writer, the selected nonzero odd Store phase is already a source-native
      matter route.  Independently, on a common locked--Clifford carrier the
      uniform Clifford-twirl scalar is positive exactly when a matter route
      exists; its zero branch is the grading supported entirely in the normal
      multiplicity commutant.  The complete Store generator need not be purely
      odd.
\item Two graded parallel Store cells derive the weak CAR algebra and all four
      incidence rows.  The primitive selected phase has one scalar doublet;
      branch completeness, rather than a downstream one-Higgs assumption,
      decides whether an additional odd direction is present.  One nonzero
      route is sufficient for structural matter; nonvanishing of every typed
      residue edge is a stronger physical claim audited by the unsplit
      transition curvatures.
\item An exact unitary mixer is not required for the coherent source branch.
      A forward/reverse CPTP pair through the identity is sufficient when its
      differentiated channel has zero Hamiltonian, reversal, and source-core
      residual.  Bounded second-order noise is removed by direct or bracket
      Klein refocusing.  Positive occurrence-packet orbit matrices decide
      source-native odd-sector exhaustion, and a finite pulse commutator Gram
      controls the generator relative Howe gap.
\item The locked $K_4$ edge packet gives one centered positive rank-three
      endpoint source.  Its orthogonal cycle triplet is loop provenance, not a
      second generation copy.
\item Krylov saturation removes full-cell leakage by adjoining every actual
      innovation.  On the branch-complete selected phase the complete odd
      generator is the finite-Dirac operator; the even generator remains a
      legitimate gauge/scalar/normal sector.
\item The five residue slots, their tetrahedral-breaking components, spectra,
      mixing, and CP invariants are finite readouts of that one operator.  Their
      nonzero numerical values are not fixed by representation theory.

\subsection{Physical-unit writer orientation and coherence completion}
\label{sec:SMST-writer-coherence}
% =============================================================================

The scalar coefficient writer is constrained first by the commuting physical
unit packet and only afterward by dynamical or variational selection.  Let
$E_\omega^{\rm a}$ and $E_\omega^{\rm u}$ be the action and unit fibres of one
complete mass, clock, volume, and field-incidence signature $\omega$.

\begin{theorem}[Unit-character writer dimension of the repaired scalar bank]
\label{thm:SMST-unit-writer-dimension}
Every physical scalar coefficient writer is a unit intertwiner
\[
 B=\bigoplus_\omega B_\omega,
 \qquad
 B_\omega:E_\omega^{\rm a}\to E_\omega^{\rm u}.
\]
For the repaired nonconstant scalar census through degree four, the
coefficient dimensions and real unit-covariant writer dimensions are
\[
 \boxed{
 \begin{array}{c|ccc}
 \text{degree}&2&3&4\\ \hline
 \dim E&4&6&24\\
 \dim\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal U}&4&8&46
 \end{array}}
 \tag{SMW.1}
\]
and therefore
\[
 \boxed{34^2=1156\quad\longrightarrow\quad
 \dim\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal U}=58.}
 \tag{SMW.2}
\]
The block multiplicities consist of thirteen simple blocks, nine rank-two
blocks, and one rank-three block:
\[
 \boxed{58=13\cdot1^2+9\cdot2^2+1\cdot3^2.}
 \tag{SMW.3}
\]
Thus forty-five coordinates belong to repeated equal-signature blocks and are
not fixed by endpoint dimensions or unit charges.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Unit covariance deletes every cross-signature block by Hilbert--Schmidt
orthogonal projection.  The writer dimension is the sum of the squared
multiplicities.  The displayed scalar census gives $4+8+46=58$ and the stated
multiplicity decomposition.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Joint writer covariance and the twelve connected angles]
\label{thm:SMST-joint-writer-orientation}
Let $F_\omega$, $G_\omega$, and $C_\omega$ be the faithful fine, coarse, and
mixed score Grams from one same-history conditional/coarse writer experiment.
The whitened overlap
\[
 \boxed{W_\omega=F_\omega^{-1/2}C_\omega G_\omega^{-1/2}=U_\omega P_\omega}
 \tag{SMW.4}
\]
has positive coherence modulus $P_\omega$, orientation $U_\omega$, and
innovation $G_\omega^{1/2}(I-P_\omega^2)G_\omega^{1/2}$.  On the square
zero-innovation, identity-connected real branch, the continuous orientation
space has dimension
\[
 \boxed{
 \sum_\omega\frac{m_\omega(m_\omega-1)}2
 =9+3=12.}
 \tag{SMW.5}
\]
If $F(0)=G(0)=C(0)=M$, its infinitesimal connected writer is
\[
 \boxed{\Omega_\omega
 =\frac12M_\omega^{-1}(C_{1,\omega}-C_{1,\omega}^*).}
 \tag{SMW.6}
\]
The endpoint Fisher derivatives determine the metric stretch, not this skew
orientation.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Apply polar decomposition to the normalized joint-source contraction.  Zero
Schur innovation makes the polar modulus the identity.  The connected
orientation group is $SO(m_\omega)$, with dimension $m_\omega(m_\omega-1)/2$;
the multiplicities in \textup{(SMW.3)} give twelve.  Differentiating the
metric-unitary identity gives \textup{(SMW.6)}.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Relative action--unit holonomy and residual writer selection]
\label{thm:SMST-relative-writer-selection}
Let $T_{\gamma,\omega}$ and $P_{\gamma,\omega}$ be the independently measured
action and unit transports around physical cycles.  On the writer fibre define
\[
 \mathscr S_{\gamma,\omega}(B)
 =P_{\gamma,\omega}B-BT_{\gamma,\omega},
 \qquad
 L_{\omega}^{\rm hol}
 =\sum_\gamma a_\gamma
 \mathscr S_{\gamma,\omega}^*\mathscr S_{\gamma,\omega}.
 \tag{SMW.7}
\]
For a complete paired writer-Read map $R_\omega$, the block decomposes
orthogonally as
\[
 \boxed{
 E_\omega^{\rm writer}
 =\Ran R_\omega^*
 \oplus
 \bigl(\ker R_\omega\ominus
       (\ker R_\omega\cap\ker L_\omega^{\rm hol})\bigr)
 \oplus
 (\ker R_\omega\cap\ker L_\omega^{\rm hol}).}
 \tag{SMW.8}
\]
The three terms are Read-forced, holonomy-nonflat, and flat intertwiner
orientations.  The nonflat term is priced by the positive holonomy action but
is selected only after an independently physical Euler, stationarity, or
intervention law is supplied.  The flat term requires a primitive Ward,

\[

 \ker L_\omega^{\rm hol}
 =\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{Hol}}
   (E_\omega^{\rm a},E_\omega^{\rm u}).}
 \tag{SMW.9}
\]
Finally, a physical coefficient transport must pass the word-level residual
of \Cref{thm:GT-monoidal-transport} on the actual scalar invariant
contractions; linear Fisher orientation alone does not certify occurrence
transport.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The first decomposition is the orthogonal split by the Read range and the
positive operator $L_\omega^{\rm hol}$ on its kernel.  The kernel condition in
\textup{(SMW.9)} is exactly the family of relative intertwining equations.
The selection statements follow from
\Cref{fire:GT-action-inertia-not-selection}; the final statement is
\Cref{thm:GT-monoidal-transport}.
\end{proof}

The joint loaded tensor must distinguish two questions.  The internal

\begin{theorem}[Universal coupled gravity--internal action carrier]
\label{thm:SMST-universal-coupled-action}
Work on the future-minimal relational carrier of
\Cref{def:relational-grand-tensor}.  Let
\[
 S_{\rm g}:E_{\rm g}\to\mathcal H_{\rm cyl},
 \qquad
 S_{\rm i}:E_{\rm i}\to\mathcal H_{\rm cyl}
\]
be the source syntheses of the complete gravitational and internal physical
variation banks on one same-history event, and assume the gravitational bank
has already been reduced to its faithful quotient.  Put
\[
 G_{\rm g}=S_{\rm g}^*S_{\rm g},\qquad
 G_{\rm i}=S_{\rm i}^*S_{\rm i},\qquad
 C=S_{\rm i}^*S_{\rm g},
\]
\[
 \boxed{
 G_{{\rm i}\mid{\rm g}}
 :=G_{\rm i}-CG_{\rm g}^{-1}C^*
 =S_{\rm i}^*(I-P_{\rm g})S_{\rm i}.}
 \tag{CA.1}
\]
Then:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(C\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item the complete variation Gram has the exact factorization
      \[
       \boxed{
       \begin{pmatrix}G_{\rm g}&C^*\\C&G_{\rm i}\end{pmatrix}
       =
       \begin{pmatrix}I&0\\CG_{\rm g}^{-1}&I\end{pmatrix}
       \begin{pmatrix}G_{\rm g}&0\\0&G_{{\rm i}\mid{\rm g}}\end{pmatrix}
       \begin{pmatrix}I&G_{\rm g}^{-1}C^*\\0&I\end{pmatrix};}
       \tag{CA.2}
      \]
      hence the common carrier is faithful exactly when
      $G_{{\rm i}\mid{\rm g}}\succ0$, and the number of genuinely new internal
      source directions is $\rank G_{{\rm i}\mid{\rm g}}$;
\item the source-minimal internal variation space is
      \[
       \boxed{
       E_{{\rm i}\mid{\rm g}}^{\min}
       :=E_{\rm i}/\Ker G_{{\rm i}\mid{\rm g}};}
       \tag{CA.3}
      \]
      it is invariant under unread record refinements and source-fixing changes
      of Hankel coordinates;
\item an explicit positive branch is obtained by adjoining independent centred
      point-readable neighbouring-law interventions on the future-minimal
      internal tangent and whitening their covariance.  On that branch
      \[
       \boxed{C=0,\qquad G_{{\rm i}\mid{\rm g}}=I,}
       \tag{CA.4}
      \]
      while the old renewal and gravitational cylinders are unchanged;
\item let $\Phi=(U,\phi,\Psi,\overline\Psi)$ be the finite internal
      configuration and let one signed action
      $\mathscr S_{\rm int}^{\rm cl}$ and one positive operational cost
      $\mathscr A_{\rm int}^{+}$ be written from the same links, Higgs field,
      finite Dirac operator, Yukawa map, geometric weights, and coefficient
      bank.  Exact gauge and tangential invariance imply
      \[
       \boxed{
       \mathcal R_{\Phi}^*\nabla\mathscr S_{\rm int}^{\rm cl}=0,
       \qquad s^2=0,
       \qquad s\mathscr S_{\rm int}^{\rm cl}=0,}
       \tag{CA.5}
      \]
      and, with
      $E_\Phi=D_\Phi\mathscr S_{\rm int}^{\rm cl}$ and
      $\mathsf T^{\rm int}=-2D_q\mathscr S_{\rm int}^{\rm cl}$,
      \[
       \boxed{
       \mathcal L_q^*\mathsf T^{\rm int}
       =2\mathcal L_\Phi^*E_\Phi.}
       \tag{CA.6}
      \]
      Thus current and stress conservation hold on the internal field shell;
\item at the invariant internal vacuum
      \[
       U_e=I,\qquad \phi_v=vh_0,\qquad
       \Psi_v=\overline\Psi_v=0,
       \tag{CA.7}
      \]
      where $h_0$ is a fixed unit vector in the weak doublet, the positive
      gauge, scalar, and fermion graph terms vanish, so
      \[
       \boxed{
       \mathscr S_{\rm int}^{\rm cl}
       =\mathscr A_{\rm int}^{+}=0,
       \qquad E_\Phi=0,
       \qquad\mathsf T^{\rm int}=0;}
       \tag{CA.8}
      \]
\item if $Q_{{\rm g},X}$ is the completed gravitational Perron--Doob row, the
      total vacuum loading has the unique driven row
      \[
       \boxed{
       Q_{{\rm tot},X}
       =Q_{{\rm g},X}\otimes\delta_{\Phi^{(0)}},}
       \tag{CA.9}
      \]
      with the same pressure and Perron vector as gravity.  Hence the common
      provenance and accepted/action gaps vanish;
\item every fixed finite internal representation rank uses the existing
      spacetime Hodge and compact spectral screens.  If $P_X(\Lambda)$ is a
      gravitational screen and $r_{\rm fib}$ is the internal fibre rank, then
      \[
       \boxed{
       \rank P_X^{\rm int}(\Lambda)
       \le r_{\rm fib}\,\rank P_X(\Lambda).}
       \tag{CA.10}
      \]
      No second compactness, trace, memory, or refinement primitive is needed.
\end{enumerate}
Consequently the explicitly repaired Grand Tensor has a faithful common
classical gravity--internal action carrier with vanishing complete first
variation on every completed vacuum gravity branch.  A nonzero backreacting
solution is a model-specific finite or cofinal Euler-map problem, not an
additional universal coordinate.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Equation \textup{(CA.1)} is the Gram of $(I-P_{\rm g})S_{\rm i}$, and direct
block multiplication gives \textup{(CA.2)}.  Positivity, the faithfulness
criterion, the rank increment, and the quotient \textup{(CA.3)} follow from
\Cref{thm:source-Schur,thm:joint-source-universality}.  Independent centred
intervention scores have zero mixed covariance with the gravitational score
bank; whitening gives \textup{(CA.4)}.  The port is conservative by
\Cref{thm:relational-completion}.

The local action forms and their zero sets are
\Cref{thm:SMST-action-rigidity}.  Differentiating finite gauge invariance gives
the Ward identity; the standard finite BRST differential is the infinitesimal
gauge action with $sc=-c^2$, so the Jacobi identity gives $s^2=0$ and gauge
invariance gives $s\mathscr S_{\rm int}^{\rm cl}=0$.  Differentiating common
tangential relabeling invariance gives \textup{(CA.6)}, as in
\Cref{thm:SMST-finite-action-Einstein}.  At \textup{(CA.7)} every plaquette is
trivial, every covariant Higgs difference is zero, the radial potential is at
its minimum, and the fermion bilinear vanishes, proving \textup{(CA.8)}.

The tilted total vacuum matrix is the tensor product of the gravitational
tilted row with the one-point internal row.  Perron uniqueness therefore gives
\textup{(CA.9)}.  Finally, tensoring a positive spatial/Hodge operator with a
fixed finite internal identity multiplies every low-energy multiplicity by at
most the fibre rank and leaves all cutoff powers unchanged, proving
\textup{(CA.10)}.  The complete gravitational plus internal first variation
vanishes by \Cref{thm:SMST-finite-action-Einstein} and faithfulness of
\textup{(CA.2)}.
\end{proof}


\begin{theorem}[Explicit regulated classical Standard-Model action on the active carrier]
\label{thm:SM-active-SM-II}
Assume the active structural packet of \Cref{thm:SM-active-SM-I} on either the
flat regulator of \Cref{cor:relational-flat-vacuum} or the curved regulator of
\Cref{thm:relational-deSitter-branch}.  Let $V_X,E_X,F_X$ be the finite
spacetime vertices, oriented edges, and plaquettes, with positive companion
Hodge weights $\star_{0,X},\star_{1,X},\star_{2,X}$.  A classical internal
configuration consists of
\[
 U_e\in G_{\rm SM},\qquad H_v\in W_2,
 \qquad
 \Psi_v\in\mathcal S_v\otimes G\otimes\mathcal H_F^{(1)},
 \tag{CA.11}
\]
and an independent dual amplitude $\overline\Psi_v$.  Let
$F_{p,X}=|p|^{-1}\operatorname{Log} U_{\partial p}$ on the principal logarithm chart and
let $D_UH$ be the covariant edge difference.  For positive
$g_3,g_2,g_1,\lambda_H$ and $v_H\ge0$, and generation matrices
$\boldsymbol Y=(Y_u,Y_d,Y_e,Y_\nu,M_R)$ with $M_R^{\mathsf T}=M_R$, define
\[
 \boxed{
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathscr S_{{\rm SM},X}^{E}
 ={}&\frac12\langle F_X,\star_{2,X}F_X\rangle_{g_3,g_2,g_1}
 +\frac12\langle D_UH,\star_{1,X}D_UH\rangle\\
 &+\sum_vm_{v,X}\lambda_H(\|H_v\|^2-v_H^2)^2\\
 &+\operatorname{Re}\langle\overline\Psi,
 \star_{0,X}\bigl(D_{{\rm sp},X}^{U}
 +\Gamma_{\rm Cl}\otimes D_F^{\boldsymbol Y}(H)\bigr)\Psi\rangle .
 \end{aligned}}
 \tag{CA.12}
\]
Here the invariant gauge metric has one coefficient on each simple or central
Lie-algebra factor.  The Lorentzian action uses the reconstructed temporal
Hodge signs.  Then:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(R\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item \textup{(CA.12)} is exactly gauge invariant and has cutoff-independent
      support radius: its terms are supported on one vertex, one edge, or one
      plaquette;
\item its Euler covectors satisfy the exact finite Ward identity
      \[
       \boxed{
       d_U^*E_U+\mathcal R_H^*E_H
       +\mathcal R_\Psi^*E_\Psi
       +\mathcal R_{\overline\Psi}^*E_{\overline\Psi}=0;}
       \tag{CA.13}
      \]
\item the standard finite ghost extension
      $sc=-c^2$, $sU=c_tU-Uc_s$, $sH=cH$, $s\Psi=c\Psi$,
      $s\bar c=B$, $sB=0$ is nilpotent and annihilates the action;
\item metric and coframe variation of the same action gives the matter stress,
      and common relabeling invariance gives
      \[
       \boxed{
       \mathcal L_q^*\mathsf T
       =2\mathcal L_U^*E_U+2\mathcal L_H^*E_H
        +2\mathcal L_\Psi^*E_\Psi
        +2\mathcal L_{\overline\Psi}^*E_{\overline\Psi};}
       \tag{CA.14}
      \]
\item every local Gibbs row built from the action increment, and the global
      Perron--Doob row on a compact configuration screen, has exactly zero
      accepted/common-action relative-entropy gap and is gauge equivariant;
\item the periodic configuration
      \[
       U_e=I,
       \qquad H_v=v_Hh_0,
       \qquad\Psi_v=\overline\Psi_v=0
       \tag{CA.15}
      \]
      is a stationary internal vacuum.  For $v_H>0$ its gauge stabilizer is
      \[
       \boxed{U(3)\cong
       (SU(3)\times U(1)_{\rm em})/\mathbb Z_3,}
       \tag{CA.16}
      \]
      the gauge-orbit mass form has rank three, and the radial Higgs Hessian is
      $8\lambda_Hv_H^2$;
\item the gauge, Higgs-gradient, potential, and fermion graph norms inherit the
      spacetime Hodge and compact screens.  No second compactness primitive is
      required.
\end{enumerate}
The coefficients in \textup{(CA.12)} remain physical parameters; changing
them does not change the V22 structural representation packet.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Plaquette holonomy transforms by conjugation, the covariant Higgs difference
transforms in the target fibre, and
$D_F^{\boldsymbol Y}(gH)=\rho_L(g)D_F^{\boldsymbol Y}(H)\rho_R(g)^{-1}$ by the
multiplicity-one incidence construction.  These identities prove gauge
invariance and locality.  Differentiation gives \textup{(CA.13)}.  The BRST
calculation is the graded Jacobi identity together with the same covariance.
Differentiating common relabeling invariance gives \textup{(CA.14)}.  The Gibbs
and Perron--Doob statements are the relative-entropy completion theorem applied
to the one common local cost.

At \textup{(CA.15)} every plaquette and covariant Higgs difference is trivial,
the quartic is at its minimum, and the fermion bilinear vanishes.  The Higgs
stabilizer inside $S(U(3)\times U(2))$ is canonically $U(3)$; its codimension is
three.  Expanding the quartic in the radial real coordinate gives the stated
Hessian.  Finally, all internal fibres have fixed finite rank and the finite
Dirac term is a bounded sitewise perturbation, so the reducing-router and Kato
estimates transfer the existing spacetime screens.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Classical SM-II continuum handoff]
\label{thm:SM-active-SM-II-continuum}
Sample a smooth $G_{\rm SM}$ connection, Higgs doublet, and classical spinor
fields on a compact physical slab by link parallel transport and vertex
restriction.  If the numerical coefficients converge, then
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathscr S_{{\rm SM},X}^{L}\longrightarrow
 \mathscr S_{\rm SM}^{L}}
 \tag{CA.17}
\]
with
\[
 \boxed{
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathscr S_{\rm SM}^{L}
 =\int_{\mathcal M}\sqrt{|g|}\,\dd^4x\,
 \bigg[&-\frac14\langle F_{\mu\nu},F^{\mu\nu}\rangle_{\boldsymbol g}
 +(D_\mu H)^\dagger D^\mu H
 -\lambda_H(\|H\|^2-v_H^2)^2\\
 &+\operatorname{Re}\,\overline\Psi
 \bigl(i\not\!D_A+\Gamma_{\rm Cl}\otimes
 D_F^{\boldsymbol Y}(H)\bigr)\Psi\bigg].
 \end{aligned}}
 \tag{CA.18}
\]
The finite Euler, Ward, BRST, current, and stress identities converge to their
classical continuum counterparts.  If the positive sector energies converge
to the energies of a weak limit, the common screens upgrade curvature and
Higgs-gradient convergence to strong local $L^2$ and Higgs convergence to
strong local $L^4$, so every quadratic current, Yukawa insertion, and stress
term passes to the limit.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
For a smooth connection,
$|p|^{-1}\operatorname{Log} U_{\partial p}=F_A(p)+O(h_X)$; covariant Taylor expansion gives
$\ell_e^{-1}(U_eH_s-H_t)=D_AH(e)+O(h_X)$; and the completed centred spacetime
Dirac with gauge links has the symbol of $\not\!D_A$ with an $O(h_X)$
graph-norm error.  The sitewise finite Dirac converges pointwise.  The Hodge
weights are the spacetime Riemann-sum weights, which proves
\textup{(CA.17)--(CA.18)}.  Exact algebraic Ward and BRST identities pass by
coefficient convergence.  The strong statement is uniform convexity of the
positive gauge and Higgs sectors on the common Hodge screens, followed by the
bundle Sobolev estimate.
\end{proof}

\begin{assessment}[SM-II boundary]
The explicitly completed active primitive now carries a regulated classical
Standard Model on the same cofinal spacetime family.  This does not construct
the Grassmann integral, determinant or Pfaffian section, its Berry curvature
or global phase, nor does it determine the numerical couplings, running,
matching, or an interacting renormalized quantum continuum.  Those questions
begin the quantum SM-III programme and do not reopen the finite structural or
classical action carrier.
\end{assessment}

\subsubsection{Reference-compatible Wilsonian reduction and marginal projective flow}
\label{sec:SM-Wilsonian-marginal-flow}
% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

The finite action theorem supplies the regulated functional.  Numerical
running requires a further chain: one common action must first survive exact
shell marginalization, the physical coefficient origin must be fixed by the
reference law, and the complete marginal block must be treated before a
one-dimensional running coefficient is extracted.


\begin{assessment}[Common-carrier entrance to numerical Standard-Model running]
Before the constant localizer or marginal cone is diagonalized, the complete
physically executable returned-word grammar must be frozen.  At each round the
old words and all one-letter extensions are acquired in one common panel
containing the ordinary blocks $H,C,D$ and the localizing-action blocks
$G,J,K$.  The adaptive compiler of
\Cref{thm:GT-word-localizer-extension,thm:GT-adaptive-word-localizer-stop}
then appends only positive polar innovations, tests flat action consistency,
and executes a held-out word.  The source-cyclic localizer audit begins only
at the genuine common-carrier stop.  On any verified positive reflected
subsector, the dynamical action entrance may first be reduced by
\Cref{thm:GT-three-cylinder-action-response}: the conditional action writer and
three lag Grams either make the present temporal head reducing or append its
canonical missing writer before the localizer is diagonalized.  This supplies
a source-native route into the common word/action panel; it neither populates
the literal Spin$(10)$ extension rows nor supplies the independent absolute-
pressure coordinate.
\end{assessment}

\begin{theorem}[Common-action integrability and exact shell inheritance]
\label{thm:SM-common-action-integrability}
Let $z^A$ be a finite graded coordinate bank and let
$\omega=\sum_A\dd z^A F_A(z)$ be a proposed force one-form on a star-shaped
superdomain.  Put
\[
 \mathfrak C_{AB}
 =\partial_AF_B-
 (-1)^{\epsilon_A\epsilon_B}\partial_BF_A.
 \tag{RG.1}
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathfrak C_{AB}=0\ \forall A,B
 \iff
 F_A=\partial_AS\ \text{for one even action }S.}
 \tag{RG.2}
\]
The action is reconstructed, up to a constant, by radial integration.
Consequently sectorwise gauge, scalar, fermion, or Yukawa fits define one
physical theory only when their complete mixed graded curl vanishes.

For an equivariant coarse Read $\pi:\Omega_Y\to\Omega_X$ and a compatible
reference law, the exact shell action is
\[
 \boxed{
 e^{-S_{Y\to X}^{\rm eff}(x)}
 =\mathbb E_{\rho_Y}
  \left[e^{-S_Y(Y)}\mid\pi(Y)=x\right].}
 \tag{RG.3}
\]
It is gauge invariant, BRST closed, reflection positive whenever the fine
packet and conditional expectation have those properties, and it composes
exactly through nested cutoffs.  Exact marginalization generally leaves the
renormalizable action bank; the Wilsonian object is a finite local head plus a
generated quasilocal tail.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The first claim is the graded Poincar\'e lemma on a star-shaped finite domain.
The conditional-expectation formula is the definition of the exact potential
of mean force; equivariance and positivity pass through conditional
expectation, and the tower property gives nested composition.  A scalar
quartic example already generates a sextic term after one hidden sign is
summed, so exact degree-four closure is not generic.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Operational marginal numerical packet]
\label{def:SM-operational-numerical-packet}
At a cutoff $X$, the loaded numerical marginal packet is
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathfrak M_X^{\rm num}
 =\bigl(
 H_X,\mathbb I_X^{\rm eff},\mathbb D_X^{\rm dir},L_{0,X},F_X,
 \{\mathscr L_{j,X}\}_j,\nu_X,\mathcal Q_X,b_X,\ell_{g,X}
 \bigr).}
 \tag{RG.3a}
\]
Here $H_X$ is the flat returned-word Gram; $\mathbb I_X^{\rm eff}$ is the
physical efficient score localizer after one common nuisance short;
$\mathbb D_X^{\rm dir}$ is the independently reconstructed direct
second-action or partition row; $L_{0,X}$ is the constant Gaussian localizer;
$F_X$ is the complete future-signature map on its kernel;
$\mathscr L_{j,X}$ are the matrix-valued stability, reality, phase, support,
and positivity writers; $\nu_X$ is a physical calibration functional;
$\mathcal Q_X$ and $b_X$ are the quadratic shell and leading source forcing;
and $\ell_{g,X}$ is the physical scalar Read used for the gauge comparison.
No component of this packet is selected from a target value.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Operational marginal cone and future-visible neutral carrier]
\label{thm:SM-operational-cone}
Let $R_X:E_X\to F_X^{\rm eq}$ assemble all homogeneous equality writers and put
$E_{0,X}=\Ker R_X$.  Assemble every physical matrix-order writer before
quotienting,
\[
 \mathscr L_X=\bigoplus_j\mathscr L_{j,X},
 \qquad
 \mathcal K_X
 =\{x\in E_{0,X}:\mathscr L_{j,X}(x)\succeq0\ \forall j\}.
 \tag{RG.3b}
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{\mathcal K_X\cap(-\mathcal K_X)=\Ker\mathscr L_X.}
 \tag{RG.3c}
\]
Only
$\Ker\mathscr L_X\cap\Ker F_X$ may be quotiented without loss.  Every
$z\in\Ker\mathscr L_X$ with $F_Xz\ne0$ is a future-visible neutral marginal
coordinate and must either receive a new physical order writer or remain in the
coupled shell system.

If $W_{j,X}\succ0$ are independently physical calibration matrices, then
\[
 \boxed{
 \nu_X(x)=\sum_j\Tr(W_{j,X}\mathscr L_{j,X}(x))}
 \tag{RG.3d}
\]
is strictly positive on every nonzero ray of the pointed quotient cone, and
\[
 \boxed{\mathcal B_X=\{x\in\mathcal K_X:\nu_X(x)=1\}}
 \tag{RG.3e}
\]
is a compact convex base.  Thus admissibility, lineality, and normalization are
physical outputs of the writer packet, not consequences of an unsigned scalar
Gram.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
If $x$ and $-x$ are both admitted, every positive matrix
$\mathscr L_{j,X}(x)$ and its negative are positive, hence both vanish.  This
proves \textup{(RG.3c)}.  Quotienting a direction detected by $F_X$ would
identify two physically distinct futures.  On the pointed quotient, every
nonzero cone point has at least one nonzero positive writer block, so
\textup{(RG.3d)} is strictly positive.  Its unit section is closed and bounded
in finite dimension and therefore compact.
\end{proof}

\begin{countertheorem}[Unsigned writer geometry does not determine the cone]
\label{cth:SM-writer-Gram-no-cone}
The maps
\[
 \mathscr L_+(x,y)=\diag(x,y),
 \qquad
 \mathscr L_-(x,y)=\diag(x,-y)
\]
have the identical coefficient Gram
$\mathscr L_+^*\mathscr L_+=\mathscr L_-^*\mathscr L_-=I_2$, but define the
oppositely oriented cones
$\{x\ge0,y\ge0\}$ and $\{x\ge0,y\le0\}$.  Hence singular values, absolute
values, or scalar writer Grams cannot replace the physical matrix-order panel.
\end{countertheorem}

\begin{theorem}[Constant localizer, nested Schur jets, and the complete leading ray]
\label{thm:SM-localizer-jets}
Assume the complete frozen grammar has passed
\Cref{thm:GT-word-localizer-descent,thm:GT-adaptive-word-localizer-stop},
the flat action relations and one held-out direct word have passed, and the
source-cyclic localizer carrier has closed as in
\Cref{cor:GT-two-stage-localizer-flatness}.  Let
$L_X(s)\succeq0$ be a one-sided $C^2$ physical width family,
$L_X(0)=L_{0,X}$, and write
\[
 P=P_{\Ker L_{0,X}},\qquad Q=I-P,
 \qquad QL_{0,X}Q\succeq\gamma_XQ\quad(\gamma_X>0).
\]
The exact localizer induced on the constant kernel is
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal S_X(s)
 =PL_X(s)P
 -PL_X(s)Q[QL_X(s)Q]^{-1}QL_X(s)P\succeq0.}
 \tag{RG.3f}
\]
With $L_1=L_X'(0)$, $L_2=L_X''(0)$,
$A_0=QL_{0,X}Q$, one has
\[
 \boxed{K_{1,X}=\mathcal S_X'(0)=PL_1P\succeq0,}
 \tag{RG.3g}
\]
and, on $P_1=P_{\Ker K_{1,X}}$,
\[
 \boxed{
 K_{2,X}
 =P_1\bigl(PL_2P-2PL_1QA_0^{-1}QL_1P\bigr)P_1\succeq0.}
 \tag{RG.3h}
\]
The negative term is the exact hard-range relaxation and cannot be omitted.
For a marginal graph $z(s)=sr+O(s^2)$ and gauge step
$s^+=s+\beta s^2+O(s^3)$, the complete leading equation is
\[
 \boxed{
 b_X+\mathcal Q_X(r,r)-K_{1,X}r-\beta r=0.}
 \tag{RG.3i}
\]
A direction in $\Ker K_{1,X}$ is an $O(s^2)$ follower only if its projection of
$b_X+\mathcal Q_X(r,r)$ vanishes.  The second jet first contributes to the next
ratio correction and does not repair a failed leading follower condition.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Completing the square over the hard range gives \textup{(RG.3f)} and its
variational positivity.  Since $\mathcal S_X(s)\succeq0$ for $s\ge0$ and
$\mathcal S_X(0)=0$, its one-sided first derivative is positive.  On the
kernel of that derivative the one-sided second derivative is positive.  Direct
differentiation of the Schur term gives \textup{(RG.3h)}.  Substitution of the
invariant graph and gauge step into the reduced marginal recurrence gives
\textup{(RG.3i)}; the coefficient of the next graph term cancels at order
$s^2$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Reference-compatible origin and Gaussian marginal block]
\label{thm:SM-reference-origin-marginal-block}
Assume the reference laws satisfy $\rho_X=\pi_*\rho_Y$, the fine zero-action
packet obeys $S_Y(\cdot;0)=0$, and the coefficient normalization and invariant
tail graph preserve zero.  Then the reduced shell satisfies
\[
 \boxed{\Sigma_{\rm red}(0)=0.}
 \tag{RG.4}
\]
A nonzero affine translation is therefore a reference, normalization, tail
origin, or action-bank defect rather than a free selector.

Assume that at the Gaussian origin the reduced Gaussian shell is the
engineering scaling map
\(
 \Sigma_{\rm red}^{\rm G}(x)_\Delta=b^{4-\Delta}x_\Delta
\)
on the finite operator-dimension bank.  Then its Fr\'echet derivative gives
\[
 \boxed{
 D\Sigma_{\rm red}(0)
 =\bigoplus_\Delta b^{4-\Delta}I_{E_\Delta},
 \qquad
 \ker(I-D\Sigma_{\rm red}(0))=E_4.}
 \tag{RG.5}
\]
Thus the complete dimension-four coefficient bank is a semisimple marginal
block.  Only the strictly irrelevant complement can be linearly slaved.
Writing the reduced marginal step as
\[
 x^+=x+\mathcal Q(x,x)+O(\|x\|^3),
 \qquad x\in E_4,
 \tag{RG.6}
\]
every differentiable Gaussian trajectory $x(s)=sa+O(s^2)$ must solve
\[
 \boxed{\mathcal Q(a,a)=\beta_a a.}
 \tag{RG.7}
\]
The gauge component alone, including the held-out value $29/132$, cannot
select the complete ray.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
At zero action the conditional weight in \textup{(RG.3)} is one, so the coarse
action is zero relative to the pushed-forward reference.  The Gaussian
Jacobian is the engineering rescaling on each operator-dimension block.
Substitution of $x(s)$ into \textup{(RG.6)} gives \textup{(RG.7)} at order
$s^2$.
\end{proof}

The coefficient coordinates in \textup{(RG.6)} must themselves be physically
calibrated.  Let $\mathfrak g$ be the tangent algebra of executable marginal
commands and $\mathfrak k=[\mathfrak g,\mathfrak g]$ its represented operation
ideal.  Additive coefficient coordinates factor through
$\mathfrak g_{\rm ab}=\mathfrak g/\mathfrak k$ and retain an independently
calibrated orientation and unit.

\begin{theorem}[Command quotient, palindromic Hessian, and harmonic lift]
\label{thm:SM-command-quotient-hessian}
Let the calibrated shell response have expansion
\[
 F(z)=Jz+\frac12B(z,z)+O(\|z\|^3).
\]
For shrinking commands $g_X(h),g_Y(h)$, the commutator square reconstructs
$[D_X,D_Y]$.  A raw sequential mixed probe contains the alias
$\frac12J[X,Y]$, whereas the palindromic command
\[
 g_X(h/2)g_{\pm Y}(h)g_X(h/2)
\]
has no quadratic Baker--Campbell--Hausdorff term and reconstructs $B(X,Y)$.

The response descends intrinsically through the operation fibre exactly when
\[
 \boxed{J|_{\mathfrak k}=0,
 \qquad B(\mathfrak k,\mathfrak g)=0.}
 \tag{RG.8}
\]
If these fail but the operation fibre is source free and its common-action
block
\[
 \begin{pmatrix}A&C\\C^*&D\end{pmatrix}\succeq0
\]
has $D\succ0$, the unique minimum-action representative is the harmonic lift
\[
 \boxed{z_{\mathfrak k}=-D^{-1}C^*z_{\rm ab},
 \qquad
 S_{\rm op}=A-CD^{-1}C^*.}
 \tag{RG.9}
\]
A soft or independently sourced operation direction must instead remain in the
marginal projective system.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The command square is the second-order definition of the Lie bracket.
Symmetric Baker--Campbell--Hausdorff expansion cancels the order-$h^2$
commutator in the palindromic word.  Changing a local lift adds vertical first
and mixed second response terms; their vanishing is exactly \textup{(RG.8)}.
Completion of the common-action square gives \textup{(RG.9)} and its
uniqueness.
\end{proof}

Fix the physical coefficient metric on $E_4$ and define the beta one-form
\[
 \alpha_x(h)=\langle h,\mathcal Q(x,x)\rangle.
\]
Let $\Omega=\dd\alpha$.

\begin{theorem}[Variational--circulating marginal tensor and cone ray]
\label{thm:SM-beta-curl-cone-ray}
The quadratic tensor has a unique metric-orthogonal decomposition
\[
 \boxed{\mathcal Q=\mathcal Q_{\rm var}+\mathcal Q_{\rm circ},}
 \tag{RG.10}
\]
where $\mathcal Q_{\rm var}$ is generated by the cubic potential
$\Phi(x)=\frac13\langle x,\mathcal Q(x,x)\rangle$ and
$\langle x,\mathcal Q_{\rm circ}(x,x)\rangle=0$.  The circulation is exactly
the beta-form curl:
\[
 \boxed{
 \langle h,\mathcal Q_{\rm circ}(u,v)\rangle
 =\frac16\bigl[\Omega_v(u,h)+\Omega_u(v,h)\bigr].}
 \tag{RG.11}
\]

Let $\mathcal K\subset E_4$ be the physically admissible stability/reality
cone and let $\nu$ calibrate a compact base
$\mathcal B_\nu=\{x\in\mathcal K:\nu(x)=1\}$.  If
\[
 \mathcal Q(\mathcal B_\nu,\mathcal B_\nu)
 \subseteq\mathcal K\setminus\{0\},
\]
then the normalized quadratic shell has at least one physical projective ray.
If the normalized map is a strict contraction on the base, that ray is unique.
For a variational cone candidate $a$ with dual slack $s$, the complete-ray
condition is the tangent identity
\[
 \boxed{
 \frac13\Omega_a(a,h)=\langle h,s\rangle
 \quad(h\perp a).}
 \tag{RG.12}
\]
Thus an interior candidate in an $n$-dimensional marginal block needs at most
$n-1$ palindromic tangent-curl reads, rather than the complete ambient
three-index tensor.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Symmetrizing the metric trilinear form gives the gradient tensor; the
orthogonal complement is radial-free and yields \textup{(RG.11)} by direct
polarization.  Brouwer's theorem applied to the normalized cone map gives
existence, and Banach contraction gives uniqueness.  The Karush--Kuhn--Tucker
condition for the variational maximizer supplies the slack; subtracting it
from the complete tensor gives \textup{(RG.12)}.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Operational projective map, residual certification, and coordinate covariance]
\label{thm:SM-certified-projective-ray}
On the compact physical base of \Cref{thm:SM-operational-cone}, define the
complete leading map
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal F_X(x)=b_X+\mathcal Q_X(x,x)-K_{1,X}x.}
 \tag{RG.13}
\]
Assume
$\mathcal F_X(\mathcal B_X)\subseteq\mathcal K_X\setminus\{0\}$ and put
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal T_X(x)
 =\frac{\mathcal F_X(x)}{\nu_X(\mathcal F_X(x))}.}
 \tag{RG.14}
\]
Then $\mathcal T_X$ has a fixed point $a_X\in\mathcal B_X$, and
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal F_X(a_X)=\beta_Xa_X,
 \qquad
 \beta_X=\nu_X(\mathcal F_X(a_X))>0.}
 \tag{RG.15}
\]
If $\mathcal T_X$ is $q_X$-contractive with $q_X<1$, the ray is unique.  For
any approximation $\widehat a_X\in\mathcal B_X$,
\[
 \boxed{
 \|\widehat a_X-a_X\|
 \le\frac{\|\widehat a_X-\mathcal T_X(\widehat a_X)\|}{1-q_X}.}
 \tag{RG.16}
\]
Consequently every physical scalar Read satisfies
\[
 \boxed{
 |\ell_{g,X}(\widehat a_X)-\ell_{g,X}(a_X)|
 \le
 \|\ell_{g,X}|_{\Ker\nu_X}\|_*
 \frac{\|\widehat a_X-\mathcal T_X(\widehat a_X)\|}{1-q_X}.}
 \tag{RG.17}
\]

For an invertible physical coefficient transport $A:E_X\to E_Y$, transport
\[
 \mathcal K_Y=A\mathcal K_X,
 \quad\nu_Y=\nu_XA^{-1},
 \quad\mathcal F_Y(Ax)=A\mathcal F_X(x),
 \quad\ell_{g,Y}=\ell_{g,X}A^{-1}.
\]
Then $a_Y=Aa_X$ and
\[
 \boxed{\ell_{g,Y}(a_Y)=\ell_{g,X}(a_X).}
 \tag{RG.18}
\]
Thus a coordinate component of the ray is not a numerical prediction.  The
physical Read and the complete transported packet are indispensable.  The
interval in \textup{(RG.17)} is frozen before comparison with any perturbative
or experimental target.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The map \textup{(RG.14)} is a continuous self-map of the compact convex base,
so Brouwer gives a fixed point and \textup{(RG.15)}.  Banach's theorem gives
uniqueness on the contractive branch.  For an approximate point,
\[
 \|\widehat a-a\|
 \le\|\widehat a-\mathcal T(\widehat a)\|
    +q\|\widehat a-a\|,
\]
which proves \textup{(RG.16)}; duality gives \textup{(RG.17)}.  The transport
identities conjugate the normalized map, so they carry fixed points and scalar
Reads exactly, proving \textup{(RG.18)}.
\end{proof}
