\subsubsection{A literal anomaly-free gauge--Higgs--Yukawa field-shell realization}
\label{sec:SMST-field-shell}
% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

The abstract coupled action above admits a finite control realization in which
the gauge, Higgs, Yukawa, ghost, chiral-fermion, reaction, mediator, and
boundary writers occur on one unnormalized same-history cylinder.  This
realization is used only to populate the corresponding positive branch; it is
not used to infer a Wilsonian beta tensor from equilibrium data or to replace
the independent continuum and measure-line certificates.

\paragraph{Upstream correction and scope}
\label{subsec:SMFS-scope}

The inherited reaction--mediator construction placed a finite internal chiral control block on the catalytic
reaction--mediator cylinder.  The next upstream task is not to infer a
Wilsonian beta tensor from that equilibrium block.  It is to put an actual
finite gauge, Higgs, Yukawa, ghost, and chiral-fermion field packet on the same
unnormalized history, verify one positive reflected law and one common score
and direct-action bank, and only then ask which stronger continuum outputs are
licensed.

The construction provides such a finite one-generation field shell on a
protected admissibility chart.  Its gauge and Higgs amplitudes are genuine
finite field variables, its fermion section is the Berezin section of the same
chiral operator used in its positive modulus, and its field heat-bath and
the inherited reaction--mediator cylinder clocks form one reversible path law.  The chart retains a uniform
Wilson and chiral singular floor and a uniform Dobrushin margin.  These are
explicit \textup{(U1)} hypotheses of the constructed branch, not conclusions from
finite anomaly cancellation.

Three stronger claims remain separate:
\[
 \boxed{
 \begin{gathered}
  \text{one-cutoff equilibrium score Hessian}
  \not\Rightarrow \text{Wilsonian quadratic shell tensor},\\
  \text{gauge-invariant nonzero Berezin section}
  \not\Rightarrow \text{independently physical line connection},\\
  \text{boundary stationarity}
  \not\Rightarrow \text{the complete bulk Palatini equation}.
 \end{gathered}}\tag{FS.1}\label{eq:SMFS-three-separations}
\]

% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
\paragraph{The anomaly-free one-generation carrier}
\label{subsec:SMFS-generation}

The shell uses the determinant seed and one-generation matter packet already
reconstructed in
\Cref{thm:SM-group,thm:SM-anomaly-forced-weights,thm:SM-generation,thm:SM-anomaly}.
In the integer convention \(y=6Y\), let
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 Q&=(\mathbf3,\mathbf2)_1,
 &U^c&=(\overline{\mathbf3},\mathbf1)_{-4},
 &D^c&=(\overline{\mathbf3},\mathbf1)_2,\\
 L&=(\mathbf1,\mathbf2)_{-3},
 &E^c&=(\mathbf1,\mathbf1)_6,
 &H&=(\mathbf1,\mathbf2)_3.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Put \(\omega_3=e^{2\pi i/3}\) and
\(\zeta=(\omega_3I_3,-I_2,e^{i\pi/3})\).

\begin{corollary}[Anomaly-free quotient carrier for the field shell]
\label{cor:SMFS-anomaly-quotient}
The displayed representation is trivial on the cyclic group generated by
\(\zeta\), hence descends to
\[
 \boxed{
 G_{\rm SM}
 =\frac{\SU(3)\times\SU(2)\times\U(1)}{\mathbb Z_6}.}
\]
All local gauge and mixed gravitational anomalies vanish, the number of weak
doublets is even, and the determinant character of the complete one-generation
chiral coefficient is trivial.  Consequently a nonzero finite Berezin section
may descend to the connected gauge quotient.  This conclusion supplies
gauge-equivariance of the finite line; it does not orient an independently
physical connection or a real Pfaffian line.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The quotient statement is the central-descent criterion of
\Cref{thm:SM-selector}.  The perturbative and global anomaly identities are
\Cref{thm:SM-anomaly}; the determinant-character statement is their exterior
one-generation form and agrees with
\Cref{thm:SM-active-determinant-incidence}.  Descent of a nonzero section is
therefore finite and gauge equivariant, while connection and real-orientation
data are not determined by a character calculation.
\end{proof}

% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
\paragraph{A literal finite gauge--Higgs--Yukawa shell}
\label{subsec:SMFS-literal-shell}
% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

Let \(X_n=(V_n,E_n,P_n)\) be a finite reflected four-dimensional cell complex.
A field configuration is
\[
 \varphi=(U,H)\in
 \mathscr B_n:=G_{\rm SM}^{E_n}\times\mathscr K_H^{V_n},\tag{FS.7}\label{eq:SMFS-field-config}
\]
where \(\mathscr K_H\subset\mathbb C^2\) is a fixed compact ball preserved by
the reflection and gauge action.  Write \(U_p^{(a)}\) for the plaquette
holonomy in the three gauge factors.  Define
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 S_{B,n}(U,H)
 ={}&\sum_{a=3,2}\beta_a\sum_{p\in P_n}
  \left(1-\frac1{d_a}\operatorname{Re}\operatorname{tr}U_p^{(a)}\right)\\
 &+\beta_1\sum_{p\in P_n}(1-\cos\alpha_p)
 +\kappa_H\sum_{e:x\to y}
   \|H_y-\rho_H(U_e)H_x\|^2\\
 &+\sum_{x\in V_n}
   \left(m_H^2\|H_x\|^2+\lambda_H\|H_x\|^4\right).
 \end{aligned}\tag{FS.8}\label{eq:SMFS-bosonic-action}
\]

Let \(H_{W,n}(U)\) be a gauge-covariant Hermitian Wilson kernel and assume on a
fixed gauge- and reflection-invariant compact chart \(\mathscr K_n\subseteq
\mathscr B_n\) that
\[
 \boxed{g_*I\preceq |H_{W,n}(U)|\preceq M_*I.}\tag{FS.9}\label{eq:SMFS-Wilson-window}
\]
Put
\[
 \varepsilon_n=\operatorname{sgn}H_{W,n},
 \qquad
 D_{{\rm ov},n}=a_n^{-1}(I+\gamma_5\varepsilon_n),
 \qquad
 \widehat P_{-,n}=\frac12(I+\varepsilon_n).\tag{FS.10}\label{eq:SMFS-overlap}
\]
Let \(\mathscr Y_n(H;Y_u,Y_d,Y_e)\) be the gauge-covariant Yukawa map of
the one-generation packet in \Cref{cor:SMFS-anomaly-quotient}.  On the index-zero sector define the chiral block
\[
 \boxed{
 D_{\chi,n}(U,H,\mathbf Y)
 =P_+D_{{\rm ov},n}(U)\widehat P_{-,n}(U)
  +\mathscr Y_n(H;\mathbf Y).}\tag{FS.11}\label{eq:SMFS-chiral-block}
\]
The target and source determinant lines are understood with the moving source
space \(\Ran\widehat P_{-,n}\).  The protected chiral chart is defined by
\[
 \boxed{s_{\min}(D_{\chi,n})\ge\tau_*>0.}\tag{FS.12}\label{eq:SMFS-chiral-floor}
\]

\begin{theorem}[Same-operator chiral Berezin shell]
\label{thm:SMFS-same-operator-shell}
On the chart \eqref{eq:SMFS-Wilson-window}--\eqref{eq:SMFS-chiral-floor}, the
coordinate-free Berezin section
\[
 \boxed{
 \sigma_n(\varphi)=\operatorname{Det}D_{\chi,n}(\varphi)
 \in
 \det(P_+\mathcal H_n)\otimes
 \det(\widehat P_{-,n}\mathcal H_n)^*}\tag{FS.13}\label{eq:SMFS-Berezin-section}
\]
is nowhere zero and satisfies
\[
 \boxed{\|\sigma_n(\varphi)\|^2
 =\det(D_{\chi,n}^*D_{\chi,n})>0.}\tag{FS.14}\label{eq:SMFS-section-metric}
\]
For every differentiable parameter \(s\),
\[
 \boxed{
 \partial_s\log\|\sigma_n\|^2
 =2\operatorname{Re}\operatorname{Tr}
   (D_{\chi,n}^{-1}\partial_sD_{\chi,n}),}\tag{FS.15}\label{eq:SMFS-Jacobi-first}
\]
and
\[
 \boxed{
 \begin{aligned}
 \partial_s\partial_t\log\|\sigma_n\|^2
 =2\operatorname{Re}\operatorname{Tr}
 \bigl(&D_{\chi,n}^{-1}\partial_{st}D_{\chi,n}\\
 &-D_{\chi,n}^{-1}(\partial_tD_{\chi,n})
  D_{\chi,n}^{-1}(\partial_sD_{\chi,n})\bigr).
 \end{aligned}}\tag{FS.16}\label{eq:SMFS-Jacobi-second}
\]
If the first two operator derivatives are bounded on the compact coefficient
chart, all displayed responses have regulator-independent finite-screen bounds
controlled by \(\tau_*^{-1}\).
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The top exterior power of an invertible linear map is a nonzero element of its
determinant line, and the induced Hermitian metric gives
\(\|\wedge^{\rm top}D\|^2=\det(D^*D)\).  The two derivative formulas are
Jacobi's identity and its derivative.  The singular floor gives
\(\|D^{-1}\|\le\tau_*^{-1}\), so the trace bounds follow from finite internal
rank and the declared derivative bounds.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Gauge descent of the one-generation section]
\label{thm:SMFS-gauge-descent}
Let \(\mathcal G_n=G_{\rm SM}^{V_n}\) be the finite gauge group.  Suppose
\[
 D_{\chi,n}(g\varphi)=U_{-,n}(g,\varphi)
 D_{\chi,n}(\varphi)U_{+,n}(g,\varphi)^{-1}.\tag{FS.17}\label{eq:SMFS-gauge-covariance}
\]
Then the transformation cocycle of \(\sigma_n\) is
\[
 c_n(g,\varphi)
 =\frac{\det U_{-,n}(g,\varphi)}{\det U_{+,n}(g,\varphi)}.\tag{FS.18}\label{eq:SMFS-section-cocycle}
\]
For the complete generation of \Cref{cor:SMFS-anomaly-quotient},
\[
 \boxed{c_n(g,\varphi)=1.}\tag{FS.19}\label{eq:SMFS-section-invariant}
\]
Hence \(\sigma_n\) and its positive metric descend to the protected finite gauge
quotient \(\mathscr K_n/\mathcal G_n\).
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Taking top exterior powers in \eqref{eq:SMFS-gauge-covariance} gives
\eqref{eq:SMFS-section-cocycle}.  The determinant character is the product over
vertices and lattice spin copies of the complete one-generation character.
It is one by the determinant-character statement in
\Cref{cor:SMFS-anomaly-quotient}.  The \(\mathbb Z_6\) quotient
causes no residual character because its generator already acts trivially on
every multiplet.
\end{proof}

% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
\paragraph{The common positive field--reaction cylinder}
\label{subsec:SMFS-common-cylinder}
% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

Let \(d\lambda_n(U,H)\) be product Haar--Lebesgue measure restricted to
\(\mathscr K_n\).  Define the unnormalized field cylinder
\[
 \boxed{
 d\Lambda_{F,n}(\varphi)
 =e^{-S_{B,n}(\varphi)}\|\sigma_n(\varphi)\|^2
  d\lambda_n(\varphi),}\tag{FS.20}\label{eq:SMFS-field-cylinder}
\]
with partition \(Z_{F,n}\) and normalized law \(\nu_n\).  Finiteness and
strict positivity follow from compactness and the chiral floor.  Its absolute
volume growth is retained as a pressure row; no cutoff-independent bound on
\(Z_{F,n}\) itself is assumed.

Partition the local field coordinates into blocks \(i\in I_n\).  Let
\(K_{n,i}\) be conditional expectation under \(\nu_n\) with every coordinate
except block \(i\) frozen, and put
\[
 \mathcal L_n^{\rm fld}=\rho_F\sum_{i\in I_n}(K_{n,i}-I).\tag{FS.21}\label{eq:SMFS-field-heatbath}
\]
For block oscillations \(\delta_iF\), define the Dobrushin matrix by the least
numbers \(c_{ij}^{(n)}\) satisfying
\[
 \delta_j(K_{n,i}F)\le c_{ij}^{(n)}\delta_iF
 \qquad(i\ne j),\tag{FS.22}\label{eq:SMFS-Dobrushin-matrix}
\]
and assume the uniform protected margin
\[
 \boxed{
 \alpha_*:=\sup_n\sup_i\sum_{j\ne i}c_{ij}^{(n)}<1.}\tag{FS.23}\label{eq:SMFS-Dobrushin-margin}
\]

\begin{theorem}[Uniform field gap and influence transport]
\label{thm:SMFS-Dobrushin-gap}
Under \eqref{eq:SMFS-Dobrushin-margin}, the field heat-bath form satisfies
\[
 \boxed{
 -\langle F,\mathcal L_n^{\rm fld}F\rangle_{\nu_n}
 \ge \rho_F(1-\alpha_*)\operatorname{Var}_{\nu_n}(F).}\tag{FS.24}\label{eq:SMFS-field-gap}
\]
Moreover its semigroup \(P_n^{\rm fld}(t)\) obeys
\[
 \boxed{
 \delta(P_n^{\rm fld}(t)F)
 \le e^{-\rho_Ft(I-C_n)}\delta(F)}\tag{FS.25}\label{eq:SMFS-field-influence}
\]
componentwise.  If \(C_n\) has uniformly finite interaction range, this gives a
regulator-independent Poisson-tail light cone.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The heat-bath form is
\[
 -\langle F,\mathcal L_n^{\rm fld}F\rangle
 =\rho_F\sum_i\mathbb E_{\nu_n}\operatorname{Var}(F\mid\mathscr F_{i^c}).
\]
Successive conditional projections and the contraction matrix \(C_n\) give the
approximate tensorization inequality
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_{\nu_n}(F)
 \le(1-\alpha_*)^{-1}
 \sum_i\mathbb E\operatorname{Var}(F\mid\mathscr F_{i^c}).
\]
One proves it by iterating the conditional martingale decomposition; each
unresolved block oscillation is bounded by the geometric series
\(I+C_n+C_n^2+\cdots\), whose row norm is at most
\((1-\alpha_*)^{-1}\).  This gives \eqref{eq:SMFS-field-gap}.

For the influence estimate, apply one heat-bath update during an interval
\(dt\).  The updated oscillation vector is bounded by
\([I-\rho_Fdt(I-C_n)]\delta(F)+o(dt)\).  Iteration and passage to the limit give
\eqref{eq:SMFS-field-influence}.  Finite interaction range bounds the matrix
exponential by the tail of the number of local update steps needed to cross a
given graph distance.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[A directly checkable small-coupling row]
A sufficient finite criterion for \eqref{eq:SMFS-Dobrushin-margin} is obtained by
bounding the oscillation of every mixed local energy.  On the chiral chart,
\eqref{eq:SMFS-Jacobi-second} gives the fermionic contribution
\[
 c_{ij}^{F}
 \le C_r\left(
  \tau_*^{-1}\|\partial_{ij}D_{\chi,n}\|
  +\tau_*^{-2}\|\partial_iD_{\chi,n}\|
                  \|\partial_jD_{\chi,n}\|
 \right).\tag{FS.26}\label{eq:SMFS-fermion-influence}
\]
Adding the plaquette, Higgs-edge, catalyst, and ghost-chart oscillations gives a
finite matrix \(C_n\).  The inequality \(\sup_i\sum_jc_{ij}<1\) is the explicit
small-coupling/admissibility row.  Finite anomaly cancellation does not imply
it.
\end{remark}

Let \(\Pi_{\boldsymbol\lambda}\) be the inherited product-Poisson particle law.  Let
\(a_n(z;\varphi)\) be a gauge-invariant, reflection-even catalytic factor with
\[
 \boxed{0<a_*\le a_n(z;\varphi)\le a^*<\infty.}\tag{FS.27}\label{eq:SMFS-catalyst-window}
\]
Multiply both directions of the inherited pair--dimer reaction at \(z\) by this same
factor, and let the field heat bath act independently between physical jumps.

\begin{theorem}[Literal common reversible field--reaction slab]
\label{thm:SMFS-common-reversible-slab}
The sum of the particle kinetic and renewal generator, the catalysed inherited reaction--mediator generator, and \(\mathcal L_n^{\rm fld}\) is reversible with respect to
\[
 \boxed{
 \mu_n^{\rm com}
 =\Pi_{\boldsymbol\lambda}\otimes\nu_n.}\tag{FS.28}\label{eq:SMFS-common-law}
\]
Its Dirichlet form is closed and satisfies
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal E_n^{\rm com}(F,F)
 \ge g_{48}\operatorname{Var}_{\mu_n^{\rm com}}(F),
 \qquad
 g_{48}=\min\{m_*,\rho_F(1-\alpha_*)\}.}\tag{FS.29}\label{eq:SMFS-common-gap}
\]
For every bounded positive-time path functional \(F\), the stationary two-sided
path law satisfies the exact Osterwalder--Schrader square
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathbf E_n[\overline{F(\Theta\omega)}F(\omega)]
 =\int\left|\mathbf E_n[F\mid\omega_0=x]\right|^2
  d\mu_n^{\rm com}(x)\ge0.}\tag{FS.30}\label{eq:SMFS-Markov-OS}
\]
The inherited charge Green writer and fourth charge cumulant remain unchanged.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Conditional on \(\varphi\), multiplying both reaction orientations by the same
positive factor preserves the inherited detailed-balance measure identity.  The
field heat bath is reversible by construction, and the particle kinetic and
renewal terms are reversible with respect to the Poisson factor.  Their sum is
therefore symmetric on the product law.  Removing the reaction form leaves the
sum of two independent gapped forms, whose gap is the minimum of their two
gaps; adding the nonnegative reaction form cannot reduce it.  The Markov OS
identity is the conditional-independence square of the past and future given
the time-zero state.  The reaction preserves the signed charge, and the field
heat bath acts only on \(\varphi\), so the held-out charge formulas of the inherited reaction--mediator cylinder are
unchanged.
\end{proof}

% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
\paragraph{Ghost quartet and BRST descent}
\label{subsec:SMFS-ghost-BRST}
% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

On a protected gauge-fixing chart let \(L_n(\varphi)\) be a real positive
Faddeev--Popov block.  Introduce a real gauge-fixing variable \(\chi\) and
Grassmann ghosts \((\bar c,c)\).

\begin{theorem}[Exact orientation-positive quartet cancellation]
\label{thm:SMFS-ghost-quartet}
If \(L_n(\varphi)\succ0\), then
\[
 \boxed{
 (2\pi)^{-r_n/2}
 \int d\chi\,d\bar c\,dc\,
 e^{-\frac12\|L_n\chi\|^2-\bar c^{\mathsf T}L_nc}=1.}\tag{FS.31}\label{eq:SMFS-ghost-cancel}
\]
For any parameter derivative, the bosonic gauge-fixing determinant response and
the ghost determinant response cancel after complete quartet assembly.  If a
finite nilpotent BRST derivation \(s_n\) satisfies
\(S_{{\rm gf+gh},n}=s_n\Psi_n\) and the Berezin integral has no boundary term,
then every BRST-exact coefficient direction has zero common partition score.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The Gaussian integral is \((\det L_n)^{-1}\) because \(L_n\) is positive, while
the Grassmann integral is \(\det L_n\).  Their product is one.  Differentiating
this exact identity gives cancellation of every assembled derivative.  BRST
integration by parts gives \(\int s_n(\Psi e^{-S})=0\), which is the vanishing of
the exact-direction score.
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[Gauge chart versus global gauge fixing]
The theorem is a local protected-chart statement.  It does not remove Gribov
or topological gauge-fixing obstructions on a global gauge atlas.  A chart
transition or orientation change is retained as a physical line or component
row.
\end{firewall}

% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
\paragraph{Complete common score and direct-action panels}
\label{subsec:SMFS-score-bank}
% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

Fix a finite physical coefficient bank
\[
 \mathcal E_{48}
 =\mathcal E_g\oplus\mathcal E_H\oplus\mathcal E_Y
  \oplus\mathcal E_{\rm med}\oplus\mathcal E_R
  \oplus\mathcal E_{\rm gh}.\tag{FS.32}\label{eq:SMFS-coefficient-bank}
\]
On a finite path interval \([0,T]\), write \(W_{n,\vartheta}\) for the full
unnormalized cylinder density relative to one fixed reference path law.  It
contains the initial field weight \eqref{eq:SMFS-field-cylinder}, the jump
likelihood of the catalysed reaction, and the quartet factor before its exact
cancellation.  Put
\[
 a_{n,i}=\partial_i\log W_{n,\vartheta}|_0,
 \qquad
 b_{n,ij}=\partial_i\partial_j\log W_{n,\vartheta}|_0,
 \qquad
 s_{n,i}=a_{n,i}-\mathbf E_na_{n,i}.\tag{FS.33}\label{eq:SMFS-scores}
\]

\begin{theorem}[Full same-cylinder Hessian and integrability]
\label{thm:SMFS-full-Hessian}
On every fixed time interval and protected coefficient chart, all first and
second writers in \eqref{eq:SMFS-scores} belong to every finite \(L^p\), with
bounds uniform in \(n\) on each fixed physical source screen.  The exact
partition Hessian is
\[
 \boxed{
 \partial_i\partial_j\log Z_{n,T}(0)
 =\mathbf E_n[b_{n,ij}]
  +\operatorname{Cov}_n(a_{n,i},a_{n,j}).}\tag{FS.34}\label{eq:SMFS-partition-Hessian}
\]
The covariance block is positive semidefinite.  The direct second-action block
is independent and may have either sign.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Field scores are bounded on the compact chart by the bosonic derivative bounds
and \Cref{thm:SMFS-same-operator-shell}.  Finite-time jump scores are compensated
counts with uniformly bounded intensities, hence have moments of every finite
order.  The quartet score cancels after assembly by
\Cref{thm:SMFS-ghost-quartet}.  Differentiating the finite unnormalized path
integral once gives \(\partial_i\log Z=\mathbf E a_i\).  A second derivative
gives the direct expectation plus the covariance.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[A strict Higgs--Yukawa cross writer]
\label{cor:SMFS-strict-HY}
Suppose one real gauge-invariant Higgs writer \(Z\) is nonconstant and the local
fermion factor contains
\[
 g_u(Z)=(m_F^2+uZ^2)^{r_F}.
\]
If the Higgs quartic coefficient \(\lambda\) enters through
\(e^{-\lambda Z^4}\), then
\[
 \boxed{
 \partial_\lambda\partial_u\log Z_{n,T}
 =-r_F\operatorname{Cov}_{n}
 \left(Z^4,\frac{Z^2}{m_F^2+uZ^2}\right)<0.}\tag{FS.35}\label{eq:SMFS-strict-HY}
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The two uncentered scores are \(-Z^4\) and
\(r_FZ^2/(m_F^2+uZ^2)\), with zero mixed direct derivative.  Both functions of
\(Z^2\) are strictly increasing in \(Z^2\), apart from the minus sign in the
first.  The covariance of two strictly increasing functions of a nonconstant
real random variable is positive, by the independent-copy identity
\[
 2\operatorname{Cov}(f(X),g(X))
 =\mathbf E[(f(X)-f(X'))(g(X)-g(X'))].
\]
This proves strict negativity.
\end{proof}

Let \(\mathsf C_n:\mathcal E_{48}\to\operatorname{HS}(\mathcal H_{+,n},
\mathcal H_{-,n})\) be the declared operator synthesis and let
\(\Delta D_{\chi,n}\) be one completely assembled shell or cutoff operator
increment.

\begin{theorem}[Source-minimal field-shell operator birth]
\label{thm:SMFS-operator-birth}
With \(G_n=\mathsf C_n^*\mathsf C_n\), define
\[
 \delta x_n=G_n^\dagger\mathsf C_n^*\Delta D_{\chi,n},
 \qquad
 R_n^{\rm op}=(I-P_{\mathsf C_n})\Delta D_{\chi,n}.\tag{FS.36}\label{eq:SMFS-operator-birth}
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{
 \Delta D_{\chi,n}=\mathsf C_n\delta x_n+R_n^{\rm op},
 \qquad
 \mathsf C_n^*R_n^{\rm op}=0,}\tag{FS.37}\label{eq:SMFS-operator-decomposition}
\]
and
\[
 \boxed{
 \|\Delta D_{\chi,n}\|_{\rm HS}^2
 =\langle\delta x_n,G_n\delta x_n\rangle
  +\|R_n^{\rm op}\|_{\rm HS}^2.}\tag{FS.38}\label{eq:SMFS-operator-Pythagoras}
\]
The polar range of \(R_n^{\rm op}\) is the unique source-minimal new flavour,
mediator, or fermion-operator bank required by this shell.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The Moore--Penrose formula makes
\(P_{\mathsf C_n}=\mathsf C_nG_n^\dagger\mathsf C_n^*\) the orthogonal
projection onto the represented operator range.  Orthogonal decomposition gives
all three identities and the source-minimal polar interpretation.
\end{proof}

% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
\paragraph{Why the marginal ray is not yet licensed}
\label{subsec:SMFS-no-ray}
% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

\begin{countertheorem}[One-shell equilibrium data do not determine the Wilsonian tensor]
\label{cth:SMFS-Hessian-not-beta}
A common unnormalized law, its complete score Gram, and its complete direct
second-action Hessian at one cutoff do not determine the quadratic coefficient
map of a coarse-graining step.
\end{countertheorem}

\begin{proof}
Fix any finite common law and coefficient space \(E\), and let
\(Q:\operatorname{Sym}^2E\to E\) be nonzero.  Define two admissible local
coefficient routers by
\[
 \mathcal R_\pm(x)=x\pm Q(x,x)+O(\|x\|^3).
\]
Use the same unnormalized microscopic cylinder for both and apply the two
routers only after the microscopic law and its derivatives have been acquired.
The base law, every score, and every direct second-action entry are identical,
but the two quadratic Wilsonian tensors are \(\pm Q\).  Therefore no
projective ray, radial coefficient, tangent residual, or beta-form curl is
selected by the one-cutoff equilibrium Hessian.
\end{proof}

\begin{assessment}[Correct numerical boundary of the field-shell construction]
The common-carrier score and direct-action bank is now populated on the
constructed shell.  A physical marginal ray still requires an independently
specified coarse-graining operation and its direct-versus-projected coefficient
panel.  The field-shell construction therefore transports the complete positive localizer and operator
births but does not fit a projective ray from equilibrium data.
\end{assessment}

% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
\paragraph{The gauge quotient line atlas and its remaining connection freedom}
\label{subsec:SMFS-line-atlas}
% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

\begin{theorem}[Gauge-quotient control line]
\label{thm:SMFS-control-line}
The nonzero gauge-invariant section \(\sigma_n\) of
\Cref{thm:SMFS-gauge-descent} trivializes the control determinant line over the
protected finite gauge quotient.  The connection for which \(\sigma_n\) is
parallel is flat and has trivial exponential holonomy.  Every other unitary
connection preserving the same positive metric is uniquely of the form
\[
 \boxed{\nabla_n^{\rm phys}=\nabla_n^{\sigma}+i\eta_n,}\tag{FS.39}\label{eq:SMFS-connection-difference}
\]
where \(\eta_n\) is a real one-form on the quotient.  Its loop holonomy is
\[
 \boxed{
 \operatorname{Hol}_{\gamma}(\nabla_n^{\rm phys})
 =\exp\left(i\int_\gamma\eta_n\right).}\tag{FS.40}\label{eq:SMFS-loop-holonomy}
\]
Thus the control section closes the finite complex line atlas, but the
independently physical connection and its quotient-loop periods remain
separate occurrence data.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
A nowhere-zero global section trivializes a complex line.  Declaring it
parallel defines a flat connection, and parallel transport returns the same
section around every loop.  Two unitary connections on one Hermitian line
differ by an imaginary scalar one-form \(i\eta\) with \(\eta\) real.  Integrating
that difference around a loop gives \eqref{eq:SMFS-loop-holonomy}.
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[Complex line versus real Pfaffian]
The complex one-generation section does not orient an independently physical
real or Majorana Pfaffian line.  A positive doubled modulus and a trivial
complex determinant character do not determine a real orientation cocycle.
The Pfaffian compiler is invoked only when a literal real skew carrier and its
cutoff orientation maps occur.
\end{firewall}

% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
\paragraph{Projective cutoff transport of the common shell}
\label{subsec:SMFS-cutoff}
% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

Let \(J_{n+1/n}\) transport old local field and particle coordinates into the
next cutoff.  For a fixed physical region \(K\) and collar radius \(R\), let
\(\delta_n(K,R)\) bound all transported local bosonic, catalyst, operator,
section, and conditional-kernel differences inside the collar, and let
\(\eta(R)\to0\) bound the common influence tail outside it.

\begin{theorem}[Dobrushin-projective continuum theorem]
\label{thm:SMFS-projective-continuum}
Assume the common margins \eqref{eq:SMFS-Wilson-window},
\eqref{eq:SMFS-chiral-floor}, \eqref{eq:SMFS-Dobrushin-margin}, and
\eqref{eq:SMFS-catalyst-window}.  For every bounded local path writer \(F\)
supported in \(K\),
\[
 \boxed{
 \left|
 \mathbf E_{n+1}[F\circ J_{n+1/n}]-\mathbf E_nF
 \right|
 \le
 \frac{C_F}{1-\alpha_*}
 \bigl(\delta_n(K,R)+\eta(R)\bigr).}\tag{FS.41}\label{eq:SMFS-projective-bound}
\]
The same estimate holds on fixed time windows for the transfer, Green,
connected, score, direct-action, and protected determinant-line writers.
Consequently:
\[
 \boxed{
 \begin{aligned}
 &\delta_n(K,R)\to0\text{ for every fixed }K,R,
 \quad\eta(R)\to0
 &&\Longrightarrow\quad \mathrm{U4},\\
 &\sum_n\bigl(\delta_n(K,R_n)+\eta(R_n)\bigr)<\infty
 &&\Longrightarrow\quad \mathrm{U3}.
 \end{aligned}}\tag{FS.42}\label{eq:SMFS-U3U4}
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Interpolate between the two local specifications one block at a time.  A change
at block \(j\) affects a writer at block \(i\) by the \((i,j)\)-entry of the
resolvent series
\((I-C_n)^{-1}=I+C_n+C_n^2+\cdots\).  Its row sum is at most
\((1-\alpha_*)^{-1}\).  Changes outside the radius-\(R\) collar contribute the
common influence tail.  This proves the static estimate.  Duhamel's formula
and \Cref{thm:SMFS-Dobrushin-gap} give the same bound for fixed-time transfer
writers.  The determinant derivatives are uniformly Lipschitz on the chiral
floor, and the remaining finite score and direct-action writers have the
uniform moments proved in \Cref{thm:SMFS-full-Hessian}.  Ordinary Cauchy
convergence gives \(\mathrm{U4}\); summing the adjacent estimate gives the
canonical \(\mathrm{U3}\) tail.
\end{proof}

% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
\paragraph{Same-action stress and boundary-complete assembly}
\label{subsec:SMFS-boundary}
% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

Let \(h_{ab}\) be the metric on a non-null physical boundary \(\mathscr B\).
Assume the bosonic field action, catalytic reaction form, mediator profile,
chiral operator, and gauge-fixing chart are all differentiated with respect to
one common coframe family.  Denote the resulting assembled boundary stress by
\[
 \boxed{
 T_{48}^{ab}
 =T_{B}^{ab}+T_{R}^{ab}+T_{\rm med}^{ab}
  +T_F^{ab}+T_{\rm gh}^{ab}.}\tag{FS.43}\label{eq:SMFS-total-stress}
\]
The fermion contribution is the same-operator writer
\[
 \boxed{
 T_F[\dot h]
 =-2\operatorname{Re}\operatorname{Tr}
  (D_{\chi}^{-1}\dot D_{\chi}).}\tag{FS.44}\label{eq:SMFS-fermion-stress}
\]
The reaction and mediator terms are the derivatives of the common Dirichlet
form, not the turnover or Fisher rows alone.

\begin{theorem}[Boundary response generated by the common shell]
\label{thm:SMFS-boundary-response}
Suppose \(T_{48}^{ab}\) is a smooth symmetric boundary tensor.  Define
\[
 \boxed{
 K_{48}^{ab}
 =\kappa_E\left(\frac12T_{48}h^{ab}-T_{48}^{ab}\right),
 \qquad T_{48}=h_{ab}T_{48}^{ab}.}\tag{FS.45}\label{eq:SMFS-K-response}
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{
 \Pi_{\rm BY}^{ab}
 =\kappa_E^{-1}(K_{48}^{ab}-K_{48}h^{ab})
 =-T_{48}^{ab}.}\tag{FS.46}\label{eq:SMFS-BY-cancel}
\]
A smooth Gaussian-normal collar realizing this extrinsic curvature exists
locally.  With orthogonal initial and terminal caps, the corner-angle writer is
zero, and the completely assembled first boundary variation vanishes.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
In boundary dimension three, tracing \eqref{eq:SMFS-K-response} gives
\(K_{48}=\kappa_ET_{48}/2\).  Substitution gives
\eqref{eq:SMFS-BY-cancel}.  Choose a smooth collar metric
\[
 g=dn^2+h_{ab}(n,x)dx^adx^b,
 \qquad
 \partial_nh_{ab}|_{n=0}=2K_{48,ab}.
\]
A smooth extension exists for sufficiently small collar width.  The standard
boundary variation is one half of the integral of
\((\Pi_{\rm BY}^{ab}+T_{48}^{ab})\dot h_{ab}\), which vanishes.  Orthogonal caps
have zero boost or corner angle.
\end{proof}

\begin{principle}[Assembly before boundary shorting]
The five terms in \eqref{eq:SMFS-total-stress} are first added as signed writers.
Only the assembled tensor is matched by \eqref{eq:SMFS-K-response}.  Separately
shorting the matter, mediator, fermion, or geometric packets would erase the
router-dispersion and cancellation terms already identified in the earlier
boundary-complete calculus.
\end{principle}

% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
\paragraph{Palatini spectral tail and the remaining bulk row}
\label{subsec:SMFS-Palatini}
% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

Let \(\mathscr V\) be the Hilbert completion of the assembled coframe,
connection, matter-flux, GHY, Brown--York, and corner variation bank.  Let
\(\mathscr L\ge0\) be a compact-resolvent determining operator and
\(P_\Lambda=\mathbf1_{[0,\Lambda]}(\mathscr L)\).  Let \(r_n^{48}\in\mathscr V\)
be the Riesz vector of the complete signed residual after the boundary
assembly of \Cref{thm:SMFS-boundary-response}.

\begin{theorem}[Assembled spectral-tail handoff]
\label{thm:SMFS-Palatini-tail}
If, for some \(\sigma>0\),
\[
 \sup_n\|r_n^{48}\|_{\mathscr V_\sigma}\le M_{48},
 \qquad
 \|P_{\Lambda_n}r_n^{48}\|_{\mathscr V}\le\epsilon_n,\tag{FS.47}\label{eq:SMFS-Palatini-assumptions}
\]
then
\[
 \boxed{
 \|r_n^{48}\|_{\mathscr V}
 \le
 \left[
  \epsilon_n^2+(1+\Lambda_n)^{-\sigma}M_{48}^2
 \right]^{1/2}.}\tag{FS.48}\label{eq:SMFS-Palatini-bound}
\]
Thus \(\epsilon_n\to0\) and \(\Lambda_n\to\infty\) imply the selected weak
Palatini--Einstein--matter equation.  If the regularity bound fails, there are
unit escaping variations \(v_j\) outside growing determining screens with
\[
 \boxed{|\langle r_{n_j}^{48},v_j\rangle|\ge\epsilon_*>0.}\tag{FS.49}\label{eq:SMFS-Palatini-witness}
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The spectral theorem gives
\[
 \|(I-P_\Lambda)r\|_{\mathscr V}
 \le(1+\Lambda)^{-\sigma/2}\|r\|_{\mathscr V_\sigma}.
\]
The two spectral pieces are orthogonal, yielding
\eqref{eq:SMFS-Palatini-bound}.  Failure of uniform tail exhaustion provides a
subsequence with tail norm bounded below; normalizing the tail component gives
\eqref{eq:SMFS-Palatini-witness}.
\end{proof}

\begin{assessment}[Exact Palatini status]
The field-shell construction populates the same-action boundary stress and a responding Brown--York
collar.  The complete bulk conclusion remains conditional on the finite-screen
residual and the assembled regularity bound in
\eqref{eq:SMFS-Palatini-assumptions}.  Neither the positive field shell nor the
boundary cancellation manufactures those bulk rows.
\end{assessment}

\paragraph{Terminating alternative and revised ledger}
\label{subsec:SMFS-ledger}
% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

\begin{theorem}[Finite field-shell alternative]
\label{thm:SMFS-master}
For the protected one-generation field shell, the following
compiler terminates.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(S\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item Test the \(\mathbb Z_6\) incidence, local anomaly sums, weak-doublet parity,
      and connected determinant character.
\item Test the Wilson and chiral floors.  Failure returns a Wilson divisor, a
      chiral zero, or a normalized singular vector.
\item Test the Dobrushin margin and catalyst window.  Failure returns a local
      influence or clock witness.
\item Construct the common reversible path law and test its field, reaction,
      Green, connected, and OS writers.
\item Assemble the ghost quartet and pass to BRST cohomology before retaining any
      physical score direction.
\item Acquire every score and direct second-action block and append every
      orthogonal operator birth.
\item Do not evaluate a projective marginal ray without an independently loaded
      coarse-graining map and direct coefficient panel.
\item Descend the same-operator Berezin section to the finite gauge quotient;
      retain any independently physical connection or Pfaffian difference.
\item Differentiate the same common action, assemble the signed boundary packet,
      and only then construct the Brown--York response.
\item Run the Palatini spectral-tail theorem only after the finite determining
      screen and regularity rows are populated.
\end{enumerate}
The positive output is one literal finite anomaly-free
field--reaction--mediator--fermion shell with a common positive law, reflected
path dynamics, gauge-descended control line, complete local score bank, and
boundary response.  The negative outputs are explicit anomaly, divisor,
influence, clock, BRST, operator-birth, line, boundary, Palatini, or cutoff
witnesses.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The representation gate is \Cref{cor:SMFS-anomaly-quotient}.  The field,
section, and line rows are
\Cref{thm:SMFS-same-operator-shell,thm:SMFS-gauge-descent,thm:SMFS-control-line}.
The positive dynamics and uniformity rows are
\Cref{thm:SMFS-Dobrushin-gap,thm:SMFS-common-reversible-slab,thm:SMFS-projective-continuum}.
The score and operator rows are
\Cref{thm:SMFS-ghost-quartet,thm:SMFS-full-Hessian,thm:SMFS-operator-birth}; the
ray obstruction is \Cref{cth:SMFS-Hessian-not-beta}.  Boundary and bulk rows are
\Cref{thm:SMFS-boundary-response,thm:SMFS-Palatini-tail}.  Every stage either
passes the displayed zero or positive margin or returns its displayed witness.
\end{proof}


\subsection{A projective full-coupling reflected Renewal regulator}
\label{sec:RPESM-regulator}

The finite field shell above proves that the active Standard-Model packet is
nonempty on a protected chart.  It does not by itself exhibit one nested
unbounded full-coupling law carrying the complete source, reflection, line,
locality, stress, and held-out rows at every cutoff.  The following construction
supplies that existential object.  Its role is to close finite packet
population, not to identify the old Store or to prove the continuum limit.

\begin{principle}[Regulator existence versus historical reuse]
\label{prin:RPESM-existence-reuse}
Let \(\mathsf E_n\) denote existence of one literal Renewal regulator carrying
the declared finite packet at cutoff \(n\), and let
\(\mathsf H_n(\mathsf P_n^{\rm old})\) denote existence of such a packet as a
same-history refinement of a preassigned historical Store.  Then
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathsf H_n(\mathsf P_n^{\rm old})\Longrightarrow\mathsf E_n,}
 \tag{RP.1}
\]
but the converse need not hold.  Historical reuse adds equality of the
forgetful old marginal and is therefore a strictly stronger economy statement.
Its failure cannot revoke an independently constructed existential regulator.
\end{principle}

\begin{definition}[Relational projective Einstein--Standard-Model cutoff]
\label{def:RPESM-cutoff}
Let \(d_n\uparrow\infty\), \(h_n=d_n^{-1}\), and
\[
 \Sigma_n=\Lambda_{A_3}/d_n\Lambda_{A_3},
 \qquad
 X_n=I_n\times\Sigma_n,
 \qquad
 I_n=\{-M_n,\ldots,M_n\}\delta t_n.
 \tag{RP.2}
\]
On the twelve oriented \(A_3\) roots let the fast scheduler have reference
rates
\[
 \boxed{k_{\alpha,n}=\frac1{8h_n^2}.}
 \tag{RP.3}
\]
The winner--waiting record and unit speed density then give
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal B_n=I_3,
 \qquad \mathsf N_n=1,
 \qquad \beta_n=0,}
 \tag{RP.4}
\]
while an open positive rate/speed chart supplies the full ten-dimensional ADM
tangent.  Coframe, connection, volume, and curvature writers are deterministic
functions of these scheduler coordinates.

Let
\[
 G_{\rm SM}=\frac{SU(3)\times SU(2)\times U(1)}{\mathbb Z_6}
\]
and let the bosonic record contain the link field \(U\), an unbounded Higgs
field \(H\), scheduler and derived geometric variables, gauge-fixing
auxiliaries, mediator/route data, and the physical boundary record.  The
fermion--ghost super-record contains one anomaly-free generation, a chiral
Dirac--Yukawa coefficient \(D_{\chi,n}\), a real skew coefficient \(A_n^M\),
and the assembled ghost quartet.  On the scheduler-derived geometry choose one
finite-range reflection-even common action
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 S_{B,n}={}&S_{g,n}+S_{{\rm YM},n}+S_{H,n}+S_{{\rm gf},n}
             +S_{{\rm med},n}+S_{{\rm ct},n},
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{RP.5}
\]
whose Higgs part contains \(\lambda_4\sum_x|H_x|^4\) with \(\lambda_4>0\),
whose remaining negative parts are dominated by this quartic term, and whose
declared sectors have nonzero mixed local couplings.  Retain the complex and
real line sections
\[
 \sigma_n=\det D_{\chi,n},
 \qquad p_n=\operatorname{Pf}A_n^M,
 \tag{RP.6}
\]
together with their divisors, kernels, transport, and orientations.  Choose
nonzero massive reflection-positive control sections
\(\sigma_n^+\) and \(p_n^+\) of the corresponding complex and real lines.
Their positive modulus gives the unnormalized cylinder
\[
 \boxed{
 \dd\Lambda_n^+
 =e^{-S_{B,n}}\,\|\sigma_n^+\|^2|p_n^+|^2\,\dd\lambda_n,}
 \tag{RP.7}
\]
and \(\mu_n=Z_n^{-1}\Lambda_n^+\).  The positive modulus in
\textup{(RP.7)} does not replace the marked determinant or Pfaffian line.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Normalizable stationary reflected Markov--Renewal slab]
\label{thm:RPESM-reflected-slab}
There is a nonempty open set of nonzero mixed coefficients for which
\(0<Z_n<\infty\) at every cutoff and every fixed-support polynomial field,
action, score, current, stress, zero-mode, and line-norm writer belongs to
\(L^{1+\eta}(\mu_n)\) for some \(\eta>0\).  Let \(R_nf=\int f\,\dd\mu_n\), let
\(L_n^{\rm loc}\) be a finite sum of local conditional-expectation generators
reversible with respect to \(\mu_n\), and fix \(\rho>0\).  Then
\[
 \boxed{L_n=\rho(R_n-I)+L_n^{\rm loc}}
 \tag{RP.8}
\]
is self-adjoint and nonpositive on \(L^2(\mu_n)\), and on centered writers
\[
 \boxed{-L_n\succeq\rho I.}
 \tag{RP.9}
\]
It defines a stationary two-sided c\`adl\`ag path law with physical Poisson
duration.  If \(\Theta_n\) reverses time and applies the declared field
reflection, then every bounded positive-time writer satisfies
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathbb E_n\!\left[\overline{F(\Theta_n\omega)}F(\omega)\right]
 =\int\left|\mathbb E_n[F\mid\omega_0=x]\right|^2\dd\mu_n(x)\ge0.}
 \tag{RP.10}
\]
The centered Green operator
\[
 G_n=Q_n(-L_n)^{-1}Q_n,
 \qquad Q_n=I-|1\rangle\langle1|,
\]
obeys \(0\preceq G_n\preceq\rho^{-1}Q_n\).  If one nonseparable mixed action
writer is nonconstant with nonzero coefficient, the common score Hessian and
conditional updates have a nonzero cross-sector response, so the slab is not a
product of its sector marginals.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The compact gauge, scheduler, route, and boundary variables have finite volume,
while the quartic Higgs term controls every lower-order finite-range
interaction.  Finite determinant and Pfaffian factors have polynomial growth,
so the same coercive integral gives the stated moments.  Conditional
expectation is an orthogonal projection on \(L^2(\mu_n)\); hence every local
summand is self-adjoint and nonpositive.  On centered functions \(R_nf=0\), so
the refresh contributes exactly \(\rho\|f\|^2\) to the Dirichlet form.
Reversibility gives conditional independence of past and future at time zero,
which is \textup{(RP.10)}, and the spectral theorem gives the Green bound.
\end{proof}

One physical event of this regulator is the point-readable tuple
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathfrak p_{n,k}
 =(Z_{n,k},\Gamma_{n,k},O_{n,k},\Xi_{n,k},Z_{n,k+1}),}
 \tag{RP.11}
\]
where \(Z\) is the future-minimal full-field state, \(\Gamma\) is the fast
root winner--waiting path, \(O\) is the retained Store/renewal route, and
\(\Xi\) contains initial and terminal fields, update/reverse labels, action
increment, duration, locality and boundary routes, Green/source marks,
stress/current responses, determinant transport, Pfaffian sign, and calibration
marks.  Forgetting the additional coordinates gives the chosen marginal of
this regulator, which need not be the historical Store.

\begin{theorem}[Exact projective shell, dynamic, and line transport]
\label{thm:RPESM-projective-transport}
Let \(x\) be an old field, \(y\) a new detail, and let
\(\kappa_{n+1/n}(\dd y\mid x)\) be a reflection-covariant reference kernel.
For a nonconstant finite-range interaction \(V_{n+1/n}(x,y)\), define
\[
 Z_{n+1/n}(x)
 =\int e^{-V_{n+1/n}(x,y)}\kappa_{n+1/n}(\dd y\mid x),
\]
\[
 K_{n+1/n}(\dd y\mid x)
 =Z_{n+1/n}(x)^{-1}e^{-V_{n+1/n}(x,y)}
   \kappa_{n+1/n}(\dd y\mid x),
\]
and
\[
 \boxed{
 \Lambda_{n+1}^+(\dd x,\dd y)
 =\Lambda_n^+(\dd x)K_{n+1/n}(\dd y\mid x).}
 \tag{RP.12}
\]
Then \((\pi_{n+1/n})_*\Lambda_{n+1}^+=\Lambda_n^+\) and
\((\pi_{n+1/n})_*\mu_{n+1}=\mu_n\), while the conditional detail is genuinely
coupled exactly when the normalized kernel
\(K_{n+1/n}(\mathord\cdot\mid x)\) varies with \(x\).  In particular this holds
when the Boltzmann weight is nonseparable relative to the reference kernel;
mere additive dependence \(V(x,y)=a(x)+b(y)\) is not sufficient.  The shell term
\(+\log Z_{n+1/n}(x)\) transports every old-supported first and second action
writer.

If \(P_n\) is a reversible one-step kernel for the old slab, the fine skeleton
\[
 P_{n+1}((x,y),\dd(x',y'))
 =P_n(x,\dd x')K_{n+1/n}(\dd y'\mid x')
 \tag{RP.13}
\]
is reversible with respect to \(\mu_{n+1}\) and satisfies
\[
 \boxed{
 P_{n+1}(f\circ\pi_{n+1/n})
 =(P_nf)\circ\pi_{n+1/n}.}
 \tag{RP.14}
\]
Thus the old path, clock, reflection, source, and Green rows transport exactly.

Finally, choose invertible detail chiral and real-skew blocks \(E_n,B_n\) and
local reflection-covariant determinant-one triangular/congruence maps so that
\[
 D_{\chi,n+1}=\mathsf L_n(D_{\chi,n}\oplus E_n)\mathsf R_n,
 \qquad
 A_{n+1}^M=\mathsf Q_n^{\mathsf T}(A_n^M\oplus B_n)\mathsf Q_n.
 \tag{RP.15}
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{
 \det D_{\chi,n+1}
 =\det D_{\chi,n}\det E_n,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Pf}A_{n+1}^M
 =\operatorname{Pf}A_n^M\operatorname{Pf}B_n.}
 \tag{RP.16}
\]
Kernels, cokernels, divisor orders, complex transports, real orientations, and
crossing parities are carried exactly.  A separately retained direct two-shell
stream tests the composed conditional kernel without entering either one-shell
fit.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The static marginal is the normalization of \(K_{n+1/n}\); genuine coupling is
exactly nonconstancy of that normalized conditional in the old field.  Differentiating
that normalization once and twice gives exactly the conditional score and
covariance terms supplied by the shell counterterm.  The stationary edge
measure of \textup{(RP.13)} is symmetric because the old edge measure is
symmetric and the two detail factors are exchanged together.  Integration over
\(y'\) proves the intertwining identity.  Determinant one and block triangularity
give \textup{(RP.16)}; invertibility transports kernels and cokernels, and
orders and real crossing parities add under products.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Population-complete finite full-coupling packet]
\label{thm:RPESM-population}
Freeze any finite word, source, deformation, locality, connected, line,
operator, and held-out grammar.  At every cutoff the regulator of
\Cref{def:RPESM-cutoff,thm:RPESM-reflected-slab,thm:RPESM-projective-transport}
places on the single event law \textup{(RP.11)}:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(P\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item the relational state, physical clock, scheduler-derived ADM packet,
      full bosonic/fermionic/ghost record, and common unnormalized cylinder;
\item physical reflection, positive conditional exterior kernels, a direct
      held-out higher fermion word, and zero-safe determinant/Pfaffian data;
\item local, collar, global-refresh, boundary, unresolved, and independently
      held-out split-route panels;
\item direct Green Grams, pair/triple/four-body connected words, and
      Wick/Pfaffian excesses;
\item one-action Ward, BRST, current, stress, contact, energy--Hamiltonian,
      absolute-pressure, direct second-action, and boundary-assembled variation
      rows;
\item exact adjacent static, dynamic, source, line, zero-mode, and held-out
      two-shell transport.
\end{enumerate}
Consequently the finite packet is population complete for the universal
uniform-continuum, Osterwalder--Schrader, determinant/Pfaffian, and coupled
Einstein--Standard-Model compilers.  The complete old-supported packet
transports exactly across adjacent cutoffs.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Every listed object is either a deterministic writer, a conditional law, a
direct mark, or a finite derivative of the one cylinder \textup{(RP.7)} and one
path law \textup{(RP.8)}.  Positivity and Green control are
\Cref{thm:RPESM-reflected-slab}; locality and connected rows are direct
route-resolved expectations; Ward and stress rows are derivatives of the one
common action; and all cutoff statements are
\Cref{thm:RPESM-projective-transport}.  Hence no relative source orientation or
cross-history coupling is fitted after the event law is fixed.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Optional historical-reuse residual]
\label{def:RPESM-reuse-residual}
If a historical Store manifest is later supplied, let \(Y_n^{\rm old}\) and
\(Y_n^{\rm RP}\) synthesize the complete target-relative historical and
forgetful-regulator writers, and let \(N_n\) contain the certified relabelling
and nuisance sources.  The positive residual
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathbb C_n^{\rm reuse}
 =(Y_n^{\rm old}-Y_n^{\rm RP})^*(I-P_{N_n})
  (Y_n^{\rm old}-Y_n^{\rm RP})}
 \tag{RP.17}
\]
vanishes exactly when one common nuisance/relabeling representative identifies
the two populated target packets.  Its polar range is otherwise the
source-minimal historical mismatch.  Either outcome leaves
\Cref{thm:RPESM-population} unchanged.
\end{definition}

\begin{firewall}[Finite population is not the interacting continuum]
\label{fire:RPESM-scope}
The regulator above is a literal mathematical Renewal history and closes the
finite existential population question.  It is not asserted to be nature's
regulator or the historical Store.  Exact projectivity does not by itself prove
regulator removal, uniform locality, nuclearity, split, clustering, a mass gap,
full determinant/Pfaffian holonomy on field space, observed couplings, running,
matching, Lorentzian reconstruction, scattering completeness, or the
interacting Einstein--Standard-Model continuum.  Those are now quantitative
and selection questions on a named populated sequence rather than missing
finite existence premises.
\end{firewall}


\subsection{The internal SM--spacetime commutant duality}
\label{sec:SMST-duality}
% =============================================================================

The exact duality is not an equality between the spacetime Clifford algebra and
the Standard-Model gauge algebra.  A reducible typed gauge representation
cannot generally be the full commutant of the external matrix factor.  The
correct dual pair is the joint typed action algebra and the residual
multiplicity algebra.  Equivalently, on one common multiplicity fibre, the
surviving typed multiplicity algebra is the commutant of the Yukawa/incidence
polar metric--holonomy algebra.

\begin{theorem}[Factor-commutant obstruction]
\label{thm:SMST-factor-obstruction}
Let a unital copy of $M_n(\C)$ act on a finite-dimensional Hilbert space
$\mathcal H$.  Then
\[
 \mathcal H\cong\C^n\otimes\mathcal K,
 \qquad
 M_n(\C)=M_n(\C)\otimes I_{\mathcal K},
 \qquad
 M_n(\C)'=I_n\otimes\mathcal B(\mathcal K).
\]
Consequently a reducible internal algebra with nontrivial centre, or with a
nontrivial multiplicity commutant, cannot equal the full commutant of the
external factor.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Every finite-dimensional unital representation of the simple algebra
$M_n(\C)$ is a direct sum of copies of its defining representation, giving
$\mathcal H\cong\C^n\otimes\mathcal K$.  An operator commutes with every matrix
unit on the first factor exactly when it is the identity there and arbitrary
on $\mathcal K$.  The full commutant is therefore a simple matrix algebra.  A
reducible internal algebra has either more than one central block or a
non-scalar multiplicity commutant, and hence is a proper subalgebra of that
simple commutant.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[External--internal--multiplicity decomposition]
\label{thm:SMST-trinity}
Let $\mathcal A_{\rm ext}\cong M_n(\C)$ and let
$\mathcal A_{\rm int}$ be a commuting finite-dimensional unital $C^*$-algebra
on $\mathcal H$.  Then there are spaces $V_\lambda,M_\lambda$ such that
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal H\cong
 \bigoplus_{\lambda\in\Lambda}
 \C^n\otimes V_\lambda\otimes M_\lambda,}
\]
\[
 \mathcal A_{\rm int}
 =\bigoplus_\lambda
 I_n\otimes\mathcal B(V_\lambda)\otimes I_{M_\lambda}.
\]
For
$\mathcal C=C^*(\mathcal A_{\rm ext},\mathcal A_{\rm int})$ one has
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal C=
 \bigoplus_\lambda
 \mathcal B(\C^n\otimes V_\lambda)\otimes I_{M_\lambda},}
\]
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal C'=
 \bigoplus_\lambda
 I_{\C^n\otimes V_\lambda}\otimes\mathcal B(M_\lambda),
 \qquad
 \mathcal C''=\mathcal C.}
\]
Thus the residual factors $M_\lambda$, rather than the raw internal gauge
algebra, carry generation and flavour multiplicity.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Apply \Cref{thm:SMST-factor-obstruction} to write
$\mathcal H=\C^n\otimes\mathcal K$ and
$\mathcal A_{\rm int}=I_n\otimes\widetilde{\mathcal A}_{\rm int}$.  The finite
representation theorem gives
\[
 \mathcal K\cong\bigoplus_\lambda V_\lambda\otimes M_\lambda,
 \qquad
 \widetilde{\mathcal A}_{\rm int}
 =\bigoplus_\lambda\mathcal B(V_\lambda)\otimes I_{M_\lambda}.
\]
The minimal central projections of the internal algebra belong to the joint
algebra.  On each central block the two commuting full matrix factors generate
$\mathcal B(\C^n\otimes V_\lambda)$.  An operator commuting with that full
matrix algebra is the identity on the first two factors and arbitrary on
$M_\lambda$; central projections prevent off-diagonal maps between different
$\lambda$ blocks.  This gives the commutant formula.  Applying the same
calculation to the commutant gives the bicommutant identity.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Typed multiplicity graph and residual algebra]
\label{def:typed-multiplicity-graph}
For a joint packet as in \Cref{def:SMST-packet}, let
$\Gamma_X=(\Lambda_X,E_X)$ be the graph of retained incidence histories.  The
\emph{typed multiplicity algebra} is the algebra of families
\[
 R=(R_\lambda)_{\lambda\in\Lambda_X},
 \qquad R_\lambda\in\mathcal B(M_{\lambda,X}),
\]
satisfying, for every $e:\lambda\to\mu$,
\[
 \boxed{
 R_\mu F_e=F_eR_\lambda,
 \qquad
 R_\lambda F_e^*=F_e^*R_\mu.}
\]
It is represented globally by
$\bigoplus_\lambda I_{\C^4\otimes V_\lambda}\otimes R_\lambda$ and is denoted
$\mathcal M_{{\rm type},X}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Multiplicity-one incidence factorization]
\label{lem:SMST-multiplicity-factorization}
Suppose the external--internal symmetry acts trivially on
$M_\lambda,M_\mu$ and the typed carrier-intertwiner space for an edge
$e:\lambda\to\mu$ is one dimensional, spanned by a nonzero $D_e$.  Then every
equivariant loaded incidence map has a unique factorization
\[
 \boxed{Y_e=D_e\otimes F_e.}
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Triviality on the multiplicity factors gives
\[
 \Hom_{\rm typed}
 ((\C^4\otimes V_\lambda)\otimes M_\lambda,
  (\C^4\otimes V_\mu)\otimes M_\mu)
 \cong
 \Hom_{\rm typed}(\C^4\otimes V_\lambda,
                  \C^4\otimes V_\mu)
 \otimes\Hom(M_\lambda,M_\mu).
\]
The first factor is the line $\C D_e$, proving existence and uniqueness of
$F_e$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Exact edge-commutant reconstruction]
\label{thm:SMST-edge-commutant}
For the joint action algebra
$\mathcal A_{\rm act}=C^*(\mathcal A_{\rm ext},\mathcal A_{\rm int},
Y_e,Y_e^*:e\in E)$,
\[
 \boxed{\mathcal A_{\rm act}'=\mathcal M_{\rm type}.}
\]
In particular, if the incidence graph is connected and every $F_e$ is
invertible, all multiplicity spaces have one common dimension $g$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
By \Cref{thm:SMST-trinity}, an operator commuting with the external and
internal algebras has the form
$X=\bigoplus_\lambda I_{\C^4\otimes V_\lambda}\otimes R_\lambda$.
For $Y_e=D_e\otimes F_e$,
\[
 XY_e-Y_eX
 =D_e\otimes(R_\mu F_e-F_eR_\lambda),
\]
and the commutator with $Y_e^*$ is
\[
 D_e^*\otimes(R_\lambda F_e^*-F_e^*R_\mu).
\]
Because $D_e\ne0$, each tensor product vanishes exactly when its multiplicity
factor vanishes.  Thus the commutant equations are precisely those in
\Cref{def:typed-multiplicity-graph}.  If $F_e$ is invertible, its two endpoint
spaces have equal dimension; connectedness propagates this equality through
the graph.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Singular polar-edge equivalence]
\label{lem:SMST-polar-edge}
Let $F:E\to H$ have polar decomposition $F=UP$, where
$P=(F^*F)^{1/2}$, $p=U^*U=\supp P$, and
$q=UU^*=\supp(FF^*)$.  For $R_E\in\mathcal B(E)$ and
$R_H\in\mathcal B(H)$, the equations
\[
 R_HF=FR_E,
 \qquad
 R_EF^*=F^*R_H
\]
are equivalent to
\[
 \boxed{
 [R_E,P^2]=0,
 \qquad
 R_HU=UR_E,
 \qquad
 R_EU^*=U^*R_H.}
\]
On either branch,
\[
 [R_E,p]=0,
 \qquad [R_H,q]=0,
 \qquad [R_H,UP^2U^*]=0.
\]
No invertibility or equality of the source and target dimensions is required.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
The two incidence equations imply
\[
 F^*R_HF=F^*FR_E=R_EF^*F,
\]
so $[R_E,P^2]=0$; the target-side calculation gives
$[R_H,FF^*]=0$.  Functional calculus gives commutation with $p$ and $q$.
Writing the first incidence equation as
$R_HUP=UR_EP$ and multiplying by $P^\dagger$ gives
$R_HU=UR_E$ on the supported source; both sides vanish on its orthogonal
complement.  The adjoint equation gives the reverse transport identity.
Conversely, functional calculus gives $[R_E,P]=0$, and the three displayed
conditions directly recover the two incidence equations.  Conjugating the
metric commutator by $U$ gives the final target identity.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Support-polar multiplicity action algebra]
\label{def:SMST-support-polar-algebra}
On the total multiplicity carrier
\[
 \mathscr M_X=\bigoplus_{\lambda\in\Lambda_X}M_{\lambda,X},
\]
let $Z_\lambda$ be the vertex projections.  For each incidence map
$F_e:M_{s(e),X}\to M_{t(e),X}$ write
$F_e=U_e(F_e^*F_e)^{1/2}$ and define
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal O_{F,X}^{\rm sup}
 :=C^*(Z_\lambda,F_e^*F_e,U_e,U_e^*: \lambda,e)
 \subseteq\mathcal B(\mathscr M_X).}
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Exact support-polar commutant]
\label{thm:SMST-support-polar-commutant}
For arbitrary rectangular, singular, rank-deficient, or zero incidence maps,
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal M_{{\rm type},X}
 =\bigl(\mathcal O_{F,X}^{\rm sup}\bigr)',
 \qquad
 \mathcal O_{F,X}^{\rm sup}
 =\mathcal M_{{\rm type},X}'.}
\]
Moreover,
\[
 \boxed{
 C^*(Z_\lambda,F_e,F_e^*: \lambda,e)
 =\mathcal O_{F,X}^{\rm sup}.}
\]
Thus support projections, positive support metrics, and polar partial
isometries add no finite loading; they are exact functional-calculus outputs of
the original incidence maps.  A zero singular value remains an explicit
support boundary rather than being completed by an inverse residue map.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Commutation with the vertex projections makes an operator block diagonal.
Commutation with $F_e^*F_e$, $U_e$, and $U_e^*$ is exactly the three-condition
form of \Cref{lem:SMST-polar-edge}, hence exactly the two incidence
intertwining equations defining $\mathcal M_{{\rm type},X}$.  The reverse
commutant equality is finite bicommutant closure.

For the algebra identity, $F_e^*F_e$ belongs to the incidence algebra.  On its
finite spectrum, interpolate the function $g(0)=0$ and
$g(t)=t^{-1/2}$ for $t>0$ by a polynomial.  Then
$U_e=F_eg(F_e^*F_e)$ belongs to the incidence algebra.  Conversely
$F_e=U_e(F_e^*F_e)^{1/2}$, proving equality.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Residue support algebra and multiplicity quiver]
\label{def:SMST-multiplicity-quiver}
Put
\[
 p_e=\supp(F_e^*F_e),
 \qquad q_e=\supp(F_eF_e^*),
 \qquad
 \mathcal S_{F,X}=C^*(Z_\lambda,p_e,q_e: \lambda,e).
\]
Its canonical central multiplicity decomposition is
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathscr M_X\cong\bigoplus_{a\in\mathfrak A_X}V_{a,X}\otimes N_{a,X},}
\]
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal S_{F,X}
 =\bigoplus_a\mathcal B(V_{a,X})\otimes I_{N_{a,X}},
 \qquad
 \mathcal S_{F,X}'
 =\bigoplus_a I_{V_{a,X}}\otimes\mathcal B(N_{a,X}).}
\]
Let $\bm T_X$ be any finite $*$-closed family of further reconstructed
support metrics, polar arrows, cycle products, or action generators.  For a
block
$T_{ba}:V_a\otimes N_a\to V_b\otimes N_b$, define its basis-free multiplicity
slice space by
\[
 \mathfrak B_{ba}(T)
 :=\{(\varphi\otimes\id)(T_{ba}):
       \varphi\in\mathcal B(V_a,V_b)^*\}
 \subseteq\mathcal B(N_a,N_b).
\]
The multiplicity quiver $\mathfrak Q_{F,X}(\bm T_X)$ has vertex spaces $N_a$
and arrow spaces
$\mathfrak B_{ba}=\Span_{T\in\bm T_X}\mathfrak B_{ba}(T)$.  Its endomorphism
algebra is
\[
 \boxed{
 \End\mathfrak Q_{F,X}
 =\{(X_a)_a:X_bB=BX_a
   \text{ for every }B\in\mathfrak B_{ba}\}.}
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Noncommuting-support multiplicity-quiver theorem]
\label{thm:SMST-quiver-commutant}
For the packet of \Cref{def:SMST-multiplicity-quiver},
\[
 \boxed{
 C^*(\mathcal S_{F,X},\bm T_X)'
 \cong\End\mathfrak Q_{F,X}.}
\]
If
$(T_j)_{ba}=\sum_\alpha E_\alpha^{ba}\otimes B_{j,\alpha}^{ba}$ in a
Hilbert--Schmidt orthonormal basis of $\mathcal B(V_a,V_b)$, then the
restriction of the ambient commutator form to $\mathcal S_{F,X}'$ is
\[
 \boxed{
 q_{\bm T_X}[(X_a)]
 =\frac1{\dim\mathscr M_X}
   \sum_{j,b,a,\alpha}
   \|B_{j,\alpha}^{ba}X_a-X_bB_{j,\alpha}^{ba}\|_{\HS}^2.}
\]
Its kernel is exactly $\End\mathfrak Q_{F,X}$.  Hence the first positive
quiver eigenvalue is a finite coercive certificate for the absence of
additional flavour/generation endomorphisms.  The construction is unique up
to permutation of central blocks and vertexwise unitary gauge.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
An operator commuting with $\mathcal S_{F,X}$ has the form
$\bigoplus_aI_{V_a}\otimes X_a$.  Expanding one block of each $T_j$ gives
\[
 (I\otimes X_b)(T_j)_{ba}-(T_j)_{ba}(I\otimes X_a)
 =\sum_\alpha E_\alpha^{ba}\otimes
   (X_bB_{j,\alpha}^{ba}-B_{j,\alpha}^{ba}X_a).
\]
Linear independence proves the quiver intertwining equations.  Orthogonality
of the $E_\alpha^{ba}$ gives the displayed positive form and its kernel.
Finite-dimensional representation uniqueness gives the stated gauge
independence.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Polar metric--holonomy commutant theorem]
\label{thm:SMST-polar-holonomy}
Assume the typed multiplicity graph is connected, every multiplicity space has
common dimension $g$, and each edge transport is invertible.  Write
\[
 F_e=U_eP_e,
 \qquad U_e\in U(g),
 \qquad P_e\succ0.
\]
Choose a root $o$ and a spanning tree.  Let
$Q_\lambda:M_o\to M_\lambda$ be the ordered product of the unitary factors
along the tree path, using $U_e^*$ for a reversed edge.  For
$e:\lambda\to\mu$ define on the root fibre
\[
 K_e:=Q_\lambda^*P_e^2Q_\lambda,
 \qquad
 W_e:=Q_\mu^*U_eQ_\lambda,
\]
and put
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal O_{F,X}:=C^*(K_e,W_e:e\in E_X)\subseteq M_g(\C).}
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal M_{{\rm type},X}\cong\mathcal O_{F,X}',}
\]
where $R\in\mathcal O_{F,X}'$ corresponds to the parallel family
\[
 \boxed{R_\lambda=Q_\lambda RQ_\lambda^*.}
\]
Consequently
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal O_{F,X}'=\mathcal M_{{\rm type},X}^{(o)},
 \qquad
 (\mathcal M_{{\rm type},X}^{(o)})'=\mathcal O_{F,X},}
\]
on the root multiplicity fibre.  Thus the typed multiplicity algebra and the
Yukawa/incidence polar metric--holonomy algebra reconstruct one another by a
finite commutant calculation.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
By \Cref{thm:SMST-edge-commutant,lem:SMST-polar-edge}, a residual family
satisfies on every edge
\[
 [R_\lambda,P_e^2]=0,
 \qquad R_\mu=U_eR_\lambda U_e^*.
\]
Along the chosen spanning tree, the second relation forces
$R_\lambda=Q_\lambda RQ_\lambda^*$ from the root value $R=R_o$.  The metric
condition becomes
\[
 [R,Q_\lambda^*P_e^2Q_\lambda]=[R,K_e]=0.
\]
For a non-tree edge, consistency between the tree transport and the direct
unitary edge transport is equivalent to
\[
 [R,Q_\mu^*U_eQ_\lambda]=[R,W_e]=0.
\]
Hence a residual family is determined exactly by one root operator commuting
with every generator of $\mathcal O_{F,X}$.  Conversely any such root operator
defines a family satisfying all edge and adjoint-edge equations.  These maps
are inverse unital $*$-homomorphisms.  Finally, every finite-dimensional unital
$C^*$-algebra equals its bicommutant, so
$(\mathcal O_{F,X}')'=\mathcal O_{F,X}$.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Flat and irreducible limits]
\label{cor:SMST-polar-extremes}
Under \Cref{thm:SMST-polar-holonomy}:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2.8em]
\item $\mathcal M_{{\rm type},X}^{(o)}=M_g(\C)$ exactly when every generator
      $K_e,W_e$ is scalar;
\item $\mathcal M_{{\rm type},X}^{(o)}=\C I$ exactly when
      $\mathcal O_{F,X}=M_g(\C)$;
\item if all $F_e$ are unitary, then $K_e=I$ and the obstruction reduces to
      relative-cycle unitary holonomy;
\item even on a tree, a non-scalar positive polar metric can reduce the
      residual multiplicity algebra.
\end{enumerate}
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The commutant of a set is all of $M_g(\C)$ exactly when the set is contained in
the centre.  A finite unital algebra has scalar commutant exactly when it is
$M_g(\C)$.  If $F_e$ is unitary, $P_e=I$.  The final statement follows because
$K_e$ remains among the generators even when there are no cycle holonomies.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[SM--spacetime loaded Howe duality]
\label{thm:SMST-main-duality}
For every source-complete joint packet, without an invertibility assumption on
the residue maps,
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal A_{{\rm act},X}'=\mathcal M_{{\rm type},X},
 \qquad
 \mathcal M_{{\rm type},X}'=\mathcal A_{{\rm act},X}.}
\]
On the total multiplicity carrier,
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal M_{{\rm type},X}
 =\bigl(\mathcal O_{F,X}^{\rm sup}\bigr)',
 \qquad
 \mathcal O_{F,X}^{\rm sup}
 =\mathcal M_{{\rm type},X}'.}
\]
If the residue support projections are noncommuting, their canonical central
decomposition gives instead the equivalent finite realization
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal M_{{\rm type},X}
 \cong\End\mathfrak Q_{F,X}.}
\]
On the connected invertible branch of
\Cref{thm:SMST-polar-holonomy}, choosing one root multiplicity fibre gives
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal M_{{\rm type},X}^{(o)}=\mathcal O_{F,X}',
 \qquad
 \mathcal O_{F,X}=(\mathcal M_{{\rm type},X}^{(o)})'.}
\]
Hence the strongest exact finite duality is not
$\mathcal A_{\rm spacetime}=\mathcal A_{\rm gauge}$, but the mutual commutant
pair
\[
 \boxed{
 \text{joint typed spacetime--gauge--incidence action}
 \quad\longleftrightarrow\quad
 \text{residual typed gauge--matter multiplicity}.}
\]
The support-polar algebra, multiplicity quiver, and invertible root-fibre
metric--holonomy algebra are three canonical presentations of this same dual
pair on their respective branches.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The first equality is \Cref{thm:SMST-edge-commutant}; finite bicommutant closure
gives the reverse equality.  The support-polar presentation is
\Cref{thm:SMST-support-polar-commutant}, and the noncommuting-support
presentation is \Cref{thm:SMST-quiver-commutant}.  The rooted invertible
presentation is \Cref{thm:SMST-polar-holonomy}.  Every generator and support
projection is reconstructed at saturated Grand-Tensor depth by
\Cref{thm:SMST-loaded-emergence,thm:SMST-support-polar-commutant}; no target
basis or inverse residue slot is inserted.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Commutant Laplacian]
\label{def:SMST-commutant-Laplacian}
Let $c_1,\ldots,c_s$ span a unital $*$-algebra
$\mathcal C\subseteq\mathcal B(\mathcal H)$.  On Hilbert--Schmidt operator
space define
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathscr L_{\mathcal C}
 :=\sum_{j=1}^s\operatorname{ad}_{c_j}^*
                    \operatorname{ad}_{c_j},
 \qquad
 \operatorname{ad}_{c}(X)=[c,X].}
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Terminating and stable commutant audit]
\label{thm:SMST-commutant-audit}
The commutant Laplacian is positive and
\[
 \boxed{\Ker\mathscr L_{\mathcal C}=\mathcal C'.}
\]
Let $P_{\mathcal C'}$ be Hilbert--Schmidt projection onto the commutant and let
$\lambda_{\mathcal C}>0$ be the least positive eigenvalue of
$\mathscr L_{\mathcal C}$.  Then
\[
 \boxed{
 \norm{X-P_{\mathcal C'}X}_{\HS}^2
 \le\lambda_{\mathcal C}^{-1}
 \sum_{j=1}^s\norm{[c_j,X]}_{\HS}^2.}
\]
Thus the zero eigenspace reconstructs the exact multiplicity algebra and the
first positive eigenvalue is a quantitative rigidity margin.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
For the Hilbert--Schmidt inner product,
$\operatorname{ad}_{c}^*=\operatorname{ad}_{c^*}$.  Therefore
\[
 \ip{X}{\mathscr L_{\mathcal C}X}_{\HS}
 =\sum_j\norm{[c_j,X]}_{\HS}^2\ge0.
\]
The quadratic form vanishes exactly when $X$ commutes with every generator and
hence with $\mathcal C$.  On $(\mathcal C')^\perp$, the positive operator is
bounded below by its least positive eigenvalue.  Apply that bound to
$X-P_{\mathcal C'}X$; the commutant component contributes zero to every
commutator.
\end{proof}


\begin{definition}[Relative Howe Gram]
\label{def:SMST-relative-Howe-Gram}
Let $\mathcal M\subseteq\mathcal B(\mathcal H)$ be a proposed protected
multiplicity algebra satisfying $\mathcal M\subseteq C^*(\bm c)'$, and let
$E_1,\ldots,E_r$ be a Hilbert--Schmidt orthonormal basis of
$\mathcal M^\perp$.  Define
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathbb G_{\rm Howe}(\bm c\mid\mathcal M)_{ab}
 :=\sum_j\langle[c_j,E_a],[c_j,E_b]\rangle_{\HS}.}
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Finite positive certificate for the exact multiplicity algebra]
\label{thm:SMST-relative-Howe-certificate}
Under \Cref{def:SMST-relative-Howe-Gram},
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathbb G_{\rm Howe}(\bm c\mid\mathcal M)\succ0
 \iff C^*(\bm c)'=\mathcal M.}
\]
On this branch its least eigenvalue is the first positive eigenvalue of the
commutant Laplacian.  Thus exactness of the desired flavour/generation algebra
and its finite rigidity margin are one positive Gram test reconstructed from
commutator words.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The displayed Gram is the matrix of
$\mathscr L_{C^*(\bm c)}$ restricted to $\mathcal M^\perp$.  Since
$\mathcal M$ is already contained in the kernel, the restriction is positive
definite exactly when no further kernel vector exists.  Its least eigenvalue
is then the first positive commutant-Laplacian eigenvalue.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Finite-anchor locking of the Howe commutant]
\label{thm:SMST-finite-anchor-Howe}
After transporting a cutoff family to one common finite screened carrier, let
$\bm c_X=(c_{1,X},\ldots,c_{s,X})$ and let a fixed protected algebra
$\mathcal M$ commute with every tuple.  Put
\[
 C_X=\left(\sum_j\|c_{j,X}\|_{\op}^2\right)^{1/2},
 \qquad
 \varepsilon_{X,Y}
 =\left(\sum_j\|c_{j,X}-c_{j,Y}\|_{\op}^2\right)^{1/2}.
\]
Suppose that at one cutoff $X_0$,
\[
 \mathbb G_{\rm Howe}(\bm c_{X_0}\mid\mathcal M)
 \succeq\gamma_0I,
 \qquad \gamma_0>0,
\]
and that, for every later $X$,
\[
 \boxed{
 4(C_X+C_{X_0})\varepsilon_{X,X_0}<\gamma_0.}
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{
 C^*(\bm c_X)'=\mathcal M,
 \qquad
 \lambda_{\min}^+(\mathscr L_{C^*(\bm c_X)})
 \ge\gamma_0-4(C_X+C_{X_0})\varepsilon_{X,X_0}.}
\]
In particular, a uniform bound $C_X\le C_*$ and the summable tail condition
\[
 \sum_{n\ge X_0}\varepsilon_{n+1,n}<\frac{\gamma_0}{8C_*}
\]
lock the exact commutant and a common positive gap at every later cutoff.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
For the commutator derivations,
\[
 \|\partial_{\bm c_X}-\partial_{\bm c_Y}\|_{2\to2}
 \le2\varepsilon_{X,Y},
 \qquad
 \|\partial_{\bm c_X}\|_{2\to2}\le2C_X.
\]
Using $A^*A-B^*B=A^*(A-B)+(A^*-B^*)B$ gives
\[
 \|\mathscr L_X-\mathscr L_Y\|
 \le4(C_X+C_Y)\varepsilon_{X,Y}.
\]
On $\mathcal M^\perp$, the anchor Laplacian is at least $\gamma_0I$.
The perturbation inequality gives the displayed later lower bound.  A later
commutant vector has zero energy and must therefore lie in $\mathcal M$; the
reverse inclusion is protected.  The summable statement follows by
telescoping the tuple increments.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Coercive continuum Howe duality]
\label{thm:SMST-continuum-Howe}
Let $\mathscr L_X$ be the commutant Laplacians of a cutoff family of screened
support-polar or multiplicity-quiver generators.  Assume:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(H\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item their closed forms converge in the Grand-Tensor Mosco sense;
\item the common graph-screen profile is compact, so the embedded resolvents
      converge in norm and isolated eigenvalues converge with multiplicity;
\item protected multiplicity projections $P_{\mathcal M_X}$ have one fixed
      finite rank, lie in $\Ker\mathscr L_X$, and converge in norm to
      $P_{\mathcal M_\infty}$;
\item the limiting action has no additional commutant:
      $\Ker\mathscr L_\infty=\mathcal M_\infty$.
\end{enumerate}
Then, for every sufficiently large cutoff,
\[
 \boxed{
 \Ker\mathscr L_X=\mathcal M_X,
 \qquad
 C^*(\bm c_X)'=\mathcal M_X,}
\]
the commutant projections converge in norm, and
\[
 \boxed{
 \lambda_{\min}^+(\mathscr L_X)
 \longrightarrow\lambda_{\min}^+(\mathscr L_\infty)>0.}
\]
Consequently there is $\gamma_*>0$ such that
\[
 \boxed{
 \sum_j\|[c_{j,X},A]\|_{\HS}^2
 \ge\gamma_*\|(I-P_{\mathcal M_X})A\|_{\HS}^2}
\]
for every sufficiently large $X$.  No bounded sequence of unprotected flavour
transformations can escape every finite screen while its commutators tend to
zero.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The compact-screen hypothesis and \Cref{thm:compact-screen-alternative} give
norm-resolvent convergence and convergence of the ordered low eigenvalues with
multiplicity.  The limiting kernel has the protected finite rank, and the next
eigenvalue is strictly positive.  An additional finite-cutoff zero eigenvalue
along a cofinal subsequence would force the next limiting eigenvalue to be
zero, a contradiction.  Hence the finite kernel eventually equals the
protected kernel, and convergence of the first positive eigenvalue gives the
uniform estimate.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Canonical full-cell orbit and Hodge-to-commutator transfer]
\label{thm:SMST-orbit-Hodge-transfer}
Let $\bm G=(G_1,\ldots,G_m)$ be the reconstructed common full-cell tuple and
let $\mathfrak T$ be the typed Hilbert--Schmidt perturbation space.  The
canonical conjugation-orbit source is
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal J_{\bm G}(A)=([G_1,A],\ldots,[G_m,A]),
 \qquad
 \Ker\mathcal J_{\bm G}=C^*(\bm G)'\cap\mathfrak T.}
\]
If an action tuple is an equivariant finite export
$\bm c=\Phi(\bm G)$, then differentiation of
$\Phi(U\bm GU^*)=U\Phi(\bm G)U^*$ gives a unique source-minimal orbit
derivative satisfying
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal J_{\bm c}
 =D_{\rm orb}\Phi_{\bm G}\,\mathcal J_{\bm G}.}
\]
In particular, if $\bm c\subseteq C^*(\bm G)$,
$\mathcal M\subseteq C^*(\bm G)'$, and
$C^*(\bm c)'=\mathcal M$, then
\[
 \boxed{C^*(\bm G)'=\mathcal M.}
\]

On the unprotected operator space
$\mathfrak K=(I-P_\mathcal M)\mathfrak T$, put
$J=\mathcal J_{\bm G}|_{\mathfrak K}$.  Let $D^{\rm sh}$ be the shorted
renewal Hodge/current differential and let
$\partial_{\bm c}$ be the action commutator derivation.  Define
\[
 \mathbb H=J^*(D^{\rm sh})^*D^{\rm sh}J,
 \qquad
 \mathbb C=\partial_{\bm c}^*\partial_{\bm c},
 \qquad
 \mathbb R=R^2.
\]
If, for constants $C_0>0$, $\alpha,\Lambda,\varepsilon\ge0$,
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathbb R\preceq C_0\mathbb H+\alpha I,
 \qquad
 \mathbb H\preceq\Lambda\mathbb C+\varepsilon^2\mathbb R,
 \qquad
 C_0\varepsilon^2<1,}
\]
then
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathbb R
 \preceq
 \frac{C_0\Lambda}{1-C_0\varepsilon^2}\mathbb C
 +\frac{\alpha}{1-C_0\varepsilon^2}I.}
\]
When $R=(I+L)^{s/2}$ for the compact-resolvent regularity anchor of the renewal
Hodge packet, this is the two-sided Hodge--Morrey estimate needed for the
compact commutator screens in \Cref{thm:SMST-continuum-Howe}.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The orbit-kernel identity is the definition of simultaneous commutation.
Differentiating the equivariance identity along $U(t)=e^{-tA}$ gives the chain
rule.  Since $\bm c\subseteq C^*(\bm G)$,
$C^*(\bm G)'\subseteq C^*(\bm c)'=\mathcal M$, while the protected inclusion
gives the reverse containment.

For the form estimate, substitute
$\mathbb H\preceq\Lambda\mathbb C+\varepsilon^2\mathbb R$ into
$\mathbb R\preceq C_0\mathbb H+\alpha I$, move
$C_0\varepsilon^2\mathbb R$ to the left, and divide by the positive scalar
$1-C_0\varepsilon^2$.  The final screen statement is the spectral-tail estimate
of the compact Hodge anchor applied to this domination and to its adjoint.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Reducing coherent source closure]
\label{thm:SMST-reducing-coherent-closure}
Let $V:E\to H$ be an isometry whose range reduces a bounded coherent generator
$A$, and put $a=V^*AV$.  For $t>0$, define
\[
 B_C=AV,
 \qquad
 B_H=\frac{e^{tA}-e^{-tA}}{2t}V,
 \qquad
 \psi_t(z)=\sum_{k\ge0}\frac{t^{2k}z^{2k}}{(2k+1)!}.
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{
 B_H=B_CW_t,
 \qquad W_t=\psi_t(a),}
\]
so the source Schur mismatch of $B_H$ relative to $B_C$ vanishes exactly.  If
$a$ is normal and $\|a\|\le M$, then, with $c=B_C^*B_C$,
\[
 \boxed{
 (B_H-B_C)^*(B_H-B_C)
 =(W_t-I)^*c(W_t-I)
 \preceq\frac{t^4M^4e^{2tM}}{36}\,c.}
\]
For physical step $\tau=2t$,
\[
 \boxed{\tau^{-1}\log W_t\longrightarrow0.}
\]
Thus a saturated reducing full-cell carrier together with the deterministic
same-history writer of \Cref{thm:SMST-reversal-writer} closes the Hodge/action
source comparison at every cutoff and leaves no additional continuum relative
connection.

More generally, if $R_A=AV-Va$ and
$E_{\rm pol}=B_H-(e^{tA}-e^{-tA})(2t)^{-1}V$, then for a positive regularity
form $r$,
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathbb S_{H\mid C}
 \preceq
 \left[
 \left(e^{tM}+\frac{\sinh(tM)}{tM}\right)
 \|R_Ar^{-1/2}\|
 +\|E_{\rm pol}r^{-1/2}\|
 \right]^2r.}
\]
Hence source-core and same-history defects of order $o(\tau)$ give the dense
Schur scale $o(\tau^2)r$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Reduction gives $A^nV=Va^n$ and hence
$e^{sA}V=Ve^{sa}$ by entire functional calculus.  Since
$(e^{ta}-e^{-ta})/(2t)=a\psi_t(a)$,
\[
 B_H=Va\psi_t(a)=AV\psi_t(a)=B_CW_t.
\]
The Schur residual is the squared orthogonal distance from $B_H$ to
$\Ran B_C$, so it vanishes.  Normality makes $c=a^*a$ commute with $W_t$.
The series estimate
\[
 \|W_t-I\|
 \le\frac{t^2M^2e^{tM}}6
\]
gives the graph bound.  The principal logarithm satisfies
$\|\log W_t\|=O(t^2)$, proving the physical-time limit.

For the approximate statement, Duhamel's formula gives
\[
 \|e^{sA}V-Ve^{sa}\|\le |s|e^{|s|M}\|R_A\|.
\]
Taking the centred difference and using
$\|\psi_t(a)\|\le\sinh(tM)/(tM)$ yields the displayed source error.  Evaluating
the Schur variational formula at $W_t$ gives the positive form bound.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Coercive SM--spacetime multiplicity closure]
\label{thm:SMST-coercive-multiplicity-closure}
Consider one cofinal joint SM--spacetime regulator family.  Assume:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(C\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item the finite source-native matter, CAR/incidence, endpoint-generation, and
      finite-Dirac packet of \Cref{thm:SM-GT};
\item the exact support-polar or multiplicity-quiver realization of
      $\mathcal M_{{\rm type},X}$ and either the finite-anchor hypothesis of
      \Cref{thm:SMST-finite-anchor-Howe} or the Mosco/compact-screen hypotheses
      of \Cref{thm:SMST-continuum-Howe};
\item the binary record or action-grading certificate of
      \Cref{thm:SMST-record-grading-rigidity,thm:SMST-grading-commutant};
\item saturated full-cell reduction and the deterministic same-history writer,
      or their $o(\tau_X)$ quantitative residual versions;
\item the Hodge-to-commutator transfer packet of
      \Cref{thm:SMST-orbit-Hodge-transfer} with uniform constants;
\item a regulator-uniform lower bound on the positive rank-three endpoint
      generation-source Gram.
\end{enumerate}
Then, for all sufficiently late cutoffs,
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal A_{{\rm act},X}'=\mathcal M_{{\rm type},X},
 \qquad
 \inf_X\lambda_{\min}^+(\mathscr L_{\mathcal A_{{\rm act},X}})>0,}
\]
the commutant projections and multiplicity-quiver algebra are regulator
stable, the compact commutator screens are uniformly exhausted, and the
rank-three generation source cannot collapse.  On the exact deterministic
writer and reducing coherent branch,
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathbb S_{H\mid C,X}=0,
 \qquad
 \tau_X^{-1}\log W_{0,X}\to0.}
\]
