Thus no additional multiplicity direction or relative connection survives the
continuum handoff.  The theorem does not determine the numerical residue
matrices, flavour breaking, scalar/gauge coefficients, running, matching, or
quantum determinant/Pfaffian phase.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The finite commutant is the support-polar or quiver commutant by
\Cref{thm:SMST-main-duality}.  Its exactness and uniform gap follow from
\Cref{thm:SMST-finite-anchor-Howe} or
\Cref{thm:SMST-continuum-Howe}.  The record theorems identify the grading and
same-history sources without an inserted router; full-cell flatness supplies
exact reduction as in \Cref{thm:SMST-generator-projections}.  The Hodge
transfer theorem gives the compact commutator screen, and
\Cref{thm:SMST-reducing-coherent-closure} gives the exact Schur and connection
statements.  The generation-source lower bound preserves its rank and positive
variance under the cutoff embeddings.  The final limitations are outside the
hypotheses and remain independent physical data.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Canonical one-generation incidence audit]
\label{thm:SMST-one-generation-audit}
On the five typed modules
\[
 \mathcal F_{15}=Q\oplus u\oplus d\oplus L\oplus e
\]
of \Cref{thm:SM-generation}, the gauge-generated algebra and commutant are
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal A_{\rm gauge}
 =M_6(\C)\oplus M_3(\C)\oplus M_3(\C)
  \oplus M_2(\C)\oplus\C,
 \qquad
 \mathcal A_{\rm gauge}'\cong\C^5.}
\]
If the three incidence histories
$Q\leftrightarrow u$, $Q\leftrightarrow d$, and
$L\leftrightarrow e$ are nonzero after contraction with their loaded Higgs
source, then
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal A_{\rm gauge+inc}
 =M_{12}(\C)\oplus M_3(\C),
 \qquad
 \mathcal A_{\rm gauge+inc}'\cong\C^2.}
\]
The two residual central directions are the quark and lepton components.  If a
neutral singlet and a nonzero $L$--neutral incidence are added, the second
matrix block becomes $M_4(\C)$ while the residual remains $\C^2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The five gauge modules are irreducible and pairwise inequivalent, so Schur's
lemma and the finite bicommutant theorem give the first algebra and its
five-dimensional scalar-block commutant.  A nonzero block between two full
matrix summands generates every cross map between them: if
$Y:V_s\to V_r$ is nonzero, choose $u,v$ with
$\langle u,Yv\rangle\ne0$; multiplying by endpoint rank-one matrices produces
any rank-one map $V_s\to V_r$.  Products and adjoints therefore generate the
full matrix algebra on each connected component of the incidence graph.  The
three edges have components
$\{Q,u,d\}$ and $\{L,e\}$, of dimensions $12$ and $3$, giving the displayed
algebra and a scalar on each component.  Adding one neutral vertex connected
to $L$ changes only the dimension of the lepton component.
\end{proof}

\begin{assessment}[Reader-level summary of the finite and coercive duality]
The universal Grand Tensor supplies the positive history carrier and the
finite reconstruction calculus.  The SM--spacetime loading supplies the actual
Clifford, gauge-type, incidence, support, and transport histories.  Once these
histories are on one source-minimal carrier, the finite duality is terminating:
compute the joint action algebra and its commutant.  Singular residues are
handled by the support-polar algebra, noncommuting supports by the canonical
multiplicity quiver, and the connected invertible branch by one rooted polar
metric--holonomy algebra.  The relative Howe Gram tests in one positive matrix
whether the proposed generation/flavour algebra is the complete commutant.  A
finite anchor plus a controlled tail, or Mosco convergence plus a compact
commutator screen, upgrades the same finite duality to a regulator-uniform
coercive statement.
\end{assessment}


% =============================================================================
\subsection{Spacetime dynamics and the continuum handoff inside the loaded tensor}
\label{sec:spacetime-sector}
% =============================================================================

The finite commutant duality is independent of the continuum handoff.  The
latter is a layered conditional theorem whose hypotheses are histories and
quantitative residuals inside the same loaded tensor.

\begin{theorem}[Structured spacetime source-frame noncollapse]
\label{thm:SMST-spacetime-frame}
Let the intended one-cell spacetime source at cutoff $h$ decompose orthogonally
into finitely many equivariant positive blocks $A_{\lambda,h}\succeq0$.  Assume
that every block declared to survive has
\[
 \lambda_{\min}^{+}(A_{\lambda,h})\ge c_*>0
\]
with one constant independent of $h$.  Then the one-cell source synthesis has
frame lower bound $c_*$ on the intended support.  Its threefold determinant
source has frame lower bound $c_*^3$.  Conversely, if an intended positive
eigenvalue tends to zero, a corresponding normalized eigenvector is an explicit
collapsing source direction, so finite source saturation need not survive the
regulator limit.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The equivariant block decomposition is orthogonal.  If
$x=\bigoplus_\lambda x_\lambda$ belongs to the intended supported coefficient
space, then
\[
 \sum_\lambda\langle x_\lambda,A_{\lambda,h}x_\lambda\rangle
 \ge c_*\sum_\lambda\|x_\lambda\|^2=c_*\|x\|^2.
\]
This is exactly the lower frame inequality.  Tensoring the inequality three
times gives $A_h^{\otimes3}\succeq c_*^3I$ on the tensor support, and restriction
to the alternating determinant line preserves the same lower bound.  If
$A_{\lambda,h}v_h=\varepsilon_hv_h$ with $\|v_h\|=1$ and
$\varepsilon_h\downarrow0$, then the physical source norm of $v_h$ is
$\varepsilon_h^{1/2}\to0$, which is the asserted explicit collapse.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Pressure-adapted coherent ADM packet]
\label{thm:SMST-ADM-Cartan}
Let a regulator family carry, on each compact source phase:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(P\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item an irreducible positive renewal-pressure transfer with root $\beta_h>0$,
      positive directional depths $\ell_{\mu,h}$, and physical scale
      $h_{{\rm P},h}=c_*/\beta_h$;
\item one finite-coefficient or uniquely generated jointly minimal coherent
      history kernel containing the pressure branches, the marked temporal
      branch, the three spatial generator branches, and their retained tangent
      histories;
\item exact neighboring covariance of that complete kernel under the actual
      physical links, or a same-history covariance defect tending to zero in
      the stated local $L^p$ topology;
\item a uniform completely bounded generator bound
      $\|\mathcal B_{\mu,h}\|_{\rm cb}\le M$ and near-identity links
      $\|\Phi_{e,h}-I\|_{\rm cb}\le hM$;
\item the complete-source frame floor of
      \Cref{thm:SMST-spacetime-frame}, horizontal gauge, and either uniform
      discrete Hodge--Sobolev constants on compact regulator patches or the
      finite-type weighted inverse packet of
      \Cref{thm:renewal-finite-type-closure}.
\end{enumerate}
Then:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2.8em]
\item the physical lapse is
      \[
       \boxed{\mathcal N_h=\beta_h\ell_{0,h}},
      \]
      and has positive upper and lower bounds on every compact pressure phase;
\item one environment unitary transports all pressure, temporal, and spatial
      Radon--Nikodym coordinates and their retained generator histories across
      each neighboring link;
\item after a common frame identification,
      \[
       \boxed{
       h^{-1}\|\mathcal B_{\mu,h}(y)-\mathcal B_{\mu,h}(x)\|_{\rm cb}
       \le C M^2+o(1)};
      \]
\item every actual spatial or mixed chronological face satisfies
      \[
       \boxed{
       \left\|-h^{-2}\operatorname{Log}\mathscr H_{\mu\nu,h}\right\|
       \le C\bigl(M^2+\mathfrak V_{\mu\nu,h}\bigr),}
      \]
      where $\mathfrak V_{\mu\nu,h}$ is the calibrated same-history transport
      residual for that face;
\item if the face packet is uniformly bounded in local $L^p$ for some $p>4$,
      either directly or by the regenerative finite-type graph estimate of
      \Cref{thm:SMST-regenerative-ADM}, then the horizontal connection is
      uniformly bounded in $W^{1,p}_{\rm loc}$ and the reconstructed ADM
      response metric is bounded in $C^{0,\alpha}_{\rm loc}$ for every
      $\alpha<1-4/p$.
\end{enumerate}
No smooth continuum connection is inserted before these estimates.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
A directional history of depth $\ell_{\mu,h}$ has physical duration
$\tau_{\mu,h}=c_*\ell_{\mu,h}$.  Dividing the temporal duration by the intrinsic
pressure scale gives
\[
 \frac{\tau_{0,h}}{h_{{\rm P},h}}=\beta_h\ell_{0,h}=\mathcal N_h.
\]
Compactness of the chosen positive Perron phase gives the two-sided lapse
bounds.

Two source-minimal realizations of the same complete coherent kernel are
related by one source-fixing unitary.  Applying minimal-realization uniqueness
to neighboring cells therefore gives one unitary independent of the history
label.  Differentiating the coherent intertwining identity transports every
retained tangent generator, proving item~\textup{(ii)}.

Write the exact transported generator relation in a common coefficient frame
as
\[
 \mathcal B_y(v)=\Phi_e\mathcal B_x(Q_e^{-1}v)\Phi_e^{-1}+R_e(v),
 \qquad \|R_e\|_{\rm cb}=o(h).
\]
Near identity, $\|Q_e^{-1}-I\|\le ChM$, while conjugation by $\Phi_e$ changes an
operator of norm at most $M$ by at most $2hM^2+O(h^2M^3)$.  Subtraction and
division by $h$ give item~\textup{(iii)}.

Let $W_\mu$ be the actual edge propagator, written on a unit parameter interval
as $\partial_sW_\mu=-h\mathcal B_\mu(s)W_\mu$.  Variation of constants gives
\[
 \|W_B(1)-W_C(1)\|
 \le h e^{2hM}\int_0^1\|B(s)-C(s)\|\,\dd s.
\]
Compare the actual face product with the same-base commutator face.  The
Baker--Campbell--Hausdorff remainder is $O(h^2M^2)$, and the preceding estimate
controls the base-transport error by $h^2\mathfrak V_{\mu\nu,h}$.  The principal
logarithm is defined for all sufficiently small $h$, giving item~\textup{(iv)}.

Finally, horizontal gauge removes the discrete exact component.  The uniform
Hodge estimate controls the full first difference of the connection by its
exterior derivative, codifferential, and zeroth-order norm.  The face bound
controls the exterior derivative, while the frame floor controls conversion
between source and coefficient norms.  The uniform discrete Sobolev estimate
therefore gives a $W^{1,p}$ bound.  In four dimensions, Morrey embedding yields
$C^{0,\alpha}$ for every $\alpha<1-4/p$, proving item~\textup{(v)}.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Regenerative derivation of the ADM regularity packet]
\label{thm:SMST-regenerative-ADM}
Assume the pressure-adapted histories of \Cref{thm:SMST-ADM-Cartan} and set
$\tau_h=c_*\ell_{0,h}$.  Suppose that, on a fixed compact pressure region:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(R\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item the horizontal current/outgoing source and actual face families form a
      finite physical type atlas with a positive type-mass floor;
\item their prototype source Grams have a common positive floor and their
      normalized Ward--graph and face-composition matrices have bounded
      integrated quadratic energy and controlled type-covariance residuals;
\item the protected-horizontal Hodge packet satisfies either direct $L^{p_0}$
      and $L^p$ conorm bounds for some
      $4p/(p+2)\le p_0<4<p$, or the weighted inverse branch of
      \Cref{thm:renewal-finite-type-closure};
\item the generator source is uniformly bounded and its projection outside the
      horizontal source frame is uniformly controlled.
\end{enumerate}
Then the source-frame floor converts the generator-source bound into a uniform
connection-coefficient bound.  The finite type-mass theorem converts the
quadratic Ward--graph and face energies into local amplitude caps and hence
into every finite $L^r$ bound.  In particular the actual chronological faces
are uniformly bounded in local $L^p$ for the displayed $p>4$.  The horizontal
Hodge estimate gives a uniform $W^{1,p}_{\rm loc}$ connection, and the coframe
and metric are precompact in $C^{0,\alpha}_{\rm loc}$ for every
$\alpha<1-4/p$.

If the same protected-soft Hodge form dominates a compact-resolvent anchor,
the finite-rank screen and its uniformly exhausted tails follow from
\Cref{thm:renewal-shorted-Hodge}.  Thus on this branch the separate local
amplitude, $p>4$ face, Hodge-conorm, and compact-screen hypotheses are outputs
of one finite-type regenerative packet.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The local source-frame estimate is the least-eigenvalue inequality applied to
the coefficient synthesis.  The first conclusion of
\Cref{thm:renewal-finite-type-closure} gives the local Ward--graph and face
caps from their integrated energies, and interpolation gives their finite
$L^r$ bounds.  The coherent plaquette comparison in
\Cref{thm:SMST-ADM-Cartan} transfers the spatial and mixed edge defects to the
actual faces.  The direct conorm branch is the finite Hodge estimate; on the
weighted inverse branch it follows from the final assertion of
\Cref{thm:renewal-finite-type-closure}.  Sobolev--Morrey embedding gives the
coefficient compactness.  The screen statement is
\Cref{thm:renewal-shorted-Hodge}.
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[Pressure data alone do not control curvature]
A bounded scalar pressure packet and bounded one-edge generator norms do not
control transverse generator oscillation.  Alternating neighboring generators
may have identical scalar pressure data while the normalized spatial or mixed
face curvature grows like $h^{-1}$.  The jointly coherent same-history
transport and its residual in \Cref{thm:SMST-ADM-Cartan} are therefore
load-bearing.
\end{firewall}

\begin{theorem}[Endpoint shift and Cartan closure]
\label{thm:SMST-shift-Cartan}
Assume \Cref{thm:SMST-ADM-Cartan}.  Let the retained temporal endpoint source
decompose under spatial rotations into a scalar normal line, vector endpoint
lines, and an orthogonal residual.  Let $G_h=E_h^{\mathsf T}E_h$ be the spatial
metric and let $\mathscr P_{\beta,h}$ pull the later metric back by the actual
endpoint map.  Then:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2.8em]
\item the vector-isotypic Gram is $I_3\otimes C_h$, and $\rank C_h$ is the
      number of independent physical shift ports;
\item rank zero makes the shift future null, while rank one reconstructs one
      shift $\beta_h$; if endpoint relabelings are future null, a local inverse
      flow removes $\beta_h$ without changing the physical quotient;
\item the finite extrinsic response
      \[
       K_h=\frac{\mathscr P_{\beta,h}G_h(t+h)-G_h(t)}
                   {2h\mathcal N_h}
      \]
      converges, whenever the displayed difference converges, to
      \[
       K=\frac1{2\mathcal N}
       (\partial_0G-\mathcal L_\beta G);
      \]
\item for the time-gauge coframe
      \[
       e^0=\mathcal N\,\dd t,
       \qquad e^a=E^a{}_i(\dd x^i+\beta^i\dd t),
      \]
      the complete mixed torsion is
      \[
       \boxed{
       T^a{}_{0i}=\left[(\partial_0-\mathcal L_\beta)E
       +(\omega_0-\beta^j\omega_j)E
       -\mathcal N E^{-\mathsf T}K\right]^a{}_i;}
      \]
\item the unique Cartan-compatible temporal rotation is
      \[
       \boxed{
       \omega_0^{\rm C}=\beta^j\omega_j
       +\mathcal N E^{-\mathsf T}KE^{-1}
       -(\partial_0-\mathcal L_\beta)EE^{-1},}
      \]
      and, after spatial torsion vanishes,
      \[
       \boxed{T=0\iff\omega_0=\omega_0^{\rm C}.}
      \]
\end{enumerate}
If the physical and Cartan temporal-rotation sources have the same
multiplicity-one adjoint range and preserve one nonzero ordered
$\mathfrak{so}(3)$ bracket, they are equal; the resulting connection is
Levi--Civita.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Rotation covariance makes the vector source an isotypic tensor product of the
standard real three-dimensional representation with a multiplicity space.
The real Schur lemma therefore gives $I_3\otimes C_h$, and its multiplicity rank
counts the independent vector ports.  Under a time-dependent spatial
relabeling $y=\phi_t(x)$ the shift transforms as
\[
 \widetilde\beta=D\phi_t\,\beta-\partial_t\phi_t.
\]
Solving $\partial_t\psi_t=-\beta(t,\psi_t)$ gives a local zero-shift chart when
that relabeling is physically null.  Pullback of the later metric by the actual
endpoint map and first-order expansion give the formula for $K$.

Insert the displayed coframe into Cartan's first structure equation
$T^I=\dd e^I+\Omega^I{}_J\wedge e^J$.  The spatial boost part is fixed by $K$
and $\dd\log\mathcal N$.  Collecting the $\dd t\wedge\dd x^i$ coefficients
gives the mixed-torsion matrix in item~\textup{(iv)}.  Solving that equation for
$\omega_0$ gives $\omega_0^{\rm C}$.  Its symmetric part vanishes because $K$
is defined by the symmetric metric derivative, hence
$\omega_0^{\rm C}\in\mathfrak{so}(3)$.  Once spatial torsion is zero, every
remaining torsion component is $(\omega_0-\omega_0^{\rm C})E$, proving the
equivalence.

On one adjoint source copy, equivariance makes the two source maps scalar
multiples: $S_{\rm C}=\lambda S_{\rm phys}$.  Preservation of one nonzero
relation $[J_1,J_2]=J_3$ gives $\lambda^2=\lambda$.  Nonzero source rank excludes
$\lambda=0$, so $\lambda=1$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Rigidity of the local one-doublet and minimal gauge actions]
\label{thm:SMST-action-rigidity}
Let $W_x\cong\C^2$ be the source-native weak fibres and
$U_e^W:W_x\to W_y$ the actual unitary weak transport on an oriented edge
$e:x\to y$.

\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(A\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item Let $Q_e$ be a real quadratic edge action which is locally weak-gauge
      covariant, nonnegative, and whose zero set is exactly
      $\phi_y=U_e^W\phi_x$.  Then for a unique $w_e>0$,
      \[
       \boxed{Q_e(\phi_x,\phi_y)
       =w_e\|U_e^W\phi_x-\phi_y\|^2.}
      \]
\item Let $V_x$ be weak-$U(2)$ invariant, nonnegative, polynomial of total
      degree at most four, and zero exactly on the microscopic source sphere
      $\|\phi\|=\rho_x>0$.  Then for a unique $\lambda_x>0$,
      \[
       \boxed{V_x(\phi)
       =\lambda_x(\|\phi\|^2-\rho_x^2)^2.}
      \]
\item Let a face action on $U_f\in U(n)$ be affine in the fundamental character
      and its conjugate, invariant under conjugation and reversal, nonnegative,
      and zero exactly at $U_f=I$.  Then for a unique $w_f>0$,
      \[
       \boxed{S_f(U_f)
       =w_f\bigl(n-\operatorname{Re}\Tr U_f\bigr)
       =\frac{w_f}{2}\|I-U_f\|_{\HS}^2.}
      \]
      Its Hessian at the identity is the physical invariant current metric
      $w_f\operatorname{Re}\Tr(XY)$.
\end{enumerate}
Consequently, on this local branch the scalar and minimal plaquette actions are
fixed by the actual links, source radius, and one positive coefficient per edge,
site, or gauge factor.  Higher-order, nonlocal, or higher-character terms are
not excluded and must be retained when their action residuals are nonzero.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Conjugate the edge variables by the actual transport and write the most general
simultaneously $U(2)$-invariant real quadratic form as
$a\|x\|^2+b\|y\|^2-2\operatorname{Re}(c\langle x,y\rangle)$.  Vanishing on
$x=y$ gives $a+b=2\operatorname{Re}c$ and vanishing of the imaginary cross
part.  Positivity and the requirement that the kernel be precisely the diagonal
force $a=b=c=w_e>0$.

A continuous $U(2)$-invariant polynomial depends only on
$s=\|\phi\|^2$.  Degree at most four gives $as^2+bs+c$.  Nonnegativity and a
complete zero set at $s=\rho_x^2$ make this polynomial a positive multiple of
$(s-\rho_x^2)^2$.  Finally, the assumed character branch has the form
$a-b\operatorname{Re}\Tr U$.  Vanishing at $I$, nonnegativity, and uniqueness
of the zero give $a=bn$ and $b=w_f>0$.  Expanding
$e^{i(sX+tY)}$ to second order gives the current metric.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Typed matter closure and finite Legendre reciprocity]
\label{thm:SMST-matter-Legendre}
Let $\mathscr L(z,v)$ be a finite matter Lagrangian with symmetric positive
velocity Hessian $\mathbb K=D_v^2\mathscr L\succ0$, and let
\[
 p=D_v\mathscr L(z,v),\qquad
 \mathscr H(z,p)=\langle p,v(z,p)\rangle-\mathscr L(z,v(z,p)).
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{D_p\mathscr H=v,\qquad D_z\mathscr H=-D_z\mathscr L,
 \qquad D_p^2\mathscr H=\mathbb K^{-1}.}
\]
Thus Lagrangian and Hamiltonian metric derivatives define the same stress
covector.

For typed matter sectors $r$, suppose the finite normal density has momentum
coefficient $a_r>0$ and transported spatial-gradient coefficient $b_r>0$.
Then the exact lapse-antisymmetrized matter bracket is
\[
 \boxed{
 -i[H_{{\rm m},h}[N],H_{{\rm m},h}[M]]
 =\sum_r a_rb_r\,D_{r,h}
 \!\left[\mathsf Q_{r,h}(N\dd_hM-M\dd_hN)\right],}
\]
where $\mathsf Q_{r,h}$ is the measured conductance second-moment tensor.  If
\[
 \mathcal K_{xy}^{\rm gm}=-iP[t_{{\rm g},x},h_{{\rm m},y}]P,
\]
the complete gravity--matter cross anomaly is
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal X_h^{\rm gm}(N,M)
 =\sum_{x<y}(N_xM_y-N_yM_x)
 (\mathcal K_{xy}^{\rm gm}-\mathcal K_{yx}^{\rm gm}).}
\]
Consequently, conductance matching $\mathsf Q_{r,h}=G_h^{-1}$, symmetry of the
cross kernel, and positivity of a determining species-current Gram imply total
HDA closure exactly when
\[
 \boxed{a_rb_r=1\qquad\text{for every loaded species }r.}
\]
If one positive amplitude multiplies the whole Hamiltonian sector,
$a_r=b_r=\lambda_r$, then $\lambda_r=1$.  If instead one Lagrangian sector has
action stiffness $\eta_r>0$, its Legendre descendants are
\[
 \boxed{a_r=\eta_r^{-1},\qquad b_r=\eta_r,}
\]
so HDA closure does not determine $\eta_r$.

More generally, for a cutoff family of measured kinetic Hessians $\mathbb K_h$
and independently measured Hamiltonian Hessians $\mathbb A_h$, a uniform least
singular-value margin for $\mathbb K_h$, a vanishing mixed-block residual, and
\[
 \boxed{
 \Delta_{\rm Leg,h}
 :=\|\mathbb A_h\mathbb K_h-I\|_{\HS}^2
  +\|\mathbb K_h\mathbb A_h-I\|_{\HS}^2}
\]
are respectively the exact certificates for uniform Legendre invertibility,
absence of unintended metric--matter kinetic mixing, and reciprocal Hessians.
For quadratic fermions,
$[\dd\Gamma(A),\dd\Gamma(B)]=\dd\Gamma([A,B])$, so the many-body bracket is the
CAR lift of the one-particle bracket.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Differentiate the Legendre identity at fixed $p$.  The terms involving
$D_zv$ or $D_pv$ cancel because $p=D_v\mathscr L$, giving the first two
envelope formulas.  Differentiating $p=D_v\mathscr L$ with respect to $p$
gives $D_pv=\mathbb K^{-1}$ and therefore the inverse-Hessian identity.

In the lapse antisymmetrization, momentum--momentum and multiplication--
multiplication terms commute.  A local potential contributes the coefficient
$N_xM_x-M_xN_x=0$.  Only momentum--gradient commutators remain.  On an oriented
edge they give the transported symmetrized current multiplied by
$a_rb_r(N_xM_y-M_xN_y)$.  Summation over edges gives the displayed matter
bracket and identifies $\mathsf Q_{r,h}$.

Expanding the two mixed smeared Hamiltonians and pairing the terms indexed by
$(x,y)$ and $(y,x)$ gives the cross-anomaly formula.  After conductance matching
and cross-kernel symmetry, subtracting the physical unweighted total
diffeomorphism source leaves
\[
 \sum_r(a_rb_r-1)D_{r,h}(v)=0.
\]
Let $c_r=a_rb_r-1$.  On a determining family of currents its squared physical
norm is $c^*G_{\rm sp}c$.  Positivity of the species-current Gram makes this zero
only for $c=0$, proving $a_rb_r=1$.  The two specializations are immediate; the
second is the usual inversion of a Lagrangian quadratic coefficient under the
Legendre transform.

The reciprocity residual is a sum of squares and vanishes exactly when
$\mathbb A_h$ is both a left and right inverse of $\mathbb K_h$.  A uniform
least singular value bounds $\|\mathbb K_h^{-1}\|$; inverse convergence follows
from
\[
 \mathbb K_h^{-1}-\mathbb K^{-1}
 =\mathbb K_h^{-1}(\mathbb K-\mathbb K_h)\mathbb K^{-1}.
\]
Finally, the CAR identity follows by direct computation on matrix units
$c_i^*c_j$ and linearity.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Action-derived scalar current]
For the local scalar action of \Cref{thm:SMST-action-rigidity}, let $K_x>0$ be
the transported kinetic metric and let $p_x$ be the canonical momentum.  Then
\[
 \{H(N),H(M)\}=D_{\rm sc}(\omega(N,M)),
 \qquad \omega(N,M)_{(x,y)}=N_xM_y-M_xN_y,
\]
with edge current
\[
 \boxed{
 J_e^{\rm sc}=\frac{w_e}{2}\left\langle
 \phi_y-U_e\phi_x,\ U_ep_x+p_y\right\rangle.}
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The inverse kinetic metric in the Hamiltonian cancels the transported kinetic
metric in the gradient energy.  Collecting both orientations of each edge gives
the displayed current; the local potential cancels by lapse antisymmetry.
\end{proof}


\begin{theorem}[Shared-edge normal current, reduction, and commutant]
\label{thm:shared-edge-normal-current}
Let a finite one-skeleton carry one extracted Pauli factor per edge, with
cross-edge factors commuting.  For an oriented edge $e=(x,y)$ choose the
endpoint axes $A_{e,x}=X_e$ and $A_{e,y}=Y_e$, and define
\[
 n_{x,h}=\sum_{e\ni x}\lambda_{e,x,h}A_{e,x},
 \qquad
 H_h[N]=\sum_xN_xn_{x,h}.
\]
Then nonadjacent vertex densities commute.  On $e=(x,y)$,
\[
 \boxed{
 j_{e,h}:=-ih[n_{x,h},n_{y,h}]
 =2h\lambda_{e,x,h}\lambda_{e,y,h}Z_e.}
\]
Consequently
\[
 \boxed{
 -i[H_h[N],H_h[M]]
 =\sum_{e=(x,y)}
 (N_x\nabla_eM-M_x\nabla_eN)j_{e,h}.}
\]
With the product normalized trace, distinct edge currents are orthogonal and
have squared norms
$4h^2|\lambda_{e,x,h}\lambda_{e,y,h}|^2$.

If all incidence coefficients are nonzero, the algebra generated by the
vertex normal densities contains the complete Pauli factor on every edge.  On
the minimal parallel-edge carrier it is the full tensor product and has scalar
commutant.  The carrier is reducing for the normal-history algebra.

A regulator-uniform nonzero current requires an unbounded normal scale.  More
precisely, if
$|2h\lambda_{e,x,h}\lambda_{e,y,h}|\ge\kappa_*>0$, then
\[
 \max\{|\lambda_{e,x,h}|,|\lambda_{e,y,h}|\}
 \ge\sqrt{\kappa_*/(2h)}.
\]
Under a bounded endpoint-loading ratio, both coefficients are of order
$h^{-1/2}$; the continuum passage must therefore use the quadratic-form and
ordered-product-core theory of Part~I-B.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Only a shared edge factor can contribute to the commutator of two different
vertex densities.  The Pauli identity $[X_e,Y_e]=2iZ_e$ gives the current and,
after pairing both orientations, the smeared bracket.  Product-trace
orthogonality follows because distinct currents are traceless operators on
distinct tensor factors.

Since $j_{e,h}$ is a nonzero scalar multiple of $Z_e$, the normal algebra
contains $Z_e$.  Commuting it with the endpoint density at $x$ recovers $Y_e$,
and commuting it with the endpoint density at $y$ recovers $X_e$.  Hence it
contains every edge $M_2(\C)$; on the minimal tensor-product carrier their
joint commutant is scalar.  Reduction follows because the full generated
matrix algebra leaves no exterior source-cyclic direction.  The scaling bound
is the arithmetic--geometric inequality applied to
$2h|\lambda_{e,x,h}\lambda_{e,y,h}|\ge\kappa_*$.  A bounded ratio makes the
two factors comparable.
\end{proof}

\begin{assessment}[What the shared-edge packet discharges]
On this branch the Store--score compiler supplies coherent access to the two
ordered normal words, while
\Cref{thm:shared-edge-normal-current} supplies off-edge locality, the finite
current frame, a reducing minimal carrier, and the scalar normal commutant.
The remaining HDA content is the same-history identity of this current with the
metric/tangential endpoint source, its absolute unit normalization, a physical
differentiable endpoint-flow action, and the common unbounded form/domain
limit.
\end{assessment}

\begin{theorem}[Complete finite coherent vacuum HDA]
\label{thm:finite-HDA}
Let $H_h[N]$ and $D_h[v]$ be self-adjoint normal and tangential generators on
one finite physical carrier.  Assume:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(H\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item the two ordered normal histories lie in one covered Store--score target,
      and the calibrated phases $1$ and $i$ reconstruct their complex cross
      kernel; the settings $-1$ and $-i$ are consistency checks;
\item $H_h[N]=\sum_xN_xn_{x,h}$ and
      $[n_{x,h},n_{y,h}]=0$ outside the declared one-link neighborhood;
\item the normalized edge-current source is same-history identical with the
      endpoint commutator of two unit-normal deformations and has exactly one
      physical tangential vector copy;
\item the carrier is the complete reducing source-cyclic carrier of the retained
      normal and tangential history algebra;
\item physical endpoint relabelings form a finite Lie group acting on scalar
      lapse labels, and the complete coherent normal histories transform by that
      semidirect action;
\item either the coherent relabeling histories form a strict representation, or
      the normal-history commutant is scalar and $D_h[v]$ is canonically
      centered.
\end{enumerate}
Then
\begin{align}
 -i[D_h[v],D_h[w]]&=D_h[[v,w]_h],\\
 -i[D_h[v],H_h[N]]&=H_h[\ell_h(v)N],\\
 -i[H_h[N],H_h[M]]
 &=D_h\!\left[G_h^{-1}(N\dd_hM-M\dd_hN)\right].
\end{align}
All interface or Feshbach terms vanish on the reducing carrier.  Under
consistent label, source, and metric convergence, the identities pass to the
continuum vacuum hypersurface-deformation algebra.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Expand the local normal densities.  Off-neighbor commutativity leaves only
oriented edges:
\[
 -i[H_h[N],H_h[M]]
 =\sum_{e=(x,y)}(N_xM_y-M_xN_y)(-i[n_{x,h},n_{y,h}]).
\]
Writing $j_{e,h}=-ih[n_{x,h},n_{y,h}]$, the coefficient is
$N_x\nabla_eM-M_x\nabla_eN$.  For a spacelike embedding $X$ with unit normal
$n$, differentiation of $g(n,n)=-1$ and $g(n,\partial_iX)=0$ under
$\delta_NX=Nn$ gives
\[
 \delta_Nn=G^{-1}\dd N,
 \qquad
 [\delta_N,\delta_M]_{\rm ord}X
 =G^{-1}(N\dd M-M\dd N).
\]
The same-history endpoint identity transfers this unit coefficient to the
physical edge current.  The one-copy condition removes every orthogonal vector
port, proving the $HH$ bracket.

Let $R_h(g)=e^{-isD_h[v]}$ implement endpoint flow and
$U_h(N,t)=e^{-itH_h[N]}$.  Semidirect naturality is
\[
 R_h(g)U_h(N,t)R_h(g)^{-1}=U_h(\rho_h(g)N,t).
\]
Differentiate first in $t$ and then at $g=e^{sv}$ to obtain the $DH$ bracket
with unit amplitude.

Set
\[
 Z(v,w)=-i[D_h[v],D_h[w]]-D_h[[v,w]_h].
\]
The operator Jacobi identity, the $DH$ relation, and
$[\ell_h(v),\ell_h(w)]=\ell_h([v,w]_h)$ imply
$[Z(v,w),H_h[N]]=0$ for every retained lapse.  Under the scalar-commutant branch,
$Z(v,w)$ is scalar; canonical centering makes it traceless and hence zero.  In
the strict group-law branch, direct differentiation of the representation law
gives the same conclusion.

Finally, if $P$ is the reducing source projection and $Q=I-P$, then
$QH_h[N]P=QD_h[v]P=0$.  Every Schur/Feshbach cross term such as
$PAQBP-PBQAP$ therefore vanishes.  Convergence of the finite labels and source
forms passes the three identities to the limit on a common core.
\end{proof}

\begin{assessment}[Why the HDA coefficient is not fitted]
The coefficient one in the $HH$ bracket is the measured coefficient of the
unit-normal endpoint commutator, not an inserted continuum structure function.
The canonical Store--score compiler supplies ordered-history coherence once the
normal generators occur.  On the shared-edge branch,
\Cref{thm:shared-edge-normal-current} additionally supplies off-edge locality,
a reducing carrier, and a scalar finite commutant.  The remaining content is
the physical current--geometry source identity, its absolute normalization,
semidirect endpoint flow, and the regulator-uniform unbounded-domain limit.
\end{assessment}

\begin{corollary}[Common-action provenance discharges the normal--endpoint comparison]
Let $h_x^{\rm act}$ be the action-derived normal generator, $n_x$ the
generator-native normal candidate, $a_x$ the protected affine endpoint writer,
and $V_{\rm aff}$ a whitened source-minimal synthesis.  Define
\[
 \Delta_{\rm act\to nor}=\sum_x\|n_x-h_x^{\rm act}\|_{\HS}^2,
 \qquad
 \Delta_{\rm act\to end}
 =\sum_x\|h_x^{\rm act}V_{\rm aff}-V_{\rm aff}a_x\|_{\HS}^2.
\]
Then, for $R_x=n_xV_{\rm aff}-V_{\rm aff}a_x$,
\[
 \boxed{
 \sum_x\|R_x\|_{\HS}^2
 \le2\Delta_{\rm act\to nor}+2\Delta_{\rm act\to end}.}
\]
Thus zero provenance residuals identify the generator-native normal and the
endpoint writer as restrictions of one Hamiltonian flow.  Together with the
phase, locality, cyclicity, and semidirect hypotheses of
\Cref{thm:finite-HDA}, this verifies the endpoint-source premise without an
independent one-particle HDA assumption.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Insert and subtract $h_x^{\rm act}V_{\rm aff}$ and use
$\|u+v\|^2\le2\|u\|^2+2\|v\|^2$, then sum over $x$.  If both residuals vanish,
$n_xV_{\rm aff}=V_{\rm aff}a_x$ and both are equal to the action-derived
restriction.  No cancellation between unrelated mismatches is used.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Common-action Ward, BRST, stress, and finite Einstein residual]
\label{thm:SMST-finite-action-Einstein}
Let
\[
 \mathscr S_{\rm tot}(q,\Phi)
 =\mathscr S_g(q)+\mathscr S_{\rm mat}(q,\Phi)
\]
be one finite action on the joint loaded carrier.  Define
\[
 E_\Phi=D_\Phi\mathscr S_{\rm mat},
 \qquad
 \mathsf T=-2D_q\mathscr S_{\rm mat},
\]
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal E_q^{\rm tot}
 =2D_q\mathscr S_{\rm tot}
 =2D_q\mathscr S_g-\mathsf T.}
\]
Then:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(F\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item exact finite gauge invariance gives the Ward identity
      \[
       \boxed{\operatorname{Div}_UJ+
       \mathcal R_{\rm mat,\Phi}^*E_\Phi=0;}
      \]
      on matter shell the current is conserved;
\item the standard finite BRST differential on ghosts, links, scalar fields,
      and every covariant finite-Dirac carrier is nilpotent and annihilates the
      classical action;
\item common tangential relabeling invariance gives
      \[
       \boxed{\mathcal L_q^*\mathsf T
       =2\mathcal L_\Phi^*E_\Phi,}
      \]
      and therefore tangential stress conservation on matter shell;
\item for any faithful metric $G_{\mathcal Q}$ on geometric variations,
      \[
       \boxed{
       \Delta_{\rm Ein}^{\rm fin}
       :=\langle\mathcal E_q^{\rm tot},
       G_{\mathcal Q}^{-1}\mathcal E_q^{\rm tot}\rangle\ge0}
      \]
      vanishes exactly when the finite total action is metrically stationary,
      equivalently $2D_q\mathscr S_g=\mathsf T$.
\end{enumerate}
No external stress router is required on the common-action branch.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Differentiate gauge invariance and integrate the link variations by the finite
incidence adjoint to obtain the Ward identity.  The BRST rules are the
infinitesimal gauge action with $sc=-c^2$; the Jacobi identity and covariance
give $s^2=0$, and gauge invariance gives $s\mathscr S_{\rm tot}=0$.
Differentiating tangential invariance in the same way gives the stress identity.
The final statement follows from positivity and faithfulness of
$G_{\mathcal Q}^{-1}$.
\end{proof}



% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
\subsubsection{Protected cycle rewards, renewal pressure, and common-action exactness}
\label{sec:renewal-action-pressure}
% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

The normalized score of a probability law is centered and therefore does not,
by itself, contain the affine first variation of an action.  On a marked
renewal cycle that affine coordinate is recovered from the physical duration
and the renewal-pressure normalization.  The complete action sectors must be
placed on the same resolved reward record; proportionality to the accepted
count is neither required nor expected.

\begin{definition}[Protected vector cycle-reward packet]
\label{def:protected-cycle-reward}
Let $(\Omega_X,p_X)$ be a finite faithful marked first-return law, let
$\tau_X:\Omega_X\to(0,\infty)$ be the protected physical duration, and let
$E_X$ be a finite real variation space.  A protected cycle-reward synthesis is
\[
 G_X:E_X\longrightarrow L^2(\Omega_X,p_X),
 \qquad v\longmapsto g_{v,X},
\]
whose values are actual Reads or fixed functions of protected record
coordinates.  Define
\[
 \mathcal L_X(q,r)
 =\mathbb E_X[e^{-g_{q,X}-r\tau_X}],
 \qquad
 \bar\tau_X=\mathbb E_X\tau_X,
 \qquad
 T_Xc=c\tau_X.
\]
The minimal reward record identifies precisely those cycle records with equal
$(g_X,\tau_X)$ values.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Table-derived reward pressure and complete action-slope reconstruction]
\label{thm:reward-pressure-reconstruction}
For every packet of \Cref{def:protected-cycle-reward}, the complete Laplace
transform $\mathcal L_X$ and all of its finite derivatives are reconstructed
from the marked-cycle table; no additional tilted experiment is needed for
this finite calculation.  There is a unique analytic pressure
$\mathcal P_X$ near the origin such that
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal P_X(0)=0,
 \qquad
 \mathcal L_X(q,\mathcal P_X(q))=1.}
\]
Let
\[
 p_{X,q}(\omega)
 =p_X(\omega)e^{-g_{q,X}(\omega)-\mathcal P_X(q)\tau_X(\omega)}
\]
and let $S_Xv=D\log p_{X,q}|_{q=0}[v]$.  Writing
$\pi_X=D\mathcal P_X(0)$ and
$\gamma_X=G_X^*\one$, one has
\[
 \boxed{
 \pi_X(v)=-\frac{\gamma_X(v)}{\bar\tau_X},}
\]
\[
 \boxed{
 S_Xv=-G_Xv-\pi_X(v)\tau_X,
 \qquad
 G_X=-S_X-T_X\pi_X.}
\]
Thus renewal pressure reconstructs the affine action anchor and, together with
the normalized score and duration writer, the complete uncentered physical
cycle-action slope.

The covariance rank satisfies
\[
 \boxed{
 \rank\operatorname{Cov}_{p_X}(g_X)
 =\dim\operatorname{Aff}\{g_X(\omega):\omega\in\Omega_X\}.}
\]
It is the exact number of independent fluctuating action directions present on
the resolved cycle record.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The transform is the finite sum of known probabilities times known protected
writer values; differentiating under the finite sum reconstructs every mixed
moment.  At the origin,
$\mathcal L_X(0,0)=1$ and
$\partial_r\mathcal L_X(0,0)=-\bar\tau_X<0$, so the analytic
implicit-function theorem gives the pressure root.  Differentiation of its
normalization in direction $v$ gives
\[
 0=-\mathbb E_Xg_{v,X}-\pi_X(v)\bar\tau_X,
\]
which proves the pressure-gradient identity.  Differentiating the normalized
law gives the score formula and hence the synthesis reconstruction.

For the rank statement, the quadratic form of the reward covariance on $v$ is
\[
 \mathbb E_X|\langle v,g_X-\mathbb E_Xg_X\rangle|^2.
\]
Faithfulness makes this zero exactly when $\langle v,g_X\rangle$ is constant
on the finite support.  The orthogonal complement of this kernel is the span of
all reward differences, whose dimension is the affine dimension of the reward
image.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Pressure-jet reconstruction of the complete mixed action Gram]
\label{thm:reward-pressure-jet}
In the setting of \Cref{thm:reward-pressure-reconstruction}, put
\[
 \bar\tau_X(q)=\mathbb E_{X,q}\tau_X,
 \qquad
 \delta_X=D\bar\tau_X(0),
 \qquad
 m_{2,X}=\mathbb E_X\tau_X^2.
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{
 D^2\mathcal P_X(0)=\bar\tau_X^{-1}S_X^*S_X\succeq0,}
\]
\[
 \boxed{\delta_X=T_X^*S_X,}
\]
and
\[
 \boxed{
 G_X^*G_X
 =\bar\tau_XD^2\mathcal P_X(0)
 +\delta_X^*\pi_X+\pi_X^*\delta_X
 +m_{2,X}\pi_X^*\pi_X.}
\]
Consequently, if
\[
 E_X=E_{g,X}\oplus E_{{\rm mat},X}\oplus E_{{\rm gauge},X}
 \oplus E_{{\rm pot},X}\oplus E_{{\rm ct},X}\oplus E_{{\rm bdry},X}
\]
and every sector reward is represented on the same marked cycle record, one
pressure surface reconstructs every marginal and mixed action block.  No
independent relative action router remains.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Differentiate
$\mathcal L_X(q,\mathcal P_X(q))=1$ twice.  Linearity of $q\mapsto g_{q,X}$
gives
\[
 0=\mathbb E_X\!
 \left[(g_u+\pi_X(u)\tau_X)(g_v+\pi_X(v)\tau_X)
 -D^2\mathcal P_X(0)[u,v]\tau_X\right].
\]
The first factors are $-S_Xu$ and $-S_Xv$, proving the Hessian identity.
Differentiating $\bar\tau_X(q)$ gives
$\delta_X(v)=\mathbb E_X[\tau_XS_Xv]=T_X^*S_Xv$.  Finally expand
$G_X=-S_X-T_X\pi_X$ and substitute
$S_X^*S_X=\bar\tau_XD^2\mathcal P_X(0)$,
$T_X^*S_X=\delta_X$, and $T_X^*T_X=m_{2,X}$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Protected Palatini--Cartan--Holst graph writer]
\label{thm:SMST-PCH-graph-writer}
Assume the finite protected field tuple contains the coframe, Cartan
connection, incidence, oriented normals, physical duration, boundary data, and
the already reconstructed coefficients on one nondegenerate logarithm branch.
Then the complete Palatini--Cartan--Holst bulk plus boundary functional
\[
 \boxed{g_{\rm PCH}=S_{\rm bulk}+S_{\partial}}
\]
is a deterministic real-analytic function of that tuple.  Appending the graph
coordinate
\[
 \Theta\longmapsto(\Theta,g_{\rm PCH}(\Theta))
\]
is an exactly conservative one-way writer: discarding the new coordinate
recovers every old probability and payload map, and the generated record
algebra is canonically isomorphic to the old one.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
All contractions, wedge products, incidence sums, boundary restrictions, and
matrix functions entering the finite action are fixed functions of the
protected tuple on the selected branch.  The graph map is injective and its
projection to the first coordinate is its inverse.  Summing over the appended
coordinate therefore recovers the old cylinder exactly, and every function of
the new coordinate already belongs to the old finite record algebra.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Writer-native Hodge and reward closure]
\label{thm:SMST-PCH-writer-closure}
Let
\[
 C^0\xrightarrow{d_0}C^1\xrightarrow{d_1}C^2,
 \qquad d_1d_0=0,
\]
be the protected finite variation complex, and let
\(\Sigma_{\rm PCH}:V_{\rm Ein}\to C^0\) be the directional first variation of
\(g_{\rm PCH}\).  Put
\[
 \boxed{A_{\rm PCH}=d_0\Sigma_{\rm PCH}.}
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{
 A_{\rm PCH}^*(I-d_0d_0^\dagger)A_{\rm PCH}=0,}
\]
\[
 \boxed{d_1A_{\rm PCH}=0,
 \qquad H^*A_{\rm PCH}=0,}
\]
where \(H\) synthesizes the harmonic one-cochains.  Hence every period, curl,
and harmonic residual of the differentiated writer vanishes.

If the same deterministic function \(g_{\rm PCH}\) is inserted as the
protected gravitational reward in the renewal-pressure packet and the same
nuisance sources are shorted from the pressure and Palatini--Holst--volume
columns, the pressure reconstruction returns that reward exactly and its
shorted source lies in the Palatini--Holst--volume source range.  The
corresponding Palatini Schur residual is therefore zero.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
By construction \(A_{\rm PCH}\subseteq\Ran d_0\), so the orthogonal projection
onto the exact range fixes it.  The relation \(d_1d_0=0\) gives the curl
identity, and the harmonic space is orthogonal to \(\Ran d_0\).  Renewal
pressure reconstructs the complete uncentered reward uniquely from its
protected score and duration; inserting \(g_{\rm PCH}\) therefore returns the
same function.  Orthogonal nuisance shorting is linear, so the shorted reward
remains the same fixed coefficient combination of the shorted physical action
columns, and its Schur innovation vanishes.
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[Deterministic action provenance is not dynamical stationarity]
The preceding writer theorem proves that the proposed finite action is
non-arbitrary and that its formal Hodge and reward provenance close.  It does
not prove that the observed accepted transition is Gibbs, Bregman proximal, or
generated by that action.  The same-history accepted/common-action likelihood
test and the reference-measure Ward tests remain independent.
\end{firewall}

\begin{firewall}[Accepted count versus physical action]
\label{fire:count-action-residual}
The accepted-count source is the constant line in the accepted-cycle record.
For a physical action synthesis $G_X$, its count-short residual is
\[
 G_X^*(I-P_{\one})G_X
 =G_X^*G_X-(G_X^*\one)(G_X^*\one)^*\succeq0.
\]
It vanishes only when every action slope is cyclewise constant.  The accepted
count therefore calibrates the affine action component; its orthogonal
residual is generally genuine physical fluctuation and must not be forced to
zero.
\end{firewall}

\begin{theorem}[Finite common-action exactness]
\label{thm:common-action-exactness}
Let $\mathscr V_X$ be the finite protected variation complex: vertices are
finite physical configurations, oriented edges are primitive geometric or
matter variations, and $2$-cells encode commuting-variation or declared
relation loops.  Let $\alpha_X\in C^1(\mathscr V_X;\R)$ be the protected
cycle-action increment.  There is a scalar common action
$\mathscr S_X$ with
\[
 \boxed{\alpha_X=d_0\mathscr S_X}
\]
if and only if
\[
 \boxed{d_1\alpha_X=0}
\]
on every $2$-cell and all periods of $\alpha_X$ on one integral basis of
$H_1(\mathscr V_X;\Z)$ vanish.  After fixing one action anchor,
$\mathscr S_X$ is unique and is reconstructed by path integration.

If $P_{\rm ex}$, $P_{\rm har}$, and $P_{\rm coex}$ are the finite Hodge
projections on $C^1$ and $\sigma_{\rm coex}>0$ is the least singular value of
$d_1$ on the coexact range, then
\[
 \boxed{
 \operatorname{dist}(\alpha_X,\Ran d_0)^2
 \le\|P_{\rm har}\alpha_X\|^2
 +\sigma_{\rm coex}^{-2}\|d_1\alpha_X\|^2.}
\]
Thus face-curl and period Grams give a quantitative obstruction to one common
scalar action.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
If $\alpha_X=d_0\mathscr S_X$, telescoping gives zero face sums and zero
periods.  Conversely fix a base configuration and define $\mathscr S_X(q)$ by
summing $\alpha_X$ along a path from the base to $q$.  Face closure makes the
sum invariant under elementary relation moves and the period conditions make
it invariant under the remaining homology class.  This gives a well-defined
primitive.  Anchoring removes the additive constant.

The finite Hodge decomposition is
$C^1=\Ran d_0\oplus\mathcal H^1\oplus\Ran d_1^*$.  The distance to the exact
range is the squared norm of the harmonic and coexact components.  On the
coexact range,
$\|d_1\beta\|\ge\sigma_{\rm coex}\|\beta\|$, which yields the estimate.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Potential and counterterm exactness]
\label{thm:potential-counterterm-exactness}
Let $r_y(\phi)>0$ be a protected conditional Radon--Nikodym coordinate on a
finite field-configuration record.  Then
\[
 \boxed{V_y(\phi)=-\log r_y(\phi)}
\]
is a protected potential writer and the primitive field-move force
\[
 f_y(\phi\to\phi')
 =-\log\frac{r_y(\phi')}{r_y(\phi)}
\]
satisfies
\[
 \boxed{f_y=d_0V_y.}
\]
Thus all field-space curls and periods vanish identically.  Conditional
likelihood ratios determine the matter Euler force; an additive function of
the external geometry remains invisible to that conditional law and is fixed
by the pressure/partition anchor.

Likewise, a proposed local counterterm derivative
$c_X\in C^1(\mathscr V_X;\R)$ is the derivative of a scalar counterterm action
if and only if
\[
 \boxed{d_1c_X=0}
\]
and its periods vanish.  Given a predeclared allowed counterterm synthesis
$C_X:F_X\to\mathcal H_X$ and a raw action source
$R_X:E_X\to\mathcal H_X$, the irreducible residual after optimal allowed
cancellation is
\[
 \boxed{
 R_X^*(I-P_{C_X})R_X
 =R_X^*R_X-R_X^*C_X(C_X^*C_X)^\dagger C_X^*R_X.}
\]
A nonzero exactness or Schur residual is a genuine anomaly or additional force
source rather than a removable scheme choice.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The potential identity is the logarithm of a ratio and therefore telescopes on
every path.  Strict positivity and finite functional calculus place $V_y$ in
the same protected classical algebra.  Multiplication of $r_y$ by a positive
factor depending only on $y$ shifts $V_y$ by an external additive function,
leaving all field differences unchanged.

The counterterm exactness criterion is
\Cref{thm:common-action-exactness} applied to $c_X$.  For the cancellation
formula, write
$R_X=P_{C_X}R_X+(I-P_{C_X})R_X$.  For any coefficient router $K$,
\[
 R_X+C_XK=(I-P_{C_X})R_X
 +C_X\bigl(K+(C_X^*C_X)^\dagger C_X^*R_X\bigr),
\]
and the two terms are orthogonal.  Minimizing the Gram over $K$ leaves exactly
the displayed Schur residual.
\end{proof}


% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
\subsubsection{Accepted determining-field quotient and same-history action consistency}
\label{sec:accepted-action-consistency}
% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

The accepted-response clock determines when an update occurs, but it does not
by itself determine the updated physical field.  The correct field state and
action comparison are reconstructed from the complete accepted cylinder rather
than selected after the fact.

\begin{definition}[Minimal determining-field quotient and accepted kernel]
\label{def:minimal-determining-field}
Let $\widetilde\Theta_X$ be the finite generated ledger carrying the declared
coframe, connection, matter, gauge, boundary, metric, common-action, reward,
duration, and resolved accepted-branch coordinates.  Two ledger values are
future equivalent, $x\sim_{{\rm fld},X}y$, when every admitted future word and
every one of these determining coordinates has the same value from $x$ and
$y$, including all branch-domain indicators.  Put
\[
 \boxed{
 \Theta_{{\rm fld},X}^{\min}
 :=\widetilde\Theta_X/\!\sim_{{\rm fld},X}.}
\]
For the set $\mathscr A_{{\rm acc},X}$ of resolved accepted subbranches, define
on the positive-acceptance domain
\[
 \boxed{
 K_X^{\rm acc}(\theta'\mid\theta)
 :=\frac{1}{p_{{\rm acc},X}(\theta)}
   \sum_{\substack{a\in\mathscr A_{{\rm acc},X}:\\
        u_a^{\min}(\theta)=\theta'}}p_{a,X}(\theta).}
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Terminating determining-field and accepted-kernel compiler]
\label{thm:determining-field-compiler}
The quotient of \Cref{def:minimal-determining-field} is the unique coarsest
finite record through which every selected determining-field future and every
primitive update factors.  A partition refinement beginning with the immediate
coordinates and branch domains stabilizes after at most
$|\widetilde\Theta_X|-1$ strict rounds.  The kernel $K_X^{\rm acc}$ is well
defined, table native, and is the unique accepted transition reproducing all
selected post-accepted field futures.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Future equality is a typed right congruence: if $x\sim_{{\rm fld},X}y$, then
for every primitive branch $a$ and continuation $w$,
$d(u_wu_a(x))=d(u_{wa}(x))=d(u_{wa}(y))=d(u_wu_a(y))$.  Hence every update
descends.  At each refinement round split two states whenever an immediate
coordinate differs or one primitive update reaches different blocks.  The
$k$th partition identifies exactly the states not separated by a future of
length at most $k$; each strict refinement increases the number of blocks, so
termination is finite.  The stable quotient has the stated universal property.
The accepted branch probabilities and target quotient classes are constant on
its fibres, which makes the displayed kernel well defined.  Summing the
resolved branches whose target lies in a prescribed quotient class gives the
probability of that post-accepted Read, proving uniqueness.
\end{proof}


\begin{definition}[Stationary accepted joint table and residuals]
\label{def:accepted-joint-table}
Let
\[
 J_{xy}=\Pr(X_0=x,X_1=y\mid\mathrm{acc})
\]
be a finite stationary accepted initial--terminal table with faithful marginal
$\mu$, and put $D_\mu=\operatorname{diag}(\mu)$.  Define
\[
 \Delta_{\rm marg}
 =\|J\one-\mu\|_2^2+\|J^*\one-\mu\|_2^2,
\]
\[
 \Delta_{\rm rev}=\|J-J^*\|_{\rm HS}^2,
 \qquad
 \Delta_{\rm idem}=\|JD_\mu^{-1}J-J\|_{\rm HS}^2.
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Accepted-table reconstruction of a Gibbs partition projection]
\label{thm:accepted-joint-table}
The three residuals of \Cref{def:accepted-joint-table} vanish if and only if
\[
 R=D_\mu^{-1}J
\]
is a stochastic, $\mu$-reversible, idempotent Markov kernel.  On that branch
there is a unique partition $\mathscr P$ of the accepted field space such that
\[
 \boxed{
 R_{xy}=\one_{\{C(x)=C(y)\}}
 \frac{\mu_y}{\mu(C(x))},
 \qquad
 J_{xy}=\one_{\{C(x)=C(y)\}}
 \frac{\mu_x\mu_y}{\mu(C(x))}.}
\]
The blocks are the connected components of the support graph $J_{xy}>0$.
The same table reconstructs the stationary free action
\[
 \boxed{\mathcal F_J(x)=-\log\mu_x}
\]
up to an additive constant and, on every supported transition,
\[
 \boxed{
 \log\frac{R_{xy}}{R_{yx}}
 +\mathcal F_J(y)-\mathcal F_J(x)=0.}
\]
Thus a separate free-action-increment column is redundant on the reversible
accepted branch.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The marginal residual makes $R$ stochastic and stationary for $\mu$.
Symmetry of $J=D_\mu R$ is detailed balance, and the idempotency residual is
exactly $R^2-R$ after multiplication by $D_\mu$.  A reversible idempotent
kernel is an orthogonal projection in $L^2(\mu)$ which is also positive and
unital.  Its range is therefore a finite function algebra, hence the functions
constant on the blocks of a unique partition.  Orthogonal projection onto that
algebra is conditional expectation, giving the displayed rows.  The support
components recover the blocks because every row is strictly positive on its
own block.  Finally detailed balance gives the logarithmic free-action
identity.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Finite affinity Hodge compiler]
\label{thm:accepted-affinity-Hodge}
For a general bidirected accepted support graph, define the edge affinity
\[
 \ell_{xy}=\log\frac{R_{xy}}{R_{yx}}.
\]
Let $B$ be an oriented incidence matrix and put
\[
 P_{\rm cut}=B^*(BB^*)^\dagger B,
 \qquad P_{\rm cyc}=I-P_{\rm cut}.
\]
Then the following are equivalent:
\[
 \boxed{\ell=-B^*\mathcal F\text{ for some scalar }\mathcal F,}
\]
\[
 \boxed{P_{\rm cyc}\ell=0,}
\]
and vanishing of every cycle affinity.  The canonical least-squares free action
is
\[
 \boxed{\mathcal F_*=-(BB^*)^\dagger B\ell,}
\]
and
\[
 \boxed{
 \inf_{\mathcal F}\|\ell+B^*\mathcal F\|_2^2
 =\|P_{\rm cyc}\ell\|_2^2.}
\]
A spanning forest reconstructs the candidate potential and one period on each
fundamental cycle completes the audit.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The orthogonal decomposition of edge cochains is
$\C^E=\Ran B^*\oplus\Ker B$.  Projection onto the first summand gives the
Moore--Penrose solution and projection onto the second gives the minimum
residual.  An edge cochain lies in $\Ran B^*$ exactly when all of its cycle
periods vanish.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Protected Reads surviving an accepted projection]
\label{thm:accepted-projection-read-survival}
Let $R_{\mathscr P}$ be the conditional expectation associated with an
accepted partition $\mathscr P$, and let $G$ be a protected physical Read.
Then $R_{\mathscr P}$ preserves every function of $G$ if and only if every
partition block is contained in one fibre of $G$.  If the retained Reads
separate all field configurations, the only preserving idempotent accepted
kernel is the identity.

For the count projection $R_K$ on $M$ exchangeable renewal cells,
\[
 \boxed{R_K\varphi_i=\frac1M\sum_{j=1}^{M}\varphi_j,}
 \qquad
 \boxed{\|(I-R_K)\varphi_i\|_2^2=1-\frac1M.}
\]
Every nonconstant spatial Fourier mode $\Phi_k$ satisfies
\[
 \boxed{R_K\Phi_k=0.}
\]
Hence count equilibration can preserve a local spacetime field only when it
acts on a separate microscopic factor:
\[
 \mathsf X=\mathsf X_{\rm geom}\times\mathsf X_{\rm micro},
 \qquad R=I_{\rm geom}\otimes R_{\rm mix},
\]
up to source-minimal equivalence.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Conditional expectation fixes a function exactly when it is measurable with
respect to the partition algebra.  This is equivalent to constancy on each
partition block and proves the first claim.  Exchangeability gives
$\mathbb E[\varphi_i\mid K]=M^{-1}\sum_j\varphi_j$; orthogonality and unit
variance give the norm formula.  A nonconstant Fourier coefficient sums to
zero and is orthogonal to every function of the count, proving its
annihilation.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Exact first-chaos spectrum and projection--persistence tradeoff]
\label{thm:projection-persistence-tradeoff}
For the unmodulated flip--interchange regulator on the three-torus,
\[
 \mathcal L_N^0\Phi_N(c)
 =\Phi_N\left(\kappa_NN^2\Delta_Nc-\frac{22\lambda_N}{15}c\right).
\]
A Fourier mode $e_{k,N}$ has decay rate
\[
 \boxed{
 \Lambda_{k,N}=\frac{22\lambda_N}{15}
 +4\kappa_NN^2\sum_{j=1}^{3}\sin^2\frac{\pi k_j}{N}.}
\]
Put
\[
 q_N=4\frac{\kappa_N}{\lambda_N}N^2\sin^2\frac\pi N.
\]
For the actual completed-private dwell, the operator-norm error of pure
interchange relative to the count projection obeys
\[
 \boxed{
 \varepsilon_N^{\rm proj}\ge
 E(q_N):=\frac{8/15}{(q_N+4/5)(q_N+2/3)}.}
\]
The renewal-clock persistence of the first nonconstant spatial mode is
\[
 \boxed{A_N(s)=\exp\left[-s\left(\frac{22}{15}+q_N\right)\right].}
\]
If $0<\varepsilon_N^{\rm proj}\le\varepsilon\le1$, then
\[
 \boxed{
 q_N\ge\frac{\sqrt{1+120/\varepsilon}-11}{15},}
\]
and therefore
\[
 \boxed{
 A_N(s)\le
 \exp\left[-\frac{s}{15}
 \left(11+\sqrt{1+120/\varepsilon}\right)\right].}
\]
In particular, projection accuracy tending to zero and persistence of one
nonconstant spatial mode for a positive renewal time are incompatible.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The first-chaos generator follows by combining the local renewal eigenvalue
$-22\lambda_N/15$ with the discrete exchange Laplacian.  The completed-private
dwell has generating function
$8z^2/[(5-z)(3-z)]$; applying spectral calculus to the slowest nonconstant
interchange eigenvalue gives $E(q_N)$.  The persistence formula is the same
first-chaos eigenvalue expressed in renewal time.  Solving
$E(q_N)\le\varepsilon$ for $q_N\ge0$ and substituting it in $A_N(s)$ gives the
last two inequalities.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Singular two-clock limit]
\label{thm:renewal-interchange-two-clock}
Assume $\kappa_N/\lambda_N\to\infty$.  For every smooth test profile $f$:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2.8em]
\item on the fast clock $t=\sigma/\kappa_N$,
      \[
       \boxed{
       e^{(\sigma/\kappa_N)\mathcal L_N^0}\Phi_N(f)
       \longrightarrow\Phi_N(e^{\sigma\Delta}f);}
      \]
\item on the slow renewal clock $t=s/\lambda_N$, $s>0$,
      \[
       \boxed{
       e^{(s/\lambda_N)\mathcal L_N^0}\Phi_N(f)
       \longrightarrow e^{-22s/15}\Phi_N(\overline f).}
      \]
\end{enumerate}
Thus the count projection is a fast nuisance reduction followed by a slow
scalar count relaxation.  It is not a local reaction--diffusion evolution on
the same slow clock.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Use the exact Fourier spectrum of
\Cref{thm:projection-persistence-tradeoff}.  On the fast clock the reaction
factor tends to one and each fixed Fourier exchange factor tends to the heat
multiplier.  On the slow clock every nonzero spatial mode has exponent
$-s(\kappa_N/\lambda_N)4\pi^2|k|^2+o(1)$ and vanishes, while the zero mode
retains the reaction multiplier $e^{-22s/15}$.
\end{proof}

\begin{assessment}[Free action and the accepted-field boundary]
The accepted stationary table reconstructs its own free-action cochain.  A
Palatini, matter, counterterm, or reference writer enters only through a
same-history comparison with that cochain.  Stationarity of the accepted free
law is therefore weaker than vanishing first variation of an independently
loaded Einstein action.  Likewise, an idempotent count projection and a local
spacetime evolution are different clock-level objects unless the projection
acts only on a protected microscopic factor.
\end{assessment}

Let $\Theta\subset\R^d$ be one compact determining-field chart.  Let
$\Psi\in C^2(\Theta)$ be the operational Fisher potential,
$G(\theta)=\nabla^2\Psi(\theta)$, and assume
\[
 mI\preceq G(\theta)\preceq MI.
\]
Let the reconstructed common action $\mathcal A\in C^2(\Theta)$ satisfy
\[
 -\lambda G(\theta)\preceq D^2\mathcal A(\theta)
 \preceq L G(\theta),
 \qquad \eta\lambda<1.
\]
For
\[
 D_\Psi(y,\theta)
 =\Psi(y)-\Psi(\theta)
  -\langle\nabla\Psi(\theta),y-\theta\rangle,
\]
define
\[
 \Phi_\theta(y)=\mathcal A(y)+\eta^{-1}D_\Psi(y,\theta),
 \qquad y_\theta^*=\arg\min_y\Phi_\theta(y).
\]

\begin{definition}[Accepted Fisher--Bregman action gap]
\label{def:accepted-action-gap}
For one observed accepted transition $\theta\to y$, put
\[
 \boxed{
 \Delta_\Psi(\theta,y)
 :=\Phi_\theta(y)-\Phi_\theta(y_\theta^*)\ge0.}
\]
If the complete feedback kernel is
$K=(1-\vartheta)I+\vartheta K^{\rm acc}$ with state-independent
$\vartheta>0$ and stationary law $\nu$, define
\[
 \boxed{
 \overline\Delta_\Psi
 :=\int\nu(\dd\theta)K^{\rm acc}(\dd y\mid\theta)
       \Delta_\Psi(\theta,y).}
\]
The supported stationarity form is
\[
 \mathfrak S(\theta)
 :=\nabla\mathcal A(\theta)^*G(\theta)^{-1}
   \nabla\mathcal A(\theta).
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Accepted Bregman gap forces common-action stationarity]
\label{thm:accepted-Bregman-stationarity}
Put
\[
 \Lambda_\Phi=(\eta^{-1}+L)M,
 \qquad \ell=\max\{\lambda,L\}.
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{
 \int D_\Psi(y,\theta)\,
       \nu(\dd\theta)K^{\rm acc}(\dd y\mid\theta)
 \le\eta\overline\Delta_\Psi,}
\]
\[
 \boxed{
 \int\|y-\theta\|^2\,
       \nu(\dd\theta)K^{\rm acc}(\dd y\mid\theta)
 \le\frac{2\eta}{m}\overline\Delta_\Psi,}
\]
and
\[
 \boxed{
 \int\mathfrak S(\theta)\,\nu(\dd\theta)
 \le C_{\Psi,\mathcal A,\eta}\overline\Delta_\Psi,}
\]
where
\[
 \boxed{
 C_{\Psi,\mathcal A,\eta}
 =\frac{4\Lambda_\Phi}{m}
  +\frac{4M^2(1+\eta\ell)^2}{m^2\eta}.}
\]
In particular, $\overline\Delta_\Psi=0$ forces the complete represented
common-action first variation to vanish $\nu$-almost surely.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Stationarity of $K$ and state independence of acceptance give
$\nu K^{\rm acc}=\nu$.  Since $y_\theta^*$ minimizes $\Phi_\theta$,
\[
 \mathcal A(y)-\mathcal A(\theta)
 +\eta^{-1}D_\Psi(y,\theta)
 \le\Delta_\Psi(\theta,y).
\]
Averaging cancels the action difference and proves the first estimate.  The
metric floor gives $D_\Psi(y,\theta)\ge(m/2)\|y-\theta\|^2$, proving the
second.

The KKT residual
\[
 r_\Psi(\theta,y)
 =\nabla\Psi(y)-\nabla\Psi(\theta)+\eta\nabla\mathcal A(y)
\]
satisfies
$\|r_\Psi\|^2\le2\eta^2\Lambda_\Phi\Delta_\Psi$ by smooth convexity of
$\Phi_\theta$.  Moreover
\[
 \eta\nabla\mathcal A(\theta)
 =r_\Psi-\bigl(\nabla\Psi(y)-\nabla\Psi(\theta)\bigr)
 +\eta\bigl(\nabla\mathcal A(\theta)-\nabla\mathcal A(y)\bigr).
\]
The Hessian bounds control the two differences by $M\|y-\theta\|$ and
$\ell M\|y-\theta\|$.  Squaring in the inverse Fisher metric, integrating,
and using the first two bounds gives the displayed constant.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Finite Gibbs/KL accepted-row certificate]
\label{cor:accepted-Gibbs-gap}
Let $p_\theta(y)>0$ be the pre-update reference law on a finite terminal field
record and let $c_\theta(y)$ be the independently reconstructed same-history
common-action cost.  Then
\[
 \boxed{
 q_\theta^*(y)
 =\frac{p_\theta(y)e^{-\eta c_\theta(y)}}
        {\sum_zp_\theta(z)e^{-\eta c_\theta(z)}}}
\]
is the unique entropy-proximal row, and
\[
 \boxed{
 \Delta_{{\rm Gibbs},\theta}
 :=\eta^{-1}D_{\rm KL}
   \bigl(K^{\rm acc}(\cdot\mid\theta)\Vert q_\theta^*\bigr)}
\]
is exactly the row-wise action gap.  Its stationary average is an instance of
$\overline\Delta_\Psi$ and vanishes precisely when the observed likelihood
ratio obeys the common-action Gibbs identity.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
For a probability row $q$,
\[
 \sum_yq(y)c_\theta(y)+\eta^{-1}D_{\rm KL}(q\Vert p_\theta)
 =\eta^{-1}D_{\rm KL}(q\Vert q_\theta^*)
  -\eta^{-1}\log\sum_zp_\theta(z)e^{-\eta c_\theta(z)}.
\]
Relative entropy is nonnegative and vanishes only at equality.  The
negative-entropy Fisher potential identifies this row gap with the Bregman gap
of \Cref{def:accepted-action-gap}.
\end{proof}

% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
\subsubsection{Source-preserving accepted occurrence and entropic stationarization}
\label{sec:accepted-occurrence-compiler}
% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

\begin{definition}[Finite accepted occurrence packet]
\label{def:accepted-occurrence-packet}
Let $\Theta$ be a finite determining-field record and let
$\mathcal E\subseteq\Theta_{\rm s}\times\Theta_{\rm t}$ be the physical
same-history accepted-transition relation.  Let $\nu$ be a faithful
probability on both copies and let $Q$ be the independently reconstructed
common-action comparator, with
\[
 Q(x,y)>0\iff(x,y)\in\mathcal E,
 \qquad \sum_yQ(x,y)=1.
\]
Put
\[
 \boxed{R(x,y)=\nu(x)Q(x,y),
 \qquad \rho=\nu Q.}
 \tag{AO.1}
\]
For probability laws $\alpha,\beta$ on the source and target copies, define
\[
 \Pi_{\mathcal E}(\alpha,\beta)
 =\left\{\pi\ge0:
   \sum_y\pi(x,y)=\alpha(x),\qquad
   \sum_x\pi(x,y)=\beta(y)
  \right\}.
 \tag{AO.2}
\]
The stationary occurrence polytope is
$\Pi_{\mathcal E}(\nu):=\Pi_{\mathcal E}(\nu,\nu)$.
The comparator $Q$ and its support are fixed before an observed accepted law
is examined.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Weighted Hall occurrence and exact unroutable mass]
\label{thm:accepted-weighted-Hall}
For $U\subseteq\Theta_{\rm s}$ let
\[
 N(U)=\{y\in\Theta_{\rm t}:\exists x\in U\text{ with }(x,y)\in\mathcal E\}.
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{
 \Pi_{\mathcal E}(\alpha,\beta)\ne\varnothing
 \iff
 \alpha(U)\le\beta(N(U))
 \quad\text{for every }U\subseteq\Theta_{\rm s}.}
 \tag{AO.3}
\]
Furthermore, the maximum mass transportable from $\alpha$ to $\beta$ along
$\mathcal E$ is
\[
 \boxed{
 1-\mathfrak h_{\mathcal E}(\alpha,\beta),
 \qquad
 \mathfrak h_{\mathcal E}(\alpha,\beta)
 =\max_U[\alpha(U)-\beta(N(U))]_+.}
 \tag{AO.4}
\]
Thus a positive Hall defect is the exact mass which no admitted same-history
transition can route.  In particular, a $\nu$-stationary accepted law exists
exactly when $\nu(U)\le\nu(N(U))$ for every $U$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Necessity follows because all mass emitted from $U$ must arrive in $N(U)$.
For sufficiency, form a network with source capacities $\alpha(x)$, target
capacities $\beta(y)$, and infinite-capacity edges precisely on
$\mathcal E$.  A finite cut determined by $U$ has capacity
$1-\alpha(U)+\beta(N(U))$.  The Hall inequalities make every cut have
capacity at least one, so max-flow/min-cut gives a unit coupling.  Without the
inequalities, the minimum cut is
$1-\max_U[\alpha(U)-\beta(N(U))]$, proving \textup{(AO.4)}.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Canonical entropic occurrence law and information Pythagoras]
\label{thm:accepted-entropic-projection}
Assume $\Pi_{\mathcal E}(\nu)$ is nonempty and restrict $\mathcal E$ to the
union of supports of its feasible couplings.  Then the problem
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathfrak D_{\rm occ}
 :=\min_{\pi\in\Pi_{\mathcal E}(\nu)}
   D_{\rm KL}(\pi\Vert R)}
 \tag{AO.5}
\]
has a unique minimizer $\pi^{\rm occ}$.  There are source and target
potentials $a,b$ such that, on the feasible edge face,
\[
 \boxed{
 \pi^{\rm occ}(x,y)=R(x,y)e^{a(x)+b(y)},
 \qquad
 K^{\rm occ}(x,y)=Q(x,y)e^{a(x)+b(y)}.}
 \tag{AO.6}
\]
The coupling is unique; on each connected component of the feasible bipartite
support, $(a,b)$ is unique up to the gauge
$a\mapsto a+c$, $b\mapsto b-c$.
For every stationary feasible coupling $\pi$,
\[
 \boxed{
 D_{\rm KL}(\pi\Vert R)
 =D_{\rm KL}(\pi\Vert\pi^{\rm occ})
  +D_{\rm KL}(\pi^{\rm occ}\Vert R).}
 \tag{AO.7}
\]
Hence, for an observed stationary coupling $\pi^{\rm obs}$, the selection
residual
\[
 \mathfrak D_{\rm sel}
 :=D_{\rm KL}(\pi^{\rm obs}\Vert\pi^{\rm occ})
\]
satisfies
\[
 \boxed{
 D_{\rm KL}(\pi^{\rm obs}\Vert R)
 =\mathfrak D_{\rm occ}+\mathfrak D_{\rm sel}.}
 \tag{AO.8}
\]
The unavoidable occurrence cost vanishes exactly when $\nu Q=\nu$; the
selection residual vanishes exactly when the observed law is the canonical
entropic projection.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The feasible set is a nonempty compact polytope.  On its canonical feasible
face, $R$ is positive, and relative entropy is strictly convex; existence and
uniqueness follow.  Lagrange multipliers for the two marginals give
$\log(\pi^{\rm occ}/R)=a(x)+b(y)$ and hence \textup{(AO.6)}.  For any two
couplings with the same marginals,
\[
 \sum_{x,y}(\pi-\pi^{\rm occ})(a(x)+b(y))=0.
\]
Expanding the three relative entropies therefore proves \textup{(AO.7)}.
Finally, $R$ itself is stationary exactly when $\rho=\nu$, and relative
entropy vanishes only at equality.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Source-shorted occurrence Laplacian and Thomson correction]
\label{thm:accepted-occurrence-Laplacian}
Equip $\R^{\mathcal E}$ with
\[
 \langle h,k\rangle_{R^{-1}}
 =\sum_{(x,y)\in\mathcal E}\frac{h(x,y)k(x,y)}{R(x,y)}.
\]
Let $Ah$ and $Bh$ be the source row-sum and target column-sum maps, and put
\[
 P_{\rm s}=I-A^*\operatorname{diag}(\nu)^{-1}A,
 \qquad
 \boxed{
 \mathcal L_{\nu,Q}=BP_{\rm s}B^*
 =\operatorname{diag}(\rho)
  -Q^{\mathsf T}\operatorname{diag}(\nu)Q\succeq0.}
 \tag{AO.9}
\]
For every target potential $u$,
\[
 \boxed{
 \langle u,\mathcal L_{\nu,Q}u\rangle
 =\sum_x\nu(x)\operatorname{Var}_{Q(x,\cdot)}(u).}
 \tag{AO.10}
\]
Let $d=\nu-\rho$.  The constraints
$Ah=0$, $Bh=d$ are solvable exactly when
$d\in\Ran\mathcal L_{\nu,Q}$, and on that branch
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal E_{\rm occ}
 :=\min_{Ah=0,\,Bh=d}\|h\|_{R^{-1}}^2
 =\langle d,\mathcal L_{\nu,Q}^{\dagger}d\rangle.}
 \tag{AO.11}
\]
The unique minimum-norm correction is
\[
 \boxed{
 h_*(x,y)=R(x,y)\bigl[u(y)-(Qu)(x)\bigr],
 \qquad
 u=\mathcal L_{\nu,Q}^{\dagger}d.}
 \tag{AO.12}
\]
Its leverage is
\[
 \vartheta_{\rm occ}
 =\max_{(x,y)\in\mathcal E}|u(y)-(Qu)(x)|.
\]
If $\vartheta_{\rm occ}\le\tfrac12$, then
$\pi^{\rm lin}=R+h_*$ is a positive element of
$\Pi_{\mathcal E}(\nu)$ and
\[
 \boxed{
 \frac13\mathcal E_{\rm occ}
 \le D_{\rm KL}(\pi^{\rm lin}\Vert R)
 \le\mathcal E_{\rm occ},
 \qquad
 \mathfrak D_{\rm occ}\le\mathcal E_{\rm occ}.}
 \tag{AO.13}
\]
The kernel of $\mathcal L_{\nu,Q}$ consists of functions constant on every
connected component of the target-overlap graph generated by common row
supports of $Q$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The weighted adjoints are
$(A^*f)(x,y)=R(x,y)f(x)$ and
$(B^*g)(x,y)=R(x,y)g(y)$, while
$AA^*=\operatorname{diag}(\nu)$ and
$BB^*=\operatorname{diag}(\rho)$.  Hence $P_{\rm s}$ is the orthogonal
projection onto $\Ker A$, and direct multiplication gives \textup{(AO.9)}.
Expanding its quadratic form proves \textup{(AO.10)} and the kernel statement.
Restricting $B$ to $\Ker A$, its target Gram is $BP_{\rm s}B^*$; the
Moore--Penrose minimum-norm theorem gives \textup{(AO.11)} and
$h_*=P_{\rm s}B^*\mathcal L_{\nu,Q}^{\dagger}d$.  Expanding the projection
gives \textup{(AO.12)}.

Under the leverage bound, every factor
$1+h_*(x,y)/R(x,y)$ lies in $[1/2,3/2]$, so $R+h_*$ is positive and has the
required marginals.  For $|t|\le1/2$,
\[
 \frac13t^2\le(1+t)\log(1+t)-t\le t^2.
\]
Summing with $t=h_*/R$ proves the entropy bounds.  Minimality of
$\pi^{\rm occ}$ gives the final inequality.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Observable and discrepancy control from the occurrence energy]
\label{cor:accepted-occurrence-observables}
Under the range and leverage hypotheses of
\Cref{thm:accepted-occurrence-Laplacian}, write
$K^{\rm lin}(x,y)=\pi^{\rm lin}(x,y)/\nu(x)$.  Then
\[
 \boxed{
 \sum_x\nu(x)
 \|K^{\rm lin}(x,\cdot)-Q(x,\cdot)\|_1^2
 \le2\mathcal E_{\rm occ},}
 \tag{AO.13a}
\]
\[
 \boxed{
 \|\pi^{\rm lin}-R\|_1
 \le\sqrt{2\mathcal E_{\rm occ}},
 \qquad
 \|\nu-\nu Q\|_2^2\le\mathcal E_{\rm occ}.}
 \tag{AO.13b}
\]
Consequently every bounded same-history observable $F$ satisfies
\[
 \boxed{
 \left|\mathbb E_{\pi^{\rm lin}}F-\mathbb E_RF\right|
 \le\|F\|_\infty\sqrt{2\mathcal E_{\rm occ}}.}
 \tag{AO.13c}
\]
Thus the Thomson energy controls not only the action-relative entropy but also
all bounded target Reads and the raw failure of $\nu$ to be stationary for the
common-action comparator.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Pinsker's inequality applied row by row, followed by
\textup{(AO.13)}, gives the first estimate; joint Pinsker gives the first
estimate in \textup{(AO.13b)}.  For $d=\nu-\nu Q=\mathcal L_{\nu,Q}u$,
one has
$0\preceq\mathcal L_{\nu,Q}\preceq\operatorname{diag}(\rho)\preceq I$, and
therefore
\[
 \|d\|_2^2
 =\langle u,\mathcal L_{\nu,Q}^2u\rangle
 \le\langle u,\mathcal L_{\nu,Q}u\rangle
 =\mathcal E_{\rm occ}.
\]
The bounded-observable estimate is total-variation duality.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Occurrence control of the accepted common-action stationarity gap]
\label{cor:accepted-occurrence-stationarity}
Let the comparator $Q$ be the finite Gibbs row of
\Cref{cor:accepted-Gibbs-gap} at action scale $\eta>0$, and let
$\pi^{\rm obs}(x,y)=\nu(x)K^{\rm acc}(x,y)$ be an observed stationary
accepted coupling.  Then
\[
 \boxed{
 \overline\Delta_{\rm Gibbs}^{\rm obs}
 =\eta^{-1}
  \bigl(\mathfrak D_{\rm occ}+\mathfrak D_{\rm sel}\bigr).}
 \tag{AO.14}
\]
On the range and leverage branch of
\Cref{thm:accepted-occurrence-Laplacian},
\[
 \boxed{
 \overline\Delta_{\rm Gibbs}^{\rm obs}
 \le\eta^{-1}
   \bigl(\mathcal E_{\rm occ}+\mathfrak D_{\rm sel}\bigr).}
 \tag{AO.15}
\]
Consequently the hypotheses of
\Cref{thm:accepted-Bregman-stationarity} give
\[
 \boxed{
 \int\mathfrak S(\theta)\,\nu(\dd\theta)
 \le
 \frac{C_{\Psi,\mathcal A,\eta}}{\eta}
 \bigl(\mathcal E_{\rm occ}+\mathfrak D_{\rm sel}\bigr).}
 \tag{AO.16}
\]
Thus regulator-uniform decay of the occurrence energy and the independently
physical selection residual closes the represented common-action first
variation.  On an entropy-optimal or Perron--Doob selected branch,
$\mathfrak D_{\rm sel}=0$.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The same source marginal gives
$D_{\rm KL}(\pi^{\rm obs}\Vert R)$ as the stationary average of the row-wise
relative entropies.  Apply \textup{(AO.8)}, then
\textup{(AO.13)}, and finally
\Cref{thm:accepted-Bregman-stationarity}.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Endpoint fusion invariance of the occurrence action]
\label{thm:accepted-reader-fusion}
Let $\mathcal N$ be the finite physical endpoint record, let
$\mathcal A_n$ be an auxiliary allocation fibre over $n$, and define
\[
 \mathcal H=\ell^2(\mathcal N),
 \qquad
 \widetilde{\mathcal H}
 =\bigoplus_{n\in\mathcal N}\ell^2(\mathcal A_n),
 \qquad
 (Fy)(n)=\sum_{\alpha\in\mathcal A_n}y(n,\alpha).
\]
For a physical endpoint functional $e:\mathcal H\to\C$, put
$\widetilde A=(eF)^*(eF)$.  Then, for every $x\in\Ran F$,
\[
 \boxed{
 \inf_{Fy=x}\langle y,\widetilde Ay\rangle=|ex|^2.}
 \tag{AO.17}
\]
Hence expansion into gauge, Higgs, fermion, gravity, boundary, counterterm,
chart, or provenance coordinates only pulls back the same physical endpoint
action.  The Hall, Thomson, and entropy compilers must be evaluated after
fusion to the physical reader unless an allocation slice is independently
loaded as a source and all mixed allocation blocks are retained.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
If $Fy=x$, then
$\langle y,\widetilde Ay\rangle=\|eFy\|^2=|ex|^2$, independently of the
representative.  Taking the infimum proves the identity and the stated
source-noncreation consequence.
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[Occurrence feasibility is not physical selection]
\label{fire:accepted-occurrence-selection}
The Hall criterion and the entropic or Thomson correction prove that a
stationary action-compatible candidate exists on the declared transition
relation.  They do not prove that the microscopic accepted process uses that
candidate.  The observed kernel and $\mathfrak D_{\rm sel}\to0$, or an
independently loaded entropy-optimal, Perron--Doob, or equivalent selection
law, remain physical rows.  Choosing $Q$ after observing the accepted kernel
would make the test tautological and is inadmissible.
\end{firewall}

\begin{countertheorem}[The accepted renewal bit does not determine a field kernel]
\label{cth:accepted-bit-no-field-kernel}
Fix any state-independent acceptance probability and any two-state determining
field.  The identity accepted kernel and an arbitrary full-support reset kernel
are both idempotent and produce exactly the same acceptance/no-acceptance
record, first-acceptance law, and accepted-count pressure, while their terminal
field laws and common-action Gibbs gaps are generally different.  Hence the
locked accepted-response record alone does not determine the accepted
spacetime-field operation.
\end{countertheorem}

\begin{proof}
Let $K_0^{\rm acc}=I$ and let every row of $K_1^{\rm acc}$ equal one fixed
full-support law $\rho$.  Then $K_0^2=K_0$ and $K_1^2=K_1$.  Apply either map
only after the same state-independent accepted mark and apply the identity on
rejection.  Discarding the terminal field gives the same Bernoulli acceptance
process and all the same renewal-time statistics.  The terminal laws differ.
For a nonconstant independently fixed cost, the identity and reset rows cannot
both equal the same Gibbs comparator for every initial state, so their KL gaps
differ.
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[The action cost is not fitted from the observed kernel]
The Gibbs or Bregman certificate is physical only when the terminal cost is the
common gravitational--matter--gauge--potential--counterterm--boundary action
reconstructed from the protected reward packet.  Every positive transition can
be written as a Gibbs tilt for a cost chosen afterward; such a fitted cost has
no stationarity content.
\end{firewall}

\begin{assessment}[Refined accepted/common-action occurrence boundary]
The determining-field compiler and the Gibbs/Bregman gap decide whether an
acquired accepted update is generated by the reconstructed common action.
When that update additionally lies on a positive reflected branch,
\Cref{cor:SMST-three-cylinder-action-response} reduces its first temporal
closure to one conditional action-response writer and the three stationary
Grams $M_0^\Gamma,M_1^\Gamma,M_2^\Gamma$.  Rank stability certifies that the
current joint gravity--internal action head is reducing; rank growth returns
the exact mixed memory writer to append.  Consequently the remaining classical
occurrence problem is no longer an unnamed dynamical principle.  It is the
