literal acquisition of the accepted/reflected law, the common-action incidence
row, the three-cylinder closure packet, and their cutoff-uniform margins.  The
marginal accepted bit still does not force any of these objects.
\end{assessment}


% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
\subsubsection{Derivative-free face linearization, memory shorting, and torsion control}
\label{sec:renewal-Palatini-upgrade}
% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

The localized gravitational score is evaluated after the persistent geometric
carrier has been fixed and every resolved cut-memory coordinate has been
retained.  Binary renewal divisibility then replaces an assumed derivative at
the zero face, while the connection Euler source replaces an assumed
vanishing torsion.

\begin{theorem}[Derivative-free renewal face linearization]
\label{thm:renewal-face-linearization}
Let $E$ be a finite-dimensional real normed space, let $U\subset E$ be a
balanced convex neighborhood of zero, and let $A:U\to\R$ satisfy $A(0)=0$.
Assume
\[
 \boxed{A(z)=2A(z/2)}
\]
for every $z\in U$, that $A$ is bounded on a neighborhood of zero, and that
for some $r,H>0$,
\[
 \boxed{
 |A(x+y)-A(x)-A(y)|\le H\|x\|\,\|y\|}
\]
whenever $x,y,x+y\in U$ and their norms are at most $r$.  Then $A$ is the
restriction of a unique real linear functional on $E$.

More generally, let
\[
 L_m(z)=2^mA_m(2^{-m}z)
\]
be renormalized face scores on a fixed bounded balanced set.  If
\[
 |L_{m+1}(z)-L_m(z)|\le\varepsilon_m\|z\|,
 \qquad \sum_m\varepsilon_m<\infty,
\]
\[
 |L_m(x+y)-L_m(x)-L_m(y)|
 \le\eta_m\|x\|\,\|y\|,
 \qquad \eta_m\longrightarrow0,
\]
and one $L_m$ is continuous at zero, then $L_m$ converges locally uniformly
to one continuous linear functional $L$, with
\[
 \boxed{
 |L(z)-L_m(z)|
 \le\left(\sum_{n\ge m}\varepsilon_n\right)\|z\|.}
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
For the exact branch, iterate the divisibility relation.  For all sufficiently
large $m$,
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 A(x+y)-A(x)-A(y)
 &=2^m\bigl[A(2^{-m}(x+y))-A(2^{-m}x)-A(2^{-m}y)\bigr],
 \end{aligned}
\]
whose absolute value is at most
$H2^{-m}\|x\|\,\|y\|$.  Letting $m\to\infty$ proves additivity.  An additive
map bounded on a neighborhood of zero is continuous there; rational
homogeneity and continuity then give real homogeneity.  Uniqueness follows
because $U$ contains a neighborhood of zero.

For the stable branch, telescoping gives
\[
 |L_n(z)-L_m(z)|
 \le\left(\sum_{j=m}^{n-1}\varepsilon_j\right)\|z\|,
\]
so $(L_m)$ is locally uniformly Cauchy and has the displayed tail bound.
Passing to the limit in the polarized estimate proves additivity.  The
summable transport bound transfers continuity from one $L_m$ to the limit,
and a continuous additive map on $E$ is linear.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Complete classical--quantum cut-memory short]
\label{thm:renewal-memory-cumulant}
Let a resolved finite cut-memory coordinate have faithful classical--quantum
state and linear face perturbation
\[
 \rho_{\rm cq}=\bigoplus_{\omega}p_\omega\rho_\omega,
 \qquad
 K_{\rm cq}(z)=\bigoplus_\omega K_\omega(z),
\]
where $p_\omega>0$, $\sum_\omega p_\omega=1$, and every $\rho_\omega$ is
faithful on its support.  Put
\[
 m_\omega(x)=\Tr(\rho_\omega K_\omega(x)),
 \qquad
 \bar m(x)=\sum_\omega p_\omega m_\omega(x),
\]
\[
 \widetilde K_\omega(x)
 =K_\omega(x)-m_\omega(x)I,
\]
and define the complete memory log-partition
\[
 \boxed{
 M_{\rm cq}(z)
 =\log\Tr\exp(\log\rho_{\rm cq}+K_{\rm cq}(z))-\bar m(z).}
\]
Then $M_{\rm cq}(0)=0$, $DM_{\rm cq}(0)=0$, and
\[
 \boxed{
 \begin{aligned}
 D^2M_{\rm cq}(0)[x,y]
 ={}&\sum_\omega p_\omega
 (m_\omega(x)-\bar m(x))(m_\omega(y)-\bar m(y))\\
 &+\sum_\omega p_\omega\int_0^1
 \Tr\!\left(
 \rho_\omega^s\widetilde K_\omega(x)
 \rho_\omega^{1-s}\widetilde K_\omega(y)
 \right)\dd s.
 \end{aligned}}
\]
Both summands are positive.  They vanish identically exactly when all branch
mean slopes agree and every quantum perturbation is scalar on its support.
If $A_{\rm coarse}$ is the logarithmic face score after the memory mark has
been forgotten, then
\[
 \boxed{A_{\rm sh}=A_{\rm coarse}-M_{\rm cq}}
\]
is the canonical fully memory-shorted face score.  The subtraction removes
the complete memory log-partition, not only its quadratic Taylor coefficient.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The block exponential and trace split over the classical label.  For a single
faithful block the Duhamel formula
\[
 D e^B[C]=\int_0^1e^{(1-s)B}Ce^{sB}\,\dd s
\]
gives first derivative $\Tr(\rho K(x))$ and second logarithmic derivative
\[
 \int_0^1\Tr(\rho^s\widetilde K(x)
 \rho^{1-s}\widetilde K(y))\,\dd s.
\]
Differentiating the outer finite log-sum-exp adds the covariance of the branch
means.  Diagonalizing each $\rho_\omega$ shows that every coefficient in the
Kubo--Mori quadratic form is strictly positive; hence its zero directions are
precisely the scalar perturbations.  The covariance zero criterion follows
from faithfulness of the finite classical weights.  The final identity is the
definition of the orthogonal memory removal at the level of the complete
log-partition.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Connection stationarity and the torsion alternative]
\label{thm:Palatini-torsion}
Let $e^I$ be a nondegenerate four-dimensional coframe, let $\omega^{IJ}$ be a
metric-compatible Cartan connection, and put
\[
 B^{IJ}=e^I\wedge e^J,
 \qquad T^I=De^I,
 \qquad P_{\alpha,\beta}=\alpha\star+\beta I.
\]
If $(\alpha,\beta)\ne(0,0)$, then
\[
 \boxed{
 P_{\alpha,\beta}^{-1}
 =\frac{\beta I-\alpha\star}{\alpha^2+\beta^2}.}
\]
For the Palatini--Holst action and matter spin current $\Sigma^{IJ}$, the
connection Euler equation is
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal E_\omega^{IJ}
 =-D(P_{\alpha,\beta}B)^{IJ}-\Sigma^{IJ}=0.}
\]
The Cartan map
\[
 \mathcal K_e(T)^{IJ}=T^I\wedge e^J-e^I\wedge T^J
\]
is injective.  Consequently, on the spinless branch, connection stationarity
implies $T=0$; with spin it gives the unique Einstein--Cartan torsion sourced
by $\Sigma$.  At finite cutoff, if
$\sigma_{\min}(\mathcal K_{e,X})\ge\kappa_*>0$, then
\[
 \boxed{
 \|T_X\|
 \le\kappa_*^{-1}\|P_{\alpha_X,\beta_X}^{-1}\|
 \bigl(\|\mathcal E_{\omega,X}\|+\|\Sigma_X\|\bigr).}
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The inverse formula follows from $\star^2=-I$.  Varying the connection and
integrating by parts gives the displayed Euler source, since $\star$ is
Lorentz natural and commutes with $D$.  To prove injectivity, expand
$T^I=\frac12T^I{}_{KL}e^K\wedge e^L$ in the coframe basis.  In
$T^I\wedge e^J-e^I\wedge T^J=0$, choosing $J$ distinct from $I,K,L$ first
forces $T^I{}_{KL}=0$ whenever $K,L\ne I$.  The remaining coefficients
$t_{I,K}=T^I{}_{IK}$ obey $t_{I,K}+t_{J,K}=0$ for all distinct $I,J,K$;
using three indices different from $K$ forces all of them to vanish.  Thus
$DB=0$ implies $T=0$.  Inverting $P_{\alpha,\beta}$ and then the Cartan map
gives the finite norm estimate and the stated torsion alternatives.
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[Renewal is localized, not a transparent reset of spacetime]
A complete replacement channel has superoperator rank one, whereas a nontrivial
reversible channel on $M_d(\C)$ has superoperator rank $d^2$.  Pre- and
post-processing cannot increase the rank of a replacement channel.  Therefore
a complete renewal replacement cannot be transparent inside the full
reversible spacetime history.  Every subdivision hypothesis below acts on the
relative action or residual-multiplicity carrier while the persistent geometric
algebra is fixed pointwise.
\end{firewall}

\begin{theorem}[Localized renewal--Palatini insertion]
\label{thm:Palatini}
Let $Z_X$ be the integrated Cartan-completed chronological face coordinate on
a compact spacetime cylinder.  Assume:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(E\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item after the complete classical--quantum correction of
      \Cref{thm:renewal-memory-cumulant} has been subtracted, the protected
      binary face subdivision satisfies either the exact or the summably
      stable hypotheses of \Cref{thm:renewal-face-linearization};
\item the resulting linear face score is real and Lorentz natural, its
      commutators with the complete typed internal action vanish in the limit,
      and the residual typed-history commutant on the selected face carrier is
      scalar;
\item determinant coframe volume is represented, the Palatini--Holst
      coefficient pair is uniformly nonzero, and the connection Euler and
      matter spin-current sources satisfy the torsion alternative of
      \Cref{thm:Palatini-torsion};
\item the compact spatial packet gives
      $e_X\to e$ strongly in $L^2_{\rm loc}$ and

\begin{proof}
The first hypothesis and \Cref{thm:renewal-face-linearization} give one unique
real linear primitive after the complete memory log-partition has been
removed.  Both coframe bivectors and Lorentz curvature lie in
$\Lambda^2\R^{1,3}$.  After complexification this module splits into the

therefore gives
\[
 \End_{SO^+(1,3)}(\Lambda^2\R^{1,3})
 =\Span_{\R}\{I,\star\}.
\]
The scalar typed commutant excludes an additional internal tensor.  The only
alternating Lorentz-invariant four-coframe scalar is determinant volume, so

The connection statement is \Cref{thm:Palatini-torsion}.  On the spinless

give the Einstein and cosmological insertions.

It remains to pass the product to the limit.  If $p'=p/(p-1)$, the strict
inequality $p>3/2$ gives $2p'<6$.  Interpolation between strong $L^2$ and the
uniform $L^6$ bound yields $e_X\to e$ strongly in $L^{2p'}$.  Hence
\[
 \|e_X\wedge e_X-e\wedge e\|_{L^{p'}}
 \le C(\|e_X\|_{L^{2p'}}+\|e\|_{L^{2p'}})
       \|e_X-e\|_{L^{2p'}}\longrightarrow0.
\]
Pairing this strongly convergent bivector with the weakly convergent
$L^p$ curvature passes both Palatini and Holst terms.  Strong $L^4$
convergence also passes determinant volume in $L^1$.  Contracting the coframe
Euler form with the symmetric coframe lift of $k^{\mu\nu}$ gives the displayed
metric insertion.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Compact positive-screen coercive upgrade]
\label{thm:SMST-positive-screen}
Fix a compact spacetime cylinder $K$ and identify all cutoff quadratic packets
with one Hilbert space $\mathcal Y_K$.  Let $Y_h\rightharpoonup Y$ weakly and let
$\mathbb A_h$ be positive operators satisfying
\[
 mI\preceq\mathbb A_h\preceq MI,
 \qquad \mathbb A_h^{-1/2}\longrightarrow\mathbb A^{-1/2}
 \quad\text{strongly},
\]
with $0<m\le M<\infty$.  Put $Z_h=\mathbb A_h^{1/2}Y_h$ and assume
$Z_h\rightharpoonup Z=\mathbb A^{1/2}Y$.

For every radius $R$, suppose there are operators $S_{h,R}$ and a compact
operator $S_R$ on $\mathcal Y_K$ such that
\[
 \|S_{h,R}-S_R\|\longrightarrow0,
 \qquad
 \lim_{R\to\infty}\sup_h\|(I-S_{h,R})Z_h\|=0,
\]
and the same tail condition holds for $Z$.  Then
\[
 \boxed{Z_h\to Z\text{ strongly},\qquad Y_h\to Y\text{ strongly in }\mathcal Y_K.}
\]
In the spacetime application
\[
 Y_h=(K_h,u_h,\nabla\phi_h),
 \qquad \mathbb A_h=|\mathbb K_h|\oplus\mathbb Q_h,
\]
so every quadratic insertion converges in $L^1(K)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
For fixed $R$, compactness of $S_R$ converts weak convergence into strong
convergence: $S_RZ_h\to S_RZ$.  Operator-norm convergence of $S_{h,R}$ gives
$S_{h,R}Z_h-S_RZ_h\to0$ because $(Z_h)$ is bounded.  Hence
$S_{h,R}Z_h\to S_RZ$ strongly.  Decompose
\[
 Z_h-Z=(I-S_{h,R})Z_h+(S_{h,R}Z_h-S_RZ)+(S_R-I)Z.
\]
Taking the limsup in $h$ and then $R\to\infty$ proves $Z_h\to Z$ strongly.
Uniform coercivity bounds $\|\mathbb A_h^{-1/2}\|\le m^{-1/2}$.  Therefore
\[
 \|Y_h-Y\|
 \le m^{-1/2}\|Z_h-Z\|
 +\|(\mathbb A_h^{-1/2}-\mathbb A^{-1/2})Z\|\longrightarrow0.
\]
For a quadratic tensor $Q(Y)=B(Y,Y)$ with bounded local coefficient $B$,
\[
 \|Q(Y_h)-Q(Y)\|_{L^1}
 \le C\|Y_h-Y\|_{L^2}
      (\|Y_h\|_{L^2}+\|Y\|_{L^2}),
\]
which gives the final claim.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Global non-null GHY--corner completion]
\label{thm:SMST-global-boundary}

      +\Gamma_{{\rm Cl},X}(q)\otimes
       D_{F,X}^{\boldsymbol Y}(H)
                    \Bigr):E_X\longrightarrow F_X.}
 \tag{SMQ.0a}
\]
The positive vertex Hodge factor changes the modulus by a positive determinant
but contributes no complex phase.  The internal finite-Dirac map
$D_{F,X}^{\boldsymbol Y}(H)$ is a constituent of \textup{(SMQ.0a)}, not the
complete quantum fermion family.
\end{definition}

\begin{proposition}[Gauge covariance of the complete coefficient]
\label{prop:SMST-complete-fermion-gauge-covariance}
For every finite gauge transformation $g$ there are unitary source and target
representations such that
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal K_X(g\lambda)
 =U_{F,X}(g,\lambda)\mathcal K_X(\lambda)
  U_{E,X}(g,\lambda)^{-1}.}
 \tag{SMQ.0b}
\]
Consequently the rank, singular values, divisor, graph-regulator gap, and
zero-mode multiplicities of $\mathcal K_X$ are gauge invariant.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Gauge-link transport makes the spacetime difference covariant; the
multiplicity-one Yukawa construction makes the finite internal term covariant;
and the Clifford and positive Hodge factors intertwine the same action.
Unitary left--right multiplication preserves rank and singular values.
\end{proof}

\begin{countertheorem}[The internal finite Dirac does not determine the full phase]
\label{cth:SMST-internal-Dirac-not-full-phase}
The determinant phase of $D_{F,X}$ does not determine the phase of
$\mathcal K_X$.  This failure occurs already in one complex dimension.
\end{countertheorem}

\begin{proof}
Take $E=F=\C$, $\star_0=\Gamma_{\rm Cl}=1$, and fix $D_F=1$.  On the
parameter circle set
\[
 D_{\rm sp}(\theta)=e^{i\theta}-1.
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{\mathcal K(\theta)=D_{\rm sp}(\theta)+D_F=e^{i\theta}.}
 \tag{SMQ.0c}
\]
The internal determinant and all of its derivatives are constant, whereas the
full determinant winds once.  Hence no construction from the internal
determinant alone can recover the physical fermionic phase.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Canonical graph regulator for a finite chiral coefficient]
\label{thm:SMST-graph-regulator}
Let $D:E\to F$ be a fully assembled finite chiral coefficient and let $m>0$.
For the physical Standard-Model shell one takes
$D=\mathcal K_X(\lambda)$; the internal $D_F$ alone is only one constituent.
Define
\[
 H_m^+(D)=\begin{pmatrix}mI_E&D^*\\D&-mI_F\end{pmatrix},
 \qquad
 H_m^-(D)=\begin{pmatrix}-mI_E&D^*\\D&mI_F\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{
 (H_m^\pm)^2
 =\operatorname{diag}(D^*D+m^2I_E,DD^*+m^2I_F),}
\]
so both Hamiltonians have spectral gap at least $m$.  Their negative spectral
projectors
\[
 P_m^\pm=\frac12\left(I-H_m^\pm((H_m^\pm)^2)^{-1/2}\right)
\]
are finite functional-calculus outputs of $D$ and are gauge covariant.  The
relative graph line
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathscr L_m^{\rm graph}(D)
 =\det\Ran P_m^+(D)\otimes(\det\Ran P_m^-(D))^*}
\]
is canonically isomorphic to the chiral amplitude line
$(\det E)^*\otimes\det F$.

Put
\[
 R_E=(D^*D+m^2I_E)^{1/2},
 \qquad R_F=(DD^*+m^2I_F)^{1/2}.
\]
In the canonical graph frames its Berry connection is
\[
 \boxed{
 \alpha_m(D)
 =-\operatorname{Im}\Tr_E
 \left[R_E^{-1}(R_E+m)^{-1}D^*\dd D\right].}
\]
For an infinitesimal gauge generator $X=(X_E,X_F)$ its vertical moment is
\[
 \boxed{
 \mu_m^D(X)
 =i\Tr_F\!\left[X_F(I-mR_F^{-1})\right]
 -i\Tr_E\!\left[X_E(I-mR_E^{-1})\right].}
\]
The gauge cocycle of the graph section is nevertheless only the fixed-fibre
character
$\det U_F\det U_E^{-1}$.  Hence the anomaly-free finite SM packet admits a
global gauge-invariant graph measure section.  At positive $m$, ordinary
unweighted anomaly cancellation does not by itself force the connection to be
basic, because the moment is spectrally weighted.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Block multiplication gives the square identity and the gap.  Spectral
functional calculus gives the projectors and their covariance.  The negative
spaces have explicit graph isometries obtained from $R_E,R_F$; taking their
top exterior powers identifies the relative graph line with
$(\det E)^*\otimes\det F$.  Differentiating the graph frames and using
$D f(D^*D)=f(DD^*)D$ gives the connection formula.  Substitution of
$\dd D=X_FD-DX_E$ and cyclicity of trace gives the moment formula.  Exterior
powers show that the gauge action on the line is the stated determinant
character, which is trivial for the complete finite anomaly-free SM packet.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Massless full-rank and zero-mode alternatives]
\label{cor:SMST-graph-massless}
On a constant-rank branch,
\[
 \boxed{\alpha_m(D)\longrightarrow
 -\operatorname{Im}\Tr(D^\dagger\dd D)}
\]
as $m\downarrow0$.  The surviving curvature is the curvature of
\[
 \boxed{(\det\ker D)^*\otimes\det\operatorname{coker}D.}
\]
If $D$ is square and invertible, then
\[
 \boxed{\alpha_0=-\dd\arg\det D,\qquad\Omega_0=0.}
\]
Thus the full-rank massless graph connection is flat after the normalized
determinant phase is included; zero modes carry the exact remaining local
obstruction.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
On the nonzero singular support,
$R_E^{-1}(R_E+m)^{-1}D^*\to(D^*D)^\dagger D^*=D^\dagger$.
Kernel and cokernel exterior powers give the residual determinant line.  In the
invertible square case $D^\dagger=D^{-1}$ and the logarithmic determinant
identity gives the final formula.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Finite zero-mode factorization and saturation]
\label{thm:SMST-zero-mode-saturation}
Let $D:H_+\to H_-$ be a finite chiral map and put
$K_+=\ker D$, $K_-=\ker D^*$.  On the orthogonal complements
$E_+=K_+^\perp$ and $E_-=K_-^\perp$, the restriction
$D^\perp:E_+\to E_-$ is invertible, and the determinant line has the canonical
factorization
\[
 \boxed{
 (\det H_+)^*\otimes\det H_-
 \cong
 \underbrace{\det K_-\otimes(\det K_+)^*}_{\mathscr Z_D}
 \otimes
 \underbrace{\det E_-\otimes(\det E_+)^*}_{\mathscr L_D^{\rm red}}.}
 \tag{SMQ.1}
\]
The reduced determinant $\det'(D)=\det(D^\perp)$ is nonzero in
$\mathscr L_D^{\rm red}$ and
\[
 \boxed{\|\det'(D)\|=\prod_{s_j(D)>0}s_j(D).}
 \tag{SMQ.2}
\]
If $D:\C^n\to\C^n$ has rank $n-k$, choose zero-mode-adapted bases in which
$D=0_k\oplus D'$.  For the corresponding Grassmann variables,
\[
 \boxed{
 \int e^{-\bar\psi D\psi}
 \prod_{a=1}^{k}\bar\psi_a\psi_a\,
 \dd\bar\psi\,\dd\psi
 =\pm\det D'.}
 \tag{SMQ.3}
\]
The unsaturated vacuum integral vanishes.  Hence passage through a zero-mode
stratum requires an independently oriented insertion or boundary writer in
$\mathscr Z_D^*$; deleting the kernel and retaining only the
pseudodeterminant does not define the physical amplitude.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Take top exterior powers of the orthogonal decompositions
$H_+=K_+\oplus E_+$ and $H_-=K_-\oplus E_-$.  The restriction $D^\perp$ is
injective and has equal finite source and target dimensions, hence is
invertible; singular-value decomposition proves \textup{(SMQ.2)}.  In the
Grassmann integral the exponential contains no zero-mode variables, so the
vacuum integrand has insufficient top degree.  The displayed insertion
supplies exactly the missing zero-mode degree, and the remaining Gaussian
integral is $\det D'$ up to the chosen orientation sign.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Line-valued quantum action and covariant Einstein residual]
\label{thm:SMST-line-valued-Einstein}
Let $(\mathscr L_{\rm ph},\nabla)$ be the total phase line and let
$\mathscr Z_{\rm tot}$ be a nowhere-zero quantum amplitude section.  There is a
unique complex one-form $\Xi_{\mathscr Z}$ such that
\[
 \nabla\mathscr Z_{\rm tot}
 =\Xi_{\mathscr Z}\otimes\mathscr Z_{\rm tot}.
\]
Writing
$\mathscr Z_{\rm tot}=e^{-\mathscr S_{\mathbb R}}s_{\rm ph}$ with
$\|s_{\rm ph}\|=1$ and
$\nabla s_{\rm ph}=i\alpha_{\rm ph}\otimes s_{\rm ph}$ gives
\[
 \boxed{
 -\Xi_{\mathscr Z}
 =\dd\mathscr S_{\mathbb R}-i\alpha_{\rm ph},
 \qquad
 \dd\Xi_{\mathscr Z}=i\Omega_{\rm ph}.}
\]
Thus a globally ordinary scalar effective action exists exactly when the total
phase line has zero curvature and trivial holonomy.  Otherwise the line-valued
amplitude is intrinsic.

Let
\[
 \mathcal E_q^{\mathbb R}
 =2D_q\mathscr S_g-\mathsf T_{\rm cl}-\mathsf T_{\rm mod},
 \qquad
 \mathsf t_{\rm ph}=2\alpha_{\rm ph}|_{T_q\mathcal C}.
\]
For the faithful inverse geometric metric define
\[
 \boxed{
 \Delta_{\rm Ein,q}^{\rm cov}
 =\|\mathcal E_q^{\mathbb R}\|_{G_{\mathcal Q}^{-1}}^2
  +\|\mathsf t_{\rm ph}\|_{G_{\mathcal Q}^{-1}}^2.}
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{
 \Delta_{\rm Ein,q}^{\rm cov}=0
 \iff \mathcal E_q^{\mathbb R}=0
 \text{ and }\mathsf t_{\rm ph}=0.}
\]
A real Einstein-source mismatch cannot cancel a phase stress.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The decomposition of the covariant derivative follows from the Leibniz rule
and metric compatibility of the unit section.  Applying another covariant
derivative gives the curvature identity.  A parallel global unit section exists
exactly on the zero-curvature, trivial-holonomy branch.  The Einstein residual
is the squared norm of the real and imaginary parts of the logarithmic
covariant metric response in the real direct sum; faithfulness proves the
zero criterion and orthogonality proves noncancellation.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Correct dual-line and independent-measure criterion]
\label{thm:SMST-corrected-dual-measure}
For a finite-Dirac family $D:E\to F$, distinguish
\[
 D^c=\overline D:\overline E\to\overline F,
 \qquad
 D^\vee=\overline{D^*}=D^{\mathsf T}:\overline F\to\overline E.
\]
Their graph connections satisfy
\[
 \boxed{
 \alpha_m(D^c)=-\alpha_m(D),
 \qquad
 \alpha_m(D^\vee)=\alpha_m(D),}
\]
and the same sign table holds for curvature and vertical moment.  Hence
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathscr L_m^{\rm graph}(D^c)
 \cong(\mathscr L_m^{\rm graph}(D))^*,
 \qquad
 \mathscr L_m^{\rm graph}(D^\vee)
 \cong\mathscr L_m^{\rm graph}(D).}
\]
The finite real/Nambu completion therefore does not by itself provide a second
cancelling determinant.  Exact complex phase cancellation requires an
independently sourced Berezin factor with block operator $D\oplus\overline D$,
or another independently reconstructed line with the dual connection and
inverse holonomy.  A positive bosonic Gaussian determinant contributes only to
the real modulus and cannot cancel a complex fermionic phase.

A genuinely real/Pfaffian measure line has zero local curvature and local phase
response but may retain a global $\mathbb Z_2$ holonomy.  Its final certificate
is therefore the sign holonomy, not a complex determinant cancellation.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Complex conjugation sends every graph frame and its connection to the complex
conjugate frame, reversing the imaginary trace.  Transpose together with
source--target reversal exchanges the two graph factors and the dual in the
relative-line definition, producing a second copy of the original connection.
For the scalar family $D=se^{i\varphi}$, $D^\vee=D$ and the connection is
nonzero, which rules out transpose cancellation directly.  The Nambu
skew matrix has Pfaffian equal, up to its fixed sign, to $\det D$; it is a
rewriting of one complex determinant rather than a product with
$\det\overline D$.  An independently integrated conjugate packet tensors the
line with its dual and the evaluation section is parallel.  A positive bosonic
quadratic form has positive determinant and hence no complex phase line.  A
connection-preserving real structure forces local real unit sections to be
parallel, while parallel transport around a loop may reverse their sign.
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[Finite anomaly freedom versus physical quantum phase]
Triviality of the finite SM determinant character gives a gauge-invariant
measure section; it does not determine a unique gauge-invariant phase, make the
Berry connection basic at positive graph mass, or remove a theta-like period.
Likewise, the finite real structure supplies charge-real and Majorana relations
but not an independently integrated conjugate species.  Projector provenance,
section/connection provenance, and global holonomy are separate operational
certificates.
\end{firewall}

\subsubsection{Conditional Gaussian fermion slabs, reflected exterior kernels,
and a zero-safe Pfaffian handoff}
\label{sec:SMST-conditional-Gaussian}
% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

The determinant-line construction identifies the correct one-dimensional phase
carrier, but the reflected fermionic word hierarchy should not be treated as an
arbitrary independent matrix once the same-history fermion action has been
physically assembled and is quadratic.  The following calculus replaces that
inflated input by the complete time-split Dirac--Yukawa precision, its physical
reflection, the scalar line weight, and a small held-out occurrence packet.
Soft tail modes, divisor crossings, and real Pfaffian signs remain explicit.

\paragraph{Purpose, upstream reduction, and exact scope}
\label{subsec:SMQG-purpose}

The preceding determinant and boundary-perturbation layer reduced the first unresolved row to the literal full-coupling reflected
fermionic slab.  Its endpoint still treated the complete mixed reflected-word
matrix as an independently acquired object.  For the Standard-Model fermion
sector this is stronger than necessary on every fixed bosonic history: after
all gauge, Higgs, Yukawa, ghost, boundary, and regulator rows have been
assembled, the fermionic action is quadratic in the Grassmann variables.
Conditionally on that assembled bosonic history, the fermion functional is
therefore Gaussian.

The correct upstream question is consequently
\[
 \boxed{
 \begin{gathered}
 \text{Does one physically occurring assembled quadratic slab}\\
 \text{produce a positive reflected one-particle covariance?}
 \end{gathered}}
 \tag{QG.1}
\]
If it does, all gauge-invariant reflected fermionic words are exterior powers
of that one-particle covariance.  The complete reflected kernel of the earlier direct-word formulation is then a
derived output, not a separately fitted table.  If it does not, the first
failure is already visible as a non-Hermitian or negative one-particle word,
a failure of Gaussian occurrence, a complex or negative determinant-line
weight, a divisor, or a real Pfaffian sign obstruction.

This reduction has four firewalls.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(F\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item The fermionic Gaussian statement is conditional on one fixed bosonic
      history.  Positive mixing over bosonic histories preserves positivity
      but generally destroys quasi-free closure.
\item A quadratic formal expression is not enough.  The precision operator,
      physical reflection, source incidence, determinant/Pfaffian line
      pairing, boundary condition, and normalization must occur on the same
      slab.
\item At a partition zero, the normalized covariance is not defined.  The
      unnormalized exterior-adjugate hierarchy and zero-mode line take over.
\item On a real/skew branch, Pfaffian overlap and crossing signs remain direct
      physical data even when the complex reflected covariance is positive.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{theorem}[Quadratic-fermion priority theorem]
\label{thm:SMQG-priority}
Let one finite reflected fermionic slab have a physically assembled quadratic
Grassmann action and a physical antiunitary line pairing.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2.8em]
\item On the nonzero partition branch, the direct reflected one-particle
      covariance $P$ determines every conditional gauge-invariant mixed word
      by the exterior second quantization
      \[
       \Gamma_\wedge(P)=\bigoplus_{r\ge0}\bigwedge^rP.
 \tag{QG.2}
\]
\item The complete conditional reflected word kernel is positive if and only
      if the reflected scalar weight is nonnegative and $P\succeq0$.
\item One assembled precision operator with an invertible eliminated block
      reconstructs $P$ by a Feshbach inverse.  Elimination before complete
      assembly can change $P$ and its positivity.
\item A direct grade-two or higher word retained outside the fit is a genuine
      falsification test for Gaussian occurrence.  Complete certification uses
      the independently occurring quadratic/Berezin theorem or the complete
      represented higher-word bank.
\item Positive bosonic mixing preserves the reflected kernel but generally
      produces an interacting, non-quasi-free mixed fermion functional.
\item At a divisor, the normalized covariance is forbidden; the first
      nonzero exterior-adjugate coefficient gives the zero-mode-saturated
      reflected packet.
\item On a real/Pfaffian branch, Wick moments are Pfaffians and the direct real
      overlap/crossing sign is independent of the determinant-square kernel.
\item Exact one-particle cutoff transport functorially transports all exterior
      grades.  Target-relative uniform integrability gives cofinal convergence
      of the unnormalized mixed-word cylinders.
\end{enumerate}
Hence the first literal OS population packet is reduced to
\[
 \boxed{
 \begin{gathered}
 \text{one assembled quadratic slab and physical reflection}\\
 +\text{ one reflected one-particle covariance}\\
 +\text{ one held-out higher word}\\
 +\text{ one nonnegative determinant/Pfaffian line weight}\\
 +\text{ direct real signs and cutoff/UI data}.
 \end{gathered}}
 \tag{QG.3}
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The eight assertions are proved in
\Cref{thm:SMQG-Grassmann-Wick,thm:SMQG-exterior-positivity,thm:SMQG-Feshbach-covariance,thm:SMQG-Gaussian-occurrence,thm:SMQG-positive-mixture,thm:SMQG-zero-safe,thm:SMQG-Pfaffian-Wick,thm:SMQG-cutoff-exterior,thm:SMQG-cofinal}.
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[No target inflation]
The present conditional-Gaussian construction derives the direct mixed reflected kernel only on the physical
conditional Gaussian branch.  It does not reconstruct a bosonic path law,
prove that the active Standard-Model discretization has the required
reflection factorization, orient a real Pfaffian line, prove uniform
integrability, or establish the interacting OS continuum.
\end{firewall}

% =============================================================================
\paragraph{Finite reflected Grassmann Gaussian and exterior second quantization}
\label{sec:SMQG-Grassmann}
% =============================================================================

\begin{definition}[Exterior Fock carrier]
\label{def:SMQG-exterior-Fock}
Let $E$ be a finite-dimensional complex Hilbert space of dimension $d$.  Put
\[
 \mathfrak F_\wedge(E)
 =\bigoplus_{r=0}^{d}\bigwedge^rE,
 \qquad
 \bigwedge^0E=\C.
 \tag{QG.4}
\]
For $P\in\operatorname{End}(E)$ define
\[
 \boxed{
 \Gamma_\wedge(P)
 =\bigoplus_{r=0}^{d}\bigwedge^rP.}
 \tag{QG.5}
\]
The positive-time Grassmann word associated with
$f_1\wedge\cdots\wedge f_r$ is denoted
$\psi(f_1)\cdots\psi(f_r)$.  The physical fermionic reflection is the
antilinear order-reversing map
\[
 \Theta_F\!
 \left(
 \psi(f_1)\cdots\psi(f_r)
 \right)
 =
 \overline\psi(f_r)\cdots\overline\psi(f_1),
 \tag{QG.6}
\]
with the physical Koszul convention frozen before any positivity test.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Gauge-invariant reflected Gaussian functional]
\label{def:SMQG-Gaussian-functional}
For $P\in\operatorname{End}(E)$, define the normalized gauge-invariant Grassmann functional
$\mathcal G_P$ by
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal G_P
 \left(
 \Theta_F(\psi(f_1)\cdots\psi(f_r))
 \psi(g_1)\cdots\psi(g_s)
 \right)
 =
 \begin{cases}
 \det[\langle f_i,Pg_j\rangle]_{i,j=1}^{r},&r=s,\\
 0,&r\ne s.
 \end{cases}}
 \tag{QG.7}
\]
The vacuum value is $\mathcal G_P(1)=1$.
When $P$ is invertible, this is the normalized Berezin Gaussian with
covariance $P$.  For singular $P$, equation~\\textup{(QG.7)} is its unique
polynomial continuation.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Finite Grassmann Wick--exterior theorem]
\label{thm:SMQG-Grassmann-Wick}
For $F,G\in\mathfrak F_\wedge(E)$, interpreted as positive-time Grassmann
words,
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal G_P(\Theta_FF\,G)
 =\langle F,\Gamma_\wedge(P)G\rangle_{\mathfrak F_\wedge(E)}.}
 \tag{QG.8}
\]
Equivalently, on grade $r$ the reflected mixed-word matrix is
\[
 \boxed{K_r=\bigwedge^rP.}
 \tag{QG.9}
\]
In an orthonormal basis, every matrix coefficient is the corresponding
$r\times r$ minor of $P$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
On decomposable $r$-vectors the exterior inner product obeys
\[
 \left\langle
 f_1\wedge\cdots\wedge f_r,
 (Pg_1)\wedge\cdots\wedge(Pg_r)
 \right\rangle
 =\det[\langle f_i,Pg_j\rangle].
\]
This is exactly the Wick determinant in
\\textup{(QG.7)}.  Distinct grades are orthogonal and the functional vanishes
between them.  Linearity proves the result.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Berezin realization]
Fix an orthonormal basis and the Berezin convention
\[
 \int e^{-\overline\psi A\psi}
 D\overline\psi D\psi
 =\det A.
\]
For invertible $P$,
\[
 \mathcal G_P(F)
 =\det(P)
 \int e^{-\overline\psi P^{-1}\psi}
 F(\overline\psi,\psi)
 D\overline\psi D\psi.
 \tag{QG.10}
\]
Wick differentiation gives \\textup{(QG.7)}.  Since all moments are
polynomial in the entries of $P$, the singular extension is unique.
\end{remark}

\begin{theorem}[Exact exterior reflection-positivity criterion]
\label{thm:SMQG-exterior-positivity}
For $P\in\operatorname{End}(E)$, the following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2.8em]
\item
      \[
       \mathcal G_P(\Theta_FF\,F)\ge0
       \quad\text{for every }F\in\mathfrak F_\wedge(E);
 \tag{QG.11}
\]
\item $\Gamma_\wedge(P)\succeq0$;
\item
      \[
       \boxed{P=P^*\succeq0.}
 \tag{QG.12}
\]
\end{enumerate}
If $q\in\C$ multiplies the complete Gaussian functional and the vacuum word is
retained, then
\[
 q\,\Gamma_\wedge(P)\succeq0
 \tag{QG.13}
\]
if and only if either $q=0$, or
\[
 \boxed{q>0\text{ and }P\succeq0.}
 \tag{QG.14}
\]
If $q$ is nonreal, Hermiticity already fails.  If $q<0$, the vacuum word is a
negative witness.  If $P$ has a negative vector, that vector is a grade-one
negative reflected word.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The equivalence of the first two statements is
\Cref{thm:SMQG-Grassmann-Wick}.  Positivity of the full direct sum implies
positivity of its grade-one block $P$.  Conversely, if $P\succeq0$, then
$P^{1/2}$ exists and
\[
 \bigwedge^rP
 =
 (\bigwedge^rP^{1/2})^*
 (\bigwedge^rP^{1/2})
 \succeq0
\]
for every $r$.  The scalar statement follows first from the vacuum grade and
then from the preceding equivalence.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Rank and source-minimal reflected carrier]
\label{cor:SMQG-exterior-rank}
If $q_P=\rank P$, then
\[
 \boxed{
 \rank(\bigwedge^rP)=\binom{q_P}{r},
 \qquad
 \rank\Gamma_\wedge(P)=2^{q_P}.}
 \tag{QG.15}
\]
The source-minimal reflected Gaussian carrier is
\[
 \bigoplus_{r=0}^{q_P}
 \bigwedge^r\Ran P.
 \tag{QG.16}
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Diagonalize $P$ unitarily.  The nonzero eigenvalues of $\bigwedge^rP$ are all
$r$-fold products of distinct nonzero eigenvalues of $P$.  Counting them gives
the binomial rank, and summing over $r$ gives $2^{q_P}$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Unitary covariance]
\label{thm:SMQG-unitary-covariance}
For every unitary $U:E\to E$,
\[
 \boxed{
 \Gamma_\wedge(UPU^*)
 =\Gamma_\wedge(U)
  \Gamma_\wedge(P)
  \Gamma_\wedge(U)^*.}
 \tag{QG.17}
\]
Thus a physical gauge or source-frame change acts by unitary congruence on
every reflected word grade and preserves positivity, ranks, and all direct
word residuals.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Exterior powers are functorial:
$\bigwedge^r(UPU^*)=(\bigwedge^rU)(\bigwedge^rP)(\bigwedge^rU)^*$.
Take the direct sum over $r$.
\end{proof}

% =============================================================================
\paragraph{Occurrence from one assembled quadratic slab}
\label{sec:SMQG-slab}
% =============================================================================

\begin{definition}[Assembled conditional Gaussian slab]
\label{def:SMQG-slab}
At one bosonic history $\omega$, let
\[
 D(\omega):\mathcal H_+(\omega)\longrightarrow\mathcal H_-(\omega)
 \tag{QG.18}
\]
be the fully assembled finite fermionic precision operator after all gauge,
Higgs, Yukawa, ghost, boundary, grading, and regulator rows have been fixed.
Let the physical antiunitary reflection and determinant-line pairing identify
the negative reflected source with the conjugate of a finite positive-time
source $E$.

On the invertible branch, the normalized Gaussian covariance is $D^{-1}$.
The physical reflected source compression defines the unique operator
$P(\omega)\in\operatorname{End}(E)$ satisfying
\[
 \boxed{
 \langle f,P(\omega)g\rangle
 =
 \Lambda_{D(\omega)}^{\vartheta}
 \bigl(
 \Theta_F\psi(f)\,\psi(g)
 \bigr).}
 \tag{QG.19}
\]
The scalarized unnormalized determinant/Pfaffian line weight is denoted
$q(\omega)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Conditional Gaussian slab theorem]
\label{thm:SMQG-conditional-slab}
On the complex number-conserving branch, assume the complete finite fermion
action at one bosonic history is quadratic, the physical Berezin source
incidence is the one used in \Cref{def:SMQG-slab}, and the normalized partition
is nonzero.  Then the direct conditional mixed reflected word functional is
gauge-invariant quasi free and
obeys
\[
 \boxed{
 \Lambda_{D(\omega)}^{\vartheta}
 (\Theta_FF\,G)
 =
 q(\omega)
 \langle F,\Gamma_\wedge(P(\omega))G\rangle.}
 \tag{QG.20}
\]
Hence conditional fermionic reflection positivity is equivalent to
\[
 \boxed{
 q(\omega)\ge0,
 \qquad
 P(\omega)\succeq0.}
 \tag{QG.21}
\]
The conclusion is conditional on the complete assembled bosonic history.  It
does not identify the bosonic law or prove positivity of its scalar weight.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
A finite quadratic Grassmann integral is Gaussian.  Its normalized two-point
function is the appropriate source compression of $D^{-1}$, which is exactly
$P$ by \\textup{(QG.19)}.  Wick's theorem gives all equal-grade moments as
determinants of the two-point matrix and annihilates unequal grades.  Apply
\Cref{thm:SMQG-Grassmann-Wick}.  Multiplication by the scalar line weight gives
\\textup{(QG.20)}, and
\Cref{thm:SMQG-exterior-positivity} gives the positivity criterion.
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[Quadratic notation is not physical Gaussian occurrence]
A displayed bilinear fermion action does not by itself prove
\\textup{(QG.20)}.  The following must belong to one physical slab:
\[
 \boxed{
 \begin{gathered}
 D,\quad \Theta_F,\quad \text{source incidence},\quad
 \text{Berezin normalization},\quad q,\\
 \text{boundary condition},\quad \text{discarded record}
 \end{gathered}}
 \tag{QG.22}
\]
Changing any one of these after the word table is inspected is a fit.
\end{firewall}

\begin{definition}[One-sided dressed word map]
\label{def:SMQG-dressed-word}
Let $W:F\to\mathfrak F_\wedge(E)$ be the physically occurring linear map from
a finite represented positive-time word bank to the exterior source carrier.
It contains every one-sided action factor, source router, quotient relation,
and normalization which occurs before the positive/negative slab is glued.
The predicted direct reflected matrix is
\[
 \boxed{
 K_{P,W,q}
 =q\,W^*\Gamma_\wedge(P)W.}
 \tag{QG.23}
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{corollary}[One-sided dressing preserves positivity]
\label{cor:SMQG-dressing}
If $q\ge0$ and $P\succeq0$, then
\[
 \boxed{K_{P,W,q}\succeq0.}
 \tag{QG.24}
\]
Its source-minimal synthesis is
\[
 q^{1/2}\Gamma_\wedge(P)^{1/2}W.
 \tag{QG.25}
\]
No invertibility of $W$ is required.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Equation~\\textup{(QG.23)} is a positive congruence.  The displayed square
root is a Gram synthesis.
\end{proof}

% =============================================================================
\paragraph{Feshbach reconstruction of the reflected covariance}
\label{sec:SMQG-Feshbach}
% =============================================================================

\begin{definition}[Retained/tail precision block]
\label{def:SMQG-Feshbach}
Split the fully assembled fermion carrier as
\[
 \mathcal H_+=\mathcal R_+\oplus\mathcal T_+,
 \qquad
 \mathcal H_-=\mathcal R_-\oplus\mathcal T_-,
 \tag{QG.26}
\]
and write
\[
 \boxed{
 D=
 \begin{pmatrix}
 A&B\\
 C&E
 \end{pmatrix}.}
 \tag{QG.27}
\]
Assume first that the tail block $E:\mathcal T_+\to\mathcal T_-$ is
invertible.  Define the retained Schur operator
\[
 \boxed{S=A-BE^{-1}C.}
 \tag{QG.28}
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Exact Feshbach covariance and determinant factorization]
\label{thm:SMQG-Feshbach-covariance}
For the packet of \Cref{def:SMQG-Feshbach}:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2.8em]
\item
      \[
       \boxed{
       D=
       \begin{pmatrix}I&BE^{-1}\\0&I\end{pmatrix}
       \begin{pmatrix}S&0\\0&E\end{pmatrix}
       \begin{pmatrix}I&0\\E^{-1}C&I\end{pmatrix}.}
 \tag{QG.29}
\]
\item
      \[
       \boxed{\det D=\det E\,\det S.}
 \tag{QG.30}
\]
\item On the invertible branch,
      \[
       \boxed{\Pi_{\mathcal R_+}D^{-1}\iota_{\mathcal R_-}=S^{-1}.}
 \tag{QG.31}
\]
\item If $J_+:E\to\mathcal R_+$ and $J_-:E\to\mathcal R_-$ are the physical
      reflected source maps, then the one-particle reflected covariance is
      \[
       \boxed{P=J_+^*S^{-1}J_-}
 \tag{QG.32}
\]
      after the frozen antiunitary source identification.
\end{enumerate}
Thus the complete conditional reflected word kernel depends on the tail only
through the Schur operator and the scalar hard determinant factor.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Multiply the three factors in \\textup{(QG.29)}.  The determinant identity
follows because both triangular factors have determinant one.  Inverting the
factorization gives the retained block $S^{-1}$.  Source compression gives
\\textup{(QG.32)}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Assembly before Gaussian elimination]
\label{cor:SMQG-assembly-before-elimination}
Suppose the precision operator is a sum of physical sector contributions,
with mixed retained/tail blocks.  The correct reflected covariance is obtained
by forming the complete blocks $A,B,C,E$ and only then taking
\[
 S=A-BE^{-1}C.
 \tag{QG.33}
\]
Separately eliminating the sectors and adding their individual Schur
operators generally gives a different result.  The difference is the same
router-dispersion mechanism already present for positive actions, now acting
inside the fermionic precision and hence inside $P=S^{-1}$.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Schur complementation is nonlinear in the mixed blocks.  For two positive
Hermitian packets the exact discrepancy is the positive router-dispersion
identity.  Without Hermiticity the algebraic failure remains: in general
\[
 \sum_iB_iE_i^{-1}C_i
 \ne
 \left(\sum_iB_i\right)
 \left(\sum_iE_i\right)^{-1}
 \left(\sum_iC_i\right).
\]
Hence elimination before complete assembly changes $S$ and its inverse.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Soft-tail promotion]
\label{def:SMQG-soft-tail}
If $E$ has no protected inverse margin, choose a physically predeclared soft
screen $Z_E$ and promote $Z_E\mathcal T_\pm$ to the retained source.  Apply
\Cref{thm:SMQG-Feshbach-covariance} only on the hard complement where
\[
 \|(E|_{(I-Z_E)\mathcal T_+})^{-1}\|<\infty.
 \tag{QG.34}
\]
An exact tail zero is never divided out.
\end{definition}

\begin{countertheorem}[Aggregate determinant data do not determine the reflected covariance]
\label{cth:SMQG-determinant-no-covariance}
Two invertible retained operators can have the same determinant and different
reflected covariances.  Consequently the partition and its phase do not
reconstruct the direct mixed two-point word.
\end{countertheorem}

\begin{proof}
On $\C^2$, take
\[
 S_1=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&2\end{pmatrix},
 \qquad
 S_2=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\0&2\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Both determinants equal two, but $S_1^{-1}\ne S_2^{-1}$.  A source detecting
the off-diagonal entry separates their reflected covariances.
\end{proof}

% =============================================================================
\paragraph{Gaussian occurrence, held-out higher words, and relation descent}
\label{sec:SMQG-occurrence}
% =============================================================================

\begin{definition}[Direct word bank and quasi-free prediction]
\label{def:SMQG-occurrence}
Let
\[
 F=\bigoplus_{r=0}^{d}F_r
 \tag{QG.35}
\]
be a finite represented positive-time word space and let
\[
 W:F\to\mathfrak F_\wedge(E)
 \tag{QG.36}
\]
be its physically occurring one-sided synthesis.  Let
\[
 K^{\rm dir}=K^{\rm dir*}
 \tag{QG.37}
\]
be the directly acquired reflected mixed-word matrix on the same history
cylinder.  Given the grade-one covariance $P$, define
\[
 \boxed{
 K^{\rm qf}=qW^*\Gamma_\wedge(P)W}
 \tag{QG.38}
\]
and the Gaussian occurrence residual
\[
 \boxed{
 \Delta_{\rm qf}^{(49)}
 =\|K^{\rm dir}-K^{\rm qf}\|_{\rm HS}^2.}
 \tag{QG.39}
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Exact Gaussian-occurrence theorem]
\label{thm:SMQG-Gaussian-occurrence}
Assume the grade-one source is complete for $E$ and the scalar line weight
$q$ is fixed by an independent vacuum or top-grade anchor.  Then
\[
 \boxed{\Delta_{\rm qf}^{(49)}=0}
 \tag{QG.40}
\]
if and only if the directly occurring reflected functional is the
$q$-weighted gauge-invariant Gaussian functional with covariance $P$ on the
complete represented word bank.

If the fit uses only grades zero and one, any direct grade-two coefficient
excluded from the fit is predicted by
\[
 \boxed{
 K_2^{\rm pred}
 =q\,W_2^*(\bigwedge^2P)W_2.}
 \tag{QG.41}
\]
A positive held-out residual is an explicit non-Gaussian or same-history
failure.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The forward implication is the definition of the residual.  Conversely, zero
residual identifies every represented mixed coefficient with the Wick
exterior coefficient of \Cref{thm:SMQG-Grassmann-Wick}; completeness of the
word bank gives equality of the represented functionals.  The held-out
formula is its grade-two block.
\end{proof}

\begin{countertheorem}[Positive two-point data do not determine the four-point word]
\label{cth:SMQG-two-point-no-four-point}
Let $E=\C^2$ and $P=I_2$.  The positive kernels
\[
 K^{(1)}=1\oplus I_2\oplus 1,
 \qquad
 K^{(2)}=1\oplus I_2\oplus0
 \tag{QG.42}
\]
on
$\bigwedge^0E\oplus\bigwedge^1E\oplus\bigwedge^2E$
have the same vacuum and one-particle blocks, but only $K^{(1)}$ is the
quasi-free exterior kernel of $P$.
\end{countertheorem}

\begin{proof}
Both direct sums are positive.  Since
$\bigwedge^2I_2=1$, the quasi-free grade-two value must be one.  The second
kernel violates the Wick relation.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Ordinary word relation Gram]
\label{def:SMQG-word-relation}
Let $H=W_0^*W_0\succeq0$ be a faithful ordinary word Gram for a coefficient
synthesis $W_0:C\to F$.  Let
\[
 K_C=W_0^*K^{\rm dir}W_0.
 \tag{QG.43}
\]
With $P_H=HH^\dagger$, define
\[
 \boxed{
 \Delta_{\rm rel}^{(49)}
 =\|(I-P_H)K_C\|_{\rm HS}^2
  +\|K_C(I-P_H)\|_{\rm HS}^2.}
 \tag{QG.44}
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Gaussian kernel descends through the physical word relations]
\label{thm:SMQG-relation-descent}
If the one-sided synthesis $W$ is a well-defined map on the ordinary physical
word quotient, then the Gaussian prediction automatically satisfies
\[
 \boxed{\Delta_{\rm rel}^{(49)}=0.}
 \tag{QG.45}
\]
Conversely, a positive value proves that the proposed one-sided Gaussian
synthesis and the ordinary word relations cannot both occur on the declared
physical carrier.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
A coefficient vector in $\ker H$ synthesizes the zero ordinary word.  A
well-defined $W$ sends it to zero in the exterior carrier.  Hence both rows of
$W^*\Gamma_\wedge(P)W$ annihilate the relation.  The converse is the
contrapositive of quotient descent.
\end{proof}

\begin{assessment}[Minimum held-out packet]
For a finite conditionally Gaussian target, one does not need an arbitrary
table of all mixed fermionic words.  One needs:
\[
 \boxed{
 \begin{gathered}
 \text{source-complete grade one}
 +\text{ one scalar line anchor}\\
 +\text{ one held-out higher grade}
 +\text{ ordinary relation descent}
 \end{gathered}}
 \tag{QG.46}
\]
Higher held-out grades remain useful when the physical word bank contains
nontrivial one-sided dressing or when Gaussian occurrence itself is disputed.
\end{assessment}

% =============================================================================
\paragraph{Zero-safe unnormalized reflected packet}
\label{sec:SMQG-zero-safe}
% =============================================================================

\begin{definition}[Chiral source insertion polynomial]
\label{def:SMQG-zero-polynomial}
Let
\[
 S:\mathcal R_+\to\mathcal R_-
 \tag{QG.47}
\]
be the retained chiral Schur operator, and let
\[
 J_+:E\to\mathcal R_+,
 \qquad
 J_-:E\to\mathcal R_-
 \tag{QG.48}
\]
be the physical reflected source maps.  For
$Q\in\operatorname{End}(E)$ define
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal Z_S(Q)
 =\det\left(S+J_-QJ_+^*\right).}
 \tag{QG.49}
\]
This is a polynomial of degree at most $\dim E$, whether or not $S$ is
invertible.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Invertible and zero-safe source hierarchy]
\label{thm:SMQG-zero-safe}
For the insertion polynomial of \Cref{def:SMQG-zero-polynomial}:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2.8em]
\item If $S$ is invertible and
      \[
       P=J_+^*S^{-1}J_-,
 \tag{QG.50}
\]
      then
      \[
       \boxed{
       \mathcal Z_S(Q)
       =\det S\,\det(I_E+QP).}
 \tag{QG.51}
\]
      Hence the homogeneous degree-$r$ coefficient is
      $\det S$ times the grade-$r$ exterior covariance coefficient.
\item If
      \[
       k=\dim\ker S=\dim\ker S^*,
 \tag{QG.52}
\]
      and the source maps are complete on the kernel and cokernel, then all
      homogeneous degrees below $k$ vanish and the degree-$k$ coefficient is
      nonzero.
\item The degree-$k$ coefficient is the hard determinant factor times the
      determinant pairing between the physical kernel and cokernel source
      maps.  It is the first zero-mode-saturated reflected coefficient.
\item At $\det S=0$, the normalized covariance in
      \\textup{(QG.50)} is forbidden.  The polynomial coefficients of
      \\textup{(QG.49)}, the zero-mode line, and the physical crossing sign are
      the complete zero-safe replacement.
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
On the invertible branch, factor $S$ and apply Sylvester's determinant
identity:
\[
 \det(S+J_-QJ_+^*)
 =\det S\,
  \det(I_E+QJ_+^*S^{-1}J_-).
\]
For the singular branch, choose kernel/cokernel-adapted decompositions.  The
hard block is invertible.  A determinant term can be nonzero only after every
kernel column and cokernel row has been supplied by the source insertion;
therefore at least $k$ insertion factors are required.  Source completeness
makes the degree-$k$ minor nonzero.  Expanding the determinant along the
zero-mode block gives the stated hard-factor times zero-mode pairing.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Divisor-safe positivity order]
\label{cor:SMQG-zero-positivity-order}
At a divisor, positivity is tested only after:
\[
 \boxed{
 \begin{gathered}
 \text{zero-mode source saturation}\\
 \longrightarrow\quad
 \text{physical kernel/cokernel line pairing}\\
 \longrightarrow\quad
 \text{direct real/Pfaffian crossing sign when applicable}
 \end{gathered}}
 \tag{QG.53}
\]
Normalizing by the vanishing partition before these steps is invalid.
\end{corollary}

\begin{countertheorem}[A regular positive carrier can coexist with a partition zero]
\label{cth:SMQG-zero-positive-carrier}
There are positive trine or matrix carriers with strictly positive total mass
whose complex determinant coherence is zero.  Therefore the regularity of the
positive acquisition instrument does not license a normalized fermionic
phase at a partition zero.
\end{countertheorem}

\begin{proof}
Take two equal positive histories with complex weights $+1$ and $-1$.  Their
positive total variation is two, while their complex sum is zero.
\end{proof}

% =============================================================================
\paragraph{Bosonic mixing and loss of quasi-free closure}
\label{sec:SMQG-mixture}
% =============================================================================

\begin{definition}[Same-history conditional reflected kernel]
\label{def:SMQG-mixture}
Let $(\Omega,\rho)$ be one positive bosonic reference cylinder.  At almost
every history let
\[
 q(\omega)\ge0,
 \qquad
 P(\omega)\succeq0,
 \qquad
 W(\omega):F\to\mathfrak F_\wedge(E)
 \tag{QG.54}
\]
be the physically occurring conditional determinant/Pfaffian weight,
reflected covariance, and one-sided word synthesis.  Define
\[
 \boxed{
 K^{\rm mix}
 =\int_\Omega
 q(\omega)
 W(\omega)^*\Gamma_\wedge(P(\omega))W(\omega)
 \,d\rho(\omega).}
 \tag{QG.55}
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Positive bosonic mixing theorem]
\label{thm:SMQG-positive-mixture}
The matrix $K^{\rm mix}$ in \\textup{(QG.55)} is positive semidefinite.  If the
ordinary word relations hold conditionally almost everywhere, they also hold
for the mixed kernel.

The mixed kernel is generally not quasi free.  In particular, in general
\[
 \boxed{
 \int q(\omega)\bigwedge^rP(\omega)\,d\rho(\omega)
 \ne
 \bigwedge^r
 \left(
 \frac{\int q(\omega)P(\omega)\,d\rho(\omega)}
      {\int q(\omega)\,d\rho(\omega)}
 \right)
 \int q\,d\rho.}
 \tag{QG.56}
\]
Thus an averaged two-point reflected covariance does not determine the mixed
four-point or higher kernels.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Every integrand is positive by
\Cref{cor:SMQG-dressing}; integration preserves positivity.  Conditional
annihilation of a relation remains zero after integration.

For non-quasi-free closure, take equal weights and
\[
 P_1=\operatorname{diag}(1,0),
 \qquad
 P_2=\operatorname{diag}(0,1).
\]
Then
\[
 \frac12\bigwedge^2P_1
 +\frac12\bigwedge^2P_2=0,
\]
whereas
\[
 \bigwedge^2\left(\frac12I_2\right)=\frac14.
\]
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[Integrated positivity versus conditional physical law]
A positive integrated kernel does not prove that every conditional history
has $q(\omega)\ge0$ and $P(\omega)\succeq0$.  Negative conditional packets can
cancel after mixing.  Pointwise conditional positivity is required whenever
the same-history Gaussian mechanism or a conditional OS law is itself part of
the claim.
\end{firewall}

\begin{countertheorem}[Separate bosonic and fermionic marginals do not establish the mixture]
\label{cth:SMQG-marginals-no-mixture}
The marginal law of $q$, the marginal law of $P$, and all separate conditional
one-point statistics do not determine
\\textup{(QG.55)}.  Different couplings of the same marginals can give
different reflected word matrices.
\end{countertheorem}

\begin{proof}
Take two bosonic histories, two scalar weights, and two distinct positive
covariances.  Pair the larger weight with the first covariance in one coupling
and with the second covariance in the other.  The marginals agree while the
weighted average in \\textup{(QG.55)} differs.
\end{proof}

% =============================================================================
\paragraph{Robust one-particle and exterior certificates}
\label{sec:SMQG-robust}
% =============================================================================

\begin{lemma}[Exterior-power perturbation bound]
\label{lem:SMQG-exterior-bound}
For $A,B\in\operatorname{End}(E)$ and $r\ge1$, put
\[
 M=\max\{\|A\|,\|B\|\}.
 \]
Then
\[
 \boxed{
 \|\bigwedge^rA-\bigwedge^rB\|
 \le
 rM^{r-1}\|A-B\|.}
 \tag{QG.57}
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
On $E^{\otimes r}$, telescope
\[
 A^{\otimes r}-B^{\otimes r}
 =\sum_{j=1}^{r}
 A^{\otimes(j-1)}\otimes(A-B)
 \otimes B^{\otimes(r-j)}.
\]
Its norm is at most the displayed bound.  Compress to the antisymmetric
subspace.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Robust reflected-positivity alternative]
\label{thm:SMQG-robust-positivity}
Suppose the exact one-particle covariance is Hermitian and
\[
 \|\widetilde P-P\|\le\varepsilon_P.
 \tag{QG.58}
\]
Then:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2.8em]
\item if
      \[
       \lambda_{\min}(\widetilde P)>\varepsilon_P,
 \tag{QG.59}
\]
      then $P\succ0$;
\item if
      \[
       \lambda_{\min}(\widetilde P)<-\varepsilon_P,
 \tag{QG.60}
\]
      a bottom eigenvector of $\widetilde P$ is a certified negative grade-one
      reflected word for $P$;
\item if neither inequality holds, the packet returns a soft one-particle
      direction rather than assigning a sign;
\item every grade-$r$ prediction has error at most
      \[
       \boxed{
       rM^{r-1}\varepsilon_P}
 \tag{QG.61}
\]
      before the known source and scalar-weight errors are added.
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The first three claims are Weyl's eigenvalue inequality.  The last is
\Cref{lem:SMQG-exterior-bound}.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Held-out exterior residual]
\label{def:SMQG-heldout}
For a direct held-out grade-$r$ word map $W_r^{\rm hold}$ and observed matrix
$K_r^{\rm hold}$, define
\[
 \boxed{
 \Delta_{r,\rm hold}^{(49)}
 =
 \left\|
 K_r^{\rm hold}
 -q(W_r^{\rm hold})^*
   (\bigwedge^rP)
   W_r^{\rm hold}
 \right\|_{\rm HS}^2.}
 \tag{QG.62}
\]
This word, its line gain, and its bosonic history are excluded from the fit of
$P$.
\end{definition}

% =============================================================================
\paragraph{Complex skew and real Pfaffian branches}
\label{sec:SMQG-Pfaffian}
% =============================================================================

\begin{definition}[Skew Gaussian]
\label{def:SMQG-skew-Gaussian}
Let $V$ be a finite complex vector space of even dimension and let
\[
 A^T=-A
 \tag{QG.63}
\]
be an invertible skew precision matrix.  The normalized Majorana Grassmann
Gaussian has covariance
\[
 C=-A^{-1},
 \tag{QG.64}
\]
with the sign fixed by the chosen Berezin order and Pfaffian line frame.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Pfaffian Wick theorem]
\label{thm:SMQG-Pfaffian-Wick}
For linear Majorana fields $\chi(v_1),\ldots,\chi(v_{2r})$,
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal G_A
 \left(
 \chi(v_1)\cdots\chi(v_{2r})
 \right)
 =
 \operatorname{Pf}
 \left[
 \langle v_i,Cv_j\rangle
 \right]_{i,j=1}^{2r}.}
 \tag{QG.65}
\]
Odd moments vanish.

If a physically supplied reflection-compatible complex polarization converts
the represented even Majorana word carrier into an exterior carrier
$\mathfrak F_\wedge(E)$ and converts the reflected two-point form into a
Hermitian operator $P$, then the reflected even-word kernel is unitarily
equivalent to the corresponding parity sector of
$\Gamma_\wedge(P)$.  Positivity follows from $P\succeq0$.

Without that physical polarization, positivity of a skew covariance is not an
ordered-matrix statement and must be tested on the directly assembled
Pfaffian word matrix.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The generating identity is
\[
 \int
 e^{\frac12\chi^TA\chi+\eta^T\chi}
 D\chi
 =
 \operatorname{Pf}(A)
 e^{-\frac12\eta^TA^{-1}\eta}.
\]
Differentiating in the anticommuting source $\eta$ gives the Pfaffian Wick
formula.  On a compatible complex polarization, pairs of real generators
become creation/annihilation generators and the Pfaffian Wick rule becomes
the determinant/exterior Wick rule of
\Cref{thm:SMQG-Grassmann-Wick} on the represented parity sector.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Pfaffian sign remains independent]
\label{thm:SMQG-Pfaffian-sign}
Let $\operatorname{Pf}(A)$ be the unnormalized real/skew fermionic amplitude.
The determinant-square kernel determines
\[
 \operatorname{Pf}(A)^2=\det A
 \tag{QG.66}
\]
but does not determine:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2.8em]
\item the smooth overlap sign between two real Pfaffian charts;
\item the parity of a Pfaffian zero crossing;
\item the $w_1$ holonomy of the real Pfaffian line.
\end{enumerate}
These signs multiply the scalar $q$ in
\\textup{(QG.20)} and must be acquired directly.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The two amplitudes $\operatorname{Pf}(A)$ and
$-\operatorname{Pf}(A)$ have the same determinant square and the same
normalized complex covariance.  Along
\[
 A(t)=\begin{pmatrix}0&t\\-t&0\end{pmatrix},
\]
the Pfaffian changes sign while the determinant is $t^2$.  Loop signs are the
same local ambiguity composed around a cycle.
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[Nambu rewriting is not an independent conjugate measure]
A doubled Nambu matrix may rewrite one determinant or Pfaffian.  It does not
supply an independently integrated conjugate fermion species, the dual
measure line, or a direct real orientation.  Phase cancellation and Pfaffian
orientation require their own physical occurrence packets.
\end{firewall}

% =============================================================================
\paragraph{Adjacent-cutoff exterior functor and fine Gaussian births}
\label{sec:SMQG-cutoff}
% =============================================================================

\begin{definition}[One-particle cutoff defects]
\label{def:SMQG-cutoff}
Let
\[
 j:E_X\longrightarrow E_Y
 \tag{QG.67}
\]
be the physical one-particle source isometry.  For positive reflected
covariances $P_X,P_Y$, define
\[
 \boxed{
 \begin{aligned}
 C_{Y/X}^{P}&=j^*P_Yj-P_X,\\
 L_{Y/X}^{P}&=(I-jj^*)P_Yj,\\
 R_{Y/X}^{P}&=P_Yj-jP_X.
 \end{aligned}}
 \tag{QG.68}
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[One-particle Pythagoras and strict exterior transport]
\label{thm:SMQG-cutoff-exterior}
For the packet of \Cref{def:SMQG-cutoff},
\[
 \boxed{
 \|R_{Y/X}^{P}\|_{\rm HS}^2
 =
 \|L_{Y/X}^{P}\|_{\rm HS}^2
 +
 \|C_{Y/X}^{P}\|_{\rm HS}^2.}
 \tag{QG.69}
\]
The following are equivalent:
\[
 \boxed{
 R_{Y/X}^{P}=0,
 \qquad
 L_{Y/X}^{P}=C_{Y/X}^{P}=0.}
 \tag{QG.70}
\]
On this branch, for every grade $r$,
\[
 \boxed{
 (\bigwedge^rP_Y)(\bigwedge^rj)
 =
 (\bigwedge^rj)(\bigwedge^rP_X).}
 \tag{QG.71}
\]
Hence
\[
 \boxed{
 \Gamma_\wedge(P_Y)\Gamma_\wedge(j)
 =
 \Gamma_\wedge(j)\Gamma_\wedge(P_X).}
 \tag{QG.72}
\]
The exterior cutoff maps compose strictly.

Conversely, if the full exterior packet includes grade one, exact exterior
intertwining implies exact one-particle intertwining.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Decompose
\[
 P_Yj-jP_X
 =
 (I-jj^*)P_Yj
 +j(j^*P_Yj-P_X).
\]
The two summands have orthogonal ranges, proving the Pythagoras.  Functoriality
of exterior powers proves \textup{(71)--(72)}.  The converse is the
grade-one block.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Independent fine Gaussian factor]
\label{thm:SMQG-fine-factor}
Suppose
\[
 E_Y=jE_X\oplus F_{Y/X}
 \tag{QG.73}
\]
and
\[
 \boxed{
 P_Y
 =jP_Xj^*\oplus P_{Y/X}^{\rm fine}.}
 \tag{QG.74}
\]
Under the canonical exterior factorization,
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathfrak F_\wedge(E_Y)
 \cong
 \mathfrak F_\wedge(E_X)
 \widehat\otimes
 \mathfrak F_\wedge(F_{Y/X}),}
 \tag{QG.75}
\]
\[
 \boxed{
 \Gamma_\wedge(P_Y)
 =
 \Gamma_\wedge(P_X)
 \widehat\otimes
 \Gamma_\wedge(P_{Y/X}^{\rm fine}).}
 \tag{QG.76}
\]
If $m=\rank P_{Y/X}^{\rm fine}$, the source-minimal exterior rank is
multiplied by $2^m$.

If the off-diagonal old/fine covariance is nonzero, the tensor factorization
fails.  A held-out mixed old/fine grade-two word detects that failure.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The exterior algebra of a direct sum is the graded tensor product of the
exterior algebras.  Exterior second quantization is multiplicative on block
direct sums.  Apply \Cref{cor:SMQG-exterior-rank}.  A nonzero off-diagonal
block contributes mixed minors and therefore changes a mixed grade-two
coefficient.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Complete adjacent-cutoff Gaussian birth]
\label{def:SMQG-birth}
After transporting the physical line and one-sided word map, retain
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathfrak B_{Y/X}^{(49)}
 =
 \left(
 q_Y/q_X,
 C_{Y/X}^{P},
 L_{Y/X}^{P},
 \Delta_{\rm qf,Y}^{(49)},
 \text{fine Pfaffian sign},
 \text{divisor data}
 \right).}
 \tag{QG.77}
\]
These coordinates classify respectively scalar amplitude birth,
old-compression change, new covariance leakage, Gaussian-occurrence failure,
real orientation birth, and zero-mode birth.
\end{definition}

% =============================================================================
\paragraph{Cofinal unnormalized Gaussian reflected kernels}
\label{sec:SMQG-cofinal}
% =============================================================================

\begin{lemma}[Uniform exterior norm bound]
\label{lem:SMQG-Gamma-bound}
For $\dim E=d$,
\[
 \boxed{
 \|\Gamma_\wedge(P)\|
 \le
 \max\{1,\|P\|^d\}
 \le
 (1+\|P\|)^d.}
 \tag{QG.78}
\]
For $P,Q$ in a common bounded ball,
\[
 \boxed{
 \|\Gamma_\wedge(P)-\Gamma_\wedge(Q)\|
 \le
 \left[
 \sum_{r=1}^{d}rM^{r-1}
 \right]\|P-Q\|,}
 \tag{QG.79}
\]
where $M=\max\{\|P\|,\|Q\|\}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
The grade-$r$ norm is at most $\|P\|^r$.  Take the maximum over grades.
Sum the gradewise perturbation bounds of
\Cref{lem:SMQG-exterior-bound}.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Target-relative Gaussian-kernel Vitali theorem]
\label{thm:SMQG-kernel-Vitali}
Fix a maximum represented fermion grade $d$.  On one transported positive
bosonic reference cylinder, let
\[
 K_n(\omega)
 =q_n(\omega)
 W_n(\omega)^*
 \Gamma_\wedge(P_n(\omega))
 W_n(\omega)
 \succeq0.
 \tag{QG.80}
\]
Assume in measure:
\[
 q_n\to q,
 \qquad
 P_n\to P,
 \qquad
 W_n\to W,
 \tag{QG.81}
\]
and assume the scalar family
\[
 \boxed{
 q_n\|W_n\|^2(1+\|P_n\|)^d}
 \tag{QG.82}
\]
is uniformly integrable.  Then
\[
 \boxed{
 \int\|K_n-K\|\,d\rho\longrightarrow0,}
 \tag{QG.83}
\]
and the corresponding matrix-valued reflected-word measures converge in
total variation.  The limit kernel is positive.

If uniform integrability fails, there are sets $A_j$ and a subsequence with
\[
 \boxed{
 \rho(A_j)\to0,
 \qquad
 \int_{A_j}\|K_{n_j}\|\,d\rho\ge\varepsilon>0.}
 \tag{QG.84}
\]
This is a determinant/Pfaffian-weighted fermionic concentration witness.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
\Cref{lem:SMQG-Gamma-bound} and the convergence in measure imply
$K_n\to K$ in measure.  The displayed scalar dominates $\|K_n\|$.
Uniform integrability and the vector-valued Vitali theorem give
\\textup{(QG.83)} and total-variation convergence.  The positive cone is
closed.  The final alternative is the negation of uniform integrability.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Cofinal conditional-Gaussian reflected packet]
\label{thm:SMQG-cofinal}
Consider a cofinal cutoff sequence transported to one fixed selected source
and bosonic reference cylinder.  Assume:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(C\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item physical determinant/Pfaffian line pairings and one-sided word maps are
      summably compatible;
\item the conditionally assembled slab precisions have protected Feshbach
      tails, or every soft tail mode is promoted to the exceptional source;
\item $q_X\ge0$ and $P_X\succeq0$ almost everywhere;
\item the one-particle cutoff defects in
      \\textup{(QG.68)} are summable on the selected source;
\item the direct held-out Gaussian occurrence residuals tend to zero;
\item divisor multiplicities, zero-mode lines, and direct real Pfaffian signs
      stabilize;
\item the uniform-integrability condition
      \\textup{(QG.82)} holds.
\end{enumerate}
Then every fixed represented reflected fermion grade has a cofinal positive
unnormalized limit.  The complete selected mixed-word kernel converges in
total variation and descends through the limiting word relations.

If the conditional covariance has a direct-sum fine factor, the exterior
cutoff functor is strict.  If a divisor occurs, the conclusion is replaced by
the cofinal zero-safe exterior-adjugate and zero-line packet; no normalized
covariance is claimed there.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Summable one-particle defects give a Cauchy covariance on the fixed source.
Exterior functoriality and
\Cref{lem:SMQG-exterior-bound} transport every fixed grade.  Gaussian
occurrence passes by the held-out residual, while relation descent is closed
under the limit.  Apply
\Cref{thm:SMQG-kernel-Vitali} to include the unnormalized bosonic weight.
Stable divisor and sign data give the zero-safe alternative.
\end{proof}

\begin{countertheorem}[Normalized conditional convergence does not control the absolute kernel]
\label{cth:SMQG-normalized-no-absolute}
Let $P_n=P$ and $W_n=W$ be constant while $q_n=e^n$.  Every normalized
conditional fermion correlation and every normalized exterior kernel is
constant, but the unnormalized reflected kernel diverges.
\end{countertheorem}

\begin{proof}
Equation~\\textup{(QG.80)} is multiplied by $e^n$.
\end{proof}
