\paragraph{Conditional-Gaussian compiler}
\label{sec:SMQG-compiler}
% =============================================================================

\begin{theorem}[Terminating conditional-Gaussian compiler]
\label{thm:SMQG-compiler}
At one cutoff and one fixed bosonic history, proceed in the following order.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(QG.\arabic*)},leftmargin=6.2em]
\item Assemble the complete fermionic precision from the gauge, Higgs, Yukawa,
      ghost, boundary, grading, regulator, and counterterm rows.
\item Freeze the physical antiunitary reflection, determinant/Pfaffian line
      pairing, positive-time source maps, Berezin order, and one-sided word
      synthesis.
\item Separate every soft tail mode.  On the hard branch compute the retained
      Schur operator and reflected covariance $P$.
\item Test Hermiticity and positivity of $P$.  Return a negative grade-one word
      or soft vector on the failing branch.
\item Acquire the scalar unnormalized line weight $q$.  Require it to be real
      and nonnegative for the conditional positive branch; retain direct real
      Pfaffian signs separately.
\item Predict the complete reflected word matrix by
      $qW^*\Gamma_\wedge(P)W$.  When the quadratic/Berezin occurrence theorem
      has independently passed, retain one or more higher words outside the
      fit; otherwise acquire the complete higher-word bank named by the target.
\item Test descent through the ordinary physical word relations.
\item At a divisor, stop normalization and retain the exterior-adjugate,
      zero-mode line, crossing, and Pfaffian-sign packet.
\item Mix over bosonic histories only through one positive same-history
      cylinder; do not replace the mixed higher grades by exterior powers of
      an averaged covariance.
\item Transport the one-particle, line, divisor, sign, and word packets across
      one adjacent cutoff and prove target-relative uniform integrability.
\end{enumerate}
The compiler returns one of:
\[
 \boxed{
 \begin{gathered}
 \text{positive conditional Gaussian reflected kernel},\quad
 \text{negative/non-Hermitian one-particle word},\\
 \text{soft tail mode},\quad
 \text{Gaussian Wick failure},\quad
 \text{word-relation failure},\\
 \text{complex or negative line weight},\quad
 \text{divisor/zero-mode packet},\\
 \text{Pfaffian sign obstruction},\quad
 \text{non-quasi-free bosonic mixture},\\
 \text{cutoff leakage or concentration witness}
 \end{gathered}}
 \tag{QG.85}
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The branches are
\Cref{thm:SMQG-conditional-slab,thm:SMQG-Feshbach-covariance,thm:SMQG-exterior-positivity,thm:SMQG-Gaussian-occurrence,thm:SMQG-relation-descent,thm:SMQG-zero-safe,thm:SMQG-positive-mixture,thm:SMQG-Pfaffian-sign,thm:SMQG-cutoff-exterior,thm:SMQG-kernel-Vitali}.
\end{proof}

\subsubsection{Absolute quantum cylinders, reflection positivity, and exact Wilsonian transport}
\label{sec:SMST-quantum-cylinder}
% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

The determinant-line theorems above identify the correct phase carrier.  The
following layer applies only on a branch on which an absolute normalization and
a physical orientation or scalarization of that line have independently
produced a nonnegative finite weight.  It does not manufacture such a branch.

\begin{definition}[Finite oriented quantum cylinder]
\label{def:SMST-quantum-cylinder}
At cutoff $X$, let $\Omega_X$ be finite, let
$\theta_X:\Omega_X\to\Omega_X$ be a physical Euclidean reflection with
$\theta_X^2=I$, and let $\mathcal A_{X,+}\subseteq\C^{\Omega_X}$ be a unital
positive-time cylinder algebra.  Let $W_X:\Omega_X\to[0,\infty)$ be a
nonzero absolute weight, put
\[
 Z_X=\sum_{\omega}W_X(\omega),
 \qquad
 \mu_X=Z_X^{-1}W_X,
\]
and assume $(\theta_X)_*\mu_X=\mu_X$.  The Osterwalder--Schrader form is
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathscr Q_X^{\rm OS}(F,G)
 =\sum_{\omega\in\Omega_X}
   \overline{F(\theta_X\omega)}G(\omega)\mu_X(\omega),
 \qquad F,G\in\mathcal A_{X,+}.}
 \tag{QRP.1}
\]
The cylinder is reflection positive when
$\mathscr Q_X^{\rm OS}(F,F)\ge0$ for every $F\in\mathcal A_{X,+}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Finite reflection-Gram compiler]
\label{thm:SMST-reflection-Gram}
For any basis $f_1,\ldots,f_m$ of $\mathcal A_{X,+}$, the matrix
\[
 \boxed{
 G_X^{\rm RP}(i,j)=\mathscr Q_X^{\rm OS}(f_i,f_j)}
 \tag{QRP.2}
\]
is Hermitian and
\[
 \boxed{
 \mu_X\text{ is reflection positive on }\mathcal A_{X,+}
 \iff G_X^{\rm RP}\succeq0.}
 \tag{QRP.3}
\]
Its inertia is basis independent.  In the boundary decomposition
$\Omega_X=B_X^-\times B_X^+$ with
$\theta_X(a,b)=(b,a)$ and positive-time functions depending only on the second
coordinate, the form is represented by the boundary matrix
$K_X(a,b)=\mu_X(a,b)$; hence reflection positivity is equivalent to
$K_X\succeq0$.

If
$G_X^{\rm RP}=G_{X,+}^{\rm RP}-G_{X,-}^{\rm RP}$ is its spectral Jordan
split, then
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathbb C_X^{\rm RP}:=\|G_{X,-}^{\rm RP}\|_{\rm HS}^2
 =\min_{H\succeq0}\|G_X^{\rm RP}-H\|_{\rm HS}^2.}
 \tag{QRP.4}
\]
Every negative eigenvector gives an explicit positive-time observable of
negative reflected norm.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Reflection invariance and $\theta_X^2=I$ make the form Hermitian.  For
$F=\sum_ic_if_i$, one has
$\mathscr Q_X^{\rm OS}(F,F)=c^*G_X^{\rm RP}c$, proving
\textup{(QRP.3)}.  In the boundary decomposition, for
$F(a,b)=f(b)$ and $G(a,b)=g(b)$ the form is $f^*K_Xg$, proving the
boundary-kernel criterion.  A basis change acts by invertible congruence, so
inertia is unchanged.  Diagonalizing the Hermitian matrix reduces the nearest-positive
problem to replacing every negative eigenvalue by zero, which proves
\textup{(QRP.4)}.
\end{proof}

\begin{countertheorem}[Pointwise positive weights need not be reflection positive]
\label{cth:SMST-positive-no-reflection}
Let the boundary alphabet be $B=\{1,2\}$ and take the symmetric positive-entry
kernel
\[
 K=\begin{pmatrix}1&2\\2&1\end{pmatrix}.
\]
After normalization, it is a pointwise positive reflection-invariant
probability, but its boundary reflection matrix has eigenvalues proportional
to $3$ and $-1$.  Thus pointwise weight positivity, determinant positivity,
and a chosen Pfaffian orientation do not replace the reflection-Gram test.
\end{countertheorem}

\begin{theorem}[Reflection-positive reweighting, marginalization, and equivariant coarse graining]
\label{thm:SMST-reflection-pushforward}
In the boundary-kernel setting, if $K\succeq0$ and $H\succeq0$, then their
entrywise product
\[
 \boxed{K^{\rm new}=K\circ H\succeq0.}
 \tag{QRP.4a}
\]
In particular, every reflected-square insertion
$H(a,b)=\sum_{r=1}^N\overline{h_r(a)}h_r(b)$ preserves reflection positivity;
pointwise nonnegativity of an insertion is not sufficient unless its reflected
boundary kernel is positive semidefinite.

Suppose next that a reflected boundary kernel
$K_{(a,\alpha),(b,\beta)}$ on $B_X\times F_X$ is positive semidefinite.  Its
exact marginal
\[
 \boxed{
 \overline K(a,b)=\sum_{\alpha,\beta\in F_X}
 K_{(a,\alpha),(b,\beta)}}
 \tag{QRP.5}
\]
is positive semidefinite.  More generally, if
$\pi:\Omega_Y\to\Omega_X$ satisfies
$\pi\theta_Y=\theta_X\pi$ and
$\pi^*\mathcal A_{X,+}\subseteq\mathcal A_{Y,+}$, then reflection positivity
of $\mu_Y$ implies reflection positivity of $\pi_*\mu_Y$.
Consequently exact fermion elimination and exact reflection-equivariant
Wilsonian pushforward preserve reflection positivity.  Replacing the exact
pushforward by a head-only truncation is a new measure and requires its own
reflection Gram or a positive reflected boundary-kernel factorization.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Write $K_{ab}=\langle u_a,u_b\rangle$ and
$H_{ab}=\langle v_a,v_b\rangle$.  Then
$(K\circ H)_{ab}=\langle u_a\otimes v_a,u_b\otimes v_b\rangle$, proving
\textup{(QRP.4a)}.  For marginalization, define
$V:\C^{B_X}\to\C^{B_X\times F_X}$ by
$(Vf)(a,\alpha)=f(a)$.  Then $\overline K=V^*KV\succeq0$.  For equivariant
pushforward,
\[
 \mathscr Q_{\pi_*\mu_Y}^{\rm OS}(F,F)
 =\mathscr Q_{\mu_Y}^{\rm OS}(F\circ\pi,F\circ\pi)\ge0.
\]
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Summable cutoff correction and reflection-positive projective limit]
\label{thm:SMST-quantum-projective-limit}
Let the finite cutoff maps compose and be reflection equivariant, and put
\[
 \delta_X^{\rm TV}
 =\| (\pi_{X+1,X})_*\mu_{X+1}-\mu_X\|_{\rm TV},
 \qquad
 \|\sigma\|_{\rm TV}
 =\sup_{\|f\|_\infty\le1}\left|\int f\,\dd\sigma\right|.
\]
If every $\mu_X$ is reflection positive and
\[
 \sum_X\delta_X^{\rm TV}<\infty,
\]
then for every fixed $m$ the pushed measures
$(\pi_{n,m})_*\mu_n$ converge in total variation to a probability
$\overline\mu_m$, the family $(\overline\mu_m)_m$ is exactly projectively
compatible, and
\[
 \boxed{
 \|\overline\mu_m-\mu_m\|_{\rm TV}
 \le\sum_{j\ge m}\delta_j^{\rm TV}.}
 \tag{QRP.6}
\]
There is a unique inverse-limit cylinder probability with these marginals,
and its restriction to every finite positive-time algebra is reflection
positive.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Total variation contracts under pushforward, so for $n\ge m$,
\[
 \|(\pi_{n+1,m})_*\mu_{n+1}-(\pi_{n,m})_*\mu_n\|_{\rm TV}
 \le\delta_n^{\rm TV}.
\]
The telescoping series gives convergence and \textup{(QRP.6)}.  Passing the
finite compatibility equations to the limit gives an exact projective family,
which determines the inverse-limit cylinder measure.  For
$F\in\mathcal A_{m,+}$, every pushed fine measure has nonnegative reflected
quadratic form on $F$; total-variation convergence passes that bounded integral
to $\overline\mu_m$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Absolute tightness, correlation passage, and nontriviality]
\label{thm:SMST-quantum-tightness}
Let $\iota_X:\Omega_X\to E$ map the cylinders into a Polish field space and
let $\mathcal V:E\to[0,\infty]$ be lower semicontinuous with compact sublevel
sets.  If, for some $\alpha>0$,
\[
 \boxed{
 \sup_X
 \frac{\sum_{\omega}W_X(\omega)
 e^{\alpha\mathcal V(\iota_X\omega)}}{Z_X}
 \le C,}
 \tag{QRP.7}
\]
then the field laws $\widehat\mu_X=(\iota_X)_*\mu_X$ are tight and
\[
 \sup_X\widehat\mu_X\{\mathcal V>R\}\le Ce^{-\alpha R}.
\]
The same conclusion holds on a Hilbert field space if there are finite-rank
projections $P_R\uparrow I$ such that
\[
 \sup_X\int\|\phi\|^2\,\dd\widehat\mu_X<\infty,
 \qquad
 \sup_X\int\|(I-P_R)\phi\|^2\,\dd\widehat\mu_X\longrightarrow0.
 \tag{QRP.8}
\]
If $\widehat\mu_{X_j}\Rightarrow\mu$, continuous protected writers
$F_j\to F$ locally uniformly, and
\[
 \sup_j\int|F_j|^{1+\delta}\,\dd\widehat\mu_{X_j}<\infty
\]
for some $\delta>0$, then
\[
 \boxed{
 \int F_j\,\dd\widehat\mu_{X_j}
 \longrightarrow\int F\,\dd\mu.}
 \tag{QRP.9}
\]
If the corresponding $2+\delta$ bound holds for $O_j$ and
$\inf_j\operatorname{Var}_{\widehat\mu_{X_j}}(O_j)>0$, then the limiting
variance is positive and the protected limit is nontrivial.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Markov's inequality proves the exponential tail.  Under \textup{(QRP.8)},
choose a sequence of screens with summable expected tails and intersect the
resulting finite-dimensional compact bounds; Markov's inequality and a union
bound give uniform tightness.  For \textup{(QRP.9)}, first restrict to a compact
set supplied by tightness and use weak convergence and local uniform
convergence there; H\"older's inequality and the uniform moment bound control
the complement.  Apply the same argument to $O_j$ and $|O_j|^2$ to pass the
variance lower bound.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Fermionic gap, spectral-flow, and gauge-line alternatives]
\label{thm:SMST-fermionic-phase-transport}
Let $D_X$ be the finite-Dirac family after the exact kernel line and reduced
determinant of \Cref{thm:SMST-zero-mode-saturation} have been retained.
Exactly one of the following occurs along any sequence:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(F\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item there is a uniform reduced gap
      $s_{\min}^+(D_X)\ge\gamma>0$;
\item there are unit vectors $u_j\perp\ker D_{X_j}$ with
      $\|D_{X_j}u_j\|\to0$.
\end{enumerate}
For a $C^1$ Hermitian path with invertible endpoints and simple regular
crossings,
\[
 \boxed{
 \operatorname{sgn}\det H(1)
 =(-1)^{\operatorname{sf}(H)}\operatorname{sgn}\det H(0).}
 \tag{QRP.10}
\]
For a loop $D:S^1\to\operatorname{GL}_n(\C)$,
\[
 \boxed{
 \operatorname{wind}(\det D)
 =\frac1{2\pi i}\int_{S^1}\operatorname{tr}(D^{-1}\dd D)\in\Z,}
 \tag{QRP.11}
\]
and a continuous determinant logarithm exists exactly when this integer
vanishes.  For a finite gauge-line cocycle
$a(g,\omega)\in U(1)$ on one orbit $G\omega_0$, scalarization is possible
exactly when
\[
 \boxed{a(h,\omega_0)=1
 \quad\text{for every }h\in\operatorname{Stab}(\omega_0).}
 \tag{QRP.12}
\]
Cutoff-compatible scalarization additionally requires trivial holonomy of the
resulting orbit-to-orbit phase cochain.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Failure of a uniform positive singular-value floor produces the singular
vectors in item~\textup{(F2)}.  At a simple Hermitian crossing one eigenvalue
changes sign, so determinant sign changes with the parity of spectral flow.
Jacobi's formula gives
$\dd\log\det D=\operatorname{tr}(D^{-1}\dd D)$ locally and integration gives
\textup{(QRP.11)}.  A gauge trivialization
$a(g,\omega)=b(g\omega)b(\omega)^{-1}$ is necessarily trivial on stabilizers;
conversely \textup{(QRP.12)} makes
$b(g\omega_0)=a(g,\omega_0)b(\omega_0)$ well defined.  Compatibility across
cutoffs is the ordinary vanishing-cycle condition for the residual $U(1)$
edge cochain.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Exact Wilsonian counterterm cocycle and source-minimal tail]
\label{thm:SMST-Wilsonian-counterterm-cocycle}
Let $\pi_{Y/X}:\Omega_Y\to\Omega_X$ and let the absolute weights be strictly
positive on their retained supports.  Define the exact shell counterterm
\[
 \boxed{
 C_{Y/X}(x)
 =-\log\frac{(\pi_{Y/X})_!W_Y(x)}{W_X(x)},
 \qquad
 (\pi_{Y/X})_!W_Y(x)=\sum_{y\mapsto x}W_Y(y).}
 \tag{QRP.13}
\]
For $Z\to Y\to X$, let
\[
 \kappa_{Y|x}(y)=
 \frac{W_Y(y)}{(\pi_{Y/X})_!W_Y(x)}
 \qquad(y\mapsto x).
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{
 C_{Z/X}(x)=C_{Y/X}(x)
 -\log\mathbb E_{\kappa_{Y|x}}e^{-C_{Z/Y}(Y)}.}
 \tag{QRP.14}
\]
The cocycle is additive exactly on the branch where $C_{Z/Y}$ is constant on
every $Y\to X$ fibre.

Let $\mathcal C_X^{\rm head}\subset L^2(\Omega_X,\mu_X)$ be a predeclared
finite-dimensional symmetry-reducing real space containing constants.  The
orthogonal split
\[
 \boxed{
 C_{Y/X}=C_{Y/X}^{\rm head}+T_{Y/X}^{\rm gen}}
 \tag{QRP.15}
\]
is the unique minimum-$L^2(\mu_X)$ head approximation and obeys exact
Pythagoras.  If the generated tail has an interaction representation
$T_X=\sum_A\Phi_{X,A}$ with
\[
 \sup_{x\in\Lambda_X}\sum_{A\ni x}
 e^{a\operatorname{diam}(A)}\|\Phi_{X,A}\|_\infty\le C,
\]
then, for every finite region $B$, omitting interactions of diameter greater
than $R$ changes the $B$-local counterterm action by at most
\[
 \boxed{|B|Ce^{-aR}.}
 \tag{QRP.16}
\]
Thus the exact Wilsonian object is the finite head together with its generated
quasilocal tail; the head alone is licensed only after both the tail and its
reflection defect are controlled.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Apply the pushforward identity twice:
\[
 (\pi_{Z/X})_!W_Z(x)
 =\sum_{y\mapsto x}e^{-C_{Z/Y}(y)}W_Y(y).
\]
Factoring out $(\pi_{Y/X})_!W_Y(x)=e^{-C_{Y/X}(x)}W_X(x)$ and taking the
negative logarithm proves \textup{(QRP.14)}.  Orthogonal projection gives
\textup{(QRP.15)} and its Pythagoras.  For the local tail, overcount every
omitted interaction meeting $B$ by one vertex of $A\cap B$ and use
$e^{a\operatorname{diam}(A)}>e^{aR}$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Reflection-positive protected Euclidean continuum alternative]
\label{thm:SMST-reflection-positive-continuum}
Assume a cofinal scalarized quantum-cylinder branch satisfying:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(Q\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item $\mathbb C_X^{\rm RP}=0$ and the cutoff maps are reflection equivariant;
\item $\sum_X\delta_X^{\rm TV}<\infty$;
\item either the absolute exponential row \textup{(QRP.7)} or the compact-screen
      row \textup{(QRP.8)} is uniform;
\item the fermionic family has a uniform reduced gap, or its zero-mode line is
      explicitly saturated with compatible spectral-flow and Pfaffian
      orientation;
\item every finite gauge stabilizer residual and cutoff phase holonomy
      vanishes;
\item the generated Wilsonian tail is uniformly quasilocal and vanishes on
      every fixed protected cylinder after the required counterterms are
      retained;
\item protected products are uniformly integrable, at least one transported

\subsubsection{OS-represented current and stress sectors, Ward contact
cohomology, and Hamiltonian incidence}
\label{sec:SMST-OS-stress-current}
% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

Reflection positivity and a positive transfer reconstruct a Hilbert space and
Hamiltonian, but they do not by themselves identify the represented current,
stress, contact, energy-density, or trace-anomaly operators.  Those objects
must be assembled on the same Osterwalder--Schrader quotient and tested against
the same source atlas, contact product, Hamiltonian, and cutoff maps.  The
following finite calculus performs that audit without promoting expectation
identities to operator identities.

\paragraph{Purpose and exact target}

The preceding composite-operator construction reconstructs a finite renormalized composite $*$-algebra on the
physical OS carrier, including its product, contact terms, direct triple
occurrence, common graph domain, and finite scheme cocycle.  A current or
stress tensor is stronger data.  It must act on that same represented algebra,
its Ward identities must include the coincident contact terms generated when a
symmetry derivative crosses an insertion, and its Euclidean energy density
must generate the already reconstructed OS time translation rather than a
second fitted Hamiltonian.

The surrounding Grand-Tensor programme already contains generic common-action,
Ward, source-short, and fusion compilers.  The present specialization therefore does
not repeat those abstract results.  It specializes them to the OS quotient and
separates the exact rows which a represented stress/current sector requires:
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \begin{gathered}
 \text{one source-complete renormalized composite algebra and graph core}\\
 \Downarrow\\
 \text{direct current/stress insertions and all Ward contact panels}\\
 \Downarrow\\
 \text{one simultaneous improvement/EOM/BRST/boundary short}\\
 \Downarrow\\
 \text{operator-level conservation, symmetry, locality, and Ward associativity}\\
 \Downarrow\\
 \text{Euclidean energy-density incidence with the same OS Hamiltonian}\\
 \Downarrow\\
 \text{one physical scale deformation and a scheme-covariant trace class}\\
 \Downarrow\\
 \text{one transported stress--composite Wick/Pfaffian excess}.
 \end{gathered}}
 \label{eq:SMOS-target-chain}
\end{equation}
An expectation-level Ward identity is not an operator identity.  A formal
improvement is not a physical quotient.  A beta-function coefficient is not a
trace-anomaly operator without an occurring scale deformation.  A time-time
stress component which merely has the correct vacuum expectation is not the
OS Hamiltonian.  Each distinction below is decided by a positive Gram or an
explicit finite obstruction.

% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
\paragraph{Simultaneous Ward short and source-minimal obstruction}
\label{subsec:SMOS-Ward-short}
% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

\begin{definition}[Completely assembled Ward-response packet]
\label{def:SMOS-Ward-packet}
Let $\mathcal K_{\rm W}$ be the finite direct-sum carrier of every declared Ward
response channel.  Its summands may include translation, rotation, internal
gauge, BRST, stress-symmetry, disjoint-support locality, and coincident-contact
rows.  Let
\[
 Y:E_{\rm W}\longrightarrow\mathcal K_{\rm W}
\]
synthesize the direct defect between the occurring response and the proposed
Ward prediction.

Let
\[
 N:F_{\rm triv}\longrightarrow\mathcal K_{\rm W}
\]
synthesize, on the same response carrier and with one common coefficient
vector, every admitted trivial modification: improvements, equation-of-motion
operators, BRST-exact insertions whose reflected Ward-null condition has
already passed, total divergences, and physical boundary-source corrections.
Put
\[
 G_N=N^*N,
 \qquad
 P_N=NG_N^\dagger N^*.
\]
The nuisance list and its support grammar are frozen before the terminal Ward
values are inspected.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Simultaneous Ward-short Pythagoras]
\label{thm:SMOS-Ward-short}
For the packet of \Cref{def:SMOS-Ward-packet}, define
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 Y_{\rm phys}=(I-P_N)Y,
 \qquad
 \mathbb C_{\rm W}^{\rm phys}=Y^*(I-P_N)Y\succeq0.}
 \label{eq:SMOS-Ward-short-Gram}
\end{equation}
For every proposed trivial coefficient map $L:E_{\rm W}\to F_{\rm triv}$,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 (Y-NL)^*(Y-NL)
 =\mathbb C_{\rm W}^{\rm phys}
 +(L-L_0)^*G_N(L-L_0),}
 \label{eq:SMOS-Ward-short-Pythagoras}
\end{equation}
where
\[
 L_0=G_N^\dagger N^*Y.
\]
Consequently,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathbb C_{\rm W}^{\rm phys}=0
 \iff
 \Ran Y\subseteq\Ran N
 \iff
 \exists L:\ Y=NL.}
 \label{eq:SMOS-Ward-short-zero}
\end{equation}
Moreover,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \rank(N,Y)-\rank N
 =\rank\mathbb C_{\rm W}^{\rm phys}.}
 \label{eq:SMOS-Ward-short-rank}
\end{equation}
The polar range of $Y_{\rm phys}$ is the unique source-minimal Ward obstruction
remaining after every admitted trivial source has been assembled.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The Moore--Penrose formula makes $P_N$ the orthogonal projection onto
$\Ran N$.  Since $NL_0=P_NY$, one has the orthogonal decomposition
\[
 Y-NL=(I-P_N)Y+N(L_0-L).
\]
Taking Grams proves \eqref{eq:SMOS-Ward-short-Pythagoras}.  Its two summands are
positive and have orthogonal ranges, giving the zero alternative.  Appending
$Y$ to $N$ adds exactly the orthogonal range of $(I-P_N)Y$, proving the rank
identity.  Polar decomposition gives the source-minimal obstruction carrier.
\end{proof}

\begin{countertheorem}[Separate Ward-row repairs need not share one improvement]
\label{cth:SMOS-separate-Ward-shorts}
Separate rowwise minimization can falsely report closure.  Let
\[
 \mathcal K_{\rm W}=\C\oplus\C,
 \qquad
 Yx=(x,x),
 \qquad
 N\ell=(\ell,-\ell).
\]
The first row can be cancelled by $\ell=x$ and the second by $\ell=-x$ when
fitted separately.  No one coefficient cancels both rows, and in fact
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 P_NY=0,
 \qquad
 \mathbb C_{\rm W}^{\rm phys}=2I.}
 \label{eq:SMOS-separate-short-counterexample}
\end{equation}
Thus improvement, EOM, BRST, and boundary effects must be assembled with their
complete mixed response blocks before any short is taken.
\end{countertheorem}

\begin{proof}
The vectors $(1,1)$ and $(1,-1)$ are orthogonal.  Hence the projection of the
range of $Y$ onto the range of $N$ is zero and the residual Gram is
$Y^*Y=2I$.
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[Only physically null directions may be shorted]
A formal EOM relation, BRST coboundary, total derivative, or improvement is not
entered into $N$ merely because it is algebraically familiar.  It is admitted
only after its own word descent, OS-null or boundary-incidence, domain, and
same-history occurrence rows have passed.  Shorting an unverified direction
can erase a genuine Ward anomaly or a physical boundary current.
\end{firewall}

\paragraph{Source completeness and the expectation-level no-go theorem}
\label{subsec:SMOS-source-completeness}
% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

\begin{definition}[Ward source atlas]
\label{def:SMOS-Ward-atlas}
Let $\mathcal D$ be the common finite-cutoff graph domain of the inherited renormalized composite algebra and the proposed current/stress insertions.  Let
\[
 B:F\longrightarrow\mathcal D
\]
be a physical source atlas.  For a graph-bounded Ward defect operator
$D_{\rm W}:\mathcal D\to\mathcal H_{\rm OS}$, define
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathbb G_{\rm W}(B)
 =B^*D_{\rm W}^*D_{\rm W}B\succeq0.}
 \label{eq:SMOS-Ward-atlas-Gram}
\end{equation}
If $P_{\rm tar}$ is the declared target-carrier projection and $P_B$ the range
projection of $B$, define the atlas residual
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathbb C_{\rm W}^{\rm atlas}(B)
 =P_{\rm tar}(I-P_B)P_{\rm tar}\succeq0.}
 \label{eq:SMOS-Ward-atlas-residual}
\end{equation}
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Operator Ward identity from a source-complete atlas]
\label{thm:SMOS-Ward-atlas}
At finite cutoff, suppose
\[
 \mathbb C_{\rm W}^{\rm atlas}(B)=0
\]
and $D_{\rm W}$ is supported on $P_{\rm tar}\mathcal H_{\rm OS}$.  Then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathbb G_{\rm W}(B)=0
 \iff
 D_{\rm W}P_{\rm tar}=0.}
 \label{eq:SMOS-Ward-atlas-equivalence}
\end{equation}
For an exhausting continuum atlas $B_n$, the same conclusion holds on the
closure of the common core when $D_{\rm W}$ is closed and vanishes on every
$\Ran B_n$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Zero atlas residual gives $\Ran B=P_{\rm tar}\mathcal H_{\rm OS}$.  The Gram
vanishes exactly when $D_{\rm W}B=0$, hence exactly when $D_{\rm W}$ vanishes
on the target range.  In the continuum case the union of the atlas ranges is a
core; closedness extends the zero relation from the core to the operator
closure.
\end{proof}

\begin{countertheorem}[Expectation Ward identities are insufficient]
\label{cth:SMOS-expectation-Ward}
Let
\[
 \mathcal H=\C^2,
 \qquad
 \Omega=e_1,
 \qquad
 D_{\rm W}=|e_2\rangle\langle e_2|.
\]
Then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \langle\Omega,D_{\rm W}\Omega\rangle=0,
 \qquad
 D_{\rm W}\ne0.}
 \label{eq:SMOS-expectation-no-go}
\end{equation}
Thus a Ward identity tested only in the vacuum expectation, or on any
non-source-complete state family, does not establish the operator identity on
the represented OS algebra.
\end{countertheorem}

\begin{proof}
The defect annihilates $e_1$ and fixes $e_2$.  The displayed expectation is
therefore zero while the operator has rank one.
\end{proof}

% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
\paragraph{Ward contact cochains and associativity}
\label{subsec:SMOS-Ward-contact}
% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

\begin{definition}[Graded Ward pair and contact packet]
\label{def:SMOS-Ward-contact}
Let $(E,\mu,\sharp,e,R)$ be the finite graded composite algebra reconstructed in
the inherited renormalized-composite packet, represented on its supported OS metric $R$.  Let $d:E\to E$ be a
homogeneous linear symmetry action of parity $p\in\{0,1\}$ and let
\[
 c:E\otimes E\longrightarrow E
\]
be a homogeneous contact cochain of the same parity.  For homogeneous $x,y$
define the Ward--Leibniz defect
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathcal L_{d,c}(x,y)
 =d\mu(x,y)-\mu(dx,y)
 -(-1)^{p|x|}\mu(x,dy)-c(x,y).}
 \label{eq:SMOS-Ward-Leibniz-defect}
\end{equation}
Its positive OS residual is
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathbb C_{d,c}^{(2)}
 =\mathcal L_{d,c}^*R\mathcal L_{d,c}\succeq0.}
 \label{eq:SMOS-Ward-Leibniz-Gram}
\end{equation}
Define the graded Ward contact associator
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \begin{aligned}
 (\delta_\mu^pc)(x,y,z)
 ={}&\mu(c(x,y),z)+c(\mu(x,y),z)\\
 &-(-1)^{p|x|}\mu(x,c(y,z))-c(x,\mu(y,z)).
 \end{aligned}}
 \label{eq:SMOS-Ward-contact-cocycle}
\end{equation}
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Ward contact cocycle theorem]
\label{thm:SMOS-Ward-contact-cocycle}
Assume $\mu$ is associative on the supported OS quotient.  If
\[
 \mathbb C_{d,c}^{(2)}=0,
\]
then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{\delta_\mu^pc=0.}
 \label{eq:SMOS-Ward-contact-cocycle-zero}
\end{equation}
Equivalently, the two staged Ward expansions of a triple product agree.
Conversely, for an independently acquired pair contact table, the positive
Gram
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathbb C_{d,c}^{(3)}
 =(\delta_\mu^pc)^*R(\delta_\mu^pc)\succeq0}
 \label{eq:SMOS-Ward-contact-cocycle-Gram}
\end{equation}
vanishes exactly when that contact table is compatible with associative triple
fusion on the represented quotient.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Apply $d$ to the equality
\[
 \mu(\mu(x,y),z)=\mu(x,\mu(y,z)).
\]
Expand the left side with \eqref{eq:SMOS-Ward-Leibniz-defect} twice:
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 d((xy)z)
 ={}&(dx)yz+(-1)^{p|x|}x(dy)z
 +c(x,y)z\\
 &+(-1)^{p(|x|+|y|)}xy(dz)+c(xy,z).
 \end{aligned}
\]
The right side expands as
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 d(x(yz))
 ={}&(dx)yz+(-1)^{p|x|}x(dy)z\\
 &+(-1)^{p(|x|+|y|)}xy(dz)
 +(-1)^{p|x|}x c(y,z)+c(x,yz).
 \end{aligned}
\]
Associativity cancels the three ordinary derivation terms.  The remaining
difference is exactly \eqref{eq:SMOS-Ward-contact-cocycle}.  The final statement
is positivity and faithfulness of the supported OS metric.
\end{proof}

\begin{countertheorem}[A pair contact table need not satisfy the Ward cocycle]
\label{cth:SMOS-pair-contact-no-cocycle}
Let $E=\C^2$ with pointwise product and minimal projections $e_1,e_2$.  Define
a bilinear contact cochain by
\[
 c(e_1,e_1)=e_2,
 \qquad
 c(e_i,e_j)=0
 \quad\text{otherwise}.
\]
Then the pair table is a perfectly finite bilinear source, but
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 (\delta_\mu^0c)(e_1,e_1,e_2)=e_2\ne0.}
 \label{eq:SMOS-contact-cocycle-counterexample}
\end{equation}
Hence a direct pairwise contact panel does not establish a consistent Ward
identity on triple products.
\end{countertheorem}

\begin{proof}
Using $e_1e_2=0$ and $e_2^2=e_2$, the four terms in
\eqref{eq:SMOS-Ward-contact-cocycle} are respectively
$e_2,0,0,0$.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Direct triple Ward occurrence]
\label{def:SMOS-triple-Ward-occurrence}
Let $V_{3,\rm W}^{\rm dir}$ be the directly acquired three-insertion Ward
source.  Let $V_{3,L}^{\rm pred}$ and $V_{3,R}^{\rm pred}$ be the two staged
predictions formed from $d,c$, and $\mu$.  Define
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \Delta_{3,\rm W}^{\rm occ}
 =\|V_{3,\rm W}^{\rm dir}-V_{3,L}^{\rm pred}\|_{\HS}^2
 +\|V_{3,\rm W}^{\rm dir}-V_{3,R}^{\rm pred}\|_{\HS}^2.}
 \label{eq:SMOS-triple-Ward-occurrence}
\end{equation}
\end{definition}

\begin{corollary}[Abstract Ward consistency versus physical occurrence]
\label{cor:SMOS-Ward-occurrence}
The vanishing of \eqref{eq:SMOS-Ward-contact-cocycle-Gram} proves consistency of
the reconstructed algebraic Ward cochain.  The stronger equality
\[
 \Delta_{3,\rm W}^{\rm occ}=0
\]
proves that both staged expansions coincide with the directly occurring triple
history.  The former cannot replace the latter.
\end{corollary}

% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
\paragraph{Finite stress/current relation packet}
\label{subsec:SMOS-stress-relations}
% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

\begin{definition}[Direct stress/current response synthesis]
\label{def:SMOS-stress-response}
Fix a finite spacetime test atlas and a source-complete inherited renormalized-composite word/core atlas.
For every declared symmetry generator $\xi$ retain:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(S\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item a direct current-divergence or stress-divergence source
      $D_\xi^{\rm dir}$;
\item the represented infinitesimal action $d_\xi$ on the composite algebra;
\item every coincident Ward contact source $C_\xi$;

      $T_{\mu\nu}-T_{\nu\mu}$;
