      \Cref{def:SMOS-Ward-contact,def:SMOS-triple-Ward-occurrence}.
\end{enumerate}
Stack their signed differences into one synthesis
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 Y_{T,J}
 =\bigoplus_\xi
 \left(
 D_\xi^{\rm dir}+C_\xi-d_\xi,
 T_{\mu\nu}-T_{\nu\mu},
 [T_{\mu\nu},\mathcal A]_{\rm gr},
 \mathcal L_{d_\xi,c_\xi},
 \delta_\mu^{|d_\xi|}c_\xi,
 V_{3,\rm W}^{\rm dir}-V_{3,\rm W}^{\rm pred}
 \right).}
 \label{eq:SMOS-stacked-stress-Ward-source}
\end{equation}
All terms are evaluated on the frozen finite support and source atlas.  The
sign convention in the first component is fixed by the direct deformation
experiment.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Finite represented stress/current criterion]
\label{thm:SMOS-stress-current-criterion}
Let $N_{T,J}$ be the simultaneously assembled trivial-response synthesis for
\eqref{eq:SMOS-stacked-stress-Ward-source}.  Put
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathbb C_{T,J}^{\rm rel}
 =Y_{T,J}^*(I-P_{N_{T,J}})Y_{T,J}\succeq0.}
 \label{eq:SMOS-stress-current-residual}
\end{equation}
Assume the source atlas is complete on the declared target and every nuisance
source has independently passed its OS-null or boundary-incidence audit.  Then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathbb C_{T,J}^{\rm rel}=0}
 \label{eq:SMOS-stress-current-zero}
\end{equation}
is necessary and sufficient for the existence of one common improvement/EOM/
BRST/boundary representative on which:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(R\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item the current and stress Ward identities hold as represented operator
      relations;
\item the stress tensor is symmetric on the declared screen;
\item disjoint-support graded locality holds;
\item the symmetry action obeys the Ward--Leibniz rule with the acquired
      contact cochain;
\item the contact cochain is associative at triple fusion;
\item the direct triple Ward panel agrees with both staged predictions.
\end{enumerate}
If the residual is nonzero, its polar range is the source-minimal physical
obstruction after all admitted trivial directions have been removed.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Apply \Cref{thm:SMOS-Ward-short} to the complete direct-sum response synthesis.
Zero residual is equivalent to one common nuisance coefficient map cancelling
all stacked rows simultaneously.  Source completeness upgrades the vanishing
source Grams to the represented operator relations by
\Cref{thm:SMOS-Ward-atlas}.  The pair, cocycle, and triple statements are
\Cref{thm:SMOS-Ward-contact-cocycle,cor:SMOS-Ward-occurrence}.  The converse is
immediate by inserting the common representative into the stack.
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[Target-relative stress sector]
The theorem reconstructs only the stress/current sector visible to the frozen
local test and source atlas.  It does not require a complete ambient
stress-tensor matrix when the intended target is one selected energy, current,
or Ward response.  A full distribution-valued tensor requires an exhausting
support atlas and its own domain and transport bounds.
\end{firewall}

% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
\paragraph{Euclidean energy density and incidence with the OS Hamiltonian}
\label{subsec:SMOS-energy-Hamiltonian}
% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

\begin{definition}[Integrated energy candidate]
\label{def:SMOS-energy-candidate}
Let $H\ge0$ be the Hamiltonian reconstructed from the same reflected slab as the
the inherited renormalized composite algebra.  Let $E_\Sigma$ be the closable operator obtained by
integrating the direct Euclidean time--time stress insertion over the declared
spatial screen, after all required improvement, boundary, vacuum, and contact
terms have been completely assembled.  Let
\[
 B:F\longrightarrow\mathcal D
\]
be a common graph-core source atlas for $H$ and $E_\Sigma$.  Define
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathbb C_{E\mid H}(B)
 =B^*(E_\Sigma-H)^*(E_\Sigma-H)B\succeq0.}
 \label{eq:SMOS-energy-Hamiltonian-Gram}
\end{equation}
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Energy-density/Hamiltonian incidence]
\label{thm:SMOS-energy-Hamiltonian-incidence}
At finite cutoff, if $B$ is source complete, then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathbb C_{E\mid H}(B)=0
 \iff
 E_\Sigma=H.}
 \label{eq:SMOS-energy-Hamiltonian-equivalence}
\end{equation}
For an exhausting continuum atlas, if the union of the atlas ranges is a common
core and the two operators are closed, vanishing on every atlas implies equality
of their closures.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The Gram vanishes exactly when $(E_\Sigma-H)B=0$.  Source completeness gives
zero on the entire finite carrier.  In the continuum, equality on a common core
and closedness imply equality of the operator closures.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Commutator Ward data determine energy only after a vacuum anchor]
\label{thm:SMOS-energy-commutator-anchor}
Let $\mathfrak A_0$ be a unital represented time-zero algebra with cyclic vacuum
$\Omega$, and let
\[
 \mathcal D_0=\mathfrak A_0\Omega
\]
be invariant under two operators $H$ and $E_\Sigma$.  Put $D=E_\Sigma-H$.
Assume
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 [D,A]\psi=0
 \quad
 (A\in\mathfrak A_0,\ \psi\in\mathcal D_0).}
 \label{eq:SMOS-energy-commutator}
\end{equation}
Then:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(i)},leftmargin=3em]
\item if $D\Omega=0$, then $D=0$ on $\mathcal D_0$;
\item if $D\Omega=c\Omega$, then $D=cI$ on $\mathcal D_0$.
\end{enumerate}
Hence the translation Ward commutators determine the energy only up to the
vacuum/central fibre, and one direct unnormalized vacuum-energy or pressure row
fixes that fibre.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
For every $A\in\mathfrak A_0$,
\[
 D(A\Omega)=A(D\Omega)
\]
by \eqref{eq:SMOS-energy-commutator}.  The two conclusions follow from cyclicity.
\end{proof}

\begin{countertheorem}[Correct dynamics do not fix the absolute energy]
\label{cth:SMOS-energy-scalar-fibre}
For every real $c$,
\[
 E_\Sigma=H+cI
\]
has the same commutators with all represented observables as $H$.  It therefore
implements the same Heisenberg or Euclidean derivation, while its vacuum energy
and unnormalized pressure differ by $c$.  Commutator Ward data alone cannot
close \eqref{eq:SMOS-energy-Hamiltonian-equivalence}.
\end{countertheorem}

% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
\paragraph{Trace-source Pythagoras and scheme-covariant anomaly class}
\label{subsec:SMOS-trace-anomaly}
% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

\begin{definition}[Physical scale-response packet]
\label{def:SMOS-scale-packet}
Let $\mathcal K_{\rm sc}$ be the common response carrier of one independently
physical shrinking scale deformation.  Retain:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(A\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item an absolute identity/pressure source $I_0:C_0\to\mathcal K_{\rm sc}$;
\item a complete nuisance source $N_0:C_N\to\mathcal K_{\rm sc}$ containing
      admitted improvements, EOM, BRST-exact, total-derivative, and physical
      boundary sources;
\item a represented local composite bank $O:C_O\to\mathcal K_{\rm sc}$;
\item the direct scale derivative $S_{\rm sc}:C_{\rm sc}\to\mathcal K_{\rm sc}$;
\item the direct trace-stress source $S_\Theta$ on the same source frame.
\end{enumerate}
All sources are unnormalized occurrence data.  The identity source is kept
separate from normalized local operators.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Identity--nuisance--composite--new-anomaly Pythagoras]
\label{thm:SMOS-trace-Pythagoras}
For the packet of \Cref{def:SMOS-scale-packet}, set
\[
 P_I=I_0(I_0^*I_0)^\dagger I_0^*,
 \qquad
 N_1=(I-P_I)N_0,
\]
\[
 P_N=N_1(N_1^*N_1)^\dagger N_1^*,
 \qquad
 O_1=(I-P_I-P_N)O,
\]
\[
 P_O=O_1(O_1^*O_1)^\dagger O_1^*,
 \qquad
 S_{\rm new}=(I-P_I-P_N-P_O)S_{\rm sc}.
\]
Then $P_I,P_N,P_O$ are mutually orthogonal projections and
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 S_{\rm sc}
 =P_IS_{\rm sc}+P_NS_{\rm sc}+P_OS_{\rm sc}+S_{\rm new}.}
 \label{eq:SMOS-trace-source-decomposition}
\end{equation}
Consequently,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 S_{\rm sc}^*S_{\rm sc}
 =G_{\rm abs}+G_{\rm triv}+G_{\beta}+G_{\rm new},}
 \label{eq:SMOS-trace-Gram-Pythagoras}
\end{equation}
where the four terms are the Grams of the four orthogonal summands.  Their
meanings are respectively:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(T\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item absolute vacuum/pressure scaling;
\item improvement/EOM/BRST/boundary freedom;
\item the represented composite anomaly, with minimum supported coefficient
      map
      \[
      \boxed{
      \beta=(O_1^*O_1)^\dagger O_1^*(I-P_I-P_N)S_{\rm sc};}
      \]
\item a genuinely new scale-response source absent from the declared anomaly
      basis.
\end{enumerate}
In particular,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 G_{\rm new}=0
 \iff
 \Ran S_{\rm sc}\subseteq\Ran(I_0,N_0,O).}
 \label{eq:SMOS-trace-new-zero}
\end{equation}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The construction is successive orthogonal projection.  By definition
$\Ran N_1\perp\Ran I_0$, and $\Ran O_1$ is orthogonal to both earlier ranges.
Thus the four terms in \eqref{eq:SMOS-trace-source-decomposition} are mutually
orthogonal.  Taking Grams proves \eqref{eq:SMOS-trace-Gram-Pythagoras}.  The
Moore--Penrose coordinate is the minimum-norm coefficient of the projection
onto $\Ran O_1$.  The final equivalence is the range criterion for the last
orthogonal residual.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Scale/trace incidence]
\label{def:SMOS-scale-trace-incidence}
The scale deformation and the stress trace belong to one physical packet only
when
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \Delta_{\Theta\mid\rm sc}^{\rm occ}
 =\|S_\Theta-S_{\rm sc}\|_{\HS}^2=0,}
 \label{eq:SMOS-scale-trace-incidence}
\end{equation}
with the common sign and normalization fixed by the unnormalized deformation.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Finite scheme covariance of the physical anomaly class]
\label{thm:SMOS-trace-scheme}
Suppose a finite admissible scheme change preserves the identity source range
and has
\[
 N_0'=N_0U,
 \qquad
 O'=OM+N_0R+I_0R_0,
\]
where $U$ and $M$ are invertible.  Then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 O_1'=O_1M,}
 \label{eq:SMOS-efficient-operator-scheme}
\end{equation}
and the represented anomaly source transforms by
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 P_{O'}S_{\rm sc}=P_OS_{\rm sc},}
 \label{eq:SMOS-anomaly-range-invariance}
\end{equation}
viewed as an ambient physical vector.  If
\[
 G_O=O_1^*O_1,
 \qquad
 \beta=G_O^\dagger O_1^*(I-P_I-P_N)S_{\rm sc},
\]
then on the supported operator quotient
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 G_O'=M^*G_OM,
 \qquad
 \beta'=M^{-1}\beta,}
 \label{eq:SMOS-anomaly-coordinate-scheme}
\end{equation}
whereas the physical projected-source Gram satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 S_{\rm sc}^*P_{O'}S_{\rm sc}
 =S_{\rm sc}^*P_OS_{\rm sc}.}
 \label{eq:SMOS-anomaly-Gram-invariance}
\end{equation}
Vanishing, rank, and the represented anomaly range are scheme invariant.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The ranges of $I_0$ and $N_0$ are unchanged by the invertible transformations.
Applying $I-P_I-P_N$ to $O'$ kills the $N_0R$ and $I_0R_0$ terms and gives
$O_1M$.  Since $M$ is invertible, $\Ran O_1'=\Ran O_1$, hence their ambient
orthogonal projections agree.  The metric of the represented operator basis
transforms by congruence, while the projected physical scale source and its
Gram on the scale-source coefficient space are unchanged.
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[A beta coefficient is not an anomaly operator]
The numbers in $\beta$ are coordinates relative to the selected represented
composite basis.  They acquire physical meaning only after the scale
source, trace source, nuisance bank, absolute identity row, and incidence
\eqref{eq:SMOS-scale-trace-incidence} have occurred.  A formal beta function or
minimal-subtraction coefficient list does not populate any of these rows.
\end{firewall}

% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
\paragraph{Stress--composite Wick excess}
\label{subsec:SMOS-stress-excess}
% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

\begin{definition}[Same-source stress--composite excess]
\label{def:SMOS-stress-excess}
Let $\kappa_{T,C_1,\ldots,C_k}^{\rm dir}$ be a direct connected tensor with one
efficient stress/current slot and $k$ represented composite slots.  Let
$\kappa_{T,C_1,\ldots,C_k}^{\rm Wick}$ be the bosonic Wick or fermionic
Pfaffian prediction computed from the same primitive covariance, corrected
vacuum, OS quotient, and source frame.  Define
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathbb E_{T;C_1\ldots C_k}
 =\kappa_{T,C_1,\ldots,C_k}^{\rm dir}
 -\kappa_{T,C_1,\ldots,C_k}^{\rm Wick}.}
 \label{eq:SMOS-stress-composite-excess}
\end{equation}
The tensor is then shorted in the stress slot by the complete trivial-source
range and tested for OS-null descent in every slot as in the preceding renormalized composite layer.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Stress-linked primitive non-Gaussianity]
\label{thm:SMOS-stress-excess}
Assume the stress/current relation packet, energy/Hamiltonian incidence, and
multislot OS descent have passed.  If the quotient-visible tensor corresponding
to \eqref{eq:SMOS-stress-composite-excess} is nonzero, then the represented
primitive state is not Gaussian or quasi-free on the selected local algebra.
Its vanishing is invariant under every finite admissible composite and stress
scheme change.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
In a Gaussian or quasi-free primitive state every polynomial composite and
stress/current moment is determined by the same covariance through Wick or
Pfaffian contraction.  Therefore every such excess vanishes.  A nonzero
quotient tensor contradicts that prediction.  Direct and Wick tensors transform
by the same multilinear basis maps, while nuisance additions vanish after the
stress short; hence the excess transforms covariantly and its vanishing is
scheme invariant.
\end{proof}

\begin{countertheorem}[A raw stress--composite cumulant can be purely Wick]
\label{cth:SMOS-raw-stress-cumulant}
For $X\sim N(0,1)$, let the candidate stress composite be
\[
 T=:X^2:=X^2-1.
\]
Then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \operatorname{Var}(T)=2\ne0,}
 \label{eq:SMOS-Gaussian-stress-cumulant}
\end{equation}
but this value is exactly the Wick prediction.  The excess
\eqref{eq:SMOS-stress-composite-excess} is zero.  Therefore a nonzero raw
stress correlation is not by itself an interaction witness.
\end{countertheorem}

% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
\paragraph{Quantitative cutoff transport}
\label{subsec:SMOS-cutoff}
% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

\begin{theorem}[Transport of simultaneous Ward shorts]
\label{thm:SMOS-Ward-short-transport}
After common-screen identification, suppose
\[
 G_{N,Z}=N_Z^*N_Z\succeq\gamma I,
 \qquad
 \|N_Z\|\le M_N,
 \qquad Z\in\{X,Y\}.
\]
Put
\[
 \varepsilon_N=\|N_Y-N_X\|,
 \qquad
 \varepsilon_G=\|G_{N,Y}-G_{N,X}\|,
\]
and let $P_{N,Z}$ be the nuisance range projections.  Then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \|P_{N,Y}-P_{N,X}\|
 \le
 2\gamma^{-1/2}\varepsilon_N
 +M_N\gamma^{-3/2}\varepsilon_G.}
 \label{eq:SMOS-nuisance-projection-transport}
\end{equation}
If $\|Y_X\|\le M_Y$ and
$\varepsilon_Y=\|Y_Y-Y_X\|$, then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \|(I-P_{N,Y})Y_Y-(I-P_{N,X})Y_X\|
 \le
 \varepsilon_Y
 +M_Y\|P_{N,Y}-P_{N,X}\|.}
 \label{eq:SMOS-efficient-Ward-transport}
\end{equation}
Hence the physical Ward obstruction Grams are Cauchy under summable source and
nuisance defects with a protected nuisance floor.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Whiten the nuisance sources:
\[
 V_Z=N_ZG_{N,Z}^{-1/2},
 \qquad
 P_{N,Z}=V_ZV_Z^*.
\]
The inverse-square-root functional calculus on $[\gamma,\infty)$ gives
\[
 \|G_{N,Y}^{-1/2}-G_{N,X}^{-1/2}\|
 \le\frac{1}{2\gamma^{3/2}}\varepsilon_G.
\]
Therefore
\[
 \|V_Y-V_X\|
 \le\gamma^{-1/2}\varepsilon_N
 +\frac{M_N}{2\gamma^{3/2}}\varepsilon_G.
\]
Since $V_X,V_Y$ are isometries on the supported nuisance carrier,
\[
 \|V_YV_Y^*-V_XV_X^*\|
 \le2\|V_Y-V_X\|,
\]
proving \eqref{eq:SMOS-nuisance-projection-transport}.  Add and subtract
$(I-P_{N,Y})Y_X$ to obtain
\eqref{eq:SMOS-efficient-Ward-transport}.  Gram convergence follows from
$A^*A-B^*B=A^*(A-B)+(A^*-B^*)B$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Energy and trace packet transport]
\label{thm:SMOS-energy-trace-transport}
Let $B_X,B_Y$ be common-core source maps with norm at most $M_B$, and suppose
\[
 \|B_Y-B_X\|\le\varepsilon_B,
 \quad
 \|E_Y-E_X\|\le\varepsilon_E,
 \quad
 \|H_Y-H_X\|\le\varepsilon_H
\]
on the protected graph screen, with
$\|E_Z-H_Z\|\le M_D$.  Then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \|(E_Y-H_Y)B_Y-(E_X-H_X)B_X\|
 \le
 (\varepsilon_E+\varepsilon_H)M_B+M_D\varepsilon_B.}
 \label{eq:SMOS-energy-incidence-transport}
\end{equation}
The same estimate applies to the direct scale/trace incidence after replacing
$E-H$ by $S_\Theta-S_{\rm sc}$.  Combining it with
\Cref{thm:SMOS-Ward-short-transport} transports the efficient trace-anomaly
source and every finite Ward relation Gram.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Add and subtract $(E_Y-H_Y)B_X$ and use the triangle inequality.  The scale
statement is identical.  The efficient-source assertion follows by applying
\eqref{eq:SMOS-efficient-Ward-transport} successively to the identity, nuisance,
and represented-composite shorts.
\end{proof}

\begin{countertheorem}[Cutoffwise Ward closure can escape the local continuum]
\label{cth:SMOS-Ward-source-escape}
Let
\[
 \mathcal H_n=\Span\{\Omega,e_1,\ldots,e_n\}
\]
and let the only nonzero efficient stress source at cutoff $n$ be $e_n$.  Every
cutoff has a unit stress Gram and can satisfy all finite algebraic Ward
relations on its own carrier.  For every fixed physical screen
$Q_r=|\Omega\rangle\langle\Omega|+\sum_{j\le r}|e_j\rangle\langle e_j|$,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 Q_r e_n=0
 \qquad(n>r).}
 \label{eq:SMOS-stress-source-escape}
\end{equation}
Thus cutoffwise stress closure and a noncollapsing source norm do not produce a
local continuum stress operator without transported source incidence on an
exhausting atlas.
\end{countertheorem}

% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
\paragraph{Cofinal stress/current landing and finite compiler}
\label{subsec:SMOS-landing}
% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

\begin{theorem}[Conditional OS stress/current continuum theorem]
\label{thm:SMOS-cofinal-stress}
Suppose one regulator sequence supplies:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(C\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item the preceding determinant-line, reflected-slab, vacuum, Hamiltonian, and composite-operator packets physical line, reflected slab, corrected vacuum, common
      Hamiltonian, local composite algebra, contact, domain, and source
      transport packets;
\item direct source-complete current/stress Ward panels and one simultaneously
      transported trivial-response bank;
\item vanishing efficient conservation, symmetry, graded-locality,
      Ward--Leibniz, Ward-contact-cocycle, and direct triple-occurrence
      residuals;
\item one common-core energy-density/Hamiltonian incidence residual tending to
      zero, together with the absolute vacuum-energy/pressure anchor;
\item one physical shrinking scale deformation whose scale/trace incidence
      passes, with stable identity, nuisance, represented anomaly, and new-source
      ranks;
\item summable source, graph-domain, Ward-short, energy, trace, contact, and
      cutoff defects on an exhausting local atlas;
\item the inherited curvature or polymer compactness alternative and the inherited locality and
      temporal-continuity hypotheses;
\item one transported nonzero quotient-visible stress--composite Wick or
      Pfaffian excess.
\end{enumerate}
Then the limiting OS theory contains:
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \text{closable represented current and stress insertions on one common core},}
 \label{eq:SMOS-limit-stress-sector}
\end{equation}
which satisfy the selected operator Ward identities, symmetry, graded locality,
and Ward-contact associativity.  The spatial integral of the Euclidean energy
density is the same positive Hamiltonian $H$ reconstructed from the reflected
slab.  The trace has a scheme-covariant represented anomaly class, with the
absolute identity/pressure component retained separately.  The nonzero
stress--composite excess proves that the represented primitive state is not
Gaussian or quasi-free on the selected local algebra.

The theorem is target relative.  It does not by itself construct an exhaustive
ambient stress tensor, a quantum metric, the Einstein equation, or every
superselection-sector current.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The inherited renormalized-composite and common-domain packets give the limiting represented composite
algebra.  \Cref{thm:SMOS-Ward-short-transport} makes the efficient Ward sources
Cauchy; the zero residuals and atlas completeness pass the operator relations
by \Cref{thm:SMOS-Ward-atlas,thm:SMOS-stress-current-criterion}.  The Ward contact
cocycle and direct triple occurrence pass by multilinear continuity.

The graph-core energy sources converge by
\eqref{eq:SMOS-energy-incidence-transport}; equality on the limiting common core
and closedness give the Hamiltonian incidence of
\Cref{thm:SMOS-energy-Hamiltonian-incidence}.  The physical scale family and
stable sequential shorts transport the orthogonal decomposition
\eqref{eq:SMOS-trace-source-decomposition};
\Cref{thm:SMOS-trace-scheme} makes its represented anomaly range scheme
covariant.  Compactness supplies the OS continuum state.  Finally,
\Cref{thm:SMOS-stress-excess} converts the transported nonzero quotient excess
into the claimed non-Gaussian or non-quasi-free conclusion.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Terminating stress/Ward compiler]
\label{thm:SMOS-compiler}
At one finite cutoff, proceed in this order.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\arabic*)},leftmargin=6.4em]
\item Run the complete inherited renormalized-composite algebra, contact, domain, and source-
      transport compiler.
\item Freeze the current/stress candidates, test atlas, symmetry actions,
      coincident Ward contacts, and the complete trivial-source bank.
\item Acquire all Ward response rows on one common carrier and run the
      simultaneous short of \Cref{thm:SMOS-Ward-short}.
\item Return a source-atlas defect before interpreting a zero vacuum
      expectation as an operator identity.
\item Test the Ward--Leibniz relation, the graded contact cocycle, and the direct
      triple Ward occurrence row.
\item Test stress symmetry, conservation, and disjoint-support graded locality
      on the represented quotient.
\item Assemble the spatial energy density with every boundary and improvement
      term and test its common-core incidence with the OS Hamiltonian.
\item Acquire the physical shrinking scale family, run the trace-source
      Pythagoras, and compare the scale source with the stress trace.
\item Evaluate one same-source stress--composite Wick/Pfaffian excess and retain
      one held-out contact, energy, and trace command.
\item Repeat the complete packet at one adjacent cutoff and run the transport
      bounds before claiming a continuum stress/current sector.
\end{enumerate}
The compiler returns exactly one of
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \begin{gathered}
 \text{an inherited composite/contact/domain obstruction},\\
 \text{a nonphysical nuisance short or source-atlas defect},\\
 \text{a source-minimal Ward anomaly writer},\\
 \text{a contact-cocycle or triple-occurrence failure},\\
 \text{a conservation, symmetry, or graded-locality witness},\\
 \text{an energy-density/OS-Hamiltonian mismatch},\\
 \text{an unfixed absolute energy/pressure fibre},\\
 \text{a new trace source beyond the declared basis},\\
 \text{a scale/trace occurrence or scheme-transport defect},\\
 \text{a Gaussian/quasi-free stress response},\\
 \text{a moving stress source without a local limit},\\
 \text{or a represented stress/current sector with nonzero}\\
 \text{scheme-covariant stress--composite excess}.
 \end{gathered}}
 \label{eq:SMOS-compiler-output}
\end{equation}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Each step is the first applicable theorem, countertheorem, or positive residual
in the listed order.  The nuisance, represented-composite, and scale-source
shorts have finite rank and therefore terminate.  Every later test is a finite
Gram, support, domain, or held-out occurrence comparison.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Canonical accepted/action states, trajectory closure, and driven fluctuations}
\label{sec:accepted-state-trajectory-tilt}
% =============================================================================

The determining-field quotient and the common-action comparator solve two
finite reconstruction problems but do not by themselves specify the smallest
output state required by every subsequent use.  Comparison with a retained
initial class, autonomous output reconstruction, repeated updates, complete
trajectory likelihoods, and long-time conditioned fluctuations are distinct
operational tasks.  This subsection gives the canonical finite quotient and
the exact positive residual appropriate to each task.


% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
\subsubsection{Target-native scalar layer and one-history projections}
\label{sec:accepted-target-native-layer}
% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

Before constructing the canonical accepted/action state records below, one
must identify the strength of the intended output.  A complete relative-entropy
family, autonomous accepted dynamics, trajectory likelihood, and driven
process require the corresponding quotient, kernel, or path packet.  One
selected scalar expectation may close earlier.

\begin{corollary}[Selected accepted/action scalar before state reconstruction]
\label{cor:accepted-target-native-scalar}
Let $w$ be one bounded same-history accepted/action writer and let $Y$ be one
physical Read of it.  If
\[
 \mathbb C_{\Span\{\one\}}^{\rm cal}(Y\mid w)=0,
\]
then
\[
 \boxed{\mathbb EY=\mathbb Ew.}
\]
If $w$ is not directly readable, any physical lower--upper sandwich closes the
certified interval of \Cref{thm:GT-target-sandwich}.  These scalar branches do
not require the likelihood-ratio quotient, projective experiment quotient,
future-saturated state, Markov retract, occupation-flow record, or Feynman--Kac
operator.  Those remain the minimum objects for their stronger families of
outputs.
\end{corollary}

\begin{corollary}[One nonvacuum history viewed through three projections]
\label{cor:accepted-one-history-three-projections}
Let one physical endpoint history on the scheduler-separated spacetime branch
carry deterministic projections
\[
 \pi_{\rm F},\qquad \pi_{\rm P},\qquad \pi_{\rm N}
\]
onto, respectively, a stopped Foundational record, a positive
factor/action/boundary record on every branch where that factorization is
physically valid, and an assembled state--current record.  Then:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2.8em]
\item the Foundational reference law is the pushforward of this history, rather
      than an independently selected comparator law;
\item the Phase factor cylinder and the spacetime current are two representations
      of the same source germ whenever their incidence residuals vanish;
\item every writer common to the three projections has one expectation, and
      every apparent branchwise source birth must be shorted against the common
      joint source Gram before it is counted;
\item pairwise branch compatibility does not establish a common history or a
      genuinely triple writer.
\end{enumerate}
The last alternative is decided by the positive common-cylinder audit of
\Cref{thm:GT-one-history-projection}.
\end{corollary}

\begin{corollary}[Intrinsic cylinder before likelihood coordinates]
\label{cor:accepted-cylinder-before-LR}
Suppose the accepted/action experiment is supplied by one positive
unnormalized cylinder $\Lambda$ and one physical payoff $A$.  Then the selected
normalized value is intrinsic to $(\Lambda,A)$.  Any full-support reference law
and likelihood ratio represent the same value by
\[
 \mathbb E_\mu A=\mathbb E_\nu[W_\nu A],
\]
but the pair $(\nu,W_\nu)$ is not unique.  The likelihood-ratio quotient below
is therefore canonical only relative to the physically declared actual and
comparator row families; it is not a preferred factorization of an intrinsic
positive cylinder.
\end{corollary}

\begin{firewall}[Scalar agreement, common occurrence, and process closure]
\label{fire:accepted-target-native-scope}
Three separately obtained scalar agreements do not prove that the
Foundational, Phase, and spacetime writers occurred on one history.  Conversely,
once a same-event mixed Read has occurred and has been calibrated for the
declared use class, no complete state or path reconstruction is charged merely
to report its mean.  Static scalar closure, common-history occurrence,
relative-entropy sufficiency, semigroup autonomy, path likelihood, fluctuation
closure, and driven-process closure remain distinct levels.
\end{firewall}


% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
\subsubsection{Minimum co-retention and the fine accepted/action comparison}
\label{sec:accepted-master-comparison}
% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

\begin{theorem}[Canonical minimum of a co-retained accepted tuple]
\label{thm:accepted-master-tuple}
Let \(r_j:\Omega\to\Omega_j\), \(1\le j\le m\), be finitely many protected
coordinates produced at possibly different stages of one accepted history, and
put
\[
 \tau=(r_1,\ldots,r_m):\Omega\longrightarrow\Omega_\tau:=\tau(\Omega).
\]
Then the classical algebra generated by all coordinate Reads is exactly
\[
 \boxed{\mathfrak R_\tau=\tau^*C(\Omega_\tau).}
\]
Its nonzero minimal projections are the joint-tuple indicators.  Every sharp
record through which all \(r_j\) factor maps onto \(\Omega_\tau\); hence the
minimum sharp co-retention cost is \(|\Omega_\tau|\), not the cardinality of
the ambient Cartesian product.

If a coordinate would be erased before the common terminal cut, copying it to
an append-only classical ledger immediately before erasure is conservative:
tracing the ledger recovers the original complete process, and no feedback is
created unless a later operation is explicitly given an input wire from the
copy.  With tuple projections \(p_t\), a saturated word bank \(W_\alpha\), and
insertions \(X_\lambda\), the master panel
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathbb M^{(\lambda)}_{(t,\alpha),(u,\beta)}
 =\langle p_tW_\alpha,X_\lambda p_uW_\beta\rangle}
\]
contains every finite provenance, pulse, chronological, determining-field, and
action subpanel by finite compression.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Every coordinate function is constant on a tuple fibre, so the generated
algebra is contained in \(\tau^*C(\Omega_\tau)\).  Conversely the indicator of
a tuple value is the product of its coordinate point indicators, so every
point function on \(\Omega_\tau\) is generated.  If \(r_j=f_j\circ q\), then
\(\tau=(f_1,\ldots,f_m)\circ q\), giving the universal surjection and the
cardinality bound.  A passive copy has block form
\(\oplus_\omega\rho_\omega\mapsto
 \oplus_\omega\rho_\omega\otimes|r_j(\omega)\rangle\langle r_j(\omega)|\);
partial trace is the identity, and induction gives conservativity for
sequential copies.  Finally every derived panel is obtained by applying its
coefficient synthesis and compression maps to the complete master Gram.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Fine accepted comparison datum]
\label{def:accepted-fine-comparison}
Let \(\Omega_0\) be the finite initial accepted-history support with faithful
law \(\mu_x\), let \(\mathcal U\) be the complete fine accepted output record,
and let
\[
 \kappa_x(u)=\Pr(U=u\mid X=x,\mathrm{acc})
\]
be the observed row.  Let \(q_x^*\) be the independently reconstructed
common-action comparator.  Put
\[
 \Sigma(x)=(\kappa_x,q_x^*)
\]
and define \(x\sim_{\rm cmp}x'\) when \(\Sigma(x)=\Sigma(x')\).  The quotient
is denoted
\[
 \boxed{F_{\rm cmp}:\Omega_0\twoheadrightarrow\Theta_{\rm cmp}.}
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Canonical initial comparison quotient]
\label{thm:accepted-comparison-quotient}
The actual and comparator row families factor uniquely through
\(F_{\rm cmp}\).  Every other deterministic initial record through which both
families factor maps uniquely onto \(\Theta_{\rm cmp}\).  If all admitted
future accepted cylinders are included in the signatures, finite partition
refinement reconstructs this quotient after at most \(|\Omega_0|-1\) strict
splits.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The two row families are constant on the displayed equivalence classes.  If a
second quotient identifies \(x,x'\), factorization through it forces equality
of both rows and hence \(x\sim_{\rm cmp}x'\).  This gives the universal map.
The finite refinement argument is identical to the minimal-readable-record
compiler: split a block whenever one actual or comparator future signature
differs, and terminate because the number of blocks strictly increases.
\end{proof}

Let \(F:\Omega_0\to\Theta\) be any quotient through which the comparator
factors, put
\[
 \nu_\theta=\sum_{F(x)=\theta}\mu_x,
 \qquad
 \bar\kappa_\theta
 =\nu_\theta^{-1}\sum_{F(x)=\theta}\mu_x\kappa_x,
\]
and let \(C:\mathcal U\to\mathcal Z\) be any coarse terminal Read.

\begin{theorem}[Four-term accepted/action information Pythagoras]
\label{thm:accepted-four-term-Pythagoras}
With superscript \(C\) denoting pushforward and conditional rows taken inside
\(C\)-fibres, define
\[
 \Delta_{\rm lump}^{C}
 =\sum_x\mu_x\operatorname{KL}
   (\kappa_x^{C}\|\bar\kappa_{F(x)}^{C}),
\]
\[
 \Delta_{\rm fld}^{\rm hid}
 =\sum_{x,z}\mu_x\kappa_x^C(z)
   \operatorname{KL}
   (\kappa_x(\cdot\mid z)\|\bar\kappa_{F(x)}(\cdot\mid z)),
\]
\[
 \eta\overline\Delta_{\rm act}^{C}
 =\sum_\theta\nu_\theta
   \operatorname{KL}(\bar\kappa_\theta^C\|q_\theta^{*,C}),
\]
and
\[
 \eta\overline\Delta_{\rm act}^{\rm hid}
 =\sum_{\theta,z}\nu_\theta\bar\kappa_\theta^C(z)
   \operatorname{KL}
   (\bar\kappa_\theta(\cdot\mid z)\|q_\theta^*(\cdot\mid z)).
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{
 \begin{aligned}
 \sum_x\mu_x\operatorname{KL}(\kappa_x\|q_{F(x)}^*)
 &=\Delta_{\rm lump}^{C}+\Delta_{\rm fld}^{\rm hid}\\
 &\quad+\eta\overline\Delta_{\rm act}^{C}
       +\eta\overline\Delta_{\rm act}^{\rm hid}.
 \end{aligned}}
\]
All four terms are nonnegative.  They vanish simultaneously exactly when the
fine observed and comparator rows agree on every supported coordinate.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Insert the conditional mean row \(\bar\kappa_{F(x)}\).  The standard
relative-entropy projection identity separates the field insufficiency from
the action mismatch.  Applying the relative-entropy chain rule to the map
\(C\) in each of the two terms gives the displayed four summands.  Equality is
equivalent to equality in every faithful relative entropy.
\end{proof}

% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
\subsubsection{Canonical static output records}
\label{sec:accepted-static-output-quotients}
% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

Assume first that every comparator row \(q_\theta^*\) is faithful.  Define the
complete likelihood-ratio signature
\[
 \Lambda(u)=
 \left(\frac{\kappa_\theta(u)}{q_\theta^*(u)}
 \right)_{\theta\in\Theta_{\rm cmp}}.
\]

\begin{theorem}[Canonical likelihood-ratio quotient]
\label{thm:accepted-LR-quotient}
The quotient
\[
 \boxed{
 C_{\rm LR}:\mathcal U\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal Z_{\rm LR},
 \qquad
 u\sim_{\rm LR}v\iff\Lambda(u)=\Lambda(v)}
\]
is the unique coarsest deterministic output record preserving every classwise
accepted/action relative entropy:
\[
 \boxed{
 \operatorname{KL}(\kappa_\theta\|q_\theta^*)
 =\operatorname{KL}
  (\kappa_\theta^{\rm LR}\|q_\theta^{*,\rm LR}).}
\]
Inside every quotient cell the actual and comparator conditional laws agree.
Consequently there is a class-dependent common conditional kernel \(R_\theta\)
with
\[
 \boxed{
 \kappa_\theta=\kappa_\theta^{\rm LR}R_\theta,
 \qquad
 q_\theta^*=q_\theta^{*,\rm LR}R_\theta.}
\]
Total variation is preserved, and for every bounded fine observable \(f\),
its actual/comparator expectation difference is reconstructed exactly from the
quotient rows and the common conditional mean of \(f\) in each cell.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
For one pair \((p,q)\), the KL chain rule under a deterministic map is
\[
 \operatorname{KL}(p\|q)
 =\operatorname{KL}(p^C\|q^C)
 +\sum_zp^C(z)\operatorname{KL}
   (p(\cdot\mid z)\|q(\cdot\mid z)).
\]
Equality holds exactly when \(p/q\) is constant on each fibre.  Applying this
to every comparison class proves losslessness.  Any other lossless Read must
make every component of \(\Lambda\) fibrewise constant and hence refines
\(C_{\rm LR}\).  Equality of the conditional laws gives the decoder and the
observable identity; fibrewise constancy also fixes the sign of \(p-q\) and
therefore preserves total variation.
\end{proof}

For support-exact autonomous compression, let \(\{\mu_i:i\in\mathcal I\}\)
be the complete family of actual and comparator rows, let
\(m=\sum_i\omega_i\mu_i\) be any faithful positive mixture on the union
support, and put \(c(u)=(\mu_i(u))_i\).

\begin{theorem}[Canonical finite-experiment quotient and common decoder]
\label{thm:accepted-experiment-quotient}
Define
\[
 \boxed{
 u\sim_{\rm exp}v
 \iff c(u)=a\,c(v)\text{ for some }a>0,}
\]
and let \(C_{\rm exp}:\mathcal U_+\to\mathcal Z_{\rm exp}\) be the quotient.
The equivalence is independent of the mixture weights and is characterized by
vanishing of every \(2\times2\) column minor.  The kernel
\[
 \boxed{
 R(u\mid z)
 =\one_{\{C_{\rm exp}(u)=z\}}
  \frac{m(u)}{\sum_{v:C_{\rm exp}(v)=z}m(v)}}
\]
is independent of \(i\) and reconstructs every row:
\[
 \boxed{\mu_i=\mu_i^{\rm exp}R.}
\]
This is the unique coarsest deterministic output record admitting one decoder
for the complete experiment.  It preserves every pairwise finite
\(f\)-divergence, every support singularity, and every later stochastic
channel.  In particular, if \(L\) is a later channel, then
\[
 \boxed{
 \mu_iL=\mu_i^{\rm exp}L_{\rm exp},
 \qquad
 L_{\rm exp}=RL.}
\]
The experiment quotient refines \(C_{\rm LR}\); equality holds exactly when
the comparator conditionals inside each LR cell are independent of the
comparison class.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Normalized density columns \(c(u)/m(u)\) agree exactly when the probability
columns are positively proportional; this also proves independence of the
mixture.  On one quotient cell write \(\mu_i(u)=a_i(z)m(u)\).  Summation gives
\(a_i(z)=\mu_i^{\rm exp}(z)/m^{\rm exp}(z)\), proving the common decoder.
Every other common-decoder record makes the ratio of any two experiment rows
constant inside its fibres and therefore refines the projective-column
partition.  Pairwise likelihood ratios are cellwise constant, so every
\(f\)-divergence is preserved, including singular rays.  Composition with a
later channel follows by inserting the common decoder.  The relation to
\(C_{\rm LR}\) is immediate because proportional complete columns have equal
actual/comparator ratios; equality requires the class-dependent LR decoders to
coincide.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Decoder innovation]
\label{thm:accepted-decoder-innovation}
For any proposed output compression \(C\), let
\[
 R_C(u\mid z)=\one_{\{C(u)=z\}}\frac{m(u)}{m^C(z)}
\]
and define
\[
 \boxed{
 \Delta_{\rm dec}(C)
 =\sum_i\omega_i\sum_z\mu_i^C(z)
  \operatorname{KL}(\mu_i(\cdot\mid z)\|R_C(\cdot\mid z)).}
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{
 \sum_i\omega_i\operatorname{KL}(\mu_i\|m)
 =\sum_i\omega_i\operatorname{KL}(\mu_i^C\|m^C)
  +\Delta_{\rm dec}(C).}
\]
Moreover \(\Delta_{\rm dec}(C)=0\) exactly when \(C\) refines
\(C_{\rm exp}\).  Probabilistically it is the conditional mutual information
between the experiment index and the fine output given the proposed record.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Apply the KL chain rule to each pair \((\mu_i,m)\) and average.  Zero conditional
KL makes the fine conditional law independent of \(i\), which is precisely the
common-decoder condition characterized by
\Cref{thm:accepted-experiment-quotient}.
\end{proof}

% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
\subsubsection{Quantum sufficiency, Petz recovery, and process-causal closure}
\label{sec:accepted-quantum-sufficiency}
% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

The classical common-decoder quotient has a noncommutative analogue, but its
zero-loss condition is relative to the declared physical state family and does
not by itself certify a causal process map.

\begin{theorem}[Finite Petz recovery and family sufficiency]
\label{thm:accepted-Petz-sufficiency}
Let $\mathcal T_*$ be a finite CPTP map, let $\sigma\succ0$ be a faithful
reference state on the family support, put $\bar\sigma=\mathcal T_*(\sigma)$,
and let $\mathcal T$ be the Heisenberg adjoint.  The Petz map is
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal R_{\sigma,\mathcal T,*}(x)
 =\sigma^{1/2}\mathcal T
  (\bar\sigma^{-1/2}x\bar\sigma^{-1/2})\sigma^{1/2}.}
 \tag{QS.1}
\]
For every supported state $\rho$,
\[
 \boxed{
 \Delta_{\rm DPI}(\rho\mid\sigma;\mathcal T)
 =D(\rho\Vert\sigma)
  -D(\mathcal T_*\rho\Vert\bar\sigma)\ge0,}
 \tag{QS.2}
\]
and
\[
 \boxed{
 \Delta_{\rm DPI}=0
 \iff
 \mathcal R_{\sigma,\mathcal T,*}\mathcal T_*(\rho)=\rho.}
 \tag{QS.3}
\]
For a finite declared family $\rho_a$ define
\[
 e_a=\rho_a-\mathcal R_{\sigma,\mathcal T,*}\mathcal T_*(\rho_a),
 \qquad
 \boxed{[\mathbb G_{\rm rec}]_{ab}=\Tr(e_a^*e_b)\succeq0.}
 \tag{QS.4}
\]
Then $\mathbb G_{\rm rec}=0$ exactly when the channel is sufficient for the
complete family.  The zero property is independent of the chosen strictly
positive barycentric reference, although the numerical loss and recovery map
depend on the physical preparation weights.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The map in \textup{(QS.1)} is CPTP on the supported output algebra and recovers
$\sigma$.  Monotonicity of finite-dimensional relative entropy follows from
operator Jensen applied to the relative modular operator.  Equality in that
strictly operator-convex Jensen step is equivalent to intertwining the relative
modular vector by the associated weighted Stinespring contraction; rewriting
that intertwining gives exactly \textup{(QS.3)}.  The family statement follows
because \textup{(QS.4)} is the Gram of the individual recovery errors.  If one
recovery channel recovers every $\rho_a$, it recovers every positive mixture;
conversely the Petz equality criterion for any faithful positive mixture
recovers each positively weighted family member.  This proves reference-
mixture independence of the zero branch.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[BKM loss as the local data-processing Hessian]
\label{cor:accepted-BKM-loss}
For a differentiable state path $\rho_t$ through $\sigma$ with tangent $v$,
the second derivative at zero of \textup{(QS.2)} is
\[
 \boxed{
 g_\sigma^{\rm BKM}(v,v)
 -g_{\bar\sigma}^{\rm BKM}(\mathcal T_*v,\mathcal T_*v)\ge0,}
 \tag{QS.5}
\]
where
\[
 g_\sigma^{\rm BKM}(v,v)
 =\Tr\bigl(v\,\Omega_\sigma^{-1}(v)\bigr),
 \qquad
 \Omega_\sigma(X)=\int_0^1\sigma^{1-s}X\sigma^s\,\dd s.
\]
Zero BKM loss is only a tangent certificate; exact nonlinear family
sufficiency still requires \textup{(QS.3)} or \textup{(QS.4)}.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The Hessian of relative entropy at its faithful base point is the
Bogoliubov--Kubo--Mori metric.  Differentiating the two terms in
\textup{(QS.2)} and using linearity of $\mathcal T_*$ gives
\textup{(QS.5)}.  Nonnegativity follows from data processing.  Equality of one
quadratic tangent does not imply equality of the full relative modular family.
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[State recovery is not process recovery]
A CPTP map may recover every normalized Choi matrix in a declared finite state
family while failing the affine partial-trace recursion that makes those
matrices deterministic channels or multitime combs.  Process sufficiency
therefore requires, in addition to \textup{(QS.4)}, vanishing causal-recursion
residuals on the complete process span and compatibility with sequential
composition.  Ambient state recovery is not used as a substitute for a
physical superchannel.
\end{firewall}

% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
\subsubsection{Future saturation, Markov retracts, and generator memory}
\label{sec:accepted-dynamic-state}
% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

Let \(\{K_a:a\in\Sigma\}\) be a finite alphabet of later stochastic update
letters on \(\mathcal U_+\), and let \(V_0\) be the span of the complete
experiment rows.  Put
\[
 V_{r+1}=V_r+\sum_{a\in\Sigma}V_rK_a.
\]

\begin{theorem}[Finite future-saturated experiment state]
\label{thm:accepted-future-quotient}
The increasing chain \(V_r\) stabilizes after at most
\(|\mathcal U_+|-\dim V_0\) strict rank increases, at
\[
 \boxed{V_\infty=\Span\{\mu_iK_w:i\in\mathcal I,
 w\in\Sigma^*\}.}
\]
Choose a positive \(m\in V_\infty\) on the union support and a basis
\(f_1,\ldots,f_d\) of \(V_\infty\).  The joint level sets of
\[
 \left(\frac{f_1(u)}{m(u)},\ldots,\frac{f_d(u)}{m(u)}\right)
\]
define a basis-independent quotient \(C_{\rm fut}\) with one decoder
\(R_{\rm fut}\) satisfying
\[
 \boxed{f=(fC_{\rm fut})R_{\rm fut}
 \qquad(f\in V_\infty).}
\]
It is the unique coarsest deterministic record reconstructing every reachable
future row.  With
\[
 K_a^{\rm fut}=R_{\rm fut}K_aC_{\rm fut},
\]
one has, for every reachable row and word,
\[
 \boxed{
 \mu_iK_w
 = (\mu_iC_{\rm fut})K_w^{\rm fut}R_{\rm fut}.}
\]
Thus \(C_{\rm exp}\preceq C_{\rm fut}\), possibly strictly.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The chain consists of subspaces of a fixed finite-dimensional row space, so it
stabilizes.  Its stable value is invariant under every \(K_a\) and contains
all word rows; the reverse inclusion follows by construction.  The projective
column argument of \Cref{thm:accepted-experiment-quotient}, applied to a basis
of this row space, gives the quotient, common decoder, and universal property.
Invariance then gives the exact word recursion.
\end{proof}

Assume now that a faithful reference law \(m\) is stationary for every
\(K_a\).  For a deterministic quotient \(C\), let \(R\) be the stationary
conditional decoder, \(E=CR\), and \(L_a=RK_aC\).

\begin{theorem}[Universal Markov retract and the stronger reset branch]
\label{thm:accepted-Markov-retract}
For one update letter the following are equivalent:
\[
 \boxed{EK_a=K_aE,}
\]
\[
 \boxed{K_aC=CL_a,
 \qquad RK_a=L_aR,}
\]
and simultaneous strong lumpability of \(K_a\) and its stationary reversal
\[
 K_a^\sharp(v,u)=\frac{m(u)K_a(u,v)}{m(v)}
\]
through the same partition.  On this branch every fine law has exact quotient
dynamics and every decoded quotient law has exact reconstructed fine dynamics.
The unique coarsest refinement of \(C_{\rm fut}\) with this property is found
by finite partition refinement using forward and reversed block transition
masses.

The stronger fibre-reset identity is
\[
 \boxed{K_a=CL_aR=EK_aE.}
\]
It requires both Markov-retract closure and erasure of all within-cell motion;
a quotient may be exactly Markov while this reset residual remains positive.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Using \(RC=I\), the two intertwining relations imply
\(EK_a=CRK_a=CL_aR=K_aCR=K_aE\).  Conversely commutation gives
\(K_aC=EK_aC=C(RK_aC)\) and similarly for the decoder.  Taking adjoints in
\(L^2(m)\) identifies decoder invariance with forward lumpability of the
reversed kernel.  Stable finite partition refinement is the standard
simultaneous bisimulation algorithm.  The reset statement is the additional
identity that the fine update factors through the decoder on both sides.
\end{proof}

Let \(L\) be a finite continuous-time Markov generator and let
\(W_0=\Span\{\mu_i\}\), \(W_{r+1}=W_r+W_rL\).

\begin{theorem}[Generator-native state closure and Mori--Zwanzig alternative]
\label{thm:accepted-generator-closure}
The Krylov chain stabilizes finitely at
\[
 \boxed{
 W_\infty=\Span\{\mu_iL^k:i,k\}
 =\Span\{\mu_ie^{tL}:i,t\ge0\}.}
\]
Its projective-column quotient \(C_L\) reconstructs every reachable continuous
future.  For a proposed quotient with decoder \(R\), projection \(E=CR\), and
coarse generator \(A=RLC\), the following are equivalent:
\[
 \boxed{EL=LE,}
\]
\[
 \boxed{LC=CA,
 \qquad RL=AR,}
\]
and simultaneous rate lumpability of \(L\) and its stationary reversal.
Then
\[
 \boxed{e^{tL}C=Ce^{tA},
 \qquad Re^{tL}=e^{tA}R.}
\]

If commutation fails, put \(Q=I-E\).  For a fine evolving row split as
\(x(t)=p(t)E\), \(y(t)=p(t)Q\), elimination of \(y\) gives
\[
 \boxed{
 \begin{aligned}
 \dot x(t)
 &=x(t)ELE+y(0)e^{tQLQ}QLE\\
 &\quad+\int_0^t x(s)
   ELQe^{(t-s)QLQ}QLE\,\dd s.
 \end{aligned}}
\]
The visible resolvent is
\[
 \boxed{
 E(zI-L)^{-1}E
 =\left[zE-ELE-ELQ(zQ-QLQ)^{-1}QLE\right]^{-1}.}
\]
Thus failure of generator closure returns an exact initial hidden term, memory
kernel, and frequency-dependent self-energy.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Finite-dimensional Krylov stabilization and the exponential power series give
the first equality.  The projective-column proof is as in
\Cref{thm:accepted-future-quotient}.  The commutator equivalence follows from
\(RC=I\) exactly as in the discrete case, and exponentiation gives the
semigroup identities.  The coupled equations for \(x,y\) follow by inserting
\(E+Q=I\) around \(L\).  Variation of constants solves the \(Q\)-equation;
substitution gives the memory equation.  Block inversion gives the resolvent
short.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Canonical finite-rate fibre refresh]
\label{cor:accepted-Poisson-refresh}
For a coarse generator \(A\), decoder \(R\), quotient \(C\), and
\(E=CR\), the operator
\[
 \boxed{L_\lambda=CAR+\lambda(E-I)}
\]
is a fine Markov generator for sufficiently large \(\lambda\), with exact
semigroup
\[
 \boxed{
 e^{tL_\lambda}=Ce^{tA}R+e^{-\lambda t}(I-E).}
\]
It preserves exact quotient dynamics while refreshing hidden fibre memory
exponentially.  A nontrivial exact fibre reset cannot hold at every
arbitrarily small positive time in a strongly continuous semigroup, because
taking \(t\downarrow0\) would force \(E=I\).
\end{corollary}


% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
\subsubsection{Reflected action-response closure from three stationary cylinders}
\label{sec:accepted-three-cylinder-action}
% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

A future-sufficient state quotient and a static common action do not by
themselves decide whether the corresponding action-response bank reduces the
physical transfer.  On a positive reflected branch this question has an exact
finite answer.  The construction below is stated for a general bounded writer
bank and is therefore available to the fully assembled gravity--internal
packet once the accepted transfer and common-action incidence have been
verified.

\begin{definition}[Conditional action-response carr\'e du champ]
\label{def:GT-conditional-action-response}
Let $T$ be a finite positivity-preserving self-adjoint transfer satisfying
\[
 0\preceq T\preceq I,\qquad T\Omega=\Omega,
 \qquad \Omega>0,
\]
in a configuration representation with reference measure $\nu$.  Put
\[
 \dd\mu=|\Omega|^2\dd\nu,
 \qquad U_\Omega f=\Omega f,
 \qquad P=U_\Omega^{-1}TU_\Omega.
 \tag{AR.1}
\]
For a complete bounded physical writer bank
$F=(F_1,\ldots,F_d)$ define the Hermitian matrix-valued pair action
\[
 \boxed{
 [\mathcal A_F(x,y)]_{ij}
 =\frac12\,
 \overline{F_i(y)-F_i(x)}\bigl(F_j(y)-F_j(x)\bigr)}
 \tag{AR.2}
\]
and its entrance-conditional writer
\[
 \boxed{
 \Gamma_P(F)(x)
 =\int \mathcal A_F(x,y)P(x,\dd y)\succeq0.}
 \tag{AR.3}
\]
Let $Y_F:\C^d\to\mathcal H_T$ be
\[
 Y_Fc=\left(\sum_{j=1}^dF_jc_j\right)\Omega.
 \tag{AR.4}
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Reflected endpoint-action identity]
\label{thm:GT-reflected-endpoint-action}
For the packet of \Cref{def:GT-conditional-action-response}, $P$ is a positive
self-adjoint Markov contraction on $L^2(\mu)$.  If $(X_0,X_1)$ has stationary
pair law $\mu(\dd x)P(x,\dd y)$, then
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathbb E[\mathcal A_F(X_0,X_1)\mid X_0]
 =\Gamma_P(F)(X_0),}
 \tag{AR.5}
\]
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathbb E[\mathcal A_F(X_0,X_1)\mid X_1]
 =\Gamma_P(F)(X_1),}
 \tag{AR.6}
\]
and
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathbb E_\mu\Gamma_P(F)=Y_F^*(I-T)Y_F.}
 \tag{AR.7}
\]
Thus reflection identifies the entrance and exit action-response writers, and
their mean is exactly the transfer Dirichlet action on the declared bank.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The ground-state multiplication $U_\Omega$ is unitary from $L^2(\mu)$ to the
physical transfer space.  Positivity preservation, self-adjointness,
$T\Omega=\Omega$, and $0\preceq T\preceq I$ therefore make $P$ a positive
self-adjoint Markov contraction.  Conditioning \textup{(AR.2)} on $X_0=x$
gives \textup{(AR.3)} and proves \textup{(AR.5)}.  Reversibility makes the
stationary pair measure symmetric under $(x,y)\leftrightarrow(y,x)$, while
$\mathcal A_F(x,y)=\mathcal A_F(y,x)$, proving \textup{(AR.6)}.  Averaging and
expanding gives, entrywise,
\[
 \mathbb E_\mu[\Gamma_P(F)]_{ij}
 =\langle F_i,(I-P)F_j\rangle_{L^2(\mu)}.
\]
Conjugation by $U_\Omega$ is exactly \textup{(AR.7)}.
\end{proof}

Put
\[
 L_F=\mathbb E_\mu\Gamma_P(F),
 \qquad
 \gamma_F(x)=\operatorname{vec}_{\R}
 \bigl(\Gamma_P(F)(x)-L_F\bigr),
 \tag{AR.8}
\]
and define
\[
 S_\Gamma c=\langle c,\gamma_F\rangle,
 \qquad
 \boxed{
 M_n^\Gamma=S_\Gamma^*P^nS_\Gamma
 =\mathbb E[\gamma_F(X_n)\gamma_F(X_0)^*],
 \quad n=0,1,2.}
 \tag{AR.9}
\]
Let
\[
 \mathcal E_\Gamma=\Ran M_0^\Gamma,
 \qquad
 J_\Gamma=S_\Gamma(M_0^\Gamma)^{\dagger/2}
 \big|_{\mathcal E_\Gamma},
 \qquad
 \Pi_\Gamma=J_\Gamma J_\Gamma^*.
 \tag{AR.10}
\]

\begin{theorem}[Three-cylinder action-response closure]
\label{thm:GT-three-cylinder-action-response}
The first three stationary action-response cylinders determine the supported
one-step compression
\[
 \boxed{
 A_\Gamma=(M_0^\Gamma)^{\dagger/2}
 M_1^\Gamma(M_0^\Gamma)^{\dagger/2}
 =J_\Gamma^*PJ_\Gamma,
 \qquad 0\preceq A_\Gamma\preceq I,}
 \tag{AR.11}
\]
and the first exact temporal-memory innovation
\[
 \boxed{
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathbb I_\Gamma^{(1)}
 &=(M_0^\Gamma)^{\dagger/2}
 \bigl[M_2^\Gamma
 -M_1^\Gamma(M_0^\Gamma)^\dagger M_1^\Gamma\bigr]
 (M_0^\Gamma)^{\dagger/2}\\
 &=J_\Gamma^*P(I-\Pi_\Gamma)PJ_\Gamma\succeq0.
 \end{aligned}}
 \tag{AR.12}
\]
Moreover,
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathbb I_\Gamma^{(1)}=0
 \iff P\Ran J_\Gamma\subseteq\Ran J_\Gamma
 \iff \Ran J_\Gamma\text{ reduces }P,}
 \tag{AR.13}
\]
and on this branch
\[
 \boxed{J_\Gamma^*P^mJ_\Gamma=A_\Gamma^m\qquad(m\ge0).}
 \tag{AR.14}
\]
The inversion-free block moment Gram satisfies
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathbb B_\Gamma^{(1)}
 =\begin{pmatrix}
 M_0^\Gamma&M_1^\Gamma\\
 M_1^\Gamma&M_2^\Gamma
 \end{pmatrix}\succeq0,
 \qquad
 \rank\mathbb B_\Gamma^{(1)}-\rank M_0^\Gamma
 =\rank\mathbb I_\Gamma^{(1)}.}
 \tag{AR.15}
\]
If the rank increases, the canonical source-minimal missing response writer is
\[
 \boxed{
 J_\Gamma^{\rm new}
 =(I-\Pi_\Gamma)PJ_\Gamma
 (\mathbb I_\Gamma^{(1)})^{\dagger/2},}
 \tag{AR.16}
\]
an isometry on $\supp\mathbb I_\Gamma^{(1)}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The Moore--Penrose range formula makes $J_\Gamma$ an isometry onto
$\overline{\Ran S_\Gamma}$.  Hence \textup{(AR.11)} is its compression of
$P$, and positivity and contractivity follow from $0\preceq P\preceq I$.
Furthermore,
\[
 J_\Gamma^*P^2J_\Gamma
 =(M_0^\Gamma)^{\dagger/2}M_2^\Gamma
  (M_0^\Gamma)^{\dagger/2},
\]
whereas
$J_\Gamma^*P\Pi_\Gamma PJ_\Gamma=A_\Gamma^2$.
Their difference is \textup{(AR.12)}, the Gram of
$(I-\Pi_\Gamma)PJ_\Gamma$.  This proves positivity, the rank formula, and the
first equivalence in \textup{(AR.13)}.  Since $P=P^*$, invariance of the
finite-dimensional range also gives invariance of its orthogonal complement,
so the range reduces $P$.  Iteration gives \textup{(AR.14)}.  The block in
\textup{(AR.15)} is the Gram of $[S_\Gamma,PS_\Gamma]$; subtracting the first
range dimension gives the innovation rank.  Polar normalization of the
orthogonal new range gives \textup{(AR.16)}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Common-action incidence and joint SM--spacetime temporal closure]
\label{cor:SMST-three-cylinder-action-response}
Let $F^{\rm GI}$ be the complete bounded gravity--internal action-response bank
after all declared geometric, internal, nuisance, provenance, and boundary
rows have been assembled and shorted, and let $G_{\rm GI}^{\rm act}$ be the
matrix of the independently reconstructed common action on the same writer
coefficients.  On a positive reflected accepted branch define
\[
 \boxed{
 \Delta_{\Gamma\leftrightarrow\rm act}
 =\bigl\|G_{\rm GI}^{\rm act}
 -(Y_{F^{\rm GI}})^*(I-T)Y_{F^{\rm GI}}\bigr\|_{\rm HS}^2.}
 \tag{AR.17}
\]
If this residual vanishes, the first temporal closure of the joint common-
action carrier is the following exact alternative:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(T\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item $\mathbb I_\Gamma^{(1)}=0$, and the existing joint action-response head
      reduces the accepted transfer and may be iterated exactly;
\item $\mathbb I_\Gamma^{(1)}\ne0$, and
      $J_\Gamma^{\rm new}$ is the unique source-minimal mixed
      gravity--internal writer which must be appended before any continuum or
      marginal claim.
\end{enumerate}
Exact transport of the accepted stationary law, transfer, writer bank, and
physical duration through adjacent cutoffs transports
$M_0^\Gamma,M_1^\Gamma,M_2^\Gamma$, the innovation rank, and the reducing-head
alternative.  Thus, on this branch, temporal common-action completeness is a
finite population problem and does not indicate another internal or spacetime
primitive.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The residual identifies the mean transfer action of
\Cref{thm:GT-reflected-endpoint-action} with the already reconstructed joint
common action.  The alternative is then
\Cref{thm:GT-three-cylinder-action-response}.  Exact cutoff intertwining
conjugates the three moment matrices and therefore preserves their supported
Schur innovation, rank, and polar new range.
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[Scope of the three-cylinder transfer]
\label{fire:GT-three-cylinder-scope}
The compiler requires a physically acquired positive reflected transfer, its
strictly positive stationary vacuum, a complete action-writer bank, and the
incidence residual \textup{(AR.17)}.  It does not derive the accepted kernel
from the static action, force reversibility on a circulating branch, determine

coefficients, trivialize the fermionic determinant/Pfaffian line, or prove

correct decision procedure.
\end{firewall}

\subsubsection{Future-word completion and hypocoercive operation memory}
\label{sec:accepted-future-word-hypocoercive}
% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

The state quotient above is future sufficient for the declared update rows.
A stronger operation quotient is needed when an OS-null direction may return
after physical operations or after no-intervention evolution.  The following
construction performs that completion before any memory short.

Let $\mathsf N:\mathcal E\to\mathcal H_{\rm OS}$ be a finite
no-intervention loading, let $Q$ project onto $\ker\mathsf N$, and let
$\Lambda_1,\ldots,\Lambda_m$ be the primitive operation letters.  When a
calibrated continuous-time claim is made, include its reconstructed generator
$\mathfrak L$ in the mixed word alphabet.  For a word $w$ in this alphabet
put $\mathsf N_w=\mathsf NwQ$ and define
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathbb O_r^{\rm fut}
 =\sum_{1\le |w|\le r}\mathsf N_w^*\mathsf N_w\succeq0.}
 \tag{FC.1}
\]

\begin{theorem}[Finite future-word saturation]
\label{thm:GT-future-word-saturation}
The ranks of $\mathbb O_r^{\rm fut}$ are nondecreasing.  If
\[
 \rank\mathbb O_r^{\rm fut}=\rank\mathbb O_{r+1}^{\rm fut},
\]
then $\ker\mathbb O_r^{\rm fut}$ is invariant under every primitive operation
and under $\mathfrak L$; no later mixed word increases the rank.  The first
flat depth is at most $\dim Q\mathcal E$.  At that depth,
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal K_{\rm seal}=\ker\mathbb O_r^{\rm fut},
 \qquad
 \mathcal M_{\rm ret}=\supp\mathbb O_r^{\rm fut}}
 \tag{FC.2}
\]
are respectively the continuously future-sealed provenance and the
source-minimal returning-memory range.  Only $\mathcal K_{\rm seal}$ may be
quotiented without changing a future operation response.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The kernel is the intersection of the kernels of all displayed return maps.
Rank equality makes that intersection invariant under left extension by every
alphabet letter; induction then gives invariance under every later word.
Finite dimension bounds the number of strict rank increases.  The support is
the orthogonal complement of the final kernel and is minimal by the Gram
quotient universal property.
\end{proof}

Stack a flat labelled family of return maps into
$\mathsf N_{\rm fut}$ and put
$G_{\rm fut}=\mathsf N_{\rm fut}^*\mathsf N_{\rm fut}$.  Let
$H_{\rm fut}=H_{\rm fut}^*\succeq0$ be the reflected returned-cylinder
Hamiltonian and define
\[
 \Delta_{\rm fut}
 =\mathsf N_{\rm fut}\mathfrak L+H_{\rm fut}\mathsf N_{\rm fut}.
 \tag{FC.3}
\]

\begin{theorem}[Future-word OS quotient and returning-memory short]
\label{thm:GT-future-word-OS}
On the exact branch $\Delta_{\rm fut}=0$, whitening by the supported Gram gives
an isometry $U$ and a quotient generator
\[
 \boxed{
 L_{\rm fut}=-U^*H_{\rm fut}U=L_{\rm fut}^*\preceq0.}
 \tag{FC.4}
\]
Moreover
\[
 e^{tL_{\rm fut}}=U^*e^{-tH_{\rm fut}}U.
\]
If the supported quotient is split into the direct visible head
$\mathcal V$ and returned memory $\mathcal M$, write
\[
 -L_{\rm fut}
 =\begin{pmatrix}S_{VV}&C\\C^*&S_{MM}\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Then the exact memory action is
\[
 \boxed{
 S_{\rm mem}=S_{MM}-C^*S_{VV}^{\dagger}C\succeq0,}
 \tag{FC.5}
\]
with
\[
 \langle m,S_{\rm mem}m\rangle
 =\inf_v
 \left\langle\binom vm,-L_{\rm fut}\binom vm\right\rangle.
\]
A null vector returns the dressed soft source
$(-S_{VV}^{\dagger}Cm,m)$.  On the approximate shadow branch,
\[
 \left\|L_{\rm fut}+U^*H_{\rm fut}U\right\|
 \le
 \frac{\|\Delta_{\rm fut}\|}
 {\sqrt{\lambda_{\min}^+(G_{\rm fut})}}.
 \tag{FC.6}
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The flat return Gram identifies the supported quotient.  The intertwining
identity follows by multiplying \textup{(FC.3)} by the Gram whitening maps;
self-adjointness and the semigroup relation follow by compression of
$H_{\rm fut}$.  The memory formula is the Moore--Penrose Schur variational
identity.  The approximate estimate is the same whitening calculation in
operator norm.
\end{proof}

When the future-word OS shadow does not close, reconstruct calibrated forward
and reflected generators on the same supported quotient.  On the
reflection-adjoint branch write
\[
 K=-S+A,
 \qquad S=S^*\succeq0,
 \qquad A^*=-A.
 \tag{FC.7}
\]
A zero instantaneous memory short is not yet an undamped physical mode.

\begin{theorem}[Finite hypocoercive memory alternative]
\label{thm:GT-hypocoercive-memory}
On a $d$-dimensional future-visible quotient define
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathbb O_r^{\rm hyp}
 =\sum_{j=0}^{r}(A^*)^jSA^j.}
 \tag{FC.8}
\]
The ranks stabilize by depth $d-1$, and
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal K_\infty^{\rm hyp}
 =\ker\mathbb O_{d-1}^{\rm hyp}}
 \tag{FC.9}
\]
is the largest $A$-invariant subspace contained in $\ker S$.  The following
are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(H\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item $\mathbb O_{d-1}^{\rm hyp}\succ0$;
\item no nonzero $A$-invariant subspace lies in $\ker S$;
\item every eigenvalue of $K=-S+A$ has negative real part;
\item the sampled loss Gram
      \[
       W_K(T)=\int_0^T e^{tK^*}Se^{tK}\,\dd t
      \]
      is positive definite for every $T>0$;
\item the Lyapunov equation $K^*P+PK=-I$ has a unique $P\succ0$.
\end{enumerate}
In addition,
\[
 \boxed{e^{TK^*}e^{TK}=I-2W_K(T).}
 \tag{FC.10}
\]
Thus full observability gives a strict sampled contraction, whereas the flat
kernel \textup{(FC.9)} is the exact persistent undamped memory that must remain
explicit.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The kernel of \textup{(FC.8)} is
$\bigcap_{j=0}^r\ker(S^{1/2}A^j)$.  Rank stabilization makes it $A$-invariant;
Cayley--Hamilton gives the depth bound.  The spectral and Lyapunov
equivalences are the finite observability--stability theorem.  Differentiating
$e^{tK^*}e^{tK}$ gives
$-2e^{tK^*}Se^{tK}$ and integration gives \textup{(FC.10)}.
\end{proof}


\begin{corollary}[Exact sampled rate and Lyapunov decay]
\label{cor:GT-hypocoercive-decay}
On the full-observability branch of
\Cref{thm:GT-hypocoercive-memory}, put
$\omega_T=\lambda_{\min}(W_K(T))$.  Then
\[
 \boxed{\|e^{TK}\|_{\rm op}^2=1-2\omega_T,\qquad
 g_T^{\rm hyp}=-\frac1{2T}\log(1-2\omega_T)>0.}
 \tag{FC.11}
\]
If $P\succ0$ solves $K^*P+PK=-I$ and
$p_-I\preceq P\preceq p_+I$, then
\[
 \boxed{
 \|e^{tK}\|_{\rm op}
 \le\sqrt{p_+/p_-}\,e^{-t/(2p_+)}.}
 \tag{FC.12}
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The first identity is \textup{(FC.10)}.  Along
$u(t)=e^{tK}u_0$,
$\frac{\dd}{\dd t}\langle u,Pu\rangle=-\|u\|^2$; comparison with the
$P$-metric and Gronwall give \textup{(FC.12)}.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Validated approximate Lyapunov certificate]
\label{thm:GT-approx-Lyapunov}
Let $\widehat P=\widehat P^*\succ0$ satisfy
$\widehat p_-I\preceq\widehat P\preceq\widehat p_+I$ and put
\[
 R_P=K^*\widehat P+\widehat P K+I.
\]
If
\[
 \boxed{\|R_P\|_{\rm op}\le\varepsilon_P<1,}
 \tag{FC.13}
\]
then
\[
 \boxed{
 \|e^{tK}\|_{\widehat P}
 \le
 \exp\!\left[-\frac{1-\varepsilon_P}{2\widehat p_+}t\right].}
 \tag{FC.14}
\]
Hence an interval-certified linear solve gives a rigorous hypocoercive decay
interval without exact diagonalization.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Along the flow,
\[
 \frac{\dd}{\dd t}\langle u,\widehat Pu\rangle
 =-\|u\|^2+\langle u,R_Pu\rangle
 \le-(1-\varepsilon_P)\|u\|^2,
\]
and comparison with the upper $\widehat P$ bound followed by Gronwall gives
the result.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Finite circulation-to-dissipation screen]
\label{thm:GT-circulation-screen}
Let
\[
 W_A(T)=\int_0^T e^{tA^*}Se^{tA}\,\dd t,
 \qquad M=\|S\|_{\rm op}.
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{W_K(T)\succeq W_A(T)-M^2T^2I.}
 \tag{FC.15}
\]
Consequently, if $W_A(T)\succeq\omega_AI$ and
$\eta_T=\omega_A-M^2T^2>0$, then
\[
 \boxed{\|e^{TK}\|_{\rm op}\le\sqrt{1-2\eta_T}<1.}
 \tag{FC.16}
\]
This screen is sufficient but not necessary; failure leaves the exact sampled
loss, observability, and Lyapunov tests available.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Duhamel's formula and dissipativity of $K$ give
$\|e^{tK}-e^{tA}\|\le tM$.  The instantaneous quadratic losses therefore
differ by at most $2tM^2$ on unit vectors.  Integration gives
\textup{(FC.15)}, and \textup{(FC.10)} gives \textup{(FC.16)}.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Cutoff transport of the hypocoercive packet]
\label{thm:GT-hypocoercive-transport}
Suppose an isometry between adjacent cutoffs intertwines the complete
future-visible metric, the symmetric action $S$, and the circulation $A$.
Then it transports exactly
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathbb O_r^{\rm hyp},\qquad
 \mathcal K_\infty^{\rm hyp},\qquad
 W_K(T),\qquad P,}
 \tag{FC.17}
\]
whenever these objects exist.  The first flat observability depth, undamped
dimension, sampled contraction, and Lyapunov rate are therefore cutoff
invariants on the exact transport branch.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Each object is obtained functorially from the transported metric, $S$, and
$A$ by finite sums, products, functional calculus, integration, or the unique
solution of the Lyapunov equation.
\end{proof}

\begin{countertheorem}[A zero symmetric memory floor can coexist with strict decay]
\label{cth:GT-symmetric-null-positive-decay}
Take
\[
 S=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad
 A=\begin{pmatrix}0&-1/2\\1/2&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad K=-S+A.
 \tag{FC.18}
\]
The symmetric short on the second coordinate is zero, but
\[
 \mathbb O_1^{\rm hyp}
 =\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&1/4\end{pmatrix}\succ0,
 \qquad
 \det(\lambda I-K)=(\lambda+1/2)^2.
\]
Thus the complete process is exponentially stable.  Removing the circulation
leaves the same symmetric action and an exact persistent zero mode.
\end{countertheorem}

\begin{assessment}[Corrected returning-memory decision]
\label{assess:GT-corrected-memory}
On a positive reflected branch, the conditional action-response writer and
$M_0^\Gamma,M_1^\Gamma,M_2^\Gamma$ decide first whether the present response
head reduces the transfer; a positive rank increment returns the exact writer
to append.  Once that temporal carrier is complete, the symmetric memory short
is the complete reversible decision.  On a circulating branch, observability
saturation must instead precede promotion.  A full-rank observability Gram
gives hypocoercive decay; a nontrivial flat kernel is the exact persistent
undamped sector; and an independently sourced operation-memory coordinate
remains explicit in either case.  This closes the finite logical ambiguity of
returning memory.  What remains to be populated and transported is the literal
accepted forward/reflected law, the action-incidence row, and the corresponding
three-cylinder or $S/A$ packet, not a new internal or spacetime primitive.
\end{assessment}

\begin{firewall}[Three independent antisymmetric packets]
The command Lie bracket, the beta-form curl of the coefficient shell, and the
