\subsection{Prime-scale restoring shorts, boundary-labelled loading, and finite zero tomography}
\label{sec:GRH-restoring-tomography}
% =============================================================================

The finite lower bridge has a sharper donor-specific form than exact support
fusion.  On the stable old-negative branch, let $P$ be the positive coefficient
carrier, let $A_+\succ0$ on $P\mathcal E$, and write the complete positive birth
source as
\[
 \boxed{
 B=A_++C_{\rm tr}+C_{\partial}+C_{\rm ret},}
 \tag{GRH.7}
\]
where the final three terms are respectively the translated-test excess, the
taper-boundary row, and the stable-return Gram.  Let $h>0$ be the prime-atom
deficit scale.  Since $\supp A_+=P$, an exact support-fusion operator containing
$\supp A_+$ cannot collapse.  The active obstruction is the spectrum of $A_+$
relative to $h$.

\begin{theorem}[Exact low-$A_+$ restoring-short reduction]
\label{thm:GRH-prime-scale-restoring-short}
Fix $\theta>1$ and put
\[
 L_\theta=\one_{[0,\theta h)}(A_+),
 \qquad H_\theta=P-L_\theta,
 \qquad D=C_{\rm tr}+C_{\partial}+C_{\rm ret}.
\]
Let $K=B-hP$.  Then
\[
 \boxed{H_\theta K H_\theta\succeq(\theta-1)hH_\theta.}
 \tag{GRH.8}
\]
Define the exact restoring short
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal R_\theta
 =L_\theta D L_\theta
 -L_\theta D H_\theta
  (H_\theta K H_\theta)^{-1}
  H_\theta D L_\theta\succeq0.}
 \tag{GRH.9}
\]
The Schur complement of the high sector is
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathfrak S_\theta
 =L_\theta(A_+-hP)L_\theta+\mathcal R_\theta,}
 \tag{GRH.10}
\]
and
\[
 \boxed{
 n_-(B-hP)=n_-(\mathfrak S_\theta),
 \qquad
 n_0(B-hP)=n_0(\mathfrak S_\theta).}
 \tag{GRH.11}
\]
Consequently the stable atom creates no new negative direction exactly when
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal R_\theta
 \succeq L_\theta(hP-A_+)L_\theta.}
 \tag{GRH.12}
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
On $H_\theta\mathcal E$, the old-positive form is at least $\theta h$, while
$D\succeq0$, proving \textup{(GRH.8)}.  Block Gaussian elimination of $K$
relative to $L_\theta\oplus H_\theta$ gives the Schur complement
\textup{(GRH.10)} and Haynsworth inertia gives \textup{(GRH.11)}.  Rearranging
positivity of $\mathfrak S_\theta$ gives \textup{(GRH.12)}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[One harmonic witness selects the first failed restoring row]
\label{cor:GRH-restoring-row-selector}
Put
\[
 Q_\theta=-(H_\theta K H_\theta)^{-1}H_\theta DL_\theta,
 \qquad
 \mathcal H_\theta x=x+Q_\theta x.
\]
Then, for $x\in L_\theta\mathcal E$,
\[
 \boxed{
 \begin{aligned}
 \langle x,\mathcal R_\theta x\rangle
 ={}&\langle\mathcal H_\theta x,
       C_{\rm tr}\mathcal H_\theta x\rangle
   +\langle\mathcal H_\theta x,
       C_{\partial}\mathcal H_\theta x\rangle\\
 &+\langle\mathcal H_\theta x,
       C_{\rm ret}\mathcal H_\theta x\rangle
   +\langle Q_\theta x,
       H_\theta(A_+-hP)H_\theta Q_\theta x\rangle.
 \end{aligned}}
 \tag{GRH.13}
\]
If $x$ is a unit negative witness for $\mathfrak S_\theta$ and
\[
 d_\theta(x)=\langle x,L_\theta(hP-A_+)L_\theta x\rangle,
\]
then, for any predeclared positive weights summing to one, at least one of the
four nonnegative rows in \textup{(GRH.13)} is smaller than its assigned share
of $d_\theta(x)$.  The same witness therefore selects a translated-test,
taper-boundary, stable-return, or high-relaxation failure before any deeper
prime or factorization history is opened.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The vector $Q_\theta x$ is the unique high-sector minimizer in the definition
of the short, giving \textup{(GRH.13)}.  A negative Schur value says that the
sum of the four rows is strictly smaller than $d_\theta(x)$; the weighted
pigeonhole conclusion follows.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Buffered rowwise lower bound for the restoring short]
\label{thm:GRH-buffered-restoring-floor}
Let $\mathcal J=\{{\rm tr},\partial,{\rm ret}\}$ and choose
$\alpha_j>0$ with $\sum_{j\in\mathcal J}\alpha_j=1$.  Put
\[
 \gamma_\theta=(\theta-1)h,
 \qquad M_j=\|H_\theta C_jH_\theta\|.
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal R_\theta
 \succeq
 \sum_{j\in\mathcal J}
 \frac{\alpha_j\gamma_\theta}
      {M_j+\alpha_j\gamma_\theta}
 L_\theta C_jL_\theta.}
 \tag{GRH.14}
\]
In particular, high old-positive relaxation may weaken a directly loaded row,
but cannot erase it exactly.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Split the high buffer
$H_\theta(A_+-hP)H_\theta$ among the three rows with weights $\alpha_j$.
For the $j$th positive block, positivity gives
\[
 (H_\theta C_jL_\theta)^*
 (H_\theta C_jH_\theta)^\dagger
 (H_\theta C_jL_\theta)
 \preceq L_\theta C_jL_\theta.
\]
On the supported high range,
\[
 (H_\theta C_jH_\theta+\alpha_j\gamma_\theta H_\theta)^{-1}
 \preceq
 \frac{M_j}{M_j+\alpha_j\gamma_\theta}
 (H_\theta C_jH_\theta)^\dagger.
\]
Thus the $j$th local short is bounded below by the displayed fraction of
$L_\theta C_jL_\theta$.  Summing the local shorts and retaining the positive
router-dispersion term of \Cref{thm:GT-assembly-before-short} proves
\textup{(GRH.14)}.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Sharp-chain central boundary bank]
\label{thm:GRH-sharp-chain-central-bank}
For a translation chain of length $m$, let
\[
 u_j=\sqrt{\frac{2}{m+1}}
      \sin\!\left(\frac{(j+1)\pi}{m+1}\right),
 \qquad 0\le j<m,
\]
and put $b_{m,j}=|u_j|^2$.  For the predeclared central set
\[
 \mathcal J_m=
 \left\{j:\frac{m+1}{4}\le j+1\le\frac{3(m+1)}4\right\},
\]
one has
\[
 \boxed{
 \beta_m:=\sum_{j\in\mathcal J_m}b_{m,j}\ge\frac13.}
 \tag{GRH.15}
\]
Let $V_j:E\to E_j$ be isometries carrying the common multiplicity source to
the first-boundary row $j$, and let $T_j:E_j\to\mathcal Y_j$ be the actual
boundary-labelled arithmetic read.  The central loading Gram is
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathbb A_{\rm cen}
 =\sum_{j\in\mathcal J_m}
  b_{m,j}V_j^*T_j^*T_jV_j\succeq0.}
 \tag{GRH.16}
\]
Its sharp source floor is
\[
 \boxed{
 \kappa_{\rm cen}
 =\frac{\lambda_{\min}(\mathbb A_{\rm cen})}{\beta_m}.}
 \tag{GRH.17}
\]
If an actual source differs in the labelled direct sum by at most $\varepsilon$
from the sharp source of a vector $g\in E$, then its central boundary mass is
at least
\[
 \boxed{
 \left(\sqrt{\beta_m}\,\|g\|-\varepsilon\right)_+^2.}
 \tag{GRH.18}
\]
Thus sharp-chain softness cannot be diluted over arbitrarily many boundary
times.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
On the central half of the sine profile one has
$\sin^2((j+1)\pi/(m+1))\ge1/2$, and the set contains at least
$(m+1)/3$ integer sites; this gives \textup{(GRH.15)}.  Equations
\textup{(GRH.16)--(GRH.17)} are the Gram and minimum-eigenvalue identities.
The reverse triangle inequality for the central direct-sum projection proves
\textup{(GRH.18)}.
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[Boundary-labelled scores require a positive experiment]
If the first-boundary label is erased before the arithmetic row is read, the
coherent Gram contains cross terms
$\sqrt{b_{m,j}b_{m,k}}V_j^*T_j^*T_kV_k$, which may cancel the labelled
diagonal action.  When actual boundary-conditioned neighboring probability
laws are exposed, their Hellinger bank and simultaneous nuisance short
reconstruct $\mathbb A_{\rm cen}$ canonically.  Deterministic signed Weil,
completed, Euler, or gamma values alone do not determine that Fisher metric.
\end{firewall}

\begin{theorem}[Finite-height Hilbert-valued zero tomography]
\label{thm:GRH-finite-zero-tomography}
Let $\mathcal Z_T$ be a finite set of $M$ distinct zero nodes with
$|\Im\rho|\le T$, and let $G\in C_c^\infty(\R;\mathcal H)$ be a physically
loaded finite-dimensional Hilbert-valued profile.  Put
\[
 \Xi_G(s)=\int_{\R}e^{(s-1/2)t}G(t)\,\dd t,
 \qquad
 v_\rho=m(\rho)\Xi_G(\rho),
\]
and assume $v_\rho\ne0$ for every retained node.  Suppose the complete
prime, pole, conductor--gamma, completed-contour, and cutoff-edge rows can be
subtracted for the physical translations
\[
 G_k(t)=G(t-k\tau),
 \qquad 0\le k<2M,
 \qquad 0<\tau<\frac{\pi}{T}.
\]
Then the zero-side outputs have the exact form
\[
 \boxed{
 Y_k=\sum_{\rho\in\mathcal Z_T}
      \zeta_\rho^k v_\rho,
 \qquad
 \zeta_\rho=e^{\tau(\rho-1/2)}.}
 \tag{GRH.19}
\]
The block-Hankel recurrence determined by $Y_0,\ldots,Y_{2M-1}$ has the unique
monic polynomial
\[
 \boxed{Q_T(z)=\prod_{\rho\in\mathcal Z_T}(z-\zeta_\rho).}
 \tag{GRH.20}
\]
Hence every visible finite-height zero is reconstructed and
\[
 \boxed{
 \Re\rho=\frac12\ \text{for all }\rho\in\mathcal Z_T
 \iff |\zeta_\rho|=1\ \text{for every reconstructed node}.}
 \tag{GRH.21}
\]
If $\sigma_{\rm Pr}$ is the least singular value of the block-Hankel recurrence,
$m_{\rm vis}=\min_\rho\|v_\rho\|$, and $V_\zeta$ is the Vandermonde matrix,
then
\[
 \boxed{
 \sigma_{\rm Pr}
 \ge m_{\rm vis}\,\sigma_{\min}(V_\zeta)^2.}
 \tag{GRH.22}
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Translation gives
$\Xi_{G_k}(s)=e^{k\tau(s-1/2)}\Xi_G(s)$, proving \textup{(GRH.19)}.  The
choice of $\tau$ prevents aliasing in the finite height window.  If a
polynomial $p$ of degree below $M$ annihilated the block-Hankel sequence, the
invertible Vandermonde system in the output index would give
$p(\zeta_\rho)v_\rho=0$ for every node.  Visibility then forces
$p(\zeta_\rho)=0$ for all $M$ distinct nodes, a contradiction.  The least
monic recurrence is therefore \textup{(GRH.20)}.  The real-part formula
$\Re\rho=1/2+\tau^{-1}\log|\zeta_\rho|$ gives \textup{(GRH.21)}.  Finally,
the block-Hankel map factors as a left Vandermonde, the diagonal vector-weight
map, and a right Vandermonde transpose; taking least singular values gives
\textup{(GRH.22)}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Finite zero shift and positive Stein test]
\label{cor:GRH-finite-Stein}
On the visible $M$-dimensional recurrence carrier, let $S_T$ be the shift
reconstructed from \textup{(GRH.20)}.  Then
\[
 \boxed{\spec S_T=\{\zeta_\rho:\rho\in\mathcal Z_T\},}
 \tag{GRH.23}
\]
and, because the nodes are distinct,
\[
 \boxed{
 \Re\rho=\frac12\ \text{for every retained zero}
 \iff \exists\,G_T\succ0:\ S_T^*G_TS_T=G_T.}
 \tag{GRH.24}
\]
Every such invariant metric is a positive diagonal weight in the visible zero
eigenframe.  Its condition number is therefore controlled by that eigenframe,
not by critical-line location alone.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The companion shift has characteristic polynomial $Q_T$.  Distinct nodes make
it diagonalizable.  A diagonalizable matrix is similar to a unitary exactly
when all its eigenvalues have modulus one, which is equivalent to the positive
Stein equation.  Conjugating the equation into the eigenbasis shows that the
metric is diagonal there.
\end{proof}

\begin{assessment}[Physical and regulator boundary of the finite tomography]
The logarithmic translation $G(t-k\tau)$ changes the arithmetic centre and the
taper window simultaneously.  It must be an admitted physical row, or arise
from an independently loaded centre--taper scale family.  Normalized finite
differences replace the nodes by
$(e^{\tau(\rho-1/2)}-1)/\tau$ and remove the artificial small-$\tau$ node
compression, but amplify row errors by factors up to $(2/\tau)^k$.  The
finite-height reconstruction is therefore exact; the unresolved GRH inputs
are the physical dilation or scale-jet port, cutoff-uniform Mellin visibility,
Vandermonde/eigenframe conditioning, complete row subtraction, and the
independent restoring lower bridge.
\end{assessment}

\subsection{Finite Weil inertia and source-resolved first-return coherence}
\label{sec:GRH-Weil-inertia-return}
% =============================================================================

A finite compression of Weil's Hermitian form supplies an upstream signed
certificate which is complementary to, rather than a replacement for, the
completed--Euler and first-return programmes.

\begin{theorem}[Typed finite Weil rank--trace certificate]
\label{thm:GRH-Weil-inertia}
Let a normalized finite test family give
\[
 \widetilde G=P+Q+E,
\]
where $P\succeq0$ is the sum of the critical-line zero columns,
$\rank P\le s$, $Q$ is the pullback of $p$ functional-equation hyperbolic
blocks of signature $(1,1)$, and $E$ is an exterior-window tail.  Then
$n_+(Q)\le p$, and, after replacing $\widetilde G$ by
$G=P+Q$ with a trace-norm tail allowance, \Cref{thm:GT-rank-trace-indefinite}
gives
\[
 \boxed{s\ge2\Tr P+4\Tr Q-4p-\|G\|_{\rm F}^2.}
 \tag{GRH.1}
\]
If, in the atom normalization,
\[
 \Tr G=N+o(N),
 \qquad
 \|G\|_{\rm F}^2
 =\left(\frac1\lambda+\frac\lambda3\right)N+o(N),
\]
then
\[
 \boxed{
 N_0^*(T,2T)
 \ge\left(2-\frac1\lambda-\frac\lambda3-o(1)\right)N(T,2T).}
 \tag{GRH.2}
\]
The same finite linear-algebra statement applies to a fixed primitive
Dirichlet character once its explicit-formula packet and functional-equation
pairing are loaded.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Each off-line functional-equation pair is a hyperbolic form; pullback does not
increase positive index.  Apply \Cref{thm:GT-rank-trace-indefinite} and then
the displayed prime-side moment asymptotics.  Tail perturbations are handled
by trace-norm and Weyl bounds.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Parallel population and causal-signed certificates]
\label{thm:GRH-parallel-signed-certificate}
Let $N_\omega$ be the source-resolved countercoherent profile of the same
functional-equation pair histories, let $\mathbb K_{{\rm pair},R}$ be their
complete cross-record kernel, and let $\mathcal P_R$ be the actual first-return
record.  Then the pair source obeys the exact decomposition
\[
 \boxed{
 N^*N
 =\mathbb I_{{\rm pair}\mid R}
 +G_{\rm dem}^{\rm pair}
 +G_{\rm open}^{\rm pair}
 +G_{\rm cyc}^{\rm pair},}
 \tag{GRH.3}
\]
with $\mathbb I_{{\rm pair}\mid R}$ given by the conditional variance formula
\textup{(SK.3)}.  The finite Weil theorem gives a population lower bound; the
first-return packet controls source-resolved phase loss, demand, open current,
and cycle holonomy.  Neither theorem constructs a canonical spectral
complement to be passed to the other.  Their physical handoff is the common
pair label and its complete mixed kernel.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Apply \Cref{thm:GT-source-record-variance} to the pair-history source and then
\Cref{thm:GT-source-word-Hodge} at the first-return grade.  The population
statement depends only on the typed compression and moments and hence remains
parallel.
\end{proof}


\begin{theorem}[Scale-matched soft source and nonduplicating singular-event ledger]
\label{thm:GRH-soft-source-ledger}
Let $A,H$ be Hermitian on a finite physical source space, let $a>0$, and put
\[
 G_s=A+sH,
 \qquad
 \mathbb Q_{a,s}=a^2(G_s^2+a^2I)^{-1},
 \qquad 0\le s\le1.
\]
If $\|H\|\le ca$ and $G_{s_*}$ is singular for some $s_*\in[0,1]$, then
\[
 \boxed{
 \int_0^1\Tr\mathbb Q_{a,s}\,\dd s
 \ge\frac{\arctan c}{c}.}
 \tag{GRH.4}
\]
The bound is independent of the old spectral floor and the matrix dimension.

For a chronological family of such atomic insertions, define
\[
 \overline Q_j=\int_0^1\mathbb Q_{a_j,s}^{(j)}\,\dd s
 =\mathcal S_j^*\mathcal S_j
\]
after transporting all events to one same-history source metric.  The new
soft-source mass of event $j$ is the Schur innovation
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathbb I_j^{\rm soft}
 =G_{jj}^{\rm soft}
  -G_{j,<j}^{\rm soft}(G_{<j,<j}^{\rm soft})^\dagger
   G_{<j,j}^{\rm soft}\succeq0.}
 \tag{GRH.5}
\]
Thus
\[
 \boxed{
 \Tr\overline Q_j
 =\|P_{<j}^{\rm soft}\mathcal S_j\|_{\rm HS}^2
  +\Tr\mathbb I_j^{\rm soft}.}
 \tag{GRH.6}
\]
If the loaded translation/boundary heads form a nested terminal family, the
fresh soft source further decomposes, by
\Cref{thm:GT-source-terminal-nonduplication}, into old-head loading, dynamic
head promotion, irreducible boundary response, and response nullity.  Only the
irreducible fresh response has a new Thomson action.  Hence the eventwise lower
bound \textup{(GRH.4)} becomes a cofinal finite-stock charge only after source
reuse, boundary-head promotion, and response-null branches have been closed or
independently budgeted.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Choose an ordered eigenvalue $\lambda(s)$ with $\lambda(s_*)=0$.  Weyl's
inequality gives
$|\lambda(s)|\le ca|s-s_*|$, so the corresponding eigenvalue of
$\mathbb Q_{a,s}$ is at least
$(1+c^2(s-s_*)^2)^{-1}$.  Its integral is minimized when $s_*$ is an endpoint
and equals $c^{-1}\arctan c$, proving \textup{(GRH.4)}.  Equations
\textup{(GRH.5)}--\textup{(GRH.6)} are the source projection Pythagoras, and
the terminal statement is \Cref{thm:GT-source-terminal-nonduplication}.
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[No canonical ``remaining third'']
\label{fire:GRH-no-residual-third}
A lower-bound certificate does not identify the uncertified zeros with an
off-line eigenspace.  The rank--trace slack may arise entirely from
nonorthogonality of the positive evaluation frame.  The first-return compiler
must therefore act on the actual source-tagged pair histories, not on an
adverse eigenspace selected after the population estimate.
\end{firewall}

\subsection{Integrated hard-edge packets, zero modes, and the arithmetic router}
\label{sec:GRH-integrated-zero-mode}

The completed--Euler comparison above is one source-metric formulation of the
upper bridge.  A complementary hard-edge formulation arises when the total
and phase sources are first assembled over the accepted energy region.  The
order of operations is load bearing: resolving each atomic energy and shorting
there can remove the cross-energy orientation responsible for cancellation.

\begin{theorem}[Integrated-box router and zero-mode reduction]
\label{thm:GRH-integrated-zero-mode}
Let a finite accepted energy partition have complete total--phase Grams
\[
 G_{j,X}=\begin{pmatrix}A_{j,X}&B_{j,X}\\
 \overline{B_{j,X}}&A_{j,X}\end{pmatrix}\succeq0,
 \qquad A_{j,X}>0.
\]
Set
\[
 A_X=\sum_jA_{j,X},
 \qquad B_X=\sum_jB_{j,X},
 \qquad K_X=B_X/A_X,
\]
\[
 D_X^{\rm pred}=\frac{|B_X|^2}{A_X},
 \qquad
 \kappa_X=A_X-D_X^{\rm pred}.
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{
 \sum_j\frac{|B_{j,X}|^2}{A_{j,X}}
 -\frac{|B_X|^2}{A_X}
 =\sum_jA_{j,X}\left|\frac{B_{j,X}}{A_{j,X}}-K_X\right|^2\ge0.}
\]
Thus the short of the assembled complete Gram is not the sum of the
pointwise shorts.

Suppose additionally that the assembled packet is represented on a physical
Hilbert carrier by a contraction $T_X$, an accepted total source
$A_X^{\rm src}$ with $T_X^*A_X^{\rm src}=A_X^{\rm src}$, and a phase source
$Z_X$.  Let $P_{0,X}$ project onto $\Ker(I-T_X)$.  Then the predictable mixed
energy is bounded by
\[
 \boxed{
 D_X^{\rm pred}
 \le\left\|Z_X^*P_{0,X}Z_X\right\|}
\]
after the common source normalization.  In particular, any regulator estimate
\[
 \left\|Z_X^*P_{0,X}Z_X\right\|=X^{o(1)}
\]
forces a subpower predictable-stiffness deficit.  When the arithmetic loading
identifies $B_X$ with the normalized completed Euler endpoint and
$A_X=X^{1+o(1)}$, this gives the square-root-scale upper estimate required by
the corresponding hard-edge GRH bridge.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The first identity is the scalar specialization of
\Cref{thm:GT-assembly-before-short}.  For the second statement,
\Cref{thm:GT-fixed-coboundary} shows that a fixed accepted source couples only
to $P_{0,X}Z_X$ and that its normalized prediction Gram is dominated by
$Z_X^*P_{0,X}Z_X$.  The final implication is the stated arithmetic
normalization.
\end{proof}

\begin{countertheorem}[Atomic shorting can destroy the hard-edge orientation]
\label{cth:GRH-atomic-short}
There are two energy atoms for which the protected short at each atom is zero
while the short of the assembled complete Gram is strictly positive.
\end{countertheorem}

\begin{proof}
Take total and phase columns $(1,1)^\mathsf T$ and $(1,-1)^\mathsf T$.  At
each atom the two columns are proportional, so the local protected short is
zero.  The sum of the two complete Grams is $2I_2$, whose protected short is
two.
\end{proof}

\begin{assessment}[Two admissible GRH upper-bridge routes]
The relative completed--Euler metric route and the integrated hard-router
route are complementary.  The first seeks a cutoff-uniform source metric
comparison.  The second seeks a small fixed component, an exact coboundary, or
an upstream Ward symmetry for the assembled phase source.  Neither route is
closed by pointwise positivity, a finite gap, source inclusion, or a
post-terminal permutation of already counted phase fibres.
\end{assessment}

\begin{assessment}[Predictive--action and cofinal GRH handoff]
The completed--Euler and hard-edge packets must be organized on one
source-native rectangular atlas.  Future-signature or Hankel depth forms one
axis; accepted/action, occurrence, provenance, gamma, and completed--Euler
context form the other.  The mixed corner and interchange secant of
\Cref{thm:GT-rectangular-interchange} must be assembled before a positive
arithmetic birth is assigned, and the reveal grade must be fixed by the actual
prime, divisor, or bandwidth chronology.  On a nonflat branch the contextual
memory is first removed by
\Cref{thm:GT-contextual-renewal-associativity}; only the genuine arithmetic
complement enters the marked first-return transform of
\Cref{thm:GT-positive-first-return-renewal}.  A bounded or subpower head is
therefore a localization theorem, not the final descent.  Cofinal exclusion
still requires a same-history accepted/action or open-boundary balance whose
paid first-passage margins satisfy
\Cref{thm:GT-source-anchored-cofinal-descent}.  Failure returns a remote future
row, a mixed completed--Euler context, a long collision excursion, an unpaid
first exit, or a sparse cofinal arithmetic source.
\end{assessment}

\section{Affine-linear prime systems: local factors and connected tensor grades}
\label{sec:affine-prime-interface}
% =============================================================================

Ordinary linear Diophantine equations over $\Z$ are decided by Smith normal
form.  The open prime-valued problem begins only after affine coordinates are
required to lie in the primes.  The relevant Grand-Tensor object is therefore
not another integer-lattice solver but the all-support tensor correlation of
the von Mangoldt source after the complete local and proper-subset models have
been shorted.

\begin{definition}[Affine prime packet]
\label{def:GT-affine-prime-packet}
Let
\[
 \Psi=(\psi_1,\ldots,\psi_t),
 \qquad
 \psi_i(n)=\dot\psi_i(n)+b_i
\]
be nonconstant affine-linear forms $\Z^d\to\Z$, and let $K\subset\R^d$ be a
bounded convex body with boundary of measure zero.  Put
\[
 \mathcal P_{\Psi,K}(N)
 :=\sum_{n\in NK\cap\Z^d}\prod_{i=1}^t\Lambda(\psi_i(n)).
\]
For a prime $p$, define
\[
 \Lambda_p(a)=\frac p{p-1}\one_{a\not\equiv0\pmod p},
\]
\[
 \boxed{
 \beta_p(\Psi)
 :=\mathbb E_{n\in(\Z/p\Z)^d}
 \prod_{i=1}^t\Lambda_p(\psi_i(n)).}
\]
The packet is locally admissible when $\beta_p(\Psi)>0$ for every $p$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Exact local obstruction and Chinese-remainder assembly]
\label{thm:GT-affine-local-factors}
For every prime $p$,
\[
 \boxed{
 \beta_p(\Psi)>0
 \iff
 \exists n\in(\Z/p\Z)^d\text{ such that }
 p\nmid\prod_i\psi_i(n).}
\]
For squarefree $q$, the corresponding local density satisfies
\[
 \boxed{\beta_q(\Psi)=\prod_{p\mid q}\beta_p(\Psi).}
\]
Thus the finite singular product is an exact tensor product of local
zero-frequency densities.  Its infinite convergence and nonvanishing remain a
separate regulator certificate.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Every summand defining $\beta_p$ is nonnegative and is positive exactly when
none of the forms vanishes modulo $p$.  The Chinese remainder theorem
identifies $(\Z/q\Z)^d$ with the product of its prime-modulus factors, and
Fubini factorizes the uniform average.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Affine Fourier relation and the common source hierarchy]
\label{thm:GT-affine-Fourier}
Let $G$ be a finite abelian group, let $\widehat G$ be its character group, and
let $\psi_i(x)=L_ix+b_i$ be affine maps $G^d\to G$.  Define the dual relation
lattice
\[
 \mathcal R_\Psi
 :=\left\{(\chi_1,\ldots,\chi_t)\in\widehat G^t:
 \prod_i\chi_i(L_ix)=1\text{ for every }x\in G^d\right\}.
\]
For arbitrary functions $f_i:G\to\C$,
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathbb E_{x\in G^d}\prod_{i=1}^tf_i(\psi_i(x))
 =\frac1{|G|^t}
 \sum_{(\chi_i)\in\mathcal R_\Psi}
 \prod_{i=1}^t\widehat f_i(\chi_i)\chi_i(b_i).}
\]
Consequently degree-one Dirichlet-character sums and higher affine-prime
correlations are transforms of one von Mangoldt source, but they occupy
different tensor grades.  In particular a nontrivial character $\chi$ is
noninvariant at degree one while
$H_\chi\otimes H_{\overline\chi}$ lies in the neutral degree-two sector.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Insert Fourier inversion into every factor.  Averaging the product of the
characters over $G^d$ gives one exactly on $\mathcal R_\Psi$ and zero off it.
The final statement is the character-neutralization formula in
\Cref{thm:GT-positive-unitary-tensor-dichotomy}.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Conditional connected-uniformity bridge for affine primes]
\label{thm:GT-affine-connected-bridge}
At cutoff $N$, suppose the canonical arithmetic loading and its complete local
model give an orthogonal one-source decomposition
\[
 \lambda_N=\nu_N+r_N,
\]
where $\nu_N$ contains the constant, congruence, and local-factor source and
$r_N$ is the efficient residual.  For a degree-$t$ affine packet, perform:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(A\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item the simultaneous short by every proper-support tensor grade;
\item the source-fusion and occurrence audit of
      \Cref{thm:GT-source-fusion,thm:GT-complete-connected-sector};
\item the occurrence Feshbach reduction of
      \Cref{thm:GT-occurrence-Feshbach}.
\end{enumerate}
Let $Z_{\Psi,N}^{\rm eff}$ be the resulting all-support source, let
$L_{\Psi,N}^{\rm eff}\succeq0$ be the independently reconstructed effective
action, and let $P_{\Psi,N}^{\rm fix}$ project onto its kernel.  If the affine
relation source $A_{\Psi,N}$ is fixed by this action, if
\[
 \|A_{\Psi,N}\|^2=O_\Psi(N^d),
\]
\[
 \boxed{
 \left\|(Z_{\Psi,N}^{\rm eff})^*
 P_{\Psi,N}^{\rm fix}Z_{\Psi,N}^{\rm eff}\right\|
 =o_\Psi(N^d),}
\]
and if the singular product converges to a nonzero limit, then
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal P_{\Psi,K}(N)
 =N^d\operatorname{vol}(K)\prod_p\beta_p(\Psi)
 +o_\Psi(N^d).}
\]
The same conclusion holds simultaneously for every finite bank loaded into one
common effective action.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Expanding $(\nu_N+r_N)^{\otimes t}$ separates the local model from the
proper-subset and all-residual terms.  The first short removes every term
supported on a proper subset of slots.  Fusion and occurrence reduction replace
the remaining raw source by $Z_{\Psi,N}^{\rm eff}$.  Since the relation source
is fixed, \Cref{thm:GT-fixed-coboundary} bounds the squared connected correction
by
\[
 \|A_{\Psi,N}\|^2
 \left\|(Z_{\Psi,N}^{\rm eff})^*
 P_{\Psi,N}^{\rm fix}Z_{\Psi,N}^{\rm eff}\right\|
 =o_\Psi(N^{2d}).
\]
Hence the connected correction is $o_\Psi(N^d)$.  The surviving local term is
the finite singular product, and the assumed regulator convergence gives the
stated main term.
\end{proof}


\begin{theorem}[Neutral pair--switching incidence compiler]
\label{thm:affine-switching-incidence}
Let $N_{\rm par}$ be the complete source-resolved neutral pair synthesis before
the final parity short, and let $S_{\rm sw}$ be the actual divisor, Vaughan,
or switching-history synthesis.  With
$P_{\rm sw}=S_{\rm sw}(S_{\rm sw}^*S_{\rm sw})^\dagger S_{\rm sw}^*$, put
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathbb I_{{\rm par}\mid{\rm sw}}
 =N_{\rm par}^*(I-P_{\rm sw})N_{\rm par}\succeq0.}
 \tag{AFF.1}
\]
Its rank is the minimum missing switching or occurrence source dimension.
Only on the zero-innovation branch may the characteristic switching
connection or Hodge action be used to control the complete neutral pair
source.  After compression to one final parity line, every positive quadratic
action is a scalar multiple of the squared endpoint and supplies no new
parity mechanism.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The first statement is the source-incidence Schur Pythagoras.  On a
one-dimensional quotient every positive form is proportional to the unique
squared coordinate, proving endpoint equivalence.
\end{proof}


\begin{theorem}[Two-sided radical--Euler reflection and canonical parity holonomy]
\label{thm:affine-radical-reflection}
For $m>1$ put
\[
 r(m)=\prod_{p\mid m}p,
 \qquad
 \chi_{\rm rad}(m)=\mu(r(m))=(-1)^{\omega(m)},
\]
and define
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathscr E_m(z)=\frac1z\prod_{p\mid m}(1-p^{-z}).}
 \tag{AFF.2}
\]
The singularity at $z=0$ is removable.  If $k=\omega(m)$, then
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathscr E_m(z)
 =z^{k-1}\prod_{p\mid m}\log p
  \left(1-\frac z2\log r(m)+O_m(z^2)\right).}
 \tag{AFF.3}
\]
For $t>0$ one has the exact reflection law
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathscr E_m(-t)
 =-\chi_{\rm rad}(m)r(m)^t\mathscr E_m(t).}
 \tag{AFF.4}
\]
After balancing the positive radical scale,
\[
 u_t(m)=r(m)^{t/2}\mathscr E_m(t),
 \qquad
 v_t(m)=r(m)^{-t/2}\mathscr E_m(-t),
\]
so that
\[
 \boxed{v_t(m)=-\chi_{\rm rad}(m)u_t(m).}
 \tag{AFF.5}
\]
On a finite same-history affine-pair carrier, let $U_t$ and $V_t$ denote
multiplication by $u_t(L_2(\omega))$ and $v_t(L_2(\omega))$, respectively.
The reflected branches define the canonical self-adjoint unitary involution
\[
 [J_{\rm rad}f](\omega)
 =-\chi_{\rm rad}(L_2(\omega))f(\omega).
\]
The Hermitian reflection pencil
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathbb G_t(\theta)=
 \begin{pmatrix}
 U_t^2&\theta U_tJ_{\rm rad}U_t\\
 \theta U_tJ_{\rm rad}U_t&U_t^2
 \end{pmatrix}}
 \tag{AFF.6}
\]
is positive exactly for $|\theta|\le1$.  At $\theta=1$ its kernel is
\[
 \left\{(U_t^{-1}x,-U_t^{-1}J_{\rm rad}x):x\in\mathscr H_{\rm aff}\right\},
\]
and the crossing form equals $-2\|x\|^2$ on the corresponding kernel vector.
Thus radical parity is a source-fixed reflection orientation, not a sign fitted
from the terminal prime-pair answer.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Expand each factor $1-e^{-z\log p}$ at zero to obtain \textup{(AFF.3)}.  The
identity $1-p^t=-p^t(1-p^{-t})$ gives \textup{(AFF.4)} and hence
\textup{(AFF.5)}.  Congruence of \textup{(AFF.6)} by
$\operatorname{diag}(U_t,U_t)$ reduces it to
$\begin{psmallmatrix}I&\theta J_{\rm rad}\\
\theta J_{\rm rad}&I\end{psmallmatrix}$, whose eigenvalues on the
$\pm1$ parity sectors are $1\pm\theta$.  The kernel and crossing form follow
directly.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Flat parameter transport and the boundary soft-loading obstruction]
\label{thm:affine-reflected-soft-loading}
For $s,t>0$, the positive transport
\[
 D_{s\leftarrow t}=U_sU_t^{-1}
\]
is invertible, satisfies the exact cocycle law, and commutes with
$J_{\rm rad}$.  Hence every positive parameter value uses the same radical
parity source; a dyadic radical--Euler current is old-source magnitude
transport, not a sequence of fresh parity births.

Let $\mathcal A_D^{\rm rad}$ denote the complementary-divisor boundary
amplitude on the completed affine-pair carrier, put
$s_\Lambda(\omega)=\Lambda(L_1(\omega))$, and let $Q_{\mathcal N}$ be the
orthogonal complement of the simultaneously shorted nuisance/provenance
range.  Define
\[
 a_D(\omega)=\sigma_K(j(\omega))
 \mathcal A_D^{\rm rad}(L_2(\omega)),
\]
and let $M_{\chi_{\rm rad}a_D}$ denote multiplication by the displayed
signed boundary writer.  Define
\[
 [B_{D,t}f](\omega)
 =\frac{a_D(\omega)}{u_t(L_2(\omega))}f(\omega).
\]
Then the actual radical-parity writer factors exactly as
\[
 \boxed{
 M_{\chi_{\rm rad}a_D}=-B_{D,t}V_t.}
 \tag{AFF.7}
\]
After simultaneous nuisance shorting by $Q_{\mathcal N}$, its protected mixed
coefficient is
\[
 \boxed{
 C_{\rm aff}^{\rm rad}
 =-\left\langle
 Q_{\mathcal N}s_\Lambda,
 Q_{\mathcal N}B_{D,t}v_t
 \right\rangle.}
 \tag{AFF.8}
\]
The response $L_{D,t}=-Q_{\mathcal N}B_{D,t}$ has the source-minimal action
\[
 \boxed{
 d_{D,t}^{\rm ref}
 =\left\langle y_{D,t},
 (L_{D,t}L_{D,t}^*)^\dagger y_{D,t}\right\rangle
 =\min_{L_{D,t}h=y_{D,t}}\|h\|^2,}
 \tag{AFF.9}
\]
where $y_{D,t}=L_{D,t}v_t$; the orthogonal complement is the response-null
reflected history.

If $k=\omega(m)$ and $L(m)=\prod_{p\mid m}\log p$, then
\[
 \boxed{
 t^{k-1}L(m)r(m)^{-t/2}
 \le u_t(m)\le
 t^{k-1}L(m)r(m)^{t/2}.}
 \tag{AFF.10}
\]
Therefore the boundary loading has scale $t^{1-k}$ at factor depth $k$.
Prime-power depth is finite, semiprime depth is the first $t^{-1}$ soft layer,
and no regulator-uniform ambient response bound follows from positivity of the
one-sided source.  The remaining affine theorem is a source-specific estimate
for the boundary-loaded reflected correlation \textup{(AFF.8)}, not discovery
of a missing parity sign.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The transport statements follow pointwise from the positive ratio $u_s/u_t$.
Equation~\textup{(AFF.7)} is the identity
$-(a_D/u_t)v_t=a_D\chi_{\rm rad}$; projection gives
\textup{(AFF.8)}.  The Moore--Penrose minimum theorem gives
\textup{(AFF.9)}.  Finally, $xe^{-x}\le1-e^{-x}\le x$ applied to
$x=t\log p$ and multiplied over $p\mid m$ gives \textup{(AFF.10)} and its
soft-loading consequence.
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[Reflection identifies orientation but does not prove cancellation]
\label{fire:affine-reflection-not-estimate}
The reflection pencil reconstructs radical parity and the positive parameter
cocycle proves source reuse.  Neither result bounds the signed pairing with the
first-endpoint von Mangoldt source.  A further positive Gram, a fourth-moment
majorant, or the source-minimal action in \textup{(AFF.9)} cannot replace the
regulator-uniform estimate of the mixed coefficient \textup{(AFF.8)}.
\end{firewall}

\begin{firewall}[Degree-one GRH cancellation does not close neutral prime pairs]
\label{fire:GT-GRH-not-affine}
A degree-one Ward identity may annihilate every nontrivial character source
while leaving the product-one sector
$H_\chi\otimes H_{\overline\chi}$ untouched.  Twin-prime and binary-Goldbach
channels lie in such neutral quadratic sectors and may also carry a
nonmonoidal occurrence innovation.  Their closure therefore requires an
actual degree-two source fusion, proper-subset short, occurrence reduction, and
connected-uniformity estimate; it does not follow from GRH or from local
admissibility alone.
\end{firewall}


\section{Yang--Mills: transfer gaps and zero-free half-planes}
\label{sec:YM-interface}
% =============================================================================


\subsection{Common colour-law landing from the active Standard Model}
\label{sec:SMYM-common-colour-law}
% -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

The active Standard-Model carrier already contains the colour configuration
space and local gauge action.  The remaining issue is not algebraic admission
of $SU(3)$, but population of one physical full-coupling slab law and its
colour response on the same relational cylinder.

\begin{definition}[Colour-vacuum embedding]
\label{def:SMYM-colour-vacuum}
Fix a unit Higgs vacuum vector $h_0\in W_2$.  On a finite spacetime cutoff,
define
\[
 \boxed{
 \iota_{3,X}(U^{(3)})
 =\bigl(U_e=(U_e^{(3)},I_2),\ H_v=v_Hh_0,
 \ \Psi_v=\overline\Psi_v=0\bigr),}
 \tag{CY.1}
\]
for $U^{(3)}\in SU(3)^{E_X}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Exact colour-vacuum restriction of the active action]
\label{thm:SMYM-colour-restriction}
On the principal logarithm chart of
\Cref{thm:SM-active-SM-II},
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathscr S_{{\rm SM},X}^{E}\circ\iota_{3,X}
 =\frac12\langle F_X^{(3)},\star_{2,X}F_X^{(3)}\rangle_{g_3}.}
 \tag{CY.2}
\]
The right-hand side is a local gauge-invariant $SU(3)$ lattice action on the
same emerged spacetime regulator.  Its colour Ward identity is the restriction
of the Standard-Model Ward identity, and it inherits the existing Hodge and
compact screens.  No new gauge group, plaquette grammar, spatial carrier, or
Hodge operator is required.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The embedding lies in $S(U(3)\times U(2))$.  The Higgs carrier is colour
trivial and the weak link is the identity, so $D_UH=0$; the Higgs potential
vanishes at its vacuum; and the fermion bilinear vanishes.  Orthogonality of
the invariant gauge metric leaves exactly the $\mathfrak{su}(3)$ plaquette
term.  Gauge covariance and the fixed finite internal rank give the remaining
claims.
\end{proof}

\begin{countertheorem}[A static action and Gibbs state do not select a slab law]
\label{cth:SMYM-action-no-law}
For $0<a<1/2$, the matrices
\[
 P_a=\begin{pmatrix}1-a&a\\a&1-a\end{pmatrix}
 \tag{CY.3}
\]
are positive self-adjoint Markov contractions with the same stationary law
$(1/2,1/2)$ and the same static free action.  Their fixed-free eigenvalues are
$1-2a$, and hence their rates at duration $\tau$ are
$-\tau^{-1}\log(1-2a)$.  Thus a classical action, faithful Gibbs state,
reversibility, and positivity do not determine the physical transfer or its
clock.
\end{countertheorem}

\begin{theorem}[Full-to-colour Pythagoras and the first coupled-memory row]
\label{thm:SMYM-colour-law-Pythagoras}
Let $0\preceq P\preceq I$ be a physical self-adjoint full-coupling slab, let
$J:\mathcal H_3\to\mathcal H_{\rm SM}$ be the colour-vacuum source isometry,
and let $Q$ be a proposed colour slab.  Put
\[
 M_1=J^*PJ,\qquad M_2=J^*P^2J,\qquad C=M_1-Q,
\]
\[
 L=(I-JJ^*)PJ,\qquad
 \mathbb V=L^*L=M_2-M_1^2\succeq0.
 \tag{CY.4}
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{PJ-JQ=L+JC,\qquad
 (PJ-JQ)^*(PJ-JQ)=\mathbb V+C^*C.}
 \tag{CY.5}
\]
Consequently
\[
 \boxed{PJ=JQ\iff C=0\ \text{and}\ \mathbb V=0.}
 \tag{CY.6}
\]
One-step compression agreement $C=0$ is therefore insufficient.  The
lag-two row $M_2$ is the exact first witness of coupled Standard-Model memory,
and a positive $\mathbb V$ appends its source-minimal polar response bank.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Decompose $PJ-JQ$ orthogonally into the complement of $\Ran J$ and
$\Ran J$.  The first component is $L$ and the second is $JC$.  Taking the
Gram gives \textup{(CY.5)}.  Moreover
$L^*L=J^*P(I-JJ^*)PJ=M_2-M_1^2$.
\end{proof}

Let $\mathcal Z_\Gamma=\{z_1,\ldots,z_m\}$ be the finite response-signature
image of the frozen colour/Hankel--moment writer, realified when necessary.
Fix $z_\star\in\mathcal Z_\Gamma$ and put
\[
 V_\Gamma=\Span_\R\{z-z_\star:z\in\mathcal Z_\Gamma\},
 \qquad d_\Gamma=\dim V_\Gamma.
 \tag{CY.7}
\]
For a point-readable source record $L=\ell$ of probability $\mu_\ell$ and a
faithful response row $q_\ell$, write
\[
 \theta_\ell=\sum_iq_\ell(i)(z_i-z_\star),
 \qquad t_\ell=z_\star+\theta_\ell.
 \tag{CY.8}
\]

\begin{definition}[Physical affine response frame]
\label{def:SMYM-affine-frame}
For executable contrasts $a_1,\ldots,a_r\in V_\Gamma$ and setting metric
$Q_a=\diag(q_1,\ldots,q_r)\succ0$, define
\[
 (A_\Gamma v)_\alpha=\langle a_\alpha,v\rangle,
 \qquad F_\Gamma=A_\Gamma^*Q_aA_\Gamma,
\]
and the source-labelled moments
\[
 \boxed{
 b_{\ell,\alpha}
 =\mathbb E\!\left[
 \one_{\{L=\ell\}}\langle a_\alpha,Z-z_\star\rangle\right]
 =\mu_\ell(A_\Gamma\theta_\ell)_\alpha.}
 \tag{CY.9}
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Sharp affine acquisition and selector-fibre boundary]
\label{thm:SMYM-affine-minimality}
The panel \textup{(CY.9)} reconstructs every conditional response mean exactly
when
\[
 \boxed{F_\Gamma\succ0\quad\text{on }V_\Gamma,}
 \tag{CY.10}
\]
in which case
\[
 \boxed{
 \theta_\ell
 =F_\Gamma^{-1}A_\Gamma^*Q_a\,b_\ell/\mu_\ell.}
 \tag{CY.11}
\]
The sharp unrestricted linear acquisition dimension is
$d_\Gamma=\dim\operatorname{aff}(\mathcal Z_\Gamma)$.

For $t$ in the relative interior of
$\operatorname{conv}(\mathcal Z_\Gamma)$, the faithful selector fibre
\[
 \mathcal Q_\Gamma(t)
 =\{q\in\R_{>0}^m:\one^*q=1,\ \sum_iq_iz_i=t\}
 \tag{CY.12}
\]
has affine dimension
\[
 \boxed{m-d_\Gamma-1.}
 \tag{CY.13}
\]
It is a singleton exactly when the response atoms are affinely independent,
equivalently when their convex hull is the simplex with those vertices.  Thus
the affine mean determines the complete selector only on the simplicial
branch.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Condition \textup{(CY.10)} is injectivity of $A_\Gamma$ on the affine tangent
space and gives the weighted left inverse \textup{(CY.11)}.  Any linear panel
of smaller rank has a nonzero null direction in $V_\Gamma$; small positive
perturbations of a faithful selector along a coefficient preimage of that
direction give distinct means with identical acquired data.  Conversely a
basis of $V_\Gamma$ suffices.  The augmented map
$q\mapsto(\one^*q,\sum_iq_i(z_i-z_\star))$ has rank $d_\Gamma+1$, proving
\textup{(CY.13)} and the simplex criterion.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Reference-relative affine exponential family]
\label{def:SMYM-affine-exponential-family}
Let $g=(g_i)_{i=1}^m$ be a faithful independently physical reference row and
put $x_i=z_i-z_\star\in V_\Gamma$.  Define
\[
 \boxed{
 \Psi_g(\lambda)=\log\sum_{i=1}^m g_i e^{\langle\lambda,x_i\rangle},
 \qquad
 q_{g,\lambda}(i)
 =g_i e^{\langle\lambda,x_i\rangle-\Psi_g(\lambda)}.}
 \tag{CY.13a}
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Affine information projection and moment action]
\label{thm:SMYM-affine-information-projection}
For the family of
\Cref{def:SMYM-affine-exponential-family},
\[
 \boxed{
 \nabla\Psi_g(\lambda)=\mathbb E_{q_{g,\lambda}}X,
 \qquad
 \nabla^2\Psi_g(\lambda)
 =\operatorname{Cov}_{q_{g,\lambda}}(X,X)\succ0
 \quad\text{on }V_\Gamma.}
 \tag{CY.13b}
\]
The gradient is an analytic bijection
\[
 \boxed{
 \nabla\Psi_g:V_\Gamma
 \longrightarrow
 \operatorname{ri}\operatorname{conv}\{x_1,\ldots,x_m\}.}
 \tag{CY.13c}
\]
For an affine mean $\theta$ in this relative interior, let
$\lambda_\theta$ be its unique inverse image and put
$q_{g,\theta}=q_{g,\lambda_\theta}$.  Every faithful selector
$q\in\mathcal Q_\Gamma(z_\star+\theta)$ satisfies
\[
 \boxed{
 D_{\rm KL}(q\Vert g)
 =D_{\rm KL}(q\Vert q_{g,\theta})
  +D_{\rm KL}(q_{g,\theta}\Vert g).}
 \tag{CY.13d}
\]
Consequently $q_{g,\theta}$ is the unique minimum-relative-entropy comparator
in the affine fibre.  Its response-moment action
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal I_g(\theta)
 :=D_{\rm KL}(q_{g,\theta}\Vert g)
 =\langle\lambda_\theta,\theta\rangle
  -\Psi_g(\lambda_\theta)}
 \tag{CY.13e}
\]
has
\[
 \boxed{
 \nabla\mathcal I_g(\theta)=\lambda_\theta,
 \qquad
 \nabla^2\mathcal I_g(\theta)
 =\operatorname{Cov}_{q_{g,\theta}}(X,X)^{-1}\succ0.}
 \tag{CY.13f}
\]
Thus the affine response mean carries a canonical strictly convex Numerical
action relative to $g$, while the first term on the right of
\textup{(CY.13d)} is selector detail invisible to the frozen linear response
bank.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Differentiation of the finite log partition gives the mean and covariance.
No nonzero vector of $V_\Gamma$ is constant on all response atoms, so the
covariance is positive definite.  For an interior mean, strict convexity and
coercivity of
$\Psi_g(\lambda)-\langle\lambda,\theta\rangle$ give a unique critical point;
the inverse-function theorem gives the analytic bijection.  Since
$\log(q_{g,\theta}(i)/g_i)$ is affine in $x_i$, its expectation is the same
under every selector in the mean fibre.  Expanding the three relative
entropies proves \textup{(CY.13d)}.  Formula \textup{(CY.13e)} is the Legendre
transform of $\Psi_g$, and differentiation gives \textup{(CY.13f)}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[KL domination of the affine and quadratic residuals]
\label{cor:SMYM-affine-KL-control}
Let $q_\ell,g_\ell$ be faithful selector rows with affine coordinates
$\theta_\ell^q,\theta_\ell^g$, and assume
$\|z_i-z_\star\|\le B$.  Then
\[
 \boxed{
 \Delta_{\rm aff}(q,g)
 :=\sum_\ell\mu_\ell
   \|\theta_\ell^q-\theta_\ell^g\|^2
 \le 2B^2\sum_\ell\mu_\ell
   D_{\rm KL}(q_\ell\Vert g_\ell).}
 \tag{CY.13g}
\]
For one common source profile $s_\ell$, put
$M_S^2=\sum_\ell\mu_\ell\|s_\ell\|^2$ and
$M_T=\max_{\ell,\sigma\in\{q,g\}}\|t_\ell^\sigma\|$.  The corresponding
quadratic blocks satisfy
\[
 \boxed{
 \|C_q-C_g\|\le M_S\sqrt{\Delta_{\rm aff}(q,g)},
 \qquad
 \|D_q-D_g\|\le2M_T\sqrt{\Delta_{\rm aff}(q,g)}.}
 \tag{CY.13h}
\]
Hence zero affine residual gives the same first quadratic response packet.
It gives equality of the selector rows only on the simplicial branch of
\Cref{thm:SMYM-affine-minimality}.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The expectation difference is bounded by
$B\|q_\ell-g_\ell\|_1$ and Pinsker's inequality gives
$\|q_\ell-g_\ell\|_1^2\le2D_{\rm KL}(q_\ell\Vert g_\ell)$.
The Gram bounds follow by Cauchy--Schwarz and by expanding
$t_qt_q^*-t_gt_g^*$.
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[Information projection is not physical selector incidence]
The row $q_{g,\theta}$ is canonical only relative to the independently
physical reference $g$ and the declared KL geometry.  It is the nearest
comparator in the measured affine fibre; it is not the observed law unless a
selector-incidence, likelihood-ratio, or process residual separately vanishes.
No maximum-entropy convention is used to populate an unmeasured physical row.
\end{firewall}

\begin{theorem}[Affine quadratic common landing]
\label{thm:SMYM-affine-common-landing}
Let $s_\ell$ be the frozen source profile and suppose the affine panel of
\Cref{def:SMYM-affine-frame} has reconstructed every $t_\ell$.  Define
\[
 G=\sum_\ell\mu_\ell s_\ell s_\ell^*,\qquad
 C=\sum_\ell\mu_\ell s_\ell t_\ell^*,\qquad
 D=\sum_\ell\mu_\ell t_\ell t_\ell^*.
 \tag{CY.14}
\]
If the response synthesis is $T=PS_\Gamma$ for one physical positive
self-adjoint slab $0\preceq P\preceq I$, then the literal quadratic
Hankel--moment transfer triplet is
\[
 \boxed{M_0^\Gamma=G,\qquad M_1^\Gamma=C,\qquad M_2^\Gamma=D,}
 \tag{CY.15}
\]
and the first response innovation is
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathbb I_\Gamma
 =D-C^*G^\dagger C
 =\sum_\ell\mu_\ell r_\ell r_\ell^*,
 \qquad r_\ell=t_\ell-C^*G^\dagger s_\ell.}
 \tag{CY.16}
\]
The same packet gives the finite-step symmetric and skew forms
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathsf S_{\Gamma,\tau}^{\rm step}
 =\tau^{-1}\!\left[G-\frac12(C+C^*)\right]\succeq0,
 \qquad
 \mathsf A_{\Gamma,\tau}^{\rm step}
 =\frac{C-C^*}{2\tau}.}
 \tag{CY.17}
\]
For two independently physical response rows $q^{(1)},q^{(2)}$, the residual
\[
 \boxed{
 \Delta_{1/2}^{\rm aff}
 =\sum_\ell\mu_\ell\|t_\ell^{(1)}-t_\ell^{(2)}\|^2}
 \tag{CY.18}
\]
vanishes exactly when every frozen linear response writer and the complete
quadratic triplet agree.  Off the simplicial branch it does not prove equality
of quotient odds, likelihood ratios, nonlinear response writers, path laws,
or fine action coefficients.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The affine frame reconstructs the pointwise means.  Their three Gram blocks are
\textup{(CY.14)}.  The Schur identity in \textup{(CY.16)} is orthogonal
projection of the response profile away from the source range.  Since
$P$ is a self-adjoint contraction,
$G-\tfrac12(C+C^*)=S_\Gamma^*(I-P)S_\Gamma\succeq0$.
The residual statement follows by substitution, while the selector
qualification is \Cref{thm:SMYM-affine-minimality}.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Affine reflection and cutoff transport]
\label{thm:SMYM-affine-transport}
Suppose physical reflection acts affinely by
$z_\star^-+v\mapsto z_\star^++R_\Gamma v$ with $R_\Gamma$ unitary.  Then
\[
 \boxed{
 \Delta_{\rm aff}^{\rm ref}
 =\sum_\ell\mu_\ell
 \|\theta_{\Theta\ell}^- -R_\Gamma^*\theta_\ell^+\|^2=0}
 \tag{CY.19}
\]
is equivalent to reflection of the complete predictable response profile and
implies the corresponding congruences for $G,C,D$.

For adjacent cutoffs, assume the affine carriers and probe frames intertwine
and $F_{\Gamma,Y}\succeq\alpha I$.  If $\varepsilon_b$ is the aligned
$L^2$ error of the transported raw contrast moments, then
\[
 \boxed{
 \|\theta_Y\circ j-J_\Gamma\theta_X\|_{L^2(\mu)}
 \le\alpha^{-1/2}\varepsilon_b.}
 \tag{CY.20}
\]
Consequently the quadratic triplet and its Schur innovation transport with
explicit Cauchy--Schwarz bounds.  Full selector reflection still requires the
simplicial branch or an independently acquired odds panel.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The first claim is equality of reconstructed affine coordinates.  For the
cutoff claim, apply the weighted left inverse in \textup{(CY.11)} pointwise and
use the frame floor.  The Gram bounds follow by expanding rank-one differences
and applying Cauchy--Schwarz.
\end{proof}

\begin{assessment}[Exact common SM--Yang--Mills frontier]
\label{assess:SMYM-affine-frontier}
The colour configuration, local action, source-core residuals, affine-frame
minimum, selector-fibre dimension, reference-relative information projection,
positive moment action, quadratic Hankel--moment landing, reflection test, and
cutoff transport are finite theorem chains.  The general first unpopulated row
is a physical full-coupling forward/reflected colour slab.  If its Doob kernel
and complete HMT action-writer bank are directly available, the first temporal
closure requires only the conditional carr\'e-du-champ writer and
$M_0^\Gamma,M_1^\Gamma,M_2^\Gamma$ of
\Cref{thm:GT-three-cylinder-action-response}; separate entrance and exit banks
and the full affine selector are not independent acquisitions.  If only
source-labelled response means are accessible, the sharp affine frame remains
the minimal route and requires exactly $d_{\Gamma,X}$ scalar contrasts per
source record after the frozen radii are stacked.  A connected quotient-odds
panel is stronger and is needed only for selector equality as a law, nonlinear
response, or coefficient attribution.  Failure returns a missing conditional
writer, lag-moment rank direction, affine contrast, frame-floor defect,
selector fibre, or transport residual; it does not presently indicate another
gauge, internal, or spacetime primitive.  None of these finite statements
supplies the weak-coupling ultraviolet/infrared floor or the interacting
Osterwalder--Schrader continuum required for a Yang--Mills mass gap.
\end{assessment}

\begin{theorem}[Mass gap--zero-free half-plane duality]
\label{thm:gap-zero-free}
Let $T_0$ be a finite normal contraction on a non-vacuum sector, let
$q=\norm{T_0}_{\op}<1$, and put
$\Delta=-\tau^{-1}\log q>0$.  For
\[
 D_{\rm rel}(s)=\det(I-e^{-\tau s}T_0)
\]
one has
\[
 \boxed{
 \sup\{\Re s:D_{\rm rel}(s)=0\}
 =\tau^{-1}\log q=-\Delta.}
\]
Consequently $D_{\rm rel}$ is zero free in $\Re s>-\Delta$.  Conversely, if
it is zero free in $\Re s>-\Delta_0$, then
$\norm{T_0}_{\op}\le e^{-\tau\Delta_0}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
For a normal matrix the operator norm equals the largest eigenvalue modulus.
Apply \Cref{thm:eigenvalue-zero-lines} with $\ell=\tau$.  The converse follows
because every nonzero eigenvalue produces a determinant zero on the vertical
line determined by its modulus.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Primitive invariant-loop saturation]
\label{thm:YM-primitive-loop-saturation}
On a finite connected lattice, retain before centering every selected global
cycle, centre-flux, and topological record.  The algebra generated by primitive
edge-current and transported plaquette writers, adjoints, finite products,
local concatenation, reflection, gauge averaging, and the retained global
cycles is dense in the selected finite-lattice gauge-invariant algebra.  If the
finite-regulator vacuum is strictly positive almost everywhere, the centered
primitive source orbit is cyclic in the selected neutral vacuum complement.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
After maximal-tree gauge reduction, defining-representation matrix
coefficients and their conjugates separate points of the compact product of
chord holonomies.  Stone--Weierstrass and gauge averaging give the full
invariant continuous algebra; Peter--Weyl gives the same statement in the
spin-network basis.  The global cycles are necessary because contractible
plaquettes are invariant under nontrivial centre one-form transformations.
Multiplication by a strictly positive vacuum is a unitary from
$L^2(|\Omega|^2d\mu)$ onto the physical Hilbert space, so density of the
function algebra gives cyclicity.  Centering then removes only the vacuum
line.
\end{proof}


\begin{theorem}[Vacuum Doob transfer as a Koopman compression]
\label{thm:YM-Doob-Koopman}
Let $0\preceq T\preceq I$ be a finite-regulator gauge-invariant transfer with
strictly positive normalized vacuum $T\Omega=\Omega$.  In a configuration
representation with reference measure $\nu$, put
\[
 d\mu=|\Omega|^2d\nu,
 \qquad
 \mathscr P f=\Omega^{-1}T(\Omega f).
\]
Then $\mathscr P$ is a self-adjoint Markov contraction on $L^2(\mu)$.  Let
$\boldsymbol\mu$ be its stationary two-sided path law, let $U$ be the path
shift on $L^2(\boldsymbol\mu)$, and let
$Jf(\omega)=f(\omega_0)$.  For every $n\ge0$,
\[
 \boxed{J^*U^nJ=\mathscr P^n,}
\]
and
\[
 \boxed{
 2(I-\mathscr P)=J^*(U-I)^*(U-I)J.}
\]
Thus the Yang--Mills transfer Dirichlet form is exactly one half of the
untwisted Koopman augmentation energy on one-slice observables.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Multiplication by $\Omega$ is unitary from $L^2(\mu)$ to the physical transfer
space, so positivity, self-adjointness, and vacuum preservation make
$\mathscr P$ a self-adjoint Markov contraction.  Stationarity gives, for
bounded $f,g$,
\[
 \langle Jf,U^nJg\rangle
 =\mathbb E[\overline{f(X_0)}g(X_n)]
 =\langle f,\mathscr P^ng\rangle.
\]
This proves the compression identity.  Expanding
$(U-I)^*(U-I)=2I-U-U^*$ and using reversibility gives the second formula.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Yang--Mills occupies the invariant/fixed-free arm]
\label{cor:YM-no-character-arm}
If $0\preceq\mathscr P\preceq I$, then its only unit-circle spectral value is
$1$.  Hence a positive self-adjoint Yang--Mills transfer cannot supply a
nontrivial predictive character.  Its protected decomposition is the vacuum
fixed sector together with the fixed-free complement on which the mass gap is
a positive augmentation floor.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The spectrum of a positive contraction is contained in $[0,1]$.  Its
intersection with the unit circle is therefore $\{1\}$.
\end{proof}


\begin{theorem}[Volume-uniform strong-electric $SU(3)$ slab gap]
\label{thm:YM-strong-electric-gap}
For the finite-volume $SU(3)$ heat-kernel/Wilson transfer, let
$\varepsilon_\kappa=\|K_\kappa-1\|_\infty$.  If
\[
 \boxed{2\varepsilon_\kappa+12\tanh\eta<1,}
\]
then in every finite periodic spatial volume and every reducing neutral
sector,
\[
 \boxed{
 \|T_{\kappa,\eta}|_{\Omega^\perp}\|
 \le
 \frac{1-12\tanh\eta-
 \sqrt{(1-12\tanh\eta)^2-4\varepsilon_\kappa^2}}
 {2\varepsilon_\kappa}<1.}
\]
The value at $\varepsilon_\kappa=0$ is understood by continuity.  In
particular,
\[
 \boxed{\kappa\ge4,
 \qquad0\le\eta\le1/18
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 \|T|_{\Omega^\perp}\|\le9/13}
\]
uniformly in the periodic spatial volume.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The pointwise heat-kernel window bounds each of the two temporal single-link
influences by $\varepsilon_\kappa$.  A link belongs to four plaquettes and each
contains three other links, so the same-slice magnetic influence row sum is at
most $12\tanh\eta$.  The space--time Dobrushin matrix therefore has row sum
$2\varepsilon_\kappa+12\tanh\eta<1$.  Coupling the future cylinder with one
changed incoming link, passing to the Perron boundary law, and using the
one-dimensional cylinder Green function gives the displayed upper root for the
Doob slab contraction.  The Doob transform is unitarily equivalent to the
positive transfer, so the same bound holds on the vacuum complement and every
reducing neutral sector.  The heat-kernel character estimate at $\kappa\ge4$
and $\tanh\eta\le\eta\le1/18$ give the stated rational bound.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Finite regulated neutral-sector mass criterion]
\label{thm:YM-regulated-criterion}
Let a positive transfer contraction have a source-head/tail decomposition
\[
 T=\begin{pmatrix}A&B\\B^*&D\end{pmatrix},
 \qquad a=\norm A,\quad b=\norm B.
\]
Assume $\norm D\le1-\mu$ with $\mu>0$, $a<1$, and
$b^2<(1-a)\mu$.  Then
\[
 \boxed{
 \norm T\le q_{\rm reg}
 :=\frac{a+1-\mu+\sqrt{(a-1+\mu)^2+4b^2}}2<1,}
\]
and if $T=e^{-\tau H}$, the non-vacuum spectral gap obeys
\[
 \boxed{\Delta_{\rm reg}\ge-\tau^{-1}\log q_{\rm reg}>0.}
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
For $x\oplus y$ with $\norm{x\oplus y}=1$, positivity and Cauchy--Schwarz give
\[
 \ip{x\oplus y}{T(x\oplus y)}
 \le a\norm x^2+2b\norm x\norm y+(1-\mu)\norm y^2.
\]
The right side is bounded by the largest eigenvalue of
$\begin{psmallmatrix}a&b\\b&1-\mu\end{psmallmatrix}$, which is
$q_{\rm reg}$.  The strict determinant inequality
$b^2<(1-a)\mu$ places that eigenvalue below one.  The transfer relation then
converts the norm bound into the displayed energy gap.
\end{proof}



\begin{theorem}[Common-time signed compression and Stieltjes return packet]
\label{thm:YM-signed-threshold-packet}
Let $J$ be the source-range isometry between adjacent cutoffs and let
$T_X,T_Y$ be positive self-adjoint contractions at one calibrated physical
time.  Put $P=JJ^*$ and
\[
 M_1=J^*T_YJ,
 \qquad M_2=J^*T_Y^2J,
 \qquad C=M_1-T_X,
\]
\[
 L=(I-P)T_YJ,
 \qquad \mathbb V=L^*L=M_2-M_1^2\succeq0.
 \tag{YM.1}
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{T_YJ-JT_X=L+JC,
 \qquad (T_YJ-JT_X)^*(T_YJ-JT_X)=\mathbb V+C^2.}
 \tag{YM.2}
\]
Writing
$T_Y=\begin{psmallmatrix}M_1&B\\B^*&D\end{psmallmatrix}$ gives
$BB^*=\mathbb V$.  If $D\preceq dI$ with $d<q$, then
\[
 \boxed{
 qI-M_1-\frac{\mathbb V}{q-d}\succeq0
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad T_Y\preceq qI.}
 \tag{YM.3}
\]
The compression mismatch $C$ is signed: negative generalized directions
increase the threshold reserve and must not be replaced by $\|C\|I$.

If the third transported moment is available, then
\[
 \mathbb W:=BDB^*
 =M_3-M_1^3-M_1\mathbb V-\mathbb VM_1,
 \tag{YM.4}
\]
and the exact return self-energy satisfies
\[
 \boxed{
 \frac{\mathbb V}{q}+\frac{\mathbb W}{q^2}
 \preceq B(qI-D)^{-1}B^*
 \preceq
 \frac{\mathbb V}{q}+\frac{\mathbb W}{q(q-d)}.}
 \tag{YM.5}
\]
Finally,
\[
 \boxed{
 \operatorname{In}(qI-T_Y)
 =\operatorname{In}(qI-D)
 +\operatorname{In}\!\bigl(qI-M_1-B(qI-D)^{-1}B^*\bigr).}
 \tag{YM.6}
\]
Thus the head Schur complement counts exactly the threshold-failing source
directions, while the moment hierarchy adaptively reconstructs the positive
return packet.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The decomposition in \textup{(YM.2)} is the orthogonal split into the old
source range and its complement.  The Schur complement of $qI-T_Y$ gives the
exact threshold; the tail bound gives \textup{(YM.3)}.  Expanding $T_Y^3$ on
the head gives \textup{(YM.4)}.  The resolvent identity and
$0\preceq D\preceq dI$ give \textup{(YM.5)}.  Equation \textup{(YM.6)} is
\Cref{thm:GT-signed-Haynsworth}.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Two-scale Yang--Mills Feshbach gap compiler]
\label{thm:YM-two-scale-Feshbach}
Let the non-vacuum positive transfer generator at one regulator admit a
physical infrared/ultraviolet decomposition
\[
 L_X=\begin{pmatrix}A_X&B_X\\B_X^*&C_X\end{pmatrix}\succeq0.
\]
Assume
\[
 C_X\succeq\gamma_{\rm UV}I,
 \qquad
 S_X^{\rm IR}:=A_X-B_XC_X^{-1}B_X^*
 \succeq\delta_{\rm IR}I,
\]
\[
 \|C_X^{-1}B_X^*\|\le\beta.
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{
 L_X\succeq
 \min\left\{
 \frac{\delta_{\rm IR}}{1+2\beta^2},
 \frac{\gamma_{\rm UV}}2
 \right\}I.}
\]
If the three constants are uniform along a reflection-positive
weak-coupling/infinite-volume regulator family and the transfer is
$T_X=e^{-\tau L_X}$ at fixed physical $\tau>0$, the corresponding transfer gap
is uniform.  Failure returns an ultraviolet soft vector, an effective
infrared soft vector, or an unbounded relaxation router.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
For $x\oplus y$, \Cref{thm:GT-effective-action} gives
\[
 \langle x\oplus y,L_X(x\oplus y)\rangle
 =\langle x,S_X^{\rm IR}x\rangle
 +\langle y+C_X^{-1}B_X^*x,
 C_X(y+C_X^{-1}B_X^*x)\rangle.
\]
Also
\[
 \|x\oplus y\|^2
 \le(1+2\beta^2)\|x\|^2
 +2\|y+C_X^{-1}B_X^*x\|^2.
\]
Combining the two lower bounds gives the displayed constant.  Exponentiation
at fixed physical time converts a generator floor into a transfer contraction.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Boundary-complete infrared handoff]
\label{cor:YM-boundary-complete-handoff}
In the setting of \Cref{thm:YM-two-scale-Feshbach}, let the infrared and
ultraviolet carriers also feed an actual boundary or sweep-comparison map
$\mathcal D_X=(D_{{\rm IR},X}\;D_{{\rm UV},X})$.  Define
\[
 E_X=D_{{\rm IR},X}-D_{{\rm UV},X}C_X^{-1}B_X^*,
 \qquad
 K_X=D_{{\rm UV},X}C_X^{-1}D_{{\rm UV},X}^*.
\]
Then the exact boundary-complete infrared action is
\[
 \boxed{
 S_X^{\rm IR}+E_X^*(I+K_X)^{-1}E_X.}
\]
In particular, a positive patch or infrared floor in $S_X^{\rm IR}$ survives
ultraviolet boundary relaxation; only the separately measured comparison
between the effective return model and the physical transfer can consume that
floor.  Shorting the ultraviolet interior before assembling the boundary
would overestimate the additional boundary cost by the positive dispersion
$E_X^*K_X(I+K_X)^{-1}E_X$.
\end{corollary}

\begin{assessment}[Weak-coupling target]
The strong-electric Dobrushin estimate proves one nonempty finite-regulator
region.  Along the weak-coupling continuum trajectory the natural common-layer
target is instead block first: construct a physical ultraviolet floor, prove a
positive occurrence-shorted infrared action, and control the relaxation
router.  Bare-link smallness is neither required by this theorem nor expected
to persist on that trajectory.
\end{assessment}

\begin{assessment}[Action-complete weak-coupling globalization]
At weak coupling, word depth and star-action context are independent source
axes.  The complete mixed-word/action rectangle must therefore be reduced by a
physically declared reveal chronology before its positive innovations are
counted.  A nonzero contextual word innovation is not required to vanish: its
physical action is retained by the contextual Feshbach short, which
simultaneously renormalizes the protected head, the head--complement interface,
and the complement transfer.  The remaining slab complement is then governed
by the return synthesis of \Cref{thm:GT-return-synthesis-tail} and the marked
first-return transform of \Cref{thm:GT-positive-first-return-renewal}.
Endpoint-sampled reflection slabs must use the static Schur deficit of
\Cref{thm:GT-sampled-versus-killed}; a continuously monitored first-entry
protocol is a different physical experiment.  A volume- and cutoff-uniform
proper relative-radius moment yields a bounded connected critical head.
Failure returns an interchange source, a nonflat contextual-memory tail, a
remote reflection/IMS return, a long sampled excursion, or collapse of the
physical slab clock or tail edge.
\end{assessment}


\begin{firewall}[Why the Clay Yang--Mills theorem remains open]
A finite transfer gap becomes a four-dimensional Yang--Mills mass gap only
after a gauge-invariant, reflection-positive, nontrivial continuum measure is
constructed; the physical source family is proved complete; the vacuum is
unique; and the finite gap is uniform in volume and lattice spacing and
survives the Osterwalder--Schrader reconstruction.  The Grand Tensor organizes
these certificates but does not supply them.
\end{firewall}
