\section{Navier--Stokes: the exact relative-form continuation certificate}
\label{sec:NS-interface}
% =============================================================================

Let $A=-P\Delta$ be the Stokes operator on mean-zero divergence-free fields on
$\Torus^3$, let $B(u,v)=P((u\cdot\nabla)v)$, and, for $s>5/2$, put
\[
 E_s=\frac12\norm{A^{s/2}u}_2^2,
 \qquad
 D_s=\norm{A^{(s+1)/2}u}_2^2.
\]

\begin{theorem}[Conditional Navier--Stokes continuation]
\label{thm:NS-relative-form}
Suppose that on every finite interval of smooth existence there are
$\theta\in(0,1]$ and $k\in L^1_{\rm loc}$ such that
\[
 \left|\ip{A^{s/2}B(u,u)}{A^{s/2}u}\right|
 \le(1-\theta)\nu D_s+k(t)E_s.
\]
Then, with $K(t)=\int_0^tk(r)\,\dd r$,
\[
 \boxed{
 e^{-K(t)}E_s(t)
 +\theta\nu\int_0^te^{-K(r)}D_s(r)\,\dd r
 \le E_s(0).}
\]
A global estimate of this form implies global smoothness for smooth data.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The $H^s$ energy identity is
\[
 E_s'+\nu D_s
 =-\Re\ip{A^{s/2}B(u,u)}{A^{s/2}u}.
\]
Insert the assumed relative-form estimate to obtain
$E_s'+\theta\nu D_s\le kE_s$.  Multiplication by $e^{-K(t)}$ and integration
give the boxed inequality.  Since $s>5/2$, the standard local continuation
criterion rules out finite-time breakdown while $E_s$ remains finite.
\end{proof}


\begin{theorem}[Canonical $H^1$ process payment and replenishment]
\label{thm:NS-H1-process-stock}
On a strong-solution interval put
\[
 Y_1=\|A^{1/2}u\|_2^2,
 \qquad Z_1=\|Au\|_2^2,
 \qquad G_1=-\operatorname{Re}\langle B(u,u),Au\rangle.
\]
After viscosity, pressure/projector, source-birth, output, and backscatter rows
have been completely assembled, the exact balance is
\[
 \frac12Y_1'+\nu Z_1=G_1.
\]
The unique nonduplicating stock measures are
\[
 \boxed{
 \dd P_{H^1}=2(\nu Z_1-G_1)_+\,\dd t,
 \qquad
 \dd R_{H^1}=2(G_1-\nu Z_1)_+\,\dd t,}
 \tag{NS.0a}
\]
and satisfy
\[
 \boxed{
 Y_1(t)+P_{H^1}((s,t])
 =Y_1(s)+R_{H^1}((s,t]).}
 \tag{NS.0b}
\]
If viscosity and nonlinear production are split before assembly, the exact
duplicated turnover is
\[
 \boxed{
 \dd H_{H^1}
 =\bigl(\nu Z_1+|G_1|-|\nu Z_1-G_1|\bigr)\,\dd t.}
 \tag{NS.0c}
\]
Thus viscosity is a gross loss and positive nonlinear production is a gross
supply, but only \textup{(NS.0a)} is the net finite-stock payment.  A positive
local occurrence, voltage, or strain action enters this ledger only through a
separate ordered action-to-stock comparison.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The balance gives
$-\dd Y_1=2(\nu Z_1-G_1)\dd t$.  Apply the Jordan and assembly identities of
\Cref{thm:GT-process-stock-Jordan}.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Critical source--sheet Pythagoras and the work-null sector]
\label{thm:NS-source-sheet-pythagoras}
Let $g_R=A^{-1/4}F_R$ be the critical source at one finite head and let
$v_+,v_-$ be the two orthogonal protected helical sheet writers.  Put
$D_\sigma=\|v_\sigma\|^2$ and
$j_{R,\sigma}=\operatorname{Re}\langle v_\sigma,g_R\rangle$, and let
$P_{\rm sh}$ be the real orthogonal projection onto their supported span.  Then
\[
 \boxed{
 \|g_R\|_2^2
 =\sum_{\sigma=\pm}D_\sigma^\dagger j_{R,\sigma}^2
 +\|(I-P_{\rm sh})g_R\|_2^2.}
 \tag{NS.1}
\]
The first term is the minimum critical source norm visible to the two signed
sheet works; the second is the complete work-null source.

For exact-output fibres $h_{k,\sigma}$ and state writers $v_{k,\sigma}$, put
$r_{k,\sigma}=\operatorname{Re}\langle h_{k,\sigma},v_{k,\sigma}\rangle/
\|v_{k,\sigma}\|^2$ when $v_{k,\sigma}\ne0$, and
$\zeta_{k,\sigma}=h_{k,\sigma}-r_{k,\sigma}v_{k,\sigma}$.  With the weighted
sheet mean $\overline r_\sigma$, the high--high work-null source further
splits as
\[
 \boxed{
 \sum_{\sigma=\pm}\left[
 \sum_k\|v_{k,\sigma}\|^2|r_{k,\sigma}-\overline r_\sigma|^2
 +\sum_k\|\zeta_{k,\sigma}\|^2
 +\sum_{v_{k,\sigma}=0}\|h_{k,\sigma}\|^2
 \right].}
 \tag{NS.2}
\]
These are respectively exact-output router dispersion, phase quadrature, and
first-birth source mass.  They remain independent of the visible mixed-helicity
current.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The sheet writers are orthogonal, so \textup{(NS.1)} is orthogonal projection.
For each exact output, project $h_{k,\sigma}$ onto the real writer line and
then apply the weighted variance identity to the coefficients
$r_{k,\sigma}$; the zero-writer fibres are orthogonal first-birth terms.
\end{proof}


\begin{theorem}[Chronology-complete terminal short and dynamic source-head promotion]
\label{thm:NS-dynamic-terminal-short}
Let $\mathcal R_I:\mathscr X_I\to\mathscr Y_I$ be the physical terminal
Duhamel response of one completely assembled passage cylinder, after all
physical times and all-comparable, high-output, two-high, pressure, boundary,
and cutoff rows have been transported to one terminal carrier.  For a finite
represented history head $\mathscr H_L\subseteq\mathscr X_I$ and complement
$\mathscr T_L$, put
$\mathcal R_H=\mathcal R_I|_{\mathscr H_L}$ and
$\mathcal R_T=\mathcal R_I|_{\mathscr T_L}$.  Write the complete terminal
Gram as
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathbb G_{I,L}=
 \begin{pmatrix}A_L&B_L\\B_L^*&D_L\end{pmatrix}
 =\begin{pmatrix}
 \mathcal R_H^*\mathcal R_H&\mathcal R_H^*\mathcal R_T\\
 \mathcal R_T^*\mathcal R_H&\mathcal R_T^*\mathcal R_T
 \end{pmatrix}\succeq0.}
 \tag{NS.3}
\]
Then the dynamically represented-head short is
\[
 \boxed{
 S_{I,L}^{\rm irr}
 =D_L-B_L^*A_L^\dagger B_L
 =\mathcal R_T^*(I-P_{\Ran\mathcal R_H})\mathcal R_T\succeq0.}
 \tag{NS.4}
\]
The associated irreducible response
$\mathcal R_{I,L}^{\rm irr}=(I-P_{\Ran\mathcal R_H})\mathcal R_T$ has
compliance
$C_{I,L}^{\rm irr}=\mathcal R_{I,L}^{\rm irr}
(\mathcal R_{I,L}^{\rm irr})^*$.  For an assembled terminal defect
$\delta_I$, put
$\delta_{I,L}^{\rm irr}=(I-P_{\Ran\mathcal R_H})\delta_I$; its
source-minimal action is
\[
 \boxed{
 d_{I,L}^{\rm irr}
 =\langle\delta_{I,L}^{\rm irr},
 (C_{I,L}^{\rm irr})^\dagger\delta_{I,L}^{\rm irr}\rangle
 =\min_{\mathcal R_{I,L}^{\rm irr}q=-\delta_{I,L}^{\rm irr}}\|q\|^2.}
 \tag{NS.5}
\]

For nested admissible source cores $L<M$, the terminal head images are nested.
If $\Pi_L\le\Pi_M$ are their projections, then the head-relaxed residual obeys
\[
 \boxed{
 \|(I-\Pi_L)y\|^2
 =\|(\Pi_M-\Pi_L)y\|^2+\|(I-\Pi_M)y\|^2.}
 \tag{NS.6}
\]
The first term is a physical promotion into the enlarged head and cannot also
be charged as an earlier irreducible birth.

If
$\delta^{\rm irr}=\delta^{\rm cmp}+\delta^{\rm swp}+\delta^{\rm bsc}$,
the complete geometry action is the quadratic form of the mixed Gram
\[
 \boxed{
 [\mathbb A_{I,L}^{\rm geom}]_{\xi\zeta}
 =\operatorname{Re}\langle
 \delta^\xi,(C_{I,L}^{\rm irr})^\dagger\delta^\zeta\rangle,
 \qquad
 d_{I,L}^{\rm irr}=\one^*\mathbb A_{I,L}^{\rm geom}\one.}
 \tag{NS.7}
\]
The separate diagonal costs may cancel through the off-diagonal blocks and
may not be summed before common-terminal assembly.  Across repeated cylinders,
only the source-fresh, terminal-new component selected by
\Cref{thm:GT-source-terminal-nonduplication} is independently spendable.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The Anderson--Trapp short of the positive block Gram gives \textup{(NS.4)};
the Moore--Penrose Thomson principle gives \textup{(NS.5)}.  Equation
\textup{(NS.6)} is the nested-projection Pythagoras.  Expanding the assembled
quadratic form in the three physical geometry columns gives
\textup{(NS.7)}.  The final nonduplication statement is
\Cref{thm:GT-source-terminal-nonduplication}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Mixed-helicity/work-null continuation interface]
\label{cor:NS-mixed-null-continuation}
If on a maximal smooth interval $[t_0,T)$ the minimum common mixed-helicity
source action and the complete high--high work-null source in
\textup{(NS.2)} are both integrable, then
\[
 \int_{t_0}^{T}\|A^{-1/4}F_R(t)\|_2^2\,dt<\infty,
\]
and the standard critical source continuation theorem extends the solution
when $T<\infty$.  The unresolved PDE problem is to derive these integrability
bounds from the actual reproduction law, viscosity, pressure/projector rows,
open-scale current, and boundary work.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Add the visible and work-null identities and integrate.  The resulting
critical source moment is precisely the hypothesis of the inherited
continuation criterion.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Occurrence-shorted triad action and open scale current]
\label{thm:NS-effective-scale-current}
Let $H_{3,X}$ be an actual degree-three triad carrier.  Short simultaneously by
all one- and two-slot source ranges and by every nonmonoidal occurrence sector,
and let
\[
 A_{3,X}^{\rm eff}\succeq0
\]
be the resulting positive all-residual action.  Let
\[
 D_{{\rm sc},X}:H_{3,X}^{\rm eff}\longrightarrow S_X
\]
be the physical logarithmic-scale boundary map, and put
\[
 L_{{\rm sc},X}
 :=D_{{\rm sc},X}(A_{3,X}^{\rm eff})^\dagger
 D_{{\rm sc},X}^*.
\]
For every scale source $s_X\in\Ran D_{{\rm sc},X}$ orthogonal to the harmonic
obstruction,
\[
 \boxed{
 \inf_{D_{{\rm sc},X}j=s_X}
 \langle j,A_{3,X}^{\rm eff}j\rangle
 =\langle s_X,L_{{\rm sc},X}^\dagger s_X\rangle.}
\]
The minimizer is the canonical current
\[
 \boxed{
 j_X^*=(A_{3,X}^{\rm eff})^\dagger
 D_{{\rm sc},X}^*L_{{\rm sc},X}^\dagger s_X.}
\]
If the scale carrier is an open path, this cost reduces to the cumulative-sum
formula of \Cref{thm:GT-open-current}.  Any physical estimate comparing the
right side with viscosity, elapsed physical time, or boundary work therefore
charges the critical-null scale-counterflow branch without imposing an
artificial periodic character.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
This is the weighted Thomson principle.  Minimize the positive quadratic form
under the affine constraint with Lagrange multiplier $\phi$.  The normal
equation gives
$j=(A_{3,X}^{\rm eff})^\dagger D_{{\rm sc},X}^*\phi$, and the constraint gives
$L_{{\rm sc},X}\phi=s_X$.  The minimum-norm multiplier is
$\phi=L_{{\rm sc},X}^\dagger s_X$, which yields both formulas.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Translation--helical common-action handoff]
\label{thm:NS-translation-helical-handoff}
Let $D_{\rm tr}:E_{\rm tr}\to\mathcal H$ be the physically loaded translation-
strain bank and let $D_{\rm hel}:E_{\rm hel}\to\mathcal H$ be the helical
source, both represented in one positive same-history action.  Put
\[
 P_{\rm tr}=D_{\rm tr}(D_{\rm tr}^*D_{\rm tr})^\dagger D_{\rm tr}^*,
 \qquad
 R_{\rm hel}=(I-P_{\rm tr})D_{\rm hel}.
\]
For a screened interior--boundary action $A_Z=L_Z+D_Z^*D_Z$ with closed
obstruction projection $P_0$ as in the universal open-current packet, define
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathbb O_{\rm hel}
 =R_{\rm hel}^*P_0QR_{\rm hel},}
\]
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathbb K_{\rm hel}
 =R_{\rm hel}^*(Q-P_0)A_Z^\dagger(Q-P_0)R_{\rm hel}.}
\]
Then $R_{\rm hel}=0$ is exact routing of the helical source through the
translation source.  Otherwise $\mathbb O_{\rm hel}$ is the closed helical
obstruction and $\mathbb K_{\rm hel}$ is the minimum positive
interior-plus-boundary cost of the surviving source.  For each coefficient
$c$, the corresponding source has the canonical minimum decomposition
\[
 (Q-P_0)R_{\rm hel}c=L_Z^{1/2}a_c+D_Z^*j_c,
 \qquad
 \|a_c\|^2+\|j_c\|^2
 =\langle c,\mathbb K_{\rm hel}c\rangle.
\]
A signed scalar strain trace alone does not determine any of these positive
source ranges or costs.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The first residual is the Anderson--Trapp source short by the translation
range.  Orthogonal decomposition of $QR_{\rm hel}c$ into
$P_0QR_{\rm hel}c$ and its complement gives the closed obstruction.  The
minimum interior-plus-boundary representation on the complement is the
Moore--Penrose Riesz/Thomson formula for $A_Z$, yielding the displayed cost.
\end{proof}


% =============================================================================
\subsection{Critical Fourier localization, terminal cubic cylinders, and profile defects}
\label{sec:NS-critical-cylinder-profile}
% =============================================================================

\begin{theorem}[Exact Fourier-output localization of the critical source]
\label{thm:NS-Fourier-output-localization}
At a finite periodic cutoff, let $\mathscr X_N^{(2)}$ be the ordered
Fourier-donor carrier and let
\[
 \mathcal C_N^{\rm crit}:\mathscr X_N^{(2)}\longrightarrow H_N
\]
be the completely pressure-shorted critical source map.  For each output
frequency $k$, let $R_{N,k}$ project onto the ordered donor pairs $(p,q)$ with
$p+q=k$, and let $P_{N,k}$ be the output Fourier projection.  Then
\[
 \boxed{
 P_{N,k}\mathcal C_N^{\rm crit}
 =\mathcal C_N^{\rm crit}R_{N,k},
 \qquad
 \mathcal C_N^{\rm crit}
 =\bigoplus_k\mathcal C_{N,k}^{\rm crit}R_{N,k}.}
 \tag{NS.F1}
\]
Consequently the critical source Gram is block diagonal by output frequency:
\[
 \boxed{
 (\mathcal C_N^{\rm crit})^*\mathcal C_N^{\rm crit}
 =\bigoplus_k
 R_{N,k}(\mathcal C_N^{\rm crit})^*
 \mathcal C_N^{\rm crit}R_{N,k}.}
 \tag{NS.F2}
\]
For an actual donor $X=\sum_kX_k$, put
\[
 b_k=\|X_k\|^2,
 \qquad
 c_k=\|\mathcal C_N^{\rm crit}X_k\|^2.
\]
If $X\ne0$, its source-supported critical influence satisfies
\[
 \boxed{
 \frac{\|\mathcal C_N^{\rm crit}X\|^2}{\|X\|^2}
 =\frac{\sum_kc_k}{\sum_kb_k}
 \le\max_{k:b_k>0}\frac{c_k}{b_k}.}
 \tag{NS.F3}
\]
Thus influence escape first localizes to one Fourier output mode with no
cross-output multiplicity loss.  Each ordered donor atom belongs to exactly
one output block, so the source-to-output incidence degree at this stage is
one.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Fourier convolution sends an ordered pair $(p,q)$ to $k=p+q$, while the Leray
projection and the critical multiplier are diagonal in the output frequency.
This gives \textup{(NS.F1)}.  Distinct output-frequency spaces are orthogonal,
so all cross blocks in the adjoint Gram vanish, proving \textup{(NS.F2)}.
The same orthogonality gives
$\|X\|^2=\sum_kb_k$ and
$\|\mathcal C_N^{\rm crit}X\|^2=\sum_kc_k$; the final statement is the
weighted-average bound.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Rank-at-most-two Fourier carriers are exact $2$D$3$C systems]
\label{thm:NS-rank-two-carrier}
Let $\Lambda\le\Z^3$ be an additive subgroup of rank at most two, and let
$\mathcal H_\Lambda$ be the periodic divergence-free fields whose Fourier
support lies in $\Lambda$.  The Stokes semigroup, Leray projection, and
Navier--Stokes convolution preserve $\mathcal H_\Lambda$.  If $e$ is a unit
normal to the real span of $\Lambda$, every field in this carrier has the form
\[
 u=v+we,
 \qquad e\cdot v=0,
 \qquad e\cdot\nabla v=e\cdot\nabla w=0,
\]
and the three-dimensional equation reduces exactly to
\[
 \boxed{
 \partial_tv+v\cdot\nabla_\Pi v+\nabla_\Pi p-\nu\Delta_\Pi v=0,
 \qquad \nabla_\Pi\cdot v=0,}
 \tag{NS.8}
\]
\[
 \boxed{
 \partial_tw+v\cdot\nabla_\Pi w-\nu\Delta_\Pi w=0.}
 \tag{NS.9}
\]
Every smooth datum in $\mathcal H_\Lambda$ therefore gives a unique global
smooth solution.  In particular, the isolated descendant carrier generated by
two donor wavevectors, including a participation-one caloric-flat Star, is not
by itself a three-dimensional singularity mechanism.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Fourier multiplication adds frequencies, so the subgroup support is invariant;
the Leray multiplier preserves each frequency.  In coordinates adapted to the
normal $e$, the fields are independent of the normal variable.  The in-plane
component obeys two-dimensional Navier--Stokes and the normal component is a
passive advection--diffusion scalar.  Global smoothness follows from the
standard two-dimensional vorticity estimate and the scalar energy estimates.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[First genuinely three-dimensional Fourier exit]
\label{cor:NS-first-rank-three-exit}
Let $p,q\in\Z^3$ be linearly independent and put
$\Lambda_{p,q}=\Z p+\Z q$.  Every descendant generated solely by convolution,
heat flow, and Leray projection from this carrier remains in
$\mathcal H_{\Lambda_{p,q}}$ and is therefore globally smooth by
\Cref{thm:NS-rank-two-carrier}.  A mode $r$ leaves the real donor plane exactly
when
\[
 \boxed{\Delta_{\rm 3D}(p,q;r):=|\det(p,q,r)|>0.}
 \tag{NS.F4}
\]
Because the determinant is integral, every such exit satisfies
$\Delta_{\rm 3D}(p,q;r)\ge1$.  It cannot be generated internally by the
rank-two carrier and must enter through an independently present mode, a
cross-packet fusion, or an assembled external, boundary, or cutoff source.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The subgroup $\Lambda_{p,q}$ is closed under addition and negation, so every
internal convolution frequency remains in it.  The determinant vanishes
exactly on the real span of $p,q$; integrality gives the unit lower quantum on
the nonzero branch.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[A finite maximal time forces a scale-critical dyadic shell]
\label{thm:NS-critical-shell}
Let $u$ be a smooth mean-zero periodic solution on a maximal interval
$[0,T_*)$, let $s>5/2$, and let $u_q=\Delta_qu$ with $\lambda_q=2^q$.
For
\[
 \mathcal B_Q(u)=\sup_{q>Q}\lambda_q^{-1}\|u_q\|_\infty,
\]
there is $c_s>0$ such that
\[
 \mathcal B_Q(u(t))\le c_s\nu
\]
on a terminal interval implies continuation beyond its endpoint.  Hence, if
$T_*<\infty$, there are $t_j\uparrow T_*$ and $q_j\to\infty$ such that
\[
 \boxed{
 \lambda_{q_j}^{-1}\|u_{q_j}(t_j)\|_\infty\ge c_s\nu.}
 \tag{NS.10}
\]
The same shell has
\[
 \boxed{
 \|u_{q_j}(t_j)\|_2^2\ge c\nu^2\lambda_{q_j}^{-1},
 \qquad
 \|\omega_{q_j}(t_j)\|_2^2\ge c\nu^2\lambda_{q_j}.}
 \tag{NS.11}
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Bony decomposition and Bernstein inequalities give
\[
 \left|\langle A^{s/2}B(u,u),A^{s/2}u\rangle\right|
 \le C_s\|\nabla u_{\le Q}\|_\infty\|u\|_{H^s}^2
   +C_s\mathcal B_Q(u)\|u\|_{H^{s+1}}^2.
\]
For sufficiently small $c_s$, the second term is absorbed by viscosity; the
finite low-frequency coefficient is locally integrable and Gronwall gives
continuation.  The contrapositive yields \textup{(NS.10)}.  Bernstein's
inequality and frequency localization give \textup{(NS.11)}.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Pressure-compatible cubic-cylinder alternative]
\label{thm:NS-critical-cubic-cylinder}
For a critical shell $(t,q)$ of \Cref{thm:NS-critical-shell}, put
$r=\lambda_q^{-1}$ and choose $x_0$ at a point of maximal shell amplitude.
Choose a smooth periodic distance surrogate $d_0(\cdot,x_0)$ comparable to the
geodesic distance below the injectivity radius.  For $2<\alpha<3$, let
\[
 \vartheta_{r,x_0}(x)
 =\left(\frac{r^2}{r^2+d_0(x,x_0)^2}\right)^{\alpha/2}.
\]
There are constants $a,c_0>0$ such that
\[
 \boxed{
 \frac12\int_{\Torus^3}|u(t)|^2\vartheta_{r,x_0}
 \ge c_0\nu^2r.}
 \tag{NS.12}
\]
On the terminal viscous interval $I_r=[t-ar^2/\nu,t]$, at least one of the
following rows pays a fixed fraction of this packet:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(C\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item inherited localized kinetic energy at the initial end of $I_r$;
\item an assembled force, physical boundary, cutoff, or projection-commutator
      row;
\item a velocity-cubic row satisfying
      \[
       \boxed{
       \int_{I_r}\!\int\vartheta_{r,x_0}|u|^3
       \ge c\nu^2r^2.}
       \tag{NS.13}
      \]
\end{enumerate}
In the third branch there is a radius $r\le R\le1$ such that
\[
 \boxed{
 \begin{gathered}
 \displaystyle
 \int_{I_r}\int_{B_R(x_0)}|u|^3
 \ge\varepsilon_*\nu^2R^2,\\[0.35em]
 \displaystyle
 \frac1{\nu^2R^2}
 \int_{t-aR^2/\nu}^{t}\int_{B_R(x_0)}|u|^3
 \ge\varepsilon_*>0.
 \end{gathered}}
 \tag{NS.14}
\]
Along a terminal critical sequence for an unforced periodic solution, the
selected radii may be chosen with $R_j\downarrow0$.  Every pairwise disjoint
family of the enlarged cylinders obeys
\[
 \boxed{
 \sum_jR_j^2
 \le\frac1{\varepsilon_*\nu^2}
       \int_0^{T_*}\!\int_{\Torus^3}|u|^3<\infty.}
 \tag{NS.15}
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Writing $u_q=K_q*u$, rapid decay of the shell kernel and weighted
Cauchy--Schwarz give
\[
 |u_q(x_0)|^2
 \le Cr^{-3}\int_{\Torus^3}|u(x,t)|^2\vartheta_{r,x_0}(x)\,\dd x.
\]
The critical amplitude therefore gives \textup{(NS.12)}.  The displayed
weights have a uniform $A_{3/2}$ constant for $2<\alpha<3$.  Transport the
terminal weight backward by the heat semigroup.  Its gradient is bounded by
$Cr^{-1}$ times the same weight, and the periodic pressure representation
together with the weighted Calder\'on--Zygmund estimate gives
\[
 \int\vartheta|p|^{3/2}\le C\int\vartheta|u|^3.
\]
The exact local-energy identity therefore reduces the completely assembled
pressure--transport flux to $Cr^{-1}\int\vartheta|u|^3$, yielding the three
branches and \textup{(NS.13)}.  A dyadic collar decomposition of $\vartheta$
produces the first inequality in \textup{(NS.14)}; enlarging the time interval
gives the second.  Global energy and Gagliardo--Nirenberg estimates give
$u\in L^3((0,T_*)\times\Torus^3)$.  If $R_j\ge R_0>0$ on a subsequence, the
first inequality in \textup{(NS.14)} has a fixed positive lower bound while
$|I_{r_j}|\to0$, contradicting absolute continuity of the $L^3$ integral.
Thus $R_j\to0$.  Summing the second inequality over disjoint cylinders proves
\textup{(NS.15)}.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Nested-cylinder compactness and dissipation-defect alternative]
\label{thm:NS-ancient-profile-alternative}
Let $Q_j$ be a nested or non-disjoint sequence of cylinders from
\textup{(NS.14)} with $R_j\downarrow0$, and define the viscosity-one rescaling
\[
 U_j(y,s)=\frac{R_j}{\nu}
 u\left(x_j+R_jy,t_j+\frac{R_j^2}{\nu}s\right),
 \qquad
 P_j(y,s)=\frac{R_j^2}{\nu^2}
 p\left(x_j+R_jy,t_j+\frac{R_j^2}{\nu}s\right).
 \tag{NS.16}
\]
Then
\[
 \int_{-a}^{0}\int_{B_1}|U_j|^3\ge\varepsilon_*.
 \tag{NS.17}
\]
For
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathcal A_j(R)&=R^{-1}\operatorname*{ess\,sup}_{-R^2<s<0}
                   \int_{B_R}|U_j(s)|^2,\\
 \mathcal E_j(R)&=R^{-1}\int_{Q_R}|\nabla U_j|^2,\\
 \mathcal D_j(R)&=R^{-2}\int_{Q_R}
   |P_j-(P_j)_{B_R}(s)|^{3/2},
 \end{aligned}
\]
one of the following occurs after passage to a subsequence:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(A\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item for some finite $R$,
\[
 \boxed{\mathcal A_j(R)+\mathcal E_j(R)+\mathcal D_j(R)\to\infty;}
 \tag{NS.18}
\]
\item the packet is bounded on every finite cylinder and
\[
 \boxed{
 U_j\to U\ \text{strongly in }L^3_{\rm loc},
 \qquad
 P_j-c_j(s)\rightharpoonup P\ \text{in }L^{3/2}_{\rm loc},}
 \tag{NS.19}
\]
where $(U,P)$ is a nonzero suitable ancient viscosity-one solution with
\[
 \int_{-a}^{0}\int_{B_1}|U|^3\ge\varepsilon_*.
\]
Moreover, on the compactness branch there is a nonnegative Radon measure
$\mu_{\rm diss}$ such that
\[
 \boxed{
 |\nabla U_j|^2\,\dd y\,\dd s
 \stackrel{*}{\rightharpoonup}
 |\nabla U|^2\,\dd y\,\dd s+\mu_{\rm diss},}
 \tag{NS.20}
\]
and the limiting local-energy ledger contains $\mu_{\rm diss}$ as an
additional positive dissipation term.
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The rescaling gives the viscosity-one equation and the invariant cubic lower
bound.  If a dimensionless packet is unbounded, take the first branch.
Otherwise, the $L^\infty_sL^2_y\cap L^2_sH^1_y$ bounds, the equation, and
Aubin--Lions compactness yield strong local $L^3$ convergence; pressure
oscillation bounds give weak $L^{3/2}_{\rm loc}$ compactness after a
 time-dependent gauge.  Strong convergence passes the nonlinearity and the
cubic lower bound, while weak lower semicontinuity passes suitability.  The
local dissipation measures are weak-* compact; subtracting the absolutely
continuous limit $|\nabla U|^2\dd y\dd s$ gives the positive defect
$\mu_{\rm diss}$.
\end{proof}

\begin{countertheorem}[Nonzero ancient mass is not a singularity certificate]
\label{cth:NS-ancient-nontrivial}
Every nonzero constant vector field on $\R^3\times(-\infty,0]$ is a smooth
ancient suitable Navier--Stokes solution with positive local cubic mass and
zero dissipation defect.  Hence nontriviality of the profile in
\Cref{thm:NS-ancient-profile-alternative} neither proves nor excludes a
singularity.
\end{countertheorem}

\begin{theorem}[Terminal analytic closure and critical-shell radius collapse]
\label{thm:NS-terminal-analytic-radius}
Let $m>5/2$.  If an ancient solution
$U:(-\infty,\epsilon)\to H^m(\R^3)$ is real analytic in time, solves
Navier--Stokes, and satisfies $U(0)=0$, then $U\equiv0$.  Independently, for
the original periodic solution and
$\mathcal G_\sigma(t)=\|e^{\sigma|D|}u(t)\|_2$,
\[
 \boxed{
 \lambda_q^{-1}\|u_q(t)\|_\infty
 \le C\lambda_q^{1/2}e^{-c\sigma\lambda_q}
       \mathcal G_\sigma(t).}
 \tag{NS.21}
\]
Thus a critical shell with
$\lambda_q^{-1}\|u_q\|_\infty\ge c_0\nu$ forces either growth of every fixed
Gevrey stock or
\[
 \boxed{
 \sigma\le\frac1{c\lambda_q}
 \left[\log\!\left(\frac{C\mathcal G_\sigma(t)}{c_0\nu}\right)
       +\frac12\log\lambda_q\right].}
 \tag{NS.22}
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Repeated differentiation of the equation at a zero terminal trace shows that
all time derivatives vanish; real analyticity and the identity theorem give
$U\equiv0$.  On the Fourier support of $u_q$, the Gevrey weight is at least
$e^{c\sigma\lambda_q}$, while Bernstein gives
$\|u_q\|_\infty\le C\lambda_q^{3/2}\|u_q\|_2$.  Combining the two estimates
gives \textup{(NS.21)--(NS.22)}.
\end{proof}

\begin{assessment}[Exact terminal PDE frontier]
A nonzero ancient profile, a finite total dissipation measure, or another
iteration of parabolic rescaling is not a closure theorem.  The terminal
sequence must also be calibrated by
$\nu(T_*-t_j)/R_j^2$: a bounded ratio retains the packet at finite parabolic
distance from the terminal time, whereas a divergent ratio sends it to the
remote past and requires a later replenishment chain.  The remaining
Navier--Stokes inputs are therefore a terminal trace and backward-uniqueness or
epsilon-regularity theorem on the same profile, a monotone scale density that
rules out a nested normalized defect, or an explicit source, boundary, cutoff,
or remote-birth replenishment row.
\end{assessment}

\begin{assessment}[Source-anchored Navier--Stokes globalization]
The heat--time history and the physical endpoint action form a rectangular
source packet.  Transport, viscosity, pressure, output boundary, forward flux,
backscatter, source birth, and chronology must be assembled before the
production current is scalarized; the exact counterflow identity in
\Cref{thm:GT-assembly-before-return-positivity} rules out charging the positive
parts of these rows separately.  A physically graded heat--time stopping front
then either compresses the complete coherent-work source to a bounded cylinder
or returns a genuinely mixed remote source.  On the bounded head, contextual
pressure and router memory are Feshbach shorted before a killed first-return
cylinder is formed.  A strict first-return margin controls repeated
concentration only after the coherent debit is inserted into one local-energy,
viscous, pressure, and open-boundary balance.  Global continuation consequently
requires both finite recurrent-component closure and the source-anchored
cofinal first-passage theorem; a positive history Gram or an instantaneous
strain norm alone supplies neither requirement.
\end{assessment}

\begin{firewall}[The scale boundary must remain open]
\label{fire:NS-open-scale}
The triad source is a higher-grade connected object, but its logarithmic-scale
image is an open-boundary current.  Periodicizing the scale interval can reduce
the minimum transport action by an unbounded factor
\Cref{cth:GT-periodicization}; it is therefore not a harmless character
reformulation.  The unresolved PDE estimate is the comparison of the canonical
open current with the actual viscous and physical-time budget.
\end{firewall}


\begin{firewall}[A positive Schur complement is not the nonlinear estimate]
The Grand Tensor can encode the viscous form, the nonlinear insertion, and
their Schur residual.  Positivity of the ambient response does not imply the
scale-critical inequality in \Cref{thm:NS-relative-form}; proving that
inequality from the actual three-dimensional nonlinearity is the unresolved
PDE theorem.
\end{firewall}

% =============================================================================
\section{Birch--Swinnerton--Dyer: analytic jets, complexes, and determinant lines}
\label{sec:BSD-interface}
% =============================================================================

\begin{definition}[Analytic jet complex]
For an analytic germ $F$ and $m\ge1$, define the two-term finite Hilbert
complex
\[
 \mathcal C_{\rm an}(F,m):
 \qquad 0\longrightarrow\mathscr R_m
 \xrightarrow{\,M_m(F)\,}\mathscr R_m\longrightarrow0,
 \qquad \mathscr R_m=\C[z]/(z^m).
\]
Its determinant line is
\[
 \det H^\bullet(\mathcal C_{\rm an})
 :=\det H^0(\mathcal C_{\rm an})
 \otimes\det H^1(\mathcal C_{\rm an})^{-1}.
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{proposition}[Jet cohomology]
\label{prop:jet-cohomology}
If $r=\ord_0F<m$, then
\[
 \dim H^0(\mathcal C_{\rm an})
 =\dim H^1(\mathcal C_{\rm an})=r.
\]
The product of the nonzero singular values of the differential is
$|a_r|^{m-r}$ when $F(z)=a_rz^r+O(z^{r+1})$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
The kernel statement is \Cref{thm:analytic-jet}.  Since the differential is a
square matrix, its cokernel has the same dimension as its kernel.  The
nonzero-singular-value product is the square root of the pseudodeterminant in
\Cref{thm:analytic-jet}.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Conditional analytic--Selmer determinant-line bridge]
\label{thm:BSD-determinant-bridge}
Let $E/\Q$ be an elliptic curve and let
$F_E(z)=\Lambda(E,1+z)$.  Choose $m>r_{\rm an}(E)$.  Suppose an independently
constructed finite arithmetic Hilbert complex
$\mathcal C_{\rm Sel}(E,m)$ satisfies:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(B\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item its distinguished degree-zero cohomology has dimension
      $r_{\rm alg}(E)$;
\item there is a unitary chain isomorphism
      $U:\mathcal C_{\rm an}(F_E,m)\to\mathcal C_{\rm Sel}(E,m)$;
\item the determinant-line metric and the local period, Tamagawa, torsion, and
      Tate--Shafarevich normalization are identified independently.
\end{enumerate}
Then $r_{\rm an}(E)=r_{\rm alg}(E)$, and the analytic leading-coefficient
magnitude encoded by \Cref{thm:analytic-jet} equals the corresponding
arithmetic determinant-line magnitude.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
A chain isomorphism induces isomorphisms on cohomology.  Hence the degree-zero
cohomology dimensions agree, giving rank equality by
\Cref{prop:jet-cohomology}.  A unitary chain isomorphism identifies the
orthogonal complements of the kernels and preserves every nonzero singular
value of the differential.  It therefore preserves the determinant-line norm
obtained from the product of those singular values.  The third hypothesis
identifies that abstract norm with the independently normalized arithmetic
BSD line, proving the second conclusion.
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[BSD scope]
Placing an analytic jet and a Selmer object in one direct sum is not a chain
comparison.  The arithmetic complex, its local conditions, the period metric,
Tamagawa maps, torsion, and $\Sha$ contribution must be constructed without
using the desired equality.  That construction and the unitary determinant-line
comparison are the unresolved arithmetic content.
\end{firewall}

\section{Hodge conjecture: cycle observability}
\label{sec:Hodge-interface}
% =============================================================================

\begin{theorem}[Hodge cycle-observability equivalence]
\label{thm:Hodge-observability}
Let $X$ be a smooth complex projective variety and fix codimension $p$.  For
rational algebraic cycles $Z_1,\ldots,Z_m$, define
\[
 \mathcal Z_X:\C^m\longrightarrow H_{\rm Hdg}^{2p}(X;\C),
 \qquad
 c\longmapsto\sum_jc_j[Z_j].
\]
The following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2.8em]
\item the classes $[Z_j]$ span the Hodge sector;
\item $\mathcal Z_X$ is surjective;
\item $\mathcal Z_X\mathcal Z_X^*$ is positive definite on the Hodge sector;
\item $\mathcal Z_X\mathcal Z_X^*\succeq c_XI$ for some $c_X>0$.
\end{enumerate}
Thus the Hodge conjecture for $(X,p)$ is equivalent to the existence of a
finite rational-cycle family satisfying these conditions.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Spanning is surjectivity.  In finite dimensions surjectivity of
$\mathcal Z_X$ is equivalent to injectivity of $\mathcal Z_X^*$.  For every
$h$,
\[
 \ip{h}{\mathcal Z_X\mathcal Z_X^*h}=\norm{\mathcal Z_X^*h}^2,
\]
so injectivity is equivalent to positive definiteness, which in finite
dimension is equivalent to a positive least eigenvalue.  A finite rational
spanning family is exactly the fixed-sector Hodge assertion.
\end{proof}


\begin{theorem}[Finite invariants commute with cohomology]
\label{thm:Hodge-invariants-cohomology}
Let a finite group $G$ act by chain maps on a finite-dimensional complex
$(C^\bullet,d)$ over $\C$.  Then
\[
 \boxed{H^k((C^\bullet)^G)\cong H^k(C^\bullet)^G.}
\]
With a $G$-invariant Hilbert structure, the Hodge Laplacian and Green operator
commute with the Reynolds projector, and
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal H^k((C^\bullet)^G)
 =\mathcal H^k(C^\bullet)\cap(C^k)^G.}
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The Reynolds projector $P_G=|G|^{-1}\sum_g g$ commutes with $d$.  It replaces
an invariant cohomology class by an invariant representative and replaces a
primitive of an invariant exact class by an invariant primitive.  With an
invariant metric it also commutes with $d^*$ and therefore with the Hodge
Laplacian and its functional calculus.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Occurrence-shorted invariant semiregularity]
\label{thm:Hodge-occurrence-short}
Let an equivariant obstruction source split into product and occurrence
components,
\[
 \mathcal O^G=\mathcal O_{\rm prod}^G\oplus\mathcal O_{\rm occ}^G,
\]
and let the invariant semiregularity Gram be
\[
 G^{\rm sr}_G
 =\begin{pmatrix}A&B\\B^*&C\end{pmatrix}\succeq0.
\]
If $C$ is faithful on $\mathcal O_{\rm occ}^G$, define
\[
 \boxed{S_G^{\rm sr}:=A-BC^{-1}B^*\succeq0.}
\]
Then the full invariant semiregularity map is injective exactly when
$S_G^{\rm sr}$ is positive definite on $\mathcal O_{\rm prod}^G$.  On failure,
$p\in\Ker S_G^{\rm sr}$ returns the explicit invariant obstruction
\[
 \boxed{p\oplus(-C^{-1}B^*p)\in\Ker G_G^{\rm sr}.}
\]
Thus induction, orbit fusion, or another categorical occurrence construction
must be shorted before positivity of the product zero-character block is used.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Apply the completed-square identity of \Cref{thm:GT-effective-action} to
$G_G^{\rm sr}$.  Its kernel is the graph of the occurrence corrector over
$\Ker S_G^{\rm sr}$, giving both equivalence and witness.
\end{proof}


\begin{firewall}[Harmonic projection is not algebraicity]
Hodge--Dirac shorting reconstructs the harmonic sector, but it does not create
rational algebraic cycles.  The open certificate is the nondegenerate loading
$\mathcal Z_X\mathcal Z_X^*\succeq c_XI$ for an independently specified
cycle family.
\end{firewall}

\section{Complexity: resource-faithful loading}
\label{sec:PvsNP-interface}
% =============================================================================

\begin{countertheorem}[Ambient record dimension does not imply a circuit lower bound]
\label{cth:ambient-dimension-complexity}
Representing all $2^n$ Boolean inputs by orthogonal vectors forces ambient
dimension at least $2^n$, but it implies no superpolynomial circuit lower
bound.
\end{countertheorem}

\begin{proof}
The standard computational basis has dimension $2^n$.  Nevertheless the
identity, parity, and many other explicit functions on that basis have circuits
of polynomial size.  Hence storage dimension alone cannot lower-bound circuit
complexity.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Conditional resource-faithful complexity bridge]
\label{thm:PvsNP-resource-bridge}
Let $L$ be an explicit NP-complete language with Boolean family $f_n$.  Suppose
an independently defined Grand-Tensor loading has a resource functional
$R_n(f)$ satisfying
\[
 \CircuitSize(f)\ge\frac{R_n(f)}{p(n)}
\]
for one polynomial $p$, and suppose $R_n(f_n)$ grows faster than every
polynomial.  Then $L\notin P/{\rm poly}$ and, in particular, $P\ne NP$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The comparison gives superpolynomial circuit size for the explicit family
$f_n$.  Every language in $P$ has polynomial-size circuit families, so $L$ is
not in $P$; the stronger conclusion $L\notin P/{\rm poly}$ follows directly
from the stated circuit lower bound.
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[Algebraic duality need not preserve resources]
A source-minimal realization may be dense even when the primitive process is
sparse, and Schur elimination may create quadratic fill-in.  A complexity
duality must therefore preserve or compare gate count, locality, precision,
communication, memory, separator size, and circuit depth.  Pairwise Grams,
spectra, and exact algebraic equivalence do not supply those bounds.
\end{firewall}

\section{Poincar\'e as a solved scale-flow benchmark}
\label{sec:Poincare-interface}

\begin{proposition}[Perelman benchmark interface]
\label{prop:Poincare-benchmark}
A scale-indexed Grand Tensor can encode a geometrically defined monotone
entropy, canonical-neighbourhood data, no-collapse margins, and surgery jumps.
Perelman's Ricci-flow solution shows that such a package can close a global
geometric problem.  The encoding alone neither reproves Poincar\'e nor
transports those estimates to arithmetic, gauge, fluid, or complexity sectors.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Representing each finite-scale response and each surgery jump as a typed scalar
or operator port is formal.  Monotonicity, canonical-neighbourhood control,
noncollapsing, and summability of the surgery budget are additional geometric
theorems.  Their validity for Ricci flow proves compatibility of the
architecture, not validity in another sector.
\end{proof}

% =============================================================================
\section{Abelian constraints, characters, Smith data, and Gale variables}
\label{sec:abelian-dualities}
% =============================================================================

Let $G$ be a finite abelian group, let
$A:G^n\to G^m$ be a homomorphism, and let
$A^\vee:\widehat{G^m}\to\widehat{G^n}$ be the dual map.  For
$w:G\to\C$, use
$\widehat w(\chi)=\sum_{x\in G}w(x)\chi(x)$.

\begin{theorem}[Finite constraint--character partition duality]
\label{thm:constraint-character}
For arbitrary weights $w_1,\ldots,w_n:G\to\C$ and $b\in G^m$, define
\[
 Z_A(b;w_1,\ldots,w_n)
 =\sum_{\substack{x\in G^n\\Ax=b}}\prod_{j=1}^nw_j(x_j).
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{
 Z_A(b;w_1,\ldots,w_n)
 =\frac1{|G|^m}
 \sum_{\eta\in\widehat{G^m}}
 \eta(-b)\prod_{j=1}^n
 \widehat w_j\bigl((A^\vee\eta)_j\bigr).}
\]
Fourier inversion in $b$ reconstructs either side from the other.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Character orthogonality on $G^m$ gives
\[
 \one_{Ax=b}=\frac1{|G|^m}
 \sum_{\eta\in\widehat{G^m}}\eta(Ax-b).
\]
Since $A^\vee\eta$ is a product character on $G^n$,
$\eta(Ax)=\prod_j(A^\vee\eta)_j(x_j)$.  Insert the orthogonality identity,
exchange the finite sums, and factor the $G^n$ sum into the one-variable
Fourier transforms.  Invertibility is ordinary Fourier inversion on $G^m$.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Exact solution count]
Taking all $w_j=1$ gives
\[
 \#\{x\in G^n:Ax=b\}
 =\begin{cases}
 |\Ker A|,&b\in\Ran A,\\
 0,&b\notin\Ran A.
 \end{cases}
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Only characters in $\Ker A^\vee$, the annihilator of $\Ran A$, survive.
Orthogonality on $G^m/\Ran A$ gives the two cases, and the finite-group
rank--nullity identity supplies the factor $|\Ker A|$.
\end{proof}

Now let $A:\Z^n\to\Z^m$ have rank $r$, and write
$\Torus=\R/\Z$.

\begin{theorem}[Smith--Pontryagin constraint duality]
\label{thm:Smith-Pontryagin}
Let $d_1\mid\cdots\mid d_r$ be the nonzero Smith invariants of $A$.  Then
Pontryagin duality gives the exact sequence
\[
 \boxed{
 0\longrightarrow\widehat{\coker A}
 \longrightarrow\Torus^m
 \xrightarrow{\,A^{\mathsf T}\,}\Torus^n
 \longrightarrow\widehat{\Ker A}
 \longrightarrow0.}
\]
Moreover,
\[
 \widehat{\coker A}
 \cong\Torus^{m-r}\times\mu_{d_1}\times\cdots\times\mu_{d_r},
 \qquad
 \widehat{\Ker A}\cong\Torus^n/A^{\mathsf T}\Torus^m.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Choose unimodular $U,V$ with
$UAV=\diag(d_1,\ldots,d_r,0,\ldots,0)$.  The induced torus maps are
automorphisms, so calculate in Smith coordinates.  A character of $\Z^m$
vanishes on $A\Z^n$ exactly when its first $r$ coordinates lie in
$\mu_{d_i}$ and its remaining coordinates are arbitrary.  This identifies the
kernel of $A^{\mathsf T}$ with $\widehat{\coker A}$.  Multiplication by each
$d_i$ is surjective on $\Torus$, so the cokernel of the torus map is the
quotient $\Torus^n/A^{\mathsf T}\Torus^m$, canonically dual to $\Ker A$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Derived Smith--Gale exact sequence]
\label{thm:Smith-Gale-sequence}
Let $R_q=\Z/q\Z$, let $A_q:R_q^n\to R_q^m$ be reduction modulo $q$, put
$\mathcal L_A=\Ker(A:\Z^n\to\Z^m)$ and
$\mathcal C_A=\coker A$.  Then
\[
 \boxed{
 0\longrightarrow\mathcal L_A/q\mathcal L_A
 \xrightarrow{\rho_q}\Ker A_q
 \xrightarrow{\beta_q}\mathcal C_A[q]
 \longrightarrow0.}
\]
For $\bar x\in\Ker A_q$, choose a lift $x\in\Z^n$ and write $Ax=qy$;
then $\beta_q(\bar x)=[y]$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Replacing $x$ by $x+qz$ replaces $y$ by $y+Az$, so $[y]$ is well defined,
and $q[y]=[Ax]=0$.  If $\ell\in\mathcal L_A$ reduces to zero, write
$\ell=qz$; then $qAz=0$ in the torsion-free group $\Z^m$, so
$z\in\mathcal L_A$, proving injectivity.  If $\beta_q(\bar x)=0$, then
$y=Az$, whence $x-qz\in\mathcal L_A$ and $\bar x$ lies in the image of
$\rho_q$.  Conversely every reduced integral kernel vector maps to zero.
Finally, if $[y]\in\mathcal C_A[q]$, then $qy=Ax$ for some $x$; its reduction
lies in $\Ker A_q$ and maps to $[y]$.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Gale completeness criterion]
\label{cor:Gale-completeness}
The reduction of an integral Gale basis spans $\Ker A_q$ exactly when
$\mathcal C_A[q]=0$, equivalently when $\gcd(d_i,q)=1$ for every Smith
invariant.  It is complete for every $q$ exactly when $\coker A$ is torsion
free.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
By \Cref{thm:Smith-Gale-sequence}, the quotient of $\Ker A_q$ by the reduced
integral kernel is $\mathcal C_A[q]$.  In Smith coordinates, the $q$-torsion of
$\Z/d_i\Z$ has order $\gcd(d_i,q)$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Smith--Gale arithmetic gauge compiler]
\label{thm:Smith-Gale-compiler}
Assume $A_qx=\bar b$ is soluble, choose one solution $x_0$, an integral Gale
basis $B:\Z^{n-r}\to\mathcal L_A$, and a section
$s_q:\mathcal C_A[q]\to\Ker A_q$.  Every solution has a unique form
\[
 x=x_0+B_qy+s_q(t),
 \qquad y\in R_q^{n-r},\quad t\in\mathcal C_A[q].
\]
For arbitrary slot weights $w_j:R_q\to\C$,
\[
 \boxed{
 \sum_{A_qx=\bar b}\prod_jw_j(x_j)
 =\sum_{t\in\mathcal C_A[q]}\sum_{y\in R_q^{n-r}}
 \prod_jw_j(x_{0,j}+\mathbf b_j\!\cdot y+s_q(t)_j),}
\]
where $\mathbf b_j$ is the $j$th row of $B$.  Equivalently,
\[
 \boxed{
 \sum_{A_qx=\bar b}\prod_jw_j(x_j)
 =\frac1{|\operatorname{im}A_q^{\mathsf T}|}
 \sum_{\xi\in\operatorname{im}A_q^{\mathsf T}}
 e_q(-\xi\cdot x_0)\prod_j\widehat w_j(\xi_j).}
\]
Both formulas are independent of the chosen bases and section.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The first decomposition is the choice of a representative in each fibre of
$\beta_q$ in \Cref{thm:Smith-Gale-sequence}; its kernel is the injective image
of $B_q$.  Uniqueness follows from exactness.  For the second formula, the
annihilator of $\Ker A_q$ in the dual of $R_q^n$ is
$\operatorname{im}A_q^{\mathsf T}$.  Hence
\[
 \one_{x-x_0\in\Ker A_q}
 =\frac1{|\operatorname{im}A_q^{\mathsf T}|}
 \sum_{\xi\in\operatorname{im}A_q^{\mathsf T}}e_q(\xi\cdot(x-x_0)).
\]
Insert this identity and factor the coordinate sums.  A basis or section
change only reparametrizes the same fibre, so the total sum is unchanged.
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[Smith transformations are diagnostic]
General Smith column operations mix the original slots.  They classify the
congruence kernel and its dual gauge group, but they need not preserve prime
support, positivity windows, Mellin centres, local types, or resource cost.
All weighted arithmetic formulas must ultimately be pulled back to the
original typed coordinates.
\end{firewall}

% =============================================================================
\section{Nonabelian holonomy, spin networks, and Tannaka reconstruction}
\label{sec:nonabelian-dualities}
% =============================================================================

Let $G$ be a finite group and let $\Gamma=(V,E)$ be a finite oriented graph.
The gauge group $G^V$ acts on $G^E$ by
\[
 (h\cdot g)_e=h_{t(e)}g_eh_{s(e)}^{-1}.
\]


\begin{theorem}[Physical point/fibre connection and magnetic-loop alternative]
\label{thm:GT-point-fibre-holonomy}
Let $K=K^*\succ0$ act on a carrier with an independently readable point
projection
$\mathcal H=\bigoplus_{i\in V}\mathcal H_i$.  On an equal-rank supported edge,
write
\[
 -K_{ji}=V_{j\leftarrow i}A_{j\leftarrow i},
 \qquad V_{j\leftarrow i}\in U(r),
 \qquad A_{j\leftarrow i}\succ0.
\]
The block-local gauge acts by
$V_{j\leftarrow i}\mapsto G_j^*V_{j\leftarrow i}G_i$, and the cycle products
\[
 \boxed{\mathcal W_K(C)=\prod_{e\in C}V_e}
 \tag{HOL.1}
\]
are defined up to conjugacy.  A common block gauge makes every edge transport
the identity if and only if every fundamental-cycle holonomy is $I_r$.

For $\Lambda\ge\lambda_{\max}(K)$, put
$P_\Lambda=I-\Lambda^{-1}K$.  Then
\[
 \boxed{
 \log\det K
 =n\log\Lambda-
 \sum_{m\ge1}\frac1m\Tr(P_\Lambda^m),}
 \tag{HOL.2}
\]
and every trace is a convergent sum of closed-walk amplitudes carrying the
point/fibre holonomy.  On the flat rank-one branch these amplitudes can be
gauged nonnegative; on a nonflat branch they remain signed or complex magnetic
amplitudes.  Even block flatness does not scalarize the positive polar factors
$A_{j\leftarrow i}$; that requires a rank-one point Read or an independently
physical common fibre writer.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Spanning-tree gauge fixing proves the flatness criterion.  The spectrum of
$P_\Lambda$ lies in $[0,1)$, so functional calculus gives \textup{(HOL.2)};
matrix multiplication gives the closed-walk expansion.  Entrywise
nonnegativity is exactly the scalar cycle-sign criterion.  The final statement
follows because positive polar factors are unaffected by trivialization of the
unitary connection.
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[Point algebra and source overlap are prior data]
A positive matrix is diagonal in some basis, so path positivity is vacuous
until a physical point/fibre algebra is fixed.  Conversely, the source-overlap
atlas of \Cref{thm:GT-source-overlap-flatness} does not determine the kinetic
connection.  Point Reads, coherent block tomography, and kinetic transport
are separate physical inputs.
\end{firewall}

\begin{theorem}[Finite holonomy--spin-network decomposition]
\label{thm:spin-network}
The gauge-invariant Hilbert space $L^2(G^E)^{G^V}$ has an orthonormal basis
indexed by:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2.8em]
\item an irreducible unitary representation $\pi_e$ on each edge;
\item at every vertex $v$, an orthonormal basis element of the invariant space
\[
 \operatorname{Inv}_G\!\left(
 \bigotimes_{e:t(e)=v}V_{\pi_e}
 \otimes
 \bigotimes_{e:s(e)=v}V_{\pi_e}^*
 \right).
\]
The corresponding basis functions are obtained by contracting all edge matrix
coefficients with the chosen vertex intertwiners.  Thus full matrix holonomy
histories and spin-network coefficients are related by a unitary transform.
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Finite Peter--Weyl theory gives the unitary bimodule decomposition
\[
 L^2(G)\cong\bigoplus_{\pi\in\widehat G}V_\pi\otimes V_\pi^*.
\]
Tensoring over edges decomposes $L^2(G^E)$ into edge-representation blocks.
At a vertex, the gauge action is the tensor product of the defining action on
incoming representation factors and the dual action on outgoing factors.
Orthogonal projection onto $G^V$ invariants therefore replaces each vertex
factor by its invariant subspace.  Choosing orthonormal bases in those finite
invariant spaces and contracting the representation indices yields an
orthonormal basis.  Completeness follows because the Peter--Weyl decomposition
is complete before projection and orthogonal projection preserves the direct
sum of all invariant blocks.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Closed spin networks separate gauge orbits]
The complete family of spin-network coefficients determines a gauge-invariant
function on $G^E$, and hence separates distinct gauge orbits in the finite
configuration space.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The spin networks are an orthonormal basis of all gauge-invariant functions.
If two orbits had identical values for every basis function, every invariant
function would agree on them.  The indicator of either finite orbit is
invariant, giving a contradiction.
\end{proof}

Let $\omega_G:\Rep(G)\to\operatorname{Hilb}_{\rm fd}$ be the forgetful fibre
functor.

\begin{theorem}[Self-contained finite Tannaka theorem]
\label{thm:finite-Tannaka}
The map
\[
 \boxed{
 G\longrightarrow\Aut^\otimes(\omega_G),
 \qquad g\longmapsto(\rho_V(g))_{V\in\Rep(G)}}
\]
is an isomorphism.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The displayed family is natural and monoidal, and the left regular
representation makes the map injective.  For surjectivity, let
$\eta\in\Aut^\otimes(\omega_G)$ and consider
$\mathcal O(G)=\C^G$ with its left regular action.  Pointwise multiplication
and the unit are intertwiners, so naturality and monoidality make
$\eta_{\mathcal O(G)}$ a unital algebra automorphism of $\C^G$.  It therefore
permutes the primitive idempotents $\delta_x$; write
$\eta\delta_x=\delta_{\sigma(x)}$.  Right translations are intertwiners for
the left regular action, so naturality gives
$\sigma(xh^{-1})=\sigma(x)h^{-1}$.  Hence $\sigma(x)=gx$ for the fixed element
$g=\sigma(e)$.

For any representation $(V,\rho)$ and $\ell\in V^*$, the matrix-coefficient
map
\[
 j_\ell(v)(x)=\ell(\rho(x^{-1})v)
\]
is equivariant.  Naturality gives
$j_\ell(\eta_Vv)=\lambda(g)j_\ell(v)=j_\ell(\rho(g)v)$.  Evaluation at the
identity and variation of $\ell$ yield $\eta_V=\rho(g)$.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Fibre-functor-preserving duality determines the symmetry]
\label{cor:Tannaka-group-iso}
If finite groups $G,H$ admit a symmetric monoidal equivalence
$F:\Rep(G)\to\Rep(H)$ together with a monoidal natural unitary
$\omega_HF\cong\omega_G$, then $G\cong H$.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The equivalence and fibre-functor identification conjugate
$\Aut^\otimes(\omega_G)$ onto $\Aut^\otimes(\omega_H)$.  Apply
\Cref{thm:finite-Tannaka}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Frobenius as tensor holonomy]
Whenever an unramified arithmetic packet assigns to every object of a finite
rigid representation category a natural multiplicative operator compatible
with tensor products, duals, and the fibre functor, that packet is one tensor
automorphism and hence one reconstructed holonomy element of the Tannaka
group.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The compatibility assumptions are precisely the definition of a tensor
automorphism.  Apply \Cref{thm:finite-Tannaka} to a finite group, or the same
reconstruction argument in the finite rigid tensor subcategory generated by
the packet.
\end{proof}

\begin{countertheorem}[Representation dimensions are not a symmetry duality]
The multiset of irreducible representation dimensions does not determine the
symmetry group.
\end{countertheorem}

\begin{proof}
Both $\Z/4\Z$ and $(\Z/2\Z)^2$ have four one-dimensional irreducible
representations, but only the first has an element of order four.
\end{proof}

% =============================================================================
\section{Chain, Hodge--Dirac, and determinant-line duality}
\label{sec:chain-dualities}
% =============================================================================

Let $C_\bullet$ be a bounded chain complex of finitely generated free abelian
groups and put $C^k_{\Torus}=\Hom(C_k,\Torus)$ with
$\delta^k\phi=\phi\circ\partial_{k+1}$.

\begin{theorem}[Cycle--flat-connection Pontryagin duality]
\label{thm:chain-Pontryagin}
There is a canonical isomorphism
\[
 \boxed{
 H^k(C^\bullet_{\Torus},\delta)
 \cong\Hom(H_k(C_\bullet),\Torus).}
\]
If
$H_k\cong\Z^{b_k}\oplus\bigoplus_j\Z/d_{k,j}\Z$, then
\[
 H^k(C^\bullet_{\Torus})
 \cong\Torus^{b_k}\times\prod_j\mu_{d_{k,j}}.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The circle group $\Torus$ is divisible and hence injective in the category of
abelian groups.  Applying $\Hom(-,\Torus)$ to the short exact cycle/boundary
sequences is therefore exact.  The universal-coefficient extension term
vanishes, leaving
$H^k\cong\Hom(H_k,\Torus)$.  Dualizing the displayed decomposition of $H_k$
gives the final formula.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Unitary chain equivalence transports Hodge--Dirac data]
\label{thm:Hodge-Dirac-transport}
Let $(C^\bullet,d)$ and $(C'^\bullet,d')$ be finite Hilbert complexes, and let
$U_k:C^k\to C'^k$ be unitaries satisfying
$U_{k+1}d_k=d'_kU_k$.  Then
\[
 U_k\Delta_k=\Delta'_kU_k,
 \qquad
 \Delta_k=d_{k-1}d_{k-1}^*+d_k^*d_k.
\]
Consequently $U$ identifies harmonic spaces, cohomology, Hodge decompositions,
nonzero singular values, analytic torsion products, and determinant-line
metrics.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Taking adjoints of the chain relation gives
$U_kd_{k-1}^*=d_{k-1}'{}^*U_{k-1}$ and
$U_kd_k^*=d_k'{}^*U_{k+1}$.  Substitution yields the Laplacian intertwining.
Its kernel is the harmonic space, canonically isomorphic to cohomology.  A
unitary intertwiner preserves orthogonal ranges, singular values, and the
products and exterior powers from which torsion and determinant-line metrics
are constructed.
\end{proof}

\begin{countertheorem}[Cohomology rank does not determine the determinant line]
\label{cth:cohomology-rank-not-determinant}
Two finite complexes may have equal cohomology dimensions and unequal
nonzero-singular-value products.
\end{countertheorem}

\begin{proof}
For $c>0$, consider the two-term complex
$0\to\C\xrightarrow{c}\C\to0$.  Its cohomology vanishes for every $c$, but
the unique nonzero singular value is $c$.  Choosing different $c$ changes the
determinant-line metric and torsion while preserving cohomology rank.
\end{proof}
