\section{Renewal spectralization and the category-dependent relation to noncommutative geometry}
\label{sec:renewal-NCG-spectralization}
% =============================================================================

The history algebra and its regular-trace GNS representation are outputs of the
Grand-Tensor reconstruction.  They do not, by themselves, determine a metric
operator.  A spectral triple becomes canonical only after one physical
first-order differential packet has occurred on the same history carrier.  The
resulting relation with noncommutative geometry has two logically different
parts: a source-native forward construction and an inverse essential-image
problem whose answer depends on the chosen cutoff category.

\subsection{Finite differential packets and canonical real even spectralization}

Let $\mathcal A$ be a finite-dimensional unital $C^*$-algebra, let
$m:\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal A\to\mathcal A$ be multiplication, and put
\[
 \Omega_u^1(\mathcal A)=\Ker m,
 \qquad
 \dd_u a=\one\otimes a-a\otimes\one.
 \tag{SP.1}
\]
The canonical conjugate-linear reversal is
\[
 \left(\sum_i a_i\otimes b_i\right)^\natural
 =-\sum_i b_i^*\otimes a_i^*.
 \tag{SP.2}
\]

\begin{definition}[Admissible renewal differential packet]
\label{def:GT-NCG-differential-packet}
Let $\tau$ be a faithful tracial state on $\mathcal A$.  An admissible renewal
differential Gram is a positive semidefinite Hermitian form $Q$ on
$\Omega_u^1(\mathcal A)$ such that
\[
 \boxed{
 \begin{aligned}
 Q(a\omega,\eta)&=Q(\omega,a^*\eta),\\
 Q(\omega b,\eta)&=Q(\omega,\eta b^*),\\
 Q(\omega^\natural,\eta^\natural)&=Q(\eta,\omega).
 \end{aligned}}
 \tag{SP.3}
\]
Its source-minimal one-form carrier and derivation are
\[
 \mathcal H_1(Q)=\Omega_u^1(\mathcal A)/\mathcal N_Q,
 \qquad
 \mathcal N_Q=\{\omega:Q(\omega,\omega)=0\},
 \qquad
 \partial_Qa=[\dd_u a].
 \tag{SP.4}
\]
Left and right multiplication induce commuting $*$-representations
$\lambda$ and $\rho$ on $\mathcal H_1(Q)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Finite differential occurrence compiler]
\label{thm:GT-NCG-differential-occurrence}
Suppose a physically occurring tangent packet on the represented history
algebra gives a linear map $\delta:\mathcal A\to\mathcal K$, commuting left and
right $*$-representations $\lambda_{\mathcal K},\rho_{\mathcal K}$, and an
antiunitary reversal $C_{\mathcal K}$.  On any basis
$a_0=\one,a_1,\ldots,a_{n-1}$ define
\[
 \Delta_{\rm un}=\|\delta(\one)\|^2,
\]
\[
 \Delta_{\rm Leib}
 =\sum_{i,j}\|\delta(a_ia_j)
 -\lambda_{\mathcal K}(a_i)\delta(a_j)
 -\rho_{\mathcal K}(a_j)\delta(a_i)\|^2,
\]
\[
 \Delta_*=\sum_i\|\delta(a_i^*)-C_{\mathcal K}\delta(a_i)\|^2.
 \tag{SP.5}
\]
After the word-descent residual
$\Tr((I-HH^\dagger)G)$ of
\Cref{thm:GT-word-localizer-descent} has vanished, the following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(D\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item $\Delta_{\rm un}=\Delta_{\rm Leib}=\Delta_*=0$;
\item $\delta$ is a star-compatible bimodule derivation;
\item there is a unique bimodule map
      $T_\delta:\Omega_u^1(\mathcal A)\to\mathcal K$ satisfying
      $T_\delta\dd_u=\delta$ and
      $T_\delta(\omega^\natural)=C_{\mathcal K}T_\delta\omega$.
\end{enumerate}
On this branch
\[
 \boxed{Q_\delta(\omega,\eta)
 =\langle T_\delta\omega,T_\delta\eta\rangle}
 \tag{SP.6}
\]
is admissible, and its source-minimal carrier is unitarily
$\overline{\Ran T_\delta}$.  A positive residual in \textup{(SP.5)} is an
explicit finite obstruction to promoting the tangent to a first-order
spectral differential.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Vanishing on a basis gives the unit, Leibniz, and star identities everywhere by
bilinearity.  The universal property of $\Omega_u^1(\mathcal A)$ gives the
unique map $T_\delta$; explicitly,
$T_\delta(\sum_i a_i\otimes b_i)=
\sum_i\lambda_{\mathcal K}(a_i)\delta(b_i)$ on $\Ker m$.  The bimodule and
reversal identities make \textup{(SP.6)} satisfy \textup{(SP.3)}.  Its null
space is $\Ker T_\delta$, so the first isomorphism theorem gives the
source-minimal unitary.  Word descent is logically prior because a tangent
which does not annihilate a zero history word is not a map on the reconstructed
algebra.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Canonical finite real even spectralization]
\label{thm:GT-NCG-finite-spectralization}
Every packet of \Cref{def:GT-NCG-differential-packet} canonically determines
\[
 \mathcal H_Q=L^2(\mathcal A,\tau)\oplus\mathcal H_1(Q),
 \qquad
 \pi_Q(a)=L_a\oplus\lambda(a),
 \tag{SP.7}
\]
\[
 \boxed{
 D_Q=\begin{pmatrix}0&\partial_Q^*\\ \partial_Q&0\end{pmatrix},
 \qquad
 \gamma_Q=\begin{pmatrix}I&0\\0&-I\end{pmatrix}.}
 \tag{SP.8}
\]
It is an even finite spectral triple.  If
$B_a:L^2(\mathcal A,\tau)\to\mathcal H_1(Q)$ is
$B_ab=(\partial_Qa)b$, then
\[
 \boxed{
 [D_Q,\pi_Q(a)]
 =\begin{pmatrix}0&-B_{a^*}^*\\B_a&0\end{pmatrix}.}
 \tag{SP.9}
\]
For $a=a^*$,
\[
 \boxed{L_Q(a):=\|[D_Q,\pi_Q(a)]\|=\|B_a\|,}
 \tag{SP.10}
\]
and $L_Q$ defines a finite Connes metric exactly when
$\Ker\partial_Q=\C\one$.

The antiunitary
\[
 J_Q(a\oplus[\omega])=a^*\oplus[\omega^\natural]
 \tag{SP.11}
\]
implements the opposite representation
\[
 \boxed{\pi_Q^o(b)=R_b\oplus\rho(b)}
 \tag{SP.12}
\]
and satisfies the order-zero and first-order identities
\[
 [\pi_Q(a),\pi_Q^o(b)]=0,
 \qquad
 [[D_Q,\pi_Q(a)],\pi_Q^o(b)]=0.
 \tag{SP.13}
\]
Thus $(\mathcal A,\mathcal H_Q,D_Q,J_Q,\gamma_Q)$ is a real even finite
spectral triple with the algebraic KO-sign pattern
$(J^2,JD-DJ,J\gamma-\gamma J)=(+1,0,0)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The quotient identities in \textup{(SP.3)} make $\lambda$ a
$*$-representation.  All spaces are finite dimensional, so $D_Q$ is
self-adjoint with compact resolvent.  The Leibniz rule gives
$(\partial_QL_a-\lambda(a)\partial_Q)b=(\partial_Qa)b$, and taking adjoints
gives \textup{(SP.9)}.  The seminorm and kernel statements follow because
$B_a\one=\partial_Qa$.

Traciality makes $a\mapsto a^*$ antiunitary on $L^2(\mathcal A,\tau)$, while
\textup{(SP.3)} makes reversal antiunitary on one-forms.  Reversal interchanges
left and right actions, proving \textup{(SP.12)}.  The two module actions
commute, and $B_a$ is right $\mathcal A$-linear, which proves
\textup{(SP.13)}.  The grading statements are immediate from the block form.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Functoriality and the unavoidable differential-scale row]
\label{thm:GT-NCG-functor-scale}
Trace-preserving $*$-isomorphisms which isometrically transport $Q$ induce
unitaries intertwining $\pi,D,J,$ and $\gamma$; hence finite spectralization is
a functor from differential Renewal packets to real even finite spectral
triples.

However, for every $s>0$, the Gram $Q_s=s^2Q$ has the same algebra, trace,
word relations, bimodule, and reversal, while
\[
 \boxed{D_{Q_s}\simeq sD_Q,
 \qquad L_{Q_s}=sL_Q,
 \qquad d_{Q_s}=s^{-1}d_Q.}
 \tag{SP.14}
\]
The structural Grand Tensor alone therefore does not select the Dirac scale.
One physical clock, action, carr\'e-du-champ, or equivalent absolute differential
calibration is indispensable.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Naturality of the universal derivation and preservation of the quotient Gram
produce the intertwining unitaries.  For scaling, the map
$[\omega]_{Q_s}\mapsto s[\omega]_Q$ is unitary and sends
$\partial_{Q_s}$ to $s\partial_Q$, giving \textup{(SP.14)}.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Stationary renewal graphs, metric recovery, and spectral fibres}

\begin{theorem}[Canonical graph Hodge--Dirac spectralization]
\label{thm:GT-NCG-graph-spectralization}
Let $V$ be finite, $m_x>0$, and let
$k_{xy}\ge0$ be stationary renewal rates with flux
$q_{xy}=m_xk_{xy}$.  Put
\[
 c_{xy}=\frac{q_{xy}+q_{yx}}2,
 \qquad
 j_{xy}=\frac{q_{xy}-q_{yx}}2,
 \tag{SP.15}
\]
and assume the undirected support of $c$ is connected.  On
$\mathcal H_0=\ell^2(V,m)$ and
$\mathcal H_1=\ell^2(E^{\rm or},c)$ define
\[
 (\partial f)(x,y)=f(y)-f(x).
 \tag{SP.16}
\]
The corresponding spectralization satisfies
\[
 \boxed{D_{m,c}^2|_{\mathcal H_0}=\partial^*\partial=-2\mathcal L_s,}
 \tag{SP.17}
\]
where $\mathcal L_s=(\mathcal L+\mathcal L^\dagger)/2$, and
\[
 \boxed{
 L_{m,c}(f)^2
 =\max_{x\in V}\frac1{m_x}
   \sum_yc_{xy}|f(y)-f(x)|^2.}
 \tag{SP.18}
\]
The seminorm kernel is exactly the constants.  On the explicit periodic
$A_3$ regulators of
\Cref{cor:relational-flat-vacuum,thm:relational-deSitter-branch}, the pure-state
Connes distance obeys
\[
 \boxed{
 \sup_{x,y}|d_{D_h}(x,y)-d_{g_0}(x,y)|\longrightarrow0}
 \tag{SP.19}
\]
on the flat branch, while on every compact de~Sitter time slab
\[
 \boxed{
 L_{h,t}=e^{-Ht}L_{h,0},
 \qquad
 d_{h,t}=e^{Ht}d_{h,0},}
 \tag{SP.20}
\]
and $d_{h,t}$ converges uniformly to the slice metric of
$g(t)=e^{2Ht}g_0$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Stationarity makes $\mathcal L_s$ the reversible generator with rates
$c_{xy}/m_x$.  Hence
\[
 -\langle f,\mathcal L_sf\rangle_m
 =\frac12\sum_{x,y}c_{xy}|f(y)-f(x)|^2
 =\frac12\|\partial f\|_1^2,
\]
which gives \textup{(SP.17)} by polarization.  The lower commutator block is
$(B_fg)(x,y)=(f(y)-f(x))g(x)$; its operator norm relative to
$\sum_xm_x|g(x)|^2$ is the maximum in \textup{(SP.18)}.

For the periodic $A_3$ packet, the twelve roots form a tight frame,
$\frac18\sum_\alpha|\alpha\cdot v|^2=|v|^2$.  Smooth functions therefore have
discrete seminorm converging uniformly to $\|\nabla f\|_\infty$.  Conversely,
discrete unit-seminorm functions, normalized at one vertex, have uniformly
Lipschitz piecewise-affine interpolants; compactness and the tight-frame
identity force every limit to be one-Lipschitz.  Applying these two bounds to
the dual distance formula proves \textup{(SP.19)}.  Substitution of the
curved masses and rates gives $L_{h,t}^2=e^{-2Ht}L_{h,0}^2$, and the dual
formula gives \textup{(SP.20)}.
\end{proof}

\begin{countertheorem}[Universal one-step graph forms need not have a compact-resolvent limit]
\label{cth:GT-NCG-extensive-oneform-kernel}
If a connected graph has $n$ vertices and $e$ undirected edges and both edge
orientations are retained, then
\[
 \boxed{\dim\Ker D_{m,c}=2e-n+2.}
 \tag{SP.21}
\]
For the periodic $A_3$ root graph, $e=6n$ and the nullity is $11n+2$.
Therefore the unreduced universal one-form carrier cannot converge directly to
a compact-resolvent spectral triple as $n\to\infty$.  A physical face/cell
differential, spinor reduction, quotient, or other source-native removal of the
extensive null sector is a separate continuum certificate.
\end{countertheorem}

\begin{proof}
Connectedness gives $\dim\Ker\partial=1$ and $\rank\partial=n-1$.
The directed one-form space has dimension $2e$, so
$\dim\Ker\partial^*=2e-n+1$.  Since
$\Ker D=\Ker\partial\oplus\Ker\partial^*$, \textup{(SP.21)} follows.  The
resolvent equals the identity on this growing kernel and therefore cannot be
compact in a limit retaining all of it.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Graph spectral universality fibre]
\label{thm:GT-NCG-graph-fibre}
Fix a connected graph $G=(V,E)$, masses $m$, and positive conductances $c$.
Choose one orientation of each edge and let $B:\R^E\to\R^V$ be the incidence
matrix.  The stationary renewal laws with the same graph spectralization are
exactly
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal J(G,c)
 =\{j\in\Ker B:|j_e|<c_e\},}
 \tag{SP.22}
\]
through
\[
 \boxed{q_{xy}=c_{xy}+j_{xy},
 \qquad k_{xy}=\frac{c_{xy}+j_{xy}}{m_x}.}
 \tag{SP.23}
\]
The fibre dimension is
\[
 \boxed{\dim\mathcal J(G,c)=|E|-|V|+1=b_1(G).}
 \tag{SP.24}
\]
It is trivial exactly for a tree.  Within one nontrivial fibre the steady
entropy production
\[
 \boxed{
 \sigma(j)=2\sum_{e\in E}j_e
 \log\frac{c_e+j_e}{c_e-j_e}}
 \tag{SP.25}
\]
varies and vanishes only at $j=0$.  Spectralization therefore forgets genuine
nonequilibrium circulation.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The stationarity equation for $q=c+j$ is $Bj=0$, while positivity of both
directed rates is $|j_e|<c_e$.  Conversely, every stationary law has the unique
decomposition into symmetric and antisymmetric fluxes.  The Hodge--Dirac
operator depends only on $m$ and $c$, proving equality of the spectral images.
For connected $G$, $\rank B=|V|-1$, which gives \textup{(SP.24)}.  Pairing the
two directions of each edge in the standard stationary entropy-production
formula gives \textup{(SP.25)}.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Inverse realization and category-dependent essential images}

\begin{definition}[Marked, strong, and strict spectralization categories]
\label{def:GT-NCG-image-categories}
The inverse Renewal--spectral problem is considered in three distinct
categories.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(C\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item In the \emph{finite marked category}, a finite target-specific reference
      leg, calibrated operation family, grading mark, and conjugate port may be
      physically included and then audited by the complete word panel.
\item In the \emph{strong compact category}, finite spectral screens converge
      strongly on every fixed source vector, resolvent, commutator, and finite
      matrix coefficient; norm multiplicativity is not required.
\item In the \emph{strict norm-monoidal category}, the finite compressions must
      transport products in norm.  A compact-resolvent packet is
      \emph{spectrally quasidiagonal} when there are finite-rank projections
      $P_n\uparrow I$ with
      \[
       \boxed{P_nD=DP_n,
       \qquad \|[P_n,\pi(a)]\|\to0}
       \tag{SP.26}
      \]
      for every element of a dense spectral algebra, and equivariantly for
      $J$ and $\gamma$ when declared.
\end{enumerate}
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Essential-image trichotomy]
\label{thm:GT-NCG-essential-image-trichotomy}
The spectralization functor has the following exact category-dependent images.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(I\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item Every finite spectral packet has a finite marked Renewal realization.
\item Every separable compact-resolvent spectral packet is a strong cofinal
      marked Renewal limit obtained from finite spectral screens.
\item The strict norm-monoidal image is exactly the spectrally quasidiagonal
      subclass and is proper.
\end{enumerate}
For compressions $\phi_n(a)=P_n\pi(a)P_n$, the strict criterion is equivalently
\[
 \boxed{\|\phi_n(ab)-\phi_n(a)\phi_n(b)\|\to0,}
 \tag{SP.27}
\]
because
\[
 \phi_n(ab)-\phi_n(a)\phi_n(b)
 =P_n\pi(a)(I-P_n)\pi(b)P_n.
 \tag{SP.28}
\]
The Toeplitz number-operator triple gives an explicit target outside the strict
image but inside the strong image.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
For a finite packet, realize its faithful represented algebra by finitely many
controlled unitary operations on a selected reference corner.  A calibrated
unitary curve reconstructs its self-adjoint $D$ as an actual tangent; positive
commutator Grams give the source-minimal one-form carrier; controlled grading
and conjugate-port operations reconstruct $\gamma$ and $J$.  Finite comb
tomography and support reduction then produce a legitimate marked Grand Tensor
whose selected spectral image is the target.

For a separable compact-resolvent packet, let $P_n$ be increasing finite
spectral projections of $D$.  They commute with $D$ and converge strongly to
$I$.  Every fixed product defect in \textup{(SP.28)} tends strongly to zero,
and the finite marked construction applies on each screen.  This proves strong
essential surjectivity.

If \textup{(SP.26)} holds, \textup{(SP.28)} gives norm multiplicativity.  In
the converse direction, applying \textup{(SP.27)} to $(a^*,a)$ shows that
$\|(I-P_n)\pi(a)P_n\|\to0$; applying it to $a^*$ gives the opposite off-diagonal
block, hence \textup{(SP.26)}.  Thus the strict image is precisely the stated
class.

For properness, take the unilateral shift $S$ on $\ell^2(\N)$ and the number
operator $Ne_k=ke_k$.  The Toeplitz algebra generated by $S$ with $D=N$ has
compact resolvent and bounded commutator $[N,S]=S$.  Every finite-rank
projection commuting with $N$ is diagonal; any nonzero finite diagonal screen
has a last occupied basis vector, across which $[P,S]$ has norm one.  Hence no
sequence satisfies \textup{(SP.26)}, although the standard initial-segment
screens converge strongly and give the strong realization.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Precise meaning of spectral geometry downstream of Renewal geometry]
\label{cor:GT-NCG-downstream-meaning}
In the marked strong compact category, noncommutative spectral geometry is an
essentially surjective quotient of Renewal geometry: every separable compact
spectral triple has a Renewal preimage, and the inverse fibre can retain
commutant anchors, cycle currents, endpoint scales, and readable provenance
which the spectral target forgets.  In the strict norm-monoidal category,
Renewal geometry instead imposes a genuine selection rule.  Neither statement
says that one fixed austere physical Renewal source dynamically selects every
target.
\end{corollary}

\subsection{The austere finite image, anchors, and resource growth}

\begin{definition}[Compatible commutant anchor space]
\label{def:GT-NCG-commutant-anchor}
For a finite spectral packet
$\mathsf S=(\mathcal A,\mathcal H,\pi,D,J,\gamma)$ define the real vector space
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathfrak c_{\mathsf S}
 =\{C\in\pi(\mathcal A)'_{\rm sa}:
 C\gamma+\gamma C=0,
 \ JC=\varepsilon'CJ\}.}
 \tag{SP.29}
\]
Omit the corresponding linear condition when $J$ or $\gamma$ is not part of
the packet.  Let $P_{\mathfrak c_{\mathsf S}}$ be Hilbert--Schmidt projection
onto this space and put
\[
 D_{\rm der}=D-P_{\mathfrak c_{\mathsf S}}D,
 \qquad q_{\mathsf S}=\dim_{\R}\mathfrak c_{\mathsf S}.
 \tag{SP.30}
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Exact derivation-only image and sharp anchor rank]
\label{thm:GT-NCG-austere-image}
Among self-adjoint operators with the declared grading and reality signs which
implement the same derivation $[D,\pi(\,\cdot\,)]$, the complete solution set is
\[
 \boxed{D+\mathfrak c_{\mathsf S}.}
 \tag{SP.31}
\]
The centered operator $D_{\rm der}$ is the unique minimum-Hilbert--Schmidt-norm
representative.  Consequently the exact image of a derivation-only finite
Renewal source is the centered class
\[
 \boxed{P_{\mathfrak c_{\mathsf S}}D=0.}
 \tag{SP.32}
\]
An arbitrary finite target is recovered from this austere image by exactly
$q_{\mathsf S}$ independent calibrated scalar anchors; fewer leave a nonzero
affine fibre.  No fixed finite resource budget is essentially surjective onto
all finite spectral triples, although the union over all finite marked budgets
is.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Two implementers of the same commutator derivation differ by a self-adjoint
operator in $\pi(\mathcal A)'$.  Subtracting the grading and reality equations
places the difference in $\mathfrak c_{\mathsf S}$, and every element of that
space preserves all commutators and declared linear signs.  Orthogonal
projection gives
\[
 \|D+C\|_{\rm HS}^2
 =\|D_{\rm der}\|_{\rm HS}^2
  +\|P_{\mathfrak c_{\mathsf S}}D+C\|_{\rm HS}^2,
\]
proving the centered assertion.  A scalar anchor bank is a real linear map from
$\mathfrak c_{\mathsf S}$; injectivity requires and is achieved by
$q_{\mathsf S}$ coordinates.  Finally, any fixed Hilbert, algebra, operation,
one-form, record, or word-depth budget excludes finite matrix packets of
sufficiently large dimension, whereas every individual finite packet has a
finite marked realization by
\Cref{thm:GT-NCG-essential-image-trichotomy}.
\end{proof}


\subsection{Loaded Euclidean/OS landing and terminal differential incidence}
\label{subsec:GT-NCG-loaded-landing}

The abstract spectralization functor and its essential-image theorems answer
which differential packets admit Renewal realizations.  The loaded
Einstein--Standard-Model branch asks a stronger same-history question: whether
one finite cylinder carries the coefficient, reflection, fermion words, marked
OS quotient, and local line data together.  The conditional Gaussian and
field-shell constructions already provide all of the finite algebra needed for
that audit.

\begin{definition}[Finite loaded Euclidean spectral packet]
\label{def:GT-NCG-loaded-Euclidean-packet}
At cutoff \(X\), a finite loaded Euclidean packet is
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathfrak P_X^{\rm Euc}
 =\bigl(
 \Lambda_X,\mathcal K_X,\Theta_X,H_{X,+},P_X,\ell_X,
 \pi_X,J_X,\gamma_X,\{\mathbb W_X^{(n)}\}_{n\ge0}
 \bigr).}
 \tag{SP.33}
\]
Here \(\Lambda_X\) is one nonzero unnormalized same-history cylinder,
\(\mathcal K_X\) is the completely assembled spacetime--Hodge--gauge--Higgs--
Yukawa--boundary coefficient, \(\Theta_X\) is physical reflection,
\(P_X=P_X^*\) is the reflected positive-time covariance with scalar line
weight \(\ell_X\), and \(\pi_X,J_X,\gamma_X\) are the represented operation,
real, and grading structures.  The word kernels retain the vacuum grade.  A
packet is conditionally quasi-free when
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathbb W_X^{(n)}=\ell_X\bigwedge^nP_X}
 \tag{SP.34}
\]
for every word in the frozen finite grammar, with at least one direct higher
word held outside construction of \(P_X\).
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Finite common-history Euclidean/OS spectral landing]
\label{thm:GT-NCG-finite-Euclidean-landing}
For a packet of \Cref{def:GT-NCG-loaded-Euclidean-packet}, assume:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(L\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item every displayed row occurs on the one cylinder \(\Lambda_X\), and the
      complete time-split coefficient is assembled before any Feshbach
      elimination;
\item the physical reflected hopping block yields \(\ell_X\ge0\) and
      \(P_X\succeq0\);
\item the frozen exterior word grammar satisfies \textup{(SP.34)} and its
      held-out word has zero Wick/Pfaffian excess;
\item every generator of \(\pi_X\), together with \(J_X\) and \(\gamma_X\),
      preserves the OS null and satisfies the declared order-zero, first-order,
      grading, and reality identities modulo that null;
\item the local Berezin section, positive modulus, divisor order, and declared
      zero-mode exterior insertion are populated.
\end{enumerate}
Then the packet reconstructs one source-minimal finite OS carrier on which the
represented algebra, grading, and real structure descend exactly.  If
\(r_X=\rank P_X\), the source-minimal one-particle and fermion carriers are
\[
 \boxed{
 H_{X,+}^{\min}=\Ran P_X,
 \qquad
 \mathcal F_{X,-}^{\min}
 =\bigoplus_{n=0}^{r_X}\bigwedge^n\Ran P_X,}
 \tag{SP.35}
\]
and \(\dim\mathcal F_{X,-}^{\min}=2^{r_X}\).  The complete marked landing is
unique up to the unitary fixing the common source vectors.  Conversely, every
such landed packet makes the five displayed finite residual families vanish.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Complete assembly and the supported Feshbach identity give the physical
one-particle covariance.  The exterior positivity and rank theorems
\Cref{thm:SMQG-exterior-positivity,cor:SMQG-exterior-rank} give the minimum
fermion carrier.  The held-out row is the direct Gaussian-occurrence audit.
OS-null invariance and the marked relations give well-defined quotient
operators, while the zero-safe line calculus retains the local section at a
divisor.  Every step is a supported Gram quotient, so equality of the complete
marked Grams gives the common source-fixing unitary.  The converse follows by
reading each condition from the landed carrier.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Nonempty finite loaded spectral branch]
\label{cor:GT-NCG-finite-landing-nonempty}
The finite field shell together with its conditional reflected fermion slab,
and in particular the projective regulator of
\Cref{thm:RPESM-population}, provides a nonempty family satisfying
\Cref{thm:GT-NCG-finite-Euclidean-landing}.  Thus finite active
Euclidean/OS spectral landing is an exact finite-sector theorem.  Historical
reuse by the old Store and a cofinal oriented determinant/Pfaffian line remain
stronger statements.
\end{corollary}

The terminal differential row is stricter.  A deterministic coefficient can
occur in the Euclidean action without being the generator of an actual
shrinking channel family on the same represented algebra.

\begin{definition}[Terminal same-history differential demand]
\label{def:GT-NCG-terminal-germ}
Let \(S_X:E_X^{\rm phys}\to\mathcal K_X^{\rm phys}\) synthesize the actual
source-minimal rows of the finite landed packet, including any reflected field
semigroup supplied by the loaded regulator.  A terminal differential demand
requires same-carrier CPTP curves
\[
 \Phi_{X,+}(t),\qquad\Phi_{X,-}(t),\qquad
 \Phi_{X,\pm}(0)=\id,
\]
with calibrated physical duration and common source gauge, such that
\[
 \mathcal L_X^{\rm germ}
 =\lim_{t\downarrow0}
   \frac{\Phi_{X,+}(t)-\Phi_{X,-}(t)}{2t}
 =-i[D_X^{\rm germ},\,\cdot\,]
 \tag{SP.36}
\]
on the represented operation core and
\[
 \boxed{D_X^{\rm germ}=D_X^{\rm coeff}}
 \tag{SP.37}
\]
modulo the already classified compatible commutant anchor.  Let \(B_X^{[0]}\)
be the finite landed target bank and let \(B_X^{[1]}\) append this germ and its
mixed incidence rows.  Define
\[
 \boxed{
 R_X^{[k]}
 =(B_X^{[k]})^*(I-P_{S_X})B_X^{[k]},
 \qquad
 P_{S_X}=S_X(S_X^*S_X)^\dagger S_X^*.}
 \tag{SP.38}
\]
The terminal audit stops at the first nonzero prefix short.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Static coefficient and reflected Markov dynamics do not imply the terminal germ]
\label{thm:GT-NCG-static-no-germ}
Neither a finite set of static channel values nor occurrence of a deterministic
Euclidean coefficient determines \(\mathcal L_X^{\rm germ}\).  Moreover, the
self-adjoint reflected Markov generator of
\Cref{thm:RPESM-reflected-slab} supplies the symmetric OS time-translation
operator on the field algebra, but does not by itself supply an antisymmetric
inner derivation on the represented fermion operation algebra or the incidence
\textup{(SP.37)}.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Given any smooth channel path \(\Phi_t\), any Hermitian \(H\), and finitely many
nonzero sample times, choose a smooth real function \(f\) vanishing at all
sample times with \(f(0)=0\) and \(f'(0)=1\).  Then
\[
 \widetilde\Phi_t=\Ad_{e^{-if(t)H}}\circ\Phi_t
\]
has the same acquired static values but
\[
 \dot{\widetilde\Phi}_0
 =\dot\Phi_0-i[H,\,\cdot\,].
\]
Thus the derivative and its Hamiltonian component require a differentiated
same-history panel.  The RPESM generator is self-adjoint on \(L^2(\mu_X)\);
its forward and reflected Markov dynamics therefore determine the symmetric
OS Hamiltonian.  No theorem identifies that commutative field generator with
the inner derivation of \(D_X^{\rm coeff}\) on \(\pi_X(\mathcal A_X)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[First terminal short and source-minimal germ witness]
\label{thm:GT-NCG-terminal-short}
For the presently populated relational packet,
\[
 \boxed{R_X^{[0]}=0.}
 \tag{SP.39}
\]
Choose \(a_*\) in the landed operation algebra with
\([D_X^{\rm coeff},\pi_X(a_*)]\ne0\), and choose a Hilbert--Schmidt unit test
\(C_*\) detecting the nonzero commutator.  Let \(b_{\delta,X}\) be the normalized
one-dimensional target source corresponding to
\[
 q_{\delta,X}
 =\left\langle C_*,
 \mathcal L_X^{\rm germ}(\pi_X(a_*))\right\rangle_{\HS}.
\]
Until a same-carrier differentiated channel panel and its mixed incidence Gram
are supplied, this target is outside the actual source range and
\[
 \boxed{
 r_{\delta,X}
 =b_{\delta,X}^*(I-P_{S_X})b_{\delta,X}>0,
 \qquad \rank r_{\delta,X}=1.}
 \tag{SP.40}
\]
Consequently the complete terminal short is nonzero and has rank at least one.
The exact source-minimal first missing direction is
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal N_{\delta,X}
 =\Ran\bigl((I-P_{S_X})b_{\delta,X}\bigr).}
 \tag{SP.41}
\]
The rank-one statement is the exact rank of the fixed witness query, not an
upper bound on the source rank of the full differentiated channel panel.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The zero prefix is \Cref{thm:GT-NCG-finite-Euclidean-landing}.  The target
query in \textup{(SP.40)} belongs to the noncommutative antisymmetric germ and
its incidence with \(D_X^{\rm coeff}\).  The actual packet contains the finite
coefficient and a symmetric reflected field generator, but no same-carrier
source row implementing this query or identifying the two operators.  Hence
its normalized source vector has a nonzero orthogonal component.  A nonzero
positive Gram on a one-dimensional coefficient space has rank one, and its
range is exactly \textup{(SP.41)}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Exact upstream germ packet and rerun rule]
\label{cor:GT-NCG-germ-handoff}
To close the first terminal short one must append, on the same active cylinder
and source gauge:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(G\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item direct forward and reflected/reverse CPTP rows at two nested physical
      times together with the identity row;
\item the duration calibration and its adjacent-cutoff transport;
\item the complete mixed source Gram with the coefficient, reflection, OS, and
      memory source bank;
\item Hamiltonian-lineality, reversal, source-core, and held-out smaller-time
      residuals;
\item the incidence \(D_X^{\rm germ}=D_X^{\rm coeff}\) modulo the compatible
      commutant anchor.
\end{enumerate}
After appending the polar innovations of this panel, the prefix closes exactly
when \((B_X^{[1]})^*(I-P_{S_X^+})B_X^{[1]}=0\).  Only then is the audit
continued to the global graph/form domain, determinant-line connection, real
Pfaffian orientation, and adjacent-cutoff marked transport.
\end{corollary}

\begin{firewall}[No downstream substitution for the differential incidence]
\label{fire:GT-NCG-no-downstream-substitution}
A finite Dirac coefficient, a symmetric OS Hamiltonian, a determinant-line
orientation, a cofinal Euclidean measure, or a Lorentzian local net cannot
manufacture the missing same-history inner germ.  Conversely, populating that
germ does not orient the Pfaffian line or prove continuum transport.  The
ordered compiler is rerun from the first newly populated row.
\end{firewall}


\begin{firewall}[Three operators and two notions of reality]
\label{fire:GT-NCG-operator-separation}
The geometric Hodge--Dirac operator $D_{\rm geom}$, the internal finite operator
$D_F$, and the Osterwalder--Schrader Hamiltonian $H_{\rm OS}$ are distinct.
The first controls spatial commutator geometry and squares to a symmetric
renewal generator; the second controls grading-changing internal masses and
Yukawa incidence; the third generates positive reflected Euclidean time
translation.  Likewise, the algebraic reversal $J_Q$ proves the opposite-action
and first-order identities but does not orient a physical charge-conjugation,
Majorana, Berezin, determinant, or Pfaffian line.  An almost-commutative or
Lorentzian theorem must relate these objects by explicit product, occurrence,
reflection, orientation, domain, and cutoff-transport packets.
\end{firewall}

\begin{assessment}[Category-level RGT--NCG conclusion]
The rigorous relation is not a single equality of unrestricted categories.  A
differentially complete Renewal Grand Tensor canonically spectralizes.  Marked
finite and strong compact spectralization are essentially surjective and have
nontrivial universality fibres.  An austere derivation-only source forgets an
explicit commutant anchor space, while strict norm-monoidal transport selects
the spectrally quasidiagonal subclass.  On the loaded Standard-Model branch,
the finite Euclidean/OS spectral packet is now a nonempty terminating sector,
but the first stricter same-history differential incidence is the positive
rank-one germ witness of \Cref{thm:GT-NCG-terminal-short}.  Noncompact,
semifinite, modular, twisted, boundary-index, Lorentzian, and cofinal line
targets require their own spatial, finite-trace, router, orientation, causal,
differentiated-germ, domain, and transport packets; they are not silently
included in the compact positive theorem.
\end{assessment}

\section{Commutants, common action, and Legendre reciprocity}
\label{sec:commutant-action-dualities}
% =============================================================================

\begin{theorem}[Finite commutant decomposition]
\label{thm:commutant-decomposition}
Let $\mathcal A\subseteq\mathcal B(\mathcal H)$ be a finite-dimensional unital
$C^*$-algebra.  There is a unitary decomposition
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal H\cong\bigoplus_{\lambda=1}^r
 \C^{n_\lambda}\otimes\C^{m_\lambda}}
\]
such that
\[
 \mathcal A\cong\bigoplus_\lambda M_{n_\lambda}(\C)\otimes I_{m_\lambda},
 \qquad
 \mathcal A'\cong\bigoplus_\lambda I_{n_\lambda}\otimes M_{m_\lambda}(\C).
\]
In particular, $\mathcal A$ and $\mathcal A'$ are mutual commutants.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Decompose the abstract finite-dimensional algebra into simple matrix blocks.
Its minimal central projections decompose $\mathcal H$ into invariant
summands.  Every unital representation of $M_n(\C)$ is a direct sum of copies
of its defining representation, giving the displayed tensor factors.  A block
operator commutes with all matrix units on the first factor exactly when it is
identity there and arbitrary on the multiplicity factor.  Applying the same
calculation twice gives mutual commutants.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Finite Howe dual pair]
Two unital subalgebras $\mathcal A,\mathcal B\subseteq\mathcal B(\mathcal H)$
form a finite Howe dual pair when
$\mathcal A'=\mathcal B$ and $\mathcal B'=\mathcal A$.
\end{definition}

\begin{proposition}[Terminating commutant audit]
\label{prop:commutant-audit}
For finite generating sets $\{A_i\}$ and $\{B_j\}$, the Howe-pair assertion is
decidable by finite linear algebra: solve
$[X,A_i]=0$ and $[X,B_j]=0$, compare the resulting dimensions with
$\dim\operatorname{alg}(B_j)$ and $\dim\operatorname{alg}(A_i)$, and verify
the inclusions.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Each commutator equation is a homogeneous linear system in the matrix entries
of $X$.  Hence both commutants and both generated finite algebras are computed
in finitely many linear-algebra steps.  An inclusion between finite-dimensional
subspaces plus equality of dimensions is equality.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Common-action Legendre reciprocity]
\label{thm:common-action-Legendre}
Let $B$ be a nondegenerate symmetric quadratic form and let
\[
 L_\chi(q,v)=\frac\chi2B(v,v)-\chi V(q),
 \qquad \chi>0.
\]
Its Legendre transform is
\[
 \boxed{
 H_\chi(q,p)=\frac1{2\chi}B^{-1}(p,p)+\chi V(q).}
\]
Thus one common Lagrangian action coefficient produces reciprocal Hamiltonian
coefficients $a=\chi^{-1}$ and $b=\chi$, with $ab=1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The momentum is $p=\chi Bv$, so
$v=\chi^{-1}B^{-1}p$.  Substitution in
$H=p(v)-L_\chi$ gives the displayed formula.
\end{proof}

\begin{countertheorem}[A second scalar coupling need not create a branch record]
Unequal effective coefficients do not by themselves imply a nontrivial
retained discriminator.
\end{countertheorem}

\begin{proof}
On a one-dimensional action environment every self-adjoint operator is scalar.
Nevertheless two independent action coordinates
$\alpha K+\beta V$ may have $\alpha\ne\beta$.  Thus coefficient inequality can
exist without a non-scalar branch record.
\end{proof}

% =============================================================================
\section{Cycle--flavour and pointed tetrahedral source duality}
\label{sec:cycle-flavour-duality}
% =============================================================================

Let $\Gamma=(V,E)$ be a finite connected graph with incidence map
$\partial:\C^E\to\C^V$.

\begin{theorem}[Exact harmonic cycle projector]
\label{thm:cycle-projector}
The orthogonal projection onto $H_1(\Gamma;\C)=\Ker\partial$ is
\[
 \boxed{
 \Pi_{\rm cyc}=I_E-\partial^*(\partial\partial^*)^\dagger\partial.}
\]
Moreover,
$\dim H_1(\Gamma;\C)=|E|-|V|+1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
For every matrix $M$, the projection onto $\Ker M$ is
$I-M^*(MM^*)^\dagger M$.  A connected graph incidence matrix has rank
$|V|-1$, so rank--nullity gives the dimension formula.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[The $K_4$ cycle carrier]
\label{cor:K4-cycle}
$H_1(K_4;\C)$ has dimension $6-4+1=3$.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The complete graph $K_4$ has four vertices, six edges, and is connected.
Apply \Cref{thm:cycle-projector}.
\end{proof}

\subsection{A renewal-native route to tetrahedral modules}
\label{sec:renewal-native-tetrahedral-modules}

The graph-theoretic cycle carrier above may arise either from a physically
loaded one-cycle edge writer or from the chronology of a more austere renewal
record.  The following theorem states the precise finite hypotheses under
which the latter route is available.

\begin{definition}[Sourcewise-uniform renewal atom packet]
\label{def:uniform-renewal-atoms}
A sourcewise-uniform atomic refinement of the concrete two-state renewal has:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(A\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item one nonwriting $H\to H$ atom and one nonwriting $P\to P$ atom;
\item equal probability for all nonzero atoms with the same source phase;
\item individually point-readable remaining $H\to P$ opportunity atoms and
      the two point-readable completed endpoint atoms;
\item no unread parallel atom beneath these point records; and
\item stationary reset of the atom selector with no feedback from older
      provenance.
\end{enumerate}
The opportunity set is denoted $\Omega$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Atomic opportunity rigidity and relative source]
\label{thm:atomic-opportunity-rigidity}
Every packet of \Cref{def:uniform-renewal-atoms} has
\[
 \boxed{|\Omega|=4,}
\]
with source-$H$ atom weight $1/5$ and source-$P$ atom weight $1/3$.  The
opportunity label of each completed cycle is uniform on $\Omega$ and iid across
cycles, while the completed endpoint is an independent fair bit.

For the centered point contrasts
$X_i=\one_{\{O=i\}}-1/4$, the Gram is
\[
 \boxed{
 G_\Omega=\frac14P_{\rm rel},
 \qquad
 P_{\rm rel}=I-\frac14\mathbf1\mathbf1^*.}
\]
Thus
\[
 \boxed{\rank G_\Omega=3,\qquad
 \lambda_{\min}^+(G_\Omega)=\frac14.}
\]
Under the abstract relabelling action of $S_4$, the relative carrier
$V_{\rm rel}=\mathbf1^\perp$ is the irreducible standard three-dimensional
module and
\[
 \det(\sigma|_{V_{\rm rel}})=\operatorname{sgn}(\sigma).
\]
The full $S_4$ action is physical only when the complete future table is
covariant under these relabellings.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The unique $H\to H$ atom has mass $1/5$, so sourcewise uniformity gives
opportunity atom mass $1/5$.  Their total mass is $4/5$, forcing four atoms.
Likewise the $P\to P$ atom has mass $1/3$ and the completed mass $2/3$ gives
two endpoint atoms.  Geometric summation of the equal departure and completion
atoms makes the opportunity label uniform, the endpoint fair, and both
independent of the numbers of survivor loops; reset gives iid cycles.

The covariance calculation
$\mathbb E(X_iX_j)=\delta_{ij}/4-1/16$ gives the Gram.  Its range is
$\mathbf1^\perp$.  Any nonzero invariant subspace containing a vector with two
unequal coordinates contains one difference $e_i-e_j$ and hence all such
differences, proving irreducibility.  The determinant of the full permutation
module is the sign and the constant line has determinant one.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Ordered two-cycle source gives $H_1(K_4)$]
\label{thm:ordered-opportunity-cycle-source}
Condition on two successive opportunity values being distinct and retain their
order.  The twelve ordered pairs are uniform.  On the antisymmetric ordered-
pair space $\mathcal D^-$ define
\[
 \partial_-(e_i\wedge e_j)=e_j-e_i.
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{
 0\longrightarrow H_1(K_4;\C)
 \longrightarrow\mathcal D^-
 \xrightarrow{\ \partial_-\ }V_{\rm rel}
 \longrightarrow0,}
\]
with
\[
 \boxed{
 H_1(K_4;\C)=\Ker\partial_-=\Lambda^2V_{\rm rel}
 \cong V_{\rm rel}\otimes\Lambda^3V_{\rm rel}.}
\]
The cycle projector and conditional source Gram are
\[
 \boxed{
 P_{\rm cyc}=I-\frac14\partial_-^*\partial_-,
 \qquad
 G_{\rm cyc}=\frac1{12}P_{\rm cyc}.}
\]
Thus the protected order of two renewal cycles produces a canonical
three-dimensional $H_1(K_4)$ source with the necessary orientation twist and
positive margin $1/12$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The antisymmetric ordered-pair space is
$\Lambda^2(\C\mathbf1\oplus V_{\rm rel})
=(\mathbf1\wedge V_{\rm rel})\oplus\Lambda^2V_{\rm rel}$.
The incidence map is onto $V_{\rm rel}$ and vanishes on the second summand, so
its kernel is the three-dimensional exterior square.  Moreover
$\partial_-\partial_-^*=4P_{\rm rel}$, the Laplacian identity for $K_4$,
which gives the projector.  Uniformity of the twelve ordered pairs gives
$I/12$ on the antisymmetric zero-sum space, and compression gives the source
Gram.  Contraction with the determinant line gives the orientation-twisted
identification.
\end{proof}

\begin{countertheorem}[One opportunity value does not determine one local edge]
\label{cth:vertex-no-local-edge}
There is no deterministic $S_4$-equivariant map
$\Omega\to\binom{\Omega}{2}$.  A local edge incident to a given opportunity
vertex requires a further three-valued conditional coordinate.
\end{countertheorem}

\begin{proof}
The stabilizer $S_3$ of one vertex fixes no individual edge of $K_4$, whereas
equivariance would require the image edge of that vertex to be fixed by its
stabilizer.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Matching-axis half-edges and the exact two-standard plane]
\label{thm:matching-axis-half-edge}
Let $\mathscr M$ be the three perfect matchings of $K_4$.  For every
$(i,m)\in\Omega\times\mathscr M$, let $j(i,m)$ be the vertex matched with $i$
and let $\varepsilon(i,m)=\{i,j(i,m)\}$.  Then
\[
 \boxed{(i,m)\longmapsto(i,\varepsilon(i,m))}
\]
is an $S_4$-equivariant bijection from $\Omega\times\mathscr M$ to the twelve
half-edges.  For the uniform point law,
\[
 \boxed{
 L^2(\Omega\times\mathscr M)
 \cong[4]\oplus2[31]\oplus[22]\oplus[211].}
\]
On the standard coefficient space $W_0=\one_4^\perp$, define
\[
 (S_{\rm ent}x)(i,m)=x_i,
 \qquad
 (S_{\rm lock}x)(i,m)=x_i+x_{j(i,m)}.
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{S_{\rm ent}^*S_{\rm ent}=\frac14I_{W_0},\qquad
 S_{\rm lock}^*S_{\rm lock}=\frac13I_{W_0},\qquad
 S_{\rm ent}^*S_{\rm lock}=\frac16I_{W_0}.}
\]
The conditional matching-axis source
\[
 \boxed{S_{\rm ax}:=S_{\rm lock}-\frac23S_{\rm ent}}
\]
is orthogonal to the entry source and satisfies
\[
 \boxed{S_{\rm ax}^*S_{\rm ax}=\frac29I_{W_0}.}
\]
After normalization,
\[
 E_0=2S_{\rm ent},\qquad
 A_0=\frac3{\sqrt2}S_{\rm ax},\qquad
 L_0=\sqrt3S_{\rm lock},
\]
one has
\[
 \boxed{E_0^*E_0=A_0^*A_0=I,
 \qquad E_0^*A_0=0,}
\]
and
\[
 \boxed{L_0=\frac1{\sqrt3}E_0+\sqrt{\frac23}\,A_0.}
\]
Thus entry provenance occupies one standard copy, the conditional matching
axis occupies a second orthogonal copy, and the locked-edge source is their
fixed combination.  The full conditional point-Read innovation over the
vertex record has rank eight and all positive eigenvalues $1/12$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
A perfect matching contains exactly one edge incident to a specified vertex,
and every half-edge determines the unique matching containing its edge and
the disjoint complementary edge.  This proves the equivariant bijection.
Induction from the vertex stabilizer, or the character table of $S_4$, gives
the displayed twelve-dimensional decomposition.

For $x,y\in W_0$, averaging over the twelve pairs gives
\[
 \mathbb E[\overline{x_i}y_i]=\frac14\langle x,y\rangle.
\]
For fixed $i$, each $j\ne i$ occurs once among the three matchings; using
$\sum_jx_j=\sum_jy_j=0$ gives
\[
 \mathbb E[\overline{x_i}(y_i+y_j)]=\frac16\langle x,y\rangle,
\]
and expansion of the two endpoint terms gives
$S_{\rm lock}^*S_{\rm lock}=I/3$.  Subtracting the projection coefficient
$2/3$ gives orthogonality and the Gram $2I/9$.  The normalized decomposition
follows by substitution.  Finally, each of the four vertex fibres is a
uniform three-point simplex of mass $1/4$, whose centered covariance has two
eigenvalues $1/12$; summing the fibres gives rank eight.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Classical opportunity--edge source obstruction]
\label{thm:classical-entry-edge-obstruction}
Let $O$ be a uniform opportunity vertex and $E$ a uniform edge of $K_4$ in one
diagonally $S_4$-invariant classical point law.  Put
\[
 t=\Pr(O\in E).
\]
The complete joint law is
\[
 \Pr(O=i,E=e)=
 \begin{cases}
 t/12,&i\in e,\\
 (1-t)/12,&i\notin e.
 \end{cases}
\]
For the standard entry and edge sources,
\[
 \boxed{S_O^*S_O=\frac14I,
 \qquad S_E^*S_E=\frac13I,
 \qquad S_O^*S_E=\frac{2t-1}{6}I.}
\]
After normalization their cross transport is
\[
 \boxed{\rho_tI,
 \qquad \rho_t=\frac{2t-1}{\sqrt3},
 \qquad |\rho_t|\le\frac1{\sqrt3}.}
\]
Hence both normalized Schur residuals obey
\[
 \boxed{I-\rho_t^2I\succeq\frac23I.}
\]
No classical invariant opportunity--edge point record can therefore make the
entry and locked-edge triplets one normalized physical source.  The
matching-axis branch has $t=1$ and attains the maximal classical correlation,
but still retains the orthogonal axis copy of
\Cref{thm:matching-axis-half-edge}.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
There are twelve incident and twelve nonincident vertex--edge pairs, and
invariance is transitive on each orbit, which gives the joint law.  Direct
averaging of $x_O$ and $x_i+x_j$ for $E=\{i,j\}$ gives the three scalar Gram
blocks.  Whitening gives $\rho_t$, whose bound follows from $0\le t\le1$.
The Schur residual is $I-\rho_t^2I$.
\end{proof}

\begin{firewall}[Chronological cycle source versus local edge writer]
\label{fire:chronological-vs-local-k4}
The source of \Cref{thm:ordered-opportunity-cycle-source} is a two-cycle
history source.  The half-edge of
\Cref{thm:matching-axis-half-edge} is a one-stage local point record.  Neither
is automatically identical to the locked edge/order/charge writer of the
SM--spacetime loading.  Their identification requires one common physical
carrier, the mixed source Gram, the incidence and chronology relations, and
vanishing mutual Schur or cross-Hankel residuals.  Cardinality six or dimension
three alone is not a source-identity theorem.
\end{firewall}

\begin{theorem}[Finite cycle--flavour source duality]
\label{thm:cycle-flavour}
Let $(M_{\rm flav},T_{\rm flav},S_{\rm flav})$ and
$(H_1(\Gamma;\C),T_{\rm cyc},S_{\rm cyc})$ be finite source-minimal positive
transfer realizations whose Krylov packets stabilize at depth $r$.  If
\[
 S_{\rm flav}^*T_{\rm flav}^nS_{\rm flav}
 =S_{\rm cyc}^*T_{\rm cyc}^nS_{\rm cyc}
 \qquad(0\le n\le2r+1),
\]
then there is a unique source-fixing unitary $U$ with
\[
 US_{\rm flav}=S_{\rm cyc},
 \qquad UT_{\rm flav}=T_{\rm cyc}U.
\]
In particular,
$\dim M_{\rm flav}=b_1(\Gamma)$.  For $\Gamma=K_4$, the comparison implies
three loaded flavour copies.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
On stabilized Krylov sums define
\[
 U\left(\sum_{j=0}^rT_{\rm flav}^jS_{\rm flav}x_j\right)
 =\sum_{j=0}^rT_{\rm cyc}^jS_{\rm cyc}x_j.
\]
The moments through order $2r$ make the two Krylov Grams identical, hence the
map is well defined and isometric.  Stabilization and the order-$2r+1$
moments give the transfer intertwining.  Source minimality makes the map onto
and unique.  Equality of dimensions and \Cref{cor:K4-cycle} give the final
claim.
\end{proof}

\begin{countertheorem}[Dimension coincidence is not cycle--flavour duality]
Two three-dimensional carriers need not be source-dual.
\end{countertheorem}

\begin{proof}
Take identity sources and transfers
$\diag(0,1/2,3/4)$ and $\diag(0,1/3,2/3)$.  Their spectra differ, so no unitary
intertwines them.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Five-parameter pointed tetrahedral Gram]
\label{thm:five-parameter-tetrahedral}
Let a unitary $S_4$ representation act on $\mathcal H$, and let
$\Xi=(\xi_t,\xi_1,\xi_2,\xi_3,\xi_4)$ satisfy
$U_g\xi_t=\xi_t$ and $U_g\xi_i=\xi_{g(i)}$.  Then
\[
 G_\Xi=
 \begin{pmatrix}
 a&b&b&b&b\\
 \bar b&c&d&d&d\\
 \bar b&d&c&d&d\\
 \bar b&d&d&c&d\\
 \bar b&d&d&d&c
 \end{pmatrix},
 \qquad a,c,d\in\R,\ b\in\C.
\]
Thus the complete Hermitian source Gram has five real parameters.  It is
positive exactly when $c-d\ge0$ and
$\begin{psmallmatrix}a&2b\\2\bar b&c+3d\end{psmallmatrix}\succeq0$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The diagonal action of $S_4$ on ordered pairs of labels has the five orbits
$(t,t)$, $(t,i)$, $(i,t)$, $(i,i)$, and $(i,j)$ with $i\ne j$.  Invariance
therefore forces the displayed form, and Hermiticity imposes the stated
reality conditions.  The four-point permutation module splits as the average
line plus the three-dimensional augmentation module.  On the latter the Gram
acts by $c-d$; on the two trivial copies spanned by $e_t$ and the normalized
average it acts by the displayed $2\times2$ matrix.  Positivity is therefore
equivalent to positivity on those orthogonal isotypic blocks.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Terminating arithmetic--renewal source test]
Two pointed tetrahedral source families are related by a label-fixing isometry
exactly when their five Gram parameters agree.  If they are cyclic under
transfers of dimension at most $N$, equality of the five orbit panels
$\ip{T^r\xi_a}{T^s\xi_b}$ for $0\le r,s\le N$ yields a unique
source-fixing transfer intertwiner.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Equality of Grams defines the label-fixing isometry on linear combinations and
makes it well defined.  The transfer statement is the same finite Krylov Gram
construction as in \Cref{thm:cycle-flavour}, with the $S_4$ symmetry reducing
each inserted Gram to five orbit entries.
\end{proof}

\section{Common Schur innovations in the prime and GRH branches}
\label{sec:innovation-duality}
% =============================================================================

\begin{theorem}[Exact source-innovation short]
\label{thm:source-innovation}
Let $S_0:\mathcal P_0\to\mathcal H$ and
$S_1:\mathcal P_1\to\mathcal H$ be finite source maps, and put
\[
 A=S_0^*S_0,\qquad B=S_0^*S_1,\qquad D=S_1^*S_1.
\]
If $P_0=S_0A^\dagger S_0^*$ is the orthogonal projection onto
$\Ran S_0$, then
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathbb V_{1\mid0}
 :=D-B^*A^\dagger B
 =S_1^*(I-P_0)S_1\succeq0.}
\]
Its rank is the dimension of the part of $\Ran S_1$ not contained in
$\Ran S_0$, and every nonzero eigenvector reconstructs an explicit missing
source direction.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The Moore--Penrose formula for the projection onto $\Ran S_0$ is
$P_0=S_0(S_0^*S_0)^\dagger S_0^*$.  Substitution gives the identity.
Positivity is immediate.  The rank equals that of $(I-P_0)S_1$, whose range is
the orthogonal innovation space.  Applying $(I-P_0)S_1$ to a nonzero spectral
vector produces the corresponding direction.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[One complex orbit has real rank at most two]
\label{lem:one-complex-orbit-rank}
Let $v\in\C^d$.  The real span of the orbit pair $\{v,\bar v\}$ has dimension
at most two.  Hence no source requiring three independent real innovation
directions can be generated by one complex character--Mellin orbit and its
conjugate.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Write $v=x+iy$ with $x,y\in\R^d$.  Then
$v=x+iy$ and $\bar v=x-iy$ lie in the complexification of
$\Span_\R\{x,y\}$, whose real dimension is at most two.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Opposite innovation objectives]
\label{prop:opposite-innovation}
The same positive short in \Cref{thm:source-innovation} supports two logically
opposite proof objectives.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2.8em]
\item A source-completion theorem seeks a small innovation rank or a structural
      description of every nonzero innovation; in particular,
      \Cref{lem:one-complex-orbit-rank} excludes a rank-three counterstate from
      one complex orbit.
\item A cancellation or coercivity theorem seeks an upper bound for the
      innovation energy, such as
      $\Tr\mathbb V_{1\mid0}$ or
      $\ip{x}{\mathbb V_{1\mid0}x}$.
\end{enumerate}
Neither objective implies the other without additional information.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
The rank and energy are independent spectral statistics of one positive
operator.  For example, $\varepsilon I_N$ has full rank and arbitrarily small
trace for small $\varepsilon$, whereas a rank-one projection has minimal
nonzero rank and unit energy.  The one-orbit conclusion follows from
\Cref{lem:one-complex-orbit-rank}.
\end{proof}

\begin{assessment}[Prime versus GRH use of the same theorem]
In the centered prime-tuple programme, low common resonance rank is a closure
mechanism: a true all-prime counterstate must introduce a third real direction
and therefore at least a second inequivalent character--Mellin orbit.  In the
centered GRH compiler, the predictable source is first shorted away and the
target is instead a uniform upper bound for the remaining innovation energy.
The shared object is the Schur short; the required inequalities point in
opposite directions.
\end{assessment}

% =============================================================================
\section{Interface Schur gluing, scattering feedback, and spectral shift}
\label{sec:interface-duality}
% =============================================================================

Let $\mathcal E_1,\mathcal E_2$ be exterior port spaces and $\mathcal I$ a
common interface.  Suppose
\[
 \Lambda_j(z)=
 \begin{pmatrix}A_j(z)&K_j(z)\\L_j(z)&H_j(z)\end{pmatrix}
 \quad\text{on }\mathcal E_j\oplus\mathcal I,
 \qquad L_j(z)=K_j(\bar z)^*.
\]
Gluing imposes equality of interface values and conservation of outward
interface current.

\begin{theorem}[Exact matrix interface gluing]
\label{thm:interface-gluing}
Assume $H=H_1+H_2$ is invertible and put
\[
 A=\begin{pmatrix}A_1&0\\0&A_2\end{pmatrix},
 \qquad K=\binom{K_1}{K_2},
 \qquad L=\begin{pmatrix}L_1&L_2\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Then the glued exterior response is
\[
 \boxed{\Lambda_{1\#2}=A-KH^{-1}L.}
\]
For exterior value $(x_1,x_2)$, the interface value is
\[
 \boxed{u=-H^{-1}(L_1x_1+L_2x_2).}
\]
Moreover,
\[
 \boxed{
 \det\begin{pmatrix}
 A_1&0&K_1\\0&A_2&K_2\\L_1&L_2&H_1+H_2
 \end{pmatrix}
 =\det(H_1+H_2)\det\Lambda_{1\#2}.}
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The interface responses are $g_j=L_jx_j+H_ju$.  Current conservation
$g_1+g_2=0$ gives the formula for $u$.  Substitution into
$f_j=A_jx_j+K_ju$ yields the Schur formula.  The determinant identity is the
Schur determinant formula with respect to the interface block.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Herglotz closure under conservative gluing]
\label{thm:Herglotz-gluing}
If $\Lambda_1$ and $\Lambda_2$ are strict matrix Herglotz functions, then
$H_1(z)+H_2(z)$ is invertible for $\im z>0$ and
$\Lambda_{1\#2}$ is strict Herglotz.  More precisely, if $u$ is the solved
interface value, then
\[
 \boxed{
 \ip{x}{\im\Lambda_{1\#2}(z)x}
 =\sum_{j=1}^2
 \ip{(x_j,u)}{\im\Lambda_j(z)(x_j,u)}.}
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The interface block of a strict Herglotz function has positive-definite
imaginary part, so $\im(H_1+H_2)\succ0$ and the sum is invertible.  The total
boundary work is
\[
 \sum_j\ip{(x_j,u)}{\Lambda_j(x_j,u)}
 =\sum_j\ip{x_j}{f_j}+\ip{u}{g_1+g_2}
 =\ip{x}{\Lambda_{1\#2}x}.
\]
The interface term vanishes by conservation.  Taking imaginary parts proves
the identity and strict positivity.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Associative interface elimination]
\label{thm:Schur-associativity}
Let a finite response be split into exterior space $\mathcal E$ and internal
space $\mathcal I_1\oplus\mathcal I_2$.  Whenever all displayed Schur
complements exist,
\[
 \boxed{
 \bigl(L/L_{I_1I_1}\bigr)
 /\bigl(L/L_{I_1I_1}\bigr)_{I_2I_2}
 =L/L_{II}.}
\]
Hence a finite network response is independent of the order in which internal
interfaces are eliminated.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Block Gaussian elimination first on $\mathcal I_1$ and then on
$\mathcal I_2$ has the same exterior diagonal block as direct elimination on
$\mathcal I_1\oplus\mathcal I_2$.  Equivalently, both sides are obtained by
solving the same internal Euler equation and inserting its unique solution
into the quadratic form.
\end{proof}

For a self-adjoint real-axis response, define the Cayley scattering matrix
\[
 \mathcal S=(\Lambda-iI)(\Lambda+iI)^{-1}.
\]

\begin{theorem}[Schur response--Redheffer scattering equivalence]
\label{thm:Schur-Redheffer}
Under the wave coordinates
$a=2^{-1/2}(j+iu)$ and $b=2^{-1/2}(j-iu)$, the response law
$j=\Lambda u$ is equivalent to $b=\mathcal Sa$.  Conservative interface
gluing becomes the signed feedback relation
$a_2=-b_1$, $b_2=-a_1$.  Eliminating the internal waves gives the Redheffer
star product.  If the component scattering matrices are contractions
(respectively unitaries), their well-posed star product is a contraction
(respectively a unitary), and the product is associative whenever all
intermediate feedback problems are well posed.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Solving
$a=(\Lambda+iI)u/\sqrt2$ and substituting in $b$ gives the Cayley formula.
At a common interface, equality of $u$ and reversal of outward current give
the signed feedback equations.  Both the Schur response and Redheffer
scattering formulas are obtained by eliminating those same internal variables
through an invertible linear change of coordinates, so the exterior maps
coincide.

For contractive components, add their two input--output energy inequalities.
The internal incoming and outgoing norms cancel under feedback, leaving the
exterior contractive inequality.  For unitary components the inequalities are
equalities; the same argument for the adjoint gives surjectivity.  Either
parenthesization of a multiple star product solves the same finite linear
system, so uniqueness gives associativity.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Matrix continued fraction and layer stripping]
\label{thm:matrix-continued-fraction}
Let
\[
 \mathbb J=
 \begin{pmatrix}
 C_0&B_0^*&0&\cdots&0\\
 B_0&C_1&B_1^*&\ddots&\vdots\\
 0&B_1&C_2&\ddots&0\\
 \vdots&\ddots&\ddots&\ddots&B_{m-1}^*\\
 0&\cdots&0&B_{m-1}&C_m
 \end{pmatrix}
\]
be a finite self-adjoint block Jacobi chain, and let $\Lambda_k(z)$ be the
response of the tail beginning at layer $k$.  Then
\[
 \Lambda_m(z)=zI-C_m,
 \qquad
 \boxed{
 \Lambda_k(z)=zI-C_k-B_k^*\Lambda_{k+1}(z)^{-1}B_k.}
\]
If every $B_k$ is square and invertible, then
\[
 \boxed{
 \Lambda_{k+1}(z)
 =-B_k(\Lambda_k(z)-zI+C_k)^{-1}B_k^*.}
\]
In the positive gauge $B_k\succ0$, the complete response $\Lambda_0$ uniquely
reconstructs every layer.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Treat the tail beginning at $k+1$ as the hidden interior of layer $k$ and
apply the Schur formula.  Rearranging gives the reverse recursion when $B_k$
is invertible.  At high imaginary energy,
\[
 \Lambda_k(z)=zI-C_k-z^{-1}B_k^*B_k+O(z^{-2}).
\]
Thus the constant and $z^{-1}$ coefficients recover $C_k$ and $B_k^*B_k$.
The positive square root fixes $B_k$, after which layer stripping reconstructs
$\Lambda_{k+1}$; induction recovers all layers.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Boundary spectral-shift identity]
\label{thm:boundary-spectral-shift}
Let $\mathbb A_0,\mathbb A_1$ have one common interior and two boundary loads,
and let $\Lambda_0,\Lambda_1$ be their responses.  Then
\[
 \mathcal D_{10}(z)
 :=\frac{\det(\mathbb A_1-zI)}{\det(\mathbb A_0-zI)}
 =\frac{\det\Lambda_1(z)}{\det\Lambda_0(z)}
\]
and, away from the spectra,
\[
 \boxed{
 \frac{\dd}{\dd z}\log\mathcal D_{10}(z)
 =-\Tr\bigl[(\mathbb A_1-zI)^{-1}-(\mathbb A_0-zI)^{-1}\bigr].}
\]
For a contour domain $\Omega$ avoiding both spectra,
\[
 \boxed{
 N_\Omega(\mathbb A_1)-N_\Omega(\mathbb A_0)
 =\frac1{2\pi i}\int_{\partial\Omega}
 \frac{\dd}{\dd z}\log\mathcal D_{10}(z)\,\dd z.}
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The determinant ratio is the Schur determinant identity applied to the common
interior.  Jacobi's formula gives
$\frac{\dd}{\dd z}\log\det(\mathbb A_j-zI)
=-\Tr(\mathbb A_j-zI)^{-1}$; subtract.  The contour formula is the argument
principle, with zeros and poles of the ratio counting the two spectra.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Positive Wigner--Smith boundary Gram]
\label{thm:positive-delay}
On a real pole-free interval, assume $\Lambda(x)=\Lambda(x)^*$ and
$\Lambda'(x)\succ0$.  For
$\mathcal S(x)=(\Lambda(x)-iI)(\Lambda(x)+iI)^{-1}$, put
$\mathcal Q_{\mathcal S}=-i\mathcal S^*\mathcal S'$.  Then
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal Q_{\mathcal S}(x)
 =2(\Lambda+iI)^{-*}\Lambda'(x)(\Lambda+iI)^{-1}\succ0,}
\]
and
\[
 \frac{\dd}{\dd x}\arg\det\mathcal S(x)
 =\Tr\mathcal Q_{\mathcal S}(x)>0.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Differentiate the Cayley transform to obtain
$\mathcal S'=2i(\Lambda+iI)^{-1}\Lambda'(\Lambda+iI)^{-1}$.  Since
$\mathcal S^*=(\Lambda-iI)^{-1}(\Lambda+iI)$ on the real axis, multiplication
gives the positive congruence.  Finally,
$\frac{\dd}{\dd x}\log\det\mathcal S
=\Tr(\mathcal S^*\mathcal S')=i\Tr\mathcal Q_{\mathcal S}$.
\end{proof}

\begin{countertheorem}[Local spectra do not determine gluing]
\label{cth:relative-interface-frame}
Complete spectra of the component interface blocks do not determine the glued
response without their relative interface frame.
\end{countertheorem}

\begin{proof}
On $\C^2$, put
$H_1=\diag(2,1)$ and take either
$H_2=\diag(2,1)$ or $H_2'=\diag(1,2)$.  The latter two have identical spectra,
but
$H_1+H_2=\diag(4,2)$ whereas $H_1+H_2'=3I$.  With exterior coupling $K=I$,
the Schur corrections are $\diag(1/4,1/2)$ and $I/3$, respectively.
\end{proof}

\begin{countertheorem}[Schur elimination can create quadratic fill-in]
\label{cth:Schur-fill-in}
A primitive system with $n$ boundary--interior couplings can have a Schur
response with $n^2$ nonzero entries.
\end{countertheorem}

\begin{proof}
Let one hidden scalar node of energy $d$ couple to all $n$ boundary ports by
$b=(b_1,\ldots,b_n)^{\mathsf T}$ with every $b_j\ne0$.  Its self-energy is
$bb^*/(d-z)$, whose every entry $b_i\bar b_j/(d-z)$ is nonzero.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Interface and network coercivity]
\label{thm:interface-coercivity}
At a real pole-free point let
$\Lambda=A-KH^{-1}K^*$.  If
\[
 s_{\min}(A)\ge\delta_A>0,
 \qquad s_{\min}(H)\ge\delta_I>0,
 \qquad \norm K\le\kappa,
\]
then
\[
 \boxed{s_{\min}(\Lambda)\ge\delta_A-\kappa^2/\delta_I.}
\]
More generally, for a final exterior/interior split
$\mathbb A=\begin{psmallmatrix}C&B^*\\B&D\end{psmallmatrix}$, if
\[
 \norm{(D-zI)^{-1}}\le M_D,
 \qquad \norm B\le M_B,
 \qquad s_{\min}(\Lambda(z))\ge\delta_E>0,
\]
then
\[
 \boxed{
 \norm{(\mathbb A-zI)^{-1}}
 \le M_D+\frac{1+M_D^2M_B^2}{\delta_E}.}
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The Schur perturbation obeys
$\norm{KH^{-1}K^*}\le\kappa^2/\delta_I$; the minimum-singular-value
perturbation inequality proves the first bound.  For the second, the solution
operator from exterior data to the full vector is
$\gamma(z)x=(x,-(D-zI)^{-1}Bx)$, so
$\norm\gamma(z)^2\le1+M_D^2M_B^2$.  The block resolvent formula is the direct
interior resolvent plus
$\gamma(z)\Lambda(z)^{-1}\gamma(\bar z)^*$; taking norms gives the result.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Integrated interface duality]
\label{thm:integrated-interface-duality}
For finite source-minimal self-adjoint boundary systems, the following are
coordinate presentations of one interface object:
\[
 \begin{gathered}
 \text{interface gluing}
 \ \Updownarrow\ 
 \text{matrix Schur response}
 \ \Updownarrow\ 
 \text{signed Redheffer feedback}\\[0.25em]
 \Updownarrow\\[-0.1em]
 \text{matrix continued fractions and layer stripping}\\[0.25em]
 \Updownarrow\\[-0.1em]
 \text{determinant ratios, spectral shift, and positive delay}.
 \end{gathered}
\]
The complete matrix response is required for relative-frame gluing and source
loading; determinant functions are scalar shadows.  Exact interface duality
is not automatically resource faithful.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The equivalences and closure statements are
\Cref{thm:interface-gluing,thm:Herglotz-gluing,thm:Schur-associativity,thm:Schur-Redheffer,thm:matrix-continued-fraction,thm:boundary-spectral-shift,thm:positive-delay}.  The necessity of the matrix
frame and the resource boundary are
\Cref{cth:relative-interface-frame,cth:Schur-fill-in}.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Master no-overstatement boundary]
\label{prop:no-overstatement}
The results of this manuscript do not imply:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\arabic*)},leftmargin=2.8em]
\item that finite structural emergence identifies an unexposed hidden
      instrument or fine score basis, proves a downstream synchronized
      edge/order/charge loading, places the process in the optional coherent
      Store--score phase, determines a physical fringe panel, places every
      independently sourced physical history in one universal ideal, or gives a
      neutral record a domain-specific meaning;
\item that finite-cutoff Hankel rank, source completeness, prefix-comb
      support, flat depth, a finite full-record carrier, pointwise tightness, or a
      pointwise physical gap, a finite Hellinger secant, or a finite spectral
      peak implies finite recurrent CP memory, a physical tangent, bounded
      infinite-horizon action, uniform observability, a noncollapsing physical
      rate, an actual character atom, or a nontrivial physical continuum
      realization; nor that a fixed
      per-cycle gap survives a shrinking physical step, that predictor
      innovation is physical dissipation without the outgoing-energy panel, or
      that independent local gaps survive a fixed-rate random-scan scheduler;
\item that the degree-one pairwise shadow, without its word hierarchy and
      complete mixed occurrence panels, determines multiplication, higher
      fusion, associators, occurrence innovations, chain differential, positive
      cone, graded action, or resource metric;
\item that the total primitive algebra is only $M_4(\C)$, or that every
      higher-arity, relation-coloured, nonfaithful, or purposefully enriched
      loading has $(3+1)$ dimensions.  What is proved is the $3+1$ conclusion
      for the future-minimal, reciprocal, pair-homogeneous, faithful and
      compiler-minimal one-source/one-target relational branch;
\item that equality of marginal, spectral, finite-transform, or regular-trace
      data proves identity of independently loaded physical sources or metrics;
\item that the finite Standard-Model seed, anomaly theorem, a formal grading
      label, or the existence of a finite commutant fixes the autonomous odd
      Store coefficient, the regulator-stable multiplicity algebra, flavour
      matrices, masses, or mixing parameters without the record, relative Howe,
      support-tail, and Hodge-screen certificates;
\item that the displayed six-state source carries a grading-changing matter
      occurrence, that typed and colour marginals select $K_{\rm rep}$, that the
      source-native occurrence residuals vanish without differentiated
      cross-support data, or that availability of the protected score-square
      fallback proves the unchanged autonomous Store executes it;
\item that ordinary unmarked transport moments determine a numerical finite
      Dirac/Yukawa operator, a physical scalar action, or a nonzero normal source;
\item that the spacetime Clifford algebra equals the Standard-Model gauge
      algebra;
\item that additive--multiplicative Fourier duality, Frobenius copies, affine
      Wilson orbits, character Parseval, or degree-one Ward cancellation supplies
      arithmetic contraction in the neutral higher tensor grades;
\item that fixed source saturation, endpoint coalescence, the Jacobi edge, or

\item that an exact prime/factor-depth selector, local admissibility, GRH,

\item that separate old and new localizer marginals determine their mixed
      action block, kernel orientation, or global floor; that a zero symmetric
      memory Schur floor is automatically a persistent soft mode before the
      circulation-observability audit; or that equality of affine colour
      response means proves equality of quotient selector odds or nonlinear

\item that a finite transfer gap is already a continuum Yang--Mills mass gap;
\item that a harmonic projection produces rational algebraic cycles;
\item that a large Hilbert-space dimension gives a circuit lower bound;
\item that scalar local determinants determine matrix interface gluing;
\item that finite-height zero tomography or a positive finite Stein metric,

\item that any unresolved arithmetic, PDE, gauge, geometric, or complexity

\end{enumerate}

\begin{assessment}[Recommended research order]
The finite structural Grand Tensor, the renewal-native two-state process, and
the universal directed-limit, locality, coercivity, pressure-flow, and memory
frameworks are now mature.  The primitive temporal continuum is no longer the
main uncertainty: the accepted-response pressure fixes its action anchor and
the intrinsic fast phase has vanishing generator-scale feedback.  The
highest-value continuum task is now the evaluation of the actual physical
panels on one regulator family.  First construct the protected endpoint and
edge-current atlas, evaluate one pair, one triple, one four-body, one edge, and
one triangle prototype, and prove the pressure-flow cut margin through bounded
congestion, protected collars, or an integrated coordinate atlas.  This closes
the global spatial Poincar\'e and compact-screen problem.

Next place the Palatini, matter, gauge, potential, counterterm, boundary, and
duration rewards on one resolved first-return record.  Compute the reward
covariance and renewal-pressure jet, test common-action curl and periods, and
evaluate the memory short, connection Euler/spin source, exact potential and
counterterm residuals, coherent Ward Gram, and determining stationarity panel.
In parallel, audit the loaded transient spectrum and couplings: classify every
low mode as a declared field or canonical innovation, include it in the common
action, and prove decay of the high-energy Feshbach and Hankel tails.  The final
classical local target is then the $o(\tau_X)$ actual-cycle/action comparison
on those completed fields, not another abstract continuum theorem.  Once the
fine accepted/action rows are available, reconstruct first the canonical
likelihood-ratio and projective experiment records, then the future-saturated
and generator-retract states.  Only after those finite tests pass should one
compare full trajectory likelihoods, hidden entropy production, tilted Perron
spectra, and the corresponding driven rare-event dynamics.  This order avoids
using one-time row agreement as a surrogate for pathwise or long-time action
closure.

The active Standard-Model programme has crossed its first two closure
milestones.  The geometry-shorted residual, two tetrahedral controls, and one
odd root-edge seed give a finite structural SM packet; the same carrier now
supports one local gauge--Higgs--Dirac--Yukawa action with exact Ward, classical
BRST, current, stress, and cofinal classical convergence.  The next task is not
a further structural enlargement.  It is the literal numerical marginal
packet: execute the returned-word deformations, test score descent and the
common nuisance--old--new block, and, on every positive reflected subsector,
close the conditional action-response carrier by its first three stationary
lag Grams before diagonalization.  Then close the source-cyclic localizer
moments, reconstruct the operational matrix-order cone and its physical
calibration, compute the constant-localizer kernel and Feshbach jets, and
certify the full projective ray and scalar interval.  The unnormalized
partition/direct-action row and the determinant/Pfaffian modulus and phase are
then added as distinct measure components.  Only after this packet is frozen
should one address counterterms, running, matching, flavour numerics, and the
interacting quantum continuum.  The older grading, provenance, and relative-
Howe panels remain essential for historical reuse and for alternative
non-active realizations, but are no longer existence premises for the explicit

The colour sector now has a comparably sharp dynamic frontier.  Its local
$SU(3)$ action is an exact restriction of the active Standard-Model action,
but the transfer law is not selected by that action.  The next admissible
calculation is one physical full-coupling reflected slab.  When its Doob kernel

to control the selector fibre and reference-relative information projection.
Only after this finite landing should the Yang--Mills attack return to weak-
coupling ultraviolet/infrared floors and the interacting Osterwalder--Schrader
continuum.

The arithmetic joint-source programme is structurally wrapped at degree one,
but the actual-panel discipline now separates the remaining quantitative work.
For GRH, evaluate both the completed--Euler metric bridge and the integrated
hard-box fixed/coboundary leakage, together with the independent lower bridge.
For affine primes, reconstruct the degree-two occurrence panel before testing

Chain, quantum determinant-line, and resource problems retain their named
